Philosophy is marked on argument, on textual evidence, and on whether a student can state and then answer the strongest objection to their own position. This page sets out each component and the word limit attached to it. Lessons run live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Philosophy at Standard and Higher Level to Abu Dhabi students over live video. Each profile names the optional themes and prescribed texts they teach, and whether they supervise the internal assessment.

intro.heading: What the first marked Philosophy essay tells you
paragraphs: Diploma Philosophy is chosen by articulate students and marked on something articulacy does not supply. The first essay a student writes is usually fluent, well organised, and scored lower than they expected, because it sets out a position and defends it without ever stating the position that opposes it. Philosophy mark schemes reward the construction of an argument, the use of philosophical concepts with precision, and genuine engagement with a counterposition. Writing well is a prerequisite, not an achievement.

That is good news for a family deciding whether tutoring will help. The gap is structural and identifiable in one sitting. A tutor can take a student's own essay, number the premises, show where a step is missing, name the objection a philosopher in that tradition would make, and ask the student to answer it. Most students can do that work the first time it is demonstrated; what they cannot do is invent the structure unaided, because nothing earlier in school asked them to.

The course is assessed through a paper on the core theme and an optional theme, a paper on one prescribed text the school has chosen, an internally assessed philosophical analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus written to a 2,000-word ceiling, and at Higher Level a further paper on the nature of philosophical activity based on an unseen text. Confirm the current weightings with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle and a stale figure sends effort to the wrong component.

Three features of this subject consistently surprise Abu Dhabi parents. First, Paper 2 requires reading an actual philosophical text, not reading about it, and the marks depend on citing passages. Second, the internal assessment starts from something that is not philosophy at all, a film, an advertisement, a news item or an image, and the skill is extracting a genuine philosophical issue from it. Third, the word limits across the Diploma are strict and interact: a student writing a Philosophy internal assessment, a Theory of Knowledge essay and an Extended Essay is working to three different ceilings in the same term.

Lessons for UAE families run live online, one to one, with a shared screen. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. For Philosophy the shared screen earns its place: a passage from the prescribed text sits on one side, the student's paragraph on the other, and the tutor marks the point at which the argument stops following from the text. That annotated pair is saved, which is what makes the next session continuous rather than a fresh conversation.

There is one more reason families in this emirate come to us for this subject rather than for a more widely taught one. Philosophy is offered by relatively few schools here, and where it runs the class is often three or four students taught by a teacher whose main subject is something else. That is a calibration problem rather than a teaching problem. A student in a class of three has almost no marked work to compare their own against, so a competent essay can sit two bands below where they believe it sits, and nothing in the school year reveals that until a mock. An external reader who will object to the argument is the cheapest correction available.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.programmesIntro: Philosophy is a Group 3 Diploma course and is offered by relatively few schools in this emirate. Students reach it by three routes, each leaving a distinct first-term gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Assessed by a paper combining the core theme with an optional theme, a paper on one prescribed text, an internally assessed analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus, and at Higher Level a paper on the nature of philosophical activity. Every component rewards the same underlying skill: an argument set out so that each step can be examined and objected to.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Abu Dhabi schools offer Philosophy, classes here are often very small and sometimes taught by a teacher whose main subject is something else. That is not a criticism of the teaching; it is a description of the calibration problem. A class of three produces almost no marked exemplars, so students have little sense of where their work sits against the bands.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP individuals and societies and language and literature both build the habits of structured discussion and textual reading that Philosophy formalises. What the MYP does not require is the explicit identification of premises and the deliberate construction of an objection, which are the two moves every Philosophy mark scheme rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving from an Abu Dhabi MYP cohort usually write confidently and argue implicitly. The first intervention is mechanical: write the argument as numbered premises before writing prose. Students find it uncomfortable for a fortnight and then find their essays getting shorter and scoring higher, which is the point at which the habit sticks.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A CP student may take Diploma Philosophy as one of their DP courses, sitting the identical components. The reflective project in CP shares real ground with philosophical analysis, since both require a student to examine an issue and consider positions other than their own.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in this emirate taking Philosophy are typically the only candidate in their school doing so. One-to-one work supplies the thing a class normally supplies: somebody to object to the argument. Philosophy learned without opposition produces essays that have never been tested, and the examination is the first place they are.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Philosophy
programmes.description: A 4,000-word essay on a philosophical question, supervised in school. The subject-specific failure is choosing a question that is not philosophical, such as a historical or empirical question about what a thinker believed, rather than an argumentative question about whether a position can be sustained.
programmes.countryNote: Students in Abu Dhabi have good library access through the universities on Saadiyat Island, which matters because a Philosophy Extended Essay needs scholarship rather than summaries. It is also the right home for an interest in the Arabic philosophical tradition, which rarely appears on the prescribed-text list but is entirely legitimate essay territory.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the components and neighbouring courses Abu Dhabi families raise alongside Philosophy, with what each one demands.

subjects.name: Core theme: being human
subjects.levels: HL and SL, Paper 1 Section A
subjects.description: Answered from an unseen stimulus, which must be used as a starting point and not described. The marks are for identifying a philosophical issue the stimulus raises and then arguing about it, so an answer that spends a page explaining the image has spent a page on nothing.

subjects.name: Optional themes
subjects.levels: HL and SL, Paper 1 Section B
subjects.description: Ethics, epistemology, philosophy of religion, philosophy of science, political philosophy and related themes, with the school choosing which it teaches. Standard Level students study one; Higher Level students study two, which is the main content difference between the levels.

subjects.name: Prescribed text
subjects.description: One text set by the school from the IB's prescribed list, examined through questions that require passages to be used as evidence. Students who have read a summary rather than the text can discuss the ideas and cannot cite the argument, and the mark scheme can tell the difference.

subjects.name: Internal assessment
subjects.description: A philosophical analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus: a film, an advertisement, an image, a news item. Marked on the identification of the issue, the quality of the philosophical analysis and the engagement with it. Most lost marks come from describing the stimulus instead of using it.

subjects.name: Higher Level paper on philosophical activity
subjects.description: An unseen text about what philosophy is and how it proceeds, answered analytically. It rewards students who have thought about method rather than only about positions, and it is the component most often left until the final term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The closest relative Philosophy has, and the two reinforce each other directly. The TOK essay runs to a 1,600-word ceiling and the exhibition commentary to 950, so a Philosophy student is working to several limits at once and benefits from treating them as one skill.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Trains close reading, which is exactly what the prescribed text paper requires. The transfer needs stating explicitly: literary analysis asks what a text does, while philosophical analysis asks whether its argument works, and those are different questions about the same page.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A frequent companion, strong on evidence discipline and on taking opposing positions seriously. The risk is answering a philosophical question historically, by describing what thinkers believed and when, rather than assessing whether a position can be defended.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Overlaps substantially with political philosophy as an optional theme, particularly on legitimacy, rights and justice. Students taking both can use the same reading twice, provided they keep Global Politics empirical and keep Philosophy normative.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Shares the structure of formal reasoning, and students on this route often take to premise-and-conclusion analysis quickly. Epistemology and philosophy of science both benefit from a student who is comfortable with the idea of a proof and its assumptions.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities, libraries and the institutions a Philosophy student can use
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.regionsIntro: Philosophy needs texts and interlocutors rather than field sites, so these notes cover both where students live and where scholarship and relevant institutions sit in this emirate.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: University campuses with academic libraries and public lecture programmes, plus the Abrahamic Family House, which opened in 2023. For a student studying philosophy of religion, that is a documented institution raising live questions about pluralism and belief.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment communities with large Diploma cohorts and crowded evenings. Philosophy sessions work well in a fixed 60-minute slot here, because an argument-building session needs an uninterrupted stretch rather than a flexible window.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The emirate's largest Diploma population, and the corridor where Philosophy is most often taken in a class of three or four. Students here gain most from an external reader who will object to their arguments rather than agree with them.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods where several students take Philosophy alongside English A at Higher Level. That combination is strong on textual reading and needs explicit work on the difference between interpreting a text and assessing its argument.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: Home to research institutions working on artificial intelligence and energy, which makes questions about mind, agency and technology concrete rather than abstract. A useful source of internal assessment stimuli that are genuinely local and not over-used.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with younger cohorts, where Philosophy is sometimes newly introduced and the first cohort has no predecessors' work to learn from. That is the clearest case for bringing in marked exemplars from outside the school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Inside the same emirate, with a small international-school market and effectively no local Philosophy specialists. Students here who take the subject are almost always dependent on online teaching, which is the straightforward argument for it.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Mainland communities well away from the island's institutions, so library access is largely digital. For Philosophy that matters less than for most subjects, provided the student has a proper edition of the prescribed text rather than a summary.

modes.title: Argument-building sessions
modes.description: A weekly slot in which the student writes an argument as numbered premises, the tutor attacks it, and the student revises it before writing prose. Essays are then marked on screen against the band descriptors. The deliverable is the structure, because once a student can build and defend an argument the content takes care of itself.

sections.heading: The components, the word limits and where effort should go
paragraphs: Standard Level Philosophy comprises a paper covering the core theme and one optional theme, a paper on one prescribed text, and the internal assessment. Higher Level adds a second optional theme and a further paper on the nature of philosophical activity based on an unseen text. The first paper carries the largest share of the grade at both levels, which is worth knowing because it is also the paper students prepare least deliberately, treating it as the one where general ability will carry them.

The word limits are the other thing to plan around, and they are not negotiable. The Philosophy internal assessment runs to a 2,000-word ceiling. The Theory of Knowledge essay, which every Diploma student writes, runs to 1,600. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000. A Philosophy student who also chooses this subject for the Extended Essay is therefore writing three argumentative pieces to three different ceilings, often in the same two terms, and the planning failure is treating them as one task that can be left in sequence to the last minute.

The table below sets the components beside the limits so the whole load is visible on one screen. Weightings are given as indicative shares and should be confirmed with the Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises guides periodically. What does not change is the ordering of effort: the first paper is the biggest block of marks, the prescribed text is the component where unprepared students are most exposed, and the internal assessment is the one whose deadline arrives while everything else is also due.

sections.heading: Argument, not opinion: the move that changes the mark
paragraphs: The single most productive hour in Diploma Philosophy is the one in which a student learns to write their own argument as numbered premises. It looks like a classroom exercise and it is the whole subject. A claim written as prose can hide a missing step; the same claim written as premises cannot. Once a student sees that premise two does not follow from premise one, they can either repair the argument or choose a different one, and both are philosophical work. Fluent prose that conceals the gap earns nothing.

The second move is the counterposition, and students resist it because it feels like conceding. The mark schemes reward the opposite: an essay that states the strongest objection to its own position and then answers it demonstrates exactly the capacity being assessed. An essay that mentions an objection in a subordinate clause and dismisses it demonstrates that the student knows objections exist. Those two essays can contain the same information and sit two bands apart.

The third is conceptual precision. Philosophy words have technical uses, and using them loosely is the commonest invisible loss in this subject. Knowledge, justification, free will, personhood, duty, right: each has a specific role in the debates the course covers, and an essay that uses one in its everyday sense while the question uses it technically answers a different question. A tutor's work here is pedantic in the best sense, stopping at each term and asking what the student means by it.
bullets: Write the argument as numbered premises before writing any prose
State the strongest objection, then answer it; do not wave at it
Check every technical term against its use in the debate
Shorter, tighter essays frequently outscore longer fluent ones

sections.heading: Paper 1: using a stimulus instead of describing it
paragraphs: The core theme section of Paper 1 begins with an unseen stimulus: an image, a short passage, a scenario. It exists to prompt a philosophical question about being human, and the marks are for the argument that follows, not for the reading of the stimulus. Students who have not practised this spend a substantial part of their answer explaining what the stimulus shows, which is both unrewarded and time they needed for the argument.

The practised version takes about ninety seconds. Read the stimulus, identify two philosophical issues it raises, choose the one you can argue best, state it as a question, and begin. A single sentence connects the stimulus to the question, and then the stimulus is finished with. That sequence has to be drilled, because under examination pressure the instinct is to describe what is in front of you, and the instinct is wrong.

The optional theme section is a conventional essay on the theme or themes the school teaches, and it fails in a predictable way: the two-sided answer that presents a view, presents the opposite, and concludes that both have merit. Balance is not the criterion; argument is. A student may reach a modest conclusion, but it has to be a conclusion, reached by weighing the objections rather than by listing them. Standard Level students study one optional theme and Higher Level students two, which is the main content difference between the levels and the reason Higher Level revision needs sequencing rather than cramming.
bullets: Connect the stimulus to a question in one sentence, then leave it
Choose the issue you can argue, not the most interesting one
Balanced-and-therefore-undecided essays sit in the middle bands
Higher Level covers two optional themes, so sequence the revision

sections.heading: Paper 2: the prescribed text, and why summaries fail
paragraphs: Paper 2 examines one philosophical text, chosen by the school from the IB's prescribed list, which includes both Western and non-Western works. Confirm which text your child's school has set before engaging any tutor, because this is the component where the wrong specialism is least recoverable: a tutor who knows one text extremely well is of limited use to a student examined on another. The texts schools commonly set include works by Plato, Descartes, Hume, Mill, Nietzsche, Sartre and de Beauvoir, among others on the list.

The reason summaries fail is simple. The questions require the student to use the text as evidence, which means locating the passage where the argument is actually made and showing what it says. A student who has read a study guide knows the conclusions and cannot point to the reasoning, so their answer describes a position the author held rather than examining the argument the author gave. Examiners see the difference immediately, and the band descriptors are written to catch it.

The work that fixes this is slow and unglamorous. The text is read in the student's own edition, section by section, with the argument mapped rather than summarised: what is claimed, what supports it, what the author anticipates as an objection, how the reply works. Passages are marked so they can be found under examination conditions. Standard objections to the text are rehearsed, because a question asking the student to assess the argument wants a real criticism and not a complaint about style. Four or five sessions of that on the set text transforms this component.
bullets: Find out which prescribed text the school has set before choosing a tutor
Read the text itself in a proper edition, not a study guide
Map the argument section by section: claim, support, objection, reply
Mark passages so they can be cited quickly in the examination

sections.heading: The internal assessment: 2,000 words from something that is not philosophy
paragraphs: The internally assessed task asks for a philosophical analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus, written to a 2,000-word ceiling. The stimulus can be a film, an advertisement, a photograph, a news item, a song, a piece of fiction. It must not be a philosophical text, and the assessment is not of the stimulus but of the philosophical work the student does from it. Confirm the current criteria and word limit with your child's teacher, since the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle.

Stimulus choice is the decision that determines the mark, and it is made worst when made fastest. A stimulus with real traction raises a question the course's concepts can address: an advertisement that presupposes something about personal identity, a film that depends on a particular account of free will, a news item in which two conceptions of justice collide. A stimulus with no traction produces a paper that describes the film for 800 words and then attaches some philosophy to it. Testing the stimulus before writing is half an hour that saves a fortnight.

The second common loss is breadth. Two thousand words is enough for one issue examined properly, with an objection and a reply, and nothing like enough for three issues mentioned. Students who have read widely want to show it, and the ceiling punishes them for it. A word budget agreed before drafting, with the analysis given the bulk of the count, is the practical control. Feedback from a tutor is comment on drafts the student has written, naming the criterion and the marks at stake; no portion of the submitted text comes from anybody else.
bullets: The stimulus must be non-philosophical; the analysis must be philosophical
Test the stimulus for traction before writing anything
One issue analysed properly beats three issues mentioned

sections.heading: Higher Level: the paper about philosophy itself
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit an additional paper based on an unseen text concerning the nature of philosophical activity: what philosophy is, how it proceeds, what distinguishes it from other enquiry, what its methods can and cannot settle. It is the component students most often postpone, partly because it has no syllabus content to revise and partly because it sounds like something that cannot be prepared for. Both impressions are wrong.

It can be prepared, and the preparation is transferable. A student who has thought explicitly about method across the course has the material: why philosophers construct thought experiments, what an appeal to intuition is doing, how conceptual analysis differs from empirical investigation, what it means for a philosophical disagreement to be resolved. Those are questions a tutor can raise in every session for two years, which is cheaper and more effective than a crash course in the final term.

The examination skill is reading an unfamiliar text accurately under time pressure and responding to its claims about philosophy rather than to its topic. Students who have practised this stop paraphrasing and start engaging: identifying the view of philosophical activity the text advances, assessing it, and bringing their own experience of the subject to bear. Three or four practice passages, properly marked, is usually enough to turn a feared component into a predictable one. The overlap with Theory of Knowledge is substantial, so the preparation serves two parts of the Diploma at once.
bullets: No content to revise, but method can be prepared across two years
Respond to the text's claims about philosophy, not to its subject matter
Thought experiments, intuitions and conceptual analysis are the recurring material

sections.heading: Reading philosophy in a UAE classroom
paragraphs: Philosophy in this emirate is taught to classes drawn from many traditions, and students frequently arrive with philosophical interests the prescribed-text list does not cover. The Arabic tradition is the clearest example: a student who has encountered al-Farabi or Ibn Sina will find that neither is likely to be the school's set text, and may conclude that their interest has no place in the course. That conclusion is wrong, and it is worth correcting early.

The examination components are fixed: Paper 2 is on the set text, and the optional themes are the ones the school teaches. But the Extended Essay is open, and it is the right home for a serious interest in a tradition outside the prescribed list, provided the question is argumentative rather than historical. The internal assessment is also open in its choice of stimulus, so a student can take a locally resonant stimulus and analyse it with the concepts the course supplies. Both routes let an interest do real academic work rather than sitting outside it.

The classroom point is about handling disagreement, which this subject requires. Philosophy of religion, political philosophy and ethics all involve positions students hold personally, and the course asks them to state and assess arguments on several sides. Our tutors present the arguments and the objections, and require the student to defend their own view against the strongest counterargument rather than adopting the tutor's. The Abrahamic Family House on Saadiyat Island, which opened in 2023, is a local institution that makes questions about pluralism concrete, and it can be used as case material in exactly that analytical spirit.
bullets: Paper 2 and the optional themes are fixed by the school; the Extended Essay is not
A tradition outside the prescribed list belongs in the Extended Essay or the stimulus choice
Essay questions must be argumentative rather than historical

sections.heading: What to ask before you pay, and what IB Gram is not
paragraphs: Four questions separate a useful Philosophy tutor from an articulate one. Which prescribed text have you taught, and how recently. Which optional themes can you cover. Will you give me written feedback naming the criteria. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The first two are subject questions, the third is about whether the work will be auditable, and the fourth is a legal one that applies to anybody tutoring privately in this country.

On that last point the facts are public. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, and that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, so there is no good reason for a working tutor to lack one.

Two further things a parent should know. In this emirate the schools regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, described by u.ae as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools; Gulf News has reported that its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tuition of their own enrolled students, which should be verified on adek.gov.ae. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, runs no office in the UAE, and sells no finished coursework: a tutor teaches, objects, and comments on drafts the student has written, and no part of a submitted analysis or essay comes from the tutor. Market rates for a Diploma specialist here, read from providers' published pages in October 2026, run roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour online.
bullets: Ask which prescribed text and which optional themes a tutor has actually taught
Ask for written, criterion-named feedback so the work is auditable
Ask about the MoHRE permit: free for two years, issued in about two working days

process.title: Send the text, the themes and the deadline
process.description: The first message that helps names the level, the prescribed text the school has set, which optional themes it teaches, whether the internal assessment stimulus has been chosen, and the next internal deadline. The prescribed text in particular determines who can actually teach the course your child is sitting.

process.title: Free first lesson built on one paragraph
process.description: One 50-minute online lesson in one subject at no charge, no card details taken. The tutor takes a paragraph of the student's own writing, numbers its premises, shows where a step is missing, and names the objection it needs to answer. That demonstration is usually enough for a family to judge whether the work will help.

process.title: A plan against components and word limits
process.description: The written plan names each session, the component it targets, and the rate in AED, with the Diploma's competing word ceilings laid out so the internal assessment, Theory of Knowledge essay and Extended Essay are not all left to the same fortnight. Nothing recurring starts before you agree it.

process.title: Weekly slot, held through the term
process.description: Sessions keep the same hour on Gulf Standard Time and move around mock weeks, examination periods and Ramadan timings rather than lapsing. Marked essays and annotated text passages are saved from the shared screen, so each session starts from the previous one rather than from scratch.

process.title: Review on marked essays, and say so if nothing moves
process.description: Every four to six weeks the tutor reviews marked work with you by component and band: whether premises are now explicit, whether objections are being answered, whether textual evidence is being cited. If the pattern is static after a fair run, we will recommend a change of tutor or format rather than continue.

whyPoints.title: The argument taught as a structure
whyPoints.description: Numbered premises, the strongest objection, then the reply. Most students can do this the first time it is demonstrated and cannot invent it alone, because nothing earlier in school required it. It is the fastest-moving work in the subject and it improves the Theory of Knowledge essay at the same time.

whyPoints.title: The prescribed text matched before matching a tutor
whyPoints.description: Paper 2 is the component where the wrong specialism is least recoverable. We ask which text the school has set before suggesting anybody, and we work from the student's own edition so that passage references match what they will have in the examination.

whyPoints.title: Stimulus choice treated as the decision it is
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment mark is largely determined before any writing happens, by whether the stimulus has philosophical traction. Half an hour testing a candidate stimulus against the course's concepts prevents the paper that describes a film for 800 words.

whyPoints.title: All three word ceilings planned together
whyPoints.description: A Philosophy student is writing to 2,000 words, 1,600 words and 4,000 words in overlapping terms. Treating those as one planning problem rather than three separate emergencies is the single most useful thing a tutor does for a DP2 student's calendar.

whyPoints.title: Positions presented, not supplied
whyPoints.description: In ethics, political philosophy and philosophy of religion the student defends their own view against the strongest counterargument. A tutor's job is to supply the objection and the precision, which is what the mark scheme rewards, rather than a conclusion the student then reproduces.

whyPoints.title: Facts with sources, and no borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: Permit rules come from u.ae and mohre.gov.ae, the ADEK ethics position is flagged as press-reported until verified, and no IB examination date is published here because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically. We claim no regulator or board approval and operate no UAE office.

faqs.question: Why did my child's first IB Philosophy essay score lower than expected?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is a prerequisite rather than an achievement in this subject. A well-written essay that states a position and defends it, without ever stating the position that opposes it, cannot reach the upper bands. The mark schemes reward the construction of an argument, precise use of philosophical concepts, and genuine engagement with a counterposition. The repair is structural and quick to demonstrate: write the argument as numbered premises, find the missing step, name the strongest objection, and answer it. Most students manage it the first time they see it done.

faqs.question: Which prescribed text will my child be examined on in Philosophy Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the school has set from the IB's prescribed list, which includes both Western and non-Western works. Texts commonly set include works by Plato, Descartes, Hume, Mill, Nietzsche, Sartre and de Beauvoir, among others. Find out before engaging any tutor, because this is the component where the wrong specialism is least recoverable: deep knowledge of one text does not transfer to another. Ask the department directly, and ask which edition they use, so that passage references match what your child will have in the examination room.

faqs.question: Why is reading a study guide not enough for the Philosophy text paper?
faqs.answer: Because the questions require passages to be used as evidence. A student who has read a summary knows the author's conclusions and cannot point to where the reasoning happens, so the answer describes a position rather than examining an argument. Examiners detect that immediately and the descriptors are written to catch it. The work that fixes it is reading the text in a proper edition, mapping each section as claim, support, anticipated objection and reply, and marking passages so they can be found quickly under time pressure.

faqs.question: What can be used as a stimulus for the Philosophy internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Anything that is not itself a philosophical text: a film, an advertisement, a photograph, a news item, a song, a piece of fiction. The assessment is of the philosophical analysis, not of the stimulus. What matters is traction. A good stimulus presupposes something the course's concepts can examine, such as an account of personal identity or free will or justice. A stimulus with no traction produces eight hundred words of description with philosophy bolted on. Test the candidate before writing; it is half an hour that saves a fortnight.

faqs.question: How long is the Philosophy internal assessment and what else competes with it?
faqs.answer: It runs to a 2,000-word ceiling. The complication is that a Diploma student is also writing a Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words and, if they choose Philosophy for it, an Extended Essay to 4,000 words, often across the same two terms. Treating those as three separate emergencies is the usual planning failure. Mapped together at the start of DP2, with the internal assessment stimulus chosen early, the load is manageable. Confirm the current limits with your child's teacher, since the IB revises subject guides periodically.

faqs.question: What does the Higher Level Philosophy paper on philosophical activity involve?
faqs.answer: An unseen text about what philosophy is and how it proceeds, answered analytically. There is no syllabus content to revise, which is why students postpone it, but it can be prepared. The material is method: why philosophers use thought experiments, what an appeal to intuition does, how conceptual analysis differs from empirical enquiry, what resolving a philosophical disagreement would look like. Three or four marked practice passages usually convert it from a feared component into a predictable one, and the preparation overlaps heavily with Theory of Knowledge.

faqs.question: Can a student write about Islamic philosophy in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not in Paper 2, where the text is fixed by the school from the IB's list, but yes elsewhere. The Extended Essay is open, and a serious interest in al-Farabi, Ibn Sina or the wider Arabic tradition belongs there, provided the question is argumentative rather than historical: whether a position can be sustained, not what a thinker believed and when. The internal assessment stimulus is also open, so a locally resonant stimulus can be analysed with the course's concepts. Both routes let the interest do real academic work.

faqs.question: Does a balanced Philosophy essay that considers both sides score well?
faqs.answer: Only if it reaches a conclusion. Balance is not the criterion; argument is. An essay that presents a view, presents the opposite, and decides that both have merit sits in the middle bands however elegantly it is written. The upper bands want a judgement reached by weighing the objections, which may be modest and provisional but has to be a judgement. Students find this counterintuitive because even-handedness is rewarded elsewhere in school, so it usually takes two or three marked essays before the habit changes.

faqs.question: How should a student handle the Paper 1 unseen stimulus?
faqs.answer: In about ninety seconds. Read it, identify two philosophical issues it raises, choose the one you can argue best, state it as a question, connect it to the stimulus in a single sentence, and then leave the stimulus alone. The marks are for the argument, not for the reading, so time spent explaining what the image or passage shows is unrewarded. The instinct under examination pressure is to describe what is in front of you, which is why this sequence has to be drilled rather than merely understood.

faqs.question: Is Philosophy offered in many Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: Relatively few, and where it runs the classes are often very small, sometimes three students, occasionally taught by someone whose main subject is another. That creates a calibration problem rather than a teaching one: a tiny class generates almost no marked exemplars, so a student has little sense of where their work sits against the bands. External marked feedback is the cheapest correction. Ask the individuals and societies department whether Philosophy runs this year, which optional themes it covers and which text it sets.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Philosophy tutor to a home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The shared screen suits this subject particularly well: a passage from the prescribed text sits beside the student's own paragraph, and the tutor marks the point where the argument stops following from the text. That annotated pair is saved, so the next session continues rather than restarts.

faqs.question: What may a Philosophy tutor do with an internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the analysis, challenge the stimulus choice, press on a definition, name the objection the argument has to answer, and comment on drafts the student has written, naming the criterion and the marks at stake. What a tutor may not do is author any part of the submitted text, supply sentences to insert, or hand over finished work. Providers selling completed coursework are selling a malpractice risk that lands on the candidate. Our tutors state that boundary to the student in the first session rather than in small print.

faqs.question: Does a Philosophy tutor in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published anywhere we could verify. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, so asking is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: How many Philosophy sessions does a DP2 student usually book?
faqs.answer: A common shape is four or five sessions on the prescribed text, weekly argument-building work through the mock period, and internal assessment supervision timed to the school's deadline. Higher Level students add three or four marked practice passages for the unseen paper. We prefer a fixed block with a stated end point to an open weekly arrangement, and if marked essays stop moving after a fair run the honest recommendation may be a different tutor or a different format.

faqs.question: Will a tutor tell my child what to think about ethics or religion?
faqs.answer: No, and an examiner would penalise the result if they did. The course requires students to state and assess arguments on several sides, so the mark depends on the student defending their own position against the strongest counterargument. Our tutors supply the objection and the conceptual precision, not the conclusion. In practice that means a session often ends with the student holding the view they started with, but holding it for better reasons and able to say what would count against it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.closingHeading: Send one paragraph and the name of the set text
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-philosophy-tutor.closingBody: Two pieces of information make the first conversation useful: one paragraph of your child's own philosophical writing, and the name of the prescribed text their school has set. The paragraph shows whether the loss is in argument structure, conceptual precision or counterposition. The text determines who can actually teach the paper they will sit. That is what the free 50-minute online lesson is built on, in one subject, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. Lessons run online from any community in the emirate, held on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-hl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Physics at Higher Level: the rigid body mechanics and relativity that exist only at this level, the field and induction work in Theme D, the data and uncertainty questions in Paper 1B, and the four criteria that carry the twenty-four investigation marks.

intro.heading: Where Higher Level Physics actually gets hard, and when
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics has a predictable shape to its difficulty, and Abu Dhabi families tend to meet it on the same two dates. The first is a few months into DP1, when the course moves from mechanics that behaves like applied mathematics into Theme D, where fields are invisible, sign conventions matter, and a student who has been coping by pattern-matching equations suddenly cannot. The second is in DP2, when the scientific investigation draft returns and the marks are missing from evaluation and conclusion rather than from the physics.

Neither of those is a knowledge problem in the usual sense. The Theme D wall is almost always a representation problem: the student cannot picture what a field is doing, so every question becomes a search for a formula with the right letters in it. That approach works through Theme A and collapses the moment a question asks what happens to the force when the separation doubles and the charge triples. The investigation problem is a different thing again: it is a writing and reasoning task marked against four named criteria, and physics ability alone does not score it.

The course itself is large. Higher Level Physics runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, with around sixty of the Higher Level hours given to the experimental programme. The extra ninety hours are partly whole subtopics that Standard Level never sees, including rigid body mechanics, Galilean and special relativity, thermodynamics, induction and quantum physics, and partly Higher Level extensions sitting inside shared subtopics such as simple harmonic motion, gravitational and electric fields, and radioactive decay. A Higher Level student in trouble is usually in trouble inside that extra material.

On delivery, the honest statement comes first. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For Higher Level Physics this constraint is close to irrelevant, because the scarce resource is not proximity but subject depth. Higher Level Physics specialists are thin on the ground in any single city, and thinner again among those willing to drive to Al Shamkha on a Tuesday evening. Online, your child is matched from everyone who teaches the course.

What follows is the course as it is examined. The five themes with the Higher Level subtopics named rather than gestured at. The current assessment model, including the split between the multiple-choice Paper 1A and the data-based Paper 1B, which catches out students who prepare for one and not the other. The four recurring ways Higher Level candidates lose marks. The mathematics the physics course assumes but does not teach, and which Diploma mathematics route makes that easier. The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, with its mark allocations and word limit. How practical work is handled when tutoring is remote, which is a fair question and deserves a straight answer. And what ADEK's role is, and is not, in which sciences your child's school offers.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Physics sits at the end of a sequence, and what came before it predicts a great deal. These are the programmes behind an Abu Dhabi Physics enquiry and what each one leaves a student with.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level Physics is 240 hours including an experimental programme, assessed by two examination papers and an internally assessed scientific investigation worth 20 per cent and marked out of 24. The written papers carry the other 80 per cent between them.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level Physics sets in Abu Dhabi are frequently small, because the subject competes with Chemistry and Biology for the same science block. A set of four or five is common at schools on the island and in the Khalifa City corridor, and a small set cannot pause on Theme D for one student. That is the single most common reason a Higher Level Physics family reaches this page.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a 1-8 scale. MYP sciences are marked on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and the impact of science, which maps almost directly onto the Diploma investigation criteria two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students arriving in DP1 Physics from MYP already know what criterion-referenced marking feels like, and their investigation scores generally show it. Students transferring in from a British Year 11 or a CBSE Class 10 have usually never designed an investigation of their own, and that gap, rather than the physics, is what costs them in the first year.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A student taking Physics within this programme sits the same papers and submits the same scientific investigation, so the assessment detail on this page applies in full.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this route appears mainly in conversations about load. A student holding Higher Level Physics together and sinking in three other Higher Levels has a timetable problem rather than a physics problem, and the first conversation belongs with the Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Physics rarely stands alone on an Abu Dhabi timetable. These are the subjects most often taken with it, described by the specific overlap that matters when support is being planned.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes over 240 hours with an experimental programme, examined by a split Paper 1 and an extended-response Paper 2 plus a 24-mark investigation. Marks leak on units and significant figures, on algebra attempted before a principle is stated, and on evaluation sections that list problems without quantifying their effect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same five themes over 150 hours, without rigid body mechanics, relativity, thermodynamics, induction or quantum physics, and with shorter papers. A student stepping down from Higher Level keeps the investigation and loses most of Theme D's hardest material.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that most directly supports Higher Level Physics, because it teaches the calculus and algebraic fluency the physics course assumes. Students taking this combination often find that one weakness in differentiation shows up as two sinking grades.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Entirely workable alongside Higher Level Physics, with one caveat: the calculus is numerical rather than analytic, so a student may need the derivative and integral forms used in simple harmonic motion and decay taught explicitly rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the data-analysis and uncertainty demands of the sciences model, and the same investigation criteria. A student who has learned to quantify uncertainty properly for one subject should not be relearning it for the other, yet frequently is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also marked out of 24 on the same four criteria, with the same 3,000-word ceiling on the investigation. Where a student takes two sciences, the investigation work should be planned together so the two internal deadlines do not land in the same fortnight.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares the habits of modelling and systematic debugging that Theme D rewards. Students taking both often respond well to having physics problems framed as systems with inputs and constraints rather than as formula searches.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Mechanics, materials and energy transfer reappear in applied form, and the iterative design process is close kin to the investigation's research-design criterion. The useful transfer is in planning a fair test, which is the first six marks of the investigation.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation chosen by a minority of Higher Level Physics students. It is a separate task from the scientific investigation, with its own supervisor and criteria, and the usual failure is a research question that cannot be answered with the equipment available.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Higher Level Physics students have strong material here: what a measurement with an uncertainty actually claims, how a model relates to the world, and when a theory is replaced rather than corrected. A tutor can supply examples; the essay must be the student's own.

sections.heading: What a Physics home tutor search in Abu Dhabi is really asking
paragraphs: In this market, a home tutor for Higher Level Physics means a specialist who travels to your district and teaches at your table. Published UAE rates for in-home one-to-one work run roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's Dubai rate table, reaching about AED 500 in specialist home-tutor listings, with IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists quoted at AED 200 to 450 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are the market's own figures, not ours. The travel sits inside the hour whether or not anyone itemises it.

IB Gram works differently and the page should say so plainly. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell; that service exists only in India. Higher Level Physics lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week and work marked between sessions. The case for it is specific to this subject: a Higher Level Physics specialist is a scarce person in any one city, and scarcity, not distance, is what determines whether your child gets taught induction properly.

There is a second reason the format suits this subject. Physics teaching leans heavily on diagrams, graphs and worked algebra built up line by line, and a shared screen with annotation is a genuinely good medium for that, arguably better than a notebook between two people at a kitchen table. Field lines drawn, erased and redrawn while a student watches is how the Theme D representation problem gets solved, and it does not require anyone to be in the room.

The table answers the five questions Abu Dhabi parents ask first about this course, with the place to verify each answer. Verification matters more in physics than almost anywhere else on these pages, because the sciences assessment model changed with the current guide and a good deal of material online still describes the previous one. Your child's school holds the current subject guide, and that is the document to check anything on this page against.

sections.heading: The five themes, and the Higher Level material named
paragraphs: The current Physics course is organised into five themes rather than the older topic list, and knowing their letters is genuinely useful when reading a school report or a scheme of work. Theme A covers space, time and motion. Theme B covers the particulate nature of matter. Theme C covers wave behaviour. Theme D covers fields. Theme E covers nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level students take all five, with additional subtopics and additional depth inside shared ones.

Some Higher Level material is a whole subtopic that Standard Level never meets. Rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity sit in Theme A. Thermodynamics sits in Theme B. Induction sits in Theme D. Quantum physics sits in Theme E. These are not harder versions of something a Standard Level student has seen; they are new, and a student who has fallen behind in them has a teaching problem rather than a revision problem.

The rest of the Higher Level load is extension inside shared subtopics, and this is the part families find hardest to see. Simple harmonic motion acquires its calculus treatment. Gravitational and electric fields acquire potential, potential energy and escape considerations. Radioactive decay acquires its exponential law in a form that requires logarithms. A student can therefore be fluent in the Standard Level version of a subtopic and lost in the Higher Level version of the same one, which is why a report that names only the subtopic is not enough information to plan from.

The table lists the themes with their subtopics and identifies which parts belong only to Higher Level. Treat it as a map for conversations with the school rather than as a syllabus: confirm everything against the current subject guide, which the school holds and which the IB revises periodically. What is stable is the structure, and the structure is what makes the diagnosis possible.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: what each one rewards
paragraphs: The current sciences assessment model splits the first paper into two parts, and this catches out students who prepare as though it were a single thing. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the syllabus, with more questions at Higher Level than at Standard Level. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental: graphs to read, gradients to interpret, uncertainties to handle, and experimental designs to criticise. The two halves reward almost opposite habits, and a student can be strong in one and weak in the other without anybody noticing until the mock.

Paper 1A rewards breadth and speed. Every subtopic is fair game, there is no credit for partial reasoning, and a candidate who is slow on routine manipulation runs out of time rather than out of knowledge. Preparation is therefore wide and shallow by design: large numbers of short questions across the whole of Themes A to E, with the aim of making the standard forms automatic.

Paper 1B rewards exactly the skills the investigation also needs, which is why a block of work here pays twice. Reading a gradient as a physical quantity with units. Choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes linear. Propagating an uncertainty rather than quoting one. Saying what a dataset does and does not support. Abu Dhabi students who have practised only textbook questions with clean numbers are regularly surprised by how different this feels, and it is the most improvable component in the course.

Paper 2 is the extended-response paper and carries the largest single weighting. It rewards a stated principle before any algebra: conservation of energy here, Newton's second law there, flux linkage changing in this interval. Candidates who begin by hunting for an equation lose marks even when they arrive somewhere reasonable, because the mark scheme awards the physics reasoning. Teaching a student to write one line of principle before touching the algebra is among the highest-value hours available in Higher Level Physics.

sections.heading: Four recurring ways Higher Level candidates lose marks
paragraphs: The first is units and significant figures, and it is far more expensive than students believe. A physics answer without units is an incomplete answer, and a value quoted to eight digits from a calculator display tells an examiner that the student has not thought about precision. These losses are one mark at a time, spread across a paper, which makes them invisible in conversation and obvious on a marked script. They are also the fastest thing in the subject to repair.

The second is algebra before principle. Asked why a satellite in a lower orbit moves faster, a well-prepared candidate writes a line naming the relationship between gravitational force and centripetal requirement and then manipulates it. A pattern-matcher writes an equation containing the right letters and hopes. The mark scheme rewards the reasoning, so the second candidate loses marks on questions they could have answered, and loses them worst in the extended-response paper where the weighting is highest.

The third is uncertainty treated as decoration. In Paper 1B and in the investigation, uncertainty is the point rather than an afterthought: whether a difference between two results is meaningful depends entirely on it. Students who append plus-or-minus values at the end without propagating them cannot answer the question being asked, and in the investigation this costs across the data analysis and evaluation criteria simultaneously.

The fourth is Theme D as pattern matching, which is less a mark-loss pattern than a structural failure. If a student cannot picture a field, then every field question becomes a search, and the search gets harder as the questions get less standard. The repair is not more practice on the same questions; it is time spent on representation, drawing and redrawing field patterns and predicting qualitatively what happens before any number is used. That is two or three deliberate sessions, and it changes the rest of the course.

sections.heading: The mathematics Physics assumes but does not teach
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics assumes a level of mathematical fluency that the physics course itself does not deliver. Rearranging multi-variable expressions quickly and correctly. Using logarithms to handle exponential decay and to linearise data. Handling small-angle approximations in oscillation work. Reading a gradient as a rate and an area as an accumulated quantity. Where a student is losing physics marks, a surprisingly large share of the losses are mathematical, and attacking them in the physics session is often the wrong place to start.

Which Diploma mathematics route a student takes changes how much of this needs explicit teaching. Analysis and Approaches develops the calculus and algebraic manipulation that Higher Level Physics leans on, so students on that route usually arrive with the tools even when they are shaky on applying them. Applications and Interpretation is entirely workable alongside Higher Level Physics, with one real caveat: its calculus is numerical rather than analytic, so the derivative and integral forms used in simple harmonic motion and radioactive decay generally need teaching rather than assuming.

This is the single most common misdiagnosis in Abu Dhabi Higher Level Physics enquiries. A family buys physics support because the physics grade fell, when the actual cause is that the student cannot rearrange confidently under time pressure, and the physics hour is spent doing algebra slowly. A tutor who identifies that should say so, and the efficient plan is often a short block of mathematics technique followed by physics, rather than six months of physics sessions containing hidden maths lessons.

The reverse case exists too and is worth naming. A student strong in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level can glide through the mathematics of physics and still misunderstand the physics entirely, producing clean derivations that answer a different question from the one asked. That student does not need more mathematics; they need to be made to explain in words what a result means before they are allowed to write any symbols.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation carries 20 per cent of the Higher Level Physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. There is a 3,000-word limit. Two features of that structure matter enormously and are routinely missed. The marks are evenly spread, so a brilliant experiment with a weak evaluation scores no better than a modest experiment evaluated well. And half the marks sit in the two sections students write last, in a hurry.

Research design is where the grade is largely decided, because everything downstream depends on it. A clearly identified research question with a defined independent variable, dependent variable and controlled variables, a method that can actually produce enough data of sufficient range, and a stated reason for the choices. Students who begin collecting data before this is settled generally end up with a dataset that cannot answer their question, and no amount of later analysis recovers the marks.

Data analysis and conclusion are where the Paper 1B skills return. Processing raw data correctly, propagating uncertainties, choosing what to plot so the relationship can be tested, and then stating a conclusion that is justified by the data and related to the accepted physics with its source identified. Evaluation is the section students most often fill with generic statements about human error. What it asks for is specific, quantified weaknesses and realistic improvements that would address them, which is a different and more demanding thing.

The boundary for tutoring is firm and it protects the student. A tutor explains what each criterion asks, teaches the physics and the analysis techniques the student needs, reads a draft and identifies where the marks are being lost, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. No part of the submitted document originates with a tutor, and nothing is rewritten into final form by one. Keep the dated feedback: schools increasingly ask about the provenance of internally assessed work, and a written trail showing the student's own revisions is the clearest answer available.

sections.heading: Practical work when the tutoring is remote
paragraphs: This is a fair question and deserves a direct answer rather than a deflection. The experimental programme belongs to the school. Around sixty hours of practical work at Higher Level, including the collaborative sciences project, is delivered in the school laboratory under the school's supervision, and a tutor neither replaces nor supplements that. Anyone offering to provide practical hours for a Diploma science course is offering something they cannot legitimately deliver.

What a remote tutor can do is the part of practical work that is not standing at a bench. Designing a fair test and anticipating what will go wrong with it. Deciding how many data points at what spacing will actually let a relationship be seen. Processing a dataset the student has collected in school, including propagating uncertainties correctly. Choosing what to plot. Interpreting a gradient as a physical quantity with units. Criticising a method specifically enough to earn evaluation marks. Those are the skills Paper 1B examines and the investigation is marked on, and none of them require a laboratory.

In practice this works well because the division is clean. The student collects data in school, brings it to the session as a spreadsheet or a photograph of a results table, and the hour is spent on analysis, uncertainty and the written argument. Several Abu Dhabi families find that this produces better investigation marks than an in-home arrangement would, because an in-home tutor also cannot access the school laboratory and the time is therefore spent the same way, minus the drive.

One thing to be careful about. Do not pay anyone for copies of past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or subject guides, and do not accept them as a bonus. Those documents belong to the IB, and the legitimate route is for the school to provide them and for a tutor to reference and link the official source. A provider distributing board material as downloads is telling you something about how they operate.

sections.heading: Physics HL, engineering and medicine: what to verify and where
paragraphs: A large share of Higher Level Physics enquiries in Abu Dhabi are really about a university application, and the physics grade is being treated as the gatekeeper. The honest position is that Higher Level Physics is named by many engineering and physical sciences programmes and is a common requirement for them, that medicine requirements vary widely and frequently specify Chemistry and Biology rather than Physics, and that the only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific programme for the specific intake year.

That caveat is not evasion. Entry requirements differ between faculties inside one university, between campuses of the same institution, and between intake years. Several competitor pages in this market carry lists of which universities require what, and a list like that is stale within a year. Ask the school's university counsellor to confirm in writing what each target programme requires, because that is their role and they hold current information, and then plan the Diploma around the written answer rather than around a page on the internet.

For UAE equivalency, only what is sourced should be stated. On the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency requires an IELTS academic score of 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

No IB points threshold for equivalency appears on this page, because we have not read one on the Ministry of Education's own site, and an unsourced figure repeated across many pages is simply a large number of errors. Read the current position on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is also a process the family completes, not something a tutor performs, accelerates or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: ADEK, small science sets and the conversation to have at school
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is where a rating should be read. What ADEK does not determine is which sciences an individual school offers at which level; that is a staffing and timetabling decision taken by the school itself.

The consequence for Physics is set size. Physics competes with Chemistry and Biology for the same science block, and in a small Diploma cohort that often produces a Higher Level Physics set of four or five students. Small sets have real advantages in attention and real disadvantages in pace: the teacher cannot spend three weeks on Theme D fields for one student without leaving Theme E underdone for everyone. Where a student is one of two or three taking the subject, parts of the course may effectively be covered independently.

The questions worth asking the school are therefore specific. Will Higher Level Physics run next year and with how many students. Which themes are scheduled for which term, and when the experimental programme hours fall. When the internal deadlines for the investigation are, including the draft the school will comment on. What a predicted grade will be based on. Those get precise answers, and they shape a support plan more than any general conversation about progress does.

On who may legally tutor, the position is checkable. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Separately, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules says school staff may not take paid private tutoring of students at their own school; verify that on ADEK's own policy page. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none.

process.title: Say the theme and the component, not just the subject
process.description: 'Physics HL, Theme D fields collapsed and Paper 1B came back at 11 out of 25' is the sentence that matters. Physics at Higher Level is not one problem, and the difference between a Theme D representation gap and a Paper 1B uncertainty gap decides which specialist and which plan.

process.description: Where Theme D is the problem, the first sessions are spent on picturing fields and predicting behaviour qualitatively rather than on more questions.
