faqs.question: Is in-home Higher Level Physics tuition available in Abu Dhabi, and what does the market charge for it?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not send a tutor to any UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not a service we sell; that exists only in India. For context on the local market, published UAE rates put in-home one-to-one work at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, reaching about AED 500 at the specialist end, with IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are the market's figures. Our lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which also means no part of the hour is a drive.

faqs.question: Which parts of the Physics course exist only at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Several whole subtopics plus extensions inside shared ones. The whole subtopics are rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, induction in Theme D, and quantum physics in Theme E. The extensions sit inside simple harmonic motion and wave phenomena in Theme C, the gravitational and electric field subtopics in Theme D, and the radioactive decay law in Theme E, where the treatment becomes calculus and logarithm based. Confirm the current lists against your child's own copy of the subject guide, which the school holds.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 1A and Paper 1B, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal, because they reward opposite habits. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole syllabus and rewards breadth and speed with no credit for partial reasoning. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental: reading graphs, interpreting gradients as physical quantities, propagating uncertainties and criticising experimental designs. A student can be strong in one and weak in the other for a year without anyone noticing, because a combined mark hides it. Ask for the two sections to be marked and reported separately, and plan the preparation separately too.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the physics but keeps losing marks on units and significant figures. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Quickly, and it is usually worth more than it sounds. Those losses come one mark at a time across a whole paper, so they are invisible in conversation and obvious on a marked script, and a candidate can lose the better part of a grade to them. The remedy is mechanical: every answer carries a unit, every value is quoted to a justified number of figures, and marked work is returned with those specific losses circled rather than silently corrected. Three or four marked papers normally changes the habit permanently.

faqs.question: Why does my son suddenly find Theme D impossible when the rest of the course was fine?
faqs.answer: Because Theme D is where equation-matching stops working. A student who has been coping by finding a formula with the right letters in it can get through kinematics and energy, but fields are invisible and the questions ask what happens when two quantities change together. The repair is representation rather than practice: drawing and redrawing field patterns, predicting qualitatively what happens before any number is used, and only then returning to calculation. That is typically two or three deliberate sessions, and it changes how the rest of the course lands.

faqs.question: How is the scientific investigation marked, and how long is it allowed to be?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, within a 3,000-word limit, and it carries 20 per cent of the grade. The even split matters: a strong experiment evaluated weakly scores no better than a modest experiment evaluated well. Half the marks sit in the conclusion and evaluation sections, which students write last and fastest. Treat the word limit as a design constraint from the start, because reports that overrun on method end up cutting the analysis that carries marks.

faqs.question: If lessons are online, how does practical work get covered?
faqs.answer: It does not, and no honest tutor claims otherwise. The experimental programme is the school's responsibility, around sixty hours at Higher Level including the collaborative sciences project, delivered in the school laboratory under school supervision. What a remote tutor covers is the part that is not standing at a bench: designing a fair test, deciding how many data points at what spacing, processing data the student collected in school, propagating uncertainties, choosing what to plot, and criticising a method specifically enough to earn evaluation marks. Those are the examined skills.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Physics require Analysis and Approaches, or will Applications do?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation works perfectly well alongside it, with one real caveat. Higher Level Physics assumes fluency in multi-variable rearrangement, logarithms for decay and linearisation, and reading gradients and areas as physical quantities. Analysis and Approaches develops the analytic calculus the physics course leans on, so those students usually arrive with the tools. Applications teaches calculus numerically, so the derivative and integral forms used in simple harmonic motion and radioactive decay generally need teaching explicitly rather than assuming. That is a known, bounded piece of work rather than an obstacle.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Higher Level Physics student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of three problems is present, and they have very different timescales. A units, figures and presentation habit changes across three or four marked papers. A representation gap in Theme D is two or three deliberate sessions followed by practice. A whole Higher Level subtopic that was covered at speed, such as induction or thermodynamics, needs teaching and then retesting a fortnight later, so four to six sessions. A student who is behind across two themes and has an unwritten investigation is a term's work, and the first lesson will say so rather than sell a block.

faqs.question: What is the collaborative sciences project and does it carry marks?
faqs.answer: It is part of the experimental programme rather than a separately assessed component: a collaborative piece of work, typically around ten hours, in which students from different sciences address a common problem. It is not marked out of a total that appears in the grade the way the investigation is, but it is a required part of the course and it is the school's to run. Where a student has missed it through transferring schools mid-course, that is a matter for the Diploma coordinator, because only the school can resolve a shortfall in programme hours.

faqs.question: Our Abu Dhabi school has a Higher Level Physics set of four. Should we be concerned?
faqs.answer: It has genuine advantages and one specific risk. Four students get far more teacher attention than twenty-four, which is valuable in a subject built on explanation. The risk is pace: the teacher cannot spend three weeks on fields for one student without leaving Theme E underdone for the rest, so a student who stalls stays stalled. Ask which themes are scheduled for which term and when the experimental hours fall. If parts of the course are being covered semi-independently, that is exactly where one-to-one support earns its cost.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Physics matter for a medicine or engineering application from Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: For engineering and the physical sciences it is commonly required or strongly expected. For medicine the requirements vary widely and frequently specify Chemistry and Biology rather than Physics. The only reliable answer is the admissions page of the specific programme for the specific intake year, because requirements differ between faculties in one university and change between years. Ask the school's university counsellor to confirm each target programme in writing. Lists of university requirements on tutoring sites, including any we might publish, go stale within a year.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may explain what each criterion asks, teach the physics and the analysis techniques the student needs, read a draft and identify where marks are being lost, and set the next revision for the student to carry out. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a passage into final form, process the data for the student or contribute any part of the submitted report. Keep the dated feedback, because schools increasingly ask about the provenance of internally assessed work and a written trail of the student's own revisions answers that directly.

faqs.question: Who regulates Abu Dhabi schools, and does that decide which sciences are offered?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge licenses and inspects private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes its own inspection outcomes, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. It does not decide which sciences a school offers at which level; that is a staffing and timetabling decision made by the school. This is why two ADEK-inspected schools a few kilometres apart in Khalifa City can offer entirely different Higher Level science options.

faqs.question: There are eight weeks until the papers. What should the hours actually be spent on?
faqs.answer: On the components that respond fastest, in order. First, units, significant figures and the habit of stating a principle before any algebra, because those recover marks across every question in the extended-response paper. Second, Paper 1B data work, which is the most improvable component in the course and the most mechanical to train. Third, timed multiple-choice sets to fix pace. What eight weeks cannot do is deliver a theme that was never taught, and if the diagnosis finds that, the written note will say so instead of selling a block.

faqs.question: What does my child need for an online Higher Level Physics session to work properly?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A stable connection, a device with a reasonably sized screen rather than a phone, and something to write on that the tutor can see, which can be a graphics tablet, a second camera angle on paper, or photographs of work sent before the session. Headphones help in a busy household. The school's graphic display calculator and the student's own data table or marked script matter far more than any equipment: the hour is spent on diagrams, built-up algebra and marked work, and a shared annotated screen does that at least as well as a notebook between two people.

intro.heading: Why Physics HL is the subject Abu Dhabi families ask about most
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level is routinely the hardest subject on an Abu Dhabi Diploma student's timetable, and it is hard for reasons that have little to do with how clever the student is. The course runs 240 teaching hours across five themes, demands a mathematical fluency the mathematics course may not yet have delivered, and loads a significant share of its marks onto skills that are not physics at all: uncertainty handling, graph analysis, and writing an answer that matches a command term precisely.

The syllabus rebuild makes this worse before it makes it better. The current Physics guide replaced the old core-plus-options structure with five themes — space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics — each carrying its own Higher Level extensions. The options disappeared. The two separate internal assessments became one scientific investigation. A great deal of the revision material circulating in school WhatsApp groups and on second-hand shelves describes the previous course, and a student revising from it will spend hours on content that is no longer examined while missing content that is.

The assessment model is the other thing families frequently have wrong. Paper 1 carries 36% and is in two parts: Paper 1A is multiple choice, and Paper 1B is a set of data-based questions built on a single experimental scenario. Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper. The investigation carries the remaining 20%. The Paper 1B half is where many strong physicists quietly lose marks, because it tests processing and interpretation of data under time pressure rather than recall.

Abu Dhabi contributes a supply problem on top of all this. Physics HL groups in the emirate's Diploma cohorts are small — frequently under ten students — and a tutor who teaches the current guide at Higher Level, can mark an investigation against the right criteria, and is free at 5pm is a narrow intersection of requirements. Searching for that person within driving distance of Al Raha gives a family almost no choice. Searching across every time zone that teaches the Diploma gives them a real one.

Which is the argument for the delivery model, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE. Tutors travelling to a family's address is available only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing of the student's own graphs and scripts, a shared whiteboard for working, and a recording to replay. For a subject whose hardest marks involve reading a graph together on a screen, that is a reasonable medium rather than a compromise.

What follows is the detail a parent can use: the five themes and what sits inside the Higher Level extensions, how the two papers behave differently, where the uncertainty and significant-figure marks go, the four criteria of the scientific investigation with their mark allocations, how practical skills are handled when teaching is remote, the interaction between Physics HL and the mathematics route, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: A Physics HL request from Abu Dhabi comes from a Diploma family, but the diagnosis usually reaches back a year or two. What a student brings from middle years or IGCSE science determines how much of the first term is spent building rather than extending.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups plus the three core elements. Physics sits in Group 4, the sciences, and at Higher Level runs for 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the internally assessed scientific investigation at 20%, with a data booklet supplied in the examinations.
programmes.countryNote: Physics HL sets in Abu Dhabi schools are typically among the smallest in a Diploma cohort, which means strong teaching but very little individual time. The Higher Level extensions, which arrive late in DP1, are where small-cohort pace causes the most damage and where outside support is most often requested.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences taught as an integrated subject group, assessed against four criteria including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating. Those two criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation, so a student who took MYP sciences seriously arrives with real experimental-design instinct even if the content overlap is modest.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB World Schools run the continuum, so a Physics HL student may have five years of MYP science criterion reports available in the parent portal. Those reports are the fastest way to predict whether the trouble in DP1 will be the mathematics or the experimental writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson International GCSE 4PH1 are the routes most Abu Dhabi students arrive from. Both cover mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and basic nuclear physics at a level the Diploma then deepens considerably. Neither requires formal uncertainty propagation or the kind of extended explanation Paper 2 expects.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Physics-HL step is steep in two specific places: the mathematics, which moves from substitution into rearrangement, trigonometry and gradient interpretation, and the writing, which moves from one-line answers to multi-step causal explanations. The first term of tutoring usually targets exactly those two things.

programmes.name: A Level and AS Physics
programmes.description: The alternative post-sixteen route in several Abu Dhabi schools. A Level Physics covers broadly similar content with a different assessment shape: more papers, separate practical endorsement, and no internally assessed investigation of the Diploma's kind. Students occasionally transfer between the two systems mid-course.
programmes.countryNote: A transfer from AS Physics into Physics HL partway through is survivable but needs honest accounting. The content maps reasonably well; what does not transfer is the investigation, the command-term conventions and the data-booklet habit, and those take a term of deliberate work to acquire.

subjects.name: Physics

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and calculus route, and the one most physics-adjacent degrees name in their entry requirements. AA gives a physics student the manipulation and calculus fluency that makes field and circuit work feel routine rather than effortful.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, taken with technology assumed throughout. A Physics HL student in AI SL can succeed but has to build algebraic rearrangement and trigonometry separately, because the mathematics course will not supply as much of it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across six themes with its own scientific investigation. The two sciences share the uncertainty, significant-figure and graph conventions, so one session on data analysis frequently repairs marks in both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four organising themes plus the investigation. Biology's statistical tests and error-bar conventions overlap with the physics data-analysis paper, and students taking both often reuse the same processing discipline in two internal assessments.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, computational thinking, programming and a solution for a real client. Physics students who also code tend to handle the modelling and iteration parts of an investigation comfortably, especially where a spreadsheet does the processing.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle, materials, production and a major design project. It shares the physics habit of justifying a choice against evidence, and the project rewards the same careful documentation that the investigation does.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and development, with internal commentaries. A common pairing for Abu Dhabi students heading towards engineering management, and it competes with physics for the same DP2 weeks.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece. A physics essay needs a question that can actually be investigated with available equipment or published data; supervision means process coaching and feedback on the student's own research, never supplying text.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Physics gives a student unusually good TOK material: the status of models, the role of measurement and uncertainty, and what it means for a theory to be superseded rather than disproved.

sections.heading: The five themes, and why older revision material misleads
paragraphs: The current Physics guide organises the subject into five themes rather than a core plus optional units. Theme A covers space, time and motion. Theme B covers the particulate nature of matter. Theme C covers wave behaviour. Theme D covers fields. Theme E covers nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level extensions sit inside each theme rather than in a separate section, and the optional units that used to let a cohort choose astrophysics or engineering physics are gone.

Running alongside the themes are the tools and the inquiry process, which the guide treats as taught content rather than as background. The tools cover experimental technique, the use of technology, and the mathematics a physicist is expected to deploy. The inquiry process covers exploring and designing, collecting and processing data, and concluding and evaluating. Those are the headings the internal assessment is built on, which is why a school that teaches them explicitly produces better investigations than one that treats them as common sense.

For a parent the practical consequence is about materials. A great deal of physics revision content in circulation describes the previous syllabus, including option topics that are no longer examined and an internal assessment structure that no longer exists. A student working through an old guide will spend evenings on material that cannot appear and will miss Higher Level extensions that will. The first thing worth checking is the edition of whatever the student is revising from.

A tutor's first job on this page is therefore diagnostic in an unusual sense: not only which physics the student has not learned, but which physics the student has learned that is no longer on the course, and which current content has been skipped because the available resources did not mention it. That check takes one session and it saves a term.

sections.heading: How the two papers behave differently
paragraphs: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and comes in two halves that test different things. Paper 1A is multiple choice: no marks for working, no partial credit, and a strict reward for precision in reading the question. Paper 1B is a set of data-based questions built around one experimental scenario, where candidates process supplied measurements, handle uncertainties, plot or interpret a graph, and draw a conclusion. Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper, where multi-step explanation and sustained calculation live.

The split matters because the two halves of Paper 1 reward opposite habits. In Paper 1A, time spent writing full working is time lost; the skill is eliminating options quickly and recognising the physics being tested. In Paper 1B, the same student has to slow down, record intermediate values, and show processing. Students trained on only one of these approaches lose marks in the other, and the fix is simply to practise them as separate exercises rather than as one paper.

Paper 2 losses are dominated by incomplete explanation. A question asking a candidate to explain why a result occurs wants a causal chain, and the mark scheme awards the links. A student who writes the first and last step of a three-step chain has the physics right and collects one mark of three. Command terms are the published signal for how much is wanted: 'state' wants a sentence, 'outline' wants a brief account, 'explain' wants reasons, 'discuss' wants a balanced consideration, 'deduce' wants a conclusion reached from given information.

Higher Level timings are longer than Standard Level in both papers, and the exact durations for a given session should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator. The table below sets out the components, their weights and the dominant failure mode in each, which is the part that actually guides a revision plan.

sections.heading: The Higher Level extensions: what Standard Level students never meet
paragraphs: The gap between Physics SL and Physics HL is ninety teaching hours and a set of named extensions distributed through the five themes. Those extensions are not harder versions of Standard Level content; several of them are entirely new physics, and they tend to arrive late in DP1 when a cohort is also managing the investigation and the first mock examinations. That timing is the single commonest reason an Abu Dhabi family asks for Higher Level physics help in the autumn of DP2.

Within Theme A, Higher Level candidates meet rigid body mechanics, which introduces torque, moment of inertia and angular momentum, and Galilean and special relativity, which introduces time dilation, length contraction and the invariance of the speed of light. Neither appears at Standard Level. Rigid body mechanics in particular rewards a student who is fluent with vector components and punishes one who is not, which is where the mathematics route starts to matter.

In Theme D, the Higher Level work extends gravitational and electric fields into potential, potential energy, escape speed and orbital energy, and extends motion in electromagnetic fields. Theme D also carries induction as Higher Level content, which brings flux, Faraday's law and Lenz's law. Theme C extends into the Doppler effect. Theme E carries quantum physics at Higher Level, including the photoelectric effect treated quantitatively, the de Broglie relationship and the Bohr model's limitations.

Students should confirm the exact sub-topic list and its Higher Level markings against the current subject guide through their school, because the guide is the authoritative document and this page is a summary of it. What does not change is the pattern of difficulty: the extensions that depend on vector mathematics and on potential as a scalar field cause more trouble than the extensions that depend on new vocabulary, and the two need different teaching.

sections.heading: Uncertainties and significant figures: the marks nobody revises
paragraphs: A consistent share of Physics HL marks sits in skills that look like administration and are examined as physics. Absolute uncertainty, percentage uncertainty, propagating uncertainty through a sum, product or power, drawing error bars, finding maximum and minimum gradient lines to obtain an uncertainty in a gradient, and giving a final answer to a number of significant figures justified by the raw data are all examinable. They appear in Paper 1B every session, they appear in Paper 2, and they are assessed again inside the investigation.

Almost no student revises them, because they do not feel like topics. There is no chapter called uncertainties to work through, no satisfying set of fifty questions, and no sense of achievement in getting one right. The result is a predictable pattern: a student who can derive a result from first principles and then writes it to five significant figures from data recorded to two, or who quotes an uncertainty with the same precision as the measurement rather than to one significant figure.

The graph skills are the other half, and they are worth more. Linearising a relationship so that a straight-line graph can be drawn — plotting against the reciprocal, the square, or the logarithm as the physics requires — converts a hard question into an easy one, and the examination asks for it regularly. Reading a gradient and interpreting what it represents physically, with units, is a separate skill again, and students routinely find the gradient correctly and then state what it means wrongly.

This is the content that responds fastest to tutoring, which is why a short block aimed at it is often the best value available in the subject. It is bounded, it is mechanical, it is assessed in every component, and it is the kind of thing a parent can see improve on a marked Paper 1B within a few weeks. A tutor who marks these conventions strictly for six sessions usually changes them permanently.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria
paragraphs: The current science courses replaced the older pair of internal assessments with one scientific investigation, worth 20% of the grade, allocated around ten hours of class time, limited to 3,000 words, and marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each. Those criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Equal weighting is the important structural fact: the conclusion and the evaluation together are worth as much as the design and the data handling.

Research design is where most marks are lost before a single measurement is taken. The criterion rewards a clearly stated research question with a defined independent and dependent variable, identified controlled variables, and a methodology detailed enough that someone else could repeat it. Investigations that begin with an interesting phenomenon and no measurable question lose these marks irretrievably, and no amount of good data recovers them later.

Data analysis rewards appropriate processing with uncertainties carried through, and presentation that a reader can interpret. Conclusion rewards an answer to the research question that is justified by the data and placed in the context of accepted physics, including comparison with an expected value where one exists. Evaluation rewards honest discussion of the strengths and weaknesses of the method, the sources of systematic and random error, and realistic improvements — not a list of generic apologies about human error.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and should be given to a family in writing. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is measurable and viable, point at a criterion and say which descriptor the current version meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation conventions, and ask the questions that make a student see a gap. A tutor may not supply text, supply data, or hand back a rewritten report. The student signs an authenticity declaration and the work must be theirs throughout.

sections.heading: Practical work when the tutoring is remote
paragraphs: A fair question from any physics parent: if lessons are online, what happens to the laboratory? The honest answer separates two things. The practical work itself belongs to the school. Students do their experiments in their school laboratory with their school's equipment and their school's teacher supervising, and that is where the investigation data comes from. A tutor does not replace a laboratory and should not pretend to.

What remote tutoring can do is everything around the bench, which is where most of the investigation marks actually sit. Designing the experiment before a student walks into the laboratory is a conversation, and it is the conversation that earns the research design marks. Deciding what to vary, what to control, how many repeats, what range, and how to measure the dependent variable with the equipment the school has is done on paper, not at an apparatus.

Processing is equally remote-friendly and is where screen sharing earns its place. A student opens the spreadsheet, the tutor watches the formulas rather than the final numbers, and the two of them fix the uncertainty propagation where it actually went wrong. Graphs are built together, error bars added, gradient uncertainty obtained from maximum and minimum lines, and the interpretation written while the data is in front of both people. That is a genuinely better medium for the task than sitting side by side with one laptop.

For the parts of the course where a student has not seen a demonstration — a cathode ray tube, a Geiger counter, interference fringes — simulations and recorded demonstrations are used as a supplement and labelled as such. They are not a substitute for having stood next to the equipment, and a tutor should say so rather than imply otherwise. Where a school's laboratory provision is thin, that is a conversation for the school, not a gap tutoring can fill.

sections.heading: The mathematics Physics HL assumes, and the AI SL problem
paragraphs: Physics HL assumes a level of mathematical fluency that the mathematics course may or may not deliver, and the mismatch is a real and common source of difficulty in Abu Dhabi cohorts. The subject needs confident algebraic rearrangement, trigonometry and the resolution of vectors, work with reciprocals, squares and inverse-square relationships, logarithms for exponential decay, small-angle approximations, and comfort reading a gradient as a rate of change.

A student taking Analysis and Approaches, at either level, generally arrives with that fluency or acquires it in parallel. A student taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level may not, because AI SL spends a large share of its hours on statistics and modelling and relatively few on algebraic manipulation. The combination of Physics HL with AI SL is entirely possible and is taken successfully every year, but it means the physics tutoring has to carry some of the mathematics, and a family should expect that rather than discover it in February.

The specific symptoms are recognisable. A student understands the physics of a question, sets up the correct relationship from the data booklet, and then cannot rearrange it for the quantity asked. Or resolves a force into components with the sine and cosine the wrong way round. Or handles an exponential decay by trial and error because logarithms have not become automatic. None of these is a physics failure, and all of them are diagnosed in one session by watching a student work rather than by asking what they find hard.

The remedy is to treat the mathematics as part of the physics plan rather than as somebody else's problem. Twenty minutes of rearrangement drill inside a physics session, repeated weekly for a term, generally removes the bottleneck. It is unglamorous, it is not what a family expects to pay a physics specialist for, and it is frequently the intervention that moves the grade.

sections.heading: What Physics HL tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, and who may legally tutor
paragraphs: Published rates are scarce in this market, so the figures below come from providers that publish their own prices and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are market rates from those named sources, not IB Gram's fee. Abu Dhabi tracks Dubai closely, with in-home visits sitting at the upper end because the emirate's distances are longer and an evening of house calls costs a tutor more driving.

Higher Level sciences sit at the specialist end of the market for a structural reason: the pool of tutors who teach the current Physics guide at Higher Level, can mark an investigation against the right criteria, and are free in a Gulf evening slot is small. Providers that publish a level split charge more for it. Timing moves the figure too, with the final term before the May session the point at which both price and availability tighten.

On the legal question, two bodies matter and they do different jobs. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes inspection ratings. Individual private tutors are covered federally: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years to applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time.

Two practical points follow. Anyone tutoring without that permit is, in u.ae's words, subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to a parent. And press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school — which makes the one tutor a family might think of first the one they usually cannot hire. IB Gram holds no ADEK, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and claims none.

process.title: Say Higher Level and name the themes that hurt

process.title: Send a marked paper and a graph
process.description: One marked assessment plus one piece of processed experimental data tells a tutor almost everything: whether the losses are content, mathematics, uncertainty handling or command terms. Those four have four different timelines and four different plans.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute session over live video with the proposed tutor, no card details and no obligation. It runs on a real question from the student's own work and ends with the tutor naming what the first month would target and why in that order.

process.title: Check the revision material's edition
process.description: A quick but high-value step. If the student is working from a guide written for the previous syllabus, the plan starts by replacing it, because evenings spent on deleted option topics are evenings that cost marks rather than earn them.

process.title: Review the record at week four and week twelve
process.description: Two scheduled checkpoints where a parent reads the mark log and the session notes. If the log has not moved on the themes being attacked and nobody can explain why, the right response is to change the plan or the tutor, not to extend on faith.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time around bus arrivals, exam terms and Ramadan timings, and they move when a family asks. A video lesson absorbs a Yas Island event weekend or a travel week without the arrangement breaking.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Physics HL tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market figures from providers that publish them give the honest range. Qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and IB specialists higher: Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits in that survey are AED 180 to 350, with independent tutors quoted to AED 500, because driving is priced inside the hour. Higher Level sciences sit at the specialist end because the pool teaching the current guide is small. IB Gram confirms its own fee in writing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What changed when the current IB Physics syllabus came in?
faqs.answer: Three structural things. The core-plus-options arrangement became five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics, each with its own Higher Level extensions. The optional units disappeared, so astrophysics and engineering physics are no longer separately examined. And the two older internal assessments became one scientific investigation, worth 20%, limited to 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four. Revision material written for the previous course is therefore actively misleading, and checking the edition of whatever a student is using is worth doing first.

faqs.question: How is Physics Paper 1 split between multiple choice and data analysis?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and has two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice, with no credit for working and a strict premium on reading the question precisely. Paper 1B is a set of data-based questions built on a single experimental scenario, where candidates process measurements, handle uncertainties, use a graph and reach a conclusion. The two halves reward opposite habits, which is why they are best practised separately: speed and elimination for 1A, careful recorded processing for 1B. Strong physicists lose more marks in 1B than they expect.

faqs.question: Which Physics topics do Higher Level students study that Standard Level students never see?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level extensions sit inside each theme and amount to ninety extra teaching hours. They include rigid body mechanics with torque, moment of inertia and angular momentum, and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A; the Doppler effect treated quantitatively in Theme C; gravitational and electric potential, orbital energy, escape speed and induction in Theme D; and quantum physics including the photoelectric effect and the de Broglie relationship in Theme E. Confirm the exact sub-topic list against the current subject guide through the school, because the guide is the authoritative source and this is a summary.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on uncertainties when his physics is right?
faqs.answer: Because uncertainty handling is examined as physics and revised by almost nobody. The assessable skills are absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through sums, products and powers, error bars, obtaining a gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines, quoting an uncertainty to one significant figure, and giving a final answer to a precision the raw data justifies. There is no satisfying chapter to work through, so students skip it. It appears in Paper 1B every session, in Paper 2 and again in the investigation, which makes a short block on it the best-value intervention in the subject.

faqs.question: How is the IB Physics scientific investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Out of twenty-four, across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report is limited to 3,000 words and the course allocates around ten hours to it. Equal weighting is the fact families most often miss — the conclusion and evaluation together carry as much as the design and the data handling. Research design is where marks are lost before any measurement happens, because a topic without a measurable research question and defined variables cannot score there however good the data turns out to be.

faqs.question: Can my daughter do practical physics work if her tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The practical work belongs to her school laboratory, with her school's equipment and supervision, and that is where investigation data comes from. What remote tutoring covers is everything around the bench, which is where most of the marks sit: designing the experiment before she walks in, choosing what to vary and control, deciding repeats and range, then processing the data afterwards with screen sharing so a tutor can watch the spreadsheet formulas rather than just the final numbers. Simulations supplement demonstrations she has not seen and are labelled as supplements, not replacements.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL workable alongside Maths Applications and Interpretation SL?
faqs.answer: Yes, and students do it every year, but the combination has a known cost. Physics HL assumes confident algebraic rearrangement, trigonometry and vector resolution, reciprocal and inverse-square relationships, and logarithms for exponential decay. AI SL spends most of its hours on statistics and modelling rather than on manipulation, so the physics tutoring usually has to carry some of the mathematics. The symptom is recognisable: the student sets up the right relationship from the data booklet and then cannot rearrange it. Twenty minutes of drill inside a weekly physics session generally clears it over a term.

faqs.question: What is the Collaborative Sciences Project and does it affect the grade?
faqs.answer: It is a required piece of interdisciplinary work in the current science courses, allocated around ten hours, in which students from different science subjects address a real-world problem together. It is not separately graded and does not contribute marks to the subject. Families sometimes assume it is assessed and worry about it accordingly; the reason it still matters is time, because those hours sit in a DP timetable that also has to fit the scientific investigation and mock examinations. Treat it as a scheduling fact rather than an assessment risk.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Physics HL student usually need before the May exams?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the diagnosis finds, which is why an honest answer comes after a trial lesson rather than before. A student whose content is sound and who loses marks to uncertainties, command terms and the clock can gain substantially from a block of eight to twelve sessions. A student who has not learned the Theme D extensions and has no investigation needs considerably more, and should be told that plainly with the hours it would actually take. Nobody should quote a session count before seeing two pieces of the student's marked work.

faqs.question: Does my child need Physics HL for engineering or medicine?
faqs.answer: Engineering programmes commonly ask for physics and mathematics, frequently at Higher Level and frequently naming Analysis and Approaches for the mathematics. Medicine requirements vary widely by country and institution, with chemistry and biology more often specified than physics. The only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for each specific course on the shortlist, on the university's own admissions pages, in the year of application. A tutor can help a student read a requirement precisely; nobody should summarise away what the university states for itself.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 'state', 'explain' and 'discuss' in a physics question?
faqs.answer: They are published command terms and they set how much the examiner expects. 'State' wants a short answer with no supporting argument. 'Outline' wants a brief account. 'Explain' wants reasons or a causal mechanism, and the mark scheme awards the links in the chain, so a student who writes the first and last step of three collects one mark of three. 'Discuss' wants a balanced consideration with more than one side. 'Deduce' wants a conclusion reached from given information. Marking a student's own answers against these terms is usually the quickest available mark gain in Paper 2.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school physics teacher tutor him privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported and verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical effect is that the teacher a family thinks of first is usually the one person they cannot hire, which is a large part of why outside tutoring exists in this emirate at all.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on tutor input into the Physics HL investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a boundary that should be stated in writing before work starts. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is measurable, point at a criterion and say which descriptor a draft currently meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation, and ask the questions that make a student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text, supply data, or return a rewritten report. The student signs an authenticity declaration for the school and the work must be theirs throughout. Any service offering a finished investigation is selling a malpractice investigation instead.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service available only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing of the student's own graphs and scripts, and a recording available afterwards. For Physics HL that trade is a favourable one: the family gets a tutor chosen for the current guide and Higher Level experience rather than one chosen for living near Al Raha, and nobody pays a travel premium built into the hourly rate.

intro.heading: Judging Physics support on evidence rather than on atmosphere
paragraphs: There is a version of tutoring that happens in a great many Abu Dhabi households. A capable tutor arrives on time, the sessions are calm, your child does not complain, and everybody agrees things are improving. Then a mock lands at roughly the mark it would have landed at anyway. Nothing was done wrong exactly; it is simply that nobody decided at the outset what evidence of progress would look like, so for three months there was nothing to check and therefore nothing to correct.

Standard Level Physics is a good subject to fix this in, because it produces an unusual quantity of markable material. Past-paper questions with published mark schemes. A data-based section of the first paper that can be marked in twenty minutes. An extended-response paper whose mark schemes name the physics they want. A scientific investigation worth 20 per cent, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six, written in drafts across weeks. A practical programme of around forty hours producing real data tables. Every one of those is an artefact that can be looked at rather than described.

The failures are specific too, which is what makes counting possible. A Standard Level Physics candidate losing marks is usually losing them in a small number of identifiable ways: answers quoted without units or to a calculator's full display, algebra attempted before any physical principle is stated, uncertainties written down but never propagated, and evaluation sections filled with generic remarks about human error. Those recur across papers. A tutor who claims the student is improving should be able to show the count falling.

On delivery, the plain statement belongs near the top. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. For the evidence question that turns out to matter: work set in a video session is marked between sessions and returned in writing, so a family in Al Reef or Shakhbout City holds a dated record rather than a verbal summary given on the doorstep.

The rest of this page is practical. Which Physics artefacts exist and who holds them. Three questions you can ask a sixteen-year-old that reveal more than a mock mark does. What the Standard Level papers contain and the metric to track on each. How to translate a school report phrase into one of the five themes. What each pass over an investigation draft should change, and which of the four criteria is at stake. What should be visible at four, eight and twelve weeks. Why marks and grades move on different clocks. And, for families in the middle of it, what evidence should decide a move from Higher Level down to Standard Level.

subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation taken by a minority of Standard Level students. Progress is visible as draft-to-draft movement against its own criteria, and the usual failure is a research question that the available equipment cannot answer.

subjects.description: One essay and one exhibition against published criteria, so there is little to measure weekly. Physics students have strong material: what a measurement with an uncertainty actually claims, and when a model is replaced rather than corrected.

sections.heading: Three questions that tell you more than a mock mark
paragraphs: A mock mark is a single number standing in for a dozen different possible problems. Three questions, asked of the student directly, separate those problems faster than any score. They take ten minutes, they need no equipment, and a parent with no physics can run them, because what you are listening for is the shape of the answer rather than its correctness.

First, hand over a graph from a recent piece of work and ask what the gradient means. Not how to calculate it, but what physical quantity it is and in what units. A student who answers immediately has the data skills the course rewards. A student who starts computing a number has learned a procedure without its meaning, which is the exact failure the data-based paper is built to expose, and it is highly fixable.

Second, ask a prediction question with no numbers in it. If the separation doubles and the mass stays the same, what happens to the force, and why. A student who reasons from the relationship is in good shape. A student who reaches for a formula sheet is pattern-matching, and pattern-matching holds up through the early mechanics and collapses in fields. That is a representation problem rather than a knowledge gap, and it responds to two or three deliberate sessions rather than to months of practice.

Third, ask what principle they would write down first for a question they have already attempted. Conservation of energy, Newton's second law, the changing flux. A candidate who names a principle before touching the algebra is collecting the reasoning marks that the extended-response paper is mostly made of. One who starts rearranging immediately is leaving those marks on the page, and will keep doing so until somebody makes the habit explicit.

sections.heading: The Standard Level papers, and the metric to track on each
paragraphs: Standard Level Physics is assessed by two written papers carrying 80 per cent between them and an internally assessed investigation carrying 20 per cent. The first paper divides into a multiple-choice section across the whole syllabus and a data-based and experimental section, and those two halves reward almost opposite habits. The second paper is short answer and extended response, and it is the one where the largest single block of marks sits.

Tracking them separately is the whole trick, because a combined mark conceals which half is weak. A student can be quick and accurate on multiple choice and poor at reading a graph, or thorough on data questions and too slow to finish the multiple-choice section. Both patterns produce the same middling total and need opposite remedies. Ask for the two sections marked and reported separately, every time, and record them separately in whatever you keep.

For the extended-response paper the metric worth counting is not the mark but the presence of a stated principle. Go through a marked script and count the questions where the student wrote a physical statement before the algebra. That count rising is the mechanism by which the mark rises, and it rises first. The other count worth keeping is answers missing units or quoted to a calculator's full display, which should fall towards zero within a month of anyone paying attention to it.

Confirm durations, mark totals and weightings against your child's own copy of the current subject guide, which the school issues and the IB revises periodically. A good deal of material online still describes the previous sciences model, which is a genuine hazard in this subject. What is stable enough to build a tracking system on is the structure: a split first paper, an extended-response second paper, and an investigation marked out of 24 across four equal criteria.

sections.heading: Turning a school report phrase into a theme
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi science reports are written in a vocabulary that sounds informative and is not. 'Needs to apply knowledge to unfamiliar contexts' almost always means the student has learned question types rather than principles. 'Requires more precision' usually means units and significant figures. 'Developing analytical skills' typically means the data-based section. Each of those phrases points to a specific theme or component, and translating it is free and takes one email to the teacher.

The five themes are worth knowing by letter, because schemes of work use them. Theme A is space, time and motion. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter. Theme C is wave behaviour. Theme D is fields. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. A Standard Level student takes all five without the Higher Level subtopics, which means no rigid body mechanics, no relativity, no thermodynamics, no induction and no quantum physics, and without the Higher Level extensions inside shared subtopics.

That exclusion list matters when reading advice online, because a great deal of it is written for Higher Level candidates. A Standard Level student worrying about induction is worrying about material they will not be examined on, and a tutor quoting for it is quoting for the wrong course. Equally, a Standard Level student who has been given Higher Level practice questions will produce scores that mean nothing, which is a surprisingly common source of unnecessary panic in DP2.

The table maps each theme against the report language that usually accompanies it, what that language actually means, and the evidence that would show the problem had been resolved. It is written to be taken to a parents' evening and used as a list of questions rather than read as a description.

sections.heading: The investigation, draft by draft, at Standard Level
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the one component where progress can be watched rather than inferred. It carries 20 per cent of the Standard Level grade, is marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each, and is capped at 3,000 words. The four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because they are equal, a beautifully executed experiment with a thin evaluation scores no better than a modest experiment that is evaluated properly, which is not what most students assume.

The decisive pass is the first one, before any data exists. A research question with a defined independent variable, a defined dependent variable, controlled variables that are actually controllable in a school laboratory, and a method capable of producing enough data over a wide enough range to test anything. Students who start collecting before this is settled usually end up with a dataset that cannot answer their own question, and no later analysis recovers those marks.

Later passes should each target one criterion, in an order that respects dependency. Data analysis before conclusion, because a conclusion rests on processed data with propagated uncertainties. Conclusion before evaluation, because an evaluation has to explain the gap between what was found and what was expected. Evaluation last, and specifically: quantified weaknesses with realistic improvements, not a paragraph about human error. The table sets out the sequence so a family can tell whether a draft is moving or merely being retyped.

The boundary protects the student and we state it rather than imply it. A tutor explains what each criterion asks, teaches the physics and the analysis techniques needed, reads the draft and names where marks are being lost, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. No part of the submitted report originates with a tutor and nothing is rewritten into final form. Keep the dated feedback; where a school asks about the provenance of internally assessed work, a trail of the student's own revisions is the clearest possible answer.

sections.heading: What four, eight and twelve weeks should show in Physics
paragraphs: At four weeks the question is narrow: has a presentation or reasoning habit started to change. You should hold three or four marked pieces with the published scheme applied, a baseline timed section, and a short note after each session naming the error being tracked. The claim at this stage is modest and checkable: fewer answers missing units, and a stated principle appearing on more extended questions. If none of that exists, the problem is the arrangement rather than the student.

At eight weeks the question becomes whether the habit has converted into marks under conditions. That needs a second timed paper on the same scale as the baseline, marked question by question so the two can be laid side by side. A gain concentrated in the question types that were targeted is strong evidence. A gain scattered randomly may be noise, and saying so is more useful than celebrating it. The data-based section is usually where movement shows first, because it is the most trainable component in the course.

At twelve weeks the decision is continue, change or stop. By then there should be two or three comparable papers, a declining count on the tracked error, and an investigation that has moved on at least one named criterion. If all three hold, the plan is working and the sensible move may be to reduce intensity rather than extend it. If the papers are flat, buying more of the same is the least promising option available, and changing the diagnosis or the match is more likely to help.

The entire structure rests on one decision taken at the start, which costs nothing. Agree, before the first paid session, what will be looked at and when. Families who do that almost never spend a fourth month on a plan that was never going to deliver, and the awkward conversation about whether any of this is working simply does not arise, because the answer was already written down.

sections.heading: Marks, grades and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Marks and grades do not move together, and conflating them causes a lot of avoidable disappointment in DP2. Grade boundaries are set per session by the IB after the papers have been marked, they shift from session to session, and they are not published in advance. A student who gains eight marks on an extended-response paper has unambiguously improved and may or may not have crossed a boundary. The honest way to report progress is in marks on a stated scale, with the grade treated as a consequence.

This is why no tutor should be offering a specific grade, a points total or a stated improvement, and why a page that does is telling you something about itself rather than about physics. What can be committed to is process: work set and marked, a named error tracked, written notes, and a plan that changes when the evidence says it should. Anything beyond that is selling a certainty the assessment system does not contain.

Predicted grades belong to the school. A prediction is a teacher's professional judgement submitted for university applications on the basis of the evidence the school holds, which is its own assessments, mocks and classwork. Tutoring influences it only indirectly, by improving the work the school sees. Asking a school to revise a prediction because a tutor disagrees does not work; asking the teacher what the student must demonstrate in the school's own assessments for the prediction to move does.

One further honest caveat. Standard Level Physics sits inside a Diploma with five other subjects, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge in it. A student whose physics marks climb while three other subjects slide has not been helped overall, and a tutor who notices that pattern should name it. Several times a year the right recommendation is fewer physics hours and a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about load.

sections.heading: Moving down from Higher Level: the evidence that should decide it
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Standard Level Physics enquiries in Abu Dhabi come from families part-way through a Higher Level course, asking whether to step down. It is a legitimate question and it should be answered with evidence rather than with sentiment. What a Standard Level student drops is the Higher Level-only material, including rigid body mechanics, relativity, thermodynamics, induction and quantum physics, along with the extensions inside shared subtopics. The investigation carries across unchanged, and so do all four of its criteria.

The evidence worth gathering before the conversation is specific. How many of the lost marks on recent papers came from Higher Level-only content as against shared material. Whether the student's data-based and reasoning habits are sound, because if they are not, the same habits will cost marks at Standard Level too. Whether the physics is the problem at all, or whether the underlying mathematics is. And what the student's other five subjects look like, because a step down taken to protect two other grades is a different decision from one taken because physics is unreachable.

The timing is a school matter and the window is real. The school has to timetable the student into a Standard Level set that may be full, and the IB registration has to be amended, so the decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator and should be raised early rather than once the mocks have confirmed what everyone suspected. A tutor's useful contribution is the evidence: a marked script annotated to show which losses were Higher Level-only, which is a twenty-minute job and genuinely helps the meeting.

The outcome is sometimes the opposite of what the family expected. Where the lost marks are concentrated in presentation habits and unstated principles rather than in Higher Level content, stepping down removes the hardest material and leaves the actual problem untouched, and the grade does not improve as much as anyone hoped. That is worth knowing before the registration is changed, and it is exactly the kind of finding a marked script delivers and a conversation does not.

sections.heading: ADEK, the school's data and the questions that get real answers
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is where a school's rating should be read rather than from a third-party summary. An inspection band tells you nothing about one Standard Level Physics set, which is where your child's marks are actually produced.

The school holds the comparative information that makes everything else interpretable: how your child's marks sit against the set, which questions the whole set lost, whether a theme was taught thinly because of timetable pressure, when the experimental hours and the investigation deadlines fall, and what a predicted grade will rest on. Ask for those five things specifically. General questions about progress get general answers; specific questions get a diagnosis, and the school is not withholding anything, it is simply waiting to be asked.

One route to rule out before planning. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy page. Either way, your child's teacher is a source of evidence rather than a tutoring option.

For whoever you do hire, the regulatory position is checkable in a sentence. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none.

faqs.question: What evidence should we have after a month of Standard Level Physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things. A written baseline from the first lesson naming the weak component and one error to track. Three or four pieces of set work, marked against the published scheme rather than given a percentage. A short note after each session saying what was covered and which error is being tracked. And a date for the next timed paper. You should not expect the overall paper mark to have moved yet; that typically arrives a mock later. What you should see is fewer answers missing units and a principle appearing on more extended questions.

faqs.question: His mock mark went up but the predicted grade did not change. Why not?
faqs.answer: Because the two are different instruments. Grade boundaries are set per session by the IB after marking, they move between sessions and they are not published in advance, so a real gain can sit inside one band. A prediction is separately the school's professional judgement based on all the evidence it holds, not on one mock. Ask the teacher what your son would need to demonstrate, in the school's own assessments, for the prediction to move. That question gets a specific answer; asking for the prediction to be raised does not.

faqs.question: How do we tell a content gap from a technique problem on a Physics script?
faqs.answer: By the shape of the losses. Marks lost thinly across almost every question, one or two at a time, are a technique or presentation problem: missing units, values quoted to a calculator's full display, no principle stated before the algebra. Marks lost in a concentrated block, where a cluster of questions scores nothing at all, are a content gap in a theme. The two need opposite remedies, and a percentage hides which one you have. Ask for the script with per-question marks rather than the summary figure.

faqs.question: Our report says she needs to apply knowledge to unfamiliar contexts. What does that mean in Physics?
faqs.answer: Usually that she has learned question types rather than principles, so a familiar question works and a rephrased one does not. The test for it takes two minutes: ask a prediction question with no numbers in it, such as what happens to the force if the separation doubles. A student who reasons from the relationship is fine. A student who reaches for a formula sheet is pattern-matching, which holds up through early mechanics and collapses in Theme D fields. That is a representation problem and it responds to two or three deliberate sessions rather than to more practice.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level Physics leave out that Higher Level includes?
faqs.answer: Whole subtopics and extensions. The subtopics are rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, induction in Theme D and quantum physics in Theme E. The extensions sit inside shared subtopics such as simple harmonic motion, the gravitational and electric field material, and the radioactive decay law. This matters practically: a Standard Level student revising induction is revising material they will not be examined on, and one given Higher Level practice papers produces scores that mean nothing.

faqs.question: How many drafts should the investigation go through, and what should each one change?
faqs.answer: Four or five passes, each targeting one criterion in dependency order. First, before any data exists, settle the research question and the variables so the method can actually produce enough data over a wide enough range. Then processing and uncertainty propagation. Then the conclusion, compared against accepted physics with the source identified. Then evaluation, with specific quantified weaknesses rather than remarks about human error. A final pass cuts the method to fit the 3,000-word ceiling. A draft that is being retyped rather than restructured is not a pass.

faqs.question: My son's practical work is good but his papers are not. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Easily, because they test different things. Competent bench work means he can follow a method and take readings carefully. The data-based section of the first paper asks what a gradient means physically, whether a difference between two results is meaningful given the uncertainties, and what is wrong with somebody else's method. Those are interpretive skills, and they are trained on paper rather than at a bench. The useful consequence is that this gap is one of the most improvable things in the course and it lifts the investigation marks at the same time.

faqs.question: Should a tutor be looking at our child's school laboratory record?
faqs.answer: At the data, yes; at the record as a document, no. What helps is a photograph of a recent results table, because it shows whether the student records readings with units, repeats, and sensible precision, which is exactly what the investigation's data analysis criterion rewards. What a tutor should not be doing is working inside the school's assessed practical material or anything the school is supervising. The division is simple: the school owns the experimental programme and the supervision; a tutor helps with design thinking, processing and the written argument.

faqs.question: Is in-home Standard Level Physics tuition available in Abu Dhabi from IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. We do not send a tutor to any UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not a service we sell; that exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. For the evidence question this is an advantage rather than a compromise: work set in a session is marked between sessions and returned in writing, so what you hold is a dated record of marked scripts and tracked errors instead of a verbal summary at the door.

faqs.question: Should we move our daughter from Higher Level to Standard Level Physics, and what should decide it?
faqs.answer: Evidence, and the most useful piece is a marked script annotated to separate losses on Higher Level-only content from losses on shared material. If most of the damage is in rigid body mechanics, thermodynamics, induction or quantum physics, stepping down genuinely removes it. If the damage is missing units, unstated principles and unpropagated uncertainty, those habits follow her down and the grade will not move as much as hoped. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator, because the school must have a set with space and the registration must be amended.

faqs.question: How often should a timed Physics paper be sat, and which section?
faqs.answer: Fortnightly once the relevant themes are taught, and start with the data-based section because it is short, quick to mark and the most trainable component in the course. Full extended-response papers are worth sitting monthly, under conditions with the phone in another room, with completion time logged next to the mark. Families in outer districts usually do the longer papers on a Saturday morning, because a paper sat at seven in the evening after a bus from the island measures tiredness rather than physics.

faqs.question: What should a written note after a science session actually contain?
faqs.answer: Two or three lines. What was covered, what has been set to do before the next session, and the single error currently being tracked, named the same way each week so it can be counted rather than described. Over six weeks those notes become the clearest record of whether anything is changing. Anything longer turns into a narrative, which reads well and proves nothing. If notes are not arriving, ask for them explicitly; a reluctance to put anything in writing is itself informative.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what Physics grade our child will finish with?
faqs.answer: No, and an honest one will explain why rather than hedge. Grade boundaries are set per session after the papers are marked and are not published beforehand, so any specific final grade offered in advance is invented. What a tutor can legitimately tell you is which component is losing marks, how many of those marks are recoverable from habits as against content, and roughly how long that normally takes. Predictions for university applications belong to the school and rest on its own assessment evidence.

faqs.question: Who at the school should we ask, and what exactly should we ask them?
faqs.answer: The Physics teacher first, and the Diploma coordinator if the issue is load or level. Five specific requests get real answers: the marked script with per-question marks, which questions the whole set found hardest, when the experimental hours and investigation deadlines fall, whether any theme was covered at speed because of timetable pressure, and what your child must demonstrate for a predicted grade to move. 'How is she doing' produces a sentence about effort. Those five produce a plan, and they cost nothing.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start Standard Level Physics support?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the marked script shows, which is why the first lesson is a diagnosis rather than a sale. If the content is broadly covered and the marks are going on units, unstated principles and the data-based section, then even six to eight weeks changes the picture, because those are habits and habits move quickly. If two themes were never properly taught, no short block delivers them and we will say so. An honest no at that point saves a family more than a block of hours aimed at an unreachable target.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level Physics support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE bands put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, while in-home one-to-one work runs about AED 180 to 350 and reaches around 500 at the specialist end. Standard Level Physics generally sits in the middle of the specialist band, below Higher Level. Those figures belong to the sources named rather than to IB Gram, and the first lesson is free precisely so a plan can be priced after a diagnosis instead of before one.

Ask the school for the script with per-question marks, a recent data table, the investigation draft with its comments, and the term's internal deadlines. Send those to us with the level and the theme you think is the problem, and the free first lesson comes back as a written baseline naming the leaking component and the one error to track. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, work is marked against the published schemes between sessions, and at the agreed review we will tell you plainly whether the evidence says continue, change or stop.
