process.title: Send the marked writing, not the report
process.description: A marked Paper 1 style task with the criterion marks visible tells us in two minutes what a term of reports does not. If the school does not break the mark into language, message and conceptual understanding, send the annotated script anyway — the pattern of corrections is itself the diagnosis.

process.title: Split the Paper 2 score
process.description: Listening and reading separately, if the school provides it. If not, have your child sit one listening section to time at home, audio twice and no pausing. The ratio between the two numbers decides whether the plan is grammar work or a term of recognition building.

process.title: Match on level and on the HL works
process.description: SL and HL orals are different exams, and an HL block needs a tutor who has read the two literary works your child is studying. We name which level the tutor has taught and how recently, confirm the works, and offer a second option where one exists.

process.title: Take the trial on a real task
process.description: One trial per subject, before any payment, spent marking something your child has written. By the end you should know which of the three diagnoses applies and what the first two sessions will target. A trial that was a conversation in Spanish has not told you anything you did not know.

process.title: Book a block against one diagnosis
process.description: A defined number of sessions aimed at one thing: a grammatical decision, listening recognition, the oral. Each session's artefact is agreed in advance — marked writing, a timed listening score, a recorded rehearsal — and marking between sessions is settled before the first invoice.

process.title: Re-mark at the end against the same criteria
process.description: The block closes with the same kind of task marked the same way, placed beside the baseline. Then an explicit decision: move to the next diagnosis, change tutor, or stop. Without that comparison, a block cannot tell you whether the money did anything.

whyPoints.title: The criterion split is shown, not summarised
whyPoints.description: Every marked task comes back with language out of 12, message out of 12 and conceptual understanding out of 6 shown separately. A single total hides which of three different problems a student actually has, and that is the problem the grade is hiding too.

whyPoints.title: Grammatical decisions are drilled to automatic
whyPoints.description: Ser and estar, preterite and imperfect, the subjunctive triggers, por and para: one per session, on the student's own sentences, until the choice stops being a calculation. Understanding these is easy; using them under exam pressure is what the marks measure.

whyPoints.title: Listening practice includes variety on purpose
whyPoints.description: A candidate calibrated to one teacher's accent is relying on the examination choosing that accent. We build in several Spanish varieties across a block, because regional pronunciation is the half of Paper 2 that classroom audio tends to avoid.

whyPoints.title: HL literary works prepared where they are examined
whyPoints.description: The two works feed the oral and never appear on the written papers. Sessions reduce each to a page of usable Spanish and then practise unseen extracts under the real preparation limit, rather than teaching literary criticism the component does not reward.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you what you can do free
whyPoints.description: Spanish has more accessible authentic material than almost any other language, and a good deal of this subject can be built from free sources in the right order. We say which and in what order, even when saying so means fewer booked sessions.

whyPoints.title: Claims limited to what can be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No examiner status without evidence, no grade guarantees, no statistics without a source, and no implied endorsement from ADEK, the IB or any named school. Those four appear constantly in this market and all four are liabilities rather than selling points.

faqs.question: Why does my child speak Spanish confidently and still score 4?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is not a criterion. Paper 1 is marked out of 30 with 12 for language, 12 for message and 6 for conceptual understanding, and the oral uses the same shape. A confident speaker who guesses on Spanish's recurring grammatical decisions — the two verbs meaning 'to be', the split between the preterite and imperfect past, whether a clause triggers the subjunctive, and which word for 'for' belongs here — produces fluent Spanish that drops small language marks in nearly every sentence. The marked script looks like a page of minor corrections rather than one identifiable problem, which is exactly why it goes unaddressed.

faqs.question: Which Spanish grammar points are worth paying a tutor to fix?
faqs.answer: Four, in this order. The preterite and imperfect split, because English has one simple past and a student narrating anything has to choose in every clause. The two verbs meaning 'to be', particularly with adjectives whose meaning changes depending on the choice. The present subjunctive after roughly ten identifiable triggers, which is a finite list and demonstrates range when used once correctly. And the two words for 'for', which is low stakes individually and very high in volume. Together these account for more lost language marks than every other grammatical issue combined.

faqs.question: How is Spanish B Paper 1 marked, and how long should the task be?
faqs.answer: Out of 30: language 12, message 12, conceptual understanding 6. The word range is 250 to 400 at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher Level, and writing outside it costs marks in both directions. Short answers cannot develop a message enough for the 12 available message marks; very long ones lose control of language and overrun. Have your child measure once what their own handwriting looks like at the top and bottom of the range, so length can be judged in the exam without spending minutes counting words.

faqs.question: Which of the three Paper 1 tasks should my child choose?
faqs.answer: The one whose text type they have practised, not the one whose topic feels familiar. That is the opposite of what most candidates do in the ninety seconds they spend deciding. A narrative task lets a student display the past tenses they have drilled; a proposal or a speech invites the subjunctive naturally through recommendations and wishes. An unfamiliar topic in a practised form almost always beats a comfortable topic in a form never attempted. Teaching that comparison takes one session and changes the decision permanently.

faqs.question: What are the six conceptual understanding marks in Spanish B?
faqs.answer: They credit recognising the audience, context and purpose the task sets, choosing a suitable text type and using its conventions. They are the cheapest marks on the paper because they require no better Spanish. A task asking for a blog post, answered with accurate undifferentiated prose and no title, no reader addressed and no closing hook, loses most of them. One page of text-type reference — what a blog post, a formal letter, a speech, an interview and a diary entry each need — plus three timed attempts, is usually enough to stop the leak permanently.

faqs.question: Why is my child's Spanish listening score so much lower than their reading?
faqs.answer: Because Spanish gives readers two advantages that listeners do not get. Spelling maps onto sound transparently, so a reader is never unsure which word they are looking at, and English shares a large Latin-derived vocabulary, so abstract words are often transparent on sight. Natural Spanish is fast, runs words together, drops consonants in several major varieties and uses regional vocabulary classroom material avoids. If listening sits around half of reading, the issue is recognition rather than knowledge, and more vocabulary learning will not close it.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child learns Latin American or peninsular Spanish?
faqs.answer: The examination accepts any standard variety provided the student is consistent, and consistency is the part that matters. The plural form of address differs between Spain and most of Latin America and affects verb endings. Some regions use a distinct second-person singular with its own forms. Everyday vocabulary varies. None of that costs marks when used consistently; mixing varieties inside one task does. Choose the variety the household or school uses, stay in it, and treat varied listening practice as separate insurance for Paper 2.

faqs.question: Do the two Higher Level literary works appear on the Spanish B papers?
faqs.answer: No. Spanish B at Higher Level requires two literary works studied in Spanish, and they appear on neither Paper 1 nor Paper 2. Their role is in the individual oral, where the starting extract is drawn from one of them. HL students who read the works in DP1 and then revise only for the written papers have left 25% of the grade on half-remembered material. The useful preparation reduces each work to a page of usable Spanish — situation, main figures, two or three concerns — then practises unseen extracts under real timing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor prepare the HL oral without it becoming a script?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a script would fail on its own terms anyway. The oral includes unscripted conversation, so a memorised candidate collapses at the first unexpected question. Legitimate preparation is full rehearsals with unseen extracts from the two works, recorded and reviewed against language, message and interactive skills, plus practice placing an extract in the work and linking it to a concern. What a tutor may not do is supply memorised answers to be delivered as the student's own thinking. The risk of that falls on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Where can a student in Abu Dhabi actually practise Spanish?
faqs.answer: It has to be engineered, because unlike Arabic or French, Spanish has little incidental presence in this emirate. The good news is that accessible material is abundant and mostly free. Short news articles from Spanish-language outlets build reading pace in a register close to Paper 2. Subtitled drama with Spanish rather than English subtitles gives natural speed with a safety net. Graded learner podcasts build recognition, and native-speaker podcasts take over once recognition exists. What is genuinely scarce is unscripted speaking, which is the part a weekly session supplies.

faqs.question: Will a Spanish tutor come to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Spanish B sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format suits the work: the script is annotated on a shared screen while both people look at the same sentence, and audio replays from the same window. In-home tuition exists in this market at roughly AED 180-500 an hour by published UAE surveys and listings, with travel inside the rate, and the drive across Abu Dhabi is part of what that pays for.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to move a Spanish B grade?
faqs.answer: It depends which of three diagnoses applies. A confident speaker losing language marks on grammatical decisions shows measurable movement in about six sessions, because each decision can be drilled to automaticity on their own writing. A student whose oral sits well below their written papers usually needs three recorded rehearsals, which is the cheapest intervention available on a component worth 25%. A listening recognition gap takes a term, because recognition is built by volume. We say which one applies before a block is booked rather than at session fifteen.

faqs.question: Is my near-native child in the right course at Spanish B?
faqs.answer: Worth examining in DP1, while a change is still possible. A student scoring 7 in Spanish B with no effort is being assessed well below their level and learning little, and Spanish A: Language and Literature is where that student usually belongs. It is also the route towards a bilingual diploma, which requires two Language A courses rather than a Group 2 course, with conditions set by the IB and worth confirming with your school's coordinator. The evidence to look at is written register and analytical writing in Spanish, not conversational ease.

faqs.question: Can we move down from Spanish B to Spanish ab initio?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the school decides within the IB's framework. Ab initio is for students with little or no previous experience of the language, so a student with three years of MYP Spanish does not qualify however shaky the grades look. If Spanish B genuinely is the wrong level, the realistic options are Standard Level rather than Higher Level, or a different Group 2 language where the student is a true beginner. Either conversation needs to happen early in DP1, because both become impossible once the course is underway.

faqs.question: Do Spanish tutors in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. Abu Dhabi adds that reported ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students.

faqs.question: What should we send when asking about Spanish B support?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is a school report. The most recent marked writing task with criterion marks if the school provides them, because the pattern of corrections is the diagnosis. The Paper 2 result split into listening and reading, or a listening section sat to time at home if the school does not split it. And the oral mark, plus the titles of the two literary works if your child is at Higher Level. We read those and say which diagnosis applies and what the first two sessions would target, at no charge.

intro.heading: What counts as evidence in a language subject
paragraphs: Parents of Spanish B students get the least legible school reports of anyone in the Diploma. A maths report carries a percentage and a topic list. A Spanish report tends to carry a predicted grade and a sentence about participation, and neither tells you where the marks are going. The result is a family that cannot tell a vocabulary problem from a task-response problem, and therefore cannot tell whether the tutoring they are paying for is addressing the right thing.

The remedy is not more communication. It is an artefact. One piece of your child's own work, marked against the published criteria, with the criterion letter written beside each annotation so you can see whether the loss sits in language, in message or in the interactive part of the oral. A listening set marked by question type rather than as a single score. A recorded oral attempt with the criteria open next to it. Those are documents. They can be compared, dated and filed. A parent who speaks no Spanish at all can read the pattern in them, because the criterion letter tells you what kind of mistake it was without you needing to judge the Spanish itself. That is the point of insisting on the letters rather than accepting a tidy page of corrections.

The second half of the method is repetition of the measure. A task in week two and a different task in week ten is not a comparison; it is two unrelated events. The same text type, marked by the same person against the same descriptors, is a comparison. That is why our fortnightly cycle deliberately returns to task types rather than always moving forward, and why the evidence file includes the earlier version rather than replacing it with the better one.

Spanish B has three components and each leaves a different kind of trace. Paper 1, written production, leaves the richest - a marked page you can hold. Paper 2, listening and reading, leaves a numerical pattern that is far more useful broken down by question stem than totalled. The individual oral, conducted and marked inside your child's school and then moderated by the IB, leaves a recording, and a rehearsal recording from six weeks earlier is one of the most persuasive documents in the whole file.

Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared document so the tutor watches the writing happen rather than receiving it afterwards. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For this method the screen is an advantage: the writing is captured, the annotations are typed and legible, the oral rehearsals record themselves, and nothing depends on a sheet of paper surviving a school bag.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-spanish-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: A subject page is more useful broken into the things that actually get marked. Each entry below is a skill area in Spanish B, with the kind of evidence it produces and how quickly that evidence tends to move.

subjects.name: Written production under time
subjects.description: The richest evidence in the subject: a marked page with criterion letters on it. Moves quickly when the problem is task response or text type, slowly when it is grammatical range. Three marked tasks usually reveal which.

subjects.name: Listening at natural speed
subjects.description: Scored evidence, and far more useful logged per question type than as a total. The usual finding is that locating stated detail is fine and inferring attitude is not, which is a technique problem rather than a vocabulary one.

subjects.name: Reading inference
subjects.description: Evidence here is the pattern of where in the paper marks stop. A student arriving at the inference questions with four minutes left has a pacing problem that looks exactly like a comprehension problem on a report.

subjects.name: Oral interaction
subjects.description: A recording, which is the most persuasive artefact a file can hold. A rehearsal from six weeks earlier played beside a current one shows fluency and recovery in a way no written comment manages.

subjects.name: The subjunctive
subjects.description: The single structure most responsible for Spanish B students writing below their actual level, because avoidance is invisible on a report. Evidence of progress is its correct appearance in unprompted writing, not in a drill.

subjects.name: The tense system beyond the present
subjects.description: Preterite against imperfect is the classic Abu Dhabi classroom casualty, taught once and never stabilised. A narrative task marked for tense choice alone is the diagnostic that settles whether it is secure.

subjects.name: Register: tu, usted and ustedes
subjects.description: Formality carries marks under language and under conceptual understanding at once, because the wrong form means the wrong reader was addressed. Quick to fix and frequently never mentioned in class.

subjects.name: Vocabulary across the five themes
subjects.description: Measured as retrieval under time rather than as lists covered. The useful evidence is which theme produces a stall, since schools choose topic depth and the gaps are therefore school-specific.

subjects.name: Connectors and discourse markers
subjects.description: The cheapest mark improvement in the subject. A dozen connectors held to automatic recall lift organisation in writing and sustain the oral discussion, and their appearance in a marked task is immediately visible.

sections.heading: Why a Spanish B report tells you so little, and what to ask for instead
paragraphs: A predicted grade and a sentence about effort is the standard output of a language report, and it is not enough to make a decision with. The predicted grade is an aggregate of unlike things - a written task, a listening score, a teacher's impression of oral fluency - and the sentence about effort describes behaviour rather than attainment. A parent reading that cannot tell whether the next six weeks should go on vocabulary, on text types or on listening technique, and will usually guess vocabulary because vocabulary is the thing everyone understands.

There are three questions that get a better answer out of any school. Which criterion is my child losing most marks on in written production. What does the breakdown of their last listening set look like by question type. Have they recorded a full oral rehearsal yet, and may we hear it. Teachers can usually answer all three, and the answers are specific enough to plan from. Asked in that form, the conversation stops being about reassurance.

Where the school cannot supply that - and with a Spanish group of eight students across two levels, often it genuinely cannot - an external fortnightly artefact fills the gap. The point is not to second-guess the teacher. It is to generate more marked data than a small shared class can produce, so that by half term there is a pattern rather than an impression, and so the conversation at the parents evening starts from a document.

sections.heading: The three components and the trace each one leaves
paragraphs: Paper 1, written production, carries a quarter of the grade and leaves the most readable evidence. It is marked out of thirty across three criteria: twelve for language, twelve for message and six for conceptual understanding. That split is worth knowing, because a student with excellent grammar and poor task response is capped around half the paper no matter how accurate the Spanish is, and that single fact reorders most tutoring plans.

Paper 2 holds listening and reading together and carries half the grade. Its evidence is numerical and almost always reported as a total, which throws away the useful part. Broken down by question stem, the same set tells you whether the problem is vocabulary, inference, or simply arriving at the last four questions with no time. Those three findings lead to three different plans, and a total leads to none.

The individual oral carries the final quarter, is conducted and marked by your child's teacher in school, and is then moderated by the IB. At Standard Level it runs from a visual stimulus linked to a prescribed theme; at Higher Level from an extract of one of the two literary works studied. Its evidence is a recording, and the value of recording rehearsals early is that you end up with a comparison rather than a single nervous performance. Most students who hear a rehearsal from two months earlier are surprised by how much has changed, and that surprise does more for motivation than any amount of encouragement from a parent or a tutor. It is also the one piece of evidence a student will volunteer to listen to again.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Paper 1 task: what the annotations mean
paragraphs: A marked task is only useful if a parent can read it, which is why every annotation carries its criterion letter. An A against a verb ending is a language point. A B in the margin beside a well-written paragraph that answers a different question than the one asked is a message point, and it is usually the expensive one. A C beside a missing salutation is conceptual understanding: the student has not written for the reader the task specified.

The pattern matters more than any individual mark. Across three tasks, most students show one dominant leak and one secondary one. A student whose annotations are nearly all A has a grammar problem and will improve slowly, over a term, with systematic work. A student whose annotations are mostly B and C has a task-response problem and can improve substantially within a few weeks, because conventions and task reading are technique rather than knowledge.

The second version of the same task type is where the file earns its keep. Same text type, same criteria, same marker, six weeks apart. If the B annotations have gone and the A annotations remain, the technique work has done its job and the grammar work is the next phase. If nothing has moved, the plan was wrong and should change rather than continue with more effort. Either conclusion is worth having, and neither is available from a predicted grade. Keeping both versions side by side also stops a tutor marking more generously over time, which is a real and largely unconscious risk when the same person marks the same student for two years.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what moves fast, what moves slowly, what plateaus
paragraphs: Not every part of a language improves at the same speed, and a plan that treats them as equivalent disappoints everyone. Text-type conventions and connectors move within two or three sessions because they are closed sets that can be learned and applied immediately. Listening technique moves in three to four weeks, since it is a change of method rather than an increase in capability. Those are the early wins and they should be taken first for exactly that reason.

Tense accuracy and the subjunctive move over a term, not a fortnight. They require noticing in unprompted production, which means repeated marked writing rather than drills, and they relapse under time pressure before they stabilise. Vocabulary breadth across five themes is slower still and depends almost entirely on retrieval habits between sessions. Oral fluency sits in the middle and improves in visible steps once the student stops reciting and starts responding.

There are genuine plateaus too. Accent rarely shifts much at sixteen and does not need to, since the criteria reward intelligibility rather than nativeness. Reading speed in a second language improves slowly and is better managed by planning an order of attack than by trying to read faster. Saying that plainly is more useful than promising even improvement, and nobody should promise a specific grade in this subject - we do not, anywhere on this site. The practical consequence is an order of work: take the fast items first, start the slow ones immediately alongside them, and stop spending sessions on the plateaus.

sections.heading: Which Spanish? Varieties in the listening paper and in your child's ear
paragraphs: Spanish B material draws on the Spanish-speaking world rather than one country, and students whose ear has only ever heard one variety meet that fact for the first time in an exam. The differences are systematic and learnable. Peninsular Spanish distinguishes the sound of c and z from s, while most of Latin America does not. Spain uses vosotros for an informal plural; Latin America uses ustedes throughout. The River Plate region uses vos with its own verb forms.

None of this changes what your child should produce. Consistency matters, not geography: a candidate who writes coherently in one variety is not penalised for choosing it. What matters is receptive flexibility, and that is a practice problem with a straightforward solution - rotate the varieties in listening material deliberately rather than letting the classroom's default supply all of it. A student who has only heard Castilian teachers will stumble on Andean or Caribbean audio for reasons that have nothing to do with vocabulary.

This is also worth asking a prospective tutor directly. A tutor from Madrid and a tutor from Bogota will both teach the course well and will model different things, and a good one tells you which without being asked. For a student already strong in one variety, deliberately pairing them with a tutor from another is sometimes the single most useful matching decision available, because it builds the flexibility the paper actually tests. Abu Dhabi makes this easy in one respect: the Spanish-speaking community in the emirate spans both sides of the Atlantic, so a student hears more than one variety socially as well as in lessons.

sections.heading: The final two terms, counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, and the fixed point to plan around is not the written paper but the school's internal deadline for the oral, which arrives earlier and is set locally. Ask for that date in writing at the start of DP2, because every other decision in the final year arranges itself around it. No specific IB session or results dates appear on this page: the IB's own site is the only place to confirm them, and your child's DP coordinator will have the school's version.

Working backwards, the oral block sits immediately before that internal window, and it is the one element with a hard local deadline attached. Before it, the useful work is content coverage across any thin themes plus the technique items that hold permanently. After it, attention moves wholly to the written papers, and that post-oral stretch is where timed full-paper practice belongs, under conditions as close to the real thing as a session allows.

The fortnightly marked task continues through all of it. Dropping it during the oral block is tempting and a mistake, because it is the thread that makes the file comparable and it is the only evidence that written production has not slipped while attention was elsewhere. In the final weeks the task becomes a full timed paper rather than a single exercise, and the earlier versions stay in the file as the baseline they always were. One more scheduling note: Abu Dhabi families travel over the spring break more than most, and a plan that pretends otherwise falls apart. Say which weeks are gone and the sequence absorbs them.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the evidence file includes recordings
paragraphs: A method built on artefacts needs a clear line about which artefacts a tutor may touch. The rule we work to is simple: practice work is ours to mark, and assessed work is the student's alone. A tutor marks rehearsal tasks, annotates them, records practice orals and reviews them against the published criteria. A tutor has no involvement in the assessed recording, supplies no content for it, and sees no part of assessed written work before the school does.

Recordings deserve a specific note because they feel different from paper. A rehearsal recording made in a tutoring session is practice material and belongs in your child's own file. It is not submitted anywhere, it is not shared with the school unless you choose to share it, and it is not a draft of the assessed performance. If your child's school asks to hear a rehearsal, that is your decision to make, and most teachers find it genuinely useful.

The wider boundary applies to the Extended Essay too, where a student choosing Spanish as the subject takes on a demanding piece of work. We coach question framing, source selection and how to use the supervision meetings well, and every word of the essay is the student's own from first question to final footnote. Machine translation sits on the wrong side of the line and is visible to any experienced reader, and the risk of it sits with the candidate rather than with us.

faqs.question: Which variety of Spanish is examined in IB Spanish B?
faqs.answer: The course draws on the Spanish-speaking world rather than one country, so listening material can carry Peninsular, Mexican, River Plate, Caribbean or Andean voices. For production, consistency matters rather than geography: a candidate writing coherently in one variety is not penalised for the choice. The practical implication is receptive flexibility, which is a practice problem. Rotate the varieties your child listens to deliberately instead of relying on whatever the classroom uses, because an ear trained on one accent stumbles on another for reasons unrelated to vocabulary.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child's tutor is from Spain or from Latin America?
faqs.answer: Both teach the course well and model different things, and a good tutor volunteers which without being asked. For a student whose ear already knows one variety, deliberately choosing a tutor from another is often the most useful matching decision available, because it builds exactly the flexibility the listening paper tests. What would matter is a tutor who treats their own variety as the only correct one, since the paper does not. Ask the question directly in the trial lesson.

faqs.question: How is IB Spanish B assessed across the two years?
faqs.answer: Three components. Paper 1 is written production, carries a quarter of the grade and is marked out of thirty across language, message and conceptual understanding. Paper 2 holds listening and reading together and carries half. The individual oral carries the final quarter, is conducted and marked by your child's teacher in school, and is moderated by the IB. Higher Level adds two literary works and replaces the visual-stimulus oral with an extract-based one. There is no coursework essay in this subject.

faqs.question: What should a marked Spanish B written task actually show me?
faqs.answer: Every annotation should carry its criterion letter, so you can read the pattern without reading Spanish. An A beside a verb ending is a language point. A B beside a well-written paragraph answering the wrong question is a message point, and that is the expensive kind. A C beside a missing salutation is conceptual understanding - the wrong reader was addressed. Across three tasks most students show one dominant leak, and that pattern is what the next six weeks should target.

faqs.question: How long does it take before the subjunctive stops costing marks?
faqs.answer: Expect a term rather than a fortnight, and expect avoidance to disappear after accuracy arrives rather than before. The honest measure is unprompted correct use in free writing, not accuracy in a drill, because students who can produce it on demand routinely sidestep it when writing under time. That sidestepping is invisible on a school report and shows up clearly in marked writing, which is one reason the fortnightly task matters more in Spanish than in some other subjects.

faqs.question: When should my child use tu and when usted in a written task?
faqs.answer: The task tells you, through its text type and its stated audience: a formal letter to an organisation takes usted, a blog post addressed to peers takes tu, and a speech depends on who is being addressed. Getting it wrong costs marks twice, under language and under conceptual understanding, because the wrong form means the wrong reader was addressed. It is quick to fix once named, and it is frequently never mentioned in a crowded class, which makes it good early value in a session.

faqs.question: What evidence should I ask my child's Spanish teacher for?
faqs.answer: Three specific things rather than a general question. Which criterion is losing the most marks in written production. What the last listening set looks like broken down by question type. Whether a full oral rehearsal has been recorded, and whether you may hear it. Teachers can usually answer all three and the answers are concrete enough to plan from. A Spanish group of eight across two levels may genuinely not have much marked data, which is useful to know rather than a complaint.

faqs.question: How quickly can Spanish B marks realistically move?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which part is leaking. Text-type conventions and connectors shift within two or three sessions because they are closed sets. Listening technique shifts in three to four weeks, since it is a change of method. Tense accuracy and the subjunctive take a term and relapse under pressure before settling. Vocabulary breadth is continuous and depends on daily retrieval. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does should worry you - but the sequence above is predictable enough to plan around.

faqs.question: Is Spanish B Higher Level worth taking if my child is not studying languages at university?
faqs.answer: Higher Level adds two literary works and a different oral task, and it demands reading time that competes with everything else in the Diploma. For a student who enjoys reading and wants the language properly, it is worthwhile on its own terms. For a student already carrying three demanding Higher Levels, Standard Level with a strong grade is frequently the better overall outcome. Check whether any target university course states a modern-language requirement, since a small number do, and decide on that rather than on general ambition.

faqs.question: What does Spanish B tutoring cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates, mostly quoted for Dubai, give the range. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. Unitors lists IGCSE tutoring from around AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes about AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits run from about AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. Those are their published figures, not our price list.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out not to be the right match?
faqs.answer: Ask that question of any provider before you book, because the models differ sharply. An agency selects the tutor and should rematch in writing. A marketplace leaves you to search and pay again. A freelance arrangement has no fallback at all. With us, tell us it is not working and we will rematch rather than ask you to persevere, and the marked artefacts in the file transfer with the student so the next tutor starts from evidence rather than from scratch.

faqs.question: How should we plan the final two terms before the written papers?
faqs.answer: Plan backwards from the school's internal oral deadline rather than from the written session, because that date is set locally and arrives earlier than families expect. Get it in writing early in DP2. The oral block sits immediately before it; full timed written practice belongs in the stretch after it. Keep the fortnightly marked task running throughout, since it is the only evidence that written production has not slipped while attention was on the oral. Confirm all IB dates with your DP coordinator.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be involved in the recorded oral my child submits?
faqs.answer: No, and the line is worth stating rather than assuming. A tutor rehearses with unfamiliar stimuli or extracts, times the presentation, practises the unseen follow-up questions and reviews recordings against the published criteria. A tutor is not present at the assessed recording, supplies no content for it, and does not script a response. Rehearsal recordings made in a session are practice material, belong in your own file, and go to the school only if you decide to share them.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi schools actually offer Spanish B, and at both levels?
faqs.answer: Several do, often with small numbers and sometimes with Standard and Higher Level sharing a timetable block. Spanish is frequently the second language acquisition option behind Arabic in this emirate, which means cohorts are smaller and individually marked written work is less frequent than in a core subject. Ask the school two questions: whether Higher Level runs this year, and how many pieces of written work are marked per term. The second answer tells you whether outside support is sensible.

faqs.question: Can sessions run in the evening after sport and activities finish?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for families in the sports-heavy communities that is usually the only slot that holds. Evening sessions suit oral rehearsal particularly well, since recorded attempts can be reviewed the following day rather than needing immediate analysis. During Ramadan the pattern shifts again and most Diploma students work best after iftar, so sessions move for the month and return afterwards. The fortnightly marked task should survive both shifts, because it is what keeps the file comparable.

intro.heading: A science that looks like sport on the option sheet and is marked like Biology
paragraphs: SEHS attracts students who play. That is the whole appeal of the subject and the root of the problem it creates. A swimmer in a Khalifa City squad or a footballer in an Abu Dhabi academy arrives knowing an enormous amount about training, recovery, nutrition and injury, all of it acquired practically. The examination does not ask what training feels like. It asks for the energy system supplying a 400-metre effort, the units on a force measurement, the interpretation of a graph of oxygen uptake against time, and a precise explanation of a physiological mechanism in the order a mark scheme expects.

So this page is built on marked work rather than motivation. A SEHS student's grade stalls for identifiable reasons, and from a report card they all look the same. Content gaps, data-question mechanics, extended-response structure and a vocabulary problem each produce a 4. Only marked writing separates them. Every arrangement described here returns criterion-level marks in writing before the lesson, so the question of whether tutoring is working has a documented answer rather than an opinion.

The second thing marked work exposes is timing. Student athletes in Abu Dhabi are often training before school, again after it, and travelling at weekends for fixtures or camps. Revision is squeezed into the gaps and nobody is tracking whether it is doing anything. A weekly timed answer, marked, is a small enough commitment to survive a training schedule and a large enough signal to tell you whether the squeeze is working or whether something has to give. Abu Dhabi families also lose weeks to travel for fixtures and camps, so the plan has to assume absence rather than treat it as a failure, and the marked record is what makes a missed week visible instead of invisible.

The current science guides changed what the subject asks for, which matters when choosing a tutor. SEHS now sits inside the same assessment architecture as the other Group 4 subjects, with a single internally assessed scientific investigation of up to 3,000 words and a collaborative project running alongside it. Material written for the previous specification is still circulating widely, so confirm with your child's IB coordinator which guide the cohort follows and ask any prospective tutor the same question before the first session.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation or endorsement from the IB, from ADEK or from any school or sports body named on this page, and we claim none. What we do is match an Abu Dhabi SEHS student with a tutor who has taught the course, run lessons live online around a training week, and keep the marked evidence where a parent can read it. Parents get the marked scripts, a named target every fortnight, and a straight answer about what can still change in the weeks that remain.

sections.heading: Why a committed athlete can still sit on a 4
paragraphs: The marked scripts tell a consistent story. A student who trains seriously writes about exercise with real authority and loses marks on everything that makes the subject a science. The answer explains that lactate builds up and performance drops, which is true and worth little; the mark scheme wanted the energy system named, the mechanism sequenced, and the effect on force production stated. Authority in the gym does not transfer to the register of an examination answer.

The second recurring loss is in the data questions, and it is the most frustrating kind, because the student usually understands the physiology perfectly. Marks go on quoting values with units, stating the magnitude of a change rather than its direction, showing working, and referring explicitly to the figure provided. Those are mechanical habits. They are also the fastest marks available in the whole subject, because nothing new has to be learned.

The third is sequencing in extended responses. Physiological explanations are chains, and a mark scheme usually awards each link. A student who writes the conclusion first and then justifies it may end up with every fact on the page and half the marks, because the chain was not laid out in order. Teaching that order explicitly, with a handful of standard chains practised until automatic, is the single highest-value thing a SEHS tutor does.

All three are visible in one marked timed answer, which is why a first session should be a marking session. Send a recent data question and an extended response, and the tutor should be able to say which of the three is costing the grade and what the first fortnight targets, in writing.

sections.heading: The themes, the papers and where each one bites
paragraphs: SEHS content sits in three themes: exercise physiology and nutrition, biomechanics, and sports psychology and motor learning, with additional Higher Level material. The written papers sample across all of them, which means a student cannot abandon the theme they dislike. In Abu Dhabi the theme most often neglected is biomechanics, usually because the student is not taking Physics and has decided the moments and projectile material is beyond them. It rarely is.

The table below sets out what each theme demands and where marks go missing, with the practice that fixes it. Confirm the exact paper structure and weightings for your child's cohort with the school, because the science guides were revised and both versions are described in material circulating online. That caution is not pedantry: the difference changes how much of the plan should go on the investigation.

One structural point is worth understanding before you buy any sessions. The internally assessed investigation is a substantial share of the grade and it closes early, usually during Year 13's first term and sometimes earlier. That means the window for useful support on it opens in Year 12. Families who come to us in February wanting investigation help are normally too late, and the money is better spent on data-question mechanics, which can still move marks across every paper.

The Higher Level material deserves its own slot in the plan rather than being folded into general revision. It is the part students have seen least often, it tends to be taught last, and it is examined with the same precision as everything else. We run it as a separate strand from roughly ten weeks out, with its own marked questions.

sections.heading: Data-based questions: the cheapest marks in the subject
paragraphs: If a family can only afford a short block of sessions, this is where to spend it. Data questions are worth a substantial share of the written marks, they appear in predictable forms, and the losses are habitual rather than conceptual. A student who learns five mechanical rules typically picks up marks on every paper for the rest of the course, with no new physiology learned at all.

The rules are unglamorous: always give units; always quote a value from the figure rather than describing its shape; always state magnitude as well as direction; always show working even when the arithmetic is trivial; and always answer the question asked rather than the one the graph suggests. Written out they sound obvious. In marked scripts from strong students they are broken constantly, because nobody has ever made them explicit and tested them.

The table shows the four question forms that recur and what each one awards. We drill them in short bursts rather than long sessions, which also happens to suit a student who trains twice a day. Twenty minutes of data questions, marked, is a better use of a Tuesday than ninety minutes of content revision, and it is far more likely to actually happen in a competition week.

There is a knock-on benefit for the investigation. A student who handles data well in examinations analyses their own data better, and the analysis and evaluation sections are where investigation marks are most often lost. The two pieces of work reinforce each other, which is why we sequence data drills before the investigation block rather than after it.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, milestone by milestone
paragraphs: The investigation is a single report of up to 3,000 words and a significant part of the grade, and its mark is largely determined by decisions taken before much writing happens. SEHS students have an advantage and a trap here. The advantage is access: they can measure heart rate, reaction time, flexibility, perceived exertion and performance on tasks they already do. The trap is ambition, usually a study requiring laboratory equipment they do not have or a sample of participants they cannot recruit.

The table sets out the milestones and, at each one, what a tutor may legitimately do and what the student must do alone. The split matters because academic honesty findings fall on the student. A tutor may teach methods, challenge a question, explain what the criteria reward and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not design the study, supply analysis, rewrite passages into their own prose, or hand over a structure with the content filled in.

In Abu Dhabi there is a practical consideration worth naming early: if the student intends to collect data from teammates or squad members, the school's own consent and safeguarding requirements apply, and so does basic ethics. Participants need to know what is being collected and why, personal data should not be kept longer than needed, and nobody under eighteen should be measured without the school's process being followed. Schools here are increasingly strict about this, and an investigation that ignores it can be stopped late.

Keep every draft. A documented development trail is both the best protection if anyone ever asks how the work was supported and the most useful teaching record there is: a student can see what changed between version one and version four, which is a far better lesson in scientific writing than any explanation of the criteria.

sections.heading: Training load, heat and Ramadan: building a timetable that holds
paragraphs: This is the part of SEHS tutoring that is specific to Abu Dhabi, and it is usually decided badly. A student training before school at five in the morning cannot absorb a demanding lesson at eight in the evening. A student with water sessions at dawn and school until three has an afternoon dip that no amount of discipline overcomes. Choosing the hour correctly is worth more than choosing the tutor correctly, and it is the first thing we ask about.

Heat shapes the year as much as the week. For much of the Abu Dhabi calendar, outdoor training moves to early morning or late evening, which pushes academic work into the middle of the day at weekends. That is workable, but it has to be planned rather than discovered. The same physiology the student is studying — thermoregulation, hydration, the effect of heat on cardiovascular drift — is being experienced in their own training, which is one of the few genuinely enjoyable teaching opportunities in the Diploma and worth using.

Ramadan requires a decision rather than an improvisation. School hours shorten, training moves to the night, and fasting changes energy availability and sleep. For SEHS students the month also supplies a direct link to the nutrition and energy-systems material, and the sensible arrangement is short post-Iftar sessions from around 8.30pm, with longer timed papers moved to weekend mornings. Because Ramadan currently sits inside the revision term for the May session, agreeing this before the month starts protects the most valuable weeks in the course.

Competition travel is the last variable. Students who miss a week should bank marked work before they go rather than attempt to catch up afterwards, and the plan should assume one or two missed weeks a term rather than treating them as emergencies. A schedule built with that slack holds; one built on perfect attendance collapses at the first tournament.

sections.heading: What the evidence folder holds after six weeks
paragraphs: The claim underneath this whole page is that progress in SEHS should be legible to a parent who has never studied physiology. After six weeks of a weekly cycle, the folder contains six marked pieces of work, each written to time, each with a mark against the criteria and a one-line reason, plus a named target per fortnight. Reading it takes ten minutes and answers the question families actually have: is this working.

What movement looks like differs by problem. The mechanical habits — units, quoted values, showing working, sequencing a mechanism — change inside two or three marked pieces, because they are rules rather than judgements. Content gaps take longer, because the material has to be learned and then retrieved under pressure, and that is six to eight weeks of short checks. Extended-response quality is the slowest, since it needs judgement about what to include and what to leave out.

If nothing has moved by week six, something is wrong with the plan, the tutor or the assumption about which problem we were solving, and that conversation should happen immediately rather than in April. We would rather change the match than defend it. The folder makes that conversation factual instead of an argument about impressions.

The folder has a second use that families discover later. When predicted grades are issued and a student in a small cohort thinks theirs is unfair, a run of independently marked timed work is the only evidence that exists outside the school's own view. It does not oblige the school to change anything, but it turns a complaint into a discussion about specific scripts.

sections.heading: What SEHS support costs in the Abu Dhabi market, by provider model
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the published numbers, attributed. Budget online providers list from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour, one platform from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is listed from AED 150, with IB work from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE rates run AED 200 to 450 and above, one UK agency publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. A Dubai rate survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500.

The table compares provider models rather than brands, because that is the decision a parent is actually making. SEHS sits at the upper end of whichever band applies, for a simple reason: the subject is taught in relatively few schools, so the pool of specialists is small, and a Biology tutor covering SEHS is not the same purchase even when the price is identical.

Two questions make quotes comparable. Does the rate include written marking, which is roughly half an hour of work per lesson and the whole source of the evidence you are paying for. And is the rate for online delivery or for a visit, because in-home bands carry the tutor's travel inside the price for identical teaching. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is live online and one-to-one.

We do not publish an IB Gram tariff here. The honest answer is that it depends on the tutor and the number of sessions, and the way to find out whether a particular match is worth paying for is the free trial lesson, which happens before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Permits, school ethics and why your child's coach is not their tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the detail is worth knowing before you hire anybody. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified.

Abu Dhabi adds a rule that matters here more than in most subjects. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way. In a sport-heavy school the obvious candidate is often the student's own teacher or coach, and that is the arrangement to avoid. It is also pedagogically weak: the person who sets the predicted grade is the last person who should be marking the evidence you intend to weigh it against.

A related confusion is worth clearing up. A strength coach, a club physiotherapist or a performance analyst knows a great deal that overlaps with SEHS content, and none of that qualifies them to teach the examination. The subject is assessed on physiology stated in the register of a science paper, on data handling, and on a written investigation marked against published criteria. Practical expertise is a wonderful source of examples and a poor substitute for somebody who has marked the course.

Finally, on materials. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB, and a tutor should cite and link them rather than hand out copies. A provider circulating bundles of restricted material is telling you how they treat rules in general, which is worth knowing in a subject with an internally assessed component attached.

faqs.question: My son plays football seriously and still gets 4s in SEHS. What is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually register rather than knowledge. He knows what training does; the paper wants the energy system named, the mechanism sequenced, the data quoted with units and the explanation written in the order a mark scheme awards. Marked scripts from athletic students follow a pattern: confident, accurate prose that collects about half the available marks because the chain of reasoning is out of order and the figures are described rather than quoted. Those are rules he can learn to apply, and they typically move within two or three marked pieces. One marked data question and one extended response are enough to confirm it.

faqs.question: Which SEHS theme do Abu Dhabi students most often neglect?
faqs.answer: Biomechanics, and almost always because the student is not taking Physics and has decided the forces, moments and projectile material is out of reach. It rarely is. The calculations recur in predictable forms and respond to short, frequent drills with units enforced, rather than to long explanatory sessions. Abandoning a theme is expensive because the papers sample across all of them, so a student who writes off biomechanics has capped their grade before revision starts. Two twenty-minute drills a week for a month usually changes the picture entirely.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor help with a subject built on practical work?
faqs.answer: By working on everything that is actually assessed. The physical activity is not marked; the papers and the written investigation are. Screen sharing covers graphs, calculations, mark schemes and the student's own drafts, which is where the marks are won and lost. For the investigation, the student collects their own data regardless of who is teaching them, and the parts that decide the mark are the question, the method, the analysis and the evaluation. Online delivery also means the specialist is chosen for having taught the course rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do on the SEHS scientific investigation, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach method design, challenge a question that cannot be answered with the equipment available, explain the statistics, explain what the criteria reward, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not design the study, supply the analysis, rewrite passages into their own prose, or hand over a structure with content filled in. The student collects the data and writes every word of the report, inside the 3,000-word ceiling. We keep a record of what the tutor reviewed and advised, and we expect every draft to be kept.

faqs.question: Can my daughter measure her own teammates for her investigation?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the school's consent and safeguarding process has to be followed first, and that is not a formality. Participants need to know what is being collected and why, data about minors should not be kept longer than the study needs, and the school may require written consent from families. Abu Dhabi schools have become notably stricter about this, and an investigation that skips the process can be stopped late, which is the worst possible timing. Raise it with the supervising teacher before any data is collected rather than after.

faqs.question: How do we schedule lessons around 5am swim training?
faqs.answer: By choosing the hour honestly. A student who was in the pool at five is not learning physiology at eight in the evening, whatever the timetable says. For early-training households we usually run short weekday sessions in the late afternoon and move anything long to a weekend morning. The pattern that holds is two short pieces of work a week rather than one long one, because a twenty-minute marked drill survives a fixture weekend and a ninety-minute session gets cancelled. Tell us the training week before the match is made, not afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan during a competition block or a tournament abroad?
faqs.answer: It should already assume one or two missed weeks a term. The practical approach is to bank marked work before travel rather than attempt a catch-up afterwards: the student takes timed questions with them, submits what they can, and the tutor marks on return. Sessions move to holiday and weekend slots during heavy blocks. A plan built on perfect weekly attendance collapses at the first tournament, which is why we ask for the fixture list at the start and build slack into the sequence rather than treating absence as a failure.

faqs.question: Does the recent change to the science guides affect which SEHS tutor we need?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a fair opening question for any candidate. The science courses moved to a common assessment architecture with a single internally assessed investigation reported in up to 3,000 words and a collaborative project alongside it. Material written for the previous specification is still widely available online, and a tutor working from it will allocate effort wrongly, which feels productive and is not. Ask how many cohorts they have taught under the current guide, and confirm with your child's IB coordinator which version the school is registered for.

faqs.question: Is SEHS accepted for sports science or physiotherapy at university?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, but it varies by course and country and it should be checked rather than assumed. Some physiotherapy and biomedical programmes specify Biology or Chemistry and will not accept SEHS as a substitute; sports science, coaching, nutrition and exercise-related degrees often welcome it. Read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on your child's list, including UAE universities, in Year 12 while a subject change is still possible. Nobody should tell you that tutoring is required for admission; that is a claim about a process, not about teaching.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both SEHS and Biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the overlap in respiration, circulation and nutrition makes it efficient. The thing to check is that the tutor keeps the two registers separate. Biology demands terminology tightly keyed to its own specification; SEHS expects the physiology applied to performance, with data handled in a sporting context. The commonest casualty is a SEHS answer written in pure Biology register that never connects the mechanism to the activity. Ask a candidate how they would mark the same respiration answer differently for each course, and listen for a specific answer.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a SEHS student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: The pattern that works is a two or three session diagnostic, a block of six to eight around the investigation in Year 12, and a ten-week run-in of short weekly drills plus one marked paper before the examinations. What matters more than the total is the review point: at week six the marked scores either moved or they did not, and if they did not, the plan or the tutor changes. Open-ended weekly sessions with no target are how families spend a great deal across two years and cannot say what changed.

faqs.question: Can my child's own PE teacher or club coach tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: The teacher at their own school should not, and in Abu Dhabi that is the clear direction of the rules: ADEK's professional-ethics requirements bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their school, and the private tuition permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. A club coach is a different person but usually the wrong teacher: coaching expertise is a good source of examples and no substitute for somebody who has marked the written papers. The value of an outside marker is precisely that they did not set the predicted grade.

faqs.question: Does fasting during Ramadan change how we should plan revision?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing, not the amount. School hours shorten, training shifts to the night, and sleep patterns move, so a 5pm lesson stops being viable. We normally run short post-Iftar sessions from about 8.30pm and move full timed papers to weekend mornings. For SEHS students the month also lines up with the nutrition, hydration and energy-systems material, which makes some of the content unusually concrete. Because Ramadan currently falls inside the revision term for the May session, agreeing the new pattern before it begins protects the most valuable weeks of the year.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the papers. What should the money go on?
faqs.answer: Data-question mechanics first, then standard explanation chains, then Higher Level material as its own strand. Those three are rules and habits rather than new content, they move marks on every paper, and eight weeks is enough to embed them. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild content coverage from scratch, and it is far too late for the investigation, which closed earlier in the year. We would run two marked pieces a week with one named target per fortnight, and review at week four rather than week six given the time available.

That is what the free trial lesson is for, and it happens before any payment. Tell us the predicted grade, the level, the version of the science guide the school follows and what the training week looks like, and we will match an Abu Dhabi student with a SEHS specialist for live one-to-one online lessons in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What you are buying when you book a SEHS tutor in this emirate
paragraphs: An IB DP Sports Exercise and Health Science tutor in Abu Dhabi is quoted at the specialist end of the market, roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, and parents are rarely told why. The reason is supply. This subject runs in a handful of schools in the emirate, often with one class in a year group, and the teachers who have taught it are mostly employed full time in those schools. A parent ringing round for Biology help has a wide field. A parent ringing round for SEHS has a short list and a waiting period.

Difficulty is not what sets the figure. SEHS content is less voluminous than Biology and the mathematics is lighter than Physics. What makes the hours valuable is that the subject is assessed in ways a generalist science tutor handles badly: data-based questions on exercise physiology, extended responses that reward applied examples, and a scientific investigation involving human participants that carries a fifth of the grade. Confirm the exact weighting with your school's IB coordinator, because the group 4 guides changed recently and schools adopted them at different points.

This page prices the subject by component rather than by month. It sets out what each part of the course demands, where Abu Dhabi students lose marks in it, what an investigation review block costs, and what the Abu Dhabi calendar does to scheduling once academy training, school fixtures and Ramadan are in the diary. Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, read in October 2026, and none of it is an IB Gram price list.

Delivery is worth stating before anything else. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work shared on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. For this subject that limitation costs a family almost nothing, because the thing being taught is how to read a graph of oxygen uptake and how to structure an answer, neither of which improves by having a tutor in the room.

A note on who tends to book. Roughly half of our Abu Dhabi SEHS caseload are students training seriously in a sport, often at a club or academy around Zayed Sports City or Al Jazira, who chose the subject because it describes what they already do. The other half chose it as the lighter group 4 route and discovered the papers are not light at all. The two groups need different hours: the first needs writing technique, the second needs physiology taught properly from the start. Knowing which group your child sits in is the cheapest diagnostic available, and it usually takes one marked paper to find out.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-heal.programmesIntro: SEHS is examined only in the Diploma, but the skills it tests are built earlier. Here is what each IB stage contributes for an Abu Dhabi student heading towards this subject, and what support at each stage is realistically for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where SEHS is taught and assessed. Students handle anatomy, exercise physiology, energy systems, biomechanics, skill acquisition and training principles, then produce a scientific investigation of their own design. Written assessment rewards applied examples and precise reading of data; the investigation rewards a method that can actually be run with willing participants and the equipment a school has.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi cohorts for this subject are small and often taught alongside Biology by the same teacher. Students who train at a club or academy frequently need sessions after 7.30pm, which is the single most requested slot in our Abu Dhabi caseload and the first one to fill each term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences and Physical and Health Education together build what SEHS later assumes: a working idea of a controlled variable, a graph that answers a question, and the vocabulary of fitness components. A Year 11 student who has written one properly structured science investigation arrives in DP1 months ahead of one who has not.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school running the Middle Years Programme sits eAssessment, and the difference shows in how formally a student has been taught to write a method. We ask which model the child has sat before deciding whether a DP1 block needs to start with investigation skills.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No link to a SEHS grade, but the habit of measuring something twice and asking why the numbers differ begins here. Primary support in Abu Dhabi is quoted far below Diploma rates and is usually booked for literacy and mathematics rather than for science content.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools under the federal requirement, so Primary timetables here are fuller than the same school's abroad. Session length is set with that in mind.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A natural fit for students combining Diploma courses with a sports or health-related career study. SEHS taken within this route is assessed against the same subject guide, so the tutoring is identical even though the certificate differs.
programmes.countryNote: This route is uncommon in Abu Dhabi, which means families often cannot find anyone nearby who has supported a student on it. Online matching is the practical answer, and it is the clearest instance where distance, not expertise, was the limiting factor.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-sports-exercise-and-heal.subjectsIntro: SEHS students in Abu Dhabi usually book one other subject in the same year. These are the Diploma courses our tutors cover alongside it, with what each one actually assesses and where the overlap helps.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology, energy systems, biomechanics and skill acquisition, plus a scientific investigation using human participants. Marks are lost on data-based questions read too quickly and on extended responses that describe a process without applying it to a named sporting example.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The nearest neighbour and the most common pairing. Respiration, circulation and homeostasis appear in both with different emphasis. A student taking both can revise once and answer twice, provided they learn which subject wants molecular detail and which wants applied performance.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Required alongside Biology by many medical and dentistry routes. Energy and equilibrium are the topics where our Abu Dhabi students most often stall, usually because multi-step calculations are set out in a way the marker cannot follow.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Shares the skill-acquisition and motivation territory of SEHS, with far stricter demands on citing studies. Students taking both benefit from one tutor keeping the evidence standards consistent across their essays.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistical content maps directly onto what a SEHS investigation needs: sampling, correlation, significance and error. A student weak here produces data they cannot interpret, which is the most expensive kind of coursework problem to fix late.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route many Abu Dhabi medicine and engineering applicants are pushed towards. Whether it is the right choice should be decided against the stated requirement of the specific universities on the list, not against reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Biomechanics in SEHS is simplified physics: force, levers, momentum and projectile motion. Students taking both find the SEHS treatment less mathematical and sometimes answer with more rigour than the command term asked for, which costs time rather than marks.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: SL and HL under the current guide
subjects.description: The other small-cohort group 4 option in this emirate, and subject to the same scarcity of specialist teachers. Families comparing the two usually want to know which is lighter; the honest answer is that they are differently heavy.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Writing technique transfers directly into SEHS extended responses. A student who structures a paragraph well in English rarely loses structure marks in a science answer; one who does not, does.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A popular SEHS choice and a common stalling point. Support is process coaching: narrowing the question, checking the data can be gathered ethically from participants, and reading what the student has already written.

sections.heading: What each part of the SEHS course actually demands
paragraphs: Parents are usually told SEHS is the easier group 4 subject and then surprised by the first marked paper. The content load genuinely is lighter than Biology. What is not lighter is the assessment style. The subject asks a student to read data from exercise physiology, interpret it in the language of energy systems or biomechanics, and apply it to a named sporting situation, all inside a command term that sets the shape of the answer.

The pattern in our Abu Dhabi caseload is consistent: students who train seriously in a sport arrive with intuition and lose marks on terminology, while students who chose the subject for its reputation arrive with neither. Both are fixable, but with different hours. The athlete needs writing structure and precise vocabulary. The other student needs the physiology taught properly before any paper technique will stick.

The table below sets out the parts of the course, what each genuinely tests, where marks go missing in this emirate, and what a session can do about it. It deliberately avoids publishing component weightings beyond the investigation, because the group 4 guides changed recently and schools in Abu Dhabi moved to them at different points. Your school's IB coordinator holds the current figures for your child's cohort, and those are the ones to plan against. Read the third column before the second: a parent who knows where the marks are going can judge a tutoring quote in a way a parent looking only at the syllabus cannot, and the losses listed there are the ones we see repeatedly in this emirate rather than a generic list copied from a subject guide.
