sections.heading: Choosing articles when you live in the Gulf
paragraphs: Article selection decides more of the mark than students expect, and living in the UAE is an advantage here that most candidates never use. The regional business press reports specific, dated, quantified economic events constantly: fee decisions, utility pricing, trade corridor changes, labour market rules, sector diversification announcements. Those are far better commentary material than a broad international opinion column, because they contain an identifiable change in an identifiable market.

The tests for a usable article are simple. Is there a specific economic event, not a general trend? Is there at least one number in it? Can you draw the relevant diagram from what the article says? Is the publication date recent relative to when you are writing? Is the source different from the ones used for your other commentaries? An article failing the first or third test should be discarded immediately, however interesting it is.

What students should avoid is the article that is really about politics, sport or technology with an economic sentence attached. The commentary has to analyse economics, and an article whose economic content is one paragraph forces the student to supply the economics from elsewhere, which reads as generic under criterion C. The other trap is an article so comprehensive that it already contains the analysis, leaving the student to paraphrase.

Local knowledge also helps evaluation. A student in Abu Dhabi writing about a regional utility price change can discuss the distributional effect on households in a way that is grounded rather than theoretical, and can question whether the article's framing captures it. That is criterion E material that a candidate reading the same story from a distance cannot produce.
bullets: A specific, dated economic event, with at least one number in it
A diagram you can draw from what the article actually says

Three different publications across the three commentaries

sections.heading: Evaluation inside 800 words
paragraphs: Criterion E is worth three marks and is the criterion most often lost to arithmetic rather than to thinking: the student wrote 700 words of application and had 100 left for evaluation. The structural fix is to allocate the words before writing. Roughly 150 for context and the diagram's setup, 350 for application and analysis, 150 for the key concept doing real work, and 150 for evaluation leaves a commentary that scores across all five criteria instead of three.

Good evaluation in 150 words is prioritised rather than balanced. Listing an advantage and a disadvantage is not evaluation; stating which effect dominates and why, under what assumption, and what would change the conclusion, is. Short run against long run is the most reliable structure available in this space, because almost every economic intervention has a different effect over different horizons and saying so takes two sentences.

The second reliable move is to question the article itself. Its data may be a single quarter, its framing may suit a particular interest, its claim may rest on an assumption about elasticity that nobody states. A student who identifies that assumption and says what happens if it fails is doing exactly what the criterion asks for, and is also using material no other candidate has.

The third is the key concept. Criterion D and criterion E reinforce each other: a commentary whose key concept reappears in the evaluation, shaping the judgement rather than decorating the introduction, tends to score well on both. A commentary where the concept appears once in the opening sentence usually scores one out of three on D and little better on E.

sections.heading: What an Economics tutor may and may not do with a commentary
paragraphs: Each commentary is assessed work and must be the student's own. The IB treats a breach as malpractice affecting the whole Diploma, not one subject grade. There are providers in this market advertising finished coursework, and a family buying a commentary is buying a risk to the award. The line is worth stating in detail here, because Economics commentaries are short enough that the temptation to supply a paragraph is unusually strong.

A tutor may teach the economics, screen an article for viability, check a diagram label by label, mark a draft against the five criteria, point out that an evaluation lists rather than judges, explain why a term is being used loosely, demonstrate a diagram on an article the student is not using, and help plan the allocation of units and key concepts across the portfolio. A tutor may also say that a commentary is good enough and needs no further sessions.

A tutor may not supply the text, draw the student's diagrams for them, select the article on their behalf or rewrite a paragraph into a better version to be pasted. The student clicks the mouse on their own diagram. That sounds pedantic and it is the practical line that keeps the work theirs, particularly in a task where a tutor could produce a competent 800 words in twenty minutes.

Keep the article itself, with its publication date, attached to each commentary as the school requires, and keep dated drafts. A portfolio where each commentary can be traced from article to plan to draft to final version is the strongest evidence of authorship a student can hold, and building it as you go costs nothing.
bullets: A tutor screens, teaches, checks diagrams and marks against the criteria
A tutor never writes text, draws the diagram or selects the article
Attach each article with its publication date, as your school requires
Keep dated drafts for all three commentaries as evidence of authorship

sections.heading: Timing across two years, Ramadan, and what it costs per commentary
paragraphs: The portfolio is written across more than a year, which makes it the only IB internal assessment where the scheduling question is about spacing rather than about a single deadline. Schools in Abu Dhabi typically set commentary one in DP1, commentary two near the end of DP1 or early in DP2, and commentary three in DP2 before the heaviest paper revision. Working back from the school's dates, the useful rhythm is article chosen two weeks before each deadline, diagram and plan one week before, draft written and marked with a week to spare.

Ramadan shifts the evening across the emirate: school days shorten and the usual late-afternoon slot stops working, so sessions move to post-iftar timing rather than pausing. If a commentary deadline falls inside Ramadan, the practical move is to choose the article before it starts, since article hunting is the part of the task that needs the most unbroken attention. Students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside should note that UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the Cambridge February and March series is offered in India only.

On cost, the natural unit for this task is the commentary rather than the hour. Two sessions per commentary, six across the portfolio, spread over more than a year, is a very different purchase from six sessions in one month, and a family can stop after the first commentary if the marks improve on their own. Published UAE rates, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 survey putting IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and BartyED at AED 650 for a named tutor. Those are their figures, not ours.

Our own position: we quote after the free trial lesson, and for most portfolios we recommend buying commentary by commentary rather than committing to the full six sessions upfront. If commentary two scores well without us, there is no reason to book for commentary three.

process.title: Tell us where the portfolio stands
process.description: Which commentaries are written, which are marked, which units and key concepts are already used, and the next deadline. Those four facts let us say how many sessions the rest of the portfolio needs and whether an Economics specialist is free.

process.title: Plan all three in the free trial
process.description: The first lesson is free and goes on the allocation grid: units against key concepts against the kinds of article each will need. A student who leaves with that grid rarely has the commentary three problem of writing with whatever options remain.

process.title: Screen the article, then build the diagram
process.description: For each commentary, the article is tested before writing and the diagram is drawn before the text. Both decisions shape the analysis, and both are far cheaper to change at this point than after 800 words exist.

process.title: Mark the draft out of fourteen
process.description: Each criterion scored separately, with the reason, sent to the family in writing. The student rewrites. Marks on diagrams and terminology usually move immediately, which makes the first marking session the most productive one.

process.title: Carry the lesson into the next commentary
process.description: The point of marking commentary one is commentary two. We record what was lost and why, and start the next commentary from that note, which is the difference between three separate pieces and a portfolio that improves.

whyPoints.title: Planned as a portfolio, not three essays
whyPoints.description: Units, key concepts and sources interlock, and students who allocate them deliberately avoid the commentary three trap of writing with whatever is left. That planning session is the cheapest hour in the task.

whyPoints.title: Diagram marks treated as marks
whyPoints.description: Nine of the portfolio's marks sit in criterion A across three commentaries, and they are lost to unlabelled axes rather than to economics. We check diagrams the way a marker does, label by label, before the text is written.

whyPoints.title: Word allocation before writing
whyPoints.description: Evaluation is three marks per commentary and the first thing to disappear when a student writes long. Allocating the 800 words in advance is what keeps criterion E from being squeezed out by criterion C.

whyPoints.title: Marked cold, criterion by criterion
whyPoints.description: Each draft is marked out of fourteen by someone who does not already know what the student meant, which approximates moderation better than a familiar teacher's read. The mark and the reason go to the family in writing.

whyPoints.title: Buy per commentary
whyPoints.description: The portfolio runs over more than a year, so there is no reason to commit to six sessions upfront. Two sessions on commentary one, then a decision. Families who stop after one commentary because the marks held up are a normal outcome.

whyPoints.title: Local articles used properly
whyPoints.description: Gulf business coverage supplies specific, dated, quantified events that make better commentary material than broad international columns, and gives a student grounded evaluation that a distant candidate cannot write.

faqs.question: How many commentaries are in the IB Economics portfolio?
faqs.answer: Three. Each is a maximum of 800 words, each draws on a different unit from the first three of the syllabus, each uses a different key concept from the nine the course specifies, and each is based on a different published article from a different source. Each commentary is marked out of 14 across five criteria, and the three together are worth thirty per cent of the Economics grade at Standard Level and twenty per cent at Higher Level. The school marks them and the IB moderates the marking externally.

faqs.question: How many marks does each Economics commentary carry?
faqs.answer: Fourteen, split across five criteria: diagrams worth three, terminology worth two, application and analysis worth three, the key concept worth three, and evaluation worth three. The distribution is worth knowing before writing, because five of those fourteen marks, in diagrams and terminology, are available for technical care rather than for economic insight. A commentary with sharp analysis, an unlabelled diagram, loose terms and a rushed evaluation typically scores around half of what the student was capable of.

faqs.question: How recent does the news article for a commentary need to be?
faqs.answer: Recent relative to when the commentary is written, not when the portfolio is submitted. That distinction matters because the portfolio spans more than a year: an article chosen in DP1 for the first commentary stays valid even though the portfolio is handed in much later. What does not work is reaching back for a story that was already old when the student found it. Record the article's publication date and the date the commentary was written on the commentary itself, as your school requires.

faqs.question: Can two commentaries use the same key concept?
faqs.answer: No, and the restriction is one students meet painfully late. Each of the three commentaries uses a different key concept from the nine available, which means using the most obvious concept on the first commentary leaves the harder ones for later. The same applies to the syllabus units and to the publications the articles come from. Allocating all three commentaries deliberately at the start, with a simple grid of units against concepts, is the single most useful piece of portfolio planning available and takes about twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Why did my child's commentary lose marks on diagrams?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly for labelling rather than for economics. Criterion A requires both axes labelled with the variable and its unit, every curve labelled including its position after a shift, the direction of the shift shown, the original and new equilibrium identified, the diagram numbered, and the text explaining what the diagram shows about the article. Drafts routinely fail two or three of those. The errors are mechanical, and students who have them pointed out once rarely repeat them, which makes this the most efficient marking any commentary receives.

faqs.question: What makes a good article for an Economics commentary in the UAE?
faqs.answer: A specific, dated economic event with at least one number in it, in a market whose diagram the student can draw from what the article says. Gulf business coverage is unusually good for this: utility and fee decisions, labour market rules, trade corridor changes and sector announcements are reported concretely rather than abstractly. What to avoid is a broad opinion column, or a story that is really about politics or technology with one economic sentence attached, because the student then has to supply the economics from elsewhere.

faqs.question: How should the 800 words be divided up?
faqs.answer: Roughly 150 words for context and the diagram's setup, 350 for application and analysis, 150 for the key concept doing real analytical work, and 150 for evaluation. Allocating before writing is what protects criterion E, which is three marks and the first thing to vanish when a student writes long and then trims. The opposite problem, a commentary that comes in well under the limit, usually means the key concept was named rather than used, which costs under criterion D as well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or redraw part of a commentary?
faqs.answer: No. Commentaries are assessed work and must be the student's own, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice affecting the whole Diploma. A tutor may teach the economics, screen an article, check a diagram label by label, mark a draft against the five criteria, explain why an evaluation lists instead of judges, and demonstrate a diagram using an article the student is not using. A tutor may not supply text, draw the student's diagram or choose their article. In an 800-word task that line needs stating explicitly.

faqs.question: Is the portfolio worth the same at SL and HL?
faqs.answer: No. The three commentaries are identical in specification, word limit, criteria and marks at both levels, but the portfolio is worth thirty per cent of the final grade at Standard Level and twenty per cent at Higher Level, because HL students also sit an additional policy paper. That makes portfolio marks proportionally more valuable to an SL student. For an HL student there is a second benefit: the evaluative habit the portfolio builds is exactly what the HL policy paper rewards, so the work is not confined to its own marks.

faqs.question: Are Economics IA sessions online or at our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Commentary work is document and diagram work, so a shared screen is the right tool: the article open in one window, the student's diagram in another, and the criteria alongside. A family in Abu Dhabi also gets a tutor who has marked commentaries against these five criteria rather than whichever economics teacher is available within an evening's drive.

faqs.question: What does Economics portfolio help cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026: AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where travel is priced in, and AED 650 at one provider for a named tutor. Those are their figures, not ours. The more useful unit here is the commentary: two sessions each, spread across more than a year, with a decision point after every one. We quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: My child's first commentary scored poorly. Can the portfolio recover?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more easily than in most IB internal assessments, because the three commentaries are marked separately and two are still unwritten. A low first mark that names a criterion is genuinely useful information: if diagrams cost the marks, that is a one-session fix applied to both remaining commentaries; if evaluation was squeezed out, the word allocation changes. What makes recovery harder is a first mark nobody has decoded, which is why the marked commentary is the first thing we ask to see.

faqs.question: Does the key concept have to appear throughout the commentary?
faqs.answer: It has to do analytical work, which in practice means appearing more than once and shaping the argument. Criterion D is three marks, and the commonest loss is a concept named in the opening sentence and then abandoned while the commentary does ordinary analysis. The strongest commentaries bring the concept back into the evaluation, so that the judgement is made through the concept rather than alongside it. That also lifts criterion E, which is why these two criteria tend to rise and fall together.

faqs.question: How do commentary deadlines interact with Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the usual late-afternoon session slot stops working, so we move to post-iftar timing rather than pausing. If a commentary deadline falls inside Ramadan, the practical step is to choose and screen the article beforehand, because article hunting needs more unbroken attention than drafting does. Diagram work and marking both sit comfortably in a shorter evening session, so a commentary can be finished during the month without the student carrying the search alongside fasting and a compressed school day.

faqs.question: What if no Economics specialist is available before the deadline?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting a general humanities tutor. Commentary marking against the five criteria is a specific skill, and internal deadlines cluster across Abu Dhabi schools, which concentrates demand into the same fortnights. The honest alternatives are a later session with written feedback on the draft in the meantime, a tutor outside the emirate on a compatible evening schedule, or using the school's own clinic time with a precise list of questions about diagrams and the key concept. A poor match on assessed work is worse than a short delay.

abu-dhabi/ib-economics-ia-help.closingHeading: Plan the three before you write the first
abu-dhabi/ib-economics-ia-help.closingBody: The Economics portfolio rewards planning more than any other IB internal assessment, because its constraints interlock and most of them cannot be undone once a commentary is submitted. Send us which commentaries exist, which units and key concepts are already used, and the next deadline, and the free trial lesson will produce the allocation grid for the rest. If the marked commentary names a criterion, bring it: a single mark lost on diagrams is usually a one-session fix that pays for itself twice over the two commentaries still to come.

abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are listed by subject and level, with the components they work on in the final phase. In exam season the match that matters is paper experience in that specific subject, because a generalist spends the first fortnight learning the assessment shape your child is three months away from sitting.

intro.heading: Price the phase, not the hour
paragraphs: Parents searching for IB exam preparation in Abu Dhabi are usually asking a cost question underneath the subject question. They have been quoted an hourly rate, sometimes two very different ones, and they cannot tell what either number buys. The hourly rate is the least informative figure in this market. What decides the bill is how many weeks you buy, in how many subjects, at which phase of the final year, and whether the hours are spent on something the remaining time can actually change.

The final year of the Diploma divides into phases that behave differently and cost differently. There is the pre-mock phase, where content gaps can still be closed and an hour of teaching is cheap relative to what it returns. There is the mock-aftermath phase, where the useful work is diagnosis and reallocation. There is the study-leave phase, where sessions get shorter, more frequent and more expensive per hour of calendar time because slots are scarce. And there is the week before each paper, which is worth almost nothing to buy and a great deal to plan.

Rates in this emirate are not a mystery either, they are simply unpublished by most providers. Rate trackers and provider pages put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visiting work at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee, and premium named tutors above that again. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market observations from October 2026, attributed to the sources that published them, and they are not IB Gram's price list.

What a family can control is allocation. Six subjects plus the core is more surface area than any budget covers properly, so the spending decision is really a triage decision: which two or three subjects have the most recoverable marks per hour, which ones are safe enough to leave alone, and which are so far behind that money spent there buys a smaller grade change than the same money spent elsewhere. That judgement needs a marked paper, not a conversation.

So this page is organised as a spend plan. It sets out what each phase is worth, what the market charges for it, the four ways exam-season money is most reliably wasted in Abu Dhabi, how to read a mock before you buy anything, and what the November session costs a family who decides a subject needs a second attempt. Every figure is labelled with where it came from. Where we do not have a sourced number, including for examination entry fees, the page says so and points you at the body that sets it.

abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Exam preparation means something different at each stage of the IB continuum, and the cost profile changes with it. Three stages matter to an Abu Dhabi family planning spend across the school years rather than just the final term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment with no external written papers for most students, so exam preparation here is really preparation for being examined later: timed writing under pressure, reading a criterion as a specification, and keeping a usable set of notes. Money spent in MYP 4 and 5 is the cheapest exam preparation a family will ever buy, because it is preventative.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families often move children into the Diploma from MYP within the same school, which hides the size of the step. The jump that catches candidates here is the shift from criteria written in sentences to mark schemes that reward specific command-term behaviours, and a few hours in the final MYP year is the least expensive way to meet it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, assessed through internal work completed across two years and written papers sat at the end. Exam preparation spend concentrates in the second year, and the allocation question is which of the six subjects returns the most marks per hour once the internally assessed components are already submitted.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates in this emirate normally sit the May session, which puts the heaviest spending window in the first months of the calendar year. Abu Dhabi's school calendars, Ramadan timings and study-leave arrangements all land inside that window, which is why the plan is built against the family's real availability before any hours are priced.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and course candidates
programmes.description: Students taking individual IB courses rather than the full Diploma, or combining IB courses with a career-related study, still sit the same external papers in those subjects. The budget is usually smaller and more focused, often a single subject where a grade is needed for a specific university or progression requirement.
programmes.countryNote: This is the group most likely to be quoted for a short, single-subject block in Abu Dhabi, and the group for whom the phase question matters most: buying six weeks before the paper and buying six months before it are different products at a similar hourly rate.

abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are where Abu Dhabi families most often concentrate final-phase spend, with a note on what the written papers reward. Confirm the exact components and weightings for your child's course in the current subject guide the school issues, because these are revised between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual first call on an exam-season budget, because its lost marks are patterned and recoverable: method marks sacrificed by writing no working, proof questions abandoned at the first line, and calculator papers attempted without the calculator strategy the paper assumes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Rewards modelling and interpretation in context, which candidates trained on pure technique find harder than the algebra. Final-phase hours go on reading a scenario, choosing a model and justifying the choice in writing rather than on computation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in the extended-response and data-analysis questions, where candidates who know the physics lose marks for not quoting values from the graph or stating an assumption. Uncertainty treatment is a finite, drillable gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the recurring content gaps, but the faster recovery is usually in command-term discipline: stating an observation where the paper asked for an explanation costs marks on knowledge the candidate already has.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes re-reading feel productive and practice feel punishing, which is why the marks sit in precise terminology and in data questions where the trend is described without the figures that earn the mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is an examinable skill: axes labelled, the correct curve shifted, the new equilibrium marked. Evaluation marks are the other recoverable block, lost by candidates who analyse thoroughly and then stop before judging.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward application to the specific organisation in front of the candidate. Generic answers that would fit any firm score in the lower bands, and that habit is correctable inside a few weeks of focused practice.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Written papers reward a controlled argument about how a text produces meaning, not a summary of what it says. Final-phase work is mostly timed essay practice with annotated marking against the assessment criteria.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study recall is finite and therefore cheap to finish, while the expensive gap is evaluation: candidates describe a study accurately and then fail to say what it fails to show. Short repeated drills move this faster than content revision.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: By the final phase these are usually submitted and the mark is fixed, which matters for the budget: money spent here late buys nothing. Where they are still open, support is feedback on the student's own draft and nothing beyond that.

abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: In exam season the scarce resources are evening slots and the student's own energy, and both vary by community. These are the Abu Dhabi areas families most often book from, with the scheduling point each raises once study leave begins.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Small Diploma cohorts and wide subject spreads, so a household often needs two different HL specialists rather than one generalist. Morning slots during study leave fill first here, which is worth booking before April.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Activity-heavy weekday evenings mean the realistic slot is often 19:30 or later, and the lesson recording gets used more than anywhere else. Short twice-weekly sessions outperform one long block in this pattern.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with both parents working, so sessions are booked around commutes rather than around school. Families here most often ask for a fixed weekly slot locked for the whole exam term rather than rolling bookings.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Long school runs across the mainland corridor already consume the late afternoon, which is why the pre-mock phase here is usually bought as weekend mornings and the study-leave phase as weekday mornings.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Dense, central and close to several large schools, so group revision is easy to find and individual diagnosis is not. The spend question here is usually whether to add one-to-one work on top of what the school already provides.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Established family areas with multiple children in the same household, where the budget is being split across siblings in different year groups. A single shared schedule planned once saves more than negotiating the hourly rate.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Zayed City
regions.note: Newer communities a long way from the island, where a visiting tutor's travel would be inside the fee. In the final phase that travel cost competes directly with the number of sessions the same money buys.

schoolClusters.city: The island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Established Diploma provision with internal mock timetables set early in the calendar year, which is what fixes when diagnostic spending is useful. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland
schoolClusters.note: Larger year groups and broader option blocks, so subject combinations differ widely between households in the same street and a single spend plan rarely transfers from one family to the next.

sections.heading: What IB exam preparation costs in Abu Dhabi, phase by phase
paragraphs: The direct answer: a specialist IB tutor working online in this market is quoted in the region of AED 200 to 450 an hour, a qualified non-specialist subject tutor AED 150 to 300, and premium named tutors above that. A rate tracker's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All of those are market figures published in October 2026 by providers and trackers, not IB Gram prices, which are quoted after a diagnostic.

The number that decides your bill, though, is the number of hours, and that follows the phase. A pre-mock block in two subjects at one session a week for ten weeks is twenty hours. A post-mock diagnostic across four subjects is eight to twelve hours and then stops. A study-leave clinic in one subject at four short sessions a week for three weeks is around nine hours. Those are very different totals at a similar hourly rate, and families who negotiate the rate while leaving the hours unplanned usually spend more.

The phase also changes what the money buys per mark. Content teaching before the mock is cheap per mark because the candidate still has time to consolidate. Diagnosis after the mock is the highest-value purchase in the whole year, because it decides where everything else goes. Technique work in study leave is narrow but reliable. The week before a specific paper is close to worthless to buy and genuinely valuable to plan, which costs nothing.

sections.heading: Four ways exam-season money gets wasted here
paragraphs: The first is paying for content re-teaching after the mock. Once the mock script shows that marks are being lost to working omission, command-term misreading and timing, buying more content coverage treats the wrong fault at full price. This is the single most common exam-season purchase in this market and the one with the weakest return, because it is also the easiest thing for a tutor to sell and to deliver.

The second is buying hours in the subject the family worries about most rather than the subject with the most recoverable marks. Worry is not evidence. A candidate frightened of Physics and quietly losing fifteen reachable marks in Economics should be spending on Economics, and only a marked script says so. Spreading hours evenly across six subjects is the same error in a politer form.

The third is the two-hour minimum. In-home visiting work in this emirate is commonly quoted at two hours, because the travel has to be worth the trip, and market rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour include that travel. In exam season, four forty-five-minute sessions beat one two-hour visit for technique work, because technique is built by frequent correction. Paying for the length of a session that exists to justify a drive is paying for the drive.

The fourth is late spending on components that are already closed. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are usually submitted before the final phase, and once submitted the mark is fixed. Hours bought against them buy nothing. A provider who takes that booking without saying so is selling calendar time, and the honest answer costs them the hours.
bullets: Content re-teaching after a mock that diagnosed a technique fault

sections.heading: Reading a mock script before you release a budget
paragraphs: A mock percentage is the least useful artefact the school will give you, and it is the one most families buy tutoring from. Two candidates on 54 can need completely different interventions costing completely different amounts. The script tells you which, and it tells you in four categories: marks lost to content not known, marks lost to technique on content that was known, marks lost to timing, and marks lost to question selection or misreading.

Those four categories price differently. Content gaps are the most expensive to close and the slowest. Technique faults are cheap, fast and transfer across every paper in the subject. Timing is a two or three session fix. Question selection is often a single conversation. A script with eighteen marks in the technique and timing categories is a far better purchase than a script with eighteen marks of missing content, at the same hourly rate.

So the order is: get the scripts, have them marked against the published scheme, categorise the losses, then decide the budget. A diagnostic of eight to twelve hours across four subjects, bought once, routinely reduces the total spend because it closes two subjects down. Families who skip it tend to buy a flat weekly commitment in four subjects for twelve weeks and never find out which two mattered.
Ask the school for the scripts rather than the grades. Schools in this emirate vary in how readily they release them, and it is worth asking early, before the mock rather than after it.

sections.heading: The November session and the cost of a second attempt
paragraphs: Where one subject is clearly not going to land, a family's real options are to spend more on it now, to accept the grade, or to plan a retake in a later session. That last option has a cost structure most providers never discuss, and it is worth setting out before the May papers rather than after the results. A retake means a further entry through a centre, a further period of tutoring at the same market rates, and a delay to whatever the grade was needed for.

Diploma candidates in Abu Dhabi normally sit the May session, and a November sitting exists as an alternative. We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and an unverified date on a fee-paying decision is worse than no date. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly, and plan the retake decision around what they confirm.

The entry fee question gets the same treatment. Examination entry is handled through the school as the centre, or through an approved centre for a candidate entering independently, and those bodies set the fees. We do not quote figures we have not read on the setting body's own page. Ask the coordinator for the entry cost, the deadline and whether the school will enter a candidate for a later session at all, because not every school does.

The decision table below is the one to fill in with your own numbers once the coordinator has answered. It is deliberately short, because the arithmetic is simple as soon as the three unknowns are filled in.

sections.heading: What you are entitled to ask before paying anything
paragraphs: Exam season is when providers are least likely to be questioned and most likely to be paid in advance, so it is the right time to be awkward. There are five questions that cost nothing to ask and change what you buy. Which exact components of this subject has the tutor taught before. Will a marked script be produced in the first fortnight. What happens to unused hours. Who is actually teaching, as opposed to who appears on the website. And what is the stated limit of what these weeks can do.

The fifth is the one that separates a tutor from a salesperson. Nobody can promise a grade or a point improvement, and any provider promising a particular score, a fixed rise in points, or money back against a result is describing something they cannot control. The honest version is a written statement of what the remaining weeks can address and what they cannot, produced after the diagnostic and before the hours are committed.

The permit question is also legitimate and easy to ask. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules also indicates that Abu Dhabi school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school, which is a reason to be wary of any arrangement marketed that way.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. Any provider claiming such status is making a specific factual claim that can be checked with the body named.

sections.heading: Exam-season scheduling in Abu Dhabi, and what it does to the price
paragraphs: Slot scarcity is a cost even when the hourly rate does not move. In the months before the May session, the best tutors in the most-requested subjects fill their Gulf Standard Time evenings first, and a family arriving in March is choosing from what is left rather than from the whole pool. Booking a fixed weekly slot in January for a May sitting is not an upsell; it is the difference between the specialist and whoever is still free at 18:00.

The Abu Dhabi calendar then reshapes the plan. Ramadan shortens school days and moves usable study time for many households to after Iftar, so sessions run from roughly 21:00, shorter and more often. Study leave inverts the pattern entirely: mornings become the right slot, because papers are sat in the morning and practising at 10:00 is itself rehearsal. Half-term travel and public holidays remove weeks that a plan drawn in a spreadsheet still contains.

That is why the schedule is agreed before the content plan. We ask which weeks are genuinely available, counting travel, Ramadan, holidays and the school's own mock and study-leave windows, and build against that figure. Twelve calendar weeks is frequently nine working weeks, and a plan priced against twelve is a plan that will overrun into the papers themselves.

One practical consequence of video delivery is worth naming here: when a family travels between Abu Dhabi and elsewhere during the exam term, the lesson follows the laptop. That removes the most common reason a programme loses two weeks in the middle.

sections.heading: Coursework at this stage, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: By the exam-preparation phase most internally assessed work is submitted, and a mark that has been submitted is fixed. Where a component is still open, the boundary is the same as it is in any other month. Your child writes the work. A tutor teaches the underlying skill, explains the criteria, asks questions about a plan, and gives feedback on a draft the student produced. No text is supplied, nothing is edited to completion, and no model is handed over to be adapted.

The reason to state this on a cost page is that exam-season pressure is exactly when the request gets made and when a provider is most tempted to take the money. The IB treats work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student. In a market where at least one provider openly sells finished internal assessments, a family paying for legitimate support deserves to be told where the line sits before they ask.

The auditable version is simple. The student sends the draft they wrote. The tutor returns questions and criterion references rather than replacement sentences. Every version is retained, so the development of the piece can be shown if the school asks how it was supported. That trail is the same whether the school asks in week two or after submission, and it is the only form of coursework support worth paying for.
Where the deadline has passed, the honest answer is that the hours belong to the written papers now. Saying so reduces the bill, which is why it is worth asking any provider the question directly.

sections.heading: Delivery, coverage and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Sessions for Abu Dhabi families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, the paper on screen and the session recorded for rewatching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. On a cost page the merits of that are easy to state, because they are mostly arithmetic.

Travel is inside an in-home fee whether or not it is itemised, which is why market rates for visiting work run to AED 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online specialist, and why visits are quoted in two-hour minimums. Removing the drive converts that money into sessions. It also widens the pool from whoever can reach your community at a fixed hour to whoever teaches the exact component your child needs, which in HL Physics or HL Economics is a materially different set of people.

The limit is honest coverage, and it is disclosed before you book. If no tutor who has taught your child's exact component has hours free in the window you need, you are told, and offered a named alternative with the trade-off stated: a second specialist on Gulf Standard Time from another country, a split of the subject across two tutors with one shared record, reallocation to a subject where the match is right, or a later start.

process.title: Send the subjects, levels and the weeks that are real
process.description: The useful opening message lists the six subjects with their levels, the ones in trouble, whether mocks have been sat, and which weeks are genuinely available after travel and school commitments. That is enough to say which phase you are in and what it is worth buying.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A single sixty-minute session at no charge, with the tutor you would keep, before any payment. It is one lesson rather than a trial week, and it exists to check the match on the component and to set the first timed paper section.

process.title: Mock scripts marked, then an allocation plan
process.description: Scripts are marked against the published scheme and the losses are categorised as content, technique, timing or selection. The written plan names which subjects get hours, which do not, and the ceiling the remaining weeks support. Families often buy fewer hours after this than before it.

process.title: Book the phase, with an end date
process.description: Hours are bought as a block with a stated end point rather than as an open weekly commitment, and the block is reviewed against evidence before the next one. That structure is what stops exam-season spending from running on past the point where it changes anything.

process.title: Review at the block boundary, not at the paper
process.description: At the end of each block the topic sheets show whether the subject is responding. Hours are moved, reduced or stopped on that evidence. Where the evidence says stop, that is the recommendation, and it is given in writing rather than left for the family to infer.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The bands on this page come from published provider pages and rate trackers in October 2026 and are labelled as market observations. What your own plan costs is quoted after the diagnostic, because an exam-season quotation given before anyone has seen a script is guesswork with a decimal point.

whyPoints.title: The diagnostic can reduce the order
whyPoints.description: Marking mock scripts across four subjects regularly closes two of them down. A provider paid by the hour has no incentive to tell you that, which is precisely why the diagnostic is sold as a discrete piece of work with its own end point rather than bundled into a term.

whyPoints.title: Phases are priced separately because they behave differently
whyPoints.description: Pre-mock content hours, post-mock diagnosis and study-leave technique clinics return different amounts per hour. Quoting one blended rate for the whole year hides that, and hiding it is how families end up buying content teaching in the week before a paper.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: There is no promised grade, no point-improvement figure and no refund tied to an outcome on this page, and no satisfaction percentage either. What is offered instead is a marked script, a tracked topic sheet and a written statement of what the weeks left cannot change.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on your child's own draft, keeping every version so the trail is auditable. Where a component is already submitted, you are told the mark is fixed and the hours are redirected to the written papers.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If the right specialist is not free in the window you need, you hear that with a named alternative and its trade-off, rather than being matched to whoever had the slot. In exam season that single disclosure is worth more than any discount on the hourly rate.

faqs.question: What does IB exam preparation actually cost for an Abu Dhabi family over a final term?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on hours than on rate. Applying published market bands of AED 150 to 450 an hour, a ten-week pre-mock block in two subjects comes to roughly AED 3,000 to 9,000, a one-off diagnostic across four subjects AED 1,200 to 5,400, and a three-week study-leave clinic in one subject AED 1,800 to 5,400. Rate trackers put specialist exam-year monthly support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a weekly hour. Those are October 2026 market observations rather than our prices, which follow the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for tutoring once the internal assessments have already been submitted?
faqs.answer: For the written papers, yes, and that is where the hours should go. For the submitted components, no, because a submitted mark is fixed and hours bought against it buy nothing. This matters because the final phase is when families often ask for internal assessment help and when providers are most willing to take the booking. The first question to ask any provider is which components are still open, and the honest answer frequently reduces the hours they can sell you.

faqs.question: Which phase of the final year gives the most grade movement per dirham spent?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis immediately after the mock, by a clear margin, because it decides where every later hour goes and often closes two subjects down entirely. Pre-mock content teaching is next, since there is still time for new knowledge to consolidate. Study-leave technique work is reliable but narrow. The week before a paper is close to worthless to buy. A family that spends eight to twelve hours on diagnosis and allocates the rest on evidence usually spends less overall than one that commits to a flat weekly block in four subjects.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child needs content teaching or exam technique work?
faqs.answer: Only the marked script tells you, and the two cost very differently. Blank or abandoned questions on identifiable topics mean content, which is the slowest and most expensive gap to close. Correct ideas scoring partial marks, missing working, described trends without quoted figures and full answers to a question the paper did not ask all mean technique, which is cheap, fast and transfers across every paper in the subject. A mock percentage cannot distinguish between the two, which is why buying from a percentage tends to buy the wrong product.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring quoted higher per hour in Abu Dhabi than online tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the travel is inside the fee whether or not it is itemised. Market rates for visiting work run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online specialist, and visits are commonly quoted with a two-hour minimum so the drive is worth making. In exam season that matters twice over: the length of the session is set by the journey rather than by what technique work needs, and four short sessions a week beat one long visit for correcting habits. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child's predicted grade changed before the school submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change a prediction, because the prediction belongs to the school. What recent marked evidence can do is give a teacher something concrete to reconsider, which is a different and smaller claim. Schools set forecasts from classwork, mocks and recent assessments, so the useful material is a marked past paper and a tracked topic sheet produced before the school's own forecast deadline rather than after it. Ask the Diploma coordinator when that deadline falls, because evidence arriving afterwards has no route into the decision.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB exam and results dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, and that is deliberate. The IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and an unverified date on a page families make paid decisions from is worse than no date at all. Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session. Confirm the exact windows, the results date and any November arrangements with your child's Diploma coordinator or directly on ibo.org, and build the spending plan around what they confirm.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to retake one IB subject in a later session?
faqs.answer: Two separate costs, and we only have a sourced figure for neither, so here is the honest version. Entry is handled by the school as the examination centre, or by an approved centre for an independent candidate, and those bodies set the fee and the deadline. Tutoring for the retake is priced at the same market bands as any other block, typically AED 200 to 450 an hour for a specialist. Ask the coordinator for the entry fee, the entry deadline and whether the school will enter a candidate for a later session at all, since not all do.

faqs.question: Should I spread the budget across all six subjects or concentrate it?
faqs.answer: Concentrate it, and let a marked script decide where. Spreading hours evenly is the most common exam-season error because it feels fair and treats every subject as equally recoverable. In practice two subjects usually hold most of the reachable marks, two are safe enough to leave alone, and one or two are too far behind for the weeks available to change. The written allocation plan should name all of those categories explicitly, including the subject being deliberately under-resourced, so the decision sits with you rather than with the tutor's diary.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi family book for a May sitting to get the tutor they want?
faqs.answer: Before the end of January for a fixed weekly evening slot, and earlier for Higher Level sciences. Slot scarcity is a real cost even when the rate does not move: the most requested specialists fill their Gulf Standard Time evenings first, and a family arriving in March is choosing from what remains rather than from the whole pool. Booking early is not an upsell, it is the difference between the right specialist and the available one. Where you are already in March, expect to trade preferred timing for subject match, and take the match.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change exam-season sessions in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the usable study window for many households moves to after Iftar, so sessions shift to around 21:00 and run shorter and more often. For exam technique that is usually an improvement, because frequent correction beats long exposure. Study leave then inverts the pattern, with mornings becoming the right slot since papers are sat in the morning and practising at that hour is itself rehearsal. We ask in the first week which weeks are genuinely available, counting Ramadan, travel and public holidays, and price the plan against that number rather than the calendar's.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and do you publish a tax registration number?
faqs.answer: Any quotation you receive will state plainly whether the figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and that is the limit of what this page says on the subject. The VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE depends on the supplier and the service, and we do not state a general tax position without a Federal Tax Authority citation to support it. The market AED bands reproduced here are taken from providers' own published figures, which may themselves be quoted on different bases, so treat them as ranges rather than as comparable net prices.

faqs.question: Are the tutors permitted to teach privately in the UAE, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask any provider directly about the permit position of the person who will teach. IB Gram itself holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership and does not claim one.

faqs.question: What happens to hours I have paid for if my child's exam timetable changes?
faqs.answer: Ask that question of every provider before paying, because the answers differ widely and exam season is when it matters. The arrangement worth having is one where hours are bought as a block with a stated end date, unused hours carry or are refunded on terms written down in advance, and rescheduling inside a stated notice period is free. Where a provider cannot answer plainly, treat the ambiguity as a price. Our own block structure exists for this reason: a block with an end point can be reviewed and stopped, an open weekly commitment cannot.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's Higher Level subjects to reduce the cost?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but it should not be the deciding factor. Mathematics and Physics is the most common workable pairing, and Economics with Business Management is another. What does not work is pairing two subjects where the assessment shapes are unrelated, because the saving in coordination is lost to a weaker match on both components. If a single tutor is genuinely strong on both, the shared context helps. If not, two specialists with one shared progress record is the better purchase at the same total hours.

abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Get the scripts, then set the budget
abu-dhabi/ib-exam-preparation.closingBody: The question worth answering before you spend anything is not what an hour costs. It is which two of your child's six subjects hold the marks that the remaining weeks can actually reach. One free diagnostic lesson and a set of marked mock scripts answer it, and the written allocation plan that follows names the subjects getting hours, the subjects that do not need them, and the ceiling those weeks support. Send the subject list, the levels and the weeks you genuinely have. If the plan that comes back is smaller than the one you were expecting to buy, that is the useful outcome.

abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below support Extended Essay work for Abu Dhabi Diploma students on live video. They are not supervisors — that role belongs to the school — and they do not write. What they do is test a research question against the criteria, name the criterion a draft is failing, and keep the record.

intro.heading: The question decides the grade before a word is written
paragraphs: Almost every weak Extended Essay is a well-written answer to a question that could not be argued about. 'How did the oil industry change the UAE economy' is a topic, not a question: a student can write four thousand competent words on it and every one of them will be description, because the question invites narration rather than analysis. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve of the thirty-four available marks, and a descriptive essay cannot access most of them no matter how fluent its prose or how extensive its bibliography.

That single fact reorders the whole project. The most valuable hour in an Extended Essay is spent before any research begins, testing whether the proposed question has an answer somebody could disagree with and whether that answer can be reached within four thousand words. An Abu Dhabi student who arrives at a drafting session with a narrow, arguable question is in a different position from one arriving with four thousand words about a broad one, and the second student cannot be rescued by editing.

The second misunderstood element is the reflection process. The Extended Essay requires reflection sessions with the school supervisor, recorded on a form, and those reflections are themselves assessed under criterion E, engagement, which carries six marks. Students routinely write them in a rush the day before a deadline, describing what they did. The criterion rewards evidence of the student's own intellectual initiative and of decisions taken during the process, which cannot be reconstructed convincingly after the fact, however carefully the final evening is spent.

The third is the forty hours. The Extended Essay is designed as roughly forty hours of work spread across a year, and that is a planning figure rather than a guideline. Compressed into three weeks it produces a piece with a bibliography assembled from the first page of results and no evidence that anybody thought about anything. Spread properly it produces the narrowing, the reading, the change of mind and the reflections that criteria C and E both reward. The forty hours get spent either way; the only question is which stages receive them, and that is a sequencing decision a family can make in September of Diploma Year 1 for nothing.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For Extended Essay work this is the right medium: comments sit in the margin of the student's own document, every version is saved and dated, and a family in Khalifa City or on Saadiyat Island works with someone who has read the criteria for their registered subject rather than with whoever is available nearby.

abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.programmesIntro: The Extended Essay runs across both Diploma years and the useful help differs completely by stage. These are the four points at which an Abu Dhabi family might reasonably intervene.

programmes.name: Choosing the subject, early in Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is registered in a subject, and that choice constrains everything afterwards: the criteria are interpreted through subject-specific guidance, the kinds of evidence that count differ, and some subjects are far harder to do well at this length than others. Choosing badly is the first available mistake and the least recoverable.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools differ in how much choice they offer and in which subjects they will supervise. Ask the coordinator which subjects the school actually supports before a student commits to one, because a subject with no available supervisor is not a real option however well it suits the student.

programmes.name: Narrowing the question, Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: The highest-value stage and the shortest. A broad question is narrowed until it has an answer somebody could dispute and until that answer is reachable in four thousand words. One or two sessions, done before reading in earnest begins, changes the ceiling of the entire essay.
programmes.countryNote: The long Abu Dhabi winter break falls at a useful point for this stage, because narrowing requires reading around a topic without a deadline attached. It is also the three weeks of the two-year course most commonly spent on nothing at all.

programmes.name: Drafting and the reflection sessions, into Diploma Year 2
programmes.description: Reading, structuring, and the recorded reflection sessions with the school supervisor. Support here reads the current draft against the criteria and names what is missing. The reflections are the student's own and happen with the supervisor; a tutor should not participate in them or write them.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay deadline in most Abu Dhabi schools falls well before the final examinations and frequently collides with Internal Assessment deadlines. Ask for the school's full internal deadline schedule in writing, because the collisions are predictable and a plan can avoid them.

programmes.name: Arriving late, with a draft and a deadline
programmes.description: The most common moment a family looks for help and the hardest to serve honestly. With four thousand words written around a broad question and three weeks remaining, the realistic options are narrowing the argument inside the existing material or accepting the grade. Both should be stated plainly rather than implied.
programmes.countryNote: No specific IB submission or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date here has been confirmed from the IB directly. The school's internal deadline is the one that binds, and the coordinator holds it.

abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.subjectsIntro: The Extended Essay is registered in a subject, and the subject determines what counts as evidence and what a strong question looks like. These are the registrations Abu Dhabi students most commonly choose.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: A popular registration and a demanding one
subjects.description: Requires a question with genuine historiographical disagreement and sources a school student can actually access. The characteristic failure is a question about a well-documented event that has one accepted answer, which leaves criterion C nothing to reward however thorough the research.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: Strong for students who can find data
subjects.description: Works well where a specific market or policy can be examined with real figures and an economic model applied to it. Fails when the question is about an entire economy, because four thousand words cannot support a claim at that scale and the essay becomes a summary of press coverage.

subjects.name: Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Needs either an experiment the student can actually run with available apparatus or a dataset they can genuinely obtain and analyse. The most common failure is discovering in Diploma Year 2 that the planned measurement is not possible, which is a feasibility question that belonged in Year 1.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: A narrower registration than students expect
subjects.description: Requires mathematics at or beyond the level of the course, developed rather than described. An essay that explains a known result accurately without doing anything with it reads as a textbook chapter, which is precisely the failure criterion C punishes most heavily.

subjects.name: English and other Language A subjects
subjects.description: Needs a question about method rather than about meaning, and a text set narrow enough to analyse closely. Students who choose three novels and a theme produce comparison at a level of generality that cannot support close reading, and close reading is what the criteria reward.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Built on published studies rather than on the student's own experiment, which makes the question's precision the whole battle. A broad question about a phenomenon produces a literature summary; a question about a specific explanatory claim produces an argument.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Works where a real organisation and real data are available and the question applies a management framework to a specific decision. Fails where the only available material is the organisation's own promotional publishing, which cannot support an evaluative argument.

subjects.name: Geography and Environmental Systems
subjects.description: Strong where a student can collect primary data in a reachable location, which in Abu Dhabi offers genuine local material. The constraint is access and timing: data that can only be collected in a season already past is not available data.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: Requires a genuinely global issue examined through two disciplines, with both disciplines doing real work. The failure is an essay that is substantively one subject with a paragraph of the other attached, which scores as neither.

subjects.name: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre
subjects.description: The essay is an analytical piece of writing rather than creative work, which surprises students who chose the subject for the practical element. The question still has to be arguable and the evidence still has to be analysed rather than described.

abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so a student works with someone who knows the criteria for their registered subject rather than with whoever lives nearby. What the area changes is the local material a question can realistically use and when a long reading session can happen.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Villa communities with long bus routes, which means the forty hours mostly have to come from weekends rather than weekday evenings. Planning the hours against a weekend rhythm is more realistic here than assuming a nightly stretch.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Short commutes and apartment living. Extended Essay work needs a screen and a document rather than silence, so an after-school reading and drafting slot is practical in a way a timed paper would not be.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cultural institutions and a concentration of mature Diploma programmes. For arts, history and World Studies registrations there is genuine primary material within reach, which matters for criterion C because a question with accessible evidence can actually be argued.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zeina
regions.note: Growing residential communities with long internal travel. Geography and environmental registrations relying on primary data collection need the site and the season checked before the question is fixed, and distance is part of that check.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and the Corniche
regions.note: Established schools with early supervisor allocation and well-published internal deadlines. Families here usually know the dates, which means the plan can be built backwards from them rather than around a guess.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Longer commutes and a wide curricular mix, with students who have transferred into the Diploma from other systems. A transferring student often needs the whole Extended Essay process explained before any question is discussed.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Al Ain
regions.note: Greater distances and, in Al Ain, a separate school ecosystem under the same emirate regulator. Online delivery matters most here, because a tutor who has read the criteria for a specific registered subject is not a local resource.

sections.heading: The criteria, and where twelve of the marks actually are
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is marked out of thirty-four across five criteria and graded on a letter scale. Criterion A covers focus and method, criterion B knowledge and understanding, criterion C critical thinking, criterion D presentation and criterion E engagement. The distribution is the part students and families almost never know: criterion C carries twelve marks, more than a third of the total and more than twice any other single criterion except where two are equal.

Knowing that redirects effort immediately. Students default to criterion B, knowledge and understanding, because reading and summarising feels like the work of a research essay and produces visible progress. Criterion B carries six marks. A student who reads extensively, understands thoroughly and argues nothing has secured the smaller prize and forfeited the larger one, and the essay will read as competent and score modestly for reasons nobody will have warned them about.

Criterion D, presentation, carries four marks and is the cheapest set of marks in the Diploma. Consistent referencing, a bibliography in a single format, pagination, a contents page, tables and figures labelled and referred to in the text. It is an afternoon of work and students lose marks on it routinely because it feels administrative. It is administrative, and it is scored.

Criterion E, engagement, carries six marks and is assessed through the reflections rather than through the essay. That makes it the only criterion a student cannot address while writing the essay itself, and the only one that cannot be reconstructed at the end, because the reflections are supposed to record decisions as they were taken. A student who writes all three reflections the night before the deadline has given away six marks for a reason that has nothing to do with their essay.

sections.heading: Narrowing a question until it can be argued
paragraphs: Narrowing is a specific operation rather than a matter of taste, and it can be demonstrated. Start with the test: could an informed person disagree with the answer? If the answer is obviously yes or obviously no, or if there is one accepted answer, the question will produce description. Then the scope test: can the answer be reached in four thousand words with evidence a school student can obtain? If reaching it requires three case studies and a literature review, it cannot.

The operation itself is a sequence of restrictions. Restrict the scope — one firm rather than an industry, one text rather than three, one decade rather than a century, one measurement rather than a phenomenon. Restrict the claim — from whether something mattered to whether a specific mechanism explains a specific outcome. Then introduce the disagreement explicitly, so that the question names the thing being weighed rather than the thing being described.

A worked example makes it concrete. 'How has tourism affected Abu Dhabi' is a topic with no answer. 'To what extent has visitor numbers growth at a named cultural institution changed the composition of local employment in its immediate area' is narrow, arguable and probably not researchable by a school student. 'To what extent does the pricing strategy of one named local operator reflect price discrimination rather than cost differences' is narrow, arguable, and answerable with obtainable data. The third version can access criterion C; the first cannot.

The reason to do this before reading is that reading follows the question. A student with a broad question reads broadly, accumulates fifty sources, and then cannot use most of them. A student with a narrow question reads narrowly, finds the two or three sources that actually bear on their claim, and has room in four thousand words to argue with them. The narrowing session therefore saves more hours than it costs, which is rare in this subject.

sections.heading: The reflections: six marks nobody plans for
paragraphs: The Extended Essay process includes reflection sessions with the school supervisor, recorded on a form, and those recorded reflections are assessed under criterion E, engagement, which carries six of the thirty-four marks. The form has a tight overall word allowance across all three reflections, which means every sentence has to carry something. Most students treat it as paperwork and write all three at the end, which is the single most avoidable loss in the component.

What the criterion rewards is evidence of the student's own intellectual engagement: decisions they took, difficulties they met, directions they abandoned and why. 'I continued my research and found more sources' records nothing. 'I had intended to compare two firms but the second published no usable figures, so I narrowed to one and shifted the question toward pricing' records a decision, a reason and a consequence, and it is the kind of sentence the criterion exists to credit.

That is why the reflections cannot be reconstructed convincingly. A student who writes them all on the final evening has to invent a process, and invented processes read as generic because the specific difficulties have been forgotten. The practical remedy is small: keep a running note of decisions during the work, three or four lines each time something changes, and draft each reflection shortly after the session it belongs to.

One boundary point matters here. The reflection sessions are with the school supervisor, and the reflections are the student's own account of their own process. A tutor should not participate in those sessions, should not present themselves as a supervisor, and should not draft reflection text. What a tutor can legitimately do is explain what criterion E rewards and remind a student to keep the running note, which is the difference between helping with a process and taking part in one that belongs to the school.
