sections.heading: Choosing the registration subject
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is registered in a subject and the criteria are applied through that subject's guidance, which makes the registration a strategic decision rather than a preference. Three things should drive it. Whether the student can find an arguable question in that subject. Whether the evidence that question needs is obtainable. And whether the school can actually supervise it, which in a smaller Abu Dhabi cohort is a real constraint.

Some registrations are harder than students expect. Mathematics requires mathematics at or beyond the course level, developed rather than explained, and an accurate account of a known result reads as a textbook chapter. Business management depends entirely on access: where the only available material is an organisation's own promotional publishing, there is nothing to evaluate. Visual arts, music and theatre essays are analytical pieces of writing rather than creative work, which surprises students who chose those subjects for the practical element.

Some are more forgiving. Economics works well when a specific market or policy can be examined with real figures. Geography and environmental systems reward primary data a student can genuinely collect, and Abu Dhabi offers material here. History is strong where genuine historiographical disagreement exists and the sources are reachable, and weak where the chosen event has one settled account.

World Studies deserves a separate note because students choose it for the wrong reason. It is an interdisciplinary registration requiring a global issue examined through two disciplines with both doing real analytical work. Chosen because a student cannot decide between two subjects, it produces an essay that is substantively one subject with a paragraph of the other attached, and it scores as neither. Chosen deliberately, with two disciplines genuinely needed to answer the question, it is a strong option.

sections.heading: Forty hours, counted backwards from the school's deadline
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is designed as approximately forty hours of student work, and the only useful way to plan it is backwards from the school's internal deadline rather than forwards from today. Abu Dhabi schools set their own submission dates ahead of the IB's upload schedule, they differ between schools, and the Extended Essay deadline frequently collides with Internal Assessment deadlines in two or three subjects. Those collisions are predictable, which means they are avoidable.

The backwards plan has a shape. Submission date. Before it, a week for presentation: referencing made consistent, bibliography in one format, figures labelled, contents page, proofreading. Before that, the final draft and the last reflection. Before that, the main writing period. Before that, the reading that follows the question. Before that, the narrowing. And at the start, the registration decision and supervisor allocation. Each stage has a date, and the dates are set by counting backwards rather than by hoping.

The common Abu Dhabi failure is that the first half of that sequence is compressed into nothing. A student registers a subject, picks a broad topic, does no narrowing, reads for months without a focus and then writes four thousand words in the final fortnight. The forty hours were spent; they were spent on the wrong stages, and criterion C and criterion E both suffer for reasons that are entirely about sequencing.

One practical note about this emirate's calendar. The long winter break sits at a useful point in Diploma Year 1, when narrowing and preliminary reading are the right activities and there is no competing deadline. It is the most commonly wasted three weeks in the two-year course. Through Ramadan, work shifts to post-Iftar hours and output drops, which should be built into a backwards plan rather than discovered in it.

sections.heading: The boundary: supervisor, tutor, and what each may do
paragraphs: The Extended Essay has a supervisor and that supervisor is appointed by the school. The relationship is formal: the supervisor conducts the reflection sessions, signs the form and knows the student's work. A tutor is not a supervisor, should not present themselves as one, and should not take part in the reflection process. Confusing the two roles damages the student's own record, because criterion E is assessed on the student's account of a process the school witnessed.

Within that limit a tutor can do a great deal that is useful. Test a research question for arguability and scope. Explain what each criterion rewards and what it is worth. Read a draft and name the criterion it is currently failing. Ask the questions that expose a descriptive passage: what is the alternative explanation here, and why is yours better? Teach the subject content or the method the essay needs. Mark a draft against the criteria and say what band it currently sits in.

What a tutor must not do is supply text. That includes the subtle version: editing a paragraph until it reads well produces the editor's sentences, and a student who submits them has submitted work that is partly not their own without anybody intending malpractice. The defensible method is comments written as questions and criterion references, with the student performing every rewrite themselves, in the session or afterwards. It is slower and it is the only version that survives a question about provenance.

The consequence of getting this wrong falls on the student. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against them, and a grade E in the Extended Essay or in Theory of Knowledge is a failing condition for the Diploma, which makes this component one where the downside is the qualification rather than a mark. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750 and the same market sells Extended Essays. Confirm the current failing conditions with the school's IB coordinator, and refuse the offer whatever the price.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi specifics: ADEK, deadlines and who may be paid to help
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK appears on none of the competitor pages found in this research, which is a conspicuous absence on pages written for Abu Dhabi families, and it is the authority whose framework a school's own academic policies sit within.

The deadline a family works to is the school's. Abu Dhabi Diploma programmes set internal Extended Essay submission dates ahead of the IB's upload schedule, and those dates vary between schools. More usefully, they are published: ask the IB coordinator in writing at the start of Diploma Year 1 for the Extended Essay deadline and the Internal Assessment schedule together, because the single most avoidable crisis in this component is a collision between the two that was visible twelve months in advance.

One rule specific to this emirate affects how help is arranged. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than read from ADEK's current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication; the practical implication is that paying a child's own supervisor for additional help may not be permitted and should not be proposed.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated generally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, applied for through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs, and what to refuse
paragraphs: This is a small purchase done properly. One or two question sessions, two or three draft readings, and possibly one triage session: five or six hours across a year rather than a weekly commitment. Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The Bestimate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650.

Measured per mark the arithmetic is unusually favourable, because the Extended Essay contributes to the three bonus points available from it and Theory of Knowledge together, and because criterion D is four marks of pure presentation available for an afternoon's work. A single question session that converts a descriptive essay into an arguable one moves the piece across criterion C's twelve marks, which no comparable number of hours spent anywhere else in the Diploma can do.

The in-home comparison runs as it does elsewhere in this market: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. For Extended Essay work online is also the correct format, because the whole method is margin comments on the student's own file with versions kept. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

Four things to refuse. A written Extended Essay, at any price, because a grade E here is a failing condition and the malpractice finding lands on the student. A promised grade, which no provider controls since the essay is externally assessed. An editing or polishing service, which quietly produces somebody else's sentences. And a bundle of exemplar essays, which is both a copyright matter and a route to work that is not the student's. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, operates no UAE office, and references rather than reproduces IB material.

The student rewrites it themselves, several times, and every version is kept with its date. This is the highest-value hour in the whole component.

process.title: Start the running decisions note

whyPoints.title: Narrowing is taught as an operation
whyPoints.description: Restrict the scope, restrict the claim, name the disagreement, check the evidence is obtainable, test against criterion C. Five steps the student performs on their own question, with every version kept and dated, rather than advice to be more focused.

faqs.question: Why do well-written Extended Essays still get mediocre grades?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is not what carries the marks. The essay is marked out of thirty-four across five criteria, and criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve of them — more than a third of the total. A descriptive essay answering a broad question cannot access most of those marks however well the prose reads or however extensive the bibliography. Students default to criterion B, knowledge and understanding, which carries six marks, because reading and summarising feels like research. They secure the smaller prize and forfeit the larger one, usually without having been told the distribution.

faqs.question: How narrow does an Extended Essay research question need to be?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough that an informed person could disagree with the answer, and narrow enough that the answer can be reached in four thousand words with evidence a school student can actually obtain. Apply three restrictions: scope, from an industry to one firm, from a century to one decade, from three texts to one. Claim, from whether something mattered to whether a specific mechanism explains a specific outcome. And disagreement, so the question names the thing being weighed. A question failing any of the three will produce description regardless of how well it is written.

faqs.question: Where does legitimate Extended Essay help stop in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth agreeing in writing first. A tutor may test the question for arguability and scope, explain what each criterion rewards and what it is worth, read a draft and name the criterion it is failing, ask the questions that expose a descriptive passage, teach the subject content or method, and mark a draft against the criteria. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the question or participate in the reflection sessions, which belong to the school supervisor. The rewriting is always the student's.

faqs.question: What is the Extended Essay reflection form and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is the record of the reflection sessions a student holds with their school supervisor, and it is assessed under criterion E, engagement, which carries six of the thirty-four marks. The word allowance across all three reflections is tight, so every sentence has to do work. The criterion rewards decisions taken, difficulties met and directions abandoned, with reasons — not an account of continuing to research. Written all in one evening at the end it reads as generic, because the specific difficulties have been forgotten. A running note of decisions during the work is what makes it writable.

faqs.question: How many hours should an Extended Essay take?
faqs.answer: Around forty hours of student work spread across a year, and the spread matters as much as the total. The common failure is spending the forty hours on the wrong stages: registering a subject, choosing a broad topic, reading for months without a focus, then writing four thousand words in a fortnight. A backwards plan from the school's deadline allocates roughly two to four hours to narrowing, twelve to fifteen to focused reading, fifteen to writing the argument, two spread across the reflections, and four or five to presentation in the final week.

faqs.question: Which subject should an Abu Dhabi student register their Extended Essay in?
faqs.answer: One where three things hold: an arguable question exists, the evidence that question needs is obtainable, and the school can actually supervise it. That third item is a real constraint in smaller Diploma cohorts and should be checked with the coordinator before a student commits. Some registrations are harder than they look: mathematics requires mathematics developed rather than explained, business management depends entirely on access to real information, and visual arts, music and theatre essays are analytical writing rather than creative work, which surprises students who chose those subjects for the practical element.

faqs.question: Is World Studies a good Extended Essay choice?
faqs.answer: It is a strong option chosen deliberately and a weak one chosen by default. World Studies requires a genuinely global issue examined through two disciplines, with both disciplines doing real analytical work on the question. Students who choose it because they cannot decide between two subjects produce an essay that is substantively one subject with a paragraph of the other attached, and it scores as neither. Students who choose it because the question genuinely cannot be answered within one discipline have a good registration. The test is whether removing one discipline would break the argument.

faqs.question: What are the cheapest marks available in the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Criterion D, presentation, which carries four marks for consistent referencing, a bibliography in one format, labelled figures referred to in the text, pagination and a contents page. It is an afternoon of work and students lose marks on it routinely because it feels administrative rather than academic. It is administrative and it is scored, and four marks out of thirty-four is a meaningful fraction of a grade boundary. Schedule a presentation week deliberately in the backwards plan rather than leaving it to the final evening alongside everything else.

faqs.question: Who sets the Extended Essay deadline in an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: The school, ahead of the IB's own upload schedule, and the school's date is the one a family must work to. It varies between schools in the emirate. More usefully, it is published, so ask the IB coordinator in writing at the start of Diploma Year 1 for the Extended Essay deadline and the Internal Assessment schedule together. The most avoidable crisis in this component is a collision between the two, and that collision is visible twelve months in advance to anyone who asked for both dates at once.

faqs.question: What happens if the Extended Essay is graded E?
faqs.answer: A grade E in the Extended Essay or in Theory of Knowledge is a failing condition for the Diploma, which makes this component one where the downside is the qualification rather than a single mark. That is also why the Extended Essay is the worst possible place to buy written work: a malpractice finding lands on the student and the exposure is the Diploma itself. Confirm the current failing conditions with the school's IB coordinator, since award rules are revised and no date or rule on a tutoring page should be relied on without checking.

faqs.question: My child has written 4,000 words on a broad question with three weeks left. Can it be saved?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer should be given in writing rather than implied. One triage session reads the whole draft and reports what can be narrowed inside the existing material — sometimes an arguable question is already latent in one section and the essay can be restructured around it — and what cannot be fixed in the time. Sometimes the recommendation is to secure criterion D's presentation marks, submit, and spend the remaining weeks on examinations. That is a legitimate outcome and a provider unwilling to say it is selling optimism.

faqs.question: Can my child's Extended Essay supervisor be paid for extra help in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask the school before proposing it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than read from ADEK's current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication. The supervisor relationship is in any case a formal school role and separate from any paid arrangement.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Done properly it is a small purchase: one or two question sessions, two or three draft readings, possibly one triage session — five or six hours across a year rather than a weekly commitment. Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. A provider proposing a weekly Extended Essay commitment is proposing the wrong shape for a component designed as forty hours of the student's own work.

faqs.question: Does online Extended Essay support work as well as in person?
faqs.answer: For this component it is the better format. The method is comments written as questions in the margin of the student's own document with the criteria visible alongside, and every version saved and dated so the narrowing of the question is part of the record. That record is what makes drift visible and what demonstrates the thinking was the student's own. It does not survive a home visit and a paper draft. The published cost difference also runs one way: AED 180-350 for qualified in-home work against AED 150-300 online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for our Extended Essay subject?
faqs.answer: You should be told, because the criteria are applied through subject-specific guidance and a tutor who has not read it cannot name what a draft is failing. Niche registrations run short — mathematics, music, theatre, a Group 2 language, World Studies with an unusual discipline pairing — and the honest options are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. All three beat generic essay coaching applied to a subject-specific component. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit.

abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.closingHeading: Spend the first hour on the question
abu-dhabi/ib-extended-essay-help.closingBody: If you buy one hour of Extended Essay help, buy it before your child reads anything. Apply two tests to their question: could an informed person disagree with the answer, and can that answer be reached in four thousand words with evidence a school student can obtain. A question that fails either test will produce a descriptive essay, and criterion C's twelve marks are largely unreachable from there. Get the school's deadline in writing, start a running note of decisions for the reflections, and ask any provider to state in writing what they will not do.

intro.heading: What Higher Level actually adds, and how you would know
paragraphs: Higher Level is not Standard Level with more homework. It is a longer course with more content, usually an extra paper or a longer one, and a different distribution of where the marks sit. The IB's own guidance recommends around 240 teaching hours for a Higher Level course against around 150 for a Standard Level one, and that ninety-hour difference is not padding. It buys topics the Standard Level student never meets and a depth of question the Standard Level paper never asks.

So the level decision should be made on mechanics and evidence rather than on a sense of a student's ceiling. Mechanics means knowing what the Higher Level version of that specific subject adds: an extra investigative paper in Mathematics, a quantitative paper in Economics, extension topics in Psychology and Biology, additional depth study and an extra paper in History, an extra written component in English. Those are concrete additions, and whether a student can meet each one is a more answerable question than whether they are strong at the subject.

Evidence means marked work, and the useful evidence is more specific than a grade. From IGCSE, component marks rather than overall grades, because a strong grade built on the questions a student always gets right while the long multi-step questions go unattempted is exactly the profile that struggles at Higher Level. From MYP, criterion marks separated out, with the analytical and investigative criteria read most closely, because those are the ones the Higher Level additions lean on hardest. Averages hide the signal.

One more piece of mechanics worth holding on to. Both levels are graded on the same one-to-seven scale, so a Higher Level 5 and a Standard Level 5 look identical on a certificate, and universities read the level alongside the grade rather than the grade alone. That is why published prerequisites name a subject at a level. A student heading for a 7 at Standard Level and a 5 at Higher Level therefore has a real decision rather than a cosmetic one, and the answer turns on whether any course they want actually specifies the Higher Level.

The most valuable evidence of all arrives after the decision, in the first four weeks of Year 12, and almost nobody uses it. By week four the student has marked work on genuine Higher Level material. If the marks on that work are low because content is missing, that is fixable. If they are low because the student cannot sustain the kind of reasoning the Higher Level question asks for, that is the level being wrong, and the school's level-change window is usually still open. We review at week four for exactly that reason.

IB Gram delivers this guidance, and the teaching that follows it, as one-to-one online sessions on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For a level decision the online format is what makes a specialist read possible at all: the person who can tell you what a Higher Level Physics extended-response answer is missing is a Physics teacher, and in Abu Dhabi, with fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, that person often does not live within a drive of your community.

abu-dhabi/ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.programmesIntro: The level decision looks different depending on where the student is coming from, because each route supplies different evidence. Here is what each stage gives you to work with.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject grade is built from externally marked papers plus an internally assessed component, and the Higher Level version of a subject typically carries an additional or extended external component. The levels are not interchangeable: Higher Level content includes material Standard Level does not cover at all.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set their own level-change windows within the registration calendar, and in practice the window for changing level is later than the window for changing subject. Ask the IB coordinator in writing for both dates in the first fortnight of Year 12, because that single email is what converts a week-four realisation into a cheap correction.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria on an eight-point scale, with the Personal Project in the final year. The criterion profile is the best pre-Diploma evidence available, because it separates what a student can analyse from what they can recall, and the Higher Level additions in most subjects lean on analysis rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: For an Abu Dhabi student moving from MYP to DP in the same school, the subject teacher already holds the evidence. Ask for criterion-level marks across the final year rather than a summary judgement, and ask specifically about the criteria concerned with analysis, investigation and evaluation.

programmes.name: IGCSE entry route
programmes.description: Many students in this emirate arrive at the Diploma from IGCSE, which supplies externally marked component data. An Extended-tier Mathematics performance, or a Physics 0625 profile separating theory from practical, gives a sharper read on Higher Level readiness than any school report does.
programmes.countryNote: Ask for component marks and the tier. A strong Extended-tier grade earned with the long algebra questions left unattempted and a strong grade earned by working through them describe very different students, and only one of them should be choosing Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses taken as individual certificates alongside a career-related study, with Personal and Professional Skills, service learning and a reflective project. The certificates are graded 1 to 7 in the same way, and the Higher Level and Standard Level distinction applies to them in exactly the same way.
programmes.countryNote: Where the honest evidence says a student cannot carry three Higher Levels, this is one of the alternatives worth examining rather than forcing a combination that will need propping up for two years. Provision is thinner in Abu Dhabi than full Diploma provision, so availability has to be checked rather than assumed.

abu-dhabi/ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.subjectsIntro: This is what Higher Level physically adds in each subject, which is the information the level decision actually turns on. Where an extra component exists, it is named.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an extended investigative paper alongside substantially more content in calculus and proof. The evidence of readiness is not speed at routine questions but whether a student can follow an unfamiliar multi-step argument without being shown each turn. That shows in marked work within three weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an extended modelling paper and deeper statistical content. Readiness shows in written interpretation rather than calculation: a student who computes correctly and then cannot say what the result means will find the extra paper punishing.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: HL adds content and extends papers
subjects.description: Higher Level adds substantial organic and energetics material and lengthens the calculation chains. Readiness shows in whether multi-step calculations survive an early error, which is visible in any marked set of questions and invisible in a grade.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: HL adds content and extends papers
subjects.description: Higher Level extends the mathematical demand as much as the physics. The readiness signal is in extended-response answers: whether the student writes the reasoning steps the mark scheme pays for, or states a correct conclusion and stops.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The Higher Level additions are mostly volume, which makes the readiness question one of retrieval stamina rather than analytical ceiling. A student who knows the content and cannot produce it precisely under time will find Higher Level a larger version of the same problem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The additional Higher Level paper is quantitative, which catches students who chose Economics to avoid mathematics. Readiness is testable directly: give the student past quantitative questions and read the marked result, which takes one session.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: HL adds a depth study and a paper
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a regional depth study and an additional paper, so the reading and writing volume rises sharply. Readiness shows in how much usable argument a student can produce in forty-five minutes, which is countable rather than impressionistic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: HL adds a written essay component
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an essay component and raises the analytical demand on unseen texts. For a student who entered English-medium education recently, this is the level decision that most changes the weekly workload across the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Higher Level adds extension content to each approach and raises the evaluative demand. Students routinely revise the core approaches thoroughly and the extensions barely, so readiness is partly about study discipline rather than ability.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level adds extension material and more demanding application to stimulus. Readiness shows in whether a student applies a framework to the case or merely names it, which is the difference between the analysis bands and the knowledge bands.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Higher Level demands more extended production in the required text types and a more demanding oral. Readiness is best read from marked writing corrected at sentence level rather than from classroom confidence.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.levels: HL raises the volume of submitted work
subjects.description: The Higher Level difference is quantity and sustained development of submitted work rather than an extra examination. Readiness is about consistent production over two years, which is a different question from talent and a more reliable predictor.

regions.note: The most established Diploma provision, so Higher Level and Standard Level groups in the same subject usually both exist, which makes a level change administratively straightforward rather than disruptive.

regions.name: Khalifa City

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach

regions.name: Saadiyat Island

regions.name: Yas Island

regions.name: Al Ain

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen

sections.heading: The extra component: what each Higher Level physically adds
paragraphs: The single most useful thing to know before making a level decision is what the Higher Level version of that specific subject adds, because the answer is different in every subject and it is concrete. In Mathematics, both routes add a third paper at Higher Level, an extended piece of investigative or modelling work. In Economics, Higher Level adds a quantitative paper. In History, Higher Level adds a regional depth study and a further paper. In English A, Higher Level adds a written essay component. In Psychology, Biology and Business Management, the addition is extension content layered onto the existing papers rather than a new paper.

That distinction between a new component and extension content matters, because they fail differently. A new component is a new skill: a student can know all the content and still score badly on an extended investigative paper, because following an unfamiliar argument under time is a separate capacity. Extension content fails in a more ordinary way, through under-revision, because students revise the core they met first and run out of time before the extensions. The first is a readiness question. The second is a study-discipline question, and it is more fixable.

The practical move is to find out which kind of addition your child's subjects involve and test the right thing. For Economics Higher Level, hand the student past quantitative questions and mark them; one session answers the question. For Mathematics Higher Level, give them a genuine extended investigative problem rather than a routine exercise set, because routine fluency tells you nothing about the paper that matters. For Biology Higher Level, the test is not an analytical one at all; it is whether the student can retrieve a large volume precisely under time.

The table below sets out what each Higher Level adds and what the matching readiness test is. It is deliberately organised by test rather than by subject, because the question a parent is actually asking is how to find out, not what the syllabus contains. No competitor page researched for this project sets out the Higher Level additions subject by subject at all, which is why the level decision in this market is usually made on impressions.

sections.heading: Where the marks are: weightings and the grade ceiling
paragraphs: A subject grade is assembled from components with published weightings, and those weightings change between Higher Level and Standard Level in most subjects. This is the arithmetic of the level decision and it is rarely explained to families. The internally assessed component, for instance, generally carries a different proportion of the Higher Level grade than of the Standard Level grade, simply because the Higher Level external assessment is larger. The same piece of coursework is therefore worth less to a Higher Level candidate's grade.

That has a direct consequence for where support should go. For a Standard Level candidate, the internally assessed component is a larger share of the grade and therefore a high-value place to spend tutoring hours, especially since it is the component done under the least time pressure. For a Higher Level candidate, the external papers dominate, so hours spent on timed paper technique are worth more than the same hours spent polishing coursework. Families often do the reverse, because coursework feels more controllable.

Both levels are graded 1 to 7, which is where a common misconception lives. A 6 at Standard Level and a 6 at Higher Level are the same number on the certificate, and universities read the level alongside the grade, which is why prerequisites are stated as a subject at a level rather than as a subject. A student who would achieve a 7 at Standard Level and a 5 at Higher Level has a real decision to make, and the right answer depends entirely on whether a published prerequisite requires the Higher Level.

Get the actual weightings for your child's specific subjects from the subject teacher or the official subject guide, and get them for the correct level. We do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, mark schemes or past papers, and we will not publish a weightings table claiming to be authoritative for every subject, because the figures differ by subject and change between syllabus revisions. What we will do is read your child's own marked work against the weightings their teacher confirms, which is the version that applies to them.

sections.heading: The week-four review, and why it is the best evidence you will get
paragraphs: Every pre-decision diagnostic is a prediction. Four weeks into Year 12 you stop predicting, because the student has marked work on genuine Higher Level material produced under the real conditions of the real course with the real teacher. That is better evidence than any taster session, and it arrives while most schools' level-change windows are still open. Almost no family uses it, because the instinct is to give it a term before worrying, and a term is exactly how long it takes for the window to close.

What to read in that work. Separate two things ruthlessly. Low marks caused by content the student has not yet met, or met and not yet consolidated, are an ordinary early-course condition and are fixable with a short bridge. Low marks caused by the student being unable to sustain the kind of reasoning the question asks for, even with the content in front of them, are the level being wrong. The tell is what happens when the content is supplied: if the answer still does not come together, it was never a content problem.

The other thing to read is time. Higher Level courses carry a markedly heavier weekly load, and some level decisions fail on hours rather than on ability. If the student is coping with the Higher Level material and sleeping five hours to do it, the level is wrong even though the marks look acceptable, and that will surface in Year 13 as a collapse across several subjects rather than one. Count the hours in week four and count them honestly.

The output of the review should be one of three recommendations, stated plainly. Continue as is. Continue with a named bridge of four to eight sessions on a specific gap. Or take the level change now while the school still permits it. We will give the third answer when it is the right one, and we say so explicitly because a tutoring business has an obvious incentive to recommend the second, and that incentive should be visible to you rather than hidden.

sections.heading: Three Higher Levels at once: counting the week honestly
paragraphs: The Diploma requires three subjects at Higher Level, and the level decision is therefore never about one subject in isolation. Three Higher Level courses at roughly 240 recommended teaching hours each, against three Standard Level courses at roughly 150, is a specific weekly load, and on top of it sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, CAS and, in UAE schools, the mandatory subjects the regulator requires alongside the licensed curriculum.

Count the output rather than the input. The question is not how many hours the courses are taught for but how many substantial pieces of work are live in the same week. Three essay-based Higher Levels plus an Extended Essay in a written discipline produces a second-year term with four major pieces of extended writing simultaneously, and that configuration defeats students who were well matched to every individual subject. The same applies to three content-heavy sciences at Higher Level, where the retrieval load rather than the writing load becomes the constraint.

The useful principle is to mix the shape of the demand rather than the difficulty. One analytical Higher Level, one content-heavy Higher Level and one with a continuous rather than concentrated workload is a manageable week. Three of any one kind is not, regardless of how able the student is, because the bottleneck is the calendar rather than the brain. In a smaller Abu Dhabi school the timetable blocks may remove the choice, in which case the honest planning question is which of the three will need standing support.

One component to place deliberately. The Extended Essay should sit in a subject that is not already one of the heaviest, because the drafting period collides with internal assessment deadlines that cluster in most schools. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix, which makes them worth protecting, and they are the first things students sacrifice when three Higher Levels go wrong in the spring.

sections.heading: When a Higher Level is required rather than chosen
paragraphs: Some Higher Level choices are not really choices. Where a published university requirement specifies a subject at Higher Level, the decision has been made elsewhere and the useful work is making it survivable rather than reconsidering it. That is a legitimate and common position, and it changes the whole conversation from whether to how.

The method is to read what each institution publishes about each specific course, record where and when you read it, and notice the distinction between a stated condition and a stated preference. Requirements differ between courses at the same institution and change between admissions cycles. No tutoring page should be the source of record for a university's requirements, including this one, and anything here should be treated as a prompt to check the institution's own page rather than as an answer.

On the UAE side, Ministry of Education equivalency has published requirements for the British and American tracks but the source used for this project states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure appears on this page. For the British track, five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority for anything concerning the IB. Equivalency and attestation are completed with the authority; IB Gram does not perform them, is not an intermediary in them and guarantees no outcome in them.

Where a Higher Level is genuinely required and the evidence says it is a stretch, the honest plan has three parts: a bridge before Year 12 on the specific gap, a weekly session with marked work throughout, and a termly review that names the point at which the pathway should be reconsidered rather than funded indefinitely. That is roughly seventy hours over two years at published UAE rates of AED 150-450 an hour, which is a five-figure AED commitment, and it should be entered into with the number known. Nothing about it guarantees the grade, and no part of equivalency, admission or progression requires tutoring at all.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with the internal assessment at either level
paragraphs: Because the internally assessed component is a larger share of a Standard Level grade, Standard Level families are often advised to put tutoring hours there, which makes the academic-honesty boundary a practical matter rather than a formality. The boundary is the same at both levels and it is firm, and stating it is more useful than assuming everybody already knows it.

A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and explain what each one actually rewards. A tutor may discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable within the word limit. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and the use of evidence. A tutor may teach referencing conventions and data-presentation technique. A tutor may mark practice work and explain where the marks went.

A tutor may not write any part of the submitted work, supply text to be inserted, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the research question outright, generate the data, or edit a draft to completion. A breach is an academic malpractice finding against the student, not against the tutor, so the consequence falls on the person whose name is on the Diploma. There is a provider in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is not a shortcut, it is an expulsion risk with a price attached.

Two related positions, stated once. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source, which is lawful and keeps the student on the current version. And we publish no guarantee of any grade, score, points total or admission, and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method behind it, which rules out most of what this market publishes about itself.

sections.heading: Who may teach, and what a parent can check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work with a verifiable permit, and a parent can ask about it directly. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free, any provider citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is inventing a cost. And because no fine schedule is published for tutoring without a permit, no amount should be quoted to you; the ministry did not specify fine amounts according to press reporting, and figures circulating as a maximum could not be verified, which is why none appears here.

For schools rather than individuals, private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes inspection ratings and regulates schools; it approves no individual tutor and sets no tutoring rate. A tuition operation with premises in Dubai is a separate matter again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

One practical boundary for a level decision specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct makes the same point. So the tempting shortcut of paying your child's own Higher Level teacher for extra hours is the one to avoid. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership, and claims none.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time, Ramadan and the weekly load at Higher Level
paragraphs: A Higher Level course is a weekly commitment rather than an exam-season one, so the practical question is how many hours exist in an Abu Dhabi school week once the commute is deducted. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, and the usable weekday window after the journey home is roughly 16:00 to 21:00, narrower in Khalifa City, Al Reef and Al Shamkha than on the island or in Al Raha because the school run is longer.

That window has to hold the Higher Level homework, the internally assessed work, CAS and any tutoring, which is why a three-Higher-Level load that looks fine on a timetable can be impossible in a household. The honest audit is to write down the actual hours for one ordinary week in October of Year 12, including travel and sleep, and see what is left. Where the answer is nothing, the level decision has already been made by arithmetic and the only question is which subject moves.

Where Ramadan falls inside the year, the pattern changes rather than pauses. School days shorten, the household reorganises around Iftar, and for many students the productive window moves to after the evening meal. A weekly Higher Level support session that insists on a 17:00 slot through the month will lose four to six sessions, which matters more at Higher Level than at Standard because the content keeps arriving regardless.

Travel is the other predictable loss. Abu Dhabi families travel in the school holidays, and for a Higher Level subject those weeks sit in the middle of content delivery rather than in a revision phase. Online sessions continue from wherever the family is, allowing for the time difference, which is a plain practical advantage over an arrangement that depends on somebody driving to a villa in Khalifa City. Write the lost weeks into the plan in September rather than discovering them in March.

process.title: Get both deadlines in writing
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the last date a subject can be changed and the last date a level can be changed. They are usually different dates, with the level change available later, and knowing them is what makes a week-four decision cheap rather than impossible.

process.title: Collect component evidence
process.description: IGCSE component marks with the tier, or MYP criterion marks separated by criterion. Averages conceal the profile that predicts Higher Level difficulty, so we work from the separated figures and ignore report comments.

process.title: Run a level diagnostic
process.description: One session on genuine Higher Level material in the subject in question, marked live against the real criteria, producing a written read that separates missing content from an unsustainable reasoning demand. Those two diagnoses lead to different decisions.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: The diagnostic can be the free trial lesson, with the proposed tutor and on real material, so you see the teaching and the marking before any commitment. If the match is wrong we offer a different tutor rather than asking you to persist.

process.title: Bridge or decide
process.description: Where the diagnosis is content, a four to eight session bridge on named topics, reassessed with the same paper format at the end. Where it is reasoning or total load, the recommendation is the level change while the school's window is open.

process.title: Review at week four and each term
process.description: Four weeks into Year 12 we read the school's own marked work with you and give one of three answers: continue, bridge, or change level. Then a termly review that names the point at which a stretch choice should be reconsidered rather than funded indefinitely.

whyPoints.title: Mechanics, not potential
whyPoints.description: We tell you what the Higher Level version of your child's subject physically adds, component by component, and what readiness test matches it. No competitor page researched for this project sets out the Higher Level additions subject by subject at all.

whyPoints.title: The week-four window used
whyPoints.description: The best evidence on a level decision is the student's own marked Higher Level work in week four, and it arrives while the change window is still open. Most families wait a term, by which point the cheap correction is no longer available.

whyPoints.title: Content gap and reasoning limit separated
whyPoints.description: Low marks because content is missing and low marks because the reasoning demand is too high look identical on a report and lead to opposite decisions. The diagnostic separates them by supplying the content and seeing whether the answer comes together.

whyPoints.title: We will recommend the change
whyPoints.description: A tutoring business has an obvious incentive to recommend a bridge over a level change. We state that incentive openly and give the change recommendation when the evidence supports it, because seventy hours of propping up is the worse outcome for your family.

whyPoints.title: Weightings read for your child's subject
whyPoints.description: Component weightings differ by subject and level and change between syllabus revisions, so we read your child's marked work against the weightings their own teacher confirms rather than publishing a table claiming to cover everything.

whyPoints.title: Nothing promised that cannot be
whyPoints.description: No grade, points total, admission or equivalency outcome is guaranteed, and no statistic appears without its sample size, date and method. Official papers, mark schemes and subject guides are cited and linked, never reproduced or distributed.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between HL and SL in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: More content, more recommended teaching time, and usually an additional or extended external component. The IB recommends around 240 teaching hours for a Higher Level course against around 150 at Standard Level. The additional component differs by subject: both Mathematics routes add a third paper, Economics adds a quantitative paper, History adds a depth study and a further paper, English A adds a written essay, while Biology, Psychology and Business Management mostly add extension content to existing papers. Knowing which kind of addition applies to your child's subject is what makes the level decision answerable.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether my child can cope with a subject at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Test the specific thing the level adds, rather than the subject in general. For Economics Higher Level, give the student past quantitative questions and mark them. For Mathematics Higher Level, give them a genuine extended investigative problem rather than a routine exercise set, because routine fluency says nothing about the paper that matters. For Biology Higher Level, test timed retrieval across a large topic. One session per subject, marked against the real criteria, produces a better answer than any amount of discussion about potential or work ethic.

faqs.question: What should we look at in my child's IGCSE results for an HL decision?
faqs.answer: Component marks and the tier, never the overall grade. A strong Mathematics grade earned on the questions a student always gets right, with the long multi-step questions at the end unattempted, predicts difficulty at Higher Level that the grade conceals completely. In the sciences, a strong multiple-choice performance and a weak extended-response performance average into a reassuring number while describing exactly the profile that struggles with Higher Level extended questions. Ask the school for the breakdown; it takes five minutes to read and it changes decisions.

faqs.question: Why does a week-four review matter more than a pre-decision assessment?
faqs.answer: Because by week four you have stopped predicting. The student has marked work on genuine Higher Level material, produced under the real conditions of the real course with the real teacher, which is better evidence than any taster can give. Most schools' level-change windows are still open at that point. Families typically wait a full term before raising concerns, and a term is roughly how long it takes for the cheap correction to disappear. Ask the coordinator for the deadline in the first fortnight so the review has somewhere to lead.

faqs.question: My child's Higher Level marks are low four weeks in. Is the level wrong?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the test is specific. Supply the missing content and see whether the answer comes together. If it does, you have an ordinary early-course consolidation problem, fixable with a four to eight session bridge on the named topics. If the answer still does not come together with the content in front of them, the difficulty is the reasoning the question demands, and that is the level being wrong rather than a gap. Those two diagnoses look identical on a school report and lead to opposite decisions, which is why the test matters.

faqs.question: Is a 6 at Standard Level worse than a 6 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: They are the same number on the certificate, and universities read the level alongside the grade, which is why prerequisites are stated as a subject at a level rather than as a subject alone. The practical decision is between likely outcomes rather than between labels: a student heading for a 7 at Standard Level and a 5 at Higher Level has a genuine choice, and the answer depends entirely on whether a published requirement for their intended course specifies the Higher Level. Check the institution's own page for the specific course, and record the date you read it.

faqs.question: Where should tutoring hours go for a Standard Level subject?
faqs.answer: Often into the internally assessed component, because it is usually a larger share of a Standard Level grade than of a Higher Level one and it is completed under the least time pressure. That makes it high-value work. At Higher Level the external papers dominate, so hours spent on timed paper technique are generally worth more than the same hours spent polishing coursework. Families frequently do the reverse because coursework feels more controllable. Get the actual weightings for your child's subject and level from the subject teacher, since they differ by subject.

faqs.question: Can my child take all three Higher Levels in content-heavy subjects?
faqs.answer: It is permitted and it is usually a mistake. Three content-heavy Higher Levels means a retrieval load that peaks simultaneously, and three essay-based Higher Levels plus an Extended Essay in a written discipline means four major pieces of extended writing live in the same term of Year 13. The principle that works is mixing the shape of the demand rather than the difficulty: one analytical, one content-heavy, one with a continuous rather than concentrated workload. Where timetable blocks remove the choice, plan which of the three will need standing support.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Higher Level subject actually take?
faqs.answer: More than the timetable shows, because homework, the internally assessed component and consolidation all sit outside lesson time. The honest audit is to write down the real hours of one ordinary week in October of Year 12, including the commute and sleep, and see what is left over. In Khalifa City, Al Reef or Al Shamkha, where the school run is long, the usable evening window runs roughly from 17:30 to 21:00, which has to hold three Higher Level workloads plus CAS. Where nothing is left, arithmetic has already made the level decision.

faqs.question: Is changing from HL to SL in Year 12 disruptive for my child?
faqs.answer: Taken early, far less than parents expect. The content overlaps substantially, in most Abu Dhabi schools both levels of a subject run as separate groups so a place exists, and the catch-up is small. The disruptive version is deferring it: carrying a Higher Level subject for eighteen months with weekly support, then arriving at Year 13 with a content debt across several subjects because one was consuming all the available time. Ask the coordinator for the last date a level can be changed, because that date rather than anybody's judgement sets what is possible.

faqs.question: Does a university requirement for a subject at Higher Level change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the conversation from whether to how. Where a published requirement specifies Higher Level, reconsidering the level is not available and the work becomes making it survivable: a bridge before Year 12 on the specific gap, a weekly session with marked work throughout, and a termly review naming the point at which the pathway itself should be reconsidered. That is roughly seventy hours over two years, a five-figure AED commitment at published UAE rates, and it should be entered into with the number visible. Verify the requirement on the institution's own page.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from an IB student?
faqs.answer: For equivalency, the published requirements cover the British and American tracks, and the source used for this project states no IB points threshold, so no IB figure appears here. The British track requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For anything concerning the IB, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and guarantees no outcome in them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the internal assessment at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary that is the same at both levels. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each rewards, discuss whether a research question is answerable within the word limit, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and evidence, teach referencing conventions, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text to insert, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the question outright or generate data. A malpractice finding falls on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Should we pay for extra hours with my child's own Higher Level teacher?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct making the same point about students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. Beyond the rules, the teacher who already delivered the material is the least likely person to find a different way into it for your child.

faqs.question: Are there enough Higher Level specialists in Abu Dhabi to support a stretch choice?
faqs.answer: Locally, often not, and this is the honest position rather than a sales line. The emirate has fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, so the resident pool in minority Higher Level subjects is thin, and in Al Ain it is thinner still. Families who insist on an in-person tutor for a Higher Level stretch choice frequently end up with someone teaching a level below the one in question. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; lessons are one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India.

faqs.question: Can you predict my child's final grade at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No. A level diagnostic tells you whether the demand of the course is within reach today and what specifically is missing; it does not forecast a grade two years out, and no honest provider does. We publish no outcome statistics at all, because a figure without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is a marketing claim rather than evidence, and several providers in this market publish exactly that. What we commit to is marked work with a written read, a week-four review and a termly review that says plainly when to change course.

abu-dhabi/ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.closingHeading: Decide on marked work, and keep the window open
abu-dhabi/ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.closingBody: If you are weighing IB HL vs SL guidance in Abu Dhabi, two steps make the decision cheap. Ask the IB coordinator in writing for the last date a subject can be changed and the last date a level can be changed, because those are different dates and both are needed. Then test what the Higher Level version of the subject actually adds, on genuine Higher Level material marked against the real criteria, and read the result as either a content gap or a reasoning limit. We will do that in a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and review again at week four while the change window is still open.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below hold a fixed weekly slot rather than a floating arrangement, because a Diploma plan that depends on weekly renegotiation does not last a term. Each teaches a named subject at a named level, keeps a shared running document the household can see, and reports on a fortnightly cycle. Tell us the subject, the level and the hour that genuinely exists in your week.

intro.heading: The arrangement breaks on logistics, not on teaching
paragraphs: Ask families in this emirate why a previous tutoring arrangement ended and the answers are strikingly consistent, and strikingly rarely about the subject. It drifted. The slot kept moving. Ramadan came and it never restarted. The tutor was good but the time did not work once football started. We went away for the summer and nobody picked it back up. Almost none of these answers is about teaching quality, which means almost none of them is fixed by finding a better tutor.

The Diploma makes this worse than it is for other courses, because it runs for two years with internal deadlines distributed across both of them. A student who loses six weeks in DP1 to a collapsed schedule does not notice immediately. They notice in the second term of DP2, when an Extended Essay deadline, a Mathematics exploration, two science investigations and a Theory of Knowledge essay all land inside a window that also contains mock examinations. The cost of a lost term is paid much later and all at once.

So this page is about the household rather than the subject. What hour genuinely exists after an Abu Dhabi school run that finishes at 15:30 and arrives home at 16:20. What happens to the plan during Ramadan and across the summer. What equipment a sixteen-year-old actually needs on a desk for a Mathematics session to work. When a deliberate pause is the right decision and when it is the beginning of the end. How a timetable survives three weeks in London or Kochi, and what happens to a minor's recorded lessons afterwards.

It is also about the term-by-term shape of the two years, because a tutoring plan should know what the school calendar is about to do. DP1 is a content year with the first coursework drafts appearing late. The transition summer between DP1 and DP2 is the single most valuable and least used period in the whole Diploma. The first term of DP2 is the deadline crush. The second is examination preparation. Support that looks identical in all four of those phases is not a plan, it is a standing order.

One point of substance before the detail. IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Everything here is delivered into the household one-to-one over live video, at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the session recorded and a shared document the family can read. Where the phrase home tuition is used on this page, it means tuition at home rather than a person at the door, and the practical consequences of that distinction are set out in full below.

Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing by arrangement, not by improvisation

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tuition.programmesIntro: Household tuition looks different at each stage, mostly because the amount of self-management the student can supply changes completely between eleven and seventeen. These four stages cover the enquiries that come from Abu Dhabi households, with what the family has to provide in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: A content year with coursework beginning to appear from the second term. The useful household rhythm here is one fixed weekly session per supported subject, long enough to teach something properly, with a timed assessment every fortnight. What families get wrong is treating DP1 as the easy year and starting support in September of DP2, by which point the deadlines are fixed and the content gaps are load-bearing.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP1 students are frequently carrying more than six timetabled subjects, because Arabic and the other federally required subjects sit alongside the Diploma in private schools in the emirate. The household consequence is that the free evening hours are fewer than a Diploma timetable alone suggests, and the honest count should be made in September rather than discovered in January.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year
programmes.description: Two distinct halves. The first term is a deadline crush in which almost every internal assessment reaches a final version and mock examinations set predicted grades. The second is examination preparation, where sessions get shorter, more frequent and almost entirely past-paper based. A plan that does not change shape between those halves is wasting one of them.
programmes.countryNote: Predicted grades matter early in this emirate because applications run to the United Kingdom, North America and UAE universities on different timetables, and the mock that produces them often sits in January. A household plan that front-loads effort into the first term of DP2 and tapers afterwards is working with that calendar rather than against it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 9 to 11
programmes.description: The years in which household habits are actually set. Support here is as much about routine as content: a fixed hour, work that gets checked, and criterion language translated into something a fourteen-year-old can act on. A student who arrives in DP1 able to manage a weekly commitment has an advantage that no amount of Diploma tutoring later replicates.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the most common reason an Abu Dhabi household makes contact. Middle Years assessment rewards process and reflection; the Diploma rewards precision under time. A student scoring 6s in MYP Mathematics can land at 4 in the first DP1 test with nothing having gone wrong, because the measuring instrument changed underneath them.

programmes.name: The DP1 to DP2 summer
programmes.description: Six to eight weeks with no teaching, no homework and every internal deadline still ahead. The highest-value use is coursework: getting an exploration or investigation to a genuine first draft, and settling an Extended Essay research question, before the autumn crush. The second-best use is closing one or two content gaps from DP1 that would otherwise be carried into examination preparation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi households travel heavily in this window, which is the usual reason it is wasted. Because sessions run over live video they continue from wherever the family is, converted from Gulf Standard Time, and a plan agreed in June survives a month abroad. Families who use this summer well describe DP2 as busy; families who do not describe it as impossible.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Which subjects a household supports is usually decided by timetable capacity rather than by need, so it is worth being deliberate. These are the courses Abu Dhabi households most often fund, with the honest weekly commitment each one implies. Two subjects at one session a week is a sustainable load for a Diploma student; four is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most commonly supported course and the one that most rewards a long uninterrupted slot. Ninety minutes once a week beats sixty minutes twice for this subject, because algebraic work needs runway. The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the grade and is best drafted in the DP1 to DP2 summer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and graphing-calculator work throughout. A household needs the correct calculator model from the school's permitted list on the desk from session one, because teaching the keystrokes on a different device wastes a term's worth of small confusions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Supported most often in the second term of DP1, when energetics and equilibrium arrive together. The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent across four criteria, and the data analysis stage is the part that genuinely benefits from an outside reader rather than more laboratory time.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Requires a handwriting channel more than any other subject, because the marks are in the derivation rather than the answer. A phone on a stand pointed at the page is sufficient and costs less than one session at the in-home market rate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, which makes it the subject where a fortnightly rhythm works better than a weekly one. Content is covered in school; the useful household session is data-based questions and command-term discipline, both of which are rarely practised at home.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation decide the grade, and both are teachable in a sixty-minute slot. This is a good second subject for a household already funding Mathematics, because the two place very different demands on the same student in the same week.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is the most rehearsable component in the Diploma and the one most often left until a fortnight before. Scheduling it deliberately into the DP1 summer or the early autumn of DP2 is a household decision more than an academic one.

subjects.name: Arabic and the federally required subjects
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those commitments occupy real hours in an Abu Dhabi student's week and belong in the household timetable rather than being treated as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Worth up to three bonus points between them, with the Extended Essay marked out of 34 and the Theory of Knowledge essay capped at 1,600 words. These are read-and-annotate commitments rather than weekly teaching, and they should be booked as defined blocks at the points the school's internal calendar actually needs them.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tuition.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi households and the hour that genuinely exists
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tuition.regionsIntro: The single most useful piece of local knowledge for a tutoring plan is when a session can realistically start in a given community, once the school run, the commute and a younger sibling's routine are counted. These seven communities cover most household enquiries in the emirate.

regions.name: The Corniche and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Apartment living with short school runs but shared rooms and noise. Headphones matter more here than anywhere else, and the viable slot is often earlier, around 17:00, because the household gets busier rather than quieter as the evening goes on.

regions.name: Al Nahyan and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Central, with many students carrying Arabic as a first language alongside the Diploma and therefore a fuller school week. The honest free-hour count here is lower than a Diploma timetable suggests, and two supported subjects is usually the ceiling.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Long school runs into the Khalifa City corridor, with arrival home frequently after 16:15. A 17:00 start is optimistic and a 19:00 one holds, which is the opposite of what most families assume when they book.

regions.name: Al Falah and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Larger villa households with several school-age children and staggered pickups. Consecutive slots for two children work well because nobody is travelling between them, and the second child's session is the one that usually needs protecting.

regions.name: Hudayriyat Island and Al Bateen
regions.note: Heavy sports and co-curricular commitments, with training often filling the early evening on two or three weekdays. Weekend morning slots are more common here than anywhere else in the emirate and work well for a ninety-minute Mathematics session.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island and Al Reem Island
regions.note: Working parents on short notice periods and frequent relocations, so plans need to be portable by design. Recorded sessions and a shared running document matter most where a family may be in a different city for part of the Diploma.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: The densest school catchment in the emirate and the shortest runs, which makes a 17:30 start genuinely viable. This is also where sibling bookings are most common, with two Diploma years in one household on consecutive evenings.

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: Short school runs and the emirate's largest concentration of IB and British provision, so the household timetable has more room than elsewhere. Internal coursework deadlines in this cluster tend to be set early, which pulls the useful support window forward into DP1.

schoolClusters.city: The island schools and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: Long-established Diploma departments with detailed internal marking, and students who often live on the mainland and travel in. The commute, not the curriculum, is what compresses the evening for these households.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island, Yas Island and the newer communities
schoolClusters.note: Growing cohorts with a high proportion of mid-year arrivals and families who may relocate again during the Diploma. Portability of the plan matters more in this cluster than in any other.
