abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees track the programme because the assessment stakes track the programme. A Diploma hour and a Primary Years hour are priced differently in every rate card in this market, and the reason is what the hour has to achieve rather than how hard it is to teach.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive hour in any Abu Dhabi rate card, because externally marked papers and a fixed two-year window remove the option of trying again next term. Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, with a 45-point ceiling of which three points come from the core.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma fees in Abu Dhabi peak twice a year rather than rising steadily: once in the autumn when DP2 families realise the Internal Assessments are real, and again in February and March when the session is close. Booking either six weeks earlier than the peak usually buys the same person at a mid-band rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Lower hourly figures across the market and a longer sensible horizon. Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a 0-8 scale, with no external papers for most students, so the measurable return on an hour is slower and less dramatic than at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Abu Dhabi families get the best value per dirham, and where most of them do not spend. A Year 9 student whose criterion marks are fixed before the Diploma starts needs far fewer paid hours in DP1 and DP2, which is the cheapest Diploma strategy available and the least popular.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The lowest band in every rate card. Inquiry-based units with no graded examinations, so support is numeracy fluency, reading and writing stamina, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education strands running alongside the licensed curriculum.
programmes.countryNote: Paying a Diploma specialist rate for primary support is the most common overspend seen among Abu Dhabi families. A capable primary teacher who understands inquiry reporting does more for a Year 4 student, at a fraction of the figure, than any subject expert.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses plus a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fees generally follow the Diploma band for the DP subject components and are negotiated individually for the career-related elements, which few tutors cover.
programmes.countryNote: Because so few Abu Dhabi schools run this programme, there is effectively no local price benchmark. Families should expect to negotiate rather than compare, and to source the reflective project support online.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Fee levels differ by subject in this market, and the reason is usually what the assessment demands rather than how difficult the content is. Each note below names where marks are actually lost, because that is what determines how many paid hours a subject needs.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Marks are lost to narrative. Paper 2 and Paper 3 reward argument built from evidence, and students who know the period well frequently write chronology instead. The Internal Assessment is a 2,200-word investigation with a distinct source-evaluation section that is routinely under-written. Mid-band fees, high hours.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is cheap to fix and command-term handling is not. The fieldwork Internal Assessment needs supervision at the design stage rather than the writing stage, which means hours spent early are worth more than hours spent late. Mid-band fees locally.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: The engagement activity and, at Higher Level, the oral presentations carry marks students rarely rehearse. Lost marks come from describing a case rather than using it as evidence for a claim about a political concept. Fewer tutors cover it in Abu Dhabi, so fees run above the humanities average.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A transdisciplinary course where students lose marks by answering as scientists and ignoring the societies half, or the reverse. The Internal Assessment requires a genuine investigation rather than secondary data, and getting that decision right early saves several paid hours later.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application, not definitions. Students who can draw a framework but not apply it to the case study sit in the middle band indefinitely. One of the cheapest IB subjects to find cover for in Abu Dhabi, so the rate should be at the lower end of any quote you receive.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Writing task register and the individual oral are where the marks go, not vocabulary. Many Abu Dhabi students are fluent speakers who lose marks on text-type conventions, which is a short, cheap fix with the right tutor and an expensive one with the wrong one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling language and calculator technique decide more marks than algebra. Students arriving from American middle schools often meet the modelling vocabulary for the first time here. Plentiful cover at Standard Level in Abu Dhabi, which keeps fees moderate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Standard Level cover is widely available; Higher Level is not, and the fee gap between them in this emirate is wider than for any other science. Marks are lost in energetics and in organic mechanisms, and the Internal Assessment variable choice drives the final criterion scores.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The highest-fee science locally because Higher Level cover is thin. Lost marks are predictable: dropped units in multi-step problems, and extended responses where the physics is correct but no principle is stated before the algebra.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Content volume and a practical investigation. Students lose marks by treating the physiology as biology and skipping the application to performance. Very few Abu Dhabi tutors cover it, so expect individually negotiated fees rather than a rate card.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: The single biggest variable in an Abu Dhabi in-home quote is where you live, because a tutor prices their round trip into the hour. The notes below describe each corridor as a travel problem rather than as a neighbourhood.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A long trip from the island in evening traffic and the reason Khalifa City families see some of the widest quote variation in the emirate. The same tutor may charge one figure for a Tuesday 7pm and another for a 5pm slot in the same week.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Out past the airport, which puts it at the far end of most tutors' acceptable range. In-home quotes here sit near the top of the market band and some tutors decline outright, which narrows the choice before price is even discussed.

regions.name: Al Ghadeer
regions.note: On the Dubai side of the emirate boundary, so some tutors treat it as a Dubai job and others as an Abu Dhabi one, with very different figures. Worth asking which city a visiting tutor is driving from before accepting a rate.

regions.name: Al Samha
regions.note: Similar distance profile to Al Ghadeer with fewer tutors willing to make the trip. Families here routinely report that the choice is between a high in-home figure and an online session, with little in between.

regions.name: Baniyas
regions.note: Mainland and well connected, but a long way from where most independent tutors live. Group arrangements within a compound are common here as a way of splitting a travel-loaded fee across households.

regions.name: Shakhbout City
regions.note: Villa community with a steady flow of students transferring between curricula. The practical effect on fees is that transition planning sessions are often needed on top of subject hours, and families should budget for both.

regions.name: Al Falah
regions.note: Compact villa clusters where sharing a tutor across neighbouring households genuinely reduces the per-family travel loading. It works for revision and fails for Internal Assessments, which must be each student's own work.

regions.name: Mussafah and the industrial corridor
regions.note: Few tutors live here and fewer will travel to it in the evening. This is the clearest case in the emirate where online delivery is not a cost preference but the only route to a subject specialist at any price.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: The corridor where Diploma demand and travel cost collide hardest. Students we support here come from a mix of IB continuum and British curriculum schools, and families commonly compare an in-home quote with travel against two online sessions for the same money.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Baniyas, Mussafah and Shakhbout City
schoolClusters.note: Mainland communities where local independent tutor supply is thin and travel-loaded quotes are the norm. Requests here skew towards Middle Years support and transfers into IB programmes from other curricula.
schools: GEMS Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: The island centre
schoolClusters.note: The one part of Abu Dhabi where an in-home visit carries little travel loading, so quotes here are the closest thing the emirate has to a pure teaching rate. Useful as a benchmark when comparing a mainland quote.

Market rates for qualified online tutors run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and specialists higher. There is no travel component because nobody travels, which is the entire reason this band sits below the in-home band.

sections.heading: The rate card: what Abu Dhabi charges, by programme and level
paragraphs: The table below is the thing almost nobody in this market publishes. Three of six competitor pages researched for Abu Dhabi and Dubai quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. Every figure here is in AED, attributed, and presented as the market rather than as our price list.

Read it as bands rather than as prices. Where a row shows a wide range, the spread is usually explained by three things: the level, how scarce that specialism is inside the emirate, and how close the examination session is. Higher Level sciences sit at the top of their band in February and in the middle of it in October, and that is a timing decision available to any family who plans ahead.

The small-group column is per student, and it is the honest budget option. It halves or quarters the hour without pretending to be one-to-one. What it cannot do is coursework, because an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay must be the individual student's own work and a shared session is the wrong place for it.

The indicative monthly column assumes one session a week. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, which lines up with the arithmetic in the table.

sections.heading: The travel component, corridor by corridor
paragraphs: This is the table that explains the fee difference nobody itemises. An Abu Dhabi tutor quoting for an in-home visit is pricing a round trip, and the round trip is frequently longer than the lesson. The figures below are typical evening driving estimates between a central Abu Dhabi base and each corridor, which is where most independent tutors in the emirate live.

The arithmetic is unforgiving. A 60-minute lesson in Al Reef costs the tutor around two and a half hours of their evening once both directions are counted. At a notional target of AED 200 for an hour of their professional time, that trip has to be priced near AED 400 to AED 500 before the tutor is earning what they would earn teaching three online hours from a desk. This is why the top of the in-home band exists, and it is not greed; it is a diary.

It also explains something families find puzzling: why the same tutor quotes differently for different slots. A 5pm start in Khalifa City crosses the worst of the evening, and a 7.30pm start does not. Where a tutor offers you two figures for the same lesson, the difference is almost always the traffic between them.

The final column is the point of the exercise. Removing the car does not reduce the teaching; it removes a cost that buys nothing educational. A family in Al Samha choosing between one in-home hour and two online hours for roughly the same money is choosing between presence and twice the teaching, and for a Diploma student the second is usually the better purchase.

sections.heading: What a 60-minute session can actually finish, and what needs 90
paragraphs: Families buy hours and tutors deliver tasks, and the mismatch between those two units wastes a surprising amount of money. Some pieces of IB work simply do not fit into sixty minutes once you include the student explaining where they got stuck, and buying them in sixty-minute units means paying twice for the same ramp-up.

The pattern is consistent. Anything diagnostic, iterative or involving a long piece of writing benefits from ninety minutes. Anything drill-like, topic-sized or focused on timed technique fits sixty comfortably and often leaves the student fresher. The worst value in this market is a ninety-minute session spent on content explanation, where attention falls away after the first hour, and a sixty-minute session spent on a full extended-response cycle, which cannot be completed.

The practical consequence for a budget is that a mixed pattern costs less than a uniform one. A Diploma student might take a weekly sixty-minute session for technique and a monthly ninety-minute session when a piece of coursework needs a proper read-through, rather than paying for ninety minutes every week on the assumption that more is better.

The table below is a planning aid rather than a rule. Use it to challenge a quote expressed only in months: a provider selling eight sessions a month without asking what those sessions are for has not thought about this, and the family is the one paying for the mismatch. It is also worth asking the tutor which length they would choose for your child's specific weakness, because a tutor who has a view on that question has thought about the teaching and one who defers to whatever you prefer has not.

sections.heading: The extras that appear after the first invoice
paragraphs: Most complaints about tutoring fees in this market are not about the hourly figure. They are about things that were not in the conversation and then were on the bill, or about services the family assumed were included and were not. All of them are avoidable with four questions asked before the first session.

Marking between sessions is the big one. If it is not included, a sixty-minute session has to contain the reading, the marking and the teaching, and a family is buying perhaps forty minutes of instruction. Ask directly whether work set between sessions is marked and returned, and whether that time is billed. A rate that looks ten per cent higher and includes it is usually the cheaper product.

Then there is the cancellation window, which for an in-home tutor is reasonably tight because a wasted trip costs them a whole evening. Twenty-four hours is common; some ask for forty-eight. A family with unpredictable work travel should establish this before committing, because the cost of two cancelled sessions a term is a meaningful share of the annual spend. Report writing, school liaison, mock marking outside sessions and holiday retention fees are the other four that appear on second invoices in this market.

Finally, ask what happens to the rate if you add a second subject or a second child. Many tutors will hold a rate for a second subject with the same student and almost none will reduce it, because the preparation doubles. Sharing a session between two children of different levels is where families most often get poor value: both get a diluted hour and the saving is smaller than it looks.

sections.heading: Tuition against school fees and examination entry
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest education line in an Abu Dhabi household budget, and seeing it next to the others changes how families decide. The table sets out the items that recur, with the figures stated as ranges and the ones that are not ours clearly attributed.

A useful anchor from the neighbouring emirate: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, and Abu Dhabi fee regulation sits with ADEK, but it tells you something about the direction of the regional conversation on education costs.

The two-year Diploma line in the table is the number worth calculating before DP1 rather than during DP2. A single weekly specialist hour across two academic years is a substantial commitment, and a family who sees that total in advance usually makes better decisions: fewer subjects supported, earlier start, more use of the Middle Years years when hours are cheaper and the return lasts longer.

Examination entry as a private candidate is included because it occasionally becomes relevant for retakes or for a student outside a school system. Entry fees are set by the board and the examination centre, not by a tutor, and should be confirmed with the centre directly rather than estimated from a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, and what each fix costs in hours
paragraphs: A fee only makes sense against a job. The most expensive tutoring in Abu Dhabi is the kind bought without a diagnosis, because it pays for a general improvement across a whole subject when the actual loss is concentrated in two or three identifiable places.

Across IB subjects the losses cluster in a small number of patterns. Content gaps, usually inherited from an earlier year, which are bounded and relatively cheap: the syllabus is finite and a tutor can work through it. Command-term handling, where a student who knows the material answers the wrong question, which is the cheapest fix of all and frequently takes four sessions. Working presentation in the quantitative subjects, where units, rounding and unstated method lose marks the student has earned. And coursework judgement, where the Internal Assessment was framed in a way that caps its ceiling regardless of execution.

The last of those is the one with the worst cost profile, because it is cheap to fix in week one and nearly impossible to fix in month four. Two ninety-minute sessions on the plan and the variable choice, bought early, prevent a situation in which no amount of later tutoring can lift the criterion scores. Families who buy those two sessions and nothing else often get better value than families who buy a term of weekly hours starting in February.

So the sequence that costs least is: get the marked evidence read, identify which of those four patterns is dominant, buy the narrow fix for it, then reassess. What costs most is buying a monthly package across three subjects and hoping the right thing gets worked on.
bullets: Content gaps: bounded, four to twelve sessions depending on how much is missing
Command-term handling: the cheapest fix, often four sessions and transferable
Working presentation and units: two to three sessions, immediate mark return
Coursework framing: two sessions in week one, or unfixable later
Timing and paper strategy: one or two sessions with timed practice

sections.heading: Packages, commitments and the questions that reduce the bill
paragraphs: Packages exist because they solve the tutor's problem, which is an unpredictable diary, and they can solve the family's problem too if the arithmetic is checked. A monthly figure for eight sessions is only good value if eight sessions a month is the right pattern, and for most Diploma students working on one subject it is not; four is.

The commitments that genuinely reduce an hourly figure in this market are the ones that reduce the tutor's risk. A term booked in advance at a fixed weekly slot is worth a real discount and most tutors will give one, because it removes diary uncertainty. Paying for a block up front is worth less than people assume and carries the obvious risk of a tutor who turns out to be the wrong match. A longer single session is not usually cheaper per hour, and for younger students it is worse teaching.

Three questions reliably move a quote. Whether a term commitment at a fixed slot attracts a lower rate, which it usually should. Whether a fortnightly pattern at ninety minutes costs less in total than a weekly sixty for coursework work, which it often does. And whether the tutor would rather hold a quieter slot at a lower figure than a contested 5pm one at a higher figure, which for anybody who can study at 8pm is the single largest saving available in this emirate.

One question to avoid: asking a tutor to beat a figure from somebody at a different tier. A specialist is not going to match a university student's rate, and the conversation signals that you are buying on price alone, which changes what you are offered. Ask for a structure that costs less instead.

sections.heading: Invoices, VAT and paying somebody who is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Two administrative points are worth settling before money changes hands, and neither takes long. The first is whether the figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay. The second is whether the person you are paying is permitted to charge for lessons in the UAE at all.

On tax: this page does not state how value added tax applies to tuition in the UAE, because that treatment should be read from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring website, and several sites in this market state it confidently and inconsistently. What a family can and should do is ask any provider a direct question: is the quoted AED figure inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and if tax is being charged, what is the provider's registration number. A provider who cannot answer that clearly is telling you something about their invoicing.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through MoHRE, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which created a private tuition work permit granted free of charge for two years. Those offering private lessons without it are, in the ministry's wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so nobody can tell you the amount. Ask to see the permit before the first paid session. It costs the tutor nothing to hold and nothing to show.

Keep a simple record either way: dates, duration, subject and amount, with a receipt or transfer reference. It matters if a dispute arises, it matters more if a tutor stops responding mid-term, and for a family running support across two Diploma years it is the only reliable way to know what the whole thing actually cost.

process.title: Send marked work before asking for a figure
process.description: A quote given without evidence is a guess, and guesses in this market are high. A marked paper with component marks, or criterion scores for a Middle Years student, lets a tutor say how many sessions the job needs. That number, not the hourly rate, is what determines the bill.

process.title: Ask what the hour includes
process.description: Marking between sessions, work set, written feedback, cancellation window, and whether the rate changes in the examination term. Four questions, two minutes, and they separate two products that are sold at similar figures and deliver very different amounts of teaching.

process.title: Take the free trial with the papers open
process.description: Forty-five minutes, no cost and no card details. Judge it on whether the tutor named a specific lost mark and said how many sessions the fix needs. A trial spent on reassurance has given you no information about value.

process.title: Pick the slot nobody else wants
process.description: The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested in the emirate. A family that can study at 8pm, or on a weekend morning, has more choice of specialist and more room on price than one that cannot. It is the largest single saving available here.

process.title: Review the spend against the evidence at four weeks
process.description: Compare newly marked work with the baseline on the specific component that was targeted. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the tutor or narrow the brief rather than buying more hours, which is how tutoring budgets in Abu Dhabi quietly double.

whyPoints.title: AED figures, with sources, in the currency you pay in
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. Every band here is in AED and attributed to the provider or survey it came from, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

whyPoints.title: The travel cost made visible
whyPoints.description: The gap between in-home and online rates in Abu Dhabi is largely a driving cost. Pricing it per corridor lets a family see what the premium buys, which is presence rather than teaching, and decide whether that is what they want for the money.

whyPoints.title: No travel billed, because nobody travels
whyPoints.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so there is no commute inside the figure and no slot priced by how bad the bridge traffic is that evening.

whyPoints.title: Hours tied to a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Every session count on this page starts from what the marked evidence shows rather than from a package structure. That makes a budget checkable before it is spent, and makes it obvious when a narrow two-session fix would do the work of a term.

whyPoints.title: Straight about tax and permits
whyPoints.description: This page does not assert how VAT applies to tuition, because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority. It does tell you to ask whether a quote includes tax, and to ask any tutor for the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: What do IB home tutor fees in Abu Dhabi usually include, and what sits outside them?
faqs.answer: Typically included: the teaching session itself and the tutor's travel, which is usually inside the hourly figure rather than itemised. Frequently outside: marking of work set between sessions, written progress reports, liaison with the school, marking of mock papers that are not done in the session, and any materials. Cancellation terms are the other variable, and for an in-home tutor they tend to be tighter because a wasted trip costs an entire evening. Ask about all five before the first session; a rate that looks higher and includes marking is often the cheaper product.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home tutor cost than an online one in this emirate?
faqs.answer: The market bands overlap but the centres are clearly apart. Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500, while qualified tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Most of that gap is driving time rather than teaching. For a family in Al Reef or Al Ghadeer the gap is widest, because the round trip is longest. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is tuition in Abu Dhabi charged per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both conventions exist in this market and the difference matters when sessions are not sixty minutes. A tutor quoting per session at ninety minutes may be cheaper per hour than one quoting hourly, or considerably more expensive, and families comparing two numbers often compare different units. Convert everything to a per-hour figure before deciding, then convert again to a monthly total using the session pattern you actually intend to run. A quote expressed only as a monthly package should be unpacked into hours before it is compared with anything.

faqs.question: Does a visiting tutor charge separately for travel to Saadiyat or Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Usually it is not itemised, which is precisely why it is easy to miss. The travel sits inside the hourly figure, which is how the same tutor can quote one rate for a lesson in Al Bateen and a noticeably higher one for Al Reef or Al Ghadeer. A 60-minute lesson in the airport corridor costs the tutor around two and a half hours of their evening once both directions are counted. Where a tutor gives you two figures for different times on the same day, the difference between them is the traffic.

faqs.question: Do tuition fees in the UAE carry VAT?
faqs.answer: This page will not state the tax treatment of tuition, because it should be read from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring site, and several sites in this market state it confidently and inconsistently. What you should do is ask the provider two direct questions: is the quoted AED figure inclusive or exclusive of tax, and if tax is charged, what is your registration number. Any provider invoicing properly can answer both in a sentence. Keep the written answer with your records.

faqs.question: Are monthly packages better value than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Only when the package matches the pattern your child actually needs. Packages seen in this market run from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Eight sessions a month is right for a student working on two subjects and wrong for one working on a single subject, where four is the sensible pattern. A term booked at a fixed weekly slot is the commitment that genuinely earns a lower hourly figure, because it removes diary uncertainty for the tutor.

faqs.question: What does a late cancellation cost in this market?
faqs.answer: For an in-home tutor, commonly the full session fee inside twenty-four hours, and some ask for forty-eight. The logic is straightforward: a cancelled visit cannot be refilled at short notice and the tutor has lost the whole evening, travel included. Online arrangements tend to be more forgiving because the slot can sometimes be reused. If your household has unpredictable travel, establish this in writing before committing to a term, because two lost sessions a term is a meaningful fraction of the annual spend.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level cost more per hour than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and neither is that the tutor works harder. First, fewer people in Abu Dhabi can teach Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches to completion, and the market prices that scarcity, which is why the specialist band runs to AED 450 and above. Second, the work itself is different: Higher Level marks sit in extended responses that have to be marked repeatedly, which costs the tutor unbilled time between sessions. A quote that treats both levels identically has not accounted for either.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Do the arithmetic rather than trusting a monthly figure. One weekly online session with a specialist across two academic years, term time only, lands somewhere around AED 12,000 to AED 30,000 depending on where in the band your subject sits. Two subjects double it. That total is worth calculating before DP1 begins, because families who see it in advance generally support fewer subjects, start earlier, and use the cheaper Middle Years years when an hour buys more lasting benefit.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one paid Diploma session to halve the fee?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per family, usually worse per child, and sometimes not allowed at all. Where both children are at the same level in the same subject and working on content or timed practice, a shared session can be genuinely good value and splits both the fee and any travel. Where they are at different levels, both get a diluted hour. And it cannot be used for Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge work, which must be each student's own work. A small group of two to four at a similar level is the structured version of this.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates rise closer to the examination session?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, even when published figures do not move. Demand across the emirate spikes in February and March, specialist slots close first, and families buying late find that the only availability is at the top of the band or in an inconvenient slot. The practical consequence is that the same person costs a family who books in October less than a family who books in March, for identical teaching. Booking early is the largest structural saving available in the Abu Dhabi tutoring market.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to move a Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Fix the command-term problem first, because it is usually the largest pool of recoverable marks and the cheapest to address: four sessions, and it transfers to every other subject the student takes. Then fix working presentation in the quantitative subjects, which is another two or three sessions with an immediate return. Only then buy content coverage, which is the expensive part because the syllabus is large. Buying in that order typically costs a third of what buying a general monthly package across three subjects costs.

faqs.question: How much does Internal Assessment support usually cost?
faqs.answer: Budget it as a block rather than a monthly commitment: four to six sessions at the specialist band, which puts it roughly in the AED 1,200 to AED 2,700 range at market rates. The timing matters more than the amount. Two ninety-minute sessions spent on the plan and the variable choice before any data is collected prevent a situation where the framing caps the criterion scores no matter how well the write-up is done. The same money spent in month four buys far less. A tutor gives feedback on the student's own work only.

faqs.question: What should we send to get an accurate quote rather than a range?
faqs.answer: Four things. The course name and level, written exactly as the school writes it. A recent marked paper with the component breakdown, or criterion scores task by task for a Middle Years student. The school's internal deadline list for any coursework. And the two or three slots your household can genuinely keep each week. With those, a tutor can tell you the session count as well as the rate, which is the figure that actually determines what you spend.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge for the first lesson?
faqs.answer: No. The trial runs 45 minutes over live video, costs nothing and takes no card details to book, and you are free to take it, decline and try a different tutor. The condition worth stating is that it is one trial per subject match rather than an open series. Use it with marked work in front of the tutor, because the only question worth answering in forty-five minutes is whether this person can locate what is actually going wrong. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so the trial is online like everything else.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Price the job, not the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: The hourly figure is the least useful number in a tutoring decision. What costs money is the number of sessions, and that comes from a diagnosis rather than from a package. So send the marked work first, ask what the hour includes, convert every quote to the same unit before comparing, and take the free trial with the papers open. Remember that a large part of any in-home figure in this emirate is a car journey that teaches nobody anything. Every AED band on this page belongs to the market and carries its source, so you can hold any quote against it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes to students living in Al Bandar and the wider Al Raha Beach precinct. Each one is matched to a named subject at a named level, then to a slot that fits your family's afternoon.

intro.heading: The Al Bandar afternoon, and why it decides your tutoring plan
paragraphs: Al Bandar sits on the Al Raha Beach waterfront, off the Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan corridor, with the marina on one side and Al Raha Mall a few minutes inland. It is a short-commute community by Abu Dhabi standards: Khalifa City is a quarter of an hour away, Al Raha Gardens less than that. The island schools are not. A child at Cranleigh on Saadiyat or Brighton College in Al Bateen is in a car for the best part of forty minutes each way, and that single fact reshapes every tutoring decision a family here makes.

Searching for an IB home tutor in Al Bandar is a reasonable response to that. The logic runs: if the tutor comes here, nobody drives anywhere, and the hour after school is salvaged. The problem is that the pool of people who will drive to a specific waterfront address at five on a Tuesday, and who also happen to teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, is very small. Proximity and specialism pull in opposite directions, and the closer you look at the arithmetic the more clearly proximity loses.

IB Gram resolves it by removing the drive rather than the tutor. Tuition for families in the UAE is one-to-one and delivered over live video, screen-shared, recorded where the family wants it recorded. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What that buys an Al Bandar family is a tutor chosen because they have taught the exact subject at the exact level, in a slot that starts the moment the car is back in the parking bay.

The practical difference shows up in the week rather than in the sales pitch. A session that needs no travel can start at four and finish at five, leaving the evening intact. It can be moved by twenty minutes when the Saadiyat run is slow, because nobody is sitting in traffic waiting to be let in. It can run on a Thursday evening in the quiet week before internal assessment deadlines and not at all in the week the school ran a residential trip. The flexibility is not a feature of the technology; it is what happens once travel stops being part of the hour.

This page is written from the school run outward. It names the schools Al Bandar families actually use, puts indicative finish times and drive times side by side, and works out when a session can realistically begin for each one. It then covers what the Abu Dhabi market charges, what the MoHRE private tuition permit means for anyone teaching your child, how ADEK fits into the picture, and where the boundary sits between legitimate coursework support and academic malpractice. If you only read one section, read the clock.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.programmesIntro: Al Bandar children sit across the full IB continuum, because the nearby school clusters include continuum schools and Diploma-only sixth forms. The three programmes below behave very differently under tutoring, and the right answer for a Year 6 child is nothing like the right answer for a DP2 student eight weeks from final papers.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so tutoring here is diagnostic rather than remedial. The work is reading fluency, number sense, written expression and the inquiry habits that the Middle Years Programme assumes a child already has. Sessions are shorter, usually forty minutes, and framed around a unit of inquiry the child is already doing at school so that nothing feels like a second school day.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Bandar often use PYP support in the Year 5 and Year 6 window, when the question of which secondary route to take becomes live. The continuum schools in Al Raha Gardens and Khalifa City take children straight through; an island school may mean a British route and IGCSE instead. A term of focused number and writing work makes that choice less fraught.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and it is the criterion language that trips students rather than the content. A child who can do the algebra may still lose marks in Criterion C because the communication is thin. Tutoring works best here when it alternates between content gaps and criterion-literate rewriting of the student's own work.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is the moment Al Bandar parents most often come looking. MYP 5 ends with a criterion grade out of seven; Diploma Mathematics at Higher Level assumes fluency the criteria never explicitly tested. Eight to ten weeks of bridging work over the summer, two sessions a week, is the pattern that keeps a student out of trouble in DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the creativity, activity, service strand. The Diploma punishes poor scheduling more than weak ability: internal assessments in four or five subjects land in the same ten weeks, and students who have not planned backwards from those deadlines lose marks they could have kept. Tutoring is part teaching, part calendar management.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts sit the May session, which means the long internal assessment season falls across the Abu Dhabi winter term. For an Al Bandar family that is the window where a weekly online slot earns its keep: no drive, no cancelled session because the Saadiyat road was closed, and a tutor who can read a draft between lessons.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs a career-related study with a small number of Diploma courses, plus a personal and professional skills core and a reflective project. It is less common in Abu Dhabi than the full Diploma, but where a school offers it the DP course components are examined identically, so tutoring for those subjects is the same work at the same standard.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools near Al Bandar run the Career-related Programme, so most families encountering it are looking at a specific sixth form rather than a local default. The reflective project is the component where support is most often wanted, and the boundary there is the same as for the Extended Essay: feedback on the student's own drafting, never drafting on their behalf.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.subjectsIntro: Subject choice drives the tutoring more than level does. The list below is weighted towards what Al Bandar and Al Raha Beach families ask for most, and each line says what the subject actually assesses rather than describing it in general terms.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy route. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and substantially harder calculus, and Paper 3 is a two-problem investigative paper that rewards students who have practised extended reasoning rather than drill questions. Most marks are lost in the move from a correct method to a fully justified one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The graphical display calculator is central, and students who have not automated their calculator work run out of time rather than ideas. Higher Level brings in matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity carry the paper, and the scientific investigation is where grades move most. Students reliably underestimate uncertainty treatment and the requirement to justify a method rather than describe it. Paper 2 extended response needs practised structure, not more content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks. Higher Level organic chemistry demands mechanism fluency that cannot be revised in a fortnight. The scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate real data in school laboratory time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who learn the command terms, and who can distinguish an outline from an explain from a discuss, convert knowledge into marks. Statistical treatment of the investigation data is a common weak point.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published articles form the internal assessment, each capped at 800 words and tied to a different unit. The diagram is where the marks sit: a well-labelled, correctly shifted diagram with explicit reference to the article beats a page of competent prose.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based analysis under time pressure. Students who can select the right framework and apply it to the stimulus material score; students who describe three frameworks do not. Higher Level adds the extended quantitative material many find unexpectedly heavy.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis and the individual oral is assessed on the global issue a student chooses. Preparation is almost entirely practice under time with feedback, which makes it well suited to a weekly online slot and a shared document.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode fluency and the solution development of the internal assessment are the two decisive elements. Higher Level adds resource management and abstract data structures. Students arriving from a programming background often struggle with the paper's formal notation rather than the logic.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: The fieldwork report is the internal assessment and it stands or falls on a researchable question with a defensible sampling method. Paper answers need named case studies with figures attached; generic examples score poorly however well written.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.regionsIntro: Al Bandar does not exist in isolation. The communities below sit within a short drive and share school clusters, traffic patterns and tutoring timing with it, which is why a tutoring plan built for one usually transfers to the next.

regions.name: Al Zeina
regions.note: The neighbouring Al Raha Beach precinct, a few minutes along the same waterfront. Families here use the same Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens schools, so session timing is effectively identical to Al Bandar's.

regions.name: Al Muneera
regions.note: Also part of Al Raha Beach, split between the island and the mainland side. The mainland crossing adds a handful of minutes in the afternoon, which usually means a 4:15 pm rather than a 4:00 pm start.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The villa community immediately inland, and the location of a well-established IB continuum school. Many Al Bandar children are driven here daily, making it the single most relevant school cluster to this page.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Fifteen to twenty minutes inland, with the densest concentration of British and American curriculum schools near Al Bandar. A large share of Al Bandar secondary students finish their day here.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Across the bridge network and roughly half an hour away in afternoon traffic. Saadiyat school families are the ones for whom an online slot most obviously beats waiting for a tutor to arrive.

regions.name: Yas Island

sections.heading: What "IB home tutor in Al Bandar" returns, and what it should return
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result: agencies with a city-wide page and no mention of Al Raha Beach, marketplace listings priced in US dollars, and classified adverts from individuals. None of them answers the question an Al Bandar parent is actually asking, which is narrower than it looks. It is not "can someone teach my child the Diploma". It is "can someone who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level be in front of my child at five o'clock on a Tuesday, every Tuesday, for the next two terms".

Those are different questions and they have different answers. The first has a large supply. The second has almost none within driving distance of a specific waterfront precinct, because the constraint is not teaching talent, it is the intersection of three things: the right subject, the right level, and a willingness to spend ninety minutes in a car for a sixty-minute lesson. Shrink the geography and you shrink the subject list. An Al Bandar family looking for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Economics with a commentary deadline in three weeks, will usually find the local pool has nobody.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the travel requirement and keep everything else. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen, in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the subject and level rather than for an address. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Said plainly, that is a smaller promise than the search phrase implies and a more useful one, because the version a parent wants is a specialist at a reliable time, and that is deliverable every week of the year.

The rest of this page is built on that premise. It starts with the clock, because in Al Bandar the clock is the binding constraint, and ends with the things nobody in this market writes down: what the Abu Dhabi rate bands really are, who is legally permitted to tutor here, and what a tutor may and may not do with a piece of assessed coursework.

sections.heading: The Al Bandar school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: The table below is the practical core of this page. It pairs the schools Al Bandar families most often use with an indicative finish time, an honest afternoon drive estimate back to Al Raha Beach, and the earliest session start that leaves room for a glass of water and a laptop. Times are indicative and your own school's timetable is the authority; bus routes in particular add fifteen to twenty-five minutes over a private car.

Two patterns fall out of it. Families using Al Raha Gardens or Khalifa City can realistically run a four o'clock session, which means homework still happens at a civilised hour and the evening is not spent catching up. Families using Saadiyat, Al Reem or Al Bateen cannot, and should plan on five or later. Pretending otherwise produces a slot that gets cancelled twice a month, and a cancelled slot teaches nothing.

The second pattern matters more for Diploma students. A five o'clock start after a forty-minute drive means the student arrives at the lesson already tired, which is survivable for revision practice and poor for new content. Where a student at an island school needs new teaching rather than consolidation, the better answer is a weekend morning slot, with the weekday session kept for past-paper work and questions arising from school. Several Al Bandar families run exactly that split across DP2.

Ramadan rearranges all of it. School days shorten, and the productive hours move to the late evening after Iftar. Online delivery absorbs that change without negotiation: the slot moves, the tutor is still available, and nobody is driving across the city at nine at night. Families here typically shift to a 9:00 pm or 9:30 pm start for the month and return to the earlier slot afterwards.

sections.heading: Why the next precinct over gets the same answer
paragraphs: Al Zeina is four minutes from Al Bandar. Al Muneera is barely further. A parent in any of the three will, at some point, ask whether moving the search one precinto over widens the pool of people who might drive to them. It does not, and the reason is arithmetic rather than opinion.

Start with the subject. A Diploma student takes six subjects at two levels, which is a dozen teachable combinations before you count the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Add the four main science and maths routes, the three language A options and the group three subjects and the realistic combination count runs well past thirty. Now ask how many people within a fifteen-minute drive of Al Raha Beach have taught any one of those combinations to examination standard. For the common ones, a handful. For Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the term the exploration is due, frequently none.

This is why the honest version of a neighbourhood tutoring page says the same thing about every neighbourhood. The local pool is thin everywhere, including in the places that look dense, because density of population is not density of Higher Level Chemistry teachers. The variable that actually changes between Al Bandar, Al Zeina and Al Raha Gardens is the drive time to school, which is what the previous section measured, and not the availability of a specialist.

Removing the travel constraint changes the pool from "people near Al Raha Beach" to "people who teach this subject at this level and are free at this hour". That is a materially larger set, and it is the only change that reliably produces a tutor who has marked the paper your child is about to sit. Everything else is a negotiation about who spends the forty minutes in the car.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition compared for an Al Bandar family
paragraphs: Market rates in Abu Dhabi and Dubai are published unevenly, and three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. The figures in the table are market bands drawn from competitor-published rates and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges; our own position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted rate after the match is made.

The in-home column is the one worth reading twice. A visiting tutor's hourly rate carries the travel inside it, which is why the band sits above the online band rather than alongside it: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. For an Al Bandar address the travel component is real, because the pool of willing visitors is small enough to price accordingly.

Group tuition looks cheapest per student and often is, but it only works where three or four students are genuinely at the same point in the same syllabus. In Al Bandar, where neighbouring children are frequently at three different schools on two different curricula, that condition is harder to meet than it sounds. Where it does hold, usually among siblings or close school friends in the same set, a small group is good value for revision and poor value for repairing a content gap.

The last column is the one families underuse. Ask what is actually included: whether the hour is teaching time or includes setting up, whether marked work between sessions is extra, whether a missed session is lost or carried. Two providers quoting the same number can differ by a third once that is settled.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: This is the question Al Bandar parents ask least often and should ask first. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the Ministry's own service page for it, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. Teachers registered in government or private schools qualify, as do employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the published material does not set out a fine schedule, so no amount can honestly be quoted here.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. That matters because "your child's own teacher, privately" is a proposition that circulates in parent groups across Khalifa City and Al Raha Beach every examination season. It is the one arrangement an Abu Dhabi family should not make, however well intentioned.

The practical check is short. Ask whether the person teaching your child holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, ask to see it, and ask whether they teach at your child's own school. A tutor who cannot answer the first question has not done the paperwork; one who answers yes to the third is proposing something ADEK's rules do not allow.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection reports and what they tell an Al Bandar parent
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai families deal with KHDA, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Al Bandar is squarely in ADEK territory, and ADEK is named by almost nobody writing about tutoring in this market.

The reason it matters to a tutoring decision is that the inspection report tells you where a school is weak, which is a better guide to what your child needs than any amount of general advice. A report that marks teaching strong but assessment practice weaker tells you the school will teach the content and your child may still misread what the examiner wants. That is exactly the gap a weekly one-to-one slot closes, and it is diagnosable from a public document.

The federal baseline sits underneath all of this. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So an Al Bandar child on the Diploma is also carrying mandatory UAE subjects, scheduled into the same week, and those lessons compete for the same afternoon hours as everything else. Any realistic tutoring plan accounts for them rather than ignoring them.

IB Gram holds no regulator approval and claims none. We are not approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and any page telling you otherwise about any provider is worth distrusting. What we can do is read the same public documents you can and build the teaching plan around what they say.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: Every Diploma student has assessed work that must be their own: a mathematical exploration, scientific investigations, an Economics commentary set, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. Those components are substantial fractions of the final grade and they are produced away from an examination hall, which is why the academic-honesty rules around them are strict and why the boundary needs stating plainly on a page like this one.

What a tutor may do: teach the underlying content, explain the published assessment criteria, ask the questions a moderator would ask, point out where an argument does not follow, flag a referencing convention that has gone wrong, and talk through how to narrow a research question until it is answerable. All of that is teaching, and all of it leaves the student holding the pen.

What a tutor may not do is produce the assessment. No tutor should draft the exploration, rewrite a paragraph of the Extended Essay into its final form, or supply a finished commentary for a student to submit. There is a market for exactly that in this region, priced in the thousands of dirhams, and a student who buys it is risking a malpractice finding that can cost the whole Diploma. We will not do it, and we say so here because it is a real differentiator in this search result rather than a disclaimer.

Practically, that shapes how coursework sessions run. The student sends a draft before the lesson. The tutor reads it and comes with questions, criterion references and a short list of things to fix. The student then fixes them, in their own words, and the next session starts from the revised version. Schools can be told exactly that, and often appreciate being told.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started has four steps and one uncomfortable possibility. You tell us the subject, the level, the school and the deadline that is worrying you. We look for a tutor who has taught that exact combination and is free in a slot that works after the Al Bandar school run. You take a free trial lesson. If it works, a weekly slot is set; if the chemistry is wrong, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persevere.

The uncomfortable possibility is that for a narrow combination in a busy week, nobody suitable is free. A Higher Level Computer Science student needing help with solution development in the fortnight before an internal deadline is a genuinely scarce request. When that happens we say so, give an honest estimate of when a slot opens, and offer the nearest useful alternative rather than putting a generalist in front of the student and hoping. Concealing a coverage gap is how families end up paying for a term of nothing.

Timing the start is its own decision. Six weeks before a mock is enough to change an outcome; six days is enough to change technique and not content. For a Diploma student the two high-value windows are the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, and the long internal assessment season in the winter term of DP2. For an Al Bandar family both are periods when the school run is at its most disruptive, which is the practical argument for a format that does not depend on anyone arriving.

There is no obligation attached to the trial lesson and no card required to book it. If the answer after it is that your child needs a different subject supported, or nothing at the moment, that is a perfectly good outcome and we would rather reach it in week one than in week eight.

The purpose is to test the match: does the tutor read this particular student well, and does the slot survive a real Tuesday. Both questions are answered faster by doing it than by discussing it.

process.description: A weekly time is set and work is keyed to the school's own assessment calendar. Every few weeks the plan is reviewed against what the school has actually set, and the format shifts between weekly, twice-weekly and coursework coaching as the term demands.

whyPoints.description: The sessions are planned from the school finish time and the drive back to Al Raha Beach, not from a generic timetable. That is why the clock table on this page exists: a slot that ignores the Saadiyat run gets cancelled, and a cancelled slot is worse than no slot because it also costs the family the plan.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Al Bandar who comes to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one and delivered live online, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that service exists only in India. Independent visiting tutors do work in Al Raha Beach and the market band for them runs roughly AED 180-500 per hour with travel priced in. The trade-off is subject choice: the pool willing to drive to one precinct is small, so a family needing Higher Level Chemistry or a specific maths route usually finds nobody locally available at a usable hour.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Al Bandar on a school day?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which school. Children at Al Raha Gardens or Khalifa City schools are usually home in time for a four o'clock start. Children at Saadiyat, Al Reem or Al Bateen schools are in a car for thirty to forty-five minutes, so five o'clock or later is the honest answer. School buses add another fifteen to twenty-five minutes over a private car. We set the slot from your actual finish time rather than a standard one, because a slot that is twenty minutes too early gets cancelled twice a month and then abandoned.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Bandar children usually attend?
faqs.answer: The nearest cluster is Al Raha Gardens, which includes an established IB continuum school, followed by the British and American schools of Khalifa City about fifteen to twenty minutes inland. Beyond that, a sizeable number of Al Bandar families drive to Saadiyat Island, Al Reem Island or Al Bateen for a specific school and accept the commute. Al Reef, towards the airport road, is also in regular use. Schools are named on this page as catchment context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Does ADEK regulate tutoring in Al Bandar as well as schools?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, which covers the schools your child attends rather than an individual tutor. Private tutoring itself is permitted through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. ADEK's professional-ethics rules do reach tutoring in one important respect: school staff in the emirate are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. IB Gram holds no ADEK approval and does not claim any.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as useful for an IB student as someone sitting beside them?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-level work it usually works better, for a specific reason: the hour is spent on a shared screen with the student's own draft, past paper or exploration open, annotated in real time, and the recording is there afterwards. The teaching also stops depending on who lives within twenty minutes. Younger children, particularly in the Primary Years Programme, often do need an adult physically present to stay on task, and in those cases a shorter session with a parent nearby works better than a long one.

faqs.question: How much does IB tutoring cost for a family in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with named or examiner-tier tutors quoted as high as AED 650. In-home visits sit at AED 180-500 because travel is inside the rate. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market bands, not IB Gram prices; our own rate is quoted after the match is made and the trial lesson is free.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 to DP1 next year. When should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: The summer between the two is the highest-value window, and it is the one most families miss. MYP criteria are marked out of eight per strand and tested things the Diploma assumes rather than re-teaching, particularly in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Eight to ten weeks of twice-weekly bridging work, aimed squarely at algebraic fluency and formal reasoning, prevents the DP1 autumn term from becoming a repair job. Starting in October instead means competing with new content for the same hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration or the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor can teach the content, explain each published criterion, challenge a research question that is too broad to answer, point out where reasoning does not hold, and check referencing conventions. A tutor cannot produce the work. No exploration, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is drafted or finished on a student's behalf, because a candidate who submits someone else's writing risks a malpractice finding against the whole Diploma. The student keeps authorship at every stage and the draft history shows it.

faqs.question: Do tutors teaching my child need a UAE permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. School teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen are all eligible to apply. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see the permit, and ask separately whether the person teaches at your child's own school.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the tutoring week in Al Bandar?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, afternoons become unproductive and the useful study hours move to after Iftar. Families here commonly shift the weekly slot to around nine or half past nine in the evening for the month and return to the earlier time afterwards. Because delivery is online, that change costs nothing and requires no one to travel late at night. It is worth planning two weeks ahead rather than in the first week, particularly where internal assessment drafts fall inside the month.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Mathematics and Physics is the most common workable pairing, as is Chemistry with Biology at Standard Level. The limit is depth: a tutor strong enough in Higher Level organic chemistry to be worth the hour is rarely the same person who should be marking a Language and Literature Paper 1. Where a pairing works, it saves scheduling effort and gives one person sight of the whole workload. Where it does not, two specialists in two slots is the better answer.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's subject in Al Bandar?
faqs.answer: We say so. For a narrow combination in a busy week, such as Higher Level Computer Science during the solution-development crunch, nobody suitable may be available immediately. You get an honest estimate of when a slot opens and the nearest useful alternative, rather than a generalist placed in front of the student to fill the gap. Concealed coverage limits are common in this market and they cost families a term. We would rather lose the booking than take it on a pretence.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi IB students sit exams in May or November?
faqs.answer: Diploma cohorts at Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, which is why the long internal assessment season falls across the winter term here. For Cambridge qualifications the position is different and worth knowing if a sibling is on a British route: UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Confirm every specific IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on the IB's own site, because published windows are revised.

faqs.question: Will my child's school know we are using a tutor, and should it?
faqs.answer: There is no requirement to tell the school, but on coursework it usually helps. Telling a Diploma coordinator that an external tutor is giving criterion-level feedback on the student's own drafts is straightforward, and it removes any ambiguity later about authorship. We keep a short record of what each coursework session covered for exactly that reason. What a school will object to is undisclosed help that blurs who wrote what, which is also the thing we decline to provide.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for Al Bandar families?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and for revision it can be good value. The condition is that everyone in the group is at the same point in the same syllabus with the same board, and in Al Bandar that is harder than it sounds because neighbouring children are often at three schools on two curricula. Siblings and close school friends in the same set are where it works. For repairing a content gap, a group dilutes the one thing you are paying for, which is attention aimed at a specific weakness.

Those two numbers decide whether a four o'clock session is real or aspirational, and they matter more than any provider's description of itself. Tell us the subject, the level, the school and the deadline that is worrying you, and we will find a tutor who has taught that exact combination and is free in a slot that survives the afternoon. intro.heading: The district comparison every Al Bateen parent runs
paragraphs: Al Bateen is one of the older parts of Abu Dhabi island: villa compounds and government housing on the western shore, the marina, the executive airport, and an embassy district spilling into Al Rawdah. Families here have two IB Diploma schools close at hand and several more within a short drive. So the search for help starts geographically, and the comparison that follows is almost always with the three districts immediately around it.

Al Khalidiyah sits inland from Al Bateen: apartment towers, a dense retail spine, shorter distances and a younger rental population. The Corniche runs along the water to the north with high-rise living and no villa stock to speak of. Al Mushrif lies across the island, inland and residential, with the longest-established British curriculum school in the emirate on its doorstep. Four districts, four different housing profiles, four different school catchments, all within fifteen minutes of each other in light traffic.

A parent reasonably assumes that these differences should change the answer about tutoring. They change some things. Session start times differ, because a child walking home in Al Khalidiyah is at a desk earlier than a child collected from a bus route that loops the western shore. Tutor density differs, because a visiting tutor working towers can fit several sessions into one evening and a tutor working villa compounds cannot. School catchment differs, which changes which subjects come up and which internal deadlines bite when.

What they do not change is the binding constraint. For an IB Diploma student the thing in short supply is not a tutor within walking distance, it is a tutor who has taught that subject at that level and supervised that internal assessment. Higher Level Chemistry, Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, Higher Level Language B, Computer Science: these are thin across the whole Gulf, not just across one island district. A parent in Al Bateen optimising for proximity and a parent in Al Mushrif optimising for proximity are both choosing from a short list, and the two short lists barely overlap with the list of people who teach the component in question.

Hence the structure of this page, and the honest position on delivery. In-home visits are not a service IB Gram sells anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India, and nobody will arrive at an Al Bateen address from us. What a family gets instead is a specialist matched to the subject and level, a session that starts when the student is actually ready to work, and a rate with no driving inside it. The district comparison in the first section is included because it is the comparison parents run, and because running it properly is what shows where the real constraint sits.
