abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes turn up in these districts, and a parent comparing neighbourhoods should know which one the nearby schools actually run before drawing conclusions about convenience.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside them. Each subject is marked out of 7, giving 42, and the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay adds up to three further points for a maximum of 45. Every subject includes internally assessed work, submitted to internal deadlines a school sets well ahead of the board's.
programmes.countryNote: Al Bateen sits close to two Diploma schools, which is unusual density for an Abu Dhabi district and the reason Diploma enquiries from here arrive earlier in Year 12 than from most of the emirate. UAE schools sit the May session. The practical effect of local density is more peer comparison and more accurate expectations, not more available specialists: the Higher Level Chemistry supervisor shortage is identical here and in Al Mushrif.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria on a one-to-eight scale rather than by examination, with a Personal Project in the final year. Because marking is criterion-referenced, a student can know the content well and still score poorly by not addressing the criterion wording. That is a specific, teachable problem and it is different in kind from anything an examination course presents.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between island districts often move between a Middle Years school and a British curriculum one, and the transition is where a year gets lost. A child coming out of criterion marking into Year 10 IGCSE, or out of IGCSE into Diploma Year 1, meets a different assessment logic rather than harder content. Support in that term is about the new rules, not about revision.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, finishing with an exhibition project. Assessment is formative and descriptive rather than graded, so parents reading a report often cannot tell where their child sits against a standard. Tutoring at this stage is about reading fluency, number fluency and the habits that make the Middle Years Programme manageable.
programmes.countryNote: Al Bateen and the Corniche both have primary provision within walking distance for many families, which is one of the genuine advantages of the island's older districts. It matters less than parents expect for tutoring, because at this age the useful support is short, frequent and content-light, and a screen session of thirty minutes is perfectly workable for reading and number work.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.subjectsIntro: Diploma subject choice decides how hard a match is to make, and it does not vary by district. The grid below names the components that create the demand, with where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits Paper 1 without technology and Paper 2 with it; Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper, and reduces each written paper's share. The exploration carries a fifth of the grade at both levels. Higher Level Paper 3 is the component with the thinnest tutoring supply in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is permitted on every paper, which moves the difficulty from manipulation to modelling and interpretation. Students who chose this route expecting an easier course find the statistics and modelling content substantial. The exploration criteria are identical to the Analysis route, so supervision needs are the same.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry, energetics and the data-based questions are where Higher Level grades move. The internal assessment is a student-designed investigation, and the common failure is scope rather than chemistry: a question too broad to control variables for. Supervision here is a short, early intervention, not a year of sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The written papers reward disciplined use of defined quantities and units, and the internal assessment rewards uncertainty handling that most students have never been taught properly. Higher Level cover is thin across the Gulf, so this is the subject where insisting on a local tutor costs the most.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and conceptually approachable, which makes structured recall and command-term discipline the highest-value work. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments are the reliable discriminator, and they are practised rather than learned. The internal assessment needs an early conversation about measurable variables.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Internally assessed commentaries on published news articles, each tied to a syllabus section, plus written papers that reward diagram accuracy and evaluation. Coaching the commentary process without touching the student's writing is straightforward and is where most of the available marks sit.

subjects.name: English Language A and Language B
subjects.description: Language A includes an Individual Oral built on a global issue explored through two extracts, which is the most structurally coachable component in the Diploma. Language B at Higher Level is among the hardest matches to make in the region, particularly for less commonly taught languages.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries running to about 950 words, and an essay of roughly 1,600 words on one of the IB's prescribed titles. Combined with the Extended Essay it is worth up to three points. Students lose marks by describing knowledge rather than examining how it is produced.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word research essay in a subject the student chooses, assessed on five criteria worth 34 marks in total. The supervisor relationship is formal and recorded. A tutor's legitimate role is process coaching - question framing, source critique, structure - and nothing beyond it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A solution developed and documented over months, plus written papers on systems and algorithms. Supply across the Gulf is thin enough that families should plan support early rather than discover the shortage in the term the solution is due.

sections.heading: Al Bateen against Al Khalidiyah, the Corniche and Al Mushrif
paragraphs: Run the comparison on the things that actually differ. Housing type, school catchment, how a child gets home, and how many households a visiting tutor can reach in one evening. Those four variables explain most of what a parent notices when comparing quotes between island districts.

Al Bateen's profile is villa compounds and collection rather than walking, with two Diploma schools nearby. That combination means accurate local expectations about the Diploma and a slightly later realistic start to a school-night session. Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche are towers: shorter journeys home, earlier desk time, and a visiting tutor able to serve several households in one building. Al Mushrif is inland villas with a strong British curriculum presence, so its subject mix skews away from the Diploma and its Diploma families travel across the island.

Those differences are real and they do change a schedule. What they do not change is who is available to teach Higher Level Chemistry on a Tuesday evening. The supply of Diploma subject specialists in Abu Dhabi is thin at Higher Level in the sciences, very thin in Computer Science and in Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, and thin for Higher Level Language B. None of that scarcity is distributed by district. It is a regional shortage, and moving four kilometres inland does not touch it.

So the comparison converges. A family in Al Bateen weighing proximity against specialism, and a family in Al Mushrif doing the same, both discover that the local shortlist is short and that it is short for the same reason. sections.heading: Why the comparison ends in the same place
paragraphs: The arithmetic behind that last column is worth stating, because it is the whole argument of this page and it is not obvious from a list of neighbourhoods.

Start from the subject. A Diploma student needs help with one named subject at one named level, and often with one named component inside it: the exploration, Paper 3, the data-based questions, the Individual Oral. The number of people in the Gulf who have taught that component to that level is not large. Filter that group for the ones willing to drive to a villa compound on the western shore of Abu Dhabi island on a weekday evening, and the number becomes very small indeed - frequently zero for the scarce components.

Now reverse the filter. Keep the subject requirement and drop the geography. The group is the same size it was before any filtering, because delivery over live video does not care which side of the island a student is on. That is not a marketing argument, it is just what happens to a set when you stop intersecting it with a travel radius. For broad, well-covered subjects the difference is modest, which is why in-home tutoring remains a reasonable purchase for Year 9 mathematics. For a Higher Level Chemistry internal assessment it is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

A second effect follows. Because the online pool is larger, the session can sit where the student works best rather than where the tutor's route allows. An Al Bateen student collected from school once lessons finish is realistically at a desk a little later than a child who walks home in Al Khalidiyah, and a session at seven that holds attention beats a session at nine that does not. Removing the drive is what makes the earlier slot available at all.

sections.heading: The Diploma core, criterion by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes an assessment criterion with its mark allocation. That absence is odd, because the criteria are the specification for the piece of work a student is being marked on, and a Diploma student who has not read them is writing blind.

The Extended Essay is the clearest case. It is capped at 4,000 words and assessed on five criteria worth 34 marks in total: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking alone carries 12 marks, more than a third of the total, which tells a student where the work belongs. Most first drafts over-invest in knowledge and understanding, which is worth 6, and under-invest in the analysis the largest criterion is actually asking for.

Theory of Knowledge splits into two assessed pieces: an exhibition of three objects with commentaries running to about 950 words, and an essay of roughly 1,600 words on one of the IB's prescribed titles. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points toward the 45-point maximum, which is routinely the margin between a conditional offer and a rejection. The common failure in both pieces is describing what is known rather than examining how it came to be known.

Subject internal assessments follow the same pattern: published criteria, published mark allocations, and a student who scores badly against a criterion they never read. The useful intervention is not content teaching. It is reading the criteria aloud beside the student's own draft and asking which sentence is earning which mark. That takes an hour and it is the single highest-value hour available in the Diploma core.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Abu Dhabi, compared honestly
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in this emirate is a real service with a real case behind it, and the comparison deserves to be made without spin. Published rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. What that buys is physical presence, which for a younger child or a disengaged teenager can be the factor that decides whether any work happens at all.

The costs sit in three places. Travel is inside the rate, and for a villa compound in Al Bateen that is a one-session evening for the tutor, priced accordingly. Tutor choice narrows to people who accept the drive. And scheduling bends to the tutor's route rather than to the student's attention, which on a school night matters more than most parents allow for.

IB Gram's position is stated plainly rather than implied: home visits are not part of what we sell in the UAE - that is an India-only service - and no tutor will arrive at an Al Bateen address from us. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, with the student's own written work on screen and the marking criteria beside it. For Diploma work in particular, where most of the session is spent reading and annotating the student's own draft, the shared screen is closer to how the work is actually done than a kitchen table is.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the emirates
paragraphs: A parent comparing districts within Abu Dhabi is working inside one regulator's territory, but families in this country move between emirates often enough that the map is worth having. It is also a map almost nobody in this market publishes: ADEK is named by none of the researched competitor pages and Sharjah's authority by one.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai falls under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge in the same role. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The depth of those powers is worth noting. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. Underneath all of it is a federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

Two things follow for a family in Al Bateen. Read a school's inspection outcome on ADEK's own listing rather than on any tutoring page, including this one. And treat any provider claiming approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson with real scepticism - that phrase is the most dangerous one available in this market, and IB Gram holds none of those designations and claims none.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an internal assessment
paragraphs: The Diploma puts more assessed work in the student's own hands than any school qualification a parent is likely to have sat themselves, and that makes the honesty boundary a practical question rather than an abstract one. It is worth being specific, because the market is not clean.

Inside the line: teaching the subject content the work depends on, explaining the assessment criteria, discussing whether a research question is answerable, critiquing a source, pointing at a weak paragraph and asking what it is trying to prove, modelling an analysis on a different example, and giving written feedback the student then acts on alone. All of that is teaching, it is what a school supervisor does, and it is what improves a mark legitimately.

Outside the line, without exception: producing text that is submitted as the student's own, editing a draft to completion, supplying an exploration or an essay, or working on the piece while the student watches. One operator found in this market sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price. A family buying that is buying an academic-honesty investigation, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. Any provider who answers the question with anything other than a flat refusal should come off the shortlist on that answer alone.

Two adjacent boundaries belong with it. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards and should be cited and linked rather than reproduced and distributed. And a tutor should not be described as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, nor should examiner status be used to imply any access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content. None of these is a difficult question; all are worth asking in a first conversation.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma shape, and when to intervene
paragraphs: A parent in any of these districts gets the timing question wrong in the same direction: help is bought too late in Year 13 and almost never in the term it would have done the most good. The Diploma is a two-year structure with a predictable set of pressure points, and knowing them is worth more than knowing a rate.

The first pressure point is the start of Diploma Year 1, when a student coming out of the Middle Years Programme or IGCSE meets a different assessment logic. Marks drop, and the drop is usually about command terms and mark schemes rather than about content. A short block here, built from the first marked piece of Diploma work, prevents a year of quiet underperformance. Almost nobody buys it.

The second is the middle of Diploma Year 1 into the first term of Year 2, when internal assessments and the Extended Essay compete with each other and with subject teaching. The risk here is a deadline, not a topic. Light supervision across months - reading criteria against drafts, keeping the Extended Essay reflections current rather than written retrospectively - costs less than any subject block and protects the three core points.

The third is the final months before the May session, when coursework should already be finished and the work is full papers under timing. Buying subject help at this point is reasonable and widely done, but a family arriving here with unfinished internal assessments is paying specialist rates to fix a scheduling failure. The cheapest version of Diploma support is the one that happens on time, which is an unglamorous thing for a tutoring page to say and the truest thing on it.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Higher Level Chemistry internal assessment, Standard Level Analysis and Approaches exploration, Language A Individual Oral. That specificity decides who can help and distinguishes a real match from a general Diploma tutor. It also tells a parent immediately whether they are in a thin-supply component.

process.title: Bring the marked work and the criteria
process.description: Returned subject work with the school's comments, and the criteria sheet for whichever component is in question. A first session spent reading those two documents together is worth more than a session spent on content, because it shows exactly which marks are being missed and why.

process.title: Free trial lesson, before anything is paid
process.description: One session per student, booked without card details. It is a diagnosis rather than an introduction: the student explains their own reasoning on their own work while the tutor listens for where the understanding stops. You leave knowing whether the problem is content, technique or timing.

process.title: A plan with the school's dates in it
process.description: Sessions are scheduled against the school's internal deadlines and mock window rather than against a generic term plan. For Diploma students those internal dates are earlier than the board's and are the ones that actually bite, so the plan is built from the school calendar outward.

process.title: Review against marked work, then stop or continue
process.description: After a defined block, the same kind of marked evidence is compared with what was there at the start. Anything not producing a visible change is removed rather than renewed. For core supervision the test is whether deadlines are being met, which is a yes or a no.

process.title: If the specialist is not free, you are told
process.description: Cover for Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Computer Science, Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 and Higher Level Language B is thin across the Gulf. Where no suitable tutor has a workable slot, that is stated with the expected wait rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The district comparison is run, not dismissed
whyPoints.description: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, the Corniche and Al Mushrif differ in housing, journey home and in-home economics, and this page sets those differences out rather than waving them away. It also shows the one column where all four are identical, which is the column that decides a Diploma match.

whyPoints.title: Criteria published with their marks
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay's five criteria appear here with their mark allocations, including the 12 marks on critical thinking that most first drafts under-serve. No researched competitor page in this market publishes a single assessment criterion with its marks.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over live video, the tutor comes from everyone who has taught that subject at that level rather than from the few who will drive to the western shore on a weekday. For the scarce Diploma components that is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled to the school's own deadlines
whyPoints.description: Diploma internal deadlines are set by the school and fall earlier than the board's. Plans are built from those dates outward, because the common Diploma failure is a missed submission rather than a weak topic, and no amount of subject teaching fixes a missed submission.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated in detail
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may do with an internal assessment is set out line by line here, because at least one operator in this market sells completed coursework outright. The consequence of that purchase falls on the student, which is why the boundary is printed rather than assumed.

whyPoints.title: No claimed accreditation, no UAE premises
whyPoints.description: IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and occupies no office, centre or branch in the UAE. A parent who knows exactly what a provider is can judge it accurately.

faqs.question: Is Al Bateen better served for IB tutoring than Al Khalidiyah?
faqs.answer: For schools, Al Bateen has an advantage: Diploma teaching sits close by on the western shore, which Al Khalidiyah does not match within walking distance. For tutoring the two districts are equivalent, because the constraint is who has taught the specific subject at the specific level rather than who lives nearby. Al Khalidiyah does have one practical edge: towers mean shorter journeys home and therefore an earlier realistic start to a school-night session. That timing difference matters more than it sounds, and it disappears entirely once sessions run online.

faqs.question: Do tutors move between Al Bateen and Al Mushrif on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Rarely for one session. The drive across the island is short in theory and unpredictable at the end of the school day, and a visiting tutor who commits to a villa compound in one district has effectively committed their evening to it. That is why in-home rates in villa areas sit toward the upper end of the published AED 180 to 500 band while tower districts support several sessions a night. Dropping the travel requirement removes the problem rather than solving it.

faqs.question: Which IB Diploma schools are closest to Al Bateen?
faqs.answer: Diploma teaching sits on the western shore itself, with further Diploma provision across the bridges in the Saadiyat and mainland clusters, and the emirate's long-established British curriculum school inland in Al Mushrif. The practical point for a tutoring plan is that local density changes expectations rather than supply: families here hear accurate things about the Diploma from neighbours, which is genuinely useful, but the shortage of Higher Level science supervisors is identical across every Abu Dhabi district.

faqs.question: Together, how many points are the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge worth?
faqs.answer: Up to three, which sit on top of the 42 available from six subjects marked out of 7, for a maximum of 45. Those three points come from the combination of the two core pieces rather than from either alone, and they are routinely the margin between meeting a conditional offer and missing it. That is why core supervision is better value than most subject blocks: a small, well-timed investment protects points that are otherwise lost to deadlines and to criteria nobody read.

faqs.question: What are the Extended Essay assessment criteria and their marks?
faqs.answer: Five criteria totalling 34 marks: focus and method at 6, knowledge and understanding at 6, critical thinking at 12, presentation at 4, and engagement at 6. The distribution is the useful information. Critical thinking alone is more than a third of the total, so analysis and evaluation are where the work belongs, while knowledge and understanding caps at 6 no matter how much context a student writes. Most first drafts invert that balance, which is the single most common reason a competent essay scores modestly.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student in Al Bateen start the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because the engagement criterion rewards reflections written across the process rather than assembled at the end. The practical sequence is to settle a narrow, answerable question first, then read widely enough to know the question survives contact with the sources, then write. Students who begin late almost always have a question too broad for 4,000 words, and broadening or narrowing it afterwards costs more time than starting properly did. Your child's school sets internal deadlines well before the board's.

faqs.question: Can a tutor review my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the most useful hours available. A tutor may read the draft against the published criteria, point at a paragraph and ask what mark it is earning, question whether the variables are controllable, critique a source, and give written feedback the student then acts on alone. What a tutor may not do is write, edit to completion or supply any part of it. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; buying that risks the qualification itself, and the risk lands on the student.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level different enough from Standard Level to need its own tutor?
faqs.answer: In the sciences and in mathematics, yes. Higher Level adds content and, in mathematics, a third paper that changes the whole character of the preparation. More importantly it changes what the examiner expects from the same question. A tutor who teaches Standard Level confidently is not automatically useful at Higher Level, and the honest ones say so. When you ask about a match, specify the level and ask directly whether that tutor has taught it and supervised its internal assessment.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor who lives on Abu Dhabi island?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work, no, and insisting on it is usually counterproductive. The session is mostly spent reading and annotating the student's own written work with the marking criteria beside it, which works at least as well on a shared screen as across a table. Local knowledge matters for school deadlines and timing, and that lives in the plan rather than in the tutor's address. Requiring an island address narrows a thin pool to a very thin one, exactly in the components where depth matters most.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Bateen session realistically start on a school night?
faqs.answer: Later than in the tower districts, because most children here are collected rather than walking home, and earlier than an in-home visit allows, because there is no drive to absorb. In practice a slot from the late afternoon onward works, in Gulf Standard Time, and the useful rule is to place the session while attention is still available rather than after dinner. During Ramadan the standard adjustment is to move sessions to after Iftar, which online delivery makes straightforward.

faqs.question: How does Abu Dhabi's school regulator differ from Dubai's?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai falls under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah have their own authorities, which also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Read any school's inspection outcome on its own regulator's site.

faqs.question: How many Diploma subjects should a family support at once?
faqs.answer: Fewer than instinct suggests. A sensible shape is one Higher Level subject where the gap is real, plus core supervision across months, and nothing else until marked work shows another genuine need. Supporting all six subjects simultaneously costs at the top of the specialist band and still leaves the coursework late, because the limiting factor in Diploma Year 2 is the student's available hours rather than the quality of teaching available to them. Start narrow and widen only against evidence.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma genuinely harder than IGCSE or A Levels?
faqs.answer: It is broader rather than simply harder. Six subjects plus three core components means more simultaneous deadlines than a three-subject A Level programme, and the internally assessed work is substantial in every subject. Depth at Higher Level is comparable to A Level in the same subject; the difference is that a Diploma student is carrying five other courses alongside it. That breadth is why Diploma failures are usually organisational rather than academic, and why timing is the thing worth paying attention to.

faqs.question: What if we move from Al Bateen to a mainland community mid-year?
faqs.answer: A move across the emirate changes the school run and nothing else about the tutoring, provided sessions already run online. That is a quiet advantage of online delivery that families only notice when it applies: an in-home arrangement usually ends with a move, because the tutor's route no longer works, and a replacement has to be found in the middle of a Diploma year. If the school changes too, the plan is rebuilt around the new internal deadlines, which differ between schools.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue through the summer and while the family travels?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the time zone adjusted to wherever the student is. Many island families spend part of the summer abroad, and for a Diploma student that period is often the best available window for the Extended Essay, when no subject teaching is competing for attention. The honest caveat is that a student who has worked hard all year benefits from a genuine break, so the sensible plan is a short, defined block rather than an unbroken schedule across the holiday.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingHeading: Run the comparison, then choose on the subject
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingBody: Comparing Al Bateen with Al Khalidiyah, the Corniche or Al Mushrif is a reasonable thing to do, and the differences in housing, journey home and in-home economics are real. The column that decides a Diploma outcome is the one where all four districts read the same: who has taught that subject at that level and supervised that internal assessment. Book the free trial, bring the marked work and the criteria sheet, and the first conversation will be about which component is losing marks rather than about which side of the island anyone lives on. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Al Falah who actually knows the Diploma? The honest version
paragraphs: Al Falah is a planned villa community out towards the airport road, a good distance from the island and from the Khalifa City and Al Raha school belt where most of Abu Dhabi's IB capacity sits. A parent here searching for an IB home tutor is asking a supply question, and the honest answer is uncomfortable: the number of people living within a reasonable drive of Al Falah who can teach a named Diploma subject at a named level is small. Not zero, and not the number a directory listing implies.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do aloud. The IB Diploma has six subject groups and most subjects run at two levels, so a single student's timetable represents six separate specialisms. A tutor who teaches the Diploma is never a tutor who teaches the Diploma; they teach Chemistry Higher Level, or Analysis and Approaches Standard Level, or English A Language and Literature. Multiply six subjects by two levels and then intersect that with people willing to drive to Al Falah on a weekday evening, and the pool for any given request thins out quickly. For common requests such as mathematics or biology it holds up. For Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, Visual Arts, Arabic A Literature or Digital Society, it does not.

This is the point in a conversation where most providers become vague, because scarcity is awkward to publish. None of the competitor pages measured for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a phone number from another country. So here is the position stated plainly. IB Gram is an online platform. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Being online is what makes the subject match possible: an Al Falah family chooses from every specialist on the roster rather than from whoever is nearby, and if a subject is still not covered we say so and tell you the expected wait.

The rest of this page is built to make you a harder customer to fool. It sets out which IB subjects are actually scarce and what the realistic match time is for each, what the Diploma's assessment architecture looks like component by component, how the mathematics exploration is marked criterion by criterion, and a twenty-minute script you can use on any tutor, ours included, to find out whether they know the syllabus or merely know the subject. Those two things are not the same, and the difference is usually worth a grade.

What this page will not do is promise an outcome. The Diploma is externally assessed, the maximum is 45 points with 24 required for the award, and nobody can guarantee a number. Any provider promising a 7 or a fixed points total is describing their marketing. What a good match buys is a student who knows what each mark is awarded for, which is the thing that actually moves a grade.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-falah.programmesIntro: Al Falah families reach us at three different stages of the IB, and the supply question looks different at each one. Here is what each stage needs and how quickly it can usually be covered.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment, and the core contributes up to three further points on top of the 42 available from subjects. Support requests here are the most specific and the hardest to match, because a Higher Level request is a request for one person rather than for a category.
programmes.countryNote: Al Falah students travel to Diploma schools in the Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas Island and island clusters, and that commute is the practical reason evening online sessions dominate here. If your child takes a minority Higher Level subject, ask about availability in Diploma Year 1 rather than in the spring of Year 2, because the wait for a scarce specialism is not something a deadline shortens.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, ending in the Personal Project. Matching is easier here because the specialisms are broader, and the most valuable early work is often explaining to a parent how criterion marks differ from percentages. Reading an MYP report as though it were a percentage grade leads to the wrong purchase.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Falah families the MYP matters mainly as the on-ramp: a student who has been assessed by criteria for five years arrives at the Diploma already used to written reflection, which is an advantage in the Internal Assessments. A student transferring in from a different system in Year 10 or 11 does not have that habit and usually needs it built deliberately.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece; the Theory of Knowledge course produces an exhibition and a 1,600-word essay; CAS is not graded but must be completed. Together the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three points. These are supervised by the school, and a tutor's role is teaching the criteria and giving feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the most commonly mistimed purchase among Abu Dhabi families. The work is produced across months, so supervision booked in Diploma Year 1 is both cheaper and more useful than crisis hours a fortnight before an internal deadline. Al Falah students with long commutes are particularly prone to leaving the Extended Essay late, because the research time competes with the car.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Diploma subject and the fastest to match. Standard Level is assessed by two papers, one without a calculator and one with, each at forty per cent, with the exploration at twenty. Higher Level adds a third paper and shifts the weightings to thirty, thirty and twenty.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Permits a calculator in both Standard Level papers and rewards modelling and interpretation. Matching is quick at Standard Level and slower at Higher Level, where the statistics and modelling content narrows the pool of tutors who have taught it to examination.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the scientific investigation drive most requests. Higher Level matches reasonably quickly in Abu Dhabi; the investigation supervision is where timing matters, because the work is produced over months and cannot be repaired in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The limiting factor is usually algebra rather than physics, so a mathematics repair block often improves a physics grade more than physics sessions do. Higher Level availability is moderate and worth securing early in Diploma Year 1.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data analysis, statistics and the structure of extended responses carry the marks. Matching is straightforward at both levels. Students who revise by reading rather than by writing timed answers consistently under-perform their own knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the difference between explain and evaluate decide most grades, and the portfolio commentaries need structured feedback. Higher Level is one of the scarcer humanities specialisms in this market, so expect a longer match time.

subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper responses reward a method rather than a reading list, and that method can be taught. Availability is good. Students arriving from a system that rewarded content recall need the analytical frame built from scratch.

subjects.description: Genuinely scarce in the UAE market, particularly at Higher Level. If your child takes either, ask about availability as early as Diploma Year 1; a request made in the spring of Year 2 may face a wait that no deadline can shorten.

subjects.name: Arabic A Literature and Arabic B
subjects.description: In demand locally and thinly covered by tutoring platforms, which tend to staff for the sciences. Availability varies by level and by the specific pathway. Where we cannot cover it we say so rather than offering an approximate match.

subjects.name: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre
subjects.description: The scarcest group in this market. The assessed components are portfolio and performance based, which makes remote support useful for the written and reflective elements and limited for the practical ones. We will tell you where the limit sits before you book.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A popular route for students balancing a science requirement against a heavy Higher Level load. Availability is moderate, and the practical work and the written components need separate attention rather than one general approach.

sections.heading: How thin is IB specialist supply around Al Falah, really?
paragraphs: Take the question literally. A Diploma student has six subjects, three of them at Higher Level. To cover that timetable in person you would need six people, each of whom teaches that subject at that level, each willing to drive to Al Falah on a weekday evening, each free in the two-hour window the household can actually protect. Nobody has that. Even a school, with a full staff room, timetables around which teachers it has rather than which it would like.

In practice a family needs one or two of those six, and the match difficulty depends entirely on which. Mathematics in either route, biology, chemistry and English A are well covered in this market. Economics at Higher Level, Business Management, Computer Science, Digital Society, Arabic A Literature, Visual Arts, Music and Theatre are not. For the scarce group the constraint is not willingness to travel; it is that the number of people in the region who have taught that subject to examination is small, and those people are mostly teaching in schools.

The useful consequence is about timing rather than about geography. If your child takes a minority Higher Level subject, the question to ask is availability now, in Diploma Year 1, not in the spring of Year 2 when the deadline has arrived. Scarcity does not respond to urgency. The table sets out the realistic picture by subject group, including the fallback position, because a provider who conceals a coverage limit is simply arranging for you to discover it later. Where we cannot cover a combination we say so and name the expected wait.

sections.heading: What knowing the syllabus actually means: the Diploma component by component
paragraphs: A tutor who knows a subject can explain the content. A tutor who knows the syllabus can tell a student which component the marks sit in, what each command term requires, and why a correct answer scored two out of four. The difference is visible within one session if you know what to listen for, and it is most of what separates the published AED bands in this market.

The architecture is worth a parent's attention because it explains where effort should go. Forty-two points come from six subjects, each marked out of seven. Up to three further points come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combined, and 24 points is the minimum for the award with the maximum at 45. Within each subject, the Internal Assessment is typically about a fifth of the grade, and it is produced at home across months. That single fact means a fifth of every subject grade is unavailable to a final-term revision push, which is the structural reason late IB interventions disappoint.

Mathematics shows the pattern clearly. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is two papers at forty per cent each, one without a calculator and one with, plus the exploration at twenty. At Higher Level it is three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty, plus the exploration at twenty. Applications and Interpretation permits a calculator throughout at Standard Level. A tutor who cannot state those weightings without looking them up has not planned a Diploma course, and that is a fair thing for a parent to test.

sections.heading: The mathematics exploration, marked criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Nobody in the competitor set names a single assessment criterion by letter, which is strange, because this is the part of the Diploma students lose most avoidable marks in. The mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and each one rewards something a student can be taught to do deliberately.

Presentation carries four marks and rewards a coherent, organised piece that a reader can follow without effort. Mathematical communication carries four and rewards correct notation, defined variables, labelled graphs and consistent terminology; students routinely lose marks here for writing informally about mathematics they have performed correctly. Personal engagement carries three and rewards genuine independent thinking rather than a declaration of interest in the introduction. Reflection carries three and rewards discussion of what the results mean and what the limitations are, which is where a strong mathematician who treats the write-up as an answer sheet loses the most. Use of mathematics carries six, the largest single allocation, and rewards work that is relevant, correct and at a level appropriate to the course.

What a tutor may do with this is clear and bounded. Teach what each criterion rewards. Work a comparable example on a different topic. Give feedback on the student's own draft against the criteria. What a tutor may not do is choose the topic for them, supply text, or edit a draft until the thinking is no longer theirs. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright; the risk of that purchase falls on the student, who faces malpractice proceedings, and not on the seller. Reading the criteria in Diploma Year 1 rather than the week before submission is the cheapest improvement available in the whole programme.

sections.heading: A twenty-minute script for testing whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Use this on any tutor, including ours. It costs nothing, it takes one trial session, and it distinguishes syllabus knowledge from subject knowledge faster than any profile description. Begin with weightings: ask what each component of your child's subject is worth. Someone who has planned a Diploma course answers immediately. Someone who has not either generalises or reaches for a document.

Then ask about the Internal Assessment criteria for that subject, by letter and mark allocation. Then ask a harder question: name the two or three places students most commonly lose marks in this subject, and what you do about each. A good answer is specific and slightly boring. A weak answer is about confidence and motivation. Then ask what they will not do with coursework, and listen for the boundary rather than for reassurance. Then ask how progress will be reported, in what units, and at what interval.

Finally, ask two administrative questions that a serious tutor will not mind. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, so a quoted permit fee is a signal in itself. And: have you taught this subject at this level to examination, and when? Nothing in that script requires you to know the subject yourself, which is the point. The script is a filter, not a test of your own knowledge.

sections.heading: Why online solves the Al Falah supply problem, and what it costs you
paragraphs: The scarcity described at the top of this page is a geography problem, and online removes the geography. An Al Falah family choosing an in-home arrangement is choosing from people willing to drive to the airport road at the evening peak; a family choosing online is choosing from every specialist available. For a common subject the two sets overlap enough that it hardly matters. For Higher Level Economics or Digital Society, the first set is often empty and the second is not.

The price difference points the same way. Published Abu Dhabi figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The gap is travel. It is also visible geographically: in-home quotes sit lower in Khalifa City, where journeys are short, and higher in the outer communities, which is the clearest available evidence that distance is being billed rather than expertise.

The costs of going online deserve naming rather than burying. A younger or distractible student is harder to supervise through a screen. For mathematics and the sciences a tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper. A practical or performance component in Visual Arts, Music or Theatre is only partly supportable remotely, and we will say where that limit falls before you book rather than after. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India. If a physical presence in the room is genuinely what your child needs, buy it locally with the travel premium understood.

sections.heading: ADEK, the school you chose, and what its report does not tell you
paragraphs: Private schools serving Al Falah are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, which is a striking omission on pages written for Abu Dhabi parents. For a Diploma family the regulator matters in a specific way: its framework says something about the school, while your child's report says something about their position in that school's cohort, and neither tells you how an examiner would mark their work.

That gap is the reason a diagnostic session is worth more than a term of reassurance. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made inside one institution. An Internal Assessment draft marked against the published criteria by someone who has applied them before is a different kind of information. Parents who ask for the second thing tend to make better decisions about what to buy, and sometimes the right decision is to buy nothing.

Two further points for an Al Falah household. First, Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, under a federal baseline that requires adherence to those subjects regardless of the curriculum a school is licensed for; they occupy real timetable space and a revision plan that ignores them overstates the hours available. Second, verify any school inspection outcome on the regulator's own site rather than on a tutoring page. And a caution about us: IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and has no premises in the UAE. Any provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth checking.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, stated before it is tested
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries work produced outside the exam hall, so the boundary needs to be set at the start of Year 1, not negotiated under deadline pressure in Year 2. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, works comparable examples, sets practice, marks it and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce your child's coursework, does not supply text to be submitted, and does not edit a draft to the point where the thinking has stopped being theirs.

This is not caution for its own sake. The exposure falls on the student. An authenticity problem in an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is a malpractice matter with consequences for the candidate, while the person who sold the work faces nothing. One page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Treat that as a reason to avoid the provider rather than as an option on a menu.

The honest version is also more effective. A student who has been taught what Criterion D rewards, and who has rewritten their own reflection section twice after feedback, can defend the work in the viva-style conversations schools increasingly hold, and can write the next piece without help. A student handed finished text cannot do either. We also do not publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We cite them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor living near Al Falah who knows my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it depends entirely on the subject and level. Al Falah is a villa community away from the Khalifa City and Al Raha belt where most of the emirate's IB capacity and most resident specialists sit. For mathematics, biology, chemistry or English A the local pool is workable. For Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, Digital Society, Arabic A Literature or the arts it is often empty at any price. Online removes the geography, so the question becomes whether the specialist exists rather than whether they will drive to the airport road.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to a villa in Al Falah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For Al Falah families lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The local in-home market does exist and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The premium is the journey, which is visible in the fact that in-home quotes are lower in Khalifa City than in the outer communities.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor knows the Diploma syllabus or just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions in the trial session. What is each component of this subject worth? Name the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations. Where do students most commonly lose marks here, and what do you do about it? Someone who has planned and taught the course answers all three immediately and specifically. Someone who knows the subject generally will generalise, talk about confidence and motivation, or reach for a document. The difference usually shows inside the first ten minutes and costs you nothing to find out.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre are the scarcest, followed by Computer Science and Digital Society, Arabic A Literature, and Higher Level Economics and Business Management. The sciences, mathematics in both routes and English A are comparatively well covered. The reason is structural: people who have taught a minority Higher Level subject to examination are few, and most of them work in schools. If your child takes one, ask about availability in Diploma Year 1 rather than in the spring of Year 2, because scarcity does not respond to urgency.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot cover my child's Higher Level subject at all?
faqs.answer: We say so, name the expected wait, and explain the nearest alternative and how it differs. We do not offer an approximate match and let you discover the gap in session four. For some requests the honest answer is that a subject-specific tutor is unavailable and that a related intervention would help more, for example a mathematics repair block for a struggling physics student. None of the competitor pages measured for this project discloses a coverage limit, which means the limit is still there and simply not mentioned.

faqs.question: How are the marks distributed in an IB Diploma, and where should effort go?
faqs.answer: Forty-two points come from six subjects marked out of seven each, and up to three more from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combined, giving a maximum of 45 with 24 required for the award. Within each subject the Internal Assessment is typically about a fifth of the grade and is produced at home across months. That means a fifth of every subject grade cannot be recovered by a final-term revision push, which is why effort placed in Diploma Year 1 on coursework quality is worth more than the same effort placed in Year 2.

faqs.question: Which criteria carry the marks in the IB maths exploration, and where do Al Falah students lose them?
faqs.answer: Out of 20 across five criteria. Presentation carries 4 marks for coherent organisation. Mathematical communication carries 4 for correct notation, defined variables and labelled graphs. Personal engagement carries 3 for genuine independent thinking. Reflection carries 3 for discussing what results mean and what the limitations are. Use of mathematics carries 6, the largest allocation, for relevant and correct mathematics at course level. Strong mathematicians most often lose marks in Reflection and Mathematical communication, because they treat the write-up as an answer sheet rather than as a piece of writing.

faqs.question: What help is a tutor allowed to give on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach what the criteria reward, help scope a research question that can actually be answered inside the 4,000-word ceiling, and give feedback on your child's own drafts. The school remains the supervisor and a tutor does not replace that role. What a tutor must not do is choose the topic for them, supply text, or edit a draft until the thinking is no longer theirs. An authenticity problem is a malpractice matter whose consequences fall on the candidate, not on whoever supplied the help.

faqs.question: When should an Al Falah family start IB support, given the commute?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do. Students here travel to the Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas Island or island school belts, and the journey competes directly with the independent research hours the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments need. Starting in Diploma Year 1 does three things: it secures a tutor in a scarce subject while availability exists, it puts coursework supervision where the drafting actually happens, and it spreads the cost across twenty-four months rather than concentrating it in a panicked final spring.

faqs.question: Does a strong school report mean my child does not need help?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, because the two measure different things. A school report places your child within that school's cohort, and ADEK's framework says something about the school itself, but neither tells you how an examiner applying the published criteria would mark the work. That is why a diagnostic session is worth more than a term of reassurance: a draft marked against the criteria by someone who has applied them before is a different kind of information, and it sometimes shows that no tutoring is needed at all.

faqs.question: Are your tutors permitted to teach privately in the UAE, and does it matter if they are abroad?
faqs.answer: The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, applies to individuals providing private lessons in the country, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Ask any UAE-based tutor to show it, and treat a quoted permit fee as a warning sign. Where a specialist teaching your child's syllabus is based outside the UAE, we tell you, because the alternative is a provider concealing delivery location behind a foreign phone number, which two competitor pages in this search do.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really see my child's working in maths or physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the thing to test in the free trial rather than take on faith. Most students write on a tablet with a stylus into a shared whiteboard, which the tutor sees stroke by stroke and can annotate as the method forms. The alternative is paper under a phone or document camera, which works and is clumsier. Watching method as it develops is often more diagnostic than seeing a finished page. If neither arrangement suits your child, you will know before any money is committed.

faqs.question: Which parts of an IB course are hardest to support remotely?
faqs.answer: The practical and performance components. Visual Arts, Music and Theatre have assessed elements that need to be made or performed, and remote support is genuinely limited there, useful for the written and reflective parts and much less so for the rest. Science practical work sits in between: the techniques are done at school, while the research design, data analysis and write-up are exactly where most marks are lost and are fully supportable online. We state where the limit falls before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: Will you guarantee my child a particular IB points total?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. The Diploma is externally assessed, the maximum is 45 points with 24 required for the award, and the grade belongs to the student on the day. We publish no score-improvement figures or satisfaction percentages either, because we could not show you the sample size, the date and the method behind them. What a good match reliably buys is a student who knows what each mark is awarded for, which is the part of the outcome that can actually be influenced.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects Al Ghadeer families ask for most often. Each one is matched to a named paper and a named syllabus, and the first lesson is free so your child can test the match before money changes hands.

intro.heading: The price question Al Ghadeer parents ask first
paragraphs: Al Ghadeer sits on the Abu Dhabi side of the emirate border, off the E11 near Al Samha, and that location shapes every tutoring conversation here. A family in a Al Ghadeer townhouse may drive their children toward Abu Dhabi island in the morning or toward the Dubai schools near Jebel Ali instead. Either way, the school day ends a long way from the front door, and a tutor who agrees to travel to the community is quoting for the drive as much as for the teaching.

That is why the honest starting point is money. Market rates for private tuition in Abu Dhabi run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university student working online to AED 650 an hour at the premium end, and the figures are published by the agencies themselves rather than estimated by us. An in-home one-to-one visit is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on who you ask, and the gap between that and an online specialist rate of AED 200 to 450 is almost entirely fuel, traffic and the tutor's unpaid hour in the car. Al Ghadeer's distance from the island means that premium lands at the top of the range, not the bottom.

Our position is simple and we state it before you read any further: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home tutoring at the door is a service we run only in India. What we sell to a Al Ghadeer family is one-to-one teaching over live video, with the same tutor each week, screen-shared past papers, and a recording of the lesson your child can go back to. The reason is not cost-cutting. It is that a Diploma student taking Chemistry HL needs somebody who knows where Paper 2 candidates lose marks on the energetics questions, and the chance of that person living twenty minutes from Al Ghadeer is small.

The rest of this page is built around the budget rather than the sales pitch. There is a table of what the Abu Dhabi market charges, by tier, with the provider who published each rate. There is a second table that converts hourly rates into the monthly figure a family actually pays, because nobody plans a Diploma year in hours. There is a plain account of where tutoring money gets wasted: paying specialist rates for homework supervision, booking two subjects with one generalist, starting in April for a May sitting. And there is the exam calendar read backwards from the June series, because the single biggest driver of cost is starting late.

Everything factual here is attributed. Rates carry the provider who quoted them and the month they were read. Regulatory points carry the authority that issued them: ADEK for private schools in this emirate, the Ministry of Education for certificate equivalency, MoHRE for the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Where a date is not verifiable we say so rather than inventing one, which is why you will find no IB exam date on this page and a link to your child's IB coordinator instead.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.programmesIntro: Al Ghadeer children are spread across three IB programmes and two directions of commute. The notes below say what each programme demands of a family in this corridor, and what online tuition can realistically carry.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP assesses through units of inquiry rather than tests, so a parent rarely sees a mark that signals trouble. What shows instead is reading fluency that stops improving, number work done on fingers in Year 4, or a child who cannot explain what their current unit is about. Support at this stage is short, frequent and skills-led rather than syllabus-led.
programmes.countryNote: PYP tuition is the cheapest tier in Abu Dhabi and the easiest to overpay for. Market rates for primary support start around AED 45 to 150 an hour online, and a Al Ghadeer family paying specialist Diploma rates for Year 4 maths is buying credentials the work does not need. Two thirty-minute online slots a week, after the commute home, usually beats one long evening session a tired child sits through.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks arrive as criterion letters A to D rather than percentages, which is where most confusion begins. A student scoring 6 on Criterion A and 3 on Criterion D in Maths is not a weak mathematician; they cannot apply the method to an unfamiliar context. Tuition that reads the criterion breakdown fixes the right thing, and MYP Year 11 is where the Diploma maths route gets decided.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP years are the cheapest point to intervene for a Al Ghadeer family, and the one most often skipped. A student who arrives in DP1 with gaps in algebraic manipulation needs two years of catch-up at specialist rates; the same gaps closed in MYP Year 10 cost a term of mid-tier tuition. Families in this corridor often notice the problem only when the Diploma subject choice form comes home.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The marks that decide the final grade are split between external papers and the Internal Assessment in each subject, and the IA is where the predictable damage happens because it is coursework with a deadline the school sets, not the IB. HL papers carry a third option paper in several sciences.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Ghadeer budgets stretch. A Diploma student taking two Higher Levels plus IA supervision can absorb four to six hours of tuition a week in the weeks before an internal deadline, then drop to one. Families who buy a flat weekly block all year pay for the quiet months and run short in the busy ones. Market specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 an hour make that difference worth planning.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a career-related study with at least two Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is far less common in this emirate than the full Diploma, and students on it often need help with the DP courses they are carrying rather than with the career strand itself.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in Abu Dhabi are a small group and a specialist match takes longer to arrange than for a mainstream Diploma subject. We say so at the point of enquiry rather than after payment. If the DP courses inside a CP are the problem, the tuition looks identical to Diploma support and the market rate is the same.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to cover, with the part of each course where hours actually convert into marks. The cost of tuition in a subject tracks how scarce the specialist is, not how hard the subject sounds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA rewards algebraic fluency and proof. HL candidates sit three papers plus the exploration, and Paper 3 is the one that separates grades because it asks extended problem-solving on unfamiliar ground. Marks leak from calculus notation and from stating a domain. AA is the most requested and most expensive subject in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling and statistics with the calculator in constant use. SL students lose marks by rounding too early and by reporting a correlation without commenting on whether the model is suitable. AI HL carries more statistics than most parents expect. A tutor who teaches AA by default will teach AI badly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics marks are lost in the explanation, not the arithmetic. A student who can compute the answer but cannot say which conservation law applies will stall in the long-response questions. HL adds the option topic and harder circuits work. The practical skills assessed in the IA need separate attention from the papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most of the lost marks we see. Students memorise reaction steps and then cannot apply them to an unseen compound. HL extends into harder thermodynamics. The IA in Chemistry is also where the honesty line matters most, because the data must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Biology candidates who revise by rereading notes score far below those who answer past-paper questions against the command terms. Statistical treatment of data in the IA catches students out, and HL candidates must handle more detail in plant and animal physiology than SL.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades here. A correctly labelled diagram with the axes and the shift explained earns marks a paragraph of prose will not. HL adds quantitative questions and a harder policy evaluation. The three commentaries in the Internal Assessment need real published articles chosen early rather than the week before.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The command terms do the work: a question asking students to evaluate and answered with a description caps the mark regardless of the content. HL carries additional content and the pre-released case study for Paper 1 rewards genuinely thorough preparation rather than last-minute reading.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, which cannot be revised by memorising content. Students need practice writing to time on texts they have never seen. The Individual Oral requires a global issue and two texts chosen and prepared well in advance, and HL adds the essay component.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: English B suits students for whom English is an additional language, and the productive skills carry the grade. Writing to a specified text type with the right register is a learnable skill that many candidates never practise. HL demands two literary works and more sustained written response.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Abu Dhabi schools run Arabic alongside the IB for every pupil, and the stream a child sits in matters. Arabic A is a first-language literature course; Arabic B is acquisition. Federal rules require Arabic in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so this is not an optional subject here.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution development in the Internal Assessment is a project with a client, and students who choose a problem too large lose weeks. Paper 1 rewards precise pseudocode and tracing. HL adds the resource management and abstract data structures that most students find the steepest part of the course.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.regionsIntro: Al Ghadeer families do not keep to one commuting pattern, so the places that matter to a tutoring schedule are spread across two emirates. These are the communities whose school runs and traffic windows show up in our scheduling conversations here.

regions.name: Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Aldar's border community off the E11, a mix of apartments and townhouses with no IB school inside it. Every Diploma student here travels, which is why evening slots after 17:00 Gulf Standard Time are the realistic ones rather than a 16:00 start.

regions.name: Al Samha
regions.note: The nearest established neighbourhood, and the first stop for groceries and clinics. Families here share the same E11 bottleneck, so a tutor's promised 16:30 arrival and an actual 17:15 arrival are separated by one accident on the Abu Dhabi carriageway.

regions.name: Al Shahama

sections.heading: What IB tuition actually costs around Al Ghadeer
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Ghadeer is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour in this market, and an online IB specialist between AED 200 and AED 450. Those are market figures published by the agencies themselves and read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. The table below shows the full spread, from a university student charging AED 45 an hour to a premium provider publishing AED 650.

Three things stand out once the figures are side by side. The first is how wide each band is: a parent ringing round five providers for the same subject at the same level will be quoted numbers that differ by a factor of four, and almost none of them will explain what the difference buys. The second is that the in-home band starts lower than the specialist online band and ends higher. That is because the in-home figure covers two different things sold under one name, a generalist who will supervise homework and a genuine subject specialist who happens to drive.

The third is that three of the six most visible providers in this market publish no price at all, and two of the remaining quote in US dollars. For a family in Al Ghadeer budgeting in dirhams against a school fee invoice, a dollar rate on a UAE page is a warning sign about how much else on that page was written for somebody else's country.

Use the table as a sanity check rather than a target. If a quote sits well above the specialist band, ask what the extra buys: examiner experience that can be evidenced, a named syllabus, a record of the papers taught. If it sits well below, ask who is teaching and at what level they studied the subject themselves.

sections.heading: What the drive out to Al Ghadeer adds to the bill
paragraphs: The gap between an online specialist rate and an in-home rate is not teaching. It is the hour a tutor spends in a car on the E11 and the risk they carry that an accident on the Abu Dhabi carriageway turns a 90-minute booking into a three-hour commitment. A tutor who prices that honestly charges more for Al Ghadeer than for a villa on the island, and one who does not price it will quietly stop taking the booking after a month.

There is a second cost that never appears in a quote. A tutor willing to drive to the border corridor is drawn from the small pool of people who live near it, which means the subject match is decided by geography. A Diploma student needing Physics HL help with the option topic gets whoever is available within a reasonable drive, and that person may last have taught the subject at a different level entirely. The hourly rate looks like the whole price; the mismatch is the real one.

Online removes both. The tutor is selected for the paper your child sits rather than the road they live near, and nobody pays for fuel. That is the entire argument, and the table below sets the two formats against each other on the terms that matter from this address: cost, travel, who is available and what happens when a lesson has to move.

To be plain about it: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. If an in-home tutor in Al Ghadeer is what you want, this page tells you honestly what the market charges for it so you can negotiate well, and then makes the case for the format we actually deliver.
