sections.heading: Budgeting a Diploma year from Al Ghadeer, month by month
paragraphs: Nobody plans a two-year Diploma in hours. They plan it in monthly outgoings against a school fee invoice, which is why the hourly rate is the wrong unit for a family decision. Converted to a month, one weekly hour with a specialist sits in the AED 1,000 to 2,000 range at the top tier, and Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle.

The shape of the spend matters more than the total. A Diploma year is not flat. There are two or three pinch points, usually an internal assessment deadline in each subject and the mock window, where a student genuinely needs three or four hours a week, and long stretches where one hour is enough to keep the method honest. Families who buy a fixed weekly block for twenty-four months pay for the quiet months at the busy months' rate.

There is also a real context point worth holding on to. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the following academic year, under Dubai's economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee decisions sit with ADEK rather than KHDA, but the broader signal is the same: tuition is the part of the education budget a family still controls, and the part most often spent without a plan.

The table converts the market bands into the units a household actually budgets in, and adds the items parents forget: the IA support block, the exam-season intensive, and the private candidate entry fee if a student sits a paper outside their school.

sections.heading: Where Al Ghadeer families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The most common waste is paying a specialist rate for work a specialist is not needed for. Homework supervision, reading practice and keeping a distracted fourteen-year-old at a desk are all legitimate things to buy, and they do not cost AED 400 an hour. Families who hire one expensive tutor to do everything end up paying Diploma rates for Year 8 revision.

The second is booking one tutor across two subjects for convenience. It halves the scheduling problem and it roughly halves the benefit, because the person who genuinely knows where Maths AA HL candidates lose marks on Paper 3 is rarely the same person who knows how the Economics commentaries are assessed. A Al Ghadeer family already managing a long commute is understandably drawn to a single point of contact; the cost of that convenience shows up in the weaker subject.

The third is timing. Starting tuition six weeks before a sitting converts almost the whole budget into exam technique, because there is no time left to repair content. The same money spread across the two terms before would have done both. Starting late is not a moral failing and it is sometimes unavoidable, but it is expensive, and the honest answer to a parent asking in late spring whether tuition is still worth it is yes for technique, no for content gaps.

The fourth is paying for group classes that do not match the student's level. A group rate of AED 100 a head looks decisive next to AED 300 one-to-one, until you notice that a class covering the whole syllabus spends four minutes on the topic your child actually cannot do. Per useful minute, that group hour can be the most expensive thing on this page.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor you pay in Abu Dhabi is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, whose own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, and the published completion time is two working days.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. Teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen can all hold the permit. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you, and if a provider cites a specific figure treat that as a sign they are repeating something they have not checked.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point that matters here. ADEK's professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same thing. So the arrangement some families quietly hope for, their child's own subject teacher paid privately, is the one arrangement to avoid. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

A separate licence applies to anybody operating with premises and staff. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific thing granted to a specific type of business. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or partnership of any kind, and any provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: The exam calendar read backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Cost follows the calendar, so the calendar is worth reading in reverse. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate in Al Ghadeer sits June, with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

The detail that catches families is zoning. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A parent should take the timetable from their own child's exams officer and from nowhere else, including this page.

For a sense of the gap between a paper and a result, the Pearson November series is the cleanest published example: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the equivalent November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Those are backward-looking dates and they are checkable.

IB dates are different and we will not publish them. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; for the exact window, your child's IB coordinator and ibo.org are the only sources worth acting on. The table below is therefore framed by milestone rather than by date, which is also the only version that stays true next year.

sections.heading: What tutoring money may not buy: the academic honesty line
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries an Internal Assessment, and the Diploma adds the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. All of it must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the method, explain the criteria, read a draft the student has written and say plainly where it falls short. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a draft into its final state, choose and execute the research for the student, or hand over a finished piece.

This is not a policy we invented to sound careful. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. A student who submits one is exposed to an IB malpractice finding, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who sold it. No refund covers a withdrawn Diploma.

The practical version for a Al Ghadeer family is a set of questions to ask any tutor before paying. What exactly will you do with my child's draft? Will the words in the final submission be my child's? What happens if my child asks you to write a paragraph? A tutor who answers those three clearly is worth more than one with a longer list of credentials, because the credentials do not survive a malpractice finding either.

The same line applies to material. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. We work from them, cite them and link to the official source, and your child's school already has legitimate access to what they need.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Ghadeer: the honest version
paragraphs: A first conversation takes about twenty minutes and is mostly listening. We ask which school, which programme, which subjects and levels, what the last report said by criterion or by grade, and what the family can actually commit to in a week given the commute. Nothing useful can be matched without the level, because an IB maths tutor who is excellent at Applications and Interpretation SL may be the wrong person for Analysis and Approaches HL.

Then a free trial lesson, with the tutor we think fits. It runs as a normal session, live over video, and the student does the talking. The point is diagnostic: the tutor needs to see how your child handles a question they cannot immediately do, which is the behaviour that predicts progress far better than a report grade. You get a note afterwards saying what was found and what the first six weeks should target.

If the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than asking your child to adjust. If no specialist is free for a genuinely niche combination, we say so at that point instead of filling the slot with somebody approximately right and letting you discover it in week three. A family in Al Ghadeer has already spent enough of its week in a car to deserve a straight answer about availability.

Everything is scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day you actually have, which in this corridor usually means a start after 17:00 on weekdays and a longer weekend slot for IA work. Lessons are online, one-to-one, and no tutor will ever be arranged to travel to a UAE address, because that is not a service we sell here.

For a MYP student the criterion letters on the last report tell us more than the overall grade. This is the information that decides who we can match, and the one most enquiries leave out.

You receive a written note afterwards covering what was diagnosed and what the first six weeks should cover, whether or not you continue.

process.title: Agree the rhythm against the school's calendar
process.description: We set the weekly pattern against your child's own internal deadlines and mock window rather than a generic plan, and we say which months will need more hours. For a Al Ghadeer family that usually means a lighter autumn and a heavier run into the internal assessment deadlines.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: The same tutor each week, screen-shared past-paper work, and a short note to you after each session saying what was covered and what the student should do before the next one. The record is what stops a new term starting with the same diagnosis as the last.

process.title: Review on evidence, change if needed
process.description: Every six to eight weeks we look at marked work rather than impressions, and decide whether to keep the pattern, change the focus or change the tutor. A tutor swap is a normal outcome of a review, not a complaint, and it costs nothing.

A family cannot negotiate against numbers nobody will state, which is why ours are attributed rather than rounded into a claim.

whyPoints.title: Matched by paper, not by proximity
whyPoints.description: A tutor who has to reach Al Ghadeer by road is chosen from the people who live near it. Online, the pool is the people who know the paper your child sits. For a Higher Level option topic that difference is the whole of the result, and it costs nothing in fuel.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one subject, one record
whyPoints.description: The same specialist each week, keeping a running record of what has been taught and what keeps breaking. Progress is cumulative and the diagnosis is not repeated every month, which is where the real saving sits compared with a rotating roster of substitutes.

whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work. We do not supply text for submission or rewrite a draft into its final form. The consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the student, so the boundary belongs on the page rather than in a conversation later.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, not padded

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Al Ghadeer cost per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tuition in Abu Dhabi is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table putting the usual band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. An online IB specialist sits at AED 200 to 450. Al Ghadeer's distance from the island pushes an in-home quote toward the upper end, because the tutor is pricing a long drive on the E11 as well as the lesson. Those figures were read in October 2026 and are what the market publishes, not IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a house in Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors visiting a family at home is a service we run only in India. For a Al Ghadeer family the lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with past papers screen-shared and annotated during the session. We are direct about this before any payment because the alternative, a vague promise followed by a video link, is how families lose trust in this market.

faqs.question: What does the travel premium actually buy on a Al Ghadeer booking?
faqs.answer: Mostly fuel and risk. The difference between an online specialist rate and an in-home rate covers the tutor's unpaid hour in the car each way and the chance that one incident on the Abu Dhabi carriageway turns a 90-minute booking into three hours. It does not buy better teaching. It also narrows the tutor pool to people living near the border corridor, so the subject match ends up decided by road distance rather than by which paper your child sits.

faqs.question: Is a monthly figure more useful than an hourly rate for planning?
faqs.answer: Yes, because that is the unit a household actually budgets in. One weekly hour converts to roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more with an IB specialist, using Bestimate's published monthly estimates. The useful refinement is to expect two or three heavier months a year, around internal assessment deadlines and mocks, rather than a flat monthly figure across the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Where do Al Ghadeer families most often waste money on tuition?
faqs.answer: Four places. Paying specialist Diploma rates for homework supervision a mid-tier tutor could do. Booking one tutor across two unrelated subjects for scheduling convenience, which weakens the second subject. Starting six weeks before a sitting, which spends the whole budget on exam technique with no time left for content. And buying a cheap group class pitched above or below the child's level, which looks economical per hour and is expensive per useful minute.

faqs.question: Can the money be concentrated into the weeks that matter most?
faqs.answer: That is usually the better plan. A Diploma year has pinch points rather than a flat workload: an internal assessment deadline in each subject and the mock window. A family can run one hour a week through the quiet terms and move to three or four in those windows, which costs less over a year than a fixed block that prices the quiet months at the busy months' rate. We say in advance which months we expect to be heavy.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects cost the most to find a tutor for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Price tracks scarcity rather than difficulty. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most requested and most expensive to staff, followed by Physics HL and Chemistry HL where the option topics narrow the pool further. Economics and Business Management sit in the middle. The cheapest are primary and lower MYP subjects, where a good general teacher is genuinely enough and specialist rates would be money spent on credentials the work does not require.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching a Al Ghadeer student need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and the published service completion time is two working days. Teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen are all eligible. You can ask any tutor to show the permit and its validity dates. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can we pay my child's own subject teacher for private lessons instead?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid in this emirate. ADEK's professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE permit is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Check the current wording on ADEK's own policy page before acting. A teacher from a different school, properly permitted, is a different matter.

faqs.question: When does a Al Ghadeer student sit Cambridge exams, given the commute?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting it at you. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The commute does not change the dates, but it changes the revision plan: a student losing two hours a day to the road needs the past-paper work spread earlier rather than compressed into the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Why are no IB exam dates printed on this Al Ghadeer page?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the IB itself. The IB's website blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project is confirmed from the source, and a wrong date is worse than no date when a family plans a revision schedule around it. UAE schools sit the May session. For the exact window, results day and any retake deadline, your child's IB coordinator and ibo.org are the only places worth taking a date from.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write part of my child's Internal Assessment if we pay extra?
faqs.answer: No, and no price changes that. A tutor teaches the method, explains the published criteria, reads a draft your child has written and says where it falls short. Supplying text, rewriting a draft into its final state or running the research is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; a student submitting one risks the Diploma, and no refund covers that.

faqs.question: Is a cheap group class near Mohammed Bin Zayed City better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the class matches your child's level. At roughly AED 100 a head a group hour looks decisive against AED 300 one-to-one, but a class working through the whole syllabus may spend four minutes on the single topic your child cannot do. Measured per useful minute, that can be the most expensive option available. Group teaching works well when every student is on the same paper at the same level and is genuinely stuck in the same place.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start for a student in Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects such as Maths AA or AI, Biology, Economics or English A, a free trial can usually be scheduled within a few days once we know the level. For a narrow combination, a specific Higher Level option topic or a less common language, it can take longer, and we tell you that at enquiry rather than booking somebody approximately right. Nothing starts until the trial has happened and you have the written note from it.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying anything in this market?
faqs.answer: Five questions sort the field quickly. Which exact syllabus and level do you teach, named? What will you do with my child's draft coursework, in your own words? Can you show your MoHRE private tuition permit? What does the hourly figure include, and is a cancelled session credited? And what happens if the match does not work? A tutor who answers all five plainly is worth more than one with a longer list of claims and vaguer answers.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.closingHeading: Start with the trial, then decide what the budget should buy

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jubail-isl.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level alongside Middle Years and Primary Years support, for families living on Al Jubail Island and the islands and communities around it.

intro.heading: An address with no school on it changes the question
paragraphs: Al Jubail Island sits in the channel between Abu Dhabi island and the Saadiyat and Yas side, a low-density residential development laid out among mangroves with villa villages rather than towers. It is a deliberately quiet place to live and it has one characteristic that matters enormously for tutoring: there is no school on it. Every school run from Al Jubail Island crosses a bridge, and most cross two.

That makes the comparison with the neighbourhoods either side worth doing properly, because families here often moved from one of them and assume the logistics transferred. They did not. A Saadiyat Island household can have a Diploma campus five minutes away. A Yas Island household has schools on the island and a straight run to Al Raha. An Al Raha or Khalifa City household sits inside the largest concentration of international schools in the emirate. An Al Jubail Island household has a bridge, then a choice of directions, and a journey that is pleasant off-peak and considerably less so at half past three.

The consequence for in-home tutoring is arithmetic rather than opinion. A tutor travelling to a villa on Al Jubail Island for a 6.30pm session makes a crossing, teaches, and crosses back. That round trip has to be paid for, and it arrives as a higher hourly rate, with in-home one-to-one in this market quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, or as a two-hour minimum nobody needs on a school night, or as the quiet unreliability of a late session held by somebody facing a long drive home.

The second consequence is the shortlist, and it is the one that actually decides grades. A tutor willing to cross a bridge twice on a Tuesday evening for one hour of teaching is a small group of people. Narrow that group to those who have taught Chemistry at Higher Level, or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Theory of Knowledge, and it is frequently nobody. At that point a family either changes what they ask for or accepts a generalist, usually without being told which has happened.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the bridge from the equation entirely and makes the match a question of subject and level. The rest of this page works through what genuinely differs between Al Jubail Island, Saadiyat, Yas and Al Raha, what does not differ at all, and what a Diploma plan should contain from any of those four addresses. None of the differences described above survives that change.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jubail-isl.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and families on Al Jubail Island commonly have children in two of its stages at once because the island's households skew towards younger families with a Diploma sibling.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry units rather than discrete subject teaching, with maths and literacy embedded in them. Parents often cannot see a gap until the transition into the Middle Years, because the reporting language describes dispositions as much as attainment. Support here is short, infrequent and usually about confidence after a school move.
programmes.countryNote: Al Jubail Island's primary-age children travel to campuses on Saadiyat Island, Yas Island and along the Al Raha corridor, which means a young child is doing a bridge crossing twice a day. For this age group that journey is the dominant factor in how much energy is left for anything in the evening.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject assessed against four criteria, with a Personal Project in the final year. The criteria reward communication and process alongside content, which is why an apparently secure MYP student can still arrive in the Diploma short of specific technical fluency in maths and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is where Al Jubail Island families most often first seek help, typically in the spring of Year 11 when the subject choices for the Diploma are being made and the implications of a Higher Level selection become visible for the first time.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, each with an Internal Assessment, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Students rarely come unstuck on the difficulty of one subject; they come unstuck when four internal deadlines coincide and nothing was started early.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Jubail Island mostly attend campuses on Saadiyat Island or along Al Raha, where Higher Level cohorts are small. That scarcity is why a tutor matched by subject and level rather than by willingness to cross a bridge is the whole quality question here.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jubail-isl.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects families on and around Al Jubail Island ask for most, with the component that actually decides each grade named rather than implied.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra-led, with proof, calculus and at Higher Level the extended-response Paper 3. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is where students consistently underperform because school practice is calculator-rich. The scarcest teaching skill in the emirate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led interpretation, with graph theory and matrices at Higher Level. Marks go to justified modelling choices rather than to correct calculator output, a distinction most students never have explained to them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and data-based questions that reward precise language. The Internal Assessment is where most of the available improvement sits, and it has to be addressed in the autumn rather than the week of submission.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides grades more than content recall does. Outline, explain, discuss and evaluate are marked differently and students answer all four the same way. Statistical handling in the Internal Assessment is the usual weak point.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical fluency is the hidden prerequisite: students who are comfortable with the physics still lose marks to algebra under time pressure. Uncertainty handling and graph analysis in the Internal Assessment carry more weight than students expect.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, the Individual Oral and the comparative essay. The marks sit in building an argument about how a text works rather than in describing what it says, which is a trainable skill and rarely trained.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course with its own assessments, often confused with English A in international cohorts. Choosing the wrong one of the two is one of the most expensive errors available in the Diploma, because it costs two years.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation command terms carry the marks rather than breadth of real-world reading. The Internal Assessment commentaries have firm word limits and exceeding them is an avoidable, unrecoverable loss.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A small field of genuine specialists, so availability rather than price is the constraint. Families needing it should ask early in Year 12 rather than in the term the essay is due, when the few people who teach it well are already committed.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Research question design, scope control and the assessment criteria, taught explicitly. A tutor questions the argument and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. No tutor may write, restructure or supply any part of it.

sections.heading: Al Jubail Island against Saadiyat, Yas and Al Raha
paragraphs: Families comparing these four addresses usually compare them on housing and quiet, and then discover that the differences which matter for schooling are elsewhere. The decisive variables are whether there is a school on your side of the water, how many crossings a weekday involves, and how large a pool of specialist tutors would consider travelling to you. On the first two Al Jubail Island is distinctive. On the third it is at a genuine disadvantage, and it is the third that affects a grade.

Saadiyat Island has established provision on the island itself, so a household can live minutes from a Diploma campus and a local tutor can reach it with one crossing. Yas Island has schools on-island and a straight inland run, with leisure traffic rather than commuter traffic as the variable. Al Raha and Khalifa City sit inside the emirate's densest cluster of international schools and have the deepest local tutoring market by a wide margin. Al Jubail Island has quiet villas, mangroves and a bridge in front of every one of those options.

The table below sets the four side by side on the terms that actually matter. Read the last column carefully, because it is the one nobody discusses. The difference between a neighbourhood with a hundred plausible local tutors and one with a handful is not convenience; it is whether the person teaching your child Higher Level chemistry was chosen because they teach Higher Level chemistry or because they were prepared to drive.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same from all four addresses
paragraphs: Having set out the differences, the honest conclusion is that they stop mattering once delivery is online, and that is worth stating plainly rather than dressing up. If you live on Saadiyat Island five minutes from a Diploma campus, you have a logistical advantage over an Al Jubail Island family in almost every respect. What you do not have is a better Higher Level chemistry teacher available at seven in the evening, because that question was never about distance.

Consider what a Higher Level Diploma subject needs. Somebody who has taught that course and level, knows what the Internal Assessment criteria reward, can say where students lose marks in each paper, and is free at the hour your household can hold. None of those four conditions has any relationship to geography. Three of them are about the tutor's teaching history and one is about a diary. Adding a fifth condition about driving distance can only reduce the set of people who satisfy the other four.

So the recommendation from Al Jubail Island, from Saadiyat, from Yas and from Al Raha is identical: match on course, level and availability, and let the bridge stop being part of the conversation. The Al Jubail Island family gains the most from this because they were paying the largest geographical penalty, but the Al Raha family with the deepest local market still gains, because even a deep local market does not reliably contain a Theory of Knowledge specialist free on a Wednesday.

sections.heading: What the Diploma actually assesses, component by component
paragraphs: Families buy tutoring by subject and the Diploma awards points by component, and the mismatch between those two habits explains a large share of wasted hours. Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment alongside its papers, and the core adds the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge on top. Knowing which component carries what, for your child's specific subjects, takes one conversation with the school.

The pattern across subjects is consistent even where the percentages differ. The Internal Assessment is a substantial share of each subject grade and is assessed against named criteria with published mark allocations. It is also the component students treat as administrative and leave until last, which is why it is where the recoverable marks sit. In maths the exploration is worth 20% at both levels. In the sciences the investigation carries a comparable share. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combine for core points that can move a final total.

What this means for a weekly hour from Al Jubail Island is a question of allocation rather than effort. A term spent on content revision while the Internal Assessment drifts and non-calculator or command-term technique goes untouched is a term spent on the smaller problem. The table maps the components and what each one actually needs from a tutor, which is a more useful planning document than a subject list. Ask the school for the component weightings for your child's six subjects in one email. Departments hold them, they are not confidential, and they are the only reliable basis for deciding what a weekly hour should be spent on.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment line, drawn before anyone pays
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is where a Diploma can be improved substantially and where it can be lost entirely, and the difference is what kind of help was bought. The boundary comes from IB academic-honesty rules and is not a matter of preference, so it belongs in the first conversation rather than in the small print.

A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each rewards, naming the mark allocations. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and press hard on whether there is enough substance in them to reach the upper bands. A tutor may teach content the investigation requires, including material slightly beyond the taught course. A tutor may question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a model or a sample was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written.

No tutor may write any part of the assessment, supply text to be pasted in, restructure the student's prose into their own, or produce results or mathematics for the student to transcribe. Bought-in work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student rather than on whoever sold it. There is a visible market in completed Internal Assessments in this region, advertised at four-figure dirham prices, and a page selling those is the clearest reason to ask any provider to state its honesty position in writing before a first session. Tell your child the boundary too, in the same words. A student who knows precisely which kinds of help are legitimate asks for them earlier and uses them better, while one who is unsure often either asks for nothing or accepts something they should have refused.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it varies by emirate
paragraphs: Al Jubail Island households often come from elsewhere in the UAE or move within it, and the regulator changes with the emirate in ways that surprise people. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. In Dubai it is KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there.

Sharjah's private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools. It is also worth knowing that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate regulator in those cases.

Two practical points follow. First, an inspection report is a genuinely useful document to read alongside your child's school report, because it comments on teaching quality against a published framework rather than on your child against a school's expectations. Second, none of these bodies approves individual private tutors on teaching merit, so a claim of regulator approval attached to a tutor should be read as marketing. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence.

sections.heading: The bridge, Ramadan and the weeks a plan has to survive
paragraphs: A weekly arrangement from Al Jubail Island faces the ordinary UAE interruptions plus one of its own, and planning for all of them in September is cheaper than renegotiating four times a year.

The island-specific one is traffic unpredictability. A bridge crossing is fast when it is fast and slow when something ahead of it is slow, and that variance falls on the school run rather than on the session if the session is online. For an in-home arrangement the variance falls on both, which is why late in-home slots from this address have a habit of becoming fortnightly without anyone deciding that they should.

Then the familiar ones. Ramadan shortens the school day across the UAE and shifts household rhythm to the evening, so a session that sat at 6.30pm often works better after iftar, with shorter and more frequent sessions suiting a shortened day better than one long block. The winter break lands shortly after mocks, making that fortnight either the most valuable of Year 13 or a write-off. And Al Jubail Island households travel, in which case an online session follows the student and only the time zone changes, while an in-home arrangement simply stops. The winter-break sessions should be booked in November for exactly that reason, because every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same fortnight and the specialists free in December are the ones nobody asked for in advance. The same applies to the weekend mornings either side of mock week, which go first and go quickly.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency for an IB family, stated with its limits
paragraphs: Families on Al Jubail Island applying to UAE universities, or planning to, will meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process. It is the Ministry's process and nobody else performs or guarantees it, which is worth saying because several providers in this market imply otherwise.

What can be stated with a source is the British track and the American track. On the British track, equivalency requires a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which contradicts the published rule. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in academic IELTS, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB specifically, no points threshold could be verified from the Ministry's own publications for this page, so none appears here. That is the honest position rather than an omission: publishing an unsourced IB points figure would be exactly the error that misleads a family planning a year. Confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, and note that tutoring is not a requirement of the process and nobody should present it as one.

sections.heading: Availability from an island address, told straight
paragraphs: Every tutoring site in this market implies that every subject is always available, and none of the pages researched for this project states a coverage limit anywhere. For a family on Al Jubail Island, where the local alternative is genuinely thin, an honest answer is worth more than an optimistic one.

Diploma Standard Level maths, biology, business management, economics and English A are comfortably covered at Abu Dhabi evening hours. The tighter requests are Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the smaller Group 2 languages, Theory of Knowledge, and Extended Essay supervision support in unusual subjects. Weekend mornings in the fortnight after mocks are the busiest slot in the Abu Dhabi calendar.

When a request cannot be met well you get one of three answers. A waiting time with a date attached. A named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist available, with that limitation spelt out so you can judge it. Or a statement that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need, which is sometimes the correct answer and always better than a mismatch that consumes a term. What does not happen is a quiet substitution: you know who is teaching your child and what they have taught, before the trial lesson rather than after it. The reason for saying all this is narrow and practical. From an address where the local alternative is thin, a family who is told no in September can still solve the problem; a family told yes and given a generalist in September discovers the position in February, when nothing can be solved.

whyPoints.description: Higher Level sciences and maths, the smaller languages and Theory of Knowledge are genuinely scarce. You get a waiting time with a date, a named alternative with its limits stated, or an honest no.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, accreditation not implied
whyPoints.description: ADEK for Abu Dhabi schools, KHDA for Dubai, SPEA for Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge for Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry elsewhere. None of them approves tutors, and we hold no accreditation from any of them.

faqs.question: Are there any schools on Al Jubail Island itself?
faqs.answer: No, which is the defining logistical fact for any family living there. Al Jubail Island is a low-density residential development laid out among mangroves, and every school run from it crosses a bridge, most commonly to Saadiyat Island, Yas Island, the Al Raha corridor or the main island. For tutoring that matters twice over: once for how late a session has to start, and once for how few local specialist tutors will consider a twice-crossed evening journey for a single hour of teaching.

faqs.question: How does Al Jubail Island compare with Saadiyat for getting a Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: Saadiyat has the better logistics and no better access to the teaching that matters. A Saadiyat household can live minutes from an IB campus and a local tutor can reach it with one crossing, so the pool of people willing to travel is larger. But what a Higher Level Diploma subject needs is somebody who has taught that course and level, knows what the Internal Assessment criteria reward and is free at your hour, and none of those conditions is geographical. Once delivery is online the two addresses have identical access.

faqs.question: Will a tutor drive out to a villa on Al Jubail Island?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Some Abu Dhabi providers will, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because that figure absorbs a round trip across the water. From this address the bigger problem is stability rather than price: a late session held by somebody facing two crossings and a long drive home is the one that quietly becomes fortnightly.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start from Al Jubail Island?
faqs.answer: Half past six on weekdays, with seven safer when the student has a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment. The school day ends between 3.00pm and 3.30pm, the run back to the island takes twenty to thirty-five minutes at pick-up hour depending on the direction, and a student needs food and a pause before abstract work. Weekend mornings are the other good window and are better suited to Internal Assessment work and whole papers, since no crossing sits on either side of the session.

faqs.question: Which part of a Diploma subject grade is most worth buying help for?
faqs.answer: The Internal Assessment, by a clear margin, provided it is bought early. Every Diploma subject carries one, it is assessed against named criteria with published mark allocations, and most of its mark is determined by the topic chosen and the depth available in it, both settled in the first fortnight. Students treat it as administrative and leave it late, which is exactly why the recoverable marks sit there. After that, timed paper practice and command-term discipline return more per hour than general content revision does.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with an IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria and what each rewards, with the mark allocations named. Discuss candidate topics and press on whether there is enough substance to reach the upper bands. Teach content the investigation needs, including material slightly beyond the taught course. Question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a sample or model was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. What no tutor may do is write any part of it, supply text, restructure the prose or produce results for the student to copy.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge support hard to find in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth asking early rather than discovering it late. Theory of Knowledge is a genuinely small specialism, far smaller than any subject, and the few people who teach it well tend to be committed by the time the essay deadline approaches. A family that asks in the autumn of Year 12 usually gets a specialist. A family that asks in the term the essay is due usually gets either a waiting time or a generalist, and the difference between those two in a core component is substantial.

faqs.question: Does the regulator change if we move from Dubai to Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it surprises families regularly. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. In Dubai the body is KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Sharjah has its own Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five are the whole map. Inspection frameworks and published ratings differ between them, so comparing a Dubai rating with an Abu Dhabi one is not straightforward.

faqs.question: Is an inspection report worth reading before choosing where to spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is one of the more useful free documents available. A school report tells you how your child is doing against that school's expectations. An inspection report comments on teaching quality, often by subject and phase, against a published framework. Where the two disagree, that gap is worth a conversation with the department, and it frequently redirects tutoring money sensibly, because a child can look comfortable against a weak departmental standard and still be underprepared for an external paper. Check the date on the report before relying on it.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require from an IB student for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No IB points threshold could be verified from the Ministry's own publications for this page, so none is stated here rather than guessed at. What is sourced is the British track, which requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade, and the American track, which uses IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing, with SAT Math 450. Confirm your own case on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can lessons keep running when the family is away from the island?
faqs.answer: Yes, and from Al Jubail Island that is more than a convenience. Households here travel, and an in-home arrangement cancels every time, which during a Diploma year can mean a three-week gap at exactly the wrong point in an Internal Assessment timetable. A live video session follows the student, so the only adjustment is the time zone. Most families thin sessions rather than stopping them across a long summer, because the technical fluency a Diploma course assumes is the first thing to decay in a ten-week break.

faqs.question: How should a Diploma plan handle Ramadan from this address?
faqs.answer: By moving rather than pausing, and by deciding the new slot in advance. The school day shortens across the UAE, household rhythm shifts towards the evening, and a session that sat at 6.30pm often works better after iftar. Shorter, more frequent sessions suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 13 this is a poor month to drop out of, because the interval before the May session is short and an Internal Assessment deadline may sit nearby. Agreeing the replacement slot in writing prevents a month of weekly cancellations.

faqs.question: Which IB campuses do your students near Al Jubail Island attend?
faqs.answer: Families on and around the island travel to campuses on Saadiyat Island and Yas Island and along the Al Raha corridor, with some reaching the main island. The names that come up include Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, West Yas Academy, Raha International School, Repton School Abu Dhabi and GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi. Those are given to describe the local education map and nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school named, and none of them is a client of ours.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: You are told, with one of three specific answers. A waiting time with a date attached. A named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist available, with that limitation spelt out so you can weigh it yourself, which is usually reasonable for Standard Level work and poor for a Higher Level extension paper. Or a statement that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need. None of the researched competitor pages in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which makes their implied availability worth very little.

faqs.question: Our child moves from MYP to the Diploma next year. When should we start?
faqs.answer: In the spring of Year 11, while the Higher Level choices are still being made, and then across the summer. Two things need doing. The subject and level choices should be checked against the actual prerequisites of the universities on the shortlist, which is free in Year 11 and expensive to fix in Year 13. And the technical fluency a Diploma course assumes from week one, particularly in maths and the sciences, should be closed before Year 12 begins rather than during it. Six to eight online sessions covers most of that, wherever the family is travelling.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jubail-isl.closingHeading: Take the bridge out of the decision
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jubail-isl.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Al Jubail Island, the one condition worth dropping is the only one that cannot affect a grade. Tell us the subjects and levels, the campus across whichever bridge your family crosses, and the evening window that genuinely works once everybody is home and fed. Send one marked piece of work per subject. The free trial runs with a named tutor whose taught courses and levels you know in advance, and it ends with a written gap list. Internal Assessment dates go into the plan first, because the school has already fixed them. Lessons are one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Work out what the date demands before you work out who to hire
paragraphs: Al Karamah sits inland on the Abu Dhabi island, next to Al Mushrif and a few minutes from the schools most of its families use. It is a quiet, established district, and its Diploma students are mostly in their second year by the time a parent starts searching. That timing is not an accident. The Diploma front-loads teaching and back-loads consequences: Year 12 feels manageable, and then internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay and mock examinations all land inside one twelve-week stretch of Year 13.

Which means the first useful question is not who to hire. It is what the next eight weeks have to achieve. A student with one weak Higher Level subject and no internal assessment pending needs a different plan from a student holding three unfinished drafts and a mock timetable. Both are common in this district and only one of them is a teaching problem. The other is a sequencing problem, and hiring a subject specialist for it wastes money that would be better spent on two sessions of planning.

The honest market picture matters here too. In-home tuition in Abu Dhabi is real, widely advertised and priced accordingly: published rates run from around AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included. That premium pays for the journey, not the teaching. In Al Karamah the drive is short, so the premium is modest; from Khalifa City it is an hour of somebody's evening. A family deciding where the money goes should see that arithmetic rather than be sold around it.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Al Karamah. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is stated on every country page on this site. For UAE families the lesson is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own drafts and papers on screen, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time and shifted after iftar during Ramadan. The trade is physical presence for specialist choice, and for Diploma-level work that trade is usually worth making.

What follows is the calendar version of a tutoring page. A term-by-term map of what each stage of the Diploma owes, the session counted backwards from results, the internal assessment crunch described as it actually arrives, what mock season in Abu Dhabi is for, how Ramadan moves the revision window, and an eight-week plan sorted by where a student is starting. Take the part that matches your date and ignore the rest. If you only read one section, read the eight-week table, because it is the one that says plainly what each starting point can and cannot expect, including the cases where the right advice is to stop rescuing one subject and protect the other five.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.programmesIntro: The three IB programmes behave differently against a calendar, which is the only thing this page cares about. Each is described in terms of what its assessment rhythm does to a family's year in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and reporting built around learner attributes rather than percentages. The calendar pressure here is the exhibition in the final year, which arrives with a research expectation most ten-year-olds have never met. Support at this stage is about study habits, reading stamina and number fluency, not about examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: Al Karamah families often have a primary child in an IB continuum school and an older one on a different route entirely, because the schools within reach of this district split between the two. That makes the household calendar more crowded than either programme alone suggests, and it is worth mapping both before committing to a weekly slot.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, assessed through tasks spread across the year rather than through terminal papers. The calendar pressure is continuous and low-grade: there is almost always a task due. Students who do not read the criterion a task is assessing lose marks all year without ever failing to understand the content.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years Programme ends just as the Diploma option form appears, so the final year doubles as a selection year. A Year 11 student in this district is often choosing between the Diploma and a linear route at a different school, and the decision deserves evidence rather than instinct. Ask for the criteria rubrics; schools rarely offer them unprompted.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the creativity, activity, service requirement, assessed through internally marked work across both years and external papers at the end. The deadline load is the defining feature. Most Year 13 students who ask for help need triage across subjects before they need teaching inside one.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a date a family books flights around has to come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. Internal deadlines are set by the school and are the ones that actually move.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Karamah families ask about most, each described by what it demands at this point in the year rather than by its syllabus in general.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with the exploration carrying a fifth of the grade. The exploration is the calendar item: it is due long before the papers and it is the thing students postpone. Higher Level adds a third paper rewarding unfamiliar problems rather than recall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Calculator technique is a learnable skill that students assume they already have. The exploration here lends itself to real data, which is a genuine advantage if the topic is chosen early and a liability if it is not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Extended responses that ask for explanation rather than calculation, plus practical and data-analysis skills that are consistently underprepared. The internal assessment needs a workable research question months before the write-up, and a weak question cannot be rescued by good analysis later.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the arithmetic slips that cost more than conceptual gaps. Most internal assessment marks are lost on methodology and evaluation rather than on chemistry. A tutor teaches the criteria and reads drafts; the student designs and writes the work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus command-term discipline: describe, explain, outline and evaluate are worth several grades across a paper. Students who revise by rereading notes plateau early. The repair is answering past questions and checking which verb the mark scheme was actually rewarding.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to real organisations, with the Higher Level research project needing primary or secondary material secured early. Students lose marks by describing a company instead of analysing a decision. The calendar risk is choosing an organisation that will not supply usable information.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essay structure and the internal assessment investigation, which requires a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit. The investigation is a term-long job that students routinely start in the final fortnight, and that is where most of the lost marks come from.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy paired with evaluation. A faultless diagram without explanation scores poorly, and so does fluent prose without a diagram. The internal assessment commentaries are dated to published articles, so the deadline work is finding suitable articles early rather than writing quickly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the unseen analysis paper reward structure under time pressure more than familiarity with the texts. Students who know the works well still lose marks by not building an argument. Preparation is rehearsal against a clock, not more reading.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Two components assessed largely on the quality of the question. A vague research question produces a capped essay however well written. Support means interrogating the question, teaching referencing, and giving feedback on drafts the student has produced themselves.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.regionsIntro: Al Karamah shares a school calendar with the districts around it, and the differences between them are mostly about travel time and when a session can start.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and in the same catchment. Mock timetables and internal deadlines tend to be identical for students from both districts, so a tutor working across the pair is planning against one calendar rather than two.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: A few minutes north-east, denser and more mixed in curriculum. Diploma numbers are smaller here than in the villa districts, so a Year 13 in Al Nahyan has fewer classmates sitting the same papers to revise with.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: West along the shore, and the district whose Diploma cohorts most resemble this one's. Several second-year students here carry the same Higher Level combinations, which makes shared mock timing a useful planning signal.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Fifteen minutes out, considerably more at pickup. Saadiyat school days end late and co-curricular programmes run long, so a realistic weekday slot for a student there starts at six rather than four.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Across the Khaleej Al Arabi towards the airport. The term-time round trip costs a travelling tutor well over an hour, which is where the in-home travel premium stops being defensible for a weekly arrangement.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: The corridor towards the Dubai road, with long bus routes. Students arrive home tired, so a shorter session held reliably beats the ninety-minute block a travelling tutor needs in order to justify the drive.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A bridge away with a young population, so most of its students are in primary and lower secondary. Diploma demand there is thin, which is one reason local tutor pools cannot be relied on for second-year support.

schoolClusters.note: The schools this district uses are minutes away, and between them they cover the Diploma and the linear route, which is why neighbouring households often run completely different calendars. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; no affiliation is implied.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks can actually achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is a real amount of time and a limited one. It is enough to repair accuracy, fix a technique that is leaking marks on every paper, finish a stalled internal assessment draft, or raise a grade where the content is understood and the execution is not. It is not enough to rebuild a two-year Higher Level course from a weak base, and a provider who tells a family otherwise in April is selling hope. Knowing which of those two situations you are in is the single most valuable thing a diagnostic session produces.

The honest version depends on the starting point. A student losing marks to presentation, rounding, command terms and timing can gain substantially in eight weeks, because those are learnable routines rather than knowledge gaps. A student who cannot access half the Higher Level syllabus needs a different conversation, which might be about dropping to Standard Level if the school still allows it, or about accepting a realistic grade and protecting the other five subjects. Both conversations are better had early.

The table below sets out what each starting point can reasonably expect from an eight-week block. It is deliberately unflattering in places. A page that promises the same outcome from every starting position is useless for planning, and planning is the entire purpose of the eight-week window. No tutor, however experienced, can guarantee a grade, and any provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards, term by term
paragraphs: Families plan forwards and the Diploma runs backwards. Everything is dated from the examination session, and by the time an external paper is sat, most of the internal grade is already fixed. That is why a Year 13 parent in February is working with far less room than the twelve remaining weeks suggest, and why a Year 12 parent in February has more room than they realise. The structure, rather than any date, is what a family needs to see.

Working back from the session: external papers come last. Before them sits the final revision stretch, and before that the school's mock window, which exists to diagnose rather than to predict. Before that the internal assessment deadlines fall, usually clustered, because every subject wants its coursework in before mocks. Before those, the Extended Essay progresses through a question, a supervisor meeting, a first draft and a final submission. And before all of it, in the first term of Year 12, sit the subject and level choices that determine how hard everything afterwards will be.

Two Abu Dhabi specifics change this picture. Schools here are inspected by ADEK, and inspection windows occupy staff attention at particular points in the year, which is not a reason to panic but is a reason not to expect rapid feedback in those weeks. And Ramadan moves earlier each year, which means the month lands at a different point in the Diploma cycle each time: some years it sits in the internal assessment crunch, others in the revision run. Plan the slot for the month before it begins.

sections.heading: Why internal deadlines bite harder than examinations
paragraphs: Parents worry about papers and students are broken by coursework. The reason is arithmetic. Internal assessment carries a meaningful share of the grade in most subjects, the deadlines are set internally rather than by the IB, and they are therefore the ones that slip, cluster and collide. A Year 13 in Al Karamah can easily face a chemistry write-up, an economics commentary, a maths exploration and an Extended Essay revision inside three weeks, each set by a different teacher who is unaware of the others.

The failure mode is predictable. The student does the one with the nearest deadline, submits it half finished, and starts the next one already behind. Nothing in that sequence is a knowledge problem, and buying subject tutoring to solve it is buying the wrong thing. What helps is a single sheet with every deadline, every draft date and every mock on it, ranked by weight and by how far the work has gone. Two sessions produce that sheet, and it usually changes what the family thought the priority was.

There is a second, quieter cost. Students who are behind on coursework stop attending to teaching, because the urgent work crowds out the important work, and a term of that leaves gaps that surface in the mock. Catching the sequencing problem early protects the teaching as well as the deadlines. This is the part of Diploma support that no competitor page in this market describes, and it is the part that most reliably changes an outcome.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Al Karamah: what the market charges, and what travel buys
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real and substantial market in Abu Dhabi, so the fair thing is to price it properly rather than dismiss it. Published rates for a one-to-one visit including travel run from about AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500. Monthly in-home packages in the market sit at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those figures belong to the providers who published them.

Compare that with a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The gap between the in-home and online bands is travel: the drive, the fuel, and the session that cannot be refilled when a family cancels at five o'clock. In Al Karamah the drive is short, so that premium is small. From the mainland communities it is the largest line in the price.

The thing travel does not buy is teaching quality, and on a calendar-driven page that matters. A travelling tutor has to fit inside a radius and inside the traffic, which shrinks the pool of people who have actually taught the Higher Level component your child is failing. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and for Al Karamah the lesson runs online instead. The case for it is in the comparison table rather than in adjectives.

sections.heading: What a mock is for, and how Abu Dhabi families misread it
paragraphs: A mock examination is a diagnostic instrument that families routinely treat as a prediction. The grade on the front is the least informative part of it. What matters is the mark breakdown by question and by criterion, because that is what tells a tutor where the marks went. A student with a grade 4 who lost most of it to timing on the last two questions is in a completely different position from a student with a grade 4 spread evenly across the paper, and the plan for each is different.

Schools in this emirate usually run mocks about a term before the session, which is late enough to be realistic and early enough to act on. The first week after results is the most productive tutoring week of the year, and it is routinely wasted on disappointment. Bring the marked script rather than the grade. A specialist reading the script will produce a ranked list of losses in twenty minutes, and that list is actionable in a way that a grade never is.

The second misreading is treating a strong mock as a finish line. Diploma mocks are typically sat before every topic has been taught, so a good grade in February says the student is on course rather than done. The useful response to a strong mock is to sharpen question choice and attack the hardest paper, not to reduce the work. Either way, the mock is evidence, and evidence beats four weeks of impressions about how sessions are going.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and where the revision window actually goes
paragraphs: Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so it does not sit at a fixed point in the Diploma cycle. In some years it lands in the internal assessment crunch, in others in the final revision run, and the planning consequences are different in each case. School hours shorten, family routines move later, and the genuinely productive study window often sits after iftar rather than in the afternoon when a tired student is fasting.

The practical approach is to decide the schedule before the month starts. Sessions can shift to post-iftar timing for the whole month and return afterwards, and students who agree that in advance keep their momentum. Those who improvise it usually lose the first fortnight and then try to recover it during Eid, when nobody is working. Online delivery makes the shift easy, because a nine o'clock session costs no one a drive across the island.

Eid and the long summer break raise a separate question: should a Diploma student work through them. For a student entering their second year, a short block over the summer on the hardest Higher Level subject is one of the highest-return things available, because it is the only period with no competing deadlines. For a student who has just finished the session, the answer is no. Rest is part of the plan, and a provider who sells August sessions to a student who has already sat their papers is selling to the parent's anxiety.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services system.

Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why no amount should be quoted at you; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. Asking a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit is entirely reasonable, and the permit is held in the individual's own name rather than by an agency on their behalf.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates that teachers may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. Beyond the rule there is a plain conflict: the person marking your child's internal assessment should not be paid to prepare it with them.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is three days away
paragraphs: The pressure point for integrity is not a student's character; it is a Tuesday with two drafts due on Thursday. That is when a service offering to finish the work looks reasonable, and at least one page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright. The consequence does not land on the provider. The school authenticates the work, the board treats submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the student's diploma is what is at risk.

The workable boundary is this. A tutor may teach the skills a component needs, explain the published criteria, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, demonstrate referencing, and read a draft the student has written and say where it does not yet meet the criterion. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure in their own words, supply paragraphs, invent data or edit a draft to completion. The test is whether the words and the thinking remain the candidate's own.

In a deadline crunch the most useful honest help is triage rather than production. Deciding which component gets the remaining hours, cutting a bloated draft back to what the criteria reward, and accepting a lower mark on one piece to protect two others is real support and it is entirely legitimate. We would rather have that conversation and lose the sale than be in the business of producing coursework, and saying so on the page is more use to a parent than saying it in the terms.
