process.title: Start with the date, not the subject
process.description: Tell us what is due and when: internal assessment deadlines, the mock window, the session. The calendar decides whether this is a teaching job or a sequencing job, and those need different people and different numbers of sessions.

process.title: Send the marked script or the draft
process.description: A mock script with the breakdown, or a draft with supervisor comments. Twenty minutes with real marked work tells a specialist more than any description, because the marks show where the loss is rather than where it feels like it is.

process.title: Free trial, spent on the diagnosis
process.description: The first session costs nothing and is used to produce a ranked list of what is costing the most marks and what the remaining weeks can realistically fix. That list is yours whether or not anything follows it.

process.title: Fix the slot and the Ramadan plan together
process.description: Choose the hour that survives the school finish, the bus run and the activity that owns a weekday evening, and agree now what happens during Ramadan. A slot decided in advance holds; one improvised in the first week of the month does not.

process.title: Re-plan when a mock lands
process.description: Mock results are the best evidence of the year and the week afterwards is the most productive tutoring week available. The sequence is rewritten then, and if the error log has flattened, fewer sessions are the honest recommendation.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the calendar backwards
whyPoints.description: The first thing we establish is what is due and when, because that determines whether a family needs subject teaching, deadline triage or a realistic conversation about a Higher Level grade. Three different answers, and only one of them is more hours.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before anything else
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Al Karamah are online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. A parent should know that from the first screen rather than at the point of booking.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what eight weeks can do
whyPoints.description: Some starting points gain a great deal in eight weeks and some do not. The table on this page says which is which, including the cases where the answer is to protect the other five subjects instead of rescuing one.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, and kept separate from our own arrangement. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote dollars at families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: The integrity line held under pressure
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here produces an internal assessment or an essay, including in the week it is due, and a competitor selling exactly that is the reason this needs saying out loud.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, not implied
whyPoints.description: Deadline season and pre-session weeks are the tightest in the year. Where the right specialist is not free, the answer is a date and an alternative rather than a booking that quietly becomes a mismatch in session two.

faqs.question: Will an IB home tutor actually come to our villa in Al Karamah?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. That is a genuine limitation and it is stated here rather than discovered at booking. The in-home market in Abu Dhabi does exist, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. What that premium pays for is the journey. The case for taking the lesson online is that the tutor can be chosen for the component rather than for the drive.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks long enough to change my son's Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where he is starting. If he understands the content and is losing marks to timing, command terms and presentation, eight weeks is genuinely productive, because those are routines rather than knowledge. If half a Higher Level course is inaccessible, the honest answer is no, and the better plan is to protect the other five subjects and discuss the level with the school. A diagnostic session on a marked script will tell you which case applies, and that is worth buying before anything else.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment should my daughter finish first?
faqs.answer: Rank them by assessment weight and by how far each has already gone, not by which deadline is nearest. The nearest-deadline strategy is why Year 13 students end the term with four half-finished pieces. Put every deadline, draft date and mock on one sheet, then decide deliberately, accepting a lower mark on one component if that protects two others. Two sessions produce that sheet, and in this district it regularly shows that the subject the parent was worried about is not the urgent one.

faqs.question: When do UAE schools sit the IB examinations?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. This page deliberately publishes no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own website blocks automated checking and a date a family books flights around should come from the school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What can be planned on is the structure: external papers last, a final revision stretch of six to eight weeks before them, the school mock window roughly a term earlier, and internal deadlines clustered before the mocks.

faqs.question: How should we use the week after mock results?
faqs.answer: It is the most productive tutoring week of the year and it is usually wasted on disappointment. Get the marked script rather than the grade, and have a specialist read it. Losses concentrated in the final questions mean timing. Losses spread evenly mean coverage. Losses on explanation questions mean command terms. Each of those has a different fix, and twenty minutes with the script produces a ranked list that is actionable in a way the grade on the front never is.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The market bands are published by the providers themselves. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Named specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and premium examiner-branded tuition quoted at AED 500 to 650, where BartyED states AED 650. In-home visits including travel are AED 180 to 500. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and confirms the rate in the match conversation.

faqs.question: How do Al Karamah families keep Diploma revision going through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing it before the month starts is the difference between keeping momentum and losing a fortnight. School hours shorten, routines move later, and the productive study window usually sits after iftar rather than in the afternoon. Ramadan shifts earlier each year, so it falls at a different point in the Diploma cycle each time, sometimes in the coursework crunch and sometimes in the revision run. Online delivery makes the change simple, because a late session costs nobody a drive across the island.

faqs.question: Is a summer block worth it before the second year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For a student entering the second year, usually yes, because it is the only stretch of the calendar with no competing deadlines. A short block on the hardest Higher Level subject, or on getting an Extended Essay question settled, pays back disproportionately. For a student who has just finished the session, no. Rest belongs in the plan, and a provider selling sessions to a student whose papers are already sat is selling to a parent's anxiety rather than to a need.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit to teach my child privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring privately without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be wary of any specific amount quoted to you.

faqs.question: Could we pay my child's own Diploma teacher for extra sessions?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi you should assume not. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct restricts serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK. There is also a conflict worth avoiding: the person who assesses an internal assessment and sets the mocks should not be paid to prepare the student for them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish an internal assessment if the deadline is in three days?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody who offers to should end your search. The school authenticates submitted work and the board treats work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, with the consequence falling on the student rather than the provider. What a tutor can legitimately do under that pressure is triage: decide which component gets the remaining hours, cut a bloated draft back to what the criteria reward, and accept a lower mark on one piece to protect two others. That is genuine help and it is often the most valuable kind.

faqs.question: My Year 12 looks fine. Is it too early to arrange anything?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, and almost nobody uses it. Year 12 is where level choices are still reversible, where an Extended Essay question can be settled calmly, and where a weak technique can be fixed before it is reinforced across two years of practice. Families who arrange support in the first year typically need fewer hours overall than families who arrive in February of the second year, because the work is preventive rather than remedial. One session a week is normally enough at that stage.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 13 in this area be doing?
faqs.answer: One a week through the autumn, moving to two in the six to eight weeks before the session if the error log justifies it. Starting at two is usually counterproductive: the student has no time to practise between sessions, so the tutor re-teaches instead of correcting. A Year 13 here also carries the mandatory Arabic, Islamic studies and social studies lessons alongside six Diploma subjects and the core, so free evenings are fewer than the subject list implies.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who is already overwhelmed?
faqs.answer: Often better than in-home, because it removes a visitor from a stressed household and because the sessions can be shorter and more frequent. A sixty-minute slot twice a week is easier to hold than one ninety-minute block that a travelling tutor needs to justify. The student's own drafts and papers stay on screen, working is written live on a shared whiteboard, and a written note after each session means the plan survives a week where nothing else does.

faqs.question: What if the right Higher Level specialist is not free this term?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you options rather than filling the slot. A later weekday hour with the right tutor usually beats an immediate hour with the wrong one. A single diagnostic session produces a ranked list the student can work through alone. A waiting list with an actual date lets a family plan. Niche Higher Level subjects and core specialists are thinner year round, and demand concentrates before the session, which is why the diagnostic is worth booking in the autumn.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.closingHeading: Tell us the date and we will tell you what it can carry
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.closingBody: Start with what is due rather than with what is wrong. Send the mock script or the stalled draft, take the free trial with it open, and finish that session with two things: a ranked list of where the marks are going and an honest view of what the remaining weeks can achieve. Lessons for Al Karamah run online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to the Abu Dhabi school week and moved after iftar during Ramadan. If the specialist you need is not free this term, we will say so and give you a date rather than a substitute.

intro.heading: The real question behind "IB home tutor in Al Khalidiyah"
paragraphs: Almost nobody searching for an IB home tutor in Al Khalidiyah actually wants a stranger in their living room. What they want is the thing a home tutor was once the only way to get: an adult who has taught the Diploma, who recognises the paper their child is about to sit, and who is in the room at the moment the confusion happens. The physical travel was never the product. It was the delivery cost attached to the product, and in Abu Dhabi that cost is high, because Al Khalidiyah sits in the dense middle of the island and the drive from Khalifa City or Mussafah at six in the evening is not a short one.

That matters because of how the Diploma is structured. The IB is not one syllabus with a general difficulty level. Mathematics alone splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level, and the HL Analysis Paper 3 is a different animal from anything in Applications SL. Chemistry HL, Economics HL and English A Language and Literature are three unrelated skills. A tutor who is excellent at one is frequently no use at another. The pool of people who can genuinely teach a specific subject at a specific level is small, and it does not get larger because you draw a circle on a map around Al Khalidiyah.

So the honest answer to the question is this. If you insist on a tutor who drives to an Al Khalidiyah address, your choice is restricted to the people willing to make that drive on that evening, and the subject match becomes whatever is left. If you drop the travel requirement, the choice becomes every specialist who teaches that subject at that level and can work at your hour. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session runs online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared screen for working through a past paper line by line.

There is a cost argument too, and it runs in the same direction. Published Abu Dhabi and Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the top of that band reflecting travel and a dedicated time slot. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at around AED 150 to 300. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car, a parking space and forty minutes of someone's evening, paid for by you and subtracted from the lesson your child actually needs.

The rest of this page does the work a parent in Al Khalidiyah would otherwise have to do by phone: what subject coverage honestly looks like and what happens when a niche Higher Level subject has no free specialist, the five questions that separate a Diploma teacher from a general maths tutor, exactly where the line sits on Internal Assessment help, what an ADEK inspection rating does and does not tell you about your child's school, and the Diploma year read backwards from the May session so you can see which eight weeks matter.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khalidiyah.programmesIntro: Al Khalidiyah families sit across the full IB continuum, because several Abu Dhabi schools run the Primary Years and Middle Years Programmes as the feeder route into the Diploma. Each programme is assessed differently, and the tutoring that helps a Year 7 MYP student is not the tutoring that helps a DP2 candidate eight weeks from exams.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Progress is judged through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, a portfolio of work and the Year 6 Exhibition. Support at this stage is about building the number sense, reading stamina and written structure that the Middle Years Programme will later assume, rather than preparing for a paper. Tutors work on fluency and confidence, and on the research and presentation habits the Exhibition rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools within reach of Al Khalidiyah run the PYP, and transfers into the island's primary years arrive from British, Indian and American systems mid-term. The gap is rarely ability. It is that a child arriving from a textbook-and-worksheet system has never been asked to pose their own research question, and the first inquiry unit lands as a shock.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with command terms that reward explanation and justification over recall. The Personal Project in Year 10 or 11 is the first substantial independent piece a student produces. Tutoring here is largely about decoding criteria language and writing to it, because a student can know the content and still score low on Criterion C or D.
programmes.countryNote: Al Khalidiyah parents often notice a dip in MYP Years 9 and 10, which is usually the point where criteria-based marking replaces right-answer marking. It is also the year to settle the Mathematics route, because the MYP extended maths strand is the natural feed into Analysis and Approaches while the standard strand feeds Applications and Interpretation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and TOK matrix. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth between 20 and 30 per cent of the final grade, which means a significant share of the result is decided long before the examination hall.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Al Khalidiyah enquiries sit. The pattern is consistent: a DP1 student copes until the first mock, then two Higher Level subjects start competing for the same evenings, and the Extended Essay deadline collides with internal assessment deadlines in March. The fix is almost never more hours. It is sequencing the term so the Exploration is drafted before the mock revision window opens.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a smaller number of DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. It suits a student who wants IB-assessed academic subjects alongside an applied qualification rather than the full six-subject Diploma, and the DP courses inside it are examined to exactly the same standard.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is less common across Abu Dhabi than the full Diploma, so a student on it often finds their school cannot staff individual subject help at the depth they need. Tutoring for a CP student in Al Khalidiyah usually targets the one or two DP courses carried inside the programme, and the reflective project's research and referencing standards.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khalidiyah.subjectsIntro: A request from Al Khalidiyah is only answerable at subject-and-level precision. "IB Maths" is four different courses. The subjects below are the ones Abu Dhabi island families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At SL, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40 per cent each and the Exploration 20. At HL the split is 30, 30, 20 and 20, with Paper 3 presenting two extended problem-solving questions. Marks are lost on proof by induction, on complex numbers in polar form, and on failing to show method where the mark scheme awards it separately from the answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, modelling and, at HL, matrices, graph theory and differential equations solved numerically. The frequent error is treating it as the easier course. It is not easier, it is different, and students who choose it to avoid algebra are caught by the volume of interpretation writing the mark scheme demands.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice, Paper 2 is structured response, and the Scientific Investigation carries 20 per cent. HL adds depth across energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. The marks go on mechanism arrows drawn imprecisely, on energetics sign conventions, and on investigation write-ups that record data without evaluating its uncertainty.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Heavy on derivation and on reading a graph gradient for a physical quantity. Students who can quote a formula still lose marks because they cannot say which assumption makes it valid. Circular motion, capacitance at HL and the whole of the uncertainty treatment in practical work are the predictable trouble spots for island school candidates.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content hides the real skill, which is applying a named process to an unfamiliar context under command-term discipline. "Outline" and "explain" carry different mark allocations and students routinely answer one when asked the other. Statistical treatment in the Scientific Investigation is where otherwise strong candidates drop a band.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of 800 words each, built on recent news articles, plus examination papers that reward a correctly labelled diagram and a developed evaluation. The usual loss is a diagram drawn without axis labels or a shifted curve left unexplained, and an evaluation paragraph that restates the analysis instead of weighing it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with an HL Internal Assessment of 1,800 words on a real organisation's issue. The tools matter less than the application: an Ansoff matrix earns nothing on its own. Students lose marks by describing a business rather than answering the question asked about it, and by ignoring the quantitative sections.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay, with an Individual Oral assessed internally and, at HL, an HL Essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. Marks are lost on Paper 1 when a student summarises a text instead of analysing how it produces its effect, and on the Individual Oral when the global issue is too broad to anchor.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title, plus an exhibition of three objects with commentaries totalling up to 950 words. TOK contributes to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Weak essays answer the title with opinion; strong ones build a claim, test it against a counterclaim and name the knowledge framework in play.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, marked out of 34 across five criteria, with Critical Thinking alone worth 12. The supervisor is the school's; a tutor's role is to question the research focus, check the method is answerable and give feedback on drafts the student has written. The student writes every word.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khalidiyah.regionsIntro: Al Khalidiyah sits in the western-central band of Abu Dhabi island, and families there routinely compare notes with neighbours a few minutes away. Online delivery removes the only variable that actually differs between these districts, which is the drive. The areas below are the ones Al Khalidiyah parents mention most.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Immediately west of Al Khalidiyah, with the marina, the airstrip and a cluster of long-established schools. Al Bateen families and Al Khalidiyah families often share a school run, which is why their session timings tend to be identical.

regions.name: The Corniche
regions.note: The waterfront strip along the island's north-west edge. Tower living means no garden and often no spare room, so a quiet corner with a laptop at a fixed hour tends to work better than a tutor arriving into a shared living space.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Inland and villa-heavy, with several of the emirate's longest-standing British and IB schools nearby. The ten-minute hop from Al Khalidiyah is short on a map and much longer at four in the afternoon on Airport Road.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: The former Tourist Club Area on the island's north-east side, dense with apartment towers and close to Al Maryah Island. Families here are frequently in two-bedroom flats where a quiet study hour is easier to protect than a visitor is to seat.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Across the bridge from the island's east side, newer and still filling out. Several Al Khalidiyah families moved there for space, kept the same school, and now run a longer school run in both directions each day.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Home to the cultural district and to some of the emirate's newest international schools. A Saadiyat school with an Al Khalidiyah address means a bridge crossing twice a day, and an evening tutor visit would mean a third.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: On the mainland, well off the island, with its own cluster of large campuses. Tutors who live in Khalifa City are exactly the people who would charge an Al Khalidiyah family the upper end of the in-home band, because the journey is real.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: On the mainland coast towards the airport, popular with families who work in the Khalifa City corridor. The distance from Al Khalidiyah is the clearest illustration of why a specialist pool defined by driving range is a small pool.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khalidiyah.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Al Khalidiyah request. All of them run online over live video. The choice is really about how much of the week the tutor is responsible for, and that depends on how far into the Diploma the student already is.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A fixed sixty or ninety-minute slot each week in a single subject at a single level. This is the default and the one that works for a DP1 student who is coping but drifting. The value sits in continuity: the tutor knows what last week's gap was and can check whether it closed, which no sequence of one-off sessions can do.

Shared screen for working through past-paper questions in real time
A short written note after each session saying what was covered

modes.title: Internal Assessment and core support
modes.description: A short block of sessions around the Exploration, the Scientific Investigation, the Extended Essay or the TOK essay. The tutor questions the research focus, checks the method will actually produce analysable data, and gives feedback on drafts the student has already written. Nothing is drafted for the student, and the school supervisor remains the authority on the task.

Criterion-by-criterion feedback against the published descriptors

modes.title: Examination-term intensive
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week through a defined window, usually the eight to ten weeks before mocks or before the May session. The work is almost entirely past-paper under timing, with the tutor marking to the published mark scheme and then teaching to whatever the script reveals. It is the most expensive format and the shortest, by design.

sections.heading: Is there an IB specialist near Al Khalidiyah who actually knows the syllabus?
paragraphs: Probably not for your specific subject and level, and that is the useful answer rather than a discouraging one. Al Khalidiyah is a residential district of a city of roughly a million and a half people, and the number of adults within a short drive who have taught, say, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and can describe what Paper 3 rewards is small. The number who are also free at six on a Tuesday is smaller still. A proximity search optimises for the wrong variable.

What a parent is really trying to buy is syllabus fluency. That means a tutor who can tell you, without looking it up, that the Maths Exploration is 20 per cent of the grade and is marked across five criteria with Use of Mathematics worth six of the twenty marks. It means someone who knows that Chemistry Paper 1 is multiple choice and that the Scientific Investigation is the single largest internally assessed component. A tutor who has only taught a national curriculum will teach the content and miss the assessment, and in the Diploma the assessment is most of the difficulty.

Removing the travel constraint changes the shape of the problem entirely. Instead of asking who is nearby, the question becomes who teaches this course, at this level, in this hour. A student in Al Khalidiyah studying Economics HL can be matched to an Economics specialist who has marked dozens of commentaries, rather than to a general humanities tutor who lives in Al Bateen. The lesson happens over live video with a shared screen, which for past-paper work is arguably better than two people leaning over one printed page.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly is the point: a UAE family should know exactly what they are buying before the trial lesson, not discover it afterwards.

sections.heading: Subject coverage, match times and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No tutoring service covers every IB subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones that go quiet after you pay. The honest version is a coverage map. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management and English A are requested constantly from Abu Dhabi island and are consequently the best covered. Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish, Global Politics, Music and Design Technology are requested rarely, and a request for one of those at Higher Level can take longer to fill.

The second variable is the hour. An Al Khalidiyah DP2 student who needs a session at eight in the evening Gulf Standard Time has a much larger pool than one who can only do seven in the morning before school. Most families settle on a window between five and nine in the evening, which overlaps comfortably with specialists in several time zones. That is a direct consequence of online delivery: the scheduling constraint is the student's calendar, not a driver's route.

When no specialist is free for a niche combination, there are three honest responses, and promising a match is not one of them. The first is to offer a waiting period with a date. The second is to propose a different but genuinely qualified tutor and say clearly what the difference is, for example a Physics HL specialist covering Sports Exercise and Health Science SL mechanics but not the physiology. The third is to decline. A declined request costs a family nothing. A bad match costs them a term.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor really knows the Diploma
paragraphs: Parents in Al Khalidiyah are often handed a WhatsApp number by a neighbour and asked to judge a tutor in a ten-minute call. Credentials are easy to assert and hard to check from a message. Assessment knowledge is almost impossible to fake, because a tutor who has prepared Diploma candidates carries the structure of the papers in their head the way a driver carries a familiar route.

Ask what the Internal Assessment in that specific subject is worth and how it is marked. A Maths specialist will say 20 per cent, five criteria, twenty marks, with six of them on Use of Mathematics. A Chemistry specialist will describe the Scientific Investigation and the criteria it is judged against. A vague answer about coursework counting towards the grade means the tutor has not sat with the published descriptors.

Ask which papers the student will sit and how long each one is. Ask what the command terms in that subject actually require, and the difference between outline, explain and evaluate in mark-scheme terms. Ask what they will not do, which is the question that separates a teacher from an essay mill: the correct answer names the boundary on Internal Assessment help without being prompted. And ask how they will know the tutoring is working, because "your child will feel more confident" is not a measure and a marked timed paper is.

Finally, ask about the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A tutor who is confused by the question is worth a second look. The official application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.
bullets: What is the Internal Assessment worth in this subject, and how is it marked?
Which papers will my child sit, how long is each, and what weighting does each carry?
What is the difference between outline, explain and evaluate in this mark scheme?
What will you refuse to do with an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay?
How will we both know, in eight weeks, whether this is working?

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the most commercially awkward section on the page and the most necessary. The Abu Dhabi and Dubai search results for IB help include operations that sell completed Internal Assessments outright, with one researched site offering finished IAs at a fixed price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A Diploma can be withheld. That risk does not appear in the advertisement.

The boundary itself is not subtle. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, interrogate a research question, point out that a planned method will not generate analysable data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not draft the text, rewrite paragraphs into their own prose, supply data, choose the title and hand it over, or edit a piece to the point where the words are no longer the student's. The test is simple: after the session, could the student explain every sentence and every decision as their own? If not, the line has been crossed.

Schools in Abu Dhabi take this seriously because they have to. The supervisor signs off on authenticity, and an IB coordinator who sees a sudden jump between a student's classwork and their Extended Essay draft will ask about it. A tutor who has worked properly makes that conversation easy, because the progress is visible across drafts the student produced. A tutor who has written it makes it unsurvivable.

There is a practical benefit to working inside the boundary, beyond staying out of trouble. The criteria reward personal engagement and reflection, and those cannot be outsourced. A ghostwritten Exploration tends to score poorly on exactly the criteria it was bought to secure, because the voice is wrong and the reflection is generic.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection ratings and what your school report is not telling you
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi is not Dubai, and the regulator is not KHDA. The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and it publishes inspection outcomes. Parents in Al Khalidiyah comparing two schools will often find both described in marketing as high performing, and the only way to compare them on the same scale is the regulator's own published rating. Competitor tutoring pages for Abu Dhabi almost universally fail to name ADEK at all, which tells you how little localisation most of them carry.

An inspection rating describes a school, not a child. A strong overall judgement means leadership, teaching quality and provision were judged strong across the cohort. It does not mean that every department is strong, and it certainly does not mean a particular Higher Level class is well staffed this year. A specific subject can be weak inside an excellent school, usually because of a mid-year staff change, and that is exactly the situation that generates a tutoring enquiry from a family who cannot understand why their child is struggling at a school with a good report.

The useful reading is to treat the rating as background and the subject-level evidence as foreground. Ask the school for the grade distribution in that subject, ask what the mock paper was marked against, and ask whether the class has had a consistent teacher this year. A school with a strong rating will answer those questions readily. If it does not, the rating has not told you what you needed to know.

One further Abu Dhabi-specific point: press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Treat that as reported rather than quoted, and verify against the current ADEK policy document, but do not go looking for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately.

sections.heading: The Diploma year read backwards from the exam session
paragraphs: Most families start tutoring at the point of panic, which is usually a mock result in January or February. Reading the year backwards instead shows why that is late. The Diploma's internally assessed components all fall due in the months before the examination session, and they compete with each other. A DP2 student in Al Khalidiyah is frequently finishing an Extended Essay, two Internal Assessments and a TOK essay in the same eight-week stretch that mock revision needs.

Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, and the November session exists as the alternative route. IB examination and results dates are not restated here: ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a page a parent acts on is worse than no date at all. Confirm the current session window and results day with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly, and treat any third-party calendar as a prompt to check rather than a source.

Where dates are genuinely verifiable, they are worth having. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge's own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, series run in May/June and November; as a worked example of how long the tail is, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The practical use of reading backwards is deciding what the next eight weeks are for. If the Exploration is undrafted in December, that is the priority and mock revision is not. If the Exploration is submitted and the mock was weak on one paper, the priority inverts. Doing both badly at once is the standard failure mode, and it is a sequencing problem rather than an effort problem.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Gulf Standard Time and when a session actually happens
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE calendar fails in predictable places. Abu Dhabi school days shorten during Ramadan, the working rhythm shifts, and evening energy moves to the hours after Iftar. A fixed six o'clock slot that worked in January becomes the worst possible time, and families who do not renegotiate it simply stop attending and then conclude that tutoring does not work for them.

The sensible approach is to agree in advance that the slot moves. For many Al Khalidiyah families the post-Iftar window is genuinely better than anything in the normal term, because the house is awake, the school day was short, and there is no homework backlog from a full timetable. For others the right answer is to pause entirely for the month and resume afterwards, which is a legitimate choice as long as it is planned rather than drifted into. The one option that does not work is keeping the old time and hoping.

Gulf Standard Time is the other scheduling fact worth stating. Sessions for Al Khalidiyah students are scheduled in local time, not converted from a European or Indian evening and handed over. That sounds obvious until you have seen a family offered a nine-thirty slot because it suited the tutor's time zone. Online delivery widens the specialist pool precisely because several time zones overlap with an Abu Dhabi evening, and the scheduling conversation should start from the student's calendar rather than the tutor's.

Summer and the long winter break deserve a decision too. A student who has chosen Higher Level subjects they are not ready for is better served by a short block of foundation work in July than by three weeks of catch-up in September. A student who is on track is better served by stopping completely. Both are defensible; drifting through the holiday with a cancelled session every other week is not.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of tutoring can realistically change, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Eight weeks of one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching. It is useful to be blunt about what that buys, because the gap between what parents hope for and what is possible is where disappointment is manufactured. Eight weeks can close a specific identified gap, and that is genuinely valuable. A student who cannot handle integration by substitution, or who loses marks on every energetics question, or who writes Economics evaluation paragraphs that only restate the analysis, can be substantially fixed in that window.

Eight weeks can also rebuild examination technique across a subject the student already broadly knows. Timed papers, marked properly against the published mark scheme, with the errors logged and re-tested, move marks reliably, because most students lose a meaningful number of marks to process rather than to ignorance. Reading the question, allocating time by mark value, showing method where the scheme awards it separately, and answering the command term asked are all learnable inside two months.

What eight weeks cannot do is teach two years of Higher Level content that was never covered, and no tutor should imply otherwise. No one can guarantee a grade, and any service that does is selling something it cannot deliver. If a DP2 student arrives in March with half of HL Physics untaught, the honest plan targets the highest-value accessible topics and the papers where marks are cheapest, and says plainly that the full syllabus is not recoverable in the time available.

This is why we agree a measure at the start. A marked timed paper in week one, a repeat in week eight, and a short written note after each session saying what was covered. If the second paper has not moved, the plan was wrong or the match was wrong, and both are fixable. Without a measure, both parent and tutor are guessing, and the guessing is usually optimistic.
bullets: Achievable in eight weeks: one diagnosed content gap closed and re-tested
Achievable: examination technique, timing and command-term discipline
Achievable: an Internal Assessment taken from a vague idea to a workable draft
Not achievable: two years of untaught Higher Level content
Not achievable: any promised grade, from anyone, at any price

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the hour
process.description: Not "IB Maths" but "Analysis and Approaches HL, DP1, needs Tuesday or Thursday after seven". The level and the hour are what determine whether a genuine specialist exists for the request, and giving them at the start saves a week of back-and-forth on both sides.

process.title: We say yes, later, or no
process.description: If a specialist is available for that course at that hour, we say so. If one will be free in two weeks, we give the date. If the combination is one we cannot staff properly, we say that instead of offering a near-enough tutor. A declined request costs you nothing; a wrong match costs a term.

process.title: A free trial lesson, before any payment
process.description: One session with the matched tutor at no cost and with no card required, so the student can judge the explanation and the tutor can diagnose rather than guess. If the fit is wrong, say so afterwards and we rematch. That is a cheaper correction in week one than in week six.

process.title: Fix the slot and agree a measure
process.description: A standing weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, plus one thing we will both look at in eight weeks. Usually that is a timed past paper marked to the official scheme, sat early and repeated at the end. The measure is agreed before the teaching starts, not invented later.

process.title: Review, adjust or stop
process.description: At the eight-week point the options are to continue, change the focus, change the tutor, or finish. Finishing is a real option and we will say so when the work is done. Open-ended tutoring that nobody reviews is how families end up paying for a habit instead of a result.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: An Al Khalidiyah student is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact course at their exact level, from the whole specialist pool rather than from the subset willing to drive across the island on a weekday evening. That is the single largest quality difference online delivery makes.

whyPoints.title: The money goes into teaching, not travel
whyPoints.description: Published Abu Dhabi in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors. The gap is a car and forty minutes of someone's evening. Spending it on a better subject match buys more than spending it on a journey.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives criterion-referenced feedback on work the student has written. Nobody drafts an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay. The boundary is stated on the page because the alternative puts a student's whole Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Some subject-and-level combinations are thin, particularly Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish and several Higher Level options. We say which, give a date or decline, and never place an unqualified tutor into a slot to avoid saying no.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled in Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set around the student's Abu Dhabi week, including a short school day in Ramadan and the post-Iftar window when that works better. The slot is agreed as movable in advance, because a timetable that cannot flex is a timetable families quietly abandon.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, figures dated
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page are attributed to the providers who publish them and described as the market rather than as our price list. Regulatory statements come from u.ae, MoHRE and ADEK. Where a date could not be verified, the page says so instead of inventing one.

faqs.question: Does anybody drive out to an Al Khalidiyah flat for lessons, or is it all on screen?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session for an Al Khalidiyah family runs online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. We state it before a trial rather than after a payment. The trade is deliberate: dropping the travel requirement means your child is matched to a specialist in their exact subject and level instead of whoever can reach the island by six, and the money that would have paid for the drive pays for teaching instead.

faqs.question: What does the Abu Dhabi market charge for an in-home IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Published rates for in-home one-to-one visits across Abu Dhabi and Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at around AED 150 to 300, and specialist IB and IGCSE tutors at AED 200 to 450 or more. Those are market figures from other providers, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: My child is at a school with a strong ADEK rating but is failing Maths HL. How?
faqs.answer: An inspection outcome describes a school across its whole cohort, not a single Higher Level class in a single year. A strong school can have a weak department, usually after a mid-year staff change, and Analysis and Approaches HL is the subject where that shows fastest because Paper 3 content is often taught last. Ask the school three questions: has this class had the same teacher all year, what was the mock marked against, and which syllabus topics remain untaught this term. The answers tell you whether the gap is your child's or the timetable's.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Maths Exploration without writing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only acceptable version. A tutor can question the topic until it becomes answerable, warn you that a planned data set will not produce analysable results, teach the five assessment criteria, and give feedback on a draft your daughter has written. A tutor cannot choose the title, supply the data, draft paragraphs or edit it into their own prose. The test is whether she could explain every sentence and every decision as her own. If she could not, the work is no longer hers and the Diploma is at risk.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Al Khalidiyah families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Which Diploma courses are the thinnest to staff for an island family like ours?
faqs.answer: Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish, Global Politics, Music and Design Technology, particularly at Higher Level. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management and English A are requested constantly from the island and are well covered, usually within a few days to a week. For the thin combinations we either give a dated waiting slot or decline. We do not fill a niche Higher Level request with a tutor who teaches something adjacent and hope it holds, because that becomes obvious in week three and costs you the term.

faqs.question: Is a session over video actually as useful as a tutor sitting next to my son?
faqs.answer: For Diploma past-paper work it is frequently better, because a shared screen shows the same worked line to both people at the same size, annotations are saved, and the session can be structured around a marked script rather than a conversation. What a video lesson needs that a visit does not is a quiet hour and a laptop the student can see properly on. What it removes is forty minutes of travel in each direction, the cost of that travel, and the risk that island traffic cancels the lesson.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a DP1 student in Al Khalidiyah start with?
faqs.answer: One subject, one session a week, sixty or ninety minutes. That is the right starting point for the overwhelming majority of DP1 enquiries, and it is deliberately less than most families expect. Two subjects at once in DP1 usually means neither gets the homework time it needs, and three means the tutoring becomes the workload. If the diagnosis after a month is that a second subject genuinely needs support, add it then. Starting small and adding on evidence costs less than starting large and cutting back.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child actually sit, and when are the dates confirmed?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, with November as the alternative route. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date that a family plans around is worse than no date. Confirm the window with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, and several competitor pages get that wrong.

faqs.question: Will the weekly slot survive Ramadan, or do we just stop for the month?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many Al Khalidiyah families that is the better slot rather than a concession. School days shorten during Ramadan and the evening rhythm shifts, so a six o'clock session that worked in January becomes the worst hour of the day. Agree in advance that the slot is movable. Some families pause for the month entirely and resume afterwards, which works fine as a planned decision. What does not work is keeping the original time and quietly missing half the sessions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Maths Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator and, at Higher Level, a Paper 3 of two extended problem-solving questions. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout and built around statistics, modelling and interpretation, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Applications is not the easier course; it is a different one, and students who choose it to avoid algebra are often caught by the volume of interpretive writing the mark scheme demands. Check the prerequisites of the degree courses your child is considering before switching.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from mocks. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to be honest about scope. Eight weeks of one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching. That is enough to close one diagnosed content gap and re-test it, and enough to rebuild examination technique across a subject the student broadly knows, which is where most students lose recoverable marks. It is not enough to teach two years of untaught Higher Level content, and no tutor should suggest otherwise. We would sit a timed paper in week one so the plan targets what the script actually shows.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both of my children, in different year groups?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the subjects and levels rather than on convenience. A specialist teaching Analysis and Approaches SL to a DP1 student can often also support an MYP Year 10 extended maths student, because the content sits on one continuum. A tutor covering Chemistry HL for one child and English A Paper 1 for another is two different specialists, and combining them would mean one of your children gets the weaker match. Separate sessions, separate tutors, same scheduling conversation.

faqs.question: Should we be looking for my child's own school teacher to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: No. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but treat the arrangement as one to avoid. A tutor who is independent of the school also gives you a second, unconflicted reading of how your child is actually doing.

faqs.question: How do we know after two months whether the tutoring worked?
faqs.answer: Because the measure is agreed before the teaching starts. In week one the student sits a timed past paper, marked against the published mark scheme rather than impressionistically. The same style of paper is repeated at week eight. Between them, each session ends with a short written note of what was covered and what is still open, and errors go into a log so the same mistake is not re-taught twice. If the second paper has not moved, either the plan or the match was wrong. Both are fixable, and both are our problem rather than yours.

intro.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: Al Manaseer is a compact residential district on the western side of Abu Dhabi island, wedged between Al Khalidiyah, Al Bateen and the Corniche. It is apartment stock rather than villa stock, which matters more than it sounds. A villa community of four hundred families generates a predictable local demand for Year 10 Maths. An apartment district generates demand spread across six curricula, four boards and twenty-odd subjects, and no single one of those reaches the volume that would make a resident specialist viable. The schools within walking distance of Al Manaseer are mostly British-curriculum or Ministry-curriculum, which is why an IB family here is looking outward from the first day of Year 12 rather than at the campus two streets away.

That is the mechanism behind the thing Al Manaseer parents keep running into. You can find somebody nearby who will sit at the kitchen table and help with homework. Finding somebody nearby who has taught Chemistry HL through two full Diploma cycles, marked against the current criteria, and knows what a 5 looks like against a 6 on the Internal Assessment, is a different search entirely. The second person exists. They are statistically unlikely to live in your building, or in the next one over.

There are roughly a dozen schools offering the International Baccalaureate across Abu Dhabi, and they are concentrated on Saadiyat Island, Al Reem Island, Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor rather than in the island's older apartment districts. A Diploma student living in Al Manaseer is therefore often commuting out to school already. Their teacher lives somewhere else again. The idea that the right subject specialist is also the nearest one is a coincidence that geography rarely supplies.

So we stopped trying to supply it. Tutoring for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. What a family in Al Manaseer gets instead is the whole matched pool rather than the fraction of it that happens to be a twenty-minute drive away, and the twenty minutes back. Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time, so the slot is set by when your child is actually home and fed rather than by how far anyone has to drive.

The rest of this page answers the question properly. What the in-home market in Abu Dhabi charges and what the travel premium buys. What a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules. And what happens, honestly, when no specialist is free for the subject you need.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-manaseer.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three school-age IB programmes. The notes below are written for Al Manaseer specifically, because what a PYP family on this part of the island needs is not what a DP2 family three streets away needs.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP runs on transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, so there is no past-paper route into it. Support at this stage is about the underlying literacy and number fluency the inquiry assumes: place value, fractions as operators, reading stamina, and writing that holds a line of argument for more than three sentences. Sessions are short and frequent, because attention rather than content is the limiting factor.
programmes.countryNote: Al Manaseer families often use a primary school close to home and then move to an IB continuum school further out for the Middle Years. That transfer is where gaps surface. A PYP child who was comfortable in a small inquiry classroom can arrive in an MYP maths set two years ahead of their fluency. Three months of number work before the move is cheaper than a year of catching up after it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment is criterion-referenced, scored A to D per subject on a one-to-eight scale, with no national paper to practise against. Families find it opaque for exactly that reason. The useful work is reading the subject's own criteria strands with the student, then marking their own piece against them until the student can predict the band before the teacher does. Criterion D, applying knowledge in unfamiliar contexts, is where most of the lost marks sit.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the one Al Manaseer parents ask about most often, because the apartment-district schools around Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen send students into Diploma cohorts at schools on Saadiyat and Al Reem. A student arriving from a generous MYP mathematics set into Analysis and Approaches HL is the single most common rescue case we see from this part of the island.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth between twenty and thirty per cent of the grade, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The written papers are the visible part; the IA and the coursework calendar are where the diploma is actually won or lost, and they are also the part no school timetable protects.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. For an Al Manaseer DP1 student, that means the real deadlines are internal ones set by their own coordinator, usually running from the autumn of DP1 for the Extended Essay through to the spring of DP2 for the last subject IA. We work to the school's calendar, not a generic one, because the school's calendar is the one with consequences.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-manaseer.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families request most, with the levels covered and what the marks actually turn on. Coverage depth varies by subject, and the later section on availability says plainly where it is thin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Al Manaseer students take when engineering or economics is in view. HL adds proof, complex numbers and a third paper sat with a calculator. Marks go on method lines left out of long questions and on calculus set up correctly then executed in a hurry.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-weighted and modelling-led, with heavier graphical calculator dependence. The common failure is treating it as the easier option and then meeting hypothesis testing and Voronoi diagrams unprepared. SL AI is a legitimate choice, not a demotion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields at HL punish weak algebra more than weak physics. Paper 2 extended response needs a stated principle before the substitution, and students who write only numbers lose the reasoning marks even when the final answer is right.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics carry the HL difficulty. The scientific investigation is where SL students most often lose a grade, usually by choosing a question with no controllable variable rather than by handling the data badly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than depth. Students who can recite a pathway still lose marks on command terms, answering a question that says evaluate as though it said describe. Practice is as much about reading the stem as learning the content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available gain: axes labelled, curves shifted the right way, the new equilibrium marked. HL Paper 3 is quantitative and is the paper Abu Dhabi students most often sit under-rehearsed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and the Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts. Students strong at content lose marks for argument that lists features instead of building a reading.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than tool recall: students who can define a decision tree still lose marks for not tying it back to the stimulus firm. The HL extension on organisational change needs real examples held in reserve.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and dry-run tracing carry disproportionate marks, and the HL abstract data structures paper rewards drawing the structure before writing anything. The internal assessment solution must solve a real client's problem, documented.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and the IA suite
subjects.description: Process coaching only. A tutor helps the student narrow a research question, plan a structure, read their own draft critically and understand the criteria. The writing is the student's, and the final section on academic honesty says exactly where that line sits.

sections.heading: What an Al Manaseer parent is really searching for
paragraphs: The phrase IB home tutor in Al Manaseer carries an assumption worth unpacking, which is that the word home is doing the important work. In practice it almost never is. When we ask families what they actually want, the answer is a person who knows the subject at the level their child is sitting it, available at a time that works, who turns up reliably and tells them the truth about progress. Home is shorthand for convenient and private, not a requirement that somebody physically enter the apartment.

That matters because the home requirement is the expensive one. It restricts the pool to tutors within driving range, adds travel cost to the hourly rate, and makes the schedule fragile in a way that a video lesson simply is not. On a district as dense as Al Manaseer, parking alone turns a sixty-minute lesson into a ninety-minute commitment for the tutor, and the rate reflects it.

Drop the geographic constraint and keep everything else and the search resolves. A Chemistry HL specialist who has taught the current syllabus through two cohorts can teach your child from wherever they are. A one-to-one video lesson with a shared whiteboard, the student's own worksheet on screen and a recording to revisit is not a compromised version of a kitchen-table lesson. For working through a problem set with annotation, it is a better room.

So this page uses the phrase parents search, and answers it honestly. IB Gram teaches Al Manaseer students online, live, one-to-one. We do not offer home visits in the UAE. What follows is the case for why that is the better trade here, with the numbers attached.
bullets: The real requirement is subject-level expertise, reliability and a workable time
Geographic proximity adds cost and fragility without adding teaching quality

sections.heading: Which Diploma subjects actually have thin coverage, and what we do about it
paragraphs: No tutoring platform has even coverage across every subject at every level, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones to be careful with. Diploma demand is heavily skewed. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics generate most requests, so the matched pool in those is deep. Specialist combinations such as Higher Level Film, Music, Global Politics or a Group 2 language at HL generate few requests, so the pool is shallow, and honesty about that is more useful to you than a promise.

The table below sets out how we handle each band. Where UAE-based coverage is thin, the fallback is a specialist teaching from elsewhere on a Gulf-Standard-Time slot, which is the same delivery format you would get anyway, since every UAE lesson is online. No in-home coverage exists in any band in the UAE, because that service is not offered here at all.

The practical consequence for an Al Manaseer family is that match time varies by subject rather than by where you live. A Maths Analysis and Approaches SL request is usually matched within a couple of days. A Higher Level Visual Arts request may take longer, and we will say so when you ask rather than after you have paid for a trial. If nothing suitable exists, the correct answer is that nothing suitable exists, and we give it. Ask which band your subject sits in when you first enquire, and you will get a realistic wait rather than an optimistic one.

sections.heading: What in-home tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that lands in a household budget. Monthly packages visible in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Convert that to the hour and the shape of the market appears. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking 200 to 500. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led tuition reaches AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure.

The gap between the online specialist band and the in-home band is the travel premium. It is not a quality premium. Nothing in a tutor's subject knowledge improves because they drove to Al Manaseer, and on this district the drive is the awkward part: evening traffic along the Corniche, visitor parking that may or may not exist, and a lift. The premium pays for the car, and the fragility it introduces is yours. One cancelled lesson because the tutor is stuck on Airport Road is a cost the rate card does not show.

These are market figures, dated October 2026 and attributed to the sources above. They are not an IB Gram price list. Our own pricing is quoted after a consultation and a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week the situation actually needs.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, measured on the things that change outcomes
paragraphs: Comparisons of this kind usually collapse into format preference. The useful version compares the variables that actually move a grade: how well the tutor knows the specification, how reliably the lesson happens, how much of the hour is teaching, and whether the student can revisit what was taught.

On specification knowledge, online wins outright in Al Manaseer, because the constraint is removed. On reliability, online wins because a video call has no traffic. On teaching minutes per paid hour, in-home loses a slice to arrival and settling even when the tutor is punctual. On revisiting, only the online format gives you a recording and a saved annotated worksheet. On the one variable where in-home has a genuine edge, which is a young child's focus in an unfamiliar format, the answer for Diploma-age students is usually moot.
The table below sets it out plainly. It compares delivery models, not named providers. Where an AED figure appears it is the market band quoted and sourced in the previous section, not our price.

Read the last column as the decision rule. If the thing you need is a Higher Level specialist for a specific syllabus, every row points the same way. If the thing you need is adult supervision in the room for a nine-year-old, tutoring of any kind is the wrong purchase and a different conversation is more useful. And if the subject is one of the thin bands above, the online route is not a preference at all; it is the only route that reaches a specialist.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a question Al Manaseer parents should ask and almost never do. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are, in u.ae's wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and figures circulating online could not be verified against an official source, so no amount is quoted here. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

There is a second rule that applies specifically in this emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document before relying on it. The practical point stands either way: hiring your child's own class teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to cause a problem for the teacher.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not operate premises in the UAE and holds no regulator permit or accreditation here, and you should treat any platform claiming regulator approval with suspicion until it shows you the permit number.
bullets: Ask any private tutor, in the UAE or elsewhere, whether they hold a current permit and under what category
The permit is free and valid for two years, so cost is not a reason for a tutor not to have one
