sections.heading: The exam calendar an Al Manaseer Diploma family should be working to
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May Diploma session. IB session and results dates are not restated here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a page is worse than no date; confirm them with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. What can be stated usefully is the shape of the year, and the shape is what families misjudge.

The written papers in May are the last thing that happens, not the main thing. Ahead of them sit the Extended Essay milestones from the autumn of DP1, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, six subject Internal Assessments with internal deadlines your school sets, and the school's own mock window. Most of the grade is decided in that sequence. A family that starts support eight weeks before the May papers has already passed the points where support was cheapest.

Households in Al Manaseer running two boards at once have a second problem. A younger sibling on the British curriculum sits Cambridge IGCSE in the June series, with November available as the resit route, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in May/June with a November series as well. That puts an older sibling's May Diploma papers and a younger sibling's June IGCSE papers in overlapping weeks on one household calendar, with one dining table and one quiet room.

One Cambridge detail is worth knowing because it has consequences. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Get the zone-correct timetable from your school's exams officer. Do not take the dates from a tutoring website, this one included.
bullets: Diploma support bought in the spring of DP2 is support bought at the least useful moment
The Extended Essay and six IAs are the part of the grade a tutor can most affect
Cambridge IGCSE in the UAE runs June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only
Always use the zone-correct Cambridge timetable supplied by your school's exams officer

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops: academic honesty on the IA, EE and TOK essay
paragraphs: This section exists because the market around these searches contains operators selling finished coursework. One competitor in the research set advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A family paying for it is buying a risk to their child's diploma.

The line is clear enough to write down. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, help the student narrow a research question until it is investigable, discuss method, ask questions about a draft the student has written, and point out where the student's own argument does not hold. A tutor may not write any part of the submission, may not edit the document, may not supply a structure to be filled in, and may not provide data the student has not generated.

In practice that shows up in how a session runs. Our tutors do not open the student's file and type. Feedback is given verbally and in session notes the student then acts on themselves. The student's supervisor at school signs off the authenticity declaration, and nothing a tutor does should make that declaration harder to sign honestly. If a tutor is willing to write the thing for you, that tells you what they would do to your child's grade when the IB asks questions.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the boards' copyright. We reference them, link the official page, and work from material the student legitimately has through their school.

sections.heading: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for families planning locally
paragraphs: Al Manaseer families whose children may apply to a UAE university ask about equivalency, usually late. It is worth knowing the shape early, because the subject count affects option choices two years before anyone applies.

For the British track, reporting of the Ministry's clarified requirements states that students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That five-subject figure is worth holding onto, because at least one page ranking for these searches publishes six, and a parent who plans around six makes different subject choices.

For the American track, English proficiency is reported as a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on moe.gov.ae, and publishing an unsourced figure would be the same error the competitor made with the subject count. Check the Ministry's own page or the emirate attestation authority.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or expedites, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. We describe it so that a Year 10 subject-choice conversation happens with the right numbers in it, and point you to the official channel for the rest.

sections.heading: How this works for a family in Al Manaseer, honestly
paragraphs: The first conversation is about diagnosis rather than booking. We want the subject, the level, the school, the most recent marked work and your own read on what is going wrong. A parent saying my son is behind in Chemistry is a starting point. A parent saying he scores well on recall questions and loses the extended response is a brief a tutor can act on in the first lesson rather than the fourth.

Then we match on subject and level, propose a slot that survives a school commute off the island, and run a free trial lesson. The trial is a real lesson on real content, not a sales call, and it is free with no card required. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again; a tutor who is excellent for one student is not automatically right for the next.

If no specialist is free for your subject, we tell you that at this stage. For the thin bands in the coverage table, that happens. The alternatives we suggest then are the honest ones: wait for a slot, widen the time window, start with a related subject, or use the school's own support, which for a Higher Level arts subject is often genuinely the better route.

After that it is weekly, in a fixed slot, with a note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. You will know who is teaching your child, by name, and it stays the same person unless you ask for a change. Lessons are online, live and one-to-one. Nobody comes to the building, and nothing about the teaching depends on anyone doing so.

process.title: Tell us the subject, level and school
process.description: Not just the subject. Analysis and Approaches HL at a school that teaches Paper 3 in DP2 is a different brief from the same subject taught front-loaded. The school's sequence changes what the first four sessions should cover, so we ask for it.

process.title: Send one marked piece of work
process.description: A marked paper, an IA draft with the teacher's comments, or a mock script. One real artefact tells a subject specialist more than a long description, and it is the difference between the first lesson diagnosing and the first lesson guessing.

process.title: Agree a slot that survives the commute
process.description: Al Manaseer students commuting to Saadiyat or Khalifa City are not home at 3.30pm. We set the slot around when your child is actually free and alert, not around when a timetable says school ends.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson on real content with the matched specialist, free and with no card required. At the end you get the tutor's read on what is wrong and what the first month should do about it.

process.title: Review after four sessions
process.description: Four sessions in, we look at whether the diagnosis held. Sometimes the problem is not the subject at all but exam technique or an unprotected coursework calendar, and the plan changes accordingly rather than continuing out of habit.

whyPoints.title: Matched on syllabus, not on distance
whyPoints.description: The constraint that makes an Al Manaseer search hard is geography. Removing it is the whole point. Your child is matched to somebody who has taught that subject at that level through full cohorts, wherever they sit.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: We do not offer home visits in the UAE, we hold no regulator accreditation here, and we will not write a word of an Internal Assessment. Each of those is in writing on this page because a platform's limits are more informative than its promises.

whyPoints.title: A named tutor who stays
whyPoints.description: You know who is teaching your child and it remains the same person. Continuity is most of what makes weekly tuition work, and rotating tutors is the most common way a platform quietly wastes a term.

faqs.question: Can I actually get an IB home tutor in Al Manaseer who visits the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We teach UAE families online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent tutors and local agencies in Abu Dhabi do advertise home visits, with market rates for in-home one-to-one quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. Our view is that the premium pays for the car rather than the teaching, and that for a Diploma subject the specialist you need is unlikely to live within driving range of Al Manaseer. The honest trade is a better-matched tutor on a screen.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor really understands the Diploma rather than just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. Which level have you taught this at, and across how many cohorts? What does the Internal Assessment criterion rubric for this subject weight most heavily? Where do students in this subject usually lose marks on the extended response? A teacher who has taught the Diploma answers all three immediately and in specifics. A general subject tutor answers the first and becomes vague on the other two. The trial lesson is the place to ask, and it is free, so the cost of checking is a card-free hour of your time.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to staff for a family living in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: Higher Level arts subjects, Group 2 languages at Higher Level, and Global Politics are the thin bands. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics and Business Management are deep. The coverage table on this page gives the bands with typical match times, and the policy is that we tell you the band before you book a trial rather than afterwards. If nothing suitable exists for your subject, we say so and suggest school-side alternatives, which for a Higher Level arts subject is often genuinely the better route anyway.

faqs.question: My child commutes from Al Manaseer to a school on Saadiyat. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. A school day that ends between 2.30pm and 3.15pm plus a bridge commute back to the island puts a student home closer to 4pm, and they need to eat before they can think. Sessions from 5pm onwards work; sessions at 4pm tend to be half wasted. Because lessons are online there is no additional tutor travel to absorb, so the slot can sit as late as 8pm if that is when your child is alert. We set the time around the student, not the timetable.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching an Al Manaseer student need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, per u.ae, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. u.ae states that anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published. Ask the tutor directly which category they hold it under; the permit costs nothing, so there is no reason not to have one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes. A tutor can teach the underlying chemistry, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help her narrow a research question until it has a genuinely controllable variable, discuss method and uncertainty, and ask hard questions about a draft she has written. A tutor cannot write it, edit it, give her a structure to fill in, or supply data she did not collect. That line is not a house style; it is what keeps her authenticity declaration honest. Any service offering to produce a finished Internal Assessment is selling her a malpractice risk.

faqs.question: What does Diploma tutoring cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Market figures for October 2026 run as follows. Budget online tuition from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors online around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tuition reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours; our own number follows a consultation and a free trial.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as effective for a Diploma student as somebody in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-age students, yes, and on several measures better. The work is problem sets, past-paper scripts and drafts, all of which live on a screen and annotate better there than on paper passed across a table. The student keeps a recording and the annotated worksheet. No lesson is lost to traffic. The one real advantage of a person in the room is holding a young child's attention, which is a primary-age consideration rather than a DP2 one. The variable that actually moves a Diploma grade is whether the tutor knows the specification.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a struggling DP1 student start with?
faqs.answer: One a week in one subject, for most families. A single weekly slot in the subject causing the most damage, running alongside the school's sequence, produces more durable change than three scattered sessions across three subjects. Two a week makes sense when a student is behind on content rather than technique and there is a fixed date to reach. Starting with four is usually a sign that the problem has not been diagnosed yet, and it is also the fastest way to exhaust a student who is already tired.

faqs.question: We are moving from the MYP into the Diploma. What gap should we expect?
faqs.answer: The commonest gap is mathematical fluency rather than understanding. MYP assessment is criterion-referenced and generous about method, so a student can be graded well while still being slow and uncertain with algebraic manipulation. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes that fluency and moves fast. The others are writing under timed conditions, which the MYP rarely demands, and command-term discipline, where a question saying evaluate expects something different from one saying describe. Six to ten weeks of targeted work before DP1 starts is usually enough.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Manaseer do the students you support attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support on this part of Abu Dhabi island attend schools including The British School Al Khubairat, Al Bateen Academy, Abu Dhabi International School, Brighton College Abu Dhabi and Repton School Abu Dhabi, and commute out to Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, Raha International School, GEMS World Academy Abu Dhabi and Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi. Those names are context for the area, not relationships. IB Gram claims no affiliation, partnership or endorsement with any school, and any platform listing schools as partners should be asked to evidence it.

faqs.question: Can one Al Manaseer tutor cover both of my children if they sit different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes for mathematics, rarely otherwise. A strong maths teacher can handle IGCSE Extended and Diploma Standard Level credibly, because the content overlaps and the skill is the same skill at different depths. Across the sciences it is less workable: Cambridge IGCSE Physics and Diploma Physics Higher Level are different specifications with different assessment logic, and a tutor who claims both equally usually knows one properly. Two specialists on two slots costs more per week and wastes less of it, which is the trade we would recommend.

faqs.question: What happens if the matched tutor is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we match again, with no reason required and nothing to justify. Fit failures are usually about pace or manner rather than competence, and they show up in the first two or three sessions. The free trial lesson exists partly to catch them before any money moves. What we will not do is keep a mismatched pairing running because changing it is administratively awkward; a term lost to a tutor your child has stopped listening to is the most expensive outcome available here.

faqs.question: Can Al Manaseer lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window shifts late, so sessions commonly move to after Iftar. Because lessons are online there is no tutor travel to arrange around it, which makes a 9pm or 10pm slot practical in a way an in-home visit at that hour would not be. We also reduce frequency in the final week of Ramadan and through Eid by default, and pick the schedule back up afterwards rather than letting a term quietly stop.

faqs.question: Does tutoring help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and nobody should tell you it does. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs on certificates a student has already earned; tutoring is not a requirement for it and we do not perform, expedite or guarantee any part of it. Where it matters is earlier. The British track is reported as requiring five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Knowing that in Year 10 changes subject choices. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae.

intro.heading: Why "is there an IB tutor near me on Al Maryah Island?" is a harder question than it looks
paragraphs: Al Maryah Island sits between the Corniche and Al Reem Island, connected by two bridges, and it was built as Abu Dhabi's central business district rather than as a family suburb. Abu Dhabi Global Market sits at one end, The Galleria in the middle, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi at the other. The residential stock is apartments in towers, and the resident population is a fraction of what a villa community like Khalifa City or Al Raha Gardens holds. None of that is a problem until you need a specific kind of teacher.

A Diploma Programme student does not need a maths tutor. They need a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL tutor who has marked that course's Paper 3, or a Chemistry HL tutor who knows which criterion on the Internal Assessment rubric is costing them two marks. Those are narrow specialisms. Abu Dhabi as a whole has a reasonable number of them. Al Maryah Island, with its handful of residential towers, statistically has almost none, and the ones who advertise locally are usually generalists who will happily take a Diploma booking and then teach around the edges of it.

That is the mismatch this page exists to name. When a parent types "IB home tutor in Al Maryah Island" into Google, what comes back is a set of agency pages that promise a tutor will arrive at the door, without ever addressing whether that tutor knows the course. The travel radius becomes the selection criterion. You end up with whoever can reach Al Maryah Island by 5pm, which is a logistics answer to an academic question.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and we say so on this page rather than burying it. For Al Maryah Island, every lesson is delivered live over video, one tutor to one student, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time. That changes what the selection criterion can be. Instead of asking who lives within a twenty-minute drive of the island, we ask who teaches Mathematics AA HL or Biology SL or Economics HL as their main subject, and match on that.

The rest of this page is the detail behind that choice. What the Abu Dhabi tutoring market actually charges, in AED, with the source for each band. What the travel premium on an in-home visit buys and what it does not. Which schools island families actually enrol in, because none of them are on the island. What happens when no specialist is free for a niche Diploma subject, and what we do instead of pretending otherwise. And what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules, which is the single most common thing parents here are quietly unsure about.

Read it in the order it is written and you will finish knowing what to ask any tutor or agency in this city, including us. That is the point. A parent who can interrogate a tutoring offer properly does not need to trust a marketing page.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maryah-isl.programmesIntro: An IB education runs from age three to eighteen across four programmes, and an Al Maryah Island family may be in any of them. What a tutor does changes completely between them, so here is what each one actually asks of a student in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, and there is no external examination. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, built around a portfolio and the Year 6 Exhibition. Support at this stage is about the mechanics underneath the inquiry: number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure, and the habit of recording evidence of thinking rather than only answers.
programmes.countryNote: PYP families on Al Maryah Island commute to schools on Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island or Al Bateen, which means a primary child is often in a car for forty minutes after a full day. Short online sessions of thirty to forty minutes work far better here than an hour, and they can run from the apartment at 5.30pm rather than requiring another journey.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, labelled A to D, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1–7 grade by school-set boundaries. There are no external papers unless the school enters students for eAssessment. The thing that catches students is criterion language: a task asking them to evaluate is marked differently from one asking them to describe, and most lost marks are command-term failures rather than knowledge gaps.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is where Al Maryah Island families most often start looking for help. MYP Year 11 maths and sciences are assessed on criteria; DP1 maths is assessed on timed papers with a formula booklet and a graphic display calculator. Families usually find that out in October of DP1, which is late. A spring bridge of six to eight online sessions handles it better.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the grade, and the externally examined papers carry the rest. Forty-two subject points plus three core points gives the maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Maryah Island Diploma students sit the May session, which is the one Abu Dhabi schools enter. Because IB exam and results dates are published by the IB itself and revised from time to time, confirm every deadline with your school's IB coordinator rather than with any tutoring site, including this one. We teach to your school's internal deadlines, which is what actually governs the IA calendar.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development component. It is a smaller UAE cohort than the Diploma but a real one, and its Diploma-course components are assessed identically to the full Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: A CP student on Al Maryah Island is usually taking two DP subjects alongside a business or applied qualification, and the tutoring need is narrow and specific: those two subjects to a defensible grade, plus structural coaching on the reflective project. Narrow needs are exactly where a national tutor pool beats a local one, because two subjects is not enough work to interest a local generalist.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maryah-isl.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Al Maryah Island families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses and the place marks are routinely dropped. Higher and Standard Level are both covered in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with HL adding a third paper of extended problem-solving. HL Paper 3 is where marks go: it is two long multi-part investigations and students who have only practised short questions run out of structure halfway through part (c).

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The graphic display calculator is central rather than incidental, and the commonest loss is method marks: a correct answer typed from the calculator with no visible model earns a fraction of the available credit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics, with HL extensions in each. Students lose marks on unit prefixes, on failing to state assumptions in extended-response questions, and on treating uncertainty propagation in the IA as an afterthought rather than a criterion.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic reaction pathways are the usual breaking point, and the IA is often weak on controlling variables — a lab that produces a clean graph still scores poorly if the method does not justify the range chosen.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the HL extensions. The paper that separates grades is the data-based one: students who can recall the content still lose marks describing a trend when the command term asked them to explain a mechanism.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and development. Diagrams carry heavy credit and must be labelled and referenced in the prose. The three commentaries that form the IA are marked on real published articles and on correct, explicit theory application, not on general commentary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. Numerical questions on ratios and investment appraisal are reliable marks that students skip. The HL research project needs a focused research question early, and a vague one is almost impossible to rescue in the final term.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, the Individual Oral, the HL Essay and Paper 1 guided analysis. Paper 1 marks are lost on description of content rather than analysis of technique, and the Individual Oral fails when the global issue is chosen late and does not genuinely link both texts.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, abstract data structures at HL, and the solution-development IA. The IA scores on documented design and testing, not on how impressive the program is, and students consistently under-evidence their development stages.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and the IA suite
subjects.description: TOK is an exhibition plus a prescribed-title essay; the EE is a 4,000-word independent piece; every subject carries its own IA. Our role on all three is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. We do not write, complete or edit to completion any assessed work.

schoolClusters.note: The closest school belt to Al Maryah Island and the one most island families use. These schools run British and IB pathways and sit a single bridge crossing away, which is why a Maryah student's school day typically ends between 3pm and 3.30pm with a short commute home.

sections.heading: What a parent on Al Maryah Island is actually asking
paragraphs: The literal answer: there is no meaningful resident pool of IB Diploma subject specialists on Al Maryah Island, because the island is a business district of roughly half a square kilometre with a small residential population. A family searching for an IB home tutor in Al Maryah Island will find agencies willing to send someone, drawn from Khalifa City, Al Reef or Mohammed Bin Zayed City, with the travel built into the rate. Whether that person teaches your child's specific course at the right level is a separate question that the search result does not answer.

This matters because the Diploma is not one subject. A student taking Mathematics AA HL, Physics HL, Economics HL, English A SL, Spanish B SL and Biology SL has six different specialisms in play, each with its own Internal Assessment and its own paper structure. The probability that one tutor living within twenty minutes of Al Maryah Island covers the two or three your child is weakest in, at the right level, is low. Parents discover this four sessions in, when the tutor starts avoiding the HL Paper 3 questions.

So the honest framing is a trade. You can optimise for proximity and accept a generalist, or you can drop the proximity requirement and select on subject expertise. Online delivery is what makes the second option available, and it is the only option IB Gram offers in the UAE. We do not send a tutor to an Al Maryah Island address. The lesson happens on live video, one student to one tutor, and the tutor is chosen because they teach that course, not because they can reach the Galleria by 5pm.

sections.heading: Al Maryah Island has no school on it, and that shapes everything
paragraphs: Every school-age child living on Al Maryah Island leaves the island each morning. There is no private school within its boundary. The nearest cluster is on Al Reem Island, one bridge away; after that, the Al Bateen and Corniche schools on the mainland, then Saadiyat, then the Khalifa City belt. This single fact determines the realistic shape of a tutoring week far more than any marketing copy about convenience.

The commute is what compresses the available window. A Reem Island school finishing at 3.15pm puts a student back in a Maryah tower by about 3.45pm on a normal day. A Saadiyat or Yas school finishing at the same time, with pickup queues and a bridge, can mean 4.30pm or later. Add an after-school activity on two days and the usable slots for a sixty-minute session that does not run past 8pm are narrower than parents expect when they start looking.

An in-home tutor has to land inside that window too, having travelled from wherever they live, usually the mainland. If they are coming from Khalifa City to Al Maryah Island at 4.30pm, the arrival time is a guess. A missed or shortened session still costs the hour. Online removes that variable entirely: the tutor is present at the time agreed, the student walks from the kitchen table to the desk, and a 7pm start is as viable as a 4pm one because nobody is driving.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a local tutor pool
paragraphs: It is worth doing this calculation openly, because it is the thing no tutoring page shows you. Start with the population of a small island of residential towers. Take the fraction who teach for a living. Take the fraction of those who teach the IB Diploma rather than a national curriculum or primary years. Then take the fraction who teach your child's specific subject at the specific level, and who have a free slot inside the window your commute allows. Each step divides the number.

By the last step, a request for a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL tutor with Thursday availability on Al Maryah Island is a request for a person who may not exist on the island at all. That is not a failure of the island. It is what happens when you apply four filters to a small population. The same arithmetic, applied to the whole of Abu Dhabi, returns a workable number. Applied across every city we recruit in, it returns a comfortable one.

The practical consequence is that an agency promising a local in-home IB tutor on Al Maryah Island is either drawing its people from the mainland and charging you for the drive, or quietly relaxing the subject filter and sending a capable generalist instead. Both are legitimate businesses and both have their place. Neither is what a Diploma student with a specific Higher Level problem in front of them needs. sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: Begin with what you are paying for rather than with the headline number. When an in-home rate in Abu Dhabi sits above an online rate for the same tutor and the same hour of teaching, the difference is the journey. It buys physical presence in the room, a tutor who can see a worked page over a student's shoulder without a document camera, and for some younger children a seriousness that a screen does not carry. Those are real things.

What it does not buy is subject depth. The premium is paid to a driver, not to an examiner. It also does not buy reliability on Al Maryah Island specifically, because the journey the premium pays for is the journey most likely to be disrupted at the hour a session needs to start. And it does not buy flexibility: a tutor who has driven forty minutes will not move your Tuesday slot to Thursday on request, because their week is built around a route.

sections.heading: Online delivery into a Maryah tower, in practice
paragraphs: The question behind the question is usually whether a screen works as well as a person in the room. For a Diploma student it generally works better, for reasons specific to the subject matter. IB work is written: a derivation, a labelled diagram, an annotated extract, a marked-up draft. A shared digital whiteboard keeps every line of that session, which a paper notebook on a dining table does not. The student can reopen Tuesday's derivation on Saturday.

The tower itself helps rather than hinders. An apartment on Al Maryah Island has fibre connectivity as standard, a desk or a kitchen table that is quiet once the island's working day ends, and no requirement to make a room presentable for a visitor. Parents frequently mention that last one. There is also no building-access problem, no visitor parking at The Galleria, and no lift wait at 5pm.

What online genuinely requires is set-up discipline. The student needs a camera the tutor can point at paper when working by hand, a stable chair at a table rather than a bed, and headphones. We ask for those in the first session and say why. Where a subject involves practical work, as the sciences do, the tutor works on the write-up, the uncertainty analysis and the evaluation rather than pretending to replicate a school laboratory. The school runs the practical; we teach what the criteria reward in the report.

To be explicit, since this page targets a home-tutor search: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. No tutor will come to an Al Maryah Island address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The comparison below is how the two formats differ for a family on this island.

sections.heading: Tutor coverage and the honest fallback
paragraphs: No tutoring service covers every Diploma subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that claim to are the ones to be careful with. Common courses are well covered and a match is usually quick. Narrow HL subjects and less-taught languages are thinner, and in those cases a family deserves to be told that rather than handed a near-miss tutor and left to discover the gap.

Our rule is that we say what coverage looks like before you commit, and if the right specialist is not free we say so and offer the alternatives explicitly: wait for a slot, start with a related subject, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. The third option is how most genuinely narrow requests get met, and it is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-sounding phone number.

That disclosure is deliberate. Several providers in this market route UAE parents to contact numbers outside the country without ever stating where the teaching actually comes from, which a parent only discovers once the first lesson starts at an awkward hour. If a tutor for your child's subject is not UAE-based, you will be told before the trial lesson, the reason will be named, and the lesson time will still be set in your evening rather than theirs.

Coverage also moves through the year. Higher Level slots tighten in the second term as Diploma families across the Gulf reach the same point in the calendar, and the quickest route to a good tutor in February is to have asked in October. If you are reading this in the autumn term and the subject is a known weakness, that timing is the single most useful thing on this page.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a fair question and almost nobody in this market answers it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Who may hold one is broader than parents assume. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The flip side is also clear: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The authorities have not published a fine schedule, so no figure should be quoted to you, and this page quotes none.

There is a separate restriction worth knowing in Abu Dhabi specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct is reported to bar the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document if it bears on your situation. What it means practically is that hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is not the shortcut it looks like.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership of any kind, in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else, and does not operate a UAE office or centre. We name the regulators because parents should know who they are, not to imply any of them endorses us.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment, and together with the Extended Essay and the TOK essay these are the pieces of work where tutoring most often goes wrong. The boundary is set by IB academic-honesty rules, and crossing it is an expulsion-level risk for the student, not a slap on the wrist. So it is worth stating exactly what help looks like.

A tutor may teach the subject content the task sits on. They may explain what each assessment criterion rewards and in what proportion. They may ask questions that make a student notice a flaw in their own method. They may read a draft the student wrote and say which criterion it is underselling and why. They may teach referencing, citation and how to describe a method so another person could repeat it. They may run a timed practice task on a different topic entirely.

A tutor may not write any part of the work. May not draft a paragraph for the student to adapt. May not edit a draft to completion or rewrite sentences so that the final text is partly theirs. May not generate a research question and hand it over. May not supply data the student did not gather. May not provide a worked model of the actual task that can be adapted. An agency in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger, and it is not a service we offer at any price.

We explain this to the student in the first core session, because the student is the one who signs the authenticity declaration. Clear boundaries also make the work better: a student who has been questioned hard about their own method writes a stronger evaluation than one handed a polished paragraph they do not understand.

Allowed: timed practice on a different topic, feedback on the student's own writing

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection ratings and what a school report actually tells you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is ADEK, and it is the body that inspects and rates the schools Al Maryah Island children attend. It is also, oddly, named by none of the competitor pages researched for this market, which tells you how little localisation the ranking pages carry.

The regulator map across the country is worth knowing if your family moves between emirates, because it changes. Dubai sits with KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's remit there extends well beyond inspection.

What an inspection rating does and does not tell you about tutoring need is the useful part. A strong overall rating is a judgement about the school as an institution: leadership, provision, outcomes across the whole cohort. It says nothing about whether your child's Chemistry HL set has a settled teacher this year, or whether the maths department is stretched across AA and AI with one specialist. Those are the conditions that actually create a tutoring need, and you find them out at a parents' evening, not in a published band.

Read a report for pattern rather than headline. If attainment in a subject group is flagged as weaker than progress, the cohort is being taught well from a low base and content gaps are the issue. If progress is the weaker measure, the teaching is where to look. Either way the inspection tells you where to ask questions, and the answers shape which subject is worth paying for.

sections.heading: Starting, in the order it actually happens
paragraphs: The first step is not booking a tutor. It is deciding which subject is the real problem, because families frequently arrive certain it is maths when the pattern of lost marks says it is written explanation across three subjects. The quickest way to find out is to put the last two marked assessments side by side and read the examiner comments rather than the grades. If the comments repeat across subjects, the problem is technique, and technique is cheaper to fix.

Then the trial lesson. It is free, it is a real lesson rather than a sales call, and the useful thing to do is send the tutor a piece of the student's recent work beforehand so the hour starts on evidence. At the end, ask the student one question: did that person know the course better than you do? A Diploma student can answer that accurately, and their answer is the one that matters.

After that the decision is frequency and duration, not whether to continue. One session a week changes a grade over a term. Two sessions a week is for a specific window: a mock, an IA deadline, the final run-in. An exam-window intensive is for the last few weeks and should end when the paper does. Anyone selling you a rolling annual commitment in week one is selling a contract, not teaching. And if we cannot staff your subject properly, we will tell you that instead of taking the booking.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send anyone to an apartment on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, including Al Maryah Island. In-home visits are a service we run in India only. Every UAE lesson is live one-to-one video with a subject specialist, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state it this directly because the search term is "home tutor" and a family deserves the answer before they enquire rather than after. What you get instead is selection on subject and level rather than on driving distance, which on a half-square-kilometre business district with few resident Diploma specialists is the more useful trade.

faqs.question: How many IB Diploma subject specialists actually live on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: We cannot give you a number, and anybody who does is guessing. What we can say is the arithmetic: the island is roughly half a square kilometre of towers and offices with a small residential population, and finding a tutor there means filtering that population for people who teach, then for people who teach the Diploma, then for your child's subject at the right level, then for availability in your window. Four filters on a small base returns close to nothing for a named Higher Level course. Widening the search to all of Abu Dhabi, or online, returns a workable pool.

faqs.question: Why is there no private school on Al Maryah Island itself?
faqs.answer: The island was developed as Abu Dhabi's central business district: Abu Dhabi Global Market, The Galleria, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and residential towers. School provision sits on the surrounding islands and the mainland instead. Practically, that means every school-age child on Al Maryah Island crosses a bridge each morning, most commonly to Al Reem Island, or further to Al Bateen, Saadiyat or the Khalifa City belt. The relevance to tutoring is timing: the commute home determines how early a session can realistically start, and that is the first thing we ask about.

faqs.question: What does the market charge for an IB tutor in Abu Dhabi, in AED?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, read in October 2026, run roughly like this. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB by Unitors. An in-home visit is quoted at AED 180–350 by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is included. A named IB or A-Level specialist runs AED 200–450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. These are the market, not IB Gram's prices; ours follow a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is a Maryah tower apartment a workable place for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and often better than the alternative. Fibre connectivity is standard in the island's residential towers, and once the business district's working day ends the apartments are quiet. There is no visitor parking to arrange at The Galleria, no building access to clear and no room to tidy for a guest. What the student does need is a desk or table rather than a bed, headphones, and a way to show handwritten working to the camera. We ask for that set-up in the first session and explain why each part of it matters.

faqs.question: How do you choose which tutor to propose for a Diploma student here?
faqs.answer: Subject and level first. If the request is Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, we look for tutors whose main teaching is that course, not maths generally, and who have worked on Paper 3 specifically. Then the assessment component that is actually failing: a student losing marks on an Internal Assessment needs someone fluent in that subject's criteria, which is a different strength from paper technique. Then your time window. Geography enters only when you want a UAE-based tutor for a particular reason, and we will tell you whether that narrows the pool for your subject.

faqs.question: My child is at a school on Al Reem Island. When can a session start?
faqs.answer: Al Reem is the shortest commute from Al Maryah Island, usually ten to twenty minutes over the bridge, so a school day ending around 3.15pm puts a student home by roughly 3.45pm. That makes a 4.30pm or 5pm start genuinely workable, which is unusual among the clusters island families use. Saadiyat or Yas enrolment pushes the realistic start to 5.30pm or 6pm because of pickup queues and cross-city distance. We plan the slot around the actual arrival time rather than the school's finish time, because the gap between them is where sessions get lost.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with an IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters more than it sounds. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, question the method until the student notices its weaknesses, read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion it is underselling, and teach referencing and citation properly. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of the work to completion, supply a research question, provide data the student did not gather, or hand over an adaptable model of the task. The student signs an authenticity declaration, and under IB rules a breach is an expulsion-level risk for them.

faqs.question: Does ADEK or any regulator approve IB Gram as a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. We name ADEK on this page because it is the body that licenses and inspects the private schools Al Maryah Island children attend, and parents should know who that is. Any provider describing its tutors as licensed by KHDA or accredited by ADEK is making a claim about a specific permit issued to institutions holding premises, and you should ask to see the permit number and check it with the regulator.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. Ask a prospective tutor to show you their permit, and apply or verify through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own subject teacher privately instead?
faqs.answer: It is not the shortcut it appears to be. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat both as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document if it affects you directly. We will not arrange or facilitate that arrangement. A specialist in the same course from outside the school carries none of the conflict and is usually more candid about the gaps.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody covers my child's Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, before you pay for anything. Common courses — the maths routes, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management, English A — are well covered and a trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days to a week. Less-taught Group 2 languages and some narrow Higher Level combinations are genuinely thinner. In that case we set out the options plainly: wait for a slot to open, start on a related component such as the Internal Assessment with a specialist in that part, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Abu Dhabi schools enter, and when should we start?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session, and a November resit route exists for individual cases. We will not publish specific IB exam or results dates here, because the IB sets and occasionally revises them and our source could not be verified directly; confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator. What governs your term is the school's internal deadline calendar for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which usually bites well before anything external. Work backwards from those internal dates and you will be early rather than late.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough, or should we book two?
faqs.answer: One session a week with the same tutor is what moves a grade across a term, because the gain comes from consistent correction rather than volume. Two a week is worth it for a defined window: the weeks before a mock, an Internal Assessment deadline, or the final run-in. Booking two indefinitely from the start tends to produce fatigue rather than marks. Start at one, choose the subject deliberately rather than funding three at once, and review against the next marked assessment. If the lost-mark pattern has not changed after a term, the fix is a different approach, not more hours.

faqs.question: Will our Al Maryah Island slot survive Ramadan and a family trip abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and this is where online delivery is simply more flexible than a driving route. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar timing, and the slot is held rather than reassigned. Families who travel between Abu Dhabi and elsewhere keep the same tutor and shift the clock, which matters in a Diploma year when a three-week absence otherwise costs a unit. Sessions can also pause across school examination weeks and resume afterwards. An in-home tutor built into a route across the island's bridges cannot usually offer any of that.

faqs.question: What should I send you before the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The most recent two marked pieces of work in the subject, including the examiner or teacher comments, and a draft if an Internal Assessment is in progress. Also the school name and the time your child actually gets home, because the commute from Al Reem, Saadiyat or the mainland determines which slots are real. With that in hand the trial hour starts on evidence instead of introductions, and the tutor can tell you at the end which specific thing is costing marks. If they cannot, that is useful information about the tutor.

intro.heading: The evening is the constraint, not the tutor
paragraphs: Tuition arrangements rarely fail because the tutor was wrong. They fail because the session was placed at a time the household could not sustain, and the failure is slow and deniable: one reschedule in week two, another in week four, a gap over a long weekend, and by week eight it has stopped without anybody deciding to stop it. The money has bought three lessons and a family conclusion that tutoring does not work.

Al Muroor is a residential district on Abu Dhabi island, strung along Muroor Road between the Airport Road corridor and the central districts, mid-rise apartment living with schools in several directions rather than one. Children from here travel in all of them — out to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, across to Al Mushrif and Al Bateen, up to the islands — which means a single building contains households whose evenings begin at ten past three and households whose child walks in at twenty-five past four.

So the useful first exercise is not choosing a tutor. It is identifying what binds your particular evening. In most Al Muroor households it is one of four things: the latest arrival time, a younger sibling's collection, a co-curricular commitment on fixed days, or a parent's own working hours. Whichever it is, the session has to be placed on the far side of it, and a session placed on the near side will be rescheduled until it dies.

The second thing worth understanding before buying anything is what the Diploma week actually contains, because parents consistently underestimate it. Six subjects set work. Three at Higher Level set more. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay have their own milestones. The mandatory UAE subjects — Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which private schools in the Emirates must teach alongside their licensed curriculum — occupy timetable space and set homework too. A student carrying all of that has less headroom than a count of their examined subjects implies.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a scheduling problem that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: a video session can start eleven minutes after a student walks in, move to a different evening in the week of a mock, run post-Iftar during Ramadan, and does not fail because a tutor is stuck on the Airport Road.

What follows is the practical material. The household patterns and what each one makes workable. The Diploma week component by component. Bus routes and the half hour nobody counts. The two-child evening. Co-curriculars and the fixed-day problem. What a session should look like when a student arrives tired. The home-visit question answered in travel-time terms with published rates. And the limits we work inside.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.programmesIntro: The programme a student is in determines the shape of the week, and therefore what kind of session placement works. These are the three an Al Muroor household is most likely managing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, graded one to seven per subject against a forty-five point total. Internally assessed work in every subject, with published criteria and word limits, running continuously alongside the taught courses.
programmes.countryNote: The practical effect on an Al Muroor evening is that the Diploma week is lumpy rather than even. Deadline weeks consume whole weekends, and a tuition arrangement that ignores the school's published internal deadline calendar collides with it two or three times a year.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, graded one to eight against four criteria per subject. The weekly load is lighter than the Diploma's and more project-shaped, which means it arrives in bursts rather than nightly.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Muroor household has an MYP student and a Diploma student, the two have genuinely different weekly rhythms, and the younger child's collection time is frequently the thing that binds the older child's tuition slot. programmes.name: Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with minimal coursework, across eight or nine subjects. The nightly load is steady and the pressure is concentrated at the end of two years, which suits a fixed weekly tuition slot better than the Diploma's deadline chain does.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma components that generate weekly work, with when each typically lands. Reading them as a week rather than as a subject list is what reveals where a session can fit.

subjects.name: Higher Level sciences
subjects.description: The heaviest nightly load of any group, with long written answers and practical write-ups. Work tends to arrive the day it is set and be due within two or three days, which makes a mid-week session the most useful placement.

subjects.name: Higher Level mathematics
subjects.description: Steady nightly demand plus periodic long problem sets. Benefits more than any other subject from short daily practice rather than a weekly block, which means a session's main output should be work for the week rather than teaching in the hour.

subjects.name: Standard Level sciences
subjects.description: Lighter than Higher Level and still regular. The internal investigation dominates particular weeks, with a three thousand word limit and marks awarded on the design of the investigation rather than on how tidy the results are.

subjects.name: Language A, Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading that must happen in advance, which students defer, plus the Individual Oral and at Higher Level an essay. The reading is the part that collides with a busy evening, because it cannot be compressed into the night before.

subjects.name: Language B and ab initio courses
subjects.description: Frequent short tasks and oral preparation rather than long assignments. Fits well around a tight evening, and suffers quietly when a week is lost because the vocabulary work is cumulative.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Essay-shaped work with longer deadlines, which makes it the subject most likely to be postponed into a deadline week. History and Economics internal assessments both carry their own criteria and limits.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Light most weeks and heavy at two points: the exhibition and the essay, each worth ten marks, with word limits of nine hundred and fifty and sixteen hundred respectively. The weeks it lands are the weeks a tuition slot needs to move.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Thirty-four marks with critical thinking alone worth twelve, and a four thousand word ceiling beyond which nothing is marked. Its milestones span a year and each one consumes a weekend, which is the clearest argument for reading the school's calendar early.

subjects.name: CAS
subjects.description: Not graded but required, and it occupies fixed afternoons and weekends in most schools. CAS commitments are a common and overlooked reason a particular weekday is unavailable for tuition all year.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, with their own lesson time and homework. They are the main reason a Diploma student's real load exceeds a count of their examined subjects.

sections.heading: What binds your evening, and what each pattern makes possible
paragraphs: Published school finish times are the least useful number in this calculation. What matters is the first moment a student could realistically sit down with a pen, and that is set by whichever constraint in a household bites latest. Identifying it takes a week of observation and saves a term of rescheduling.

In Al Muroor households it is almost always one of four things. The student's own arrival time, which for a mainland school with a bus route can be well after four. A younger sibling's collection, which binds the parent rather than the student and often sits in the middle of the useful window. A fixed co-curricular or CAS commitment on particular weekdays, which removes those days entirely rather than delaying them. Or a parent's own working hours, where the household needs an adult present for a lesson to happen at all.

The table gives the common patterns with what each makes workable. The important column is the last one, because the honest answer in two of the rows is that a weekday session is not the right purchase and a weekend one is. Families resist that, and a reliable weekend session beats a weekday slot that survives on alternate weeks by a wide margin.

Two further notes that apply across patterns. Prayer times shape some households' evenings and should be stated when a schedule is agreed rather than worked around afterwards. And during Ramadan the useful study window moves: a post-Iftar session is often the best study hour of the year, and the arrangement that fails is the one that leaves an existing four o'clock slot in place and watches the cancellations accumulate.

sections.heading: What a Diploma week actually contains
paragraphs: Parents routinely underestimate the Diploma week, and the underestimate is structural rather than careless. A count of examined subjects understates the load, because the core components and the mandatory UAE subjects both set work and neither appears in that count.

The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly. Six subjects, three of them at Higher Level with correspondingly more demand. Theory of Knowledge, light most weeks and heavy at two points in the programme. The Extended Essay, whose milestones each consume a weekend. CAS, which occupies fixed afternoons and weekends in most schools and is required even though it is not graded. And Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which private schools in the Emirates must teach alongside their licensed international curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations.

The pattern that follows is lumpy rather than even. Some weeks are ordinary and some are consumed entirely by one internal assessment deadline. A tuition arrangement built as a fixed weekly commitment with no provision for those weeks will collide with them two or three times a year, and each collision costs a session plus the momentum around it. The remedy is simply to collect the school's published internal deadline calendar in the first week of the year and mark the known heavy weeks before anything is booked.

The table sets out the components with when each lands. The most useful thing a parent can take from it is which weeks to protect and which to concede: a deadline week is not a good week to add a tuition session, and the week after a mock is the most valuable one in the term because the scripts are the freshest diagnostic evidence available all year.

sections.heading: Bus or car: the half hour nobody counts
paragraphs: The school bus is the most consistently overlooked variable in scheduling, and it is also the largest. A bus serving several districts collects and drops in sequence, and a child near the end of a route can reach home thirty to fifty minutes after the published finish time. That is not an estimate a parent should accept from a page; it is something to measure, because routes differ and position on a route matters more than distance does.

The practical consequence is blunt. A household that books a four o'clock session for a child on a mainland bus route has booked something that was never possible, and the three cancellations that follow are arithmetic rather than commitment. The same household booking five o'clock has a session that survives an ordinary bad day, and ordinary bad days are most of them during the Abu Dhabi afternoon.

Car journeys are shorter and less predictable, which creates a different problem. A parent driving from Al Muroor to a mainland school and back is subject to afternoon traffic on the Airport Road corridor and the bridges, and the variance between a good day and a bad one can be twenty-five minutes. A session booked against the good-day time will be late one week in three, and a tutor who is kept waiting twice loses the slot.

The measurement method takes a week and no effort. Write down the actual arrival time every day for five consecutive days. Take the latest of the five, not the average. Add fifteen minutes for changing, eating and a glass of water. That is the slot, and booking it is the single highest-return scheduling decision available to an Al Muroor household. Everything else on this page is downstream of it.

sections.heading: Two children, one adult, one evening
paragraphs: A large share of Al Muroor households are running more than one child, and the sibling problem is the most common reason a sound tuition plan collapses. It is also the easiest to solve once it is stated, because the solutions are mundane and nobody offers them unprompted.

The core difficulty is that a younger child's collection binds the parent in the middle of the useful window, and that a parent who is driving cannot simultaneously be present for a lesson at home. Where a household needs an adult in the building for a session to happen, the session has to sit after the last collection of the day, which in practice means later than families want.

The arrangement that works best for a two-child household is consecutive slots on the same evening with a different specialist for each child. It concentrates the disruption into one evening instead of two, keeps each match specific, and puts both children's written work on the same weekly rhythm so that a parent is checking one thing rather than two. In a community with limited local provision that is only possible over video, which is one of the practical arguments for the format rather than an abstract one.

The second thing worth saying is harder. Two children in one household with a long commute have a limited combined supply of usable evenings, and funding both thinly in the same term usually produces less than funding one properly. Tuition works through the marked written practice between lessons, and splitting a budget tends to split the practice until neither child is doing enough of it. Funding the child in an examination year at specialist level, and leaving the other to the school and their own retrieval practice for a term, is unwelcome advice and is what the pattern in this market supports.

sections.heading: CAS, co-curriculars and the fixed-day problem
paragraphs: Co-curricular commitments are different in kind from traffic, because they do not delay an evening — they remove a weekday entirely, for the whole year. A student with a Tuesday and Thursday commitment has three usable weekdays, and booking a tuition session on one of the other two is the whole of the scheduling problem solved. Booking on a Tuesday and then rescheduling it weekly is a failure that was visible in advance.

CAS in particular catches families out because it is required rather than optional and because its shape varies between schools. Some run it in fixed afternoon blocks, some in weekend activity, some as a mix with external commitments that the school does not control. The question to ask the school at the start of DP1 is simply which days CAS occupies and whether that is fixed for the year, and the answer should be written on the household calendar before a tuition slot is chosen.

Sports and music commitments behave similarly and are frequently more rigid, because a squad training session or an ensemble rehearsal cannot be moved for one student. Families sometimes approach these as negotiable in the run-up to examinations, and occasionally they are, but the better plan is to build around them from the start. A student who gives up a sport in the final term rarely recovers the time as study; more often it becomes anxiety with nothing structural to hold it.

The practical sequence is therefore: establish the fixed-day map first, then the latest arrival time on the remaining days, then choose the session. Most households do this in the opposite order, selecting a time that sounds convenient and then discovering the collisions one at a time. The map takes ten minutes to draw and it is the difference between an arrangement that runs for a year and one that runs for six weeks.

sections.heading: A session when the student arrives tired
paragraphs: Even a well-placed session often starts with a student who has been at school for seven hours and in a vehicle for forty minutes. That is the normal condition rather than an exception, and a session designed for a fresh student will underperform in it. The design matters as much as the timing.

What works is structure and a short runway. The first ten minutes should be review of last week's marked work, which is low-demand and gets the student thinking without requiring new effort. The middle block, twenty-five minutes or so, carries the teaching or repair, with the student writing rather than watching, because a tired student watching a tutor solve a problem retains almost nothing. The next block is practice under light time pressure. The last ten minutes set the week's written work with an explicit instruction about what to show.

What does not work is a long explanatory stretch at the start. A tutor who talks for twenty minutes to a student who arrived at half past four has lost them by minute six, and the student will nonetheless report that the lesson was helpful, because it felt like being taught. The signal a parent can check is whether the student can say what the session was about an hour afterwards, and whether written work exists.

Length is worth considering honestly too. Ninety minutes suits a Higher Level subject and an alert student. For a tired student late in the day, two sixty-minute sessions on different evenings consolidate better than one ninety-minute session, if the household can hold two slots. Where it cannot, sixty focused minutes with real written output beats ninety minutes of diminishing attention, and we would rather recommend the shorter session than bill for the longer one.

sections.heading: The home-visit question, answered in travel time
paragraphs: Families searching for a home tutor are asking a reasonable question and deserve a straight answer rather than a deflection. Here it is in the terms that matter for an Al Muroor household: what the visit costs, what the journey does to the hour, and what you give up by requiring it.

Published in-home visiting rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor sit at roughly AED 150 to 300. The difference is not teaching quality; it is a journey, plus the risk that the journey goes badly. In a central island district the journey is shorter than from the mainland, so the loading is smaller here than in the outer communities, and it is still a loading.

What the visit buys is physical presence, which genuinely helps some students: younger ones, those who need supervision rather than teaching, and those for whom a screen is itself an obstacle. We say that plainly because it is true and because a page that pretends one format suits every child is not useful. What you give up is choice. Requiring a Diploma specialist in a particular subject at Higher Level to also be willing to drive to Al Muroor at five in the afternoon reduces an already small set, and families faced with an empty set substitute a generalist who is available.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the table sets out the comparison that led us there. The scheduling argument matters as much as the cost one: a video session can move to a different evening in a deadline week, run post-Iftar during Ramadan, and continue while a family is travelling. None of that is possible with a tutor who has to arrive at a building.
