sections.heading: The permit, our status and what we decline
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's own service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published — press reporting states the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties — so a figure quoted as the penalty is invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current ADEK document before relying on the wording.

On assessed work, the boundary is firm and we state it to students at the first session. A tutor teaches, explains what each criterion rewards, reads a student's own draft, questions it, names the criterion a section is failing, and marks practice work against the published scheme. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions for live assessed work or sit beside a student during an assessment. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; we decline to produce assessed work at any price.

On status: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it is not a registered examination centre. No Diploma examination or results date appears on this page, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one. We publish no star rating or satisfaction statistic, no tutor can promise a grade, and board material is referenced rather than reproduced.

process.title: Draw the fixed-day map
process.description: Which weekdays are removed by CAS, sport, music or other commitments for the whole year. Those days are not available, and a session booked on one of them is a weekly reschedule waiting to happen. Ten minutes, and it narrows the choice usefully.

process.title: Measure the arrival time for five days
process.description: Write down when your child actually walks in, take the latest of the five rather than the average, and add fifteen minutes. That is the slot. From a mainland school with a bus route it will be later than you expect, and later is correct.

process.title: Collect the school's deadline calendar
process.description: Internal assessment dates, exploration and Extended Essay milestones and the mock window. Mark the heavy weeks before booking anything, so sessions are moved out of them in advance rather than cancelled during them.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: One live video lesson at the time you have established, not at a convenient-sounding one, with a specialist who has read the marked evidence. You decide afterwards, no card is required, and nothing starts automatically.

whyPoints.title: The slot is derived before the tutor is matched
whyPoints.description: Fixed-day map first, then the latest real arrival time, then the session. Most households do this in reverse and discover the collisions one at a time, which is the most common way a sound arrangement quietly ends.

whyPoints.title: The bus route is counted
whyPoints.description: A school bus typically adds thirty to fifty minutes to a published finish, and position on a route matters more than distance. A four o'clock session for a child on a mainland route was never possible, and the cancellations that follow are arithmetic.

whyPoints.title: The real Diploma load is acknowledged
whyPoints.description: Six subjects, three core components and the mandatory UAE subjects, which private schools must teach alongside their licensed curriculum. A student's load exceeds a count of their examined subjects, and we plan around that.

whyPoints.title: Interruptions planned, not discovered
whyPoints.description: Deadline weeks, mock fortnights and Ramadan timing written into the plan from the start, with sessions moved rather than cancelled. Arrangements that plan their interruptions survive them.

whyPoints.title: Sessions designed for a tired student
whyPoints.description: A short low-demand runway, a writing-heavy middle, practice under light time pressure, and work set with an instruction about what to show. A long explanation to a student who arrived at half past four is lost by minute six.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer on home visits
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run from AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online, and part of the difference is a journey. We do not offer home visits in the UAE because that service runs only in India, and we explain rather than deflect.

faqs.question: What time can an IB lesson realistically start in Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: It depends on which constraint binds your evening. A child at a nearby island school who travels by car can usually manage four o'clock. A mainland school by car pushes it to half past four, and any school by bus to five, because a bus serving several districts typically adds thirty to fifty minutes to the published finish. If a younger sibling's collection sits in the middle of that window, the honest answer is later still or a weekend session.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: No. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and do not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor, and part of that difference is the journey rather than the teaching.

faqs.question: How much does a school bus actually add to the finish time?
faqs.answer: Typically thirty to fifty minutes, and sometimes more, because a bus serving several districts collects and drops in sequence and your child's position on the route matters more than the distance does. This is the single most overlooked variable in scheduling. Do not accept an estimate from any page, including this one: write down the actual arrival time for five consecutive days and take the latest of the five.

faqs.question: Why do our tuition sessions keep getting rescheduled?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the slot was placed before the household's binding constraint rather than after it. If a session sits in front of the latest arrival time, a sibling collection or a fixed co-curricular day, it will be moved repeatedly and will stop by around week eight without anybody deciding to stop it. The fix is to map the fixed days first, measure the latest arrival, and place the session on the far side of both.

faqs.question: How heavy is a Diploma week really?
faqs.answer: Heavier than a count of six subjects suggests. Three of those are at Higher Level with correspondingly more demand. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay have their own milestones, each consuming a weekend. CAS occupies fixed afternoons and weekends in most schools and is required even though it is not graded. And Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies are taught alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with their own lesson time and homework.

faqs.question: Should we book a weekday or a weekend session?
faqs.answer: Whichever is reliable. A weekend session is often the honest answer for a household with a mainland school, two collections and a working parent, and a reliable weekend session beats a weekday slot that survives on alternate weeks by a wide margin. Retention is slightly better with two contacts a week, so where a weekend pattern is chosen we set short written work across the week and review after a month to confirm it is holding.

faqs.question: How do CAS and sports commitments affect tuition scheduling?
faqs.answer: They remove weekdays entirely for the whole year rather than delaying an evening, which makes them the first thing to map. A student with Tuesday and Thursday commitments has three usable weekdays, and choosing one of those three solves most of the scheduling problem. Ask the school at the start of DP1 which days CAS occupies and whether it is fixed, and write it on the household calendar before choosing a session time.

faqs.question: What should a session look like if my child arrives exhausted?
faqs.answer: Structured, with a short runway. Ten minutes reviewing last week's marked work, which is low-demand and gets them thinking. Twenty-five minutes of teaching or repair with the student writing rather than watching, because a tired student watching a tutor solve a problem retains very little. Then practice under light time pressure, and ten minutes setting the week's written work. A long explanation at the start is lost by about minute six.

faqs.question: Is ninety minutes better than sixty for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For an alert student, yes. For a tired student late in the day, two sixty-minute sessions on different evenings consolidate better than one ninety-minute session, if the household can hold two slots. Where it cannot, sixty focused minutes with real written output beats ninety minutes of declining attention. We would rather recommend the shorter session than bill for the longer one, and the check is whether written work actually exists afterwards.

faqs.question: How should tuition be handled during Ramadan in Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: Agree the change before the month rather than during it. School days shorten and late-afternoon energy drops, so the two workable patterns are a post-Iftar evening session — often the best study hour of the year — or a reduced cadence with short written work maintaining contact. What fails is leaving an existing four o'clock slot in place and watching the cancellations accumulate. Prayer times should also be stated when a schedule is agreed rather than worked around later.

faqs.question: Can two children share one tutor to save an evening?
faqs.answer: It saves an evening and costs one child the match. The two systems have different command vocabulary, different internal assessment rules and different calendars, and a tutor stretched across both leaves somebody underserved, usually the Diploma student whose needs are less visible week to week. What works instead is consecutive slots with a different specialist for each child, which concentrates the disruption into one evening without compromising either match.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the term should we protect for tuition?
faqs.answer: Avoid the internal deadline weeks and the mock fortnight, and protect the week immediately after a mock, which is the most valuable in the term because the scripts are the freshest diagnostic evidence available all year. Collect the school's published internal deadline calendar in the first week of the year and mark the heavy weeks before anything is booked, so sessions are moved out of them in advance rather than cancelled during them.

faqs.question: Does online tuition suit a student who needs supervision?
faqs.answer: Sometimes not, and we would rather say so during a free trial than in month three. Live video works well for most secondary students and genuinely does not suit some: younger children, students who will close a laptop and open something else when attention wanders, and those for whom a screen is itself a barrier. A parent usually knows which of their children that describes, and the trial lesson is partly there to test the format rather than only the tutor.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue if we travel during the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the practical advantages of live video from a UAE household. A family abroad for several weeks can keep a weekly session on Gulf Standard Time or shift it to a convenient local hour, which keeps the summer catch-up window usable rather than lost to travel. That window matters particularly for a student crossing into DP1 or DP2, when nothing else competes for the time and specialist availability is at its widest.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.closingHeading: Map the week, then pick the tutor
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.closingBody: Three steps, in this order. Write down which weekdays are removed for the year by CAS, sport or music. Measure the actual arrival time for five days and take the latest, not the average, then add fifteen minutes. Collect the school's internal deadline calendar and mark the heavy weeks. With those three documents a session can be placed where it will survive a year, which matters more than which tutor sits in it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, and the trial is one lesson in the real slot.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma subjects for students living in Al Mushrif and the surrounding inland districts of Abu Dhabi island. Each profile names the subject and level, so a family can check the match before committing any money at all.

intro.heading: The in-home premium, priced
paragraphs: Al Mushrif is a villa district set inland from the Corniche, with wide streets, a long-established school cluster and the kind of houses that have a study a tutor could comfortably sit in. That is precisely why the in-home quotes families here receive sit at the upper end of the published market. Rates for in-home one-to-one visits across Abu Dhabi and Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Monthly packages of four two-hour in-home sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799.

Set that beside the online figures and the shape becomes clear. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED at AED 650. Online monthly packages have been advertised at around AED 799 for eight sessions.

The gap between an in-home visit and a qualified online subject tutor is therefore not a quality gap. It is a logistics gap. Al Mushrif is inland, which means a tutor coming from the island's western side crosses Karamah Street and Airport Road at the worst hour of the day, and a tutor coming from the mainland crosses considerably more than that. Somebody pays for that journey, and in every quote you receive it is you. Worse, you also absorb its variance: the late start, the shortened session, the cancellation when the earlier visit overran.

The decision this page is actually about is not online against in-home. It is what you want the money to buy. If the budget is AED 300 an hour, you can spend it on a tutor within driving range of Al Mushrif who teaches Chemistry adequately, or on a Chemistry HL specialist anywhere who can work at your hour. The second buys more because the Diploma is not a general subject. Mathematics alone splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at two levels each, and a tutor strong in one is routinely no use in another.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which removes the travel premium from your bill and the geographic limit from your choice of specialist. What follows prices the rest of it: where Al Mushrif families pay twice, what three Higher Levels genuinely cost to support, which core components are worth paying for and which purchase is never worth making, and when in the year rates move.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.programmesIntro: What a family pays depends on the programme stage, because the thing being bought changes completely. Primary support buys fluency, middle-years support buys criteria literacy, and Diploma support buys mark-scheme technique. Paying Diploma rates for primary consolidation is a quiet and common overspend in villa districts.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and therefore no mark scheme to teach to. What support buys at this stage is number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of explaining a method, plus the research and presentation skills the Year 6 Exhibition rewards. Short blocks work better than standing arrangements, and the rate should sit low in the market.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mushrif families transferring into an Abu Dhabi PYP school sometimes buy a year of support where eight weeks would have closed the gap. Ask any tutor what they would stop doing once the gap closes. A tutor without an answer is describing a subscription.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with command terms rewarding explanation over recall. The Personal Project in Year 10 or 11 is the first substantial independent piece. Support here is inexpensive relative to the Diploma and disproportionately valuable, because it prevents the DP1 collapse that costs far more to repair.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest intervention available to an Al Mushrif family is settling the Diploma subject and level choices in Year 11 with evidence rather than optimism. Correcting a wrong Higher Level choice in DP1 means a term of catch-up bought at the specialist rate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, scored out of 45, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component worth 20 to 30 per cent, so a substantial share of the result is settled before any paper is sat and before most families start looking for help.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Mushrif enquiries arrive in the second term of DP1, after the first mock. That is the most expensive moment to start, because two needs then compete: content still being taught, and internal assessment already due. Starting a term earlier costs less and achieves more.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Fewer DP courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills. The DP courses inside it are examined to exactly the same standard as in the full Diploma, so the support required is identical even though the overall load is lighter. Budget for the course, not the programme.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small, which means schools sometimes cannot staff individual subject help at depth. For a CP student in Al Mushrif the DP course carrying external examination weight is usually the single highest-value purchase in the programme.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.subjectsIntro: A quote is only meaningful once the subject, level and component are named, because those three facts decide how scarce the right tutor is. The subjects below are the ones Al Mushrif families ask for most, with what each assesses and where the hours go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: SL carries Papers 1 and 2 at 40 per cent each with the Exploration at 20; HL adds Paper 3 and redistributes to 30, 30, 20 and 20. Paper 1 is non-calculator. Support hours go on manipulation fluency and method-mark discipline, and at HL on full-length Paper 3 practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, probability and modelling at the core and matrices, graph theory and numerical methods at Higher Level. The hours go on interpretive writing rather than algebra, which is cheaper to staff and more often underestimated.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice, Paper 2 structured response, Scientific Investigation at 20 per cent. Energetics sign conventions, equilibrium reasoning and organic mechanism precision absorb most of the support time, with uncertainty evaluation in the investigation close behind.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Derivation-heavy, with graphs read for physical quantities. Students who can quote a formula frequently cannot name the assumption that validates it, which is where explanation marks go. Circular motion and capacitance at Higher Level are the predictable hours.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume concealing one skill: applying a named process to an unfamiliar context under command-term discipline. Genetics, plant transport and the statistical treatment inside the Scientific Investigation account for most of the difference between adjacent grades.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of 800 words each on recent articles, plus papers rewarding a fully labelled diagram and developed evaluation. Support divides neatly: a short block on the commentaries, then technique work on evaluation paragraphs that weigh rather than restate.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with an HL Internal Assessment of 1,800 words on a real organisation's issue. Tools earn nothing in isolation; application earns the marks. Quantitative sections are routinely skipped in revision and routinely appear on the paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, an internally assessed Individual Oral, and at Higher Level an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The expensive habit is summarising a text where analysis of effect was required, which takes weeks rather than sessions to undo.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects with commentaries totalling up to 950 words, contributing to the three bonus points. A short block is usually enough; standing weekly TOK support is rarely worth its cost.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research, marked out of 34 across five criteria, with Critical Thinking alone worth 12. The school supervisor holds the task. A tutor questions the research focus, checks the method is answerable and gives feedback on drafts the student has written.

modes.description: A single fixed hour each week in one subject at one level. The cheapest effective arrangement, because continuity lets a tutor verify that last week's gap closed rather than rediscovering it. For a DP1 student coping but drifting it is almost always sufficient, and adding a second subject usually reduces the first one's effect.

sections.heading: Online and in-home in Al Mushrif, costed line by line
paragraphs: The comparison most tutoring pages avoid is the only one a family actually needs. Take an hour of teaching as the unit and ask what each format adds to it. An in-home visit adds travel in both directions, a dedicated time block the tutor cannot share with anyone else, and the risk that traffic eats part of the lesson. An online session adds a laptop and a quiet hour, and removes the rest.

Published rates make the arithmetic visible. In-home one-to-one across the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour; a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300; a specialist IB tutor online at AED 200 to 450 and above. For the same AED 300, an Al Mushrif family can buy the middle of the in-home band or comfortably the middle of the specialist online band. The second is a better purchase for a Diploma subject, because the Diploma rewards narrow expertise and travel rewards nobody.

There is a quality argument too, and it runs the opposite way to intuition. For Diploma past-paper work a shared screen shows the same working to both people at the same size, the annotated script persists after the session, and the lesson can be built around a marked paper rather than a conversation. What online delivery genuinely lacks is the social pressure of a person in the room, which matters for a student who will not otherwise sit down. That is a real consideration, and it is about the student rather than the format.

What online delivery removes entirely is the cancellation problem. An Al Mushrif in-home session in the late afternoon depends on a tutor crossing Karamah Street or Airport Road, and the third or fourth cancellation is usually the point where a family loses the week's rhythm and the arrangement quietly stops being useful before it stops being paid for.

sections.heading: Three things Al Mushrif families end up paying for twice
paragraphs: The first is diagnosis. A family books a block of sessions, and the first two or three are spent establishing what a marked timed paper would have shown in ninety minutes. Then, when the plan does not work, a second tutor repeats the exercise. The fix is to pay for one diagnostic at the start, get it in writing, and hand it to whoever teaches afterwards. A written diagnostic is portable; an impression is not.

The second is content that the school was going to teach anyway. A DP1 student in October is three months into a two-year syllabus, and a tutor working chapter by chapter alongside the school is being paid to duplicate it. That is useful only where the school's teaching has genuinely failed. Otherwise the money should buy what the school cannot provide: individual marked scripts, technique work and the core components. Ask any tutor to say explicitly what they are doing that the school is not.

The third is the unreviewed arrangement. A weekly session that began in November to fix a specific problem is still running in May because nobody set a review point. The problem was solved in February. Three months of sessions after that were a habit, and in the specialist band that is a significant sum. A fixed review at eight sessions, with stopping as a named option, costs nothing to agree and saves the most money of anything on this page.

There is a fourth that deserves mention because it is expensive and avoidable. Buying at the top of the market for work at the bottom of the difficulty range. An examiner-track tutor at AED 650 an hour is a sensible purchase for a DP2 student polishing Paper 3 technique in the final weeks. For a DP1 student whose actual problem is quadratic manipulation left over from Year 10, it is money spent on reassurance, and the work needed is patient and elementary.

sections.heading: Three Higher Levels: what the Diploma load actually costs to support
paragraphs: A full Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, and families budgeting support frequently think in terms of subjects rather than levels. The level is where the cost sits. Higher Level means a wider syllabus to cover, usually an additional paper, and a greater internal assessment demand, which translates directly into hours. A student taking three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels does not need six equal support plans; they need to decide which two of the three Higher Levels are at risk.

The honest guidance is to support at most two subjects at a time, and ideally one. Three concurrent weekly sessions plus school homework plus the core components produces a student who has no time to consolidate anything, and consolidation is where learning actually happens. Families who buy three sessions a week usually end up with three partially effective arrangements rather than one effective one, at three times the price.

Which subject to choose is a question with an evidence-based answer. Sit a timed paper in each candidate subject, mark them against the published scheme, and support the one where the gap is largest and most tractable. Frequently the subject a student complains about most is not the one losing the most marks, because complaint tracks discomfort rather than loss. A marked script resolves the argument in an afternoon.

The core components are the exception to the one-subject rule, because they are time-limited blocks rather than ongoing support. An Extended Essay block of four sessions in DP1 does not compete with a weekly maths arrangement in the way a second weekly subject would. Sequencing them, rather than running everything at once, is what keeps a two-year plan affordable.

sections.heading: The core: what to pay for, and the one purchase never worth making
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments together decide a large share of a Diploma score, and they are the components families understand least. Each has a published length limit and a published set of criteria, which makes them unusually easy to budget for: a defined piece of work with a defined standard needs a defined block of support rather than an indefinite arrangement.

Worth paying for: interrogation of the research focus before any work is invested in it. This is the single highest-value hour in the whole core. A student who has chosen an Extended Essay question that cannot be answered within 4,000 words, or an Exploration topic that will not generate mathematics at the course level, is about to lose marks that no amount of later polishing recovers. Also worth paying for: criterion-referenced feedback on a draft the student has written, which is work a school supervisor often has limited time to provide in depth.

Not worth paying for, and not legitimate: anybody writing, drafting, restructuring or completing the work. Operations exist in this market selling finished Internal Assessments, one at a published fixed price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, the school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. A Diploma can be withheld. That risk never appears in the advertisement.

There is also a practical reason the purchase fails on its own terms. The criteria reward personal engagement and reflection, and those cannot be outsourced. A ghostwritten Exploration or Extended Essay scores poorly on exactly the criteria it was bought to secure, because the voice is generic and the reflection is decorative. The test for any legitimate help is simple: could the student explain every sentence and every decision as their own?

sections.heading: Tutoring cost beside school fees and examination entry
paragraphs: Tutoring discussed alone sounds expensive. Set beside the other costs of a Diploma, it is a smaller and more controllable line than families expect, which is an argument for spending it deliberately rather than reflexively. School fees dominate any Abu Dhabi education budget, and fee regulation sits with ADEK in this emirate rather than with the Dubai authority whose announcements circulate more widely.

On the Dubai side, for context on direction rather than a number to plan with, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and International Baccalaureate at 7. Those figures describe Dubai, not Abu Dhabi, and an Al Mushrif family should read them as scale rather than as local fact.

Against school fees, the tutoring decision is really about which of several options to buy. One well-matched weekly session for a defined block. A short core-component block. An examination-term intensive. Or nothing, because the school's own clinic covers it. The most expensive pattern is the unreviewed weekly habit, which outlives its purpose and never appears as a decision because it was never revisited.

A note on what we will not do. We publish no invented IB Gram price list to look competitive, and we quote no competitor rate without naming the source and framing it as the market. We make no claim of approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram holds none of them. The honest route to our own number is a free trial lesson and a short conversation about subject, level and hours.

sections.heading: Scarcity, and the months when rates and availability move
paragraphs: Tutoring is a market, and its prices respond to the calendar in a way nobody advertises. Between September and December there is capacity in almost every Diploma subject, and a family has genuine choice. From January, as mock results land, demand rises sharply. By February and March every DP2 cohort in the emirate wants examination-term support in the same weeks, and the specialists who were available in October are not.

The consequence for an Al Mushrif family is simple and actionable. If you know in October that your child will need support before the May session, arranging it in October secures a better match at a normal rate. Waiting until February means competing for what is left, and what is left is either less specialised or more expensive. This is entirely predictable, which makes it manageable, and it is the single most useful piece of timing advice on this page.

Scarcity also varies by subject in ways that affect price. Analysis and Approaches at both levels is the best-covered course in the IB catalogue, so a family has real choice and should not accept the top of the market by default. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is thinner. Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish, Global Politics, Music and Design Technology are genuinely hard to staff at Higher Level, and that scarcity is real rather than manufactured.

When we cannot staff a request properly there are three honest answers, and promising a match is not among them. Offer a dated waiting slot. Offer a genuinely qualified alternative with the limitation stated plainly, for instance a Physics HL specialist covering mechanics in a related course but not its physiology content. Or decline. No researched competitor page in the Abu Dhabi cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, which is worth noticing in a market where every page implies complete coverage.

sections.heading: What to agree before any money moves
paragraphs: Five things, and all of them in writing. The first is what is being fixed, stated specifically. "Struggling with chemistry" is a feeling. "Lost most of the energetics marks and all of the uncertainty marks on the mock" is a brief, and it is the difference between a plan and a hope.

The second is the number of sessions in the block and which weeks will be skipped. The UAE academic year removes teaching weeks from every twelve-week plan: Ramadan changes the usable hour, Eid removes days, the winter break removes weeks. A block counted in sessions rather than months stays honest. The third is the measure: a timed paper marked against the published scheme at the start, repeated at the end of the block, so both sides are looking at evidence rather than impressions.

The fourth is the review point, with stopping named as an option. Eight sessions is the usual interval. At that point the honest choices are continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish, and a provider who cannot say the word finish has an incentive problem. The fifth is what the tutor will not do, specifically on the core components, because that boundary protects the student's Diploma rather than our reputation.

And one thing not to agree to. No grade promise, from anyone, at any rate. A Diploma score depends on two years of a student's own work, on internal assessment produced months before the papers, on three or two written papers in one window, and on grade boundaries nobody controls. What tutoring can reliably do is close diagnosed gaps, rebuild technique and recover the marks lost to process rather than ignorance, which for most students is a meaningful number. Anything claimed beyond that is marketing.

process.title: Say what the money is meant to fix
process.description: Subject, level and the specific marks lost, ideally from a marked mock rather than a general impression. A request described that precisely can be either filled properly or declined honestly, and both outcomes are better than a month of sessions spent discovering what the brief should have said.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic, in writing
process.description: A timed paper marked against the published scheme locates the gap in ninety minutes and separates content loss from process loss. Get it in writing, because a written diagnostic travels with your child if the tutor changes, while an impression has to be bought again.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session at no cost with no card required, built around the diagnostic rather than an introduction. The student judges the explanation, you get the written read. If the fit is wrong we rematch, and correcting a match in week one costs nothing while week six costs a term.

process.title: Buy the smallest plan that fits the gap
process.description: One weekly session in the band the diagnosis actually calls for, not the band that sounds most impressive. If the work needed is elementary consolidation, the specialist rate buys reassurance rather than progress, and we will say so even though it is the smaller invoice.

process.title: Review at eight sessions, and stop when done
process.description: Repeat the measure, compare the two scripts, then continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. The unreviewed weekly habit is the most expensive thing in this market, and the only defence against it is a review point agreed before the first session.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors. In an inland villa district the gap is largely a cross-island drive at the worst hour. Lessons run one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not visit UAE homes.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each AED rate on this page is another provider's published number, named so you can check it, and framed as the market rather than as our price. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in dollars.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end on a date
whyPoints.description: Core component support is three to five sessions and then stops. Examination intensives carry a finish date set before they start. An arrangement with no end point is a subscription, and families usually notice they have one only when they examine a year of invoices.

whyPoints.title: We will recommend the cheaper option
whyPoints.description: If the diagnosis says elementary consolidation, we match at the rate that work deserves rather than at the specialist band. Selling depth for a shallow problem is the easiest upsell in tutoring and the least defensible one.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty boundary is published
whyPoints.description: A tutor interrogates a research focus, teaches the criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. Nobody drafts an Extended Essay, Exploration or TOK essay. Completed Internal Assessments are sold in this market, and the risk of buying one falls on the student's Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Scarcity named, not exploited
whyPoints.description: Capacity is real from September to December and tight in February and March. Thin subjects stay thin all year. We say which, give a date, or decline, rather than filling a Higher Level slot with someone who does not teach the course.

faqs.question: Why are in-home quotes in Al Mushrif so much higher than online ones?
faqs.answer: Because the quote contains a journey. Published in-home one-to-one rates across the emirate run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Al Mushrif sits inland, so a tutor is crossing Karamah Street or Airport Road at the worst hour of the afternoon, and the premium funds that drive plus a dedicated block they cannot share. It also funds variance: late starts, shortened sessions and the occasional cancellation. None of that is teaching.

faqs.question: For the same AED 300 an hour, what is the better buy?
faqs.answer: Specialist depth rather than physical presence. AED 300 sits in the middle of the published in-home band and comfortably inside the specialist online band, so the choice is between a competent generalist who can reach your street and a specialist in your child's exact course and level who can work at your hour. The Diploma rewards narrow expertise: Mathematics alone splits into two courses at two levels, and a tutor strong in one is often no use in another.

faqs.question: Is it worth supporting all three Higher Level subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Three weekly sessions plus school homework plus the core components leaves a student no time to consolidate, and consolidation is where learning actually settles. Families who buy three usually get three partially effective arrangements at three times the cost. Sit a timed paper in each candidate subject, mark them against the published scheme, and support the one or two where the gap is largest and most tractable. The subject a student complains about is often not the one losing most marks.

faqs.question: What is the highest-value single hour we could buy in the IB core?
faqs.answer: Interrogation of the research focus, before any work is invested. A student who has chosen an Extended Essay question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words, or an Exploration topic that will not generate mathematics at the course level, is about to lose marks no later polishing recovers. One hour spent stress-testing the question saves several spent repairing the consequences, and it is the cheapest intervention in the whole two-year programme.

faqs.question: Someone has offered to supply a finished Internal Assessment. Should we consider it?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is practical as well as ethical. Buying completed coursework is academic malpractice under IB rules; the school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and the consequence falls on the student, whose Diploma can be withheld. It also fails on its own terms, because the criteria reward personal engagement and reflection, and a bought piece scores poorly on exactly those. A tutor may question a focus, teach criteria and give feedback on the student's own draft. Nothing beyond that.

faqs.question: When in the year is support cheapest to arrange in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Between September and December, by a clear margin, because capacity exists across almost every Diploma subject and a family has genuine choice of tutor and hour. From January, as mock results land, demand rises. By February and March every DP2 cohort in the emirate is competing for the same weeks, and what remains is either less specialised or more expensive. Arranging in October for a May session is the single most effective cost decision available.

faqs.question: Do the Dubai school fee announcements apply to us in Al Mushrif?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA regulates Dubai, and its confirmation on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year was a Dubai measure under a Dubai incentives package. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation here and handles fee matters separately. Dubai's sector figures, 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, are useful as scale and not as local fact.

faqs.question: Our son works hard and the grade will not move. Are we buying the wrong thing?
faqs.answer: Possibly. If the sessions consist of working through the textbook alongside the school, you are paying a tutor to duplicate teaching you already fund through fees. That is worth buying only where the school's teaching has genuinely failed. Otherwise the money should buy what a class of twenty-five cannot: individually marked scripts, technique work on command terms and timing, and the core components. Ask the tutor to state plainly what they are doing that the school is not.

faqs.question: How long should a block of support run before we review it?
faqs.answer: Eight sessions, counted as sessions rather than weeks. The UAE year removes teaching time from every twelve-week plan, because Ramadan changes the usable hour, Eid removes days and the winter break removes weeks, so a calendar review compares unequal amounts of teaching. At eight sessions the honest options are continue, change focus, change tutor or finish. A provider who cannot say finish has an incentive problem, and the unreviewed habit is the most expensive line in this market.

faqs.question: Is a group class a sensible saving for a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: For broad revision across a cohort shortly before the papers, yes. For a diagnosed gap, no, despite the lower headline rate. A group moves at a shared pace, so if the problem is energetics sign conventions that topic gets a few minutes of an hour while the rest covers familiar ground. Families often work this out in month three, having bought twelve hours and received perhaps ninety minutes of relevant teaching. Diagnose first, then choose the instrument.

faqs.question: What does a written diagnostic actually contain?
faqs.answer: A marked script and a short list of causes rather than a list of weak topics. Lost marks sorted into categories: genuine content gaps, method marks not awarded because working was not shown, accuracy lost to premature rounding, misread command terms, and time. Most families are surprised by how much falls outside the content category. It is written down because a written diagnostic travels with your child if the tutor changes, whereas an impression has to be paid for again.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are genuinely hard to staff at short notice?
faqs.answer: Group 2 languages beyond French and Spanish, Global Politics, Music and Design Technology, particularly at Higher Level, and almost anything during February and March. Analysis and Approaches at both levels is the best-covered course in the catalogue, so there a family should not accept the top of the market by default. When we cannot staff a request properly we give a dated waiting slot, state a limitation plainly, or decline rather than place someone adjacent.

faqs.question: Can anybody tell us what grade the money will buy?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who answers that question is selling something they cannot deliver. A Diploma score rests on two years of the student's own work, on internal assessment produced months before the papers, on papers sat in a single window, and on grade boundaries nobody controls. What support reliably does is close diagnosed content gaps, rebuild examination technique, and recover marks lost to process rather than ignorance. For most students that last category alone is a meaningful number.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to the house in Al Mushrif if we pay the premium?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, at any rate. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session here runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. We would rather say that plainly on the page than take a booking and explain it afterwards. The practical upside is that your child is matched from everyone who teaches their course rather than from everyone willing to drive inland at six o'clock.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.closingHeading: Buy the diagnostic, then decide what the plan is worth
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.closingBody: If you are pricing an IB home tutor in Al Mushrif, the cheapest useful step is not a rate comparison. It is one timed paper, marked against the published scheme, which tells you whether you are buying content, technique or a core component block, and therefore which band of the market you actually need. Send the subject, the level and the hours that work, take the free trial lesson with no card required, and we will tell you honestly if the answer is a short block, one weekly session, or nothing at all. Lessons run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma subjects for students in Al Nahyan and the inland districts around it. Each profile names the subject and level taught, which is the one claim about a tutor that a parent can check directly against their child's timetable.

intro.heading: Compared with what?
paragraphs: Al Nahyan runs inland across the middle of Abu Dhabi island, between Al Karamah and the eastern edge, a mix of villas and low-rise apartment blocks with Airport Road along one side. It is unremarkable in the way most good residential districts are, and families here looking for Diploma support face the same decision as everyone else on the island: not whether to hire someone, but what to compare that hire against.

The comparison tutoring pages make is always the same and always useless: themselves against other platforms, unnamed and conveniently worse. The comparisons a parent in Al Nahyan actually needs are different. An in-home visit against an online session, on the things that genuinely differ. A paid tutor against the school's own clinic, which is already covered by the fees you pay. One subject funded properly against three funded thinly. And, most usefully, any tutor's claims against what can be independently checked, because this market is full of assertions that cannot be. That last comparison is the one that saves the most money and the least often made, because it requires knowing which questions have answers a parent can actually check.

Take the in-home question first, since it is the phrase that brought you here. Published in-home one-to-one rates across the emirate run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist. The difference is a journey: inland Al Nahyan means crossing Airport Road or coming off the mainland at the hour traffic is worst, and that premium buys road time rather than teaching. It also buys variance, because the third or fourth traffic cancellation is usually where a family loses the week's rhythm.

On that point we are direct rather than coy. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. We would rather state that on the page than take a booking and explain it afterwards, and the trade is real: dropping the travel requirement means your child is matched from everyone who teaches their exact Diploma subject at their exact level rather than from everyone willing to drive inland on a Tuesday.

What follows is a set of honest comparisons. Where the tutors in this market actually live and what that does to a quote. In-home against online on six specific concerns rather than in general. A tutor against the free alternatives, including the option of buying nothing. Which subject groups genuinely repay one-to-one. And a short guide to separating a verifiable claim from an unverifiable one, which is the most useful skill a parent can acquire in this market.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.programmesIntro: Comparing the programmes matters because an Al Nahyan family often has children on two of them, and the support that helps one is not the support that helps another. The structures differ more than the shared IB name suggests.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, assessed through units of inquiry, a portfolio and the Year 6 Exhibition. Compared with the later programmes there is no mark scheme to teach to, so what is bought is fluency, reading stamina and the habit of explaining a method, plus the research skills the Exhibition rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Children arriving into an Abu Dhabi PYP school from a worksheet-driven system usually find the inquiry structure unfamiliar before they find the content hard. Compared with a content-based intervention, time spent on explaining reasoning aloud is far better value at this stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with command terms rewarding explanation over recall, and a Personal Project in Year 10 or 11. Compared with IGCSE, assessment is continuous rather than terminal, which means there is no single series to revise for and no obvious moment of pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Because there is no external series, MYP support is easy to postpone indefinitely. Compared with a DP1 intervention it is dramatically cheaper, and the subject and level choices made at the end of Year 11 are the most consequential dated decision in the programme.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, scored out of 45, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries internal assessment worth 20 to 30 per cent. Compared with a three-subject post-16 route, the Diploma spreads a student thinner and rewards organisation as much as ability.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, with November as the alternative. No IB examination or results date appears here, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than none.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Fewer DP courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills. Compared with the full Diploma the overall load is lighter, while the DP courses inside it are examined to exactly the same standard, so subject support needs are identical.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small, which means schools sometimes cannot staff individual subject help at depth. Compared with a full Diploma student, a CP student's one or two DP courses carry a greater share of the programme's external weight.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Nahyan families ask about most, described by what each assesses and, where it matters, by how much difference one-to-one attention actually makes compared with good class teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 40 per cent each at SL; 30, 30 and 20 with Paper 3 at HL, plus a 20 per cent Exploration. One-to-one makes a large difference here, because the recurring losses are individual habits: unshown method, premature rounding, sign errors through long work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active, built on statistics, probability and modelling, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. One-to-one helps most on the interpretive sentence that carries marks, which is hard to teach to a whole class and easy to coach individually.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice, Paper 2 structured response, Scientific Investigation at 20 per cent. Energetics sign conventions and uncertainty evaluation reward individual attention; the practical programme itself belongs to the school and cannot be replaced.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Derivation-heavy, with graphs read for physical quantities. The gap between quoting a formula and naming the assumption that validates it is exactly the sort of thing a class cannot chase individually and a tutor can close in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume concealing one skill: applying a named process to an unfamiliar context under command-term discipline. Compared with maths, more of the work here is a revision method the student can apply alone once taught, which argues for a shorter block.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of 800 words each plus papers rewarding labelled diagrams and developed evaluation. Evaluation technique responds very well to individual coaching, because it is a writing habit rather than a body of knowledge.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with an 1,800-word Higher Level internal assessment on a real organisation. Tools earn nothing in isolation; application earns the marks. Quantitative sections are routinely skipped in revision and routinely appear in the papers.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, an internally assessed Individual Oral, and an HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The habit of narrating rather than analysing takes months to change, so start early or choose a different subject to fund.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: A TOK essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title, an exhibition with commentaries totalling up to 950 words, and a 4,000-word Extended Essay marked out of 34 with Critical Thinking worth 12. Both contribute to the three bonus points.

regions.name: Al Karamah
regions.note: Immediately west along Karamah Street. A tutor based here quotes Al Nahyan a few minutes' drive, which puts their in-home rate near the bottom of the published band for no reason connected to teaching quality.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: South-west and villa-heavy, with long-established campuses nearby. Also a short hop, and also a district whose tutors therefore appear cheaper to Al Nahyan families than they would to a family across a bridge.

sections.heading: Where the tutors actually live, and what that does to a quote
paragraphs: An in-home quote is a teaching rate plus a travel rate, and nobody itemises it. That means two Al Nahyan families with identical needs can be quoted very different hourly figures depending on an accident of where the tutor happens to live, and neither family ever sees why.

The geography is straightforward. A tutor in Al Karamah or Al Mushrif is a few minutes away and quotes near the bottom of the published AED 180 to 500 band. A tutor coming from Al Zahiyah crosses the island at the worst hour. A tutor on Al Reem Island adds a bridge. A tutor in Khalifa City or Mussafah is pricing a genuinely long round trip, and that is where the top of the band comes from. None of this correlates with Diploma subject knowledge, which is distributed according to where experienced teachers happen to live rather than according to who is convenient.

There is a second, quieter effect. A tutor who makes several visits in an evening is pricing a route, not a lesson, and your session sits somewhere in that sequence. If an earlier visit overruns, yours starts late or finishes early, and neither is reflected in the invoice. Over a term, the delivered teaching time can differ noticeably from the paid teaching time, and in an inland district with one main artery that is not a theoretical concern.

Removing travel removes both effects. An online slot has hard edges: it starts when it starts and runs for the hour. And the tutor is selected from everyone who teaches your child's subject at their level rather than from the subset whose route happens to include Al Nahyan. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: In-home against online, on the six things parents actually ask about
paragraphs: General comparisons are useless because they let each side claim the ground it prefers. Six specific concerns come up in almost every Al Nahyan conversation, and each has a different answer.

On who is available, online wins decisively, because the pool stops being defined by driving range. On cost, online wins on published figures: AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor against AED 180 to 500 in-home. On reliability, online wins again, because nothing depends on Airport Road. On working through a past paper, online is at least equal and arguably better: a shared screen shows the same line to both people at the same size and the annotated script survives the session.

On two concerns in-home genuinely wins. The first is a student who will not sit down and work without a person physically present. That is a real category, it has nothing to do with intelligence, and for those students the social pressure of someone in the room is the product. The second is the very young, where attention and rapport are harder to hold through a screen, though this matters much less for a Diploma student than for a primary child.

The sixth concern is the one parents raise last and worry about most: whether a student will actually engage. The honest answer is that it depends on the student and on the tutor's ability to hold a session, not on the medium, and the only way to find out is one trial lesson. That is why the trial is free, requires no card, and is built around a diagnostic rather than an introduction: it answers the only question that cannot be answered from a page.

sections.heading: A paid tutor compared with the free alternatives
paragraphs: The comparison nobody selling tutoring wants to make is against the options that cost nothing. There are three, and for a meaningful number of Al Nahyan families one of them is the right answer.

The first is the school's own support. Almost every school in the emirate runs some form of after-school clinic, departmental help or targeted intervention, already covered by the fees you pay. It is routinely under-used, partly because parents ask vaguely. Asking the head of department about a specific topic, naming what was lost in the last assessment, often produces either a useful answer or a solved problem. The limitation is that a department cannot give one student sustained individual attention, which is the thing a tutor actually sells.

The second is fixing the working environment, which costs nothing and changes more than an hour a week. A student revising on a sofa with a phone within reach is not revising. A student rereading notes is generating familiarity rather than recall, which is why hard-working students plateau for a year and conclude they are bad at the subject. Teaching retrieval practice under timed conditions takes one session, or one honest conversation, and then the student applies it alone.

The third is diagnosis without purchase. Ask the school what the last assessment was marked against and which specific marks were lost. A detailed answer may make a tutor unnecessary. A vague answer tells you why your child cannot explain the problem either, which is itself worth knowing. A tutor becomes the right comparison when the gap needs individual time the class cannot give, when the problem is examination technique rather than content, or when confidence has gone to the point where the student no longer asks questions.

sections.heading: What two parents mean by "home tutor", compared
paragraphs: The phrase carries at least three different meanings in Abu Dhabi, and a conversation between a parent and a provider frequently proceeds with each meaning something else. Separating them removes most of the confusion in this market.

The first meaning is literal: someone who physically comes to the house. That is a delivery method, and it is what the published AED 180 to 500 band prices. The second meaning is supervisory: an adult who sits with a child while they do their homework, keeps them on task and answers questions as they arise. That is genuinely useful for some students and is a different service from subject teaching, usually at a lower rate, and it does not require Diploma subject expertise.

The third meaning, and the one most parents actually want when they say it, is private: one-to-one attention from someone who knows the subject, as distinct from being one of twenty-five in a classroom. That is the product. The house was historically just where it happened, because there was nowhere else for it to happen. Once the lesson can run over live video, the private part survives and the house part becomes optional.

Being clear which one you want changes what you should buy. If the need is supervision, a Diploma specialist at the specialist rate is an expensive way to get it, and the right answer may be a structured study routine rather than a tutor. If the need is subject expertise, insisting on physical presence restricts you to whoever will travel to Al Nahyan that evening and makes the expertise the variable that gives way. We say plainly which we provide: one-to-one subject teaching, online, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Where one-to-one makes the biggest difference, group by group
paragraphs: Not every Diploma subject repays individual attention equally, and a family with one budget should know which ones do. The pattern is consistent enough to be worth stating, and it cuts against the instinct to fund the subject the student complains about.

Mathematics repays it most, because its losses are individual habits rather than gaps in knowledge: method not shown where the mark scheme awards it separately, premature rounding, sign errors through long work, a specific topic cluster never consolidated. A class cannot chase one student's habits. A tutor can see them in a single marked script and change them in a fortnight.

The sciences come next, and the reason is the Scientific Investigation. Twenty per cent of the grade sits in a piece of work where the commonest failure is a method that cannot generate analysable data, and that is caught in conversation at the planning stage rather than in a classroom. The written papers also reward naming the assumption behind a formula, which is exactly the sort of thing one-to-one questioning exposes quickly.

The content-heavy subjects repay it least, which surprises families. Biology, history and geography need a revision method more than they need a teacher, and the method can be taught once and applied alone. English sits apart: individual attention helps enormously with the habit of analysing rather than narrating, but that habit takes months to change, so it is worth starting early or not at all. Economics and Business Management are strong candidates for a short late block, because evaluation technique is learnable in a defined window close to the papers.

sections.heading: Comparing a tutor's claims with what you can actually verify
paragraphs: This is the most useful comparison on the page, because the Abu Dhabi tutoring market runs on assertions and only some of them can be checked. Sorting them is a skill a parent acquires once and uses forever.

Verifiable: the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. You can ask to see it, and a tutor confused by the question is worth a second look. Note what it does not prove: it is a right-to-work instrument, not a statement about whether someone can teach Chemistry HL.

Also verifiable: course knowledge, through specific questions. What is the Exploration worth and how is it marked. What is in Paper 3 and does my child sit it. Which paper is non-calculator. Those answers are instant for someone who has taught the course and vague for someone who has not. And verifiable: subject and level, which a parent can check directly against the school timetable.

Not verifiable, and therefore not claimed here: examiner status, which we cannot evidence for an individual and which in any case should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Regulator accreditation, because a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to a training institute with premises and IB Gram does not hold one; nor do we hold or claim approval from ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Star ratings and review counts, unless they are real, countable and attributable. Tutor headcounts. And statistics without a stated sample, date and method, which includes every satisfaction percentage you will see in this market.

sections.heading: The first eight weeks compared with the next eight
paragraphs: Families decide whether tutoring is working somewhere around week five, usually on a feeling. Comparing what the first block should produce with what a second block should produce makes that judgement evidential rather than emotional.

The first eight sessions are mostly about finding and fixing. Session one is a timed diagnostic marked against the published scheme, with losses sorted by cause rather than topic. Sessions two to seven address the largest identified cluster and the technique losses, with marked work produced every time. Session eight repeats the diagnostic. What should exist at the end is two scripts that can be laid side by side, an error log and a decision. What should not exist is a sense that things feel better with nothing to point at.

A second block, if it happens, should look different. The cheap wins have gone: compliance losses, rounding, unshown method. What remains is either genuine content depth or a harder technique problem such as pacing across a full paper or the quality of evaluation writing. Progress in a second block is slower and the sessions should feel more demanding, which is a sign it is aimed at the right thing. A second block that feels identical to the first is a second block aimed at nothing.

The comparison also tells you when to stop, which is the decision nobody sets up in advance. If the causes identified at the start have gone, the work is done. If your child begins answering the tutor's diagnostic questions before they are finished, the session has become supervised practice they could do alone for nothing. Either is a signal to finish, and a tutor who says so unprompted has told you something useful about their intentions.

sections.heading: The Diploma compared with the routes a family might switch to
paragraphs: A minority of Al Nahyan conversations are not about tutoring at all but about whether the Diploma is the right programme. That is a legitimate question and it deserves a comparison rather than a defence, since tutoring cannot fix a structural mismatch between a student and a programme.

The Diploma spreads a student across six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with internal assessment in every subject. It rewards organisation, consistency and writing as much as subject ability, and it punishes a student who can only concentrate on what is immediately due. A three-subject A Level route concentrates on fewer subjects with most of the weight in terminal examinations, which suits a strong examination performer who dislikes coursework. An American high school diploma distributes grades across continuous assessment and a wider subject spread, with external testing largely separate from the school's own grading.

Switching is possible and expensive, and the cost is not mainly financial. A student moving out of the Diploma mid-course usually loses the internal assessment work already done, because it does not transfer, and may lose a year. A student moving in faces content gaps across six subjects at once. The window where a switch is genuinely low-cost is between Year 11 and Year 12, which is before most families have enough evidence to want one.

What tutoring can honestly contribute to that decision is evidence rather than an opinion. A marked timed paper shows whether a student's difficulty is content, technique or workload management. If it is workload management across six subjects plus the core, more tutoring in one subject will not help, and saying so is more useful than selling a weekly session into a structural problem.
