faqs.question: Why would two Al Nahyan families be quoted different in-home rates?
faqs.answer: Because an in-home quote is a teaching rate plus an unitemised travel rate. A tutor in Al Karamah is a few minutes away and quotes near the bottom of the published AED 180 to 500 band; one in Khalifa City or Mussafah is pricing a thirty to fifty minute round trip and quotes near the top. The teaching is identical. Nothing in that spread correlates with Diploma subject knowledge, which is distributed according to where experienced teachers happen to live.

faqs.question: Is there any situation where an in-home tutor genuinely beats online?
faqs.answer: Two. A student who will not sit down and work without a person physically present, which is a real category unrelated to intelligence and for whom the social presence is the product. And very young children, where attention and rapport are harder to hold through a screen, which matters far less for a Diploma student. On availability, cost, reliability and past-paper work, online is better. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes in any case; home visits are a service offered only in India.

faqs.question: What exactly can we verify about a tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Two things reliably. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, which you can ask to see. And course knowledge, through specific questions: what the Exploration is worth and how it is marked, what is in Paper 3 and whether your child sits it, which paper is non-calculator. Those answers are instant for someone who has taught the course. Everything else in this market is largely assertion.

faqs.question: Another service says it is approved by KHDA. Should that reassure us?
faqs.answer: No, it should concern you. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. It is not something an online tutoring service or an individual tutor holds. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not claim any.

faqs.question: What about a tutor described as a current IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unverifiable unless evidence is produced, because there is no public register a parent can check. More importantly, examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and a provider leaning on it that way is making an improper suggestion. We do not describe tutors as examiners, because we cannot evidence the status for an individual. Ask the course-specific questions instead; they test the same thing more honestly.

faqs.question: Could the school's own support solve this without us paying anyone?
faqs.answer: Quite possibly, and it is worth exhausting first because it is already covered by your fees. Most schools in the emirate run after-school clinics, departmental help or targeted intervention. Ask the head of department about the specific topic, naming the marks lost in the last assessment, rather than raising a general worry. The limitation is that a department cannot give one student sustained individual attention, which is precisely the thing a tutor sells and the only thing worth paying for.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are the worst value for one-to-one tuition?
faqs.answer: Content-heavy subjects, generally: biology, history and geography. Their difficulty is usually volume, and the fix is a revision method that can be taught once and then applied alone, rather than a weekly teacher. English is a particular case: individual attention helps enormously with the habit of analysing rather than narrating, but that habit takes months to change, so start early or fund something else. Mathematics and the sciences repay one-to-one most, because their losses are individual habits.

faqs.question: When we say "home tutor", are we asking for the right thing?
faqs.answer: It depends which of three things you mean. Delivery, meaning someone physically present, which is what the AED 180 to 500 band prices. Supervision, meaning an adult who keeps a child on task during homework, which is a useful and cheaper service needing no Diploma expertise. Or private, meaning one-to-one attention from someone who knows the subject, which is what most parents actually want. The house was historically just where the third one happened, and online delivery separates the two.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the first block of sessions worked?
faqs.answer: By comparing two marked scripts rather than two impressions. Session one should produce a timed diagnostic marked against the published scheme, with losses sorted by cause rather than topic. Session eight repeats it. Lay them side by side, with the error log from the weeks between. If the causes identified at the start have reduced, it worked. If nothing has moved, the plan targeted the wrong gap or the match is wrong, and both are the provider's problem to fix.

faqs.question: Should a second block feel the same as the first?
faqs.answer: No, it should feel harder, and that is the sign it is aimed correctly. The first block takes the cheap wins: compliance losses, rounding discipline, method marks, one diagnosed topic cluster. What remains afterwards is genuine content depth or a harder technique problem such as pacing across a full paper or the quality of evaluation writing. Progress is slower. A second block that feels identical to the first is a second block aimed at nothing in particular.

faqs.question: Our son is drowning across all six subjects. Will a tutor help?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and it is worth being honest about that. If a marked paper shows the difficulty is content or technique in one or two subjects, a tutor addresses it directly. If it shows the problem is workload management across six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, then adding a weekly commitment makes the week worse rather than better. That conversation belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator before any money moves.

faqs.question: Can tutoring fix a bad fit between our daughter and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No. The Diploma spreads a student across six subjects with internal assessment in each, and rewards organisation and consistent writing as much as subject ability. A student who can only work on what is immediately due will struggle with it regardless of how much individual teaching they receive. A marked paper will show whether the difficulty is content, technique or structure. If it is structure, the conversation is about the programme, and the school's coordinator is the right person to have it with.

faqs.question: Is a group revision class a fair comparison with one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. A group class is genuinely good value for cohort-wide revision shortly before the papers, and the arithmetic favours it strongly. It is poor value when a student's problem is one narrow diagnosed cluster, because a shared pace gives that topic a few minutes of the hour while the rest covers familiar ground. Diagnose with a marked paper first, then choose. Buying the cheaper instrument for the wrong problem is not a saving.

faqs.question: What statistics should we distrust in tutoring advertising?
faqs.answer: Any figure without a stated sample size, date and method. Satisfaction percentages, average score claims, improvement rates, tutor headcounts and star ratings unless they rest on real, countable, attributable reviews. Researched competitor pages in this market show different ratings in different places on the same page, and one shows a review count that does not match its own student claim. We publish no such figures, because we could not evidence them if you asked.

intro.heading: The honest answer about Diploma subject coverage
paragraphs: Al Raha Beach is a waterfront apartment community on the Abu Dhabi to Dubai road, within easy reach of several of the emirate's largest Diploma campuses. That makes it a good place to be an IB family and a slightly misleading place to search for a tutor, because proximity to a school is not proximity to a subject specialist. The two things are unrelated and families routinely conflate them.

Here is the arithmetic that nobody in this market publishes. The Diploma has six subject groups, and within them a student might be taking Biology at higher level, Economics at standard level, Spanish ab initio, Analysis and Approaches at higher level, Visual Arts, and Theory of Knowledge. Each of those is a separate specialism with its own internal assessment, its own criteria and its own paper structure. The number of adults living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Raha Beach who teach any one of them every week is small. For some of them it is zero.

That is not a failure of this community. It is what happens when you filter a narrow specialism by geography. The pool of people who teach Diploma Economics at higher level, understand how the portfolio commentaries are marked, and know where candidates lose evaluation marks is a professional population rather than a local one. Filter by subject and level and it is deep. Filter by postcode and it is almost empty.

There is a second layer of scarcity specific to the Diploma, and it is worth naming because it affects what a family can realistically expect. Internal assessment knowledge is subject-specific and non-transferable. A tutor who can teach Chemistry content competently may never have supervised a scientific investigation and may not know how the evaluation strand is marked. A tutor who teaches History well may not know what a historical investigation's source evaluation section is assessed on. Those are different competencies and they are not implied by subject knowledge.

So this page does something unusual for a tutoring page: it states coverage. Which subject groups we can staff and how quickly, which Diploma courses are scarce in this market regardless of who you ask, what we do when no suitable specialist is available, and how a parent can test subject and internal assessment knowledge in a single exchange before paying anyone. No competitor page we examined in this market discloses a coverage limit of any kind.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-beach.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, with the internal assessment named in each case, because that is the part where subject knowledge and assessment knowledge come apart.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Written papers plus the scientific investigation. The investigation is marked on criteria including evaluation, where honest treatment of limitations earns more than an ambitious topic does. A tutor who has never supervised one will teach the content well and the component badly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the reasoning load. The scientific investigation requires laboratory access the school controls, so a tutor's role is design, data handling and evaluation rather than practical work. Uncertainty treatment is where marks concentrate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward algebraic fluency; data-based questions reward graph discipline and error analysis. Students who derive correctly still lose marks for not stating assumptions, which is an explicit requirement rather than a stylistic nicety.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at standard level, three at higher, plus the exploration at a fifth of the grade. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Higher level adds proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, series and differential equations, none of which appears in the other route.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same paper structure, calculator throughout, and a very different content list: regression, chi-squared and t-tests, matrices and graph theory at higher level, Voronoi diagrams at standard. A tutor from the other route is not a near substitute.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation decide the top bands. The portfolio of commentaries is a substantial internal component with its own word limit per commentary, and a tutor needs to know how the commentaries are marked rather than only the economics.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven papers plus a research project with its own word limit. Marks follow application to the specific organisation. Recited theory without the business in front of it sits mid-band however accurate it is.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source handling in Paper 1 is assessed on its own terms: origin, purpose, content, value and limitation. The historical investigation is the internal component, with a word limit and a separately marked evaluation of sources and methods that narrative routinely crowds out.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork is the internal component, with a stated word limit and criteria rewarding methodology and evaluation over presentation. Command terms such as examine and to what extent require explicit structure students rarely supply unprompted.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, comparative essay, the individual oral and an additional essay at higher level. The individual oral is built on a global issue and two extracts, is fully knowable in advance, and is therefore the component where preparation converts into marks most reliably.

subjects.name: Languages B and ab initio
subjects.description: Papers plus listening and an individual oral. The scarcest group to staff at Diploma level in this market, because the combination of language, level and IB assessment knowledge narrows the pool sharply. Ab initio in particular is a specific course rather than beginner teaching.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of around 950 words across three objects, both marked against published criteria. Support is process coaching on the student's own work, and it is a distinct competency from any subject specialism.

sections.heading: Coverage by Diploma subject group, stated plainly
paragraphs: This is the section competitors in this market do not write. For mainstream Diploma subjects at a common evening slot, a match is usually available within a few days. For others it takes longer, and for a small number the honest answer is that we will not staff it well and you should look elsewhere with the subject and level written down.

The pattern follows demand and teacher supply rather than difficulty. Mathematics, the sciences and the individuals and societies group are the deepest, because they are the largest Diploma cohorts worldwide and therefore the largest teaching populations. English A is deep. Languages B and ab initio are much thinner, because the pool is the intersection of a specific language, a specific level and IB assessment knowledge. The arts are thinnest of all, and internal assessment coaching in the arts is a specialism of its own.

Within mathematics there is a further split worth stating, because families assume a single pool. Analysis and Approaches at standard level is the easiest match of the four. Applications and Interpretation at higher level is the hardest, because its content includes matrices with eigenvalues, graph theory and Markov chains that most Analysis and Approaches teachers have never taught. A tutor who says they can teach any of the four is describing a willingness rather than a specialism.

sections.heading: Why a Diploma specialist is scarcer than an International GCSE one
paragraphs: Families moving from the British track into the Diploma often expect tutoring to be equally easy to arrange and find it is not. There are three structural reasons, and understanding them makes a waiting time easier to accept than a vague apology would be.

The first is cohort size. International GCSE is sat by a far larger global candidate population than the Diploma, which means a far larger teaching population and therefore a far larger pool of people who could tutor it. Within the Diploma, higher level in a given subject is a smaller cohort again than standard level, and a specific route like Applications and Interpretation at higher level is smaller still.

The second is the internal assessment. Every Diploma subject has one, each has its own criteria and mark allocations, and knowing them is a separate competency from teaching the content. A teacher who has taught Chemistry for ten years in a non-IB system knows the chemistry and does not know how a scientific investigation's evaluation strand is marked. That is not a criticism; it is simply a different body of knowledge, and it is the one families most need and least often check for.

The third is the core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay have no equivalent in the British track, and coaching them requires familiarity with their published criteria and with what a 1,600-word or 4,000-word limit forces. The pool of people who can do that competently is small, and it does not overlap neatly with any subject specialism.

Taken together, those three facts mean that a Diploma family should expect to wait occasionally and should be suspicious of instant availability across every subject and level. A provider who can staff anything immediately is either very large or is matching on subject name alone, and the second is much more common than the first.

sections.heading: How to test whether a tutor knows the subject
paragraphs: A parent can establish this in one exchange, and the test is not about mathematics or chemistry. It is about assessment structure, because that is the knowledge a generalist lacks and cannot improvise. Ask a question whose answer is specific to the subject and level, and listen for whether the reply contains numbers and component names or adjectives and reassurance.

The useful questions are short. What is the internal assessment in this subject called, what share of the grade does it carry, and what are its criteria? Which papers does my child sit at this level and how are they weighted? What is the word limit on the internal component? Where do candidates at this level most often lose marks, and in which component? A specialist answers all four without hesitating. A generalist answers in terms of topics and effort.

The second test is about the student's own work. Send one marked paper or draft before the first session and see whether the tutor refers to it. A tutor who opens by naming two or three specific places on the script where marks were available is working from evidence. A tutor who opens by asking your child how they find the subject is working from a script, and that difference persists for as long as the arrangement does.

The third test is about limits. Ask what they would not do: whether they would write any part of an internal assessment, whether they can supply mark schemes, whether they would tutor a student at a school where they teach. A tutor with clear answers to those has thought about the boundaries. The correct answers are no, no and no, and in this market they are not universal, which is why the question is worth asking out loud.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: This is the part of the conversation this market avoids, and it is the reason the headline question on this page gets asked in the first place. There are three honest outcomes and we would rather name all of them than imply that the answer is always yes.

The first is a waiting time. For a subject at a level we cover but cannot staff at your preferred slot, the answer is usually a date rather than a refusal: a week, sometimes two, often with a later evening slot available sooner. A date we can meet is worth more than an immediate placement with the wrong person, and across a two-year Diploma a fortnight's wait is a small cost against a term of misdirected work.

The second is a partial match. In several cases we can cover the content but should not pretend to cover the internal assessment, or the reverse. Where that is true we say which, and a family can decide whether content support alone is worth buying while the school handles the assessment side. That is a legitimate arrangement and it is better than a tutor covering a criterion they have never seen marked.

The third is a refusal. For the thinnest cases, particularly in the arts and in some language B and ab initio combinations, the honest answer is that we will not staff it well. In that situation you get the subject, level and component written out so that you can look elsewhere with precise information, which is more useful than a sympathetic email. We would rather lose the enquiry than take a fee for a term of approximate teaching.

sections.heading: The internal assessment is where coverage really bites
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, each is marked against published criteria with stated mark allocations, and together they represent a substantial and controllable share of a student's final result. They are also where a subject-only tutor is least useful, which makes them the sharpest test of whether coverage is real.

The mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation at four marks, mathematical communication at four, personal engagement at three, reflection at three, and use of mathematics at six. A tutor who knows that can explain why an elegant piece pitched below the course level cannot reach the top band. A tutor who does not will praise the mathematics and miss the ceiling.

The same structure recurs with different criteria in every subject. The sciences have an investigation whose evaluation strand rewards honest limitations over ambitious topics. History has an investigation with a separately marked evaluation of sources and methods. Economics has a portfolio of commentaries each inside its own word limit. Geography has fieldwork marked on methodology and evaluation. Language A has an individual oral built on a global issue and two extracts, which is entirely knowable in advance.

What a tutor may legitimately do is the same across all of them: explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, test whether a topic or research question the student proposed can reach the top band, teach the techniques the student has chosen, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright, and the risk in that transaction falls on the student.

sections.heading: What the school already covers, and why to ask first
paragraphs: Before coverage becomes a problem worth solving, it is worth checking what is already provided. Diploma schools give every student a supervisor for the Extended Essay and a subject teacher responsible for internal assessment guidance. Those people know the school's internal deadlines, have seen previous cohorts' submissions, and carry accountability for the student's progress in a way no external provider does.

That matters particularly in the scarce subjects. If your child is taking a language B course or an arts subject that is hard to staff externally, the school's own teacher is not merely the free option, they may be the only person within reach with the relevant assessment knowledge. The useful move is to ask the department what support exists and when, rather than to assume the answer is a private tutor.

For content that has been missed through absence, the school is strictly better informed. The class teacher knows what was covered, which examples were used, and what the class is now assumed to know. An external tutor filling that gap will teach the topic as they normally would, which may be at a different depth or in a different order, leaving the student slightly out of step rather than caught up.

Where a paid hour then earns its place is narrow and real: individual diagnosis from the student's own work, criterion literacy explained at length, feedback on a specific draft, and coverage of a subject or route the school is thin in. That is what a block should be bought for, and it is a better conversation to have after the school has been asked than before.

sections.heading: Al Raha Beach scheduling, and the one thing that is genuinely local
paragraphs: Having argued that coverage is national rather than local, the one thing that genuinely is local deserves its own section: when a session can start. Campuses serving Al Raha Beach finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions running later on some days. The community's advantage is that several large Diploma campuses sit within a short drive, so arrival home is often between 15:40 and 16:15 rather than later.

Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, that puts a workable session start at 17:00 for most Al Raha Beach households and 16:30 for those closest to their campus. Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and across a full Diploma year the slots that survive are 18:00 and 18:30, because a slot that only works on a quiet week will break within a fortnight.

Session length should follow the component. Past-paper work needs ninety minutes, because the unit is a paper sat under conditions plus the marking and the marking is where most of the learning happens. Internal assessment coaching works in sixty, since the material is the student's own draft. Core process coaching on a research question can be shorter still. Choosing the duration before the purpose is a common and avoidable waste.

For context on cost, published market bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate quotes AED 180-350 for in-home, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200-450 and upwards. Those are attributed market figures rather than our prices, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

sections.heading: Two checks that apply to whoever you hire
paragraphs: Whatever the coverage answer turns out to be, two pieces of due diligence are the same for every provider and both are quick. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit is free and quick, an independent tutor without one has no cost excuse, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified and should be treated that way. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal category requiring an educational services permit for a training institute.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point that matters here more than elsewhere, because this community sits beside several large campuses. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as exact policy wording, and we do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school.

The second check concerns standing. Regulator approval is a numbered permit rather than an adjective. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. We name those bodies to explain what they govern. Any provider claiming otherwise about itself is making a statement you can ask them to evidence.

faqs.question: Is there an IB specialist living near Al Raha Beach for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and that is the honest answer rather than a discouraging one. Al Raha Beach sits close to several large Diploma campuses, but proximity to a school is not proximity to a subject specialist. The number of adults within a short drive who teach, say, Diploma Economics at higher level every week and know how the portfolio commentaries are marked is small. Filter by subject and level rather than by postcode and the pool is deep; filter by distance and it is nearly empty.

faqs.question: Which IB Diploma subjects are genuinely hard to staff?

The arts are thinner still, particularly for internal assessment coaching. Those are scarce everywhere, not only in this community.

faqs.question: Why is a Diploma tutor harder to find than an IGCSE one?

Higher level in a subject is a smaller cohort again, and a specific route smaller still. And every Diploma subject has an internal assessment with its own criteria, so a tutor needs assessment knowledge as well as content knowledge, and those are separate competencies that a long career teaching the subject elsewhere does not supply.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows my child's Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions. What is the internal assessment in this subject called, and what are its criteria with their mark allocations? Which papers does my child sit at this level and how are they weighted? What is the word limit on the internal component? And where do candidates at this level most often lose marks, and in which component? A specialist answers all four without hesitating. A generalist answers in terms of topics, effort and confidence.

faqs.question: What are the possible answers when a Diploma subject cannot be staffed?
faqs.answer: One of three things, all stated plainly. A waiting time, usually a week or two, often with a later evening slot available sooner. A partial match, where we cover the content but not the internal assessment or the reverse, and we say which. Or an honest no, in which case you get the subject, level and component written out so you can look elsewhere with precise information. We would rather lose an enquiry than take a fee for approximate teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches the subject also coach the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and this is the check families most often skip. A teacher with ten years in a non-IB system knows the chemistry and may never have seen how a scientific investigation's evaluation strand is marked. The criteria, their mark allocations and the common failures are a separate body of knowledge. Ask specifically whether they have coached that component and what its criteria are, rather than assuming subject expertise covers it.

faqs.question: What exactly does the mathematics exploration get marked on?
faqs.answer: Five criteria totalling twenty marks: presentation at four, mathematical communication at four, personal engagement at three, reflection at three, and use of mathematics at six. The last of those rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the course, which means an elegant piece pitched below the student's own course level cannot reach the top band however well written it is. A tutor who knows that will say so; one who does not will praise the mathematics and miss the ceiling.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send Diploma tutors to Al Raha Beach addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. On a page about coverage that is the whole reason an answer of yes is ever possible: the pool is a professional population rather than the set of people willing to drive to this community in the late afternoon.

faqs.question: Should I ask my child's school before looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and especially in a scarce subject. Every Diploma student has a supervisor for the Extended Essay and a subject teacher responsible for internal assessment guidance, both included in fees and both carrying accountability. In a language B or arts subject that is hard to staff externally, the school's teacher may be the only person within reach with the relevant assessment knowledge. For missed content the class teacher also knows exactly what was covered.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches at my child's school a good option?
faqs.answer: Not one we will arrange. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than exact policy wording, and either way we do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session start for an Al Raha Beach family?
faqs.answer: Earlier than for most Abu Dhabi communities, because several large Diploma campuses are a short drive away. Taught days finish between about 14:45 and 15:30, arrival home is often between 15:40 and 16:15, and allowing three quarters of an hour at home that makes 17:00 workable for most households and 16:30 for those closest to their campus. Our range runs 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and 18:00 and 18:30 are the slots that survive a full year.

faqs.question: How long should a Diploma session be?
faqs.answer: Let the component decide. Past-paper work needs ninety minutes, because the unit is a paper sat under genuine conditions plus the marking afterwards, and the marking is where most of the learning happens. Internal assessment coaching works well in sixty, since the material under discussion is the student's own draft. Core process coaching on a research question can be shorter again. Choosing a duration before choosing a purpose wastes part of every session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay if we already have a supervisor?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a supplement rather than a substitute. The school supervisor knows the internal deadlines, has seen previous cohorts and carries accountability. A tutor adds time: testing whether a research question is answerable within 4,000 words, explaining what each criterion rewards, teaching research and referencing skills, and giving feedback on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the essay, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion or supply text.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list every subject as available?
faqs.answer: Because that would not be true, and an undisclosed coverage limit is the norm in this market rather than the exception. No competitor page we examined discloses one at all, and several conceal the fact that delivery is not local. Stating which groups are deep, which are thin and where the answer is a refusal is more useful to a parent than a list of everything, and it is the only version of the claim we can stand behind.

faqs.question: What is the first message I should send about a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Five things: the subject, the level, which component is the problem, the campus your child attends, and the time they are realistically home. Add one marked paper or draft and the first session can open with teaching. Those five facts let us answer the coverage question honestly in one reply, and they are also exactly what any other provider needs in order to give you a truthful answer rather than a reassuring one.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-beach.closingHeading: Ask for the coverage answer, not the reassurance
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-beach.closingBody: Send the subject, the level and the component, and ask directly whether that combination can be staffed and by when. A provider who answers with a date, a partial match or an honest no is telling you something; one who answers yes to everything is matching on subject name alone. IB Gram teaches Abu Dhabi Diploma students one-to-one over live video, matches content and assessment knowledge separately, writes the detail back to you when we cannot help, and starts with a free trial lesson and no card details taken.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-garde.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are grouped by the Diploma stage they are most useful in: DP1 foundations, internal assessment feedback, and the final-term component work. A tutor who is excellent in one of those three is not automatically the right choice in another.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Parents in Al Raha Gardens usually search for a tutor in one of two months: October of DP1, after the first set of internal grades, or February of DP2, when the deadline season has visibly overwhelmed the household. Both are late. The Diploma's structure is known from the first week of DP1, and the decisions that matter are made eight to fourteen months before the exam window rather than eight weeks before it.

The reason is the coursework. Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, usually worth something in the region of 20% of the subject grade, and those deadlines are set by your child's school rather than by the IB. They do not fall evenly. They cluster, and in most schools the cluster lands in the second half of DP1 and the first half of DP2, colliding with the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the mock examinations. A student can be entirely on top of the taught content and still lose a grade to that collision.

Which means a tutoring plan has two distinct jobs with different timings. The first is content: making sure the taught syllabus is secure, which belongs in DP1 and the early part of DP2. The second is component work: internal assessment feedback, Paper 3 at Higher Level, and timed-paper technique, which belongs in defined blocks near the relevant deadlines. Buying one hour a week continuously for two years does both jobs badly and costs more than doing them in sequence.

The honest position on exam dates is that no specific IB session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so rather than publish a date that might be wrong for your child's school, the instruction is to take the exam window, the results date and all internal deadlines from your child's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. What can be stated safely is the shape of the calendar, and the shape is what a plan is built from.

There is one more reason the calendar matters more here than it would in a British or American system. A Diploma grade is assembled from several components submitted at different points, so a weak month is preserved in the final result rather than averaged away by a strong one later. A rushed internal assessment stays rushed.

On delivery, IB Gram is plain. Tuition for Al Raha Gardens families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The market for an in-home visit in Abu Dhabi is real and runs roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's rate work, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, and the section below sets out what that premium does and does not buy during the Diploma's busiest weeks. abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-garde.programmesIntro: Al Raha Gardens sits beside established IB continuum provision, so families here often follow the whole programme sequence. Each stage has its own calendar pressure, and knowing which one you are in determines what tuition should be doing.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with the exhibition in the final year as the first substantial independent project a student undertakes. There is no examination calendar, which makes the PYP the one stage where tuition timing barely matters and consistency matters a great deal. The transferable skills are reading stamina, number fluency and the habit of recording method.
programmes.countryNote: Al Raha Gardens is a villa community with a short school run, so primary-age sessions can start earlier than in the apartment communities nearby. The sensible use of money at this stage is short frequent practice rather than a weekly hour, which is the opposite of how most families buy.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed across four criteria per subject, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 as the major independent piece and an eAssessment option at the end. The calendar pressure here is the Personal Project, which runs alongside normal coursework and is the first time a student has to manage a long deadline without weekly checkpoints.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP 5 to DP1 transition is the highest-value tutoring window in the whole sequence and the one Al Raha Gardens families most often miss. Work done in the summer between them, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, removes most of the October crisis in DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internal assessment. Higher Level subjects demand more taught content and, in several subjects, an additional paper. The calendar is the defining difficulty rather than any single subject.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma cohorts in the Al Raha corridor are large enough that schools run structured internal deadline calendars, which is useful: a parent can obtain the whole year's dates in one request. That document is the single most valuable input to a tutoring plan and is rarely asked for.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study and the Personal and Professional Skills core, plus a reflective project. The calendar is different from the Diploma's: the reflective project and the career-related study carry their own deadlines, and the smaller number of DP courses changes how the exam term is shaped.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Abu Dhabi is limited to a small number of campuses, so a student may be one of very few in their year taking a particular DP course within the programme. Online matching is the practical answer, because the local pool for a single-course specialism is effectively empty.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-garde.subjectsIntro: Each Diploma subject below is listed with the component that drives its calendar, because that is what determines when tuition should be bought rather than what it should cover.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Exploration drives the DP1 calendar; Paper 3 drives the final term at Higher Level. Topic choice for the Exploration should be settled before DP2 starts, because a weak topic cannot be rescued by good writing later.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Explorations here usually need a real dataset, which has to be sourced early or the project stalls. The Higher Level matrices and graph theory content arrives late in most schemes of work, which makes it the standard final-term gap.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internal assessment investigation needs apparatus and time, so it is timetabled by the school rather than chosen freely. Students lose marks in the evaluation section, which is written last and usually in a hurry.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics arrive at different points in different schemes of work, and the internal assessment needs a defensible uncertainty treatment. The final-term gap is almost always the Higher Level extension topics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content volume spread across the whole two years, which makes a late start punishing. The internal assessment rewards a tightly controlled investigation; ambitious designs produce data that cannot be analysed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written tasks are internally scheduled and under-rehearsed almost universally. Higher Level adds the essay, which needs a text studied in enough depth to sustain an argument without quotation hunting.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries based on published news articles, spread across the two years, which means the deadlines are staggered rather than clustered. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that reward mathematical fluency.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The internal assessment differs between the levels and requires either primary or secondary research, which has to be planned early. Case-study reading discipline is the difference between a 5 and a 7 in the final papers.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is a defined-length individual piece with a research question that must be narrow enough to answer. Higher Level adds a regional option with its own content load arriving late in DP2.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, both internally deadlined. The essay is where students lose most, because they treat a knowledge question as a general opinion prompt rather than an argument about how claims are justified.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A supervised independent piece with school-set checkpoints. The research question is the whole battle; a poor question produces a weak essay regardless of effort. It should be settled before DP2 begins.

subjects.name: Languages: Spanish, French and Arabic B
subjects.description: The individual oral is internally assessed and scheduled by the school, often earlier than students expect. Thin local specialist supply at Higher Level makes this the group where online matching matters most.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, counted backwards from the exam window
paragraphs: Start at the exam series and walk backwards, because that is the only direction in which the calendar makes sense. Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates sit the May session. Everything else is positioned relative to it, and the positions are set by the school rather than by the IB, which is why the first thing a family should obtain is the school's own internal deadline calendar for the year.

Working back from the exam window, the final term is for timed papers and the components the school reached last. Before that sits the mock cycle, which in most schools lands a term ahead of the series. Before that, the internal assessment and core deadlines cluster: Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay, and most subject internal assessments. Before that again, in the second half of DP1, sit the first drafts, the Extended Essay research question, and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition.

What this ordering reveals is that the second half of DP1 is the busiest unrecognised period in the Diploma. Students experience DP2 as the hard year and it is, but most of the decisions that determine DP2's difficulty are taken in DP1: the Exploration topic, the Extended Essay question, the subject and level combination, and whether a content backlog has been allowed to form. Tuition bought in DP1 is cheaper and more effective than tuition bought in DP2 for exactly that reason.

The table below is the shape rather than the dates. No specific IB exam or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a date published wrongly is worse than no date. Ask your child's IB coordinator for the school's calendar, write the fixed points into it, and plan the tutoring blocks into the gaps rather than across them.

sections.heading: Internal assessment deadlines: what lands when, and why they collide
paragraphs: Internal assessments are the part of the Diploma that parents understand least and that costs the most grades. Each subject has one, weightings are commonly in the region of 20%, and every one of them is deadlined internally by the school so that marks and samples can be submitted on time. A student taking six subjects therefore has six pieces of substantial individual work, plus the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

They collide because schools set their internal deadlines to meet one external submission window. That compresses everything into a few weeks regardless of how evenly the work could in principle have been spread. A student who began each piece when it was set will meet the cluster comfortably. A student who began each piece when it was due will meet all eight at once, which is the single commonest reason an Al Raha Gardens family starts looking for a tutor in February of DP2.

Economics is the exception worth knowing about, because its three commentaries are set at intervals across the two years rather than as one piece. That makes it the subject where falling behind is most visible earliest, and a useful early warning signal for a parent watching for drift elsewhere.

The practical move is to ask the school for the full internal deadline calendar at the start of each year, put all of it in one place, and look for the weeks with three or more deadlines in them. Those weeks are when a student needs time rather than teaching, and they are the weeks in which a standing weekly tutoring slot is worth least. Move the hours to the fortnight before instead.

sections.heading: What a home tutor can and cannot do during deadline season
paragraphs: Al Raha Gardens is a villa community with gated access, and a visiting tutor's evening is shaped by the drive and the gate as much as by the lesson. The market rate for an in-home one-to-one visit in Abu Dhabi runs roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's rate work, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The difference is the journey, and during deadline season the journey is the problem rather than the cost.

What deadline season needs is short, frequent and reactive contact. A student with an Exploration draft due on Thursday benefits from twenty-five minutes on Tuesday evening and twenty minutes on Wednesday, not from a fixed ninety-minute slot on Saturday. A visiting arrangement cannot economically deliver that, because nobody drives to Al Raha Gardens for twenty-five minutes. An online arrangement can, and that is a genuine structural advantage rather than a marketing point.

The case for a person in the room remains real and is worth stating. Younger students, and students who disengage the moment a screen appears, work better with someone present. Supervision is easier and written work on paper is easier to see. For a Diploma student working on a research question or a Paper 3 problem, those advantages matter less than the ability to share a screen, annotate a draft live and rewatch a worked solution.

IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. Being explicit about that is more useful to a family in deadline season than a vague promise, because the worst outcome is a parent discovering at the booking stage that what they thought they had arranged does not exist.

sections.heading: The mock cycle, and how to read mock results properly
paragraphs: Mocks in most schools sit a term ahead of the exam series, and they are the most misused piece of information in the Diploma. A family receives a set of grades and treats them as a prediction. The grades are the least useful part of the document. What matters is the distribution of lost marks across topics and components, and that information is in the papers rather than in the summary.

Reading them properly takes about an hour and is the highest-value thing a parent can do with a mock. Go through each paper and sort every lost mark into one of three categories: content not known, method known but not shown, and nothing wrong except time. The three categories need completely different responses, and a tutoring block aimed at the wrong one is money spent on the wrong problem.

Content gaps are the easiest to fix and the least common at this stage. Method losses, where a student knew what to do but did not write the step the mark scheme needed, are the biggest single cluster across most subjects and respond to a handful of sessions on presentation. Time losses, where the last questions are unattempted, are a technique problem that needs timed practice rather than more teaching, and a student who does not practise under time will not fix it by understanding more.

The mock cycle also sets the honest answer to the question every family asks in the final term. Eight weeks can change technique, close two or three named topic gaps, and substantially improve attempt rate. Eight weeks cannot rebuild two years of missing content, and a provider who suggests otherwise is selling reassurance. The table sets out what each window can realistically carry.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS on the same calendar
paragraphs: The core is where the Diploma calendar genuinely differs from any other qualification, and it is the part families plan for last. Theory of Knowledge carries an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word supervised independent piece. Creativity, Activity, Service runs across both years with its own reflections and a project. None of these is examined in the May series and all of them have internal deadlines that compete with the ones that are.

The Extended Essay is the one where early action changes the outcome most. The research question determines almost everything: whether the essay can be answered in 4,000 words, whether sources exist, and whether the subject's own assessment criteria can be met. A question settled before DP2 begins leaves a clear run at the research. A question still being revised in DP2 term two guarantees a rushed essay regardless of the student's ability.

Theory of Knowledge fails for a consistent reason. Students treat a knowledge question as an invitation to give an opinion, when the task is an argument about how claims come to be justified within and across areas of knowledge. That is a skill rather than a body of content, and it is learnable in a small number of focused sessions, which makes it unusually good value for money if those sessions happen before the essay is drafted rather than after.

A tutor's role across all three is strictly bounded. They may discuss a research question, explain a published criterion, teach a method the student has chosen to use, and respond to the student's own draft with questions. They may not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text, or hand over a model to adapt. Submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, including the loss of the Diploma.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the school run and when a session actually fits
paragraphs: Scheduling matters more in the Diploma than at any other stage, because the student has less slack. Al Raha Gardens has an advantage here that the apartment communities nearby do not: the school run is short, and students are frequently home early enough for a 4.15pm start. In Al Raha Beach, Khalifa City and Al Reef the realistic window opens later, which is worth knowing if you are coordinating siblings in different schools.

Ramadan reshapes the evening entirely, and the UAE school day shortens during it. The arrangement needs deciding before the month starts rather than renegotiated weekly. Post-Iftar sessions suit many Diploma students, who find the quiet late evening their most productive concentrated stretch of the year. Others do better having the block suspended and resumed afterwards. The cost of indecision is a slot cancelled four weeks running, which is the one kind of spending with no educational return.

The summer between MYP 5 and DP1, and the summer between DP1 and DP2, are the two most under-used windows in the Diploma calendar. Bridging work in mathematics and the sciences before DP1 removes most of the October content crisis. Extended Essay reading between DP1 and DP2 removes most of the February panic. Hours bought in those windows cost the same as hours bought in term time and are worth considerably more, because nothing else is competing.

Where a family travels between Abu Dhabi and abroad during holidays, online delivery on a stated time zone means the schedule follows them rather than pausing. For a Diploma student in DP2 that continuity is worth real marks, because a four-week gap in February lands exactly where the coursework cluster does.

sections.heading: Getting started, with the calendar in hand
paragraphs: The first thing to send is not a description of the problem but the school's internal deadline calendar, together with the subject and level combination and the most recent marked work. Those three documents let a tutor say which weeks the hours should go into, which is a more useful answer than a general offer of weekly support.

The first lesson is a free trial with no card details collected. Use it as an audition and ask three questions afterwards. Which component would you work on first, and why that one. Which week of our school calendar is the worst week to book a session, and what would you do instead. And what do you want to see from the next mock. A tutor who answers those in specifics is reading the calendar; one who answers in generalities is not.

Matching takes a couple of working days for Diploma subjects with deep supply, which includes Analysis and Approaches, the main sciences, English A and Economics. It takes longer for Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, for language B courses at Higher Level, and for subjects taught to very small cohorts. Where nobody suitable is free we give a waiting date, disclose a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, or say we cannot cover it well.

What you should expect in return is a plan with dates in it rather than a standing slot. Blocks are proposed against named components and named weeks, with a review at the end of each term asking whether the thing the block was bought for actually closed. That discipline is the whole argument of this page: in a two-year programme with fixed hard weeks, when the hours are spent matters as much as how many of them there are.

process.title: Get the school's internal deadline calendar
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the whole year's internal deadlines in one document. This is the single most valuable input to a tutoring plan and the thing almost no family requests. Mark the weeks with three or more deadlines; those are the weeks to keep clear.

process.title: Send the subjects, levels and last marked work
process.description: The subject and level combination tells a tutor where the content load sits. The most recent marked paper or internal assessment draft shows where the marks are actually going. Together they replace a page of description with evidence.

process.title: Take the free trial and ask three calendar questions
process.description: Which component first and why. Which week of our calendar is the worst to book, and what instead. What do you want to see from the next mock. Specific answers mean a tutor who plans; general answers mean one who fills slots. No card details are collected for the trial.

process.title: Book blocks against named weeks
process.description: Hours attached to a component and a window rather than an open weekly slot: a feedback clinic before the school's draft deadline, a Paper 3 block in the final term, a bridging block in the summer. Each block has a defined end.

process.title: Review at the end of each term against the plan
process.description: Did the component the block was bought for actually improve. If yes, the hours move to the next fixed point on the calendar. If no, the approach changes rather than the schedule continuing unchanged. This is also the moment to request a different tutor.

whyPoints.title: Planned around your school's calendar, not a generic one
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and draft dates are set by your child's school. We ask for that calendar first and build blocks into its gaps, because hours spent in a three-deadline week are worth very little.

whyPoints.title: No unverified IB dates published
whyPoints.description: The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so this page publishes no IB exam or results date. We tell you to take them from your coordinator or ibo.org. A wrong date a parent acts on is worse than no date at all.

whyPoints.title: Short, frequent contact when the week needs it
whyPoints.description: Deadline season needs twenty minutes twice in a week rather than ninety minutes on Saturday. Online delivery makes that economic, which is a structural advantage of the format rather than a sales point.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the core
whyPoints.description: Tutors discuss research questions, explain criteria and respond to the student's own drafts with questions. They do not write, complete or supply any part of an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment. The qualification belongs to the student.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Al Raha Gardens families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Nothing here implies a tutor arrives at a villa.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years should we actually start paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and in DP1 rather than DP2. The decisions that set DP2's difficulty are taken in DP1: the Exploration topic, the Extended Essay research question, the subject and level combination, and whether a content backlog is allowed to form. A fortnightly arrangement through DP1 that keeps the taught syllabus secure costs less and achieves more than a weekly slot bought in February of DP2, when the student has coursework deadlines competing for the same hours and no slack left to absorb new teaching.

faqs.question: Why do all my child's internal assessment deadlines land in the same few weeks?
faqs.answer: Because the school sets its internal deadlines to meet a single external submission window, which compresses eight substantial pieces of work into a short period regardless of how evenly they could have been spread. A student taking six subjects has six internal assessments plus the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. The way through it is to obtain the full internal deadline calendar at the start of the year, identify the weeks holding three or more deadlines, and treat those weeks as time to be protected rather than filled.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Al Raha Gardens?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for UAE families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma student the online format also suits the work better during deadline season, because twenty minutes on a draft twice in one week is straightforward to schedule online and is not economic for anyone driving to a gated villa community for a single short session.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with the mock papers once the grades come back?
faqs.answer: Ignore the grade and read the papers. Sort every lost mark into three categories: content not known, method known but not written down, and nothing wrong except time. Those need different responses, and most families buy tutoring aimed at the wrong one. Method losses are usually the largest cluster and respond to a handful of sessions on presentation. Time losses need timed practice rather than more teaching. Content gaps are the easiest to fix and, by the mock stage, usually the smallest of the three.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks before the exams. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but worth being honest about what eight weeks carries. In that window you can rebuild exam technique, raise attempt rate, and close two or three named topic gaps in one subject. You cannot rebuild a Higher Level syllabus that was never secure, and nobody should tell you otherwise. The most productive eight-week plan is narrow: one subject, two named topics drawn from the mock analysis, and a full timed paper every week reviewed the same day it is sat.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay research question be settled?
faqs.answer: Before DP2 begins, and the reason is structural rather than motivational. The research question determines whether the essay can be answered within 4,000 words, whether sources exist to answer it, and whether the subject's assessment criteria can be met at all. A question settled in the summer between the two years leaves a clear run at the research. A question still being revised in DP2 term two produces a rushed essay regardless of how capable the student is, because the remaining time is already committed to subject coursework.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Read it and respond to it with questions, yes. Write, rewrite, edit it to completion or supply text for it, no. The Extended Essay must be the student's own work, and submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under IB rules with consequences that fall on the student, including the loss of the Diploma. What a tutor can usefully do is ask whether the question has actually been answered, point at a criterion the draft does not yet meet, and challenge a claim that the sources do not support.

faqs.question: Why do students lose so many marks on the Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: Because they answer a knowledge question as though it were an opinion prompt. The task is an argument about how claims come to be justified within and across areas of knowledge, supported by examples that are examined rather than listed. That is a skill rather than a body of content, which is good news: it is learnable in a small number of focused sessions. The condition is that those sessions happen before the essay is drafted. Feedback on a finished essay that was built on the wrong premise can only ever be partial.

faqs.question: Does tutoring stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It does not have to, and the decision should be made before the month starts rather than week by week. The UAE school day shortens during Ramadan and the evening changes shape completely. Post-Iftar sessions suit many Diploma students, who find the quiet late evening their most productive concentrated time of the year. Others do better with the block suspended and resumed afterwards, particularly if they are fasting and also sitting mocks. What wastes money is a standing slot cancelled four weeks in a row.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the summer between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: Extended Essay reading and the Exploration or investigation topic, in that order. Both are decisions rather than content, and both are far cheaper to get right in July than to repair in February. A short block of five or six hours spread across the summer, aimed at narrowing a research question and testing whether sources exist to answer it, removes the single biggest cause of a DP2 crisis. Content revision in the same window is lower value, because nothing has been forgotten yet and DP2 will revisit it anyway.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session start for a student in Al Raha Gardens?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most of the emirate. Al Raha Gardens has the corridor's shortest school run for families using the school on its doorstep, so a 4.15pm start is realistic on a weekday. Students commuting from here to Khalifa City or the island campuses land later, closer to 5pm. Because lessons run over live video, the buffer needed is the walk from the car to a desk rather than the half hour a visiting tutor would require, which is what makes the earlier slot usable at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor outside Abu Dhabi work to the internal deadlines my school sets?
faqs.answer: They will if you send them. School internal deadlines, draft dates and mock windows are set by your child's school rather than by the IB, so a tutor takes them from the calendar you provide in the first session and plans around them. What the tutor brings from outside is subject and component knowledge, which the IB sets and which does not vary by country. Where an IB Gram tutor is based outside the UAE we disclose it before you book, and lessons are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: How many hours should a Diploma subject need across the two years?
faqs.answer: There is no honest general figure, and a provider quoting one is guessing at your child. What is predictable is the distribution. A subject that is fundamentally secure needs a short block near each major component: a feedback clinic at the internal assessment draft stage and an intensive in the final term, perhaps fifteen hours in total. A subject with a real content gap needs maintenance through DP1 as well, which roughly doubles it. The figure to resist is an open weekly slot across both years with no defined endpoint.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We say which of three things is true. Either there is a waiting time with an actual date on it, or there is a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, which we disclose before you book rather than conceal behind a phone number, or we cannot cover it well and say so. The third answer loses us the booking. Supply is thinnest for Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level and for language B courses at Higher Level.

faqs.question: Should we book a weekly slot for the whole Diploma or buy blocks?
faqs.answer: Blocks, in almost every case. A weekly slot across two years is easy to set up, hard to evaluate, and tends to outlive the problem it was bought for because nobody cancels it. Blocks attached to named components and named weeks are comparable, reviewable and cheaper in total: a bridging block before DP1, maintenance through DP1 at fortnightly intervals, a feedback clinic at each internal assessment draft deadline, and a component intensive in the final term. Each one has a defined end and something specific to check against.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raha-garde.closingBody: An IB home tutor in Al Raha Gardens is worth most when the hours are placed on the Diploma calendar rather than scattered across it. Ask your IB coordinator for the school's internal deadline document, send it with the subject and level combination and the most recent marked work, and we will propose blocks against named components and named weeks. The first lesson is a free trial with no card details collected, and the right question to ask afterwards is which week of your calendar the tutor would keep clear. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Three districts, three quotes, one educational answer
paragraphs: Al Rawdah sits in the middle of Abu Dhabi island, bordered by Al Mushrif and Al Karamah, a short run from the main school corridor. Ask three agencies for an in-home Diploma tutor at an Al Rawdah address, then ask the same three for an address ten minutes away, and the quotes will differ. Nothing about the Diploma differs. The same courses, the same papers, the same internal assessment deadlines, the same places marks are lost. What differs is the drive, and once that is visible the comparison a parent is actually making becomes clear.

That is why this page is built as a comparison rather than as a description. You already know what Al Rawdah looks like. What is harder to find out is the published market rate for an in-home visit against an online specialist, what a travel premium buys, whether the tutor in front of you is permitted to work, and whether the pool of people willing to drive here on a Tuesday evening actually contains anyone who has taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level. Those four questions have answers, and they do not change between Al Rawdah and Al Karamah.

Set the published bands side by side. In-home one-to-one tuition in this market is advertised at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, on Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The gap between the columns is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour, and that gap is the journey. For a central district like Al Rawdah the journey is short, which is precisely why the premium is harder to justify here than it would be for a family out past Al Samha.

The second comparison matters more and gets discussed less. An in-home tutor is drawn from the set of adults who will travel to your address at the hour you need. An online tutor is drawn from the set of adults who have taught your child's course. For a popular Standard Level subject those two sets overlap. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, for Diploma Physics internal assessments, or for Economics commentaries built on current articles, they often do not overlap at all, and no amount of convenience compensates for a tutor learning the course alongside the student.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page will not imply otherwise to match a search phrase. What we deliver into Al Rawdah is live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time: a shared whiteboard, work annotated on the screen both people are reading, a session that starts at the minute it was booked, and a recording the student can replay before the homework. The comparison above is the argument for it, and a parent is entitled to make that comparison with real numbers rather than slogans.
