abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawdah.programmesIntro: The three IB programmes below each change what a tutor is being asked to do. A parent comparing formats should know which programme their child is in, because the case for a specialist strengthens sharply as the student moves up.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects over two years, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Most subjects carry an internal assessment worth a substantial share of the grade, and the school sets the draft deadlines. Subject grades run 1 to 7 and feed a 45-point total with up to three core points.
programmes.countryNote: This is where format stops being a matter of taste. A Diploma student needs a tutor who has taught their specific course at their specific level, and in Abu Dhabi that person is frequently not within driving distance of Al Rawdah. A family insisting on an in-home arrangement for Higher Level work is choosing from a smaller pool, which is a real trade-off rather than a neutral preference.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked 0 to 8, with a Personal Project in the final year. There is no terminal external paper in the school-assessed route, so support is about securing understanding and communication rather than examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: For MYP the local pool is broader, because the subject demand is less specialised. This is the stage where an in-home arrangement is easiest to defend on its own terms, particularly for a younger or easily distracted student, and a parent in Al Rawdah choosing that route is not making a mistake.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led learning across transdisciplinary units with no external examinations. Any support at this stage is about fluency, reading and confidence, and the honest position is that most primary students do not need a paid tutor at all.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Rawdah primary family does want help, short and infrequent beats weekly and open-ended. Be sceptical of a two-year plan sold for a nine-year-old, and more sceptical of a premium hourly rate attached to it.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rawdah.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the Diploma courses Al Rawdah families most often ask about, with the part of each that a general tutor struggles to cover. This is the list that decides whether proximity or specialism wins for your child.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, proof and calculus, with a no-calculator Paper 1 and an Exploration worth 20%. Higher Level adds complex numbers, induction and differential equations. A tutor who has not taught AA HL cannot usefully prepare a student for Paper 3, which carries a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, data and statistics with technology permitted throughout, extending at Higher Level into chi-squared testing, the Poisson distribution and hypothesis testing. Explorations here usually rest on a real data set, so data-source checking is part of the work from the first week.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields and nuclear physics, with an individual investigation. Uncertainty handling and graph treatment carry marks students rarely practise, and the gap between calculating a value and explaining a mechanism is where Higher Level grades separate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry, with an individual investigation. Organic reaction pathways and the mathematics inside equilibrium problems generate the most requests. An investigation question chosen too broadly cannot produce usable data in the time allowed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where command terms decide marks: describe, explain, outline, evaluate and discuss each want a different structure. Students who know the biology and write the wrong shape of answer lose marks that look mysterious on a report card.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with internal assessment commentaries built on published news articles. Diagram marks are routinely forfeited through missing labels, and article selection is itself a skill with a deadline attached.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools and theories applied to real organisations, with a research project at Higher Level. The common failure is description where analysis and evaluation were asked for, which is a writing problem rather than a knowledge problem and responds well to feedback on the student's own work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis, a learner portfolio and oral components fixed in the school calendar. The most common waste of tutoring hours is reading additional texts instead of practising timed analysis of the ones already studied.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with a simple experimental study as internal assessment. Marks are lost in methodology and ethics sections rather than in content, and that is teachable quickly by someone who has marked them before.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Worth up to three points on the 45-point total, and run on interim deadlines set by the school. Support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts; no part of either may be written for a student, and the supervisor signs to that effect.

sections.heading: The straight answer about home tutoring in Al Rawdah
paragraphs: In-home Diploma tutoring exists in Al Rawdah and plenty of families use it. The published market rate is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, on Bestimate's figures of AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages advertised in this market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Those are real options and a parent choosing one is not being foolish.

What IB Gram offers is not that. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our delivery into Al Rawdah is live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. Saying this plainly near the top of the page is deliberate, because the alternative is letting a parent read three screens of persuasion before discovering the format.

The case for the online format is not primarily price, although it usually is cheaper. It is the size of the pool. An in-home tutor is selected from the adults who will drive to Al Rawdah at five on a weekday. An online tutor is selected from the adults who have taught the course. For Standard Level Business Management those groups may overlap; for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or a Physics internal assessment, they frequently do not, and course experience is not a quality a short drive can substitute for.

There is one thing an in-home tutor does better and it deserves saying. Physical presence holds the attention of a young or distractible student in a way a screen does not, and it reads a page over a shoulder without being asked. For a Primary Years student that can be decisive. For a DP2 student working Paper 3 under timing, the decisive factor is whether the tutor has marked that paper before.

paragraphs: The three districts share housing types, school catchments and traffic patterns. A Diploma student in any of them is likely to attend one of the same handful of schools, meet the same internal assessment deadlines, and lose marks in the same places. On the educational questions the comparison returns identical answers, which is worth knowing before paying a premium framed as local knowledge.

Where differences appear, they are operational. Al Rawdah's position between two neighbours makes journeys short in both directions. Al Mushrif's school density means a tutor can sometimes chain two visits, which occasionally shows up as a slightly lower quote. Al Karamah behaves almost identically to Al Rawdah. Push further out, to Al Bateen or across the bridge to Al Reem, and the journey lengthens enough to change both the price and the reliability of the start time.

A parent can test this directly. Request an in-home quote for your own address and for a friend's address in the next district, with the same subject, level and session length. If the two differ by more than a rounding, ask what the difference is for. The answer will be travel, and it is legitimate for a tutor to charge for their time in a car; it is just not a cost that teaches your child anything.

The practical conclusion for all three districts is the same. Decide the format on the strength of the subject match first, then on cost, then on convenience. If the best available match for your child's course happens to live in Al Mushrif and will travel, that is a good outcome. If the best match for Higher Level Chemistry does not live in Abu Dhabi at all, a short drive is not worth the downgrade.

sections.heading: What the travel premium costs in central Abu Dhabi and what it buys
paragraphs: Take the two published columns and subtract. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit is advertised at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. Across the tiers the premium works out at roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour, and at the specialist end TutorChase publishes AED 270 while Bestimate puts specialist work at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with premium examiner-led tuition reaching AED 500 to 650 and above on BartyED's published rate.

What the premium buys is a person in the room. What it does not buy is more teaching time, better course knowledge, or a wider choice of tutor. For a short central journey it is a modest sum; across a two-year Diploma at one session a week it becomes a real line in a household budget, and it is the one line that produces no learning at all.

There is also a hidden cost that does not appear in the hourly rate. A tutor travelling to Al Rawdah at 4.45pm is subject to the same traffic as everybody else, so a booked hour can start late and still end on time. Over a term, a pattern of fifteen-minute late starts is several hours of tuition paid for and not received, which no invoice ever itemises.

Two honesty notes about these figures. They are market rates read from named published sources in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson, when course, level and session length are known. And a higher rate is not evidence of a better match: premium pricing applied to a wrong diagnosis is an expensive way to reach the same gap, which is why the first lesson here is a diagnosis rather than a sales call.

sections.heading: Format against format: the factors that decide a Diploma outcome
paragraphs: A fair comparison needs more than cost. The table below sets the two formats against the factors that actually move a Diploma grade: who is available to teach, whether the session happens when it was booked, what can be reviewed afterwards, and how quickly a missed lesson is replaced. On some of these the formats are close. On tutor pool and reviewability they are not.

Reviewability is the most underrated. Most forgetting happens between the lesson and the homework, which is often two or three days later. A recording and an annotated shared document mean a student can return to the exact moment a method was explained. When a tutor leaves a house, the explanation leaves with them, and what remains is whatever the student wrote down while trying to keep up.

Replacement matters in an examination term. If a tutor is unwell in the week before a mock, an online arrangement usually finds an alternative slot with the same or another qualified tutor within days. An in-home arrangement needs someone free and able to travel, which in practice means the session is lost. Over a term that is a continuity question rather than an inconvenience.

None of this makes in-home tuition a bad choice for every family. It makes it a choice with a specific profile: better for young students who need presence, worse for specialised Higher Level work, more expensive per hour of actual teaching, and more fragile under traffic and illness. A parent in Al Rawdah who reads that profile and still prefers a person in the room has made an informed decision, which is the point of publishing it.

sections.heading: What the local pool can hold, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi is a smaller tutoring market than Dubai, and the Diploma is a narrow qualification within it. Put those together and some courses simply do not have a local in-home specialist available at the hour a family wants. Pages that imply otherwise are making a promise the market cannot keep, and a parent discovers it in week three rather than before paying.

The pattern is predictable. Standard Level mathematics, Business Management and English have the broadest coverage. Higher Level sciences narrow sharply, particularly around internal assessment season, when the same small group of specialists is in demand across every school at once. Economics commentaries, Psychology methodology and Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 are the three requests most likely to find nobody free locally.

Our position on this is to disclose it. When no specialist for a course is available, you are told, given an expected wait, and offered the alternatives in writing: another qualified tutor on the same course in a different slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course on Gulf Standard Time and disclosed before booking, shorter and more frequent sessions until the preferred slot clears, or waiting. Several competitor sites route UAE families to non-UAE numbers without mentioning it; the syllabus is the same wherever the tutor sits, but the parent should be told.

The free trial lesson is where this becomes concrete. One full lesson with the matched tutor, no card required, used to establish whether the course and level are right, where the marks are going, and whether these two people can work together. If the match is wrong we change it, and if your child needs three sessions rather than thirty you should hear that in the first conversation rather than the tenth.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the boundary that protects the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries work that must be the student's own, and the IB treats breaches as malpractice with consequences that reach the whole Diploma rather than one grade. That makes the boundary around tutoring a safety matter rather than a policy footnote, and it is one place where this SERP contains genuinely dangerous offers.

What a tutor may do is substantial. Discuss and narrow a research question. Explain a technique the student then applies themselves. Check that the mathematics or the methodology sits at the level of the course. Read a draft the student wrote and give feedback against the published criteria. Teach the difference between describing a result and evaluating it. Help a student build a working schedule so the draft is finished before the school's deadline.

What a tutor may not do is equally clear. No part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project may be produced for a student. A tutor does not supply calculations, does not rewrite paragraphs into their own words, and does not edit a piece to completion. The supervisor signs to the authenticity of the student's work, so a breach places the student's own declaration in question.

One competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A family should treat that as disqualifying rather than convenient: it exposes the student to a malpractice finding and the school to an investigation. We also do not publish or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. Those materials should be reached through the board's own site or the school.

sections.heading: Verifying an in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi before you let them in
paragraphs: If you do choose an in-home arrangement in Al Rawdah, there are checks worth making, and they are quick. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted at you is unverified and should be treated as such.

In Abu Dhabi there is one more rule. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, and in the meantime do not arrange paid private tuition with your child's own classroom teacher however convenient it appears.

Finally, be alert to borrowed authority. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring company should imply otherwise. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific thing, and it is not what an agency means when it calls its tutors regulator-approved.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, and where a parent should actually look
paragraphs: Education regulation in the UAE is emirate by emirate, and knowing which body governs your child's school saves time when something needs raising. For Al Rawdah the body is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and covers Al Ain as well as Abu Dhabi city.

Elsewhere: Dubai is regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate regulator.

There is also a federal baseline worth knowing. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the mandatory subjects that sit alongside the Diploma on your child's timetable, and it is the reason those lessons cannot simply be dropped to make room for extra Higher Level study.

The practical instruction: read inspection ratings on the regulator's own site, ask the school for its curriculum and assessment calendar in writing, and treat any claim of regulator endorsement by a tutoring company as a reason for more scepticism rather than less. These bodies publish directly, and the published version is always better than a summary on a commercial page.

intro.heading: A long bus route and a full Diploma week: what actually fits in Al Reef
paragraphs: Al Reef sits out towards the airport, and the daily consequence is distance. Most secondary students here travel out of the community for school, often towards Khalifa City and Al Raha and sometimes across to the island, and the bus that serves several villages in sequence arrives when it arrives. A realistic home-arrival range across Al Reef runs from late afternoon into the early evening depending on the route, and the family's measured arrival time is the only number worth planning a tutoring slot from.

Against that sits a Diploma week. Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with internal assessment deadlines in most of the six landing in the same two or three months. A Higher Level subject carries roughly 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard, and that difference is absorbed by evenings rather than by the timetable. Adding tutoring to this is a scheduling decision before it is an educational one.

The in-home version of this does not work well from Al Reef, and the reason is arithmetic rather than attitude. A tutor driving out here from Khalidiyah or Al Reem Island commits most of an evening to one paid hour, so they either price it accordingly or take the booking and then drop it when a client nearer home appears. Market rates for in-home one-to-one tuition in Abu Dhabi run AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 survey, with independents reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor.

Online delivery does not shorten the bus route, but it stops the bus route choosing the tutor. A household whose child is home at 17:00 can hold a slot at 17:30. A household on a longer route can hold a slot after 20:00 and keep it for a full term, because moving a session to the following evening costs nobody a journey. Both windows cost the same, which is not true when somebody has to arrive, and the pool of available teaching is the set of people who know the course rather than the set who will drive to Al Reef.

What follows is a planning guide for a Diploma household. It sets out the realistic session windows from here, what a six-subject week actually contains and where the pressure points fall, which Diploma components respond to a weekly hour and which do not, how internal assessment season is counted backwards across several subjects at once, and when the core components have to be started. IB Gram provides no home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. What reaches your child is a shared whiteboard with their own draft or script open on it, at an hour the bus does not get to vote on.

Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS sit outside the six and compete for the same evenings. The year is governed by school internal deadlines rather than by anything the board publishes, which is the single most useful thing a parent can learn early.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date that a family acts on is worse than no date. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the written internal deadline calendar at the start of Year 12; every sensible plan for the next two years is counted backwards from it.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment against four criteria per subject, graded 1 to 8, with no terminal written papers in most schools. Students arrive in the Diploma comfortable with investigation and extended writing, and underpowered on speed and accuracy under time pressure, particularly in mathematics and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: The continuum schools serving this corridor run MYP to Year 11, so a reasonable share of the local Diploma cohort has never sat a formal terminal paper before Year 12. That gap is predictable and short, and the summer before Year 12 is the cheapest time in the whole two years to close it.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: The British-track feeder, taught in this corridor as Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Students arrive with solid paper technique and procedural accuracy, and with no experience of independent assessed writing, which is why the first internal assessment and the Extended Essay feel like a different subject rather than a different task.
programmes.countryNote: Students who sat Additional Mathematics 0606 arrive with most of the Analysis and Approaches entry gap already closed. Students who sat Core tier in a subject they now want at Higher Level need honest advice in Year 11 rather than encouragement, because that conversation is far cheaper before the course selection than after it.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reef.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects as Al Reef families actually request them, with a note on where the marks are rather than a description of the course. The useful question for each is whether a weekly hour changes anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with Standard Level Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers, vectors and considerably harder calculus, and it is the hardest Diploma course to staff from any single Abu Dhabi community.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, calculator permitted throughout, with matrices and graph theory added at Higher Level. Students who chose it as the lighter option generally need statistics support rather than algebra support, which is a different tutor.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and the energetics calculations decide most grades. The internal assessment needs a research question narrow enough to generate usable data, and a topic that cannot do that caps the mark whatever the write-up looks like.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry the papers, and the usual failure is mathematical rather than conceptual. Uncertainty handling and graph analysis are routinely under-taught and quick to fix, which makes them good value for a limited number of hours.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and largely learnable alone, so paid hours are best spent on extended-response structure and on internal assessment design. A well-written report on a flawed experiment still loses the design marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide the grade, and an evaluate question answered with explanation scores a fraction of the credit. Gulf examples are legitimate, memorable and under-used by candidates in this region.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than recall, with the internal assessment requiring real organisational material. Students who write about a company without usable information spend weeks producing something the criteria cannot reward.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the individual oral carry the course. The oral rewards a global issue that is genuinely arguable, and structure is far more teachable than reading taste, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, both marked against published criteria and both routinely started too late. Almost nobody advertises it because it is nobody's degree subject, so a match takes longer than for a named subject.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words maximum, with a school supervisor. Legitimate support is narrowing the research question, interrogating method and checking referencing. The writing is the student's entirely, and that boundary is worth confirming with any provider up front.

modes.title: Weekly hour on one subject
modes.description: One fixed hour a week on the single subject where marks are most recoverable, tracking the school's scheme of work rather than a parallel syllabus. Across two years the tutor learns which topics the student rebuilds from first principles and which are memorised and brittle, and that knowledge is what makes Year 13 revision accurate rather than generic.

modes.title: Internal assessment season block
modes.description: A bounded block across the two or three months when internal assessment deadlines in several subjects land together. Work is sequenced by deadline rather than by subject importance, which is the only ordering that prevents the last deadline being met with whatever time is left over.

modes.description: Separate from subject support, because the core is where Al Reef families most often run out of time. Work is criteria coaching and question interrogation rather than content teaching, and it is scheduled early, since neither component can be rescued in its final fortnight.

sections.heading: What time a Diploma session can start from Al Reef
paragraphs: Begin with the bus rather than the bell. Schools serving this corridor finish in the middle of the afternoon, but a route that collects several Al Reef villages in sequence completes considerably later, and the airport-road traffic in the returning direction is worse than the outbound run. Across the community a realistic arrival range is late afternoon into early evening, and the only reliable figure is the one you measure yourself over five consecutive days.

That measurement decides which of two windows you are working with. If your child is consistently home by around 17:00, a 17:30 start is dependable and is the better of the two for new content, because the school lesson is still recent and the day's worksheet can be the material. If arrival regularly runs past 17:30, the honest answer is the post-20:00 window, and the content has to be chosen for it: criteria work, past-paper sections, data analysis, technique drills rather than first teaching.

What ruins arrangements here is booking the window a family would prefer rather than the one it has. A 16:30 slot chosen on an optimistic estimate gets shortened twice and cancelled twice, and by the fourth disruption the continuity that made the arrangement worth anything has gone. Because nobody travels to Al Reef for these lessons, changing a slot costs nothing and can be done in a message, which means the correct response to two cancellations is to move the hour rather than defend it.

sections.heading: What a six-subject Diploma week actually contains
paragraphs: Parents consistently underestimate the Diploma's load, and the reason is that the timetable hides it. Six subjects look comparable to eight IGCSE subjects until you notice that three of them are Higher Level, carrying roughly 240 taught hours each against 150 at Standard, and that the extra ninety hours per subject are absorbed by evenings rather than by lesson time. Then add three core components that appear on no timetable at all.

The pressure is also unevenly distributed through the year. The autumn of Year 12 is comparatively open, which is why it is the right place to put foundation work and the Extended Essay research question. The spring of Year 12 begins the internal assessment sequence. The autumn of Year 13 is the worst period in the whole programme, with several internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all converging while mock examinations approach. The spring of Year 13 is revision, by which point anything unfinished is a liability.

A tutoring plan that ignores that shape spends evenly and helps least where help is most needed. The useful pattern is light in the autumn of Year 12, one steady weekly hour through the spring, a bounded intensive block in the autumn of Year 13 aimed at internal assessment and core deadlines, and a revision block in the final term. For an Al Reef household with a long bus route, the Year 13 autumn block is also the hardest period to schedule, which is another argument for arranging it a term ahead rather than in the week it becomes urgent.

sections.heading: Which Diploma components respond to a weekly hour
paragraphs: Not every part of the Diploma improves at the same rate per hour spent, and knowing which parts do is how a family with one usable evening slot gets value out of it. The components that respond fastest share a feature: they are governed by published criteria or by a specific technique, so there is a defined target and a way to check whether it has been hit. The ones that respond slowest are broad content loads, which need the student's own study time rather than a tutor's hour.

Internal assessments respond strongly, particularly at the design stage, because a research question that cannot generate the required analysis caps the mark permanently and no later effort recovers it. One hour spent stress-testing a question is worth more than five spent improving a write-up built on a weak one. Paper technique responds strongly too: command-term discipline, showing method, timing and question selection are all trainable in a few weeks and all visible immediately in a marked script.

Content coverage responds slowly, and that is the honest answer even though it is the thing families most often ask for. A Higher Level subject's content load is too large for a weekly hour to deliver, and attempting it produces a tutor racing through material the student then has no time to consolidate. The better arrangement is for the tutor to diagnose which content gaps matter, teach the two or three that are blocking everything else, and hand the rest back as a structured study plan the student runs alone.

sections.heading: Internal assessment season, counted backwards across subjects
paragraphs: The single most useful document in a Diploma family's possession is the school's written internal deadline calendar, and most families do not have it. It lists when drafts and final submissions are due for each subject's internal assessment, and because those dates are set by the school rather than the board they are the dates that actually bind. Ask the IB coordinator for it in writing at the start of Year 12, not in the term it becomes urgent.

With that calendar, the planning is mechanical. List the deadlines in date order rather than by subject. Work backwards from each one through revision, first full draft, completed analysis, data collection and topic approval. Then look at where the backwards plans overlap, because that is where the real problem is: two subjects both needing data collection in the same fortnight, with the Extended Essay draft due in the middle of it. That collision is visible months ahead and invisible if the deadlines are only ever considered one at a time.

The sequencing rule that follows is simple and uncomfortable. Work on the earliest deadline first even when another subject feels more urgent, because a late submission is a penalty that no quality of work offsets. Where two deadlines genuinely collide, the subject whose internal assessment carries the larger share of its grade gets the better slot. For an Al Reef household this planning matters more than for a family closer in, because the available weekly hours are fewer and there is no capacity to absorb a surprise.

sections.heading: The core components, and when they have to start
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS appear on no subject timetable, carry no weekly homework, and are therefore the three things a busy Diploma student postpones. The cost of postponing them is not evenly distributed either: a late start on CAS is recoverable, a late start on the Extended Essay is expensive, and a late start on the Theory of Knowledge essay is the most common reason an otherwise strong candidate loses points in the core.

The Extended Essay is four thousand words maximum, and the research question decides most of the outcome. A question too broad produces description, a question too narrow produces no material, and both are visible at the outset to anybody who has supervised one before. The right time to settle it is the spring or summer of Year 12, when there is space to abandon a first idea. The wrong time is Year 13 autumn, when the student is committed to whatever they have and simultaneously facing several internal assessment deadlines.

The Theory of Knowledge essay, capped at sixteen hundred words, responds to a specific kind of preparation: understanding what the prescribed title is actually asking, which is rarely what it appears to ask. The exhibition commentary, capped at nine hundred and fifty words, fails most often because objects are described rather than connected to a knowledge question. Both reward criteria coaching far more than content teaching, and both are scarce as tutoring requests because Theory of Knowledge is nobody's degree subject, so a match takes longer than for a named subject. Verify every limit against the current subject guide through your coordinator.
bullets: Extended Essay: 4,000 words maximum, question settled in Year 12
Theory of Knowledge essay: 1,600 words maximum
Exhibition commentary: 950 words maximum; connect objects, do not describe them

sections.heading: In-home or online from a community this far out
paragraphs: Al Reef is the clearest case in the emirate for separating delivery from quality, because the distances make the trade-off explicit. An in-home tutor reaching here from the island or Khalidiyah is committing most of an evening to one hour, which has three consequences: the rate includes the journey, the slot is whatever suits their route rather than your bus, and the booking is vulnerable to being replaced by a client nearer their home. None of that is bad faith; it is how the economics work.

The pool is the second issue. Insisting on somebody who can reach Al Reef narrows the field to whoever lives within a workable drive and still has an evening free, and for a specific Diploma course that field can be empty. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, and chemistry tied to an internal assessment deadline are the usual cases. A family is rarely told the pool is empty; they are offered the nearest person who agrees, and the gap appears three sessions later.

The honest counter-argument is that some students genuinely need an adult in the room, and where a professional has recommended in-person support, a local tutor is the right answer and the travel premium is money well spent. For an academic Diploma subject, a shared whiteboard with the school's own material open loses very little. The way to settle it is one free hour rather than a debate, and that hour can happen tonight rather than after somebody has driven out from the Corniche.

sections.heading: What a tutor may never do with assessed work
paragraphs: The Diploma places more independent assessed work in a student's hands than any other school qualification in this market, and that makes the honesty boundary more consequential here than on the IGCSE side. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge components are all submitted as the student's own work, with declarations, and schools in this corridor run originality checks as a matter of routine. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, not on whoever supplied the text.

At least one provider visible in UAE search results advertises completed Internal Assessments at a stated price. That is not a cheaper form of tutoring; it is a transaction in which the student carries all of the risk for a mark that can be withdrawn. No tutor may write, draft, rewrite or edit to submission any part of an assessed component, at any price and under any deadline, and a provider who will not state that plainly has answered a question you then do not need to ask twice.

What remains is the thing actually worth buying, and it is substantial. Teaching what each criterion credits and how many marks it carries. Stress-testing a research question before weeks go into it. Questioning a method until the student finds the weakness themselves. Modelling an analytical technique on entirely different data so it transfers rather than being copied. Marking a draft against the descriptors and naming the criterion at risk. Checking that referencing and data provenance will survive scrutiny. All of that moves marks legitimately and leaves the work demonstrably the student's own.
bullets: Nothing assessed drafted, rewritten or edited to submission by a tutor
Criteria and mark allocations taught before drafting begins
Techniques modelled on different data so they transfer rather than copy
Drafts marked against descriptors, naming the criterion at risk

process.title: Measure the bus for a week
process.description: Note actual arrival times across five days rather than the school's finishing time. Al Reef routes serve several villages in sequence, so the gap between the first and last stop decides whether an afternoon slot is realistic or whether the evening window is the honest answer.

process.title: Get the internal deadline calendar
process.description: Ask your school's IB coordinator in writing for the internal assessment and core deadline dates. Those are the dates that bind, they usually sit a term earlier than families expect, and every plan on this page is counted backwards from them.

process.title: Name the subject and the level
process.description: Chemistry at Higher Level, or Analysis and Approaches at Standard, plus the school. Higher and Standard are different courses with different papers, and a match made on the subject name alone is the usual cause of a wasted first month.

process.title: Take the free trial hour
process.description: One hour over live video, no card details and no commitment, worked on your child's own material: a marked script, a draft, or the criteria for an upcoming internal assessment. You are testing whether the explanation lands and whether the syllabus knowledge is real.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: Compare against whatever started the plan, whether a marked paper or a draft against the criteria. If nothing has moved, the diagnosis, the subject or the tutor changes at no additional cost, which is cheaper than extending the arrangement unchanged.

whyPoints.title: Both windows at one rate
whyPoints.description: Nobody drives to Al Reef, so a 17:30 slot and a 20:30 slot cost the same and are equally available. In-home delivery from a community this far out forces every family into whichever slot the tutor's route allows, and then prices the journey into the hour.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed for Higher Level chemistry or Standard Level Analysis and Approaches specifically, because the papers and the content differ between levels. A match made on the subject name is how a family ends up paying for the wrong half of a course.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the school's own dates
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and core work is sequenced from the written internal deadline calendar rather than from the examination window, and deadline collisions across subjects are identified months ahead rather than discovered in the week they land.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what responds
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment design and paper technique respond fast to a weekly hour; broad content coverage does not. Content gaps get diagnosed and handed back as a study plan rather than delivered at a pace the student cannot consolidate.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Nothing is drafted, rewritten or edited to submission. Criteria are taught, questions stress-tested, drafts marked against descriptors. One provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the student carries that risk alone.

whyPoints.title: A free hour, tonight rather than after a drive
whyPoints.description: One trial lesson over live video, with no card details taken and no commitment created. If the match or the format is wrong, you have spent an hour instead of a term's fees, and the next match costs nothing either.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session start for a student travelling home to Al Reef?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route rather than the school. A child at a school in the immediate corridor can usually start by 16:45 or 17:00. Routes out to Khalifa City or Al Raha push that to 17:15 or 17:30. Island and Yas Island routes often mean arrival after 17:15, in which case the dependable window is after 20:00. Measure actual arrival across five days and set the slot thirty minutes after the latest of them, rather than the average, because an optimistic slot gets cancelled.

faqs.question: Is a post-dinner IB session actually productive?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the content matches the hour. A tired Diploma student can review a marked script, work through internal assessment criteria, analyse data they have already collected, or practise timing on a past-paper section. The same student cannot absorb Higher Level calculus for the first time at half past eight. Evening arrangements fail because new content is booked into them, not because the hour is late. For Al Reef households on long routes, a consistent evening slot beats an afternoon one that keeps collapsing.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: Internal assessment design, if one is coming up. A research question that cannot generate the required analysis caps the mark permanently, and one hour spent stress-testing a question is worth more than five spent improving a write-up built on a weak one. After that, paper technique: command terms, showing method, timing and question selection are all trainable within weeks and visible immediately in a marked script. Broad content coverage is the slowest and should be diagnosed and handed back as a study plan.

faqs.question: How heavy is the Diploma compared with IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Heavier than the subject count suggests. Six subjects with three at Higher Level means three courses carrying roughly 240 taught hours each against 150 at Standard, and the extra hours come out of evenings rather than lesson time. On top of that sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, none of which appear on the timetable or generate weekly homework, which is exactly why they get postponed. The autumn of Year 13 is the worst period, with internal assessments, the core and mocks converging.

faqs.question: Why do families keep missing internal assessment deadlines?
faqs.answer: Because the deadlines are considered one subject at a time. Listed in date order rather than by subject, the collisions become obvious: two subjects needing data collection in the same fortnight with an Extended Essay draft due in the middle. That is visible months ahead from the school's written internal deadline calendar and invisible without it. Ask your IB coordinator for the calendar at the start of Year 12, work backwards from each date, and then look specifically at where the backwards plans overlap.

faqs.question: How late is too late to choose an Extended Essay question?
faqs.answer: Spring or summer of Year 12, while there is still space to abandon a first idea. The question decides most of the eventual grade: too broad produces description, too narrow produces no material, and both are visible at the outset to anybody who has supervised one. Settling it in Year 13 autumn means the student is committed to whatever they have while several internal assessment deadlines land. The essay is capped at four thousand words, and planning to that limit at outline stage avoids deleting analysis later.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge from Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the sooner the better, but expect a longer wait for the right person. Theory of Knowledge is nobody's degree subject, so almost nobody advertises it and the pool is thin everywhere rather than just locally. The work is criteria coaching and interrogating what the prescribed title is actually asking, which is rarely what it appears to ask. The exhibition commentary, capped at nine hundred and fifty words, most often fails because objects are described rather than connected to a knowledge question.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel out to Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Some independent tutors do, and the market prices the journey into the hour: in-home one-to-one in Abu Dhabi runs AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 survey, with independents reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. IB Gram is not among them. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from us, and visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Al Reef lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student here need?
faqs.answer: One reliable hour on one subject suits most students for most of the two years, with density added twice: in the autumn of Year 13 when internal assessments and the core converge, and in the final revision term. Two or three parallel subject arrangements usually produce a tired student and an exhausted budget before the period that actually decides the grades. For an Al Reef household the scheduling constraint makes this easier to accept, since there is rarely room for more than one hour anyway.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP into the Diploma. What should we fix?
faqs.answer: Speed and accuracy under time pressure, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. MYP assesses against four criteria graded 1 to 8 and credits the quality of reasoning and investigation more heavily than fast, correct manipulation, so students arrive able to think about unfamiliar problems and slow at routine technique. The Diploma assumes that fluency from the first weeks. The summer before Year 12 is the cheapest time in the whole programme to close it, because nothing competes for the time.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level always mean more tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily more hours, but different ones. Higher Level carries roughly ninety extra taught hours per subject and usually an additional paper, so the content load is beyond what a weekly hour can deliver. The sensible use of tutoring at Higher Level is diagnosis and technique: identify the two or three content gaps blocking everything else, teach those, then work on the extended-response and multi-part reasoning that the additional paper demands. The rest belongs in the student's own structured study time.

faqs.question: What if an internal assessment is already late?
faqs.answer: The useful work changes from improvement to triage. A tutor can help prioritise which criteria to rescue first, which is a legitimate and genuinely valuable intervention under time pressure. What cannot happen, at any price, is anybody drafting, rewriting or editing the submission. It is submitted as the student's own work with a declaration, schools here run originality checks routinely, and a malpractice finding falls on the candidate rather than on whoever supplied the text. Speak to the school's coordinator as well, because extensions are sometimes possible.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's six subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Mathematics with physics works well, because weak algebra usually surfaces in physics before anybody connects the two. Chemistry with biology works. A science with English or a language rarely works, because the teaching skill is genuinely different. Ask which of the two the tutor has taught most recently to an examination rather than which they are comfortable with, and remember that two Higher Level subjects with one tutor still needs two separate hours.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IB tutor be matched for an Al Reef family?
faqs.answer: Mainstream subjects such as Applications and Interpretation, biology and economics usually match within a few days, because online delivery means availability is not limited to tutors willing to drive out here. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Theory of Knowledge can take a week or more, and both tighten sharply around internal assessment season when every Diploma cohort in the corridor needs help at once. You are told which case applies before the trial, along with where the tutor is based.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting support in the final term?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the aim changes. In the final term, content teaching is largely over and the useful work is timed papers, question selection, command-term discipline and the recovery of marks that are being withheld rather than missed. Take a marked mock, count the marks lost on questions where the answer was broadly right, and that figure is roughly what technique work can recover. It is a smaller ambition than a full course rescue and a far more achievable one in eight or ten weeks.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reef.closingHeading: Measure the bus, get the calendar, book one hour
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reef.closingBody: An IB home tutor in Al Reef is working against a long route and a full Diploma week, and most arrangements fail on those rather than on teaching. Measure actual arrival times for five days, ask your IB coordinator in writing for the internal deadline calendar, and name the subject and the level rather than the subject alone. Then take the free trial hour over live video, with no card details and no commitment, worked on a real script or draft. Review it honestly after four sessions.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reem-islan.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects to students in Abu Dhabi, including the Al Reem Island towers. Each works from the current subject guide for their own subject, which is what makes a session about mark allocation rather than about general confidence.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a specification, and most tutoring ignores it
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is not awarded for understanding a subject. It is awarded for what a student produces against named components with fixed weightings, assessed on published criteria using command terms that mean specific things. A student can know a subject well and score two grades below their comprehension because nobody taught them that "outline" and "explain" are different instructions carrying different marks, or that the reflection section of an internal assessment has its own criterion with its own ceiling.

That is the gap this page is about. It is the gap a tutor should be filling, and it is not the gap most tutoring fills. The default pattern is to re-teach content the school is also teaching, at the same pace, a few days behind. That feels productive, and in the first year of the Diploma it is harmless. In the second year it is the reason a family spends a great deal and sees a grade move by one point.

Al Reem Island families are well placed to act on this, because the island's Diploma cohort is concentrated and its school internal deadlines are knowable in advance. What is needed is not more hours. It is hours pointed at the right components, early enough that the published criteria can still change what the student produces rather than merely explain the mark afterwards.

The Diploma's architecture is public and worth knowing as a parent. Six subjects, three at higher level and three at standard, each assessed by a combination of external written papers and one internal assessment carried out under the school's supervision. On top sit three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and Creativity, Activity, Service. The core components are worth real points in combination, and they are the parts most often left to run themselves.

The internal assessments are where the arithmetic gets interesting. In most subjects the internal assessment carries about a fifth of the final subject grade, and in some standard level courses closer to a quarter or more. It is marked against four or five published criteria with stated mark allocations, the student has months to do it, and the criteria are available to read. A component that carries twenty per cent of a grade, with published marking criteria and no time pressure, is the most tractable thing in the whole Diploma, and it is routinely the least prepared.

The rest of this page sets out the specification detail: component weightings by subject group, where marks are lost in each, the internal assessment criteria and what each one actually rewards, the word and page limits across components, the command terms and what they demand, and how past-paper work should be run if it is going to be worth paying for. Al Reem Island scheduling sits at the end, because it is the easy part.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reem-islan.programmesIntro: Al Reem Island households reach the Diploma from several directions, and the specification knowledge a tutor needs differs sharply by stage. These are the programmes behind an IB enquiry in this part of Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years with three at higher level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject has its own guide setting out components, weightings, command terms and internal assessment criteria. Those guides are the working document of competent Diploma tutoring, and the reason a tutor should be asked which one they teach from.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, and UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no IB session or results dates. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so nothing has been confirmed from the source, and a date a parent plans around should come from the school's IB coordinator rather than from a tutoring page.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject rather than by terminal paper, with each criterion marked out of eight and described in level descriptors. A student who has never read those descriptors is guessing at what the marks are for. This is the same literacy problem as in the Diploma, encountered five years earlier and much cheaper to fix there.
programmes.countryNote: Because not every Abu Dhabi Diploma school runs the Middle Years Programme beneath it, a DP1 class in this emirate often mixes students arriving from criterion assessment with students arriving from terminal International GCSE papers. They need different first terms, and specification literacy is where the second group is usually ahead.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece with a supervisor; Theory of Knowledge is assessed by a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of around 950 words; Creativity, Activity, Service is a completion requirement with reflective evidence. The first two carry points in combination, and both are assessed against published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Abu Dhabi families most often discover a deadline late. School internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and the TOK essay sit well before the external ones, and a tutor can only coach process and give feedback on the student's own draft, which takes time the student has to be given.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines Diploma courses with a career-related study and the CP core, including reflective projects and a language development portfolio. A smaller presence in Abu Dhabi than the full Diploma, and the support profile is different: process coaching on the reflective project rather than paper technique across six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student on Al Reem Island is on the Career-related Programme rather than the full Diploma, the component list and therefore the tutoring plan change entirely. Say which programme it is in the first message, because the two are not interchangeable.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-reem-islan.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, written from the specification rather than the prospectus. Each entry names what the internal assessment is and where the component marks sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at standard level weighted 40 per cent each; three at higher level weighted 30, 30 and 20. The exploration carries 20 per cent and is marked out of twenty across five criteria. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which is the component where classwork and exam performance diverge most.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same paper structure and the same exploration weighting as Analysis and Approaches, with a calculator permitted throughout. Marks are lost for giving a numerical answer without interpreting it in the context the question set, which is a criterion-level failure rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Written papers carry the large majority of the grade, with the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Command terms do most of the damage here: "outline" and "explain" carry different marks for the same knowledge, and students write the long answer to the short instruction and the reverse.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the quantitative and reasoning load. The scientific investigation at 20 per cent rewards a controlled design and honest uncertainty treatment far more than an ambitious topic, which is the most common planning error in Abu Dhabi cohorts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward algebraic fluency; the data-based questions reward graph discipline and error analysis. Students who can derive a result still lose marks for not stating assumptions, which is an explicit requirement rather than a presentational nicety.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation decide the top bands, and the portfolio of commentaries is a substantial internal component with its own word limit per commentary. Students who list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap themselves well below the top band.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-handling in Paper 1 is a separate skill from essay writing in Papers 2 and 3, and is examined on its own terms: origin, purpose, content, value and limitation. The historical investigation is the internal component and carries a word limit that is routinely exceeded.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork is the internal component, with a stated word limit and criteria that reward methodology and evaluation over presentation. In the written papers, command terms such as "examine" and "to what extent" require explicit structure that students rarely supply unprompted.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, comparative essay and the individual oral, with an additional higher level essay. The individual oral is assessed on a global issue and two extracts, and is the component where preparation most reliably converts into marks because its structure is entirely knowable in advance.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven in the written papers, with a research project as the internal component carrying its own word limit. Application to the specific organisation is what earns marks; theory recited without the business in front of it sits mid-band regardless of accuracy.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules covering Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. Language B and ab initio are different courses with different assessment demands, and a student placed in the wrong one struggles for reasons unrelated to ability.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of around 950 words based on three objects. Both are marked against published criteria. The essay rewards precise handling of knowledge claims rather than general reflection, and the exhibition rewards specificity about each object's link to its prompt.

sections.heading: Component weightings: where a Diploma grade is actually built
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject divides its grade between external written papers and one internal assessment supervised by the school. The split varies by subject and by level, and the variation matters because it tells a family which component is worth a paid hour. A component carrying thirty per cent of a standard level grade deserves a different amount of attention from one carrying twenty.

The broad pattern is this. In the sciences and mathematics the internal assessment carries about a fifth of the grade and the written papers the rest. In several humanities subjects the internal component is heavier at standard level than at higher level, because higher level adds a third paper that absorbs weighting. In the language A subjects the individual oral is a substantial component at standard level and sits alongside an additional higher level essay at higher level.

Two practical consequences follow. First, a standard level student in a humanities subject may have more of their grade inside the internal component than a higher level student in the same subject, which inverts the usual assumption that higher level students need more support. Second, the components with published criteria and no time limit are systematically the best value for tutoring, and they are systematically the least prepared.

The table below gives the shape by subject group. Weightings are set in each subject's current guide and are revised between syllabus versions, so confirm the exact figures for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator. The point of the table is the pattern, not a substitute for the guide.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria and what each one actually rewards
paragraphs: An internal assessment is not marked holistically. It is marked criterion by criterion, each criterion carrying a stated number of marks, and a student can produce something genuinely impressive that scores poorly because it addressed three criteria and ignored two. This is the single most common and most correctable failure in the Diploma, and it is entirely a literacy problem rather than an ability one.

Take the mathematics exploration, which is marked out of twenty. Presentation carries four marks for coherence, organisation and focus. Mathematical communication carries four for notation and consistency. Personal engagement carries three. Reflection carries three. Use of mathematics carries six, and rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the course, which means an elegant piece pitched below the course level cannot reach the top band however well written it is.

The reflection criterion is where the pattern repeats across subjects. In the exploration, three marks are available for genuine reflection on the mathematics, and a very large number of submissions use that section to summarise what the student did. In the sciences, the evaluation strand rewards honest discussion of limitations and realistic improvements rather than a list of generic sources of error. In a historical investigation, the evaluation of sources and methods is its own marked section with its own expectations.

A tutor's legitimate role here is to teach this literacy. They can explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, test whether a topic the student proposed can reach the top band, teach the techniques involved, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright, which is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's Diploma at risk rather than the provider's business.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across Diploma components
paragraphs: Limits are assessed boundaries rather than guidance, and a student who exceeds one is not penalised by a deduction so much as by having work beyond the limit disregarded, which quietly removes the conclusion they spent the most effort on. Knowing the numbers early changes how a piece is planned, and it is the cheapest thing a tutor can tell a Diploma student.

The headline figures are these. The Extended Essay has an upper limit of 4,000 words. The Theory of Knowledge essay has an upper limit of 1,600 words on a prescribed title. The Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary runs to around 950 words across three objects, which works out at roughly 300 words per object and is far less room than students assume. The science internal assessment report has a stated word limit in the current guide, as do the historical investigation, the geography fieldwork report and the business management research project. The mathematics exploration is governed by a recommended page range rather than a word count.

What those limits do to planning is more important than the numbers. A 4,000-word Extended Essay cannot carry three research strands, so the research question has to be narrow enough to answer and broad enough to sustain, which is a judgement a supervisor and a tutor can both help test. A 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay cannot survey a prescribed title; it has to take a position and defend it with precise examples. Around 300 words per exhibition object leaves room for the object, the prompt link and the justification, and nothing else.

Because limits are revised between syllabus versions, confirm the exact figure for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator before planning around any number, including the ones in the table below. The pattern is stable. The specific digits are not guaranteed to be, and a tutoring page is the wrong authority for a boundary a student's grade depends on.

sections.heading: Command terms: the instructions that carry the marks
paragraphs: Command terms are the verbs at the start of an examination question, and in the IB they are defined terms with assessment consequences. "State" asks for a specific answer with no supporting argument. "Outline" asks for a brief account. "Describe" asks for a detailed account without reasons. "Explain" asks for reasons or causes. "Analyse" asks a student to break an idea into parts and show how they relate. "Evaluate" and "discuss" ask for a judgement supported by evidence. "To what extent" asks explicitly for a weighted conclusion.

Students lose marks in two symmetrical ways. They write the long answer to the short instruction, spending five minutes producing an explanation when two marks were available for a statement, and then run out of time on the question that needed the explanation. Or they write the short answer to the long instruction, giving a description where reasons were required, and earn half the marks for knowledge that was entirely sufficient.

Neither failure is about understanding, which is why re-teaching content does not fix it. The correction is mechanical: read the command term, write down what it demands, size the answer to the marks available, and check at the end that the demanded verb was actually performed. A tutor can audit a student's own marked paper for this in a single session and the pattern is usually immediately visible, because students are consistent in which direction they err.

The same discipline applies inside internal assessments, where the criteria themselves use command-like language. A criterion asking the student to evaluate is not satisfied by description, and a criterion asking for justification is not satisfied by assertion. Teaching a student to read criteria the way they read a command term is one of the few interventions that pays off across all six subjects at once.
bullets: Size the answer to the marks available, not to how much the student knows
Check at the end that the demanded verb was actually performed

sections.heading: How past-paper work should actually be run
paragraphs: Past papers are the most over-prescribed and under-used resource in the Diploma. A student who does twenty papers without marking them properly has rehearsed their existing habits twenty times. A student who does six papers and marks each one against the published scheme, with somebody competent sitting beside them, has learned six papers' worth of what the examiner rewards.

The working unit is therefore a paper plus its marking, and that is a ninety-minute job rather than a sixty-minute one. The paper is sat under conditions: timed, no notes, calculator rules respected, and in a non-calculator component genuinely without one. Then it is marked together, question by question, against the published scheme, with the specific reason for each lost mark named. Not "careless" but "the command term asked for reasons and the answer described".

From that process comes the only artefact that matters: a ranked list of topics and techniques costing the most marks, updated after each paper. If that list is not getting shorter across six weeks, the sessions are not working and the plan should change. This is the measurable thing a parent can ask about, and it is a far better question than asking how the sessions are going.

One boundary on materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those belong to the boards and are published through the boards' own channels and through your child's school. A tutor's job is to teach a student to work with them, not to hand over a copy, and a provider offering a library of mark schemes as a download is offering something that is not theirs to give.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay and TOK: process, not product
paragraphs: The two written core components are where the authorship boundary matters most, because both are long, both are produced over months, and both are supervised rather than invigilated. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece with a school supervisor. The Theory of Knowledge essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title. Both are assessed against published criteria and both carry points in combination.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. They can help test whether a research question is answerable within 4,000 words, which is the single decision that determines whether the essay works. They can explain what each criterion rewards and how the marks are distributed. They can teach the research and referencing skills the task assumes. They can read a draft the student has written and say where it does not yet meet a criterion. They can help a student plan a timetable that meets the school's internal deadline rather than the external one.

What no tutor may do is produce the work. No tutor should write the essay, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion, or supply text for submission. The IB's academic-honesty framework makes authorship the student's responsibility, and a malpractice finding costs the student the Diploma. This is the clearest line in Diploma tutoring and it is also the one a competitor in this market crosses commercially, which is why we state it in writing rather than assume it is understood.

A practical note for Al Reem Island families specifically. School internal deadlines for both components are set per campus and sit well before the external ones. Establish those two dates in the first term of DP2, because a coaching block has to be scheduled backwards from them and a student who starts a 4,000-word essay four weeks out will produce something within the word limit and below their capability.

sections.heading: Fitting Diploma sessions around the Al Reem Island day
paragraphs: Al Reem Island is dense and vertical, and most of its secondary students leave it each morning. Campuses serving the island end their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions running later on some days. A student travelling back from the Khalifa City corridor is typically not home before 16:15, and later on an activity day.

Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, the honest earliest start is about 16:30 for a student at a campus close to the island and about 17:30 for a mainland commute. Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time. In an exam term, the slots that survive are the ones at 18:00 and 18:30, and anything after 20:00 is competing with sleep, which in DP2 is a false economy.

Component work shapes the session length more than the subject does. A past-paper block needs ninety minutes, because the marking is the point. An internal assessment coaching session works in sixty, because the material is the student's own draft. A command-term audit can be done in a single session of either length. Agreeing what the session is for also settles how long it should be, which is a better conversation than choosing a duration first.

Because the lesson is delivered over live video, a late school finish moves the session rather than cancelling it, and a family travelling over a half term keeps the arrangement with a time-zone adjustment. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, which removes the journey from both sides and removes the travel component from the rate. For the record, published market bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 for in-home work. Those are market figures, attributed, not our prices.

whyPoints.description: A tutor works from the current guide for the subject and level your child sits, which is what makes a session about component weightings, criteria and command terms rather than about general revision. Ask any tutor which guide they teach from; the answer is diagnostic.

whyPoints.title: Components named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Each session states which component it is working on and what the marks there are awarded for. That gives a parent something to evaluate, and it stops the arrangement drifting into re-teaching the school's current chapter a few days late.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessments coached to criteria
