faqs.question: What should an IB tutor for an Al Reem Island student actually be teaching?
faqs.answer: The specification. Which components carry which share of the subject grade, what each internal assessment criterion rewards and how many marks it holds, what the command terms demand, and what the word limits force a student to plan for. Re-teaching the content the school is covering at the same time is the default pattern in this market and it is the lowest-value hour a family can buy, particularly in the second Diploma year when the school is already doing it.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject grade sits in the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: In mathematics and the sciences it is typically about a fifth. In several humanities subjects the internal component is heavier at standard level than at higher level, because higher level adds a third paper that absorbs weighting. In the language A subjects the individual oral is substantial at standard level. The exact figure for your child's cohort is in the current subject guide, and the school's IB coordinator can confirm it, which is worth doing before planning around any number.

faqs.question: Why do students who understand the subject still lose marks in IB papers?
faqs.answer: Usually command terms. These are defined instructions with assessment consequences: state asks for an answer with no argument, describe asks for a detailed account without reasons, explain asks for reasons, evaluate asks for a judgement supported by evidence. Students write the long answer to the short instruction and then run out of time, or the short answer to the long instruction and earn half the marks for sufficient knowledge. Neither failure is about understanding, which is why more content teaching does not fix it.

faqs.question: What is the word limit for the Extended Essay and the TOK essay?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay has an upper limit of 4,000 words and the Theory of Knowledge essay 1,600 words on a prescribed title. The TOK exhibition commentary runs to around 950 words across three objects, roughly 300 words each. Limits are assessed boundaries, and work beyond one is disregarded rather than deducted, which quietly removes the conclusion a student worked hardest on. Confirm the current figures with your school's IB coordinator, because they are revised between syllabus versions.

faqs.question: Where does a tutor's help on an Al Reem Island student's Extended Essay have to stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor can test whether a research question is answerable within 4,000 words, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, teach the research and referencing skills the task assumes, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of a criterion, and help plan backwards from the school's internal deadline. No tutor may write the essay, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion or supply text. Authorship is the student's responsibility and a malpractice finding costs them the Diploma.

faqs.question: What does the reflection criterion in an internal assessment actually want?
faqs.answer: Genuine reflection on the work, which is not a summary of what was done. In the mathematics exploration three of twenty marks sit there, and a large share of submissions use the section to recap the method. In the sciences the evaluation strand rewards honest discussion of real limitations and realistic improvements rather than a generic list of sources of error. In a historical investigation the evaluation of sources and methods is its own marked section. In every case the criterion is published and readable in advance.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used in the final Diploma terms?
faqs.answer: One paper plus its marking is the working unit, and that needs ninety minutes rather than sixty. The paper is sat under genuine conditions, timed and without notes, with calculator rules respected. Then it is marked together against the published scheme and the specific reason for each lost mark is named, not described as carelessness. The output is a ranked list of topics and techniques costing the most marks, and the test of whether the block is working is whether that list shortens.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to apartments on Al Reem Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. For context, published market bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 for in-home work. Those are market figures from the sources named, not our prices.

faqs.question: When can a Diploma session start for a student living on Al Reem Island?
faqs.answer: It depends on the campus rather than the postcode. Schools serving the island finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, and a student commuting back from the Khalifa City corridor is often not home before 16:15. Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, the honest earliest start is 16:30 for a nearby campus and 17:30 for a mainland one. Our range runs 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the slots that survive an exam term are usually 18:00 and 18:30.

faqs.question: Should I ask for sixty or ninety minutes per Diploma session?
faqs.answer: Let the component decide. A past-paper block needs ninety minutes, because sitting the paper and marking it together are both necessary and the marking is where most of the learning happens. Internal assessment coaching works well in sixty, since the material under discussion is the student's own draft. A command-term audit on a marked paper can be done in either. Agreeing what the session is for settles its length, which is a better conversation than choosing a duration first and filling it.

faqs.question: My child is standard level in a humanities subject. Do they need less support than a higher level student?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the assumption costs families marks. In several humanities subjects the internal component carries a heavier share of the grade at standard level than at higher level, because higher level adds a third paper that absorbs weighting. A standard level student can therefore have more of their grade sitting inside a component with published criteria and a months-long timeline, which is the most tractable part of the Diploma and the part most often left unprepared.

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor hand over IB mark schemes and subject guides for us to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be cautious of anyone who offers a library of them as a download. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, reach students through the boards' own channels and through the school, and reproducing them is a copyright matter. We cite and link them. A tutor's job is to teach a student to work with those documents, which is a skill that outlasts any file they could be given.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the IB exam and results dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not confirmed them from the IB itself. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no session or results date in this project has been verified at source, and a date a parent plans around has to be checkable. Secondary sources circulate figures that disagree with one another. The reliable route is your school's IB coordinator, who holds the school's own timetable, and the IB's published assessment pages. UAE schools sit the May session.

faqs.question: How do I know whether an IB tutor really knows the specification?
faqs.answer: Ask which subject guide they teach from, which components carry what weighting in your child's subject and level, what the internal assessment criteria are and how the marks are split, and what the word limit is on the piece your child is working on. A specialist answers all four without pausing. A generalist answers in terms of topics and confidence. The rate attached tells you nothing about which you are speaking to, which is why the questions are worth asking before the first paid hour.

faqs.question: What should change after six weeks of component-focused tutoring?
faqs.answer: Two measurable things. The ranked list of topics and techniques costing the most marks should be shorter, which requires that such a list was produced in the first place. And in a paper-based block, timed scores should be moving. For an internal assessment block the equivalent test is whether the draft now addresses every criterion, which is checkable against the published criteria rather than a matter of opinion. If neither has changed, the plan should change rather than continue.

intro.heading: Work out the evening first, then the tutoring
paragraphs: Al Samha sits in the north of Abu Dhabi emirate, out along the Dubai road past Al Shahama and Al Rahba, and the thing that defines a school day here is distance. There is no cluster of Diploma schools on the doorstep. Students travel, often by bus, towards Yas Island, Al Raha, Khalifa City or the island itself, and the journey runs at both ends of the day. A family in this corridor is not short of willingness to support their child's studies; they are short of usable evening.

That changes the arithmetic of tutoring. A student who leaves at half past six in the morning and gets home between four and five has already done a ten-hour day before any homework begins. Add an in-home tutor who has to drive out from the city and the session starts later again, finishes later again, and eats the part of the evening the student needed for the work the tutor has just set. The scheduling problem is not a detail around the edge of the teaching; for this corridor it is the main constraint.

The second fact is about specialism. Diploma provision in Abu Dhabi is concentrated in a modest number of schools, none of them in Al Samha, so the student commutes for the programme. The adults who have taught a specific Higher Level course are concentrated near those schools or further away still, and almost none of them will drive to Al Samha on a weekday evening. Published in-home rates in this market run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and the travel component out here is substantial. Several tutors simply decline the distance, which is the honest answer and leaves a northern family with a far shorter list than the search results suggested.

Put those two together and the useful question changes. It is not who will come to Al Samha; it is what can be taught well in the ninety minutes that genuinely exist between the bus and a reasonable bedtime, by somebody who has actually taught the course. Answering that honestly means looking at the real timeline of a school day in this corridor, which is what the sections below do.

IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a family out here the practical consequence is specific: the session begins at the minute it was booked regardless of what the Dubai road is doing, no part of the evening is spent waiting for a car, and the tutor is selected from people who have taught the course rather than from the small set willing to make the drive.

sections.heading: What this search means out here, and the constraint that overrides the rest
paragraphs: Direct answer first: an IB home tutor in Al Samha, through IB Gram, means a Diploma specialist matched to your child's exact course and level, teaching one-to-one over live video at a time that fits the bus arrival, with a free trial lesson first. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If a tutor at the door is the requirement, that is a different purchase, and the market rate for it in this emirate is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

The overriding constraint in this corridor is time rather than money or even quality. A student bussed to Al Raha or the island has already spent two hours travelling before any lesson begins. Whatever else a tutoring arrangement does, it must not consume the hour the student needed for the work their teachers set, because then the tutoring is competing with the school rather than supporting it.

That produces advice most tutoring pages will not give. Sometimes the right answer for an Al Samha family is fewer sessions, shorter sessions, or sessions at the weekend. Sometimes it is no sessions in a particular term, because the student's real problem is that they are tired and over-scheduled. A provider that recommends two ninety-minute weekday blocks to a student with a ten-hour day has not looked at the day.

Where tutoring does fit, the online format earns its place out here more clearly than anywhere else in the emirate. There is no drive, so nothing is lost to the Dubai road at five in the afternoon. The session starts when it was booked. And the tutor is chosen from the people who have taught the course rather than from the very small group willing to come this far for one lesson.

sections.heading: Where students from this corridor actually go to school, and what the run costs
paragraphs: Because there is no Diploma school in Al Samha, every family here has already made a commuting decision, and the tutoring question follows from it rather than from the address. A student bussed towards Khalifa City has a different evening from one bussed to the island, and both have different evenings from a student whose parents drive them to Yas.

The pattern that matters is finish time plus journey length. Several Khalifa City and Al Raha schools finish earlier than island schools, which can leave a usable slot from about half past four. Island schools combined with a northern bus route frequently put a student home closer to five, sometimes later when the afternoon traffic is bad. Those two cases need different session times, and a provider offering one standard 5pm slot is serving one of them badly.

There is a second-order effect families notice but rarely articulate. A long bus run compresses not just the evening but the week: a student who is travelling four hours a day across five days has lost most of a day's working time by Friday. That is why weekend scheduling is worth more in this corridor than closer in, and why internal assessment work in particular belongs there rather than squeezed into a Tuesday.

sections.heading: The evening budget: what actually fits between the bus and bedtime
paragraphs: Set the evening out hour by hour and the tutoring decision becomes obvious rather than contested. A Diploma student home at five has, realistically, four hours before a sensible bedtime. Some of that is food and family. Some is the homework and reading their own teachers set, which is the work that generates the grade. A tutoring session takes an hour of what remains, and a session scheduled badly takes two because of the settling and the aftermath.

The honest allocation looks roughly like this. Thirty to forty-five minutes to arrive, eat and decompress, which cannot be skipped without the next hour being wasted. Then the single most productive block of the evening, which is where either tutoring or independent work belongs but not both. Then a second, lower-quality block suitable for reading, revision cards or finishing something begun earlier. Then a wind-down that students sacrifice first and should not.

The implication is that a weekday session should occupy the first productive block and should leave the second for the student's own work, which means early rather than late. A session at 7.30pm occupies the lower-quality block and displaces nothing useful, but it also achieves less, and it pushes the student's own work later still. This is the arithmetic that makes an in-home arrangement difficult out here: by the time a tutor has driven from the city, the good block has gone.

For younger students the whole budget shrinks, because fatigue arrives earlier. For a Middle Years student on a long bus run, two thirty-five minute sessions a week will reliably outperform one ninety-minute session, and any tutor who insists otherwise is describing their own preference rather than the child's capacity.

sections.heading: Diploma deadlines against a long commute, and how the two compound
paragraphs: A Diploma student with a long journey faces the same internal deadlines as a student living next to the school, with less time to meet them. Internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay interim dates and Theory of Knowledge deadlines are set by the school and arrive on the same day for everybody. Nobody adjusts them for a bus route.

The compounding effect shows up at the end of term one. A student who loses an hour a day to travel has lost roughly a working week by November, and the work that gets dropped is always the same kind: the long, unsupervised, self-directed task with a distant deadline. That is precisely the shape of an internal assessment, which is why Al Samha families tend to arrive at tutoring with a draft problem rather than a content problem.

The remedy is scheduling rather than intensity. Agree the internal assessment question early, break the work into pieces small enough to fit a compressed evening, and put the long continuous work at the weekend where the time actually exists. Four weekend sessions spread across six weeks will finish a draft that four weekday evening sessions will not, and the difference is entirely about when the hours are available rather than how many are bought.

This page does not print IB session or results dates, because the IB publishes and revises them and a wrong date a family plans around is worse than none. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the written internal calendar in September. For a family in this corridor that document is the single most useful thing to hold, because it is what makes it possible to put the heavy work in the weekends that are still free.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the weeks when the corridor empties
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic year and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so over time it drifts across the second and third terms. School hours shorten, which in this corridor is genuinely helpful: a shorter day plus a shorter run can hand a student back an hour of usable evening. Against that, late-afternoon energy drops and family routines move to the evening, so sessions shift to post-Iftar slots.

The pattern that works is the same one that works closer in, with one addition. Front-load heavy new content into the weeks before. Use the period itself for consolidation, past-paper marking and error-log review. Then resume intensity afterwards. The addition for this corridor is to take advantage of the shortened school day deliberately rather than incidentally, by moving sessions earlier for those weeks instead of leaving them at the usual time.

School breaks matter more out here too. A family in this corridor loses more weekly hours to travel than one in the city, so the breaks are where the balance can be restored. A short block of concentrated work in a holiday week, when there is no bus run at either end of the day, achieves more per hour than the same block during term. That is an argument for using one week of a break rather than all of it.

Family travel is common in this community, and a session delivered over video follows the family. A student away for three weeks in term two does not have to lose the block; the slot can move to suit the destination time zone and then move back. In an in-home arrangement those weeks are simply lost, and they are often the weeks before the mock window.

sections.heading: Checks on anybody who does come to the house
paragraphs: If an in-home arrangement is what a family wants despite the arithmetic, the checks are quick and worth doing. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fees listed and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific figure quoted at you is unverified.

In Abu Dhabi there is a further rule. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, and in the meantime avoid arranging paid tuition with your child's own classroom teacher.

Two claims to distrust regardless of format. No tutor is approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge; those bodies regulate schools, and a tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permit with a number. And no provider should offer to produce an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay: the student's work must be their own, the supervisor signs to that, and the malpractice exposure falls on the student.

sections.heading: Availability out here, and what we say when there is none
paragraphs: The slot a family in this corridor needs is often the slot everybody needs. Early-evening times between half past four and six are the most requested across the emirate, and Diploma Higher Level specialists are a small group whose availability tightens further before mock windows and internal assessment deadlines. Being honest about that is more useful than implying a full diary is always available.

When no specialist is free at a workable time, you are told and given the alternatives in writing. Those are: the same course with a different qualified tutor at a time that fits; a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same IB course, disclosed before booking and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which for this corridor sometimes produces better early-evening availability rather than worse; shorter sessions at higher frequency; a weekend block instead of a weekday one; or a named wait.

The weekend option deserves emphasis for Al Samha specifically. It is often the best answer rather than the fallback, because the time genuinely exists there and the student is rested. Families tend to treat weekends as protected and weekday evenings as flexible, when in this corridor the opposite is closer to the truth.

The free trial lesson settles the rest. One full lesson with the matched tutor, no card required, no hours bought first. It should establish where the marks are going, whether the course and level look right, and what pattern of sessions the student's actual week can carry. If the answer is two short sessions rather than one long one, or a weekend block rather than a Tuesday, that is a finding worth having before any money is spent.

process.title: Tell us the bus time, not just the subject
process.description: When your child actually gets home, which school they travel to, and what else is in the evening. Those three determine which tutors can realistically work with you, and they matter more out here than the choice between two equally qualified people.

process.title: We propose a pattern, not just a tutor
process.description: Sometimes one early-evening hour; sometimes two short sessions; sometimes a weekend block and nothing midweek. The pattern is proposed from your child's actual week rather than from a standard weekly template.

process.title: Free trial lesson at the proposed time
process.description: One full lesson, no card required, run at the slot being considered so that the fatigue question is answered honestly rather than theoretically. The tutor reports what they found, including when the slot is plainly too late.

process.title: Protect the homework window in writing
process.description: The plan names which block of the evening belongs to the session and which stays with the student's own work. A session that displaces the only hour available for an internal assessment draft has made the week worse.

process.title: Review after six to eight weeks, then adjust the pattern
process.description: Progress is checked against an error log, and so is the schedule. If the student is arriving at sessions exhausted, the fix is a different time or fewer sessions rather than more content squeezed into the same hour.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the bus, not around a template
whyPoints.description: A student bussed to the island has a different usable hour from one bussed to Khalifa City. Asking for the arrival time before anything else is what separates a workable arrangement from a slot that looks fine on paper.

whyPoints.title: No part of the evening lost to arrival
whyPoints.description: An online session begins at the booked minute regardless of the Dubai road. For a corridor where a tutor's journey would be forty minutes each way, that is the difference between a full hour and a shortened one.

whyPoints.title: Weekends treated as the primary slot, not the overflow
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment drafts, timed essays and whole papers need continuous time that a compressed weekday evening does not contain. Out here the weekend is usually where the real work belongs.

whyPoints.title: Fewer sessions recommended when that is right
whyPoints.description: A tired, over-scheduled student does not need a second weekday block. Saying so costs revenue and is the honest reading of a ten-hour day followed by a long bus run.

whyPoints.title: Travel priced out of the equation
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour include a journey that, from this corridor, is substantial. Online delivery removes that cost entirely and widens the tutor pool at the same time.

whyPoints.title: Availability and location disclosed
whyPoints.description: Early-evening slots are the most contested in the emirate. You get the expected wait in writing, and where a tutor is based outside the UAE you hear it before booking, sometimes because it improves the available times.

faqs.question: Our child gets home at five after a long bus run. Is that too late for a lesson?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the first forty minutes should not be a lesson. A student needs food and decompression before anything cognitive, so a session starting around half past five works where one starting at five does not. The more important question is what the session displaces: if it takes the only productive block of the evening, the homework their teachers set gets pushed into the tired hours. For many students in this corridor two shorter sessions a week work better than one long one.

faqs.question: Why is there no Diploma school closer to Al Samha?
faqs.answer: Diploma provision across Abu Dhabi is concentrated in a modest number of schools, most of them towards Yas, Al Raha, Khalifa City and the island, which is where the demand and the staffing have historically been. The practical consequence for a northern family is a commuting decision made before any tutoring question arises, and a school day that runs long at both ends. ADEK publishes the licensed school list and its own inspection ratings, which is the right place to compare options.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor even travel out here?
faqs.answer: Some will and many will not, and the ones who do price the journey into the rate. Published in-home bands run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and from this corridor that journey can be forty minutes or more each way into evening traffic. The practical result is a much shorter list of willing tutors than a search suggests, and a higher chance that the available ones have not taught your child's specific Diploma course.

faqs.question: Are two short sessions really better than one long one?
faqs.answer: For a student arriving home after a ten-hour day, usually yes. Two thirty-five or forty-minute sessions a week fit a compressed evening more easily, keep contact with the subject twice rather than once, and match realistic concentration after a long bus run. The exceptions are tasks that genuinely need continuous time: an internal assessment draft, timed essay practice, or a whole past paper. Those belong at the weekend rather than squeezed into a weekday evening at either length.

faqs.question: Why do you recommend weekend sessions more than most tutors do?
faqs.answer: Because in this corridor the time genuinely exists there and the student is rested. A family travelling four hours a day across five days has lost most of a working day by Friday, and the work that gets dropped is always the long self-directed task with a distant deadline. That is exactly the shape of an internal assessment. Four weekend sessions across six weeks will finish a draft that four weekday evening sessions will not, at the same cost.

faqs.question: How do we stop a tutoring session eating the homework time?
faqs.answer: By naming which block of the evening it occupies before booking anything. The honest shape of an evening is a decompression period, one genuinely productive block, one lower-quality block and a wind-down. A session belongs in the productive block only if the student's own hardest task does not, and otherwise in the second block as a shorter session. Writing that down in the plan prevents the slow drift where tutoring and school homework end up competing.

faqs.question: Does the shortened school day during Ramadan help out here?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than it does closer in, because a shorter day plus a shorter run can hand a student back an hour of usable evening. The sensible response is to move sessions earlier for those weeks deliberately rather than leaving them at the usual time, and to use the period for consolidation, past-paper marking and error-log review rather than new content. Heavy new material belongs in the weeks before, with full intensity resuming afterwards.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue during a long family trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the slot can move to suit a destination time zone for the duration and then move back. For families in this corridor who travel for several weeks in a term, that often matters more than any other scheduling feature, because the weeks away are frequently the weeks before a mock window. An in-home arrangement simply stops for the duration and then has to be restarted.

faqs.question: Our child is exhausted rather than struggling academically. Should we still book a tutor?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and a provider should be willing to say so. If the real problem is a ten-hour day plus a long bus run plus a crowded evening, adding another commitment makes it worse rather than better. The useful first step is a diagnostic lesson that looks at a marked paper and at the week together: sometimes the finding is two targeted sessions and a changed schedule rather than a term of weekly tutoring.

faqs.question: Which session time is hardest to get?
faqs.answer: Anything between half past four and six, because it is the slot almost every family in the emirate wants and Diploma Higher Level specialists are a small group. Availability tightens further in the weeks before mock windows and internal assessment deadlines, when demand peaks city-wide at once. Weekend slots and slightly later weekday slots are easier, and a tutor based outside the UAE sometimes has better early-evening availability rather than worse, depending on their own time zone.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we want is only available at 7.30pm?
faqs.answer: You should be told honestly what that costs. A 7.30pm session falls in the lower-quality block of the evening, displaces less but achieves less, and pushes the student's own work later still. For recall-based subjects it can work; for sustained problem solving in mathematics or physics it usually does not. The better options are a different qualified tutor at a workable hour, or the same tutor at a weekend slot, and both should be offered rather than one being assumed.

faqs.question: Do internal assessment deadlines take the commute into account?
faqs.answer: No. Internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay interim deadlines and Theory of Knowledge dates are set by the school and arrive on the same day for every student regardless of where they live. That is why a family in this corridor should ask the Diploma coordinator for the written internal calendar in September: holding it is what makes it possible to put the long continuous work into the weekends that are still free, before they fill up with everything else.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a specialist rate when the real problem is time?
faqs.answer: Only if the diagnosis says the problem is specialist. If a student understands the material and is simply out of hours, paying AED 270 an hour for more content delivery is buying the wrong thing; the fix is scheduling. If the student has a genuine Higher Level content gap, the specialist rate is defensible because a generalist cannot close it. The free trial lesson exists to tell those two situations apart before anybody commits money.

faqs.question: What should we send when we first get in touch?
faqs.answer: The course and level, the school your child travels to, the time they actually get home, and a photograph of a recent marked piece of work. Those four let us propose a pattern rather than just a tutor, which out here is the part that decides whether the arrangement survives past October. An enquiry that gives only the subject produces a standard weekly slot that may not fit the week it has to live in.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-samha.closingBody: For a family in Al Samha the first useful thing to tell us is not the subject but the clock: which school your child travels to, when they actually get home, and what else is already in the evening. From that we can propose a pattern that fits, match a Diploma specialist by course rather than by distance, and say honestly when the answer is two short sessions, a weekend block, or fewer sessions than you expected. The first lesson is free and runs at the slot you are considering. Tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

intro.heading: The further out you live, the stronger the comparison gets
paragraphs: Al Shamkha is a large mainland residential district on the outer edge of Abu Dhabi city, substantially family housing, with newer villa developments extending it further south. Baniyas sits on one side and Mohammed Bin Zayed City towards the city; the emirate's densest cluster of international schools, in the Khalifa City corridor, is a genuine drive away rather than a few minutes.

That geography produces a specific and under-acknowledged effect on tutoring. The resident tutors who serve this emirate cluster where the international schools are, because that is where the bookings are. So a family in Al Shamkha searching for a local IB tutor is usually offered someone travelling out from Khalifa City, Mohammed Bin Zayed City or Al Reef, with the journey folded into the hourly rate.

The honest way to frame this is as a comparison. A family in Khalifa City and a family in Al Shamkha are offered broadly the same tutors at different prices, and the difference is distance. The teaching is identical. What varies is how much of the hour you are funding is spent on a road, and how reliably the session starts when it was supposed to.

There is a second effect that matters more in the Diploma than elsewhere. A Diploma student carries six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with an Internal Assessment in every subject. That is six specialisms. A family optimising for who can reach Al Shamkha by five o'clock is selecting from a pool that has already been filtered by willingness to make a long drive — and that filter has nothing to do with whether anyone in it teaches Chemistry Higher Level.

So the comparison between Al Shamkha and the school belt resolves the same way whichever side you live on, and more strongly here: stop filtering by distance and filter by course. That conclusion is not a sales line, it is what the local supply pattern implies. A family in Khalifa City can get away with the proximity filter. A family in Al Shamkha pays a premium for it and still gets a narrower list.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor will travel to an Al Shamkha address. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the course and level in front of them. Distance stops being a variable rather than becoming a cheaper one.

What follows is the detail: the two areas compared, what distance adds to a rate, why six subjects defeats proximity, the honesty boundary on the Diploma core, what ADEK's inspections tell a family choosing a school out here, and what the market charges with the source for every figure.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-shamkha.programmesIntro: An Al Shamkha family may be at any stage of an IB education, and what distance costs differs at each one. These are the four.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with no external examination. Assessment is continuous and portfolio-based, culminating in the Year 6 Exhibition. Useful support at this stage is mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure, and recording thinking rather than only answers.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where distance bites hardest in practice. A primary child who has travelled forty minutes home from a school in the Khalifa City corridor has very little left for a visiting tutor at five o'clock. Thirty or forty focused minutes from the kitchen table works far better than an hour, and avoids making the afternoon any longer.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade on school-set boundaries, with no external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. The Personal Project runs through Year 10 or 11 and carries weight with no external examination behind it.
programmes.countryNote: Families out here often meet the MYP-to-Diploma step later than they would like, because the schools running both sit in the corridor rather than locally and the conversation happens at a parents' evening forty minutes away. The practical consequence is that the bridge work — criteria to timed papers — gets bought in DP1 rather than in the spring of Year 11, which costs more.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of its grade, with school-set internal deadlines across both years.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. IB exam and results dates are set and periodically revised by the IB and we publish none here — confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator. For an Al Shamkha family the operational point is that six subjects means six potential specialisms, which is the number no local pool can cover.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. The Diploma-course components are assessed identically to the full Diploma, including their Internal Assessments.
programmes.countryNote: A narrow need, which is exactly the case where distance is most punishing in-home. Two subjects a week is not enough work to make a long drive economic for a tutor, so the rate quoted to an Al Shamkha family for a single course is often the least attractive in the market. Online removes the problem because the journey does not exist.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-shamkha.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Al Shamkha families most often need, with where the marks actually go. Each is a separate specialism, which is the heart of this page's argument.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with Higher Level adding a third paper of extended investigations. Marks go to compressed working more often than to the mathematics, and Paper 3 is a structural skill rather than a topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The calculator is examined, and a correct result with no stated model behind it collects a fraction of the marks offered.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics with Higher Level extensions. Unit prefixes, unstated assumptions in extended answers and uncertainty treatment in the investigation are the recurring losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic pathways break first, and an investigation with a clean graph still scores poorly where the method does not justify the range chosen.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology. The data-based paper separates grades, and the loss is describing a trend where the command term asked for a mechanism.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and development. Diagrams carry heavy credit and must be referenced in the prose; the portfolio commentaries need explicit theory applied to real published articles.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. Numerical questions on ratios and investment appraisal are reliable marks students skip, and the Higher Level project needs a focused question early.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Literary and non-literary texts, the Individual Oral, the Higher Level Essay and guided analysis. Paper 1 marks go to description of content instead of analysis of technique.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, networks, abstract data structures at Higher Level and the solution-development Internal Assessment, which scores on documented design and testing rather than on how impressive the program is.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the IA suite
subjects.description: An exhibition and prescribed-title essay, a 4,000-word independent essay, and a per-subject Internal Assessment. Our role across all three is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts only.

sections.heading: Al Shamkha against Khalifa City, done honestly
paragraphs: Set the two side by side and the educational differences are smaller than the operational ones. Khalifa City holds the densest concentration of international schools in the emirate and the largest resident tutor population. Al Shamkha is a large residential district with its housing stock, its own amenities and a real drive to that school belt. Both are served, for tutoring purposes, by the same group of people.

The difference is who pays for the road. A tutor living in Khalifa City can fit four sessions into an evening across Khalifa City, Shakhbout City and the near mainland, with a few minutes between each. The same tutor taking a booking in Al Shamkha spends a substantial part of that evening driving, and prices accordingly or declines. So the Al Shamkha family is quoted more for the same hour, or offered a narrower list, or both.

This is not a complaint about tutors; it is simply how an hourly business works when travel is unpaid time. It does mean that the standard advice to "find someone local" lands differently depending on where you live. In the corridor it is reasonable advice. In Al Shamkha it means accepting whoever is willing to make the drive, which is a filter on willingness rather than on expertise.

The table sets the two areas against each other on the things that actually differ, and the last column is the point of the page: almost none of them change which IB specialist can teach your child, once the lesson stops requiring a car.

sections.heading: What distance actually adds to an hourly rate
paragraphs: It is worth putting numbers on this rather than gesturing at it. Published market rates for this emirate, read in October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table at AED 180 to 350 with independent home tutors reaching 500. The gap between those bands — roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour — is the travel component of the market.

That gap is not constant across the emirate. For a family in the corridor, where a tutor drives ten minutes, the premium sits at the bottom of the range and is arguably fair. For a family in Al Shamkha, where the same tutor drives considerably further in each direction, the premium sits higher, because it has to cover more unpaid time. The further out you live, the more of your hourly rate is a petrol and time calculation.

Then there is the reliability cost, which never appears on an invoice. A longer journey at the hour the roads are busiest produces slippage, and a session starting fifteen or twenty minutes late still bills the hour. Over a school year of weekly sessions that is several hours paid for and not received, and it falls disproportionately on the households furthest from where the tutors live.

And a flexibility cost. A tutor whose evening is a driving route cannot move your Tuesday to a Thursday, because the route is the business. For a Diploma family that matters in the specific fortnight when three internal deadlines collide — which is exactly when you need the frequency to rise.

sections.heading: Six subjects defeats proximity, every time
paragraphs: This is the structural argument and it holds regardless of where you live, just more sharply out here. A Diploma student is not studying one subject. They are carrying six, each with its own papers, its own command terms and its own Internal Assessment marked against its own criteria. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Biology Standard Level are not adjacent skills.

Now apply a geographic filter. The pool of tutors willing to drive to Al Shamkha regularly is a subset of the emirate's tutors, selected by willingness to travel rather than by subject. The probability that this subset contains a specialist in the two or three courses your child is actually weakest in, at the right level, with a free slot after a long school run, is low. Not zero, but low enough that most families end up with a capable generalist.

A generalist is genuinely useful for some things: keeping a student working, explaining a concept, sitting beside them through a problem set. What a generalist cannot do is read an Economics Internal Assessment commentary against its criteria and say which one is costing marks, or teach the structure of a Higher Level maths Paper 3, or know where Chemistry students lose marks on an organic mechanism. Those are the things that move a Diploma grade.

Dropping the geographic filter is therefore not a convenience. It changes what can be matched. sections.heading: The honesty boundary on Internal Assessments, the EE and TOK
paragraphs: Since the pages that rank for this kind of search often blur it, the boundary deserves to be stated precisely. It is set by IB academic-honesty rules, the student signs an authenticity declaration, and a breach is an expulsion-level risk for them rather than a reprimand for a provider. So this is not a policy preference; it is the only version of the service that is safe for your child.

A tutor may teach the subject content the task rests on, explain what each criterion rewards and in what proportion, question a method until the student notices its weakness, read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion it undersells and why, teach referencing and how to describe a method so another person could repeat it, interrogate whether a research question is answerable in the word count, and run timed practice on a different task.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, draft a paragraph for the student to adapt, edit a draft to completion, rewrite sentences so the final text is partly theirs, generate a research question and hand it over, supply data the student did not gather, or provide a worked model of the live task. There is an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and it is not a service we offer at any fee.

Two related boundaries, useful as tests when comparing any provider. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads — we reference them and link the official source. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, nor use examiner status to imply access to marking or grade boundaries.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspections and choosing a school from out here
paragraphs: A family in Al Shamkha makes a bigger school decision than a family in the corridor, because the realistic options span a wider range of distances and the commute is a daily cost for years. So it is worth knowing what the regulator publishes and what it does not tell you.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK inspects and publishes ratings. It is also named by none of the competitor pages researched for this market, which indicates how little localisation the pages ranking for these searches actually carry.

What an inspection rating tells you is a judgement about the school as an institution — leadership, provision, outcomes across the whole cohort. What it does not tell you is whether your child's Chemistry Higher Level set has a settled teacher this year, whether the maths department is covering both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation with one specialist, or how many students actually take the subject your child wants. Those are the conditions that create a tutoring need, and they come from a parents' evening rather than a published band.

Read a report for pattern rather than headline. If attainment in a subject group is flagged as weaker than progress, the cohort is being taught well from a low starting point and content gaps are the issue. If progress is the weaker measure, look at the teaching. And ask the admissions office directly which Diploma subjects run every year rather than which are listed, because a small cohort school may advertise a course it cannot always timetable.

sections.heading: The permit question, which matters more at a distance
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is worth raising specifically with anyone offering to drive out to Al Shamkha. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Because it is free and quick, a tutor who does not hold one has chosen not to. Asking to see it before a first paid session is a reasonable request, and it is more relevant where the arrangement is informal and the tutor was found by word of mouth.

The consequence of operating without one is stated and unquantified: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating in this market could not be verified, so treat any specific amount quoted at you with suspicion. This page quotes none.

One Abu Dhabi-specific point. ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit code of conduct is reported to bar the same. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document if it applies. And be clear that naming a regulator is not approval by one: IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, Ministry, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no UAE office.

sections.heading: Online into an Al Shamkha home, and the honest limits
paragraphs: Stated plainly, since this page answers a local search: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to an Al Shamkha address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, one student with one tutor.

What that asks of you is modest. A desk or table rather than a bed, headphones, and for maths and the sciences a camera angled at paper or a tablet and stylus so the tutor can see handwritten working as it happens. For written subjects, the draft in a form the tutor can read on screen alongside the student. We set this up in the first session and explain why each part matters.

The gains are specific rather than rhetorical. The session starts at the agreed minute regardless of the roads. A shared whiteboard retains every worked line, so last week's derivation can be reopened rather than reconstructed. The frequency can double for three weeks around a deadline collision and step back afterwards. And the tutor was chosen because they teach the course rather than because they were willing to drive out here.

The limits, stated because a page arguing for honesty should. Narrow Higher Level combinations and less-taught languages are genuinely thinner, and we say so before you pay rather than offering a near miss. Where the right specialist is not UAE-based you are told before the trial lesson, with the lesson still timed to your evening. And if we cannot staff a subject properly we will say that instead of taking the booking, which is a thing no competitor researched for this market does.

intro.heading: Eight weeks can change a Diploma grade, if they are spent on the right thing
paragraphs: A Diploma year is not a long flat stretch of study. It is a sequence of fixed dates, most of them set by your child's school inside deadlines the IB imposes, and almost every grade problem a parent brings us in Al Wahda is really a date problem. The Internal Assessment draft that was never marked against the criteria. The subject level that stayed at HL three months after it should have dropped. The mock paper that was sat but never corrected. None of those are ability failures. They are calendar failures, and a calendar failure is the one kind that a tutor can fix quickly because the work needed is already defined.

So this page is organised around the Diploma calendar rather than around a list of subjects. If your child is in DP2 as Term 1 runs out, the next eight weeks have a specific job: one timed past paper per subject, one Internal Assessment moved from draft to marked draft, and an honest decision about whether six subjects at the current levels are still the right six. If your child is in DP1, the same eight weeks have a different job, and spending them on exam technique would be a waste of the money.

Al Wahda sits in central Abu Dhabi, on the dense apartment grid around Al Wahda Mall and Hazza Bin Zayed Street. Families here are minutes from the island's older schools and a long drive from the newer campuses out on Saadiyat, Yas and the Khalifa City corridor. That geography is exactly why in-home tutoring gets expensive here: a tutor who will drive into central traffic at 4pm prices the drive into the hour, and the pool of people willing to do it shrinks the moment you ask for Chemistry HL rather than general maths support.

IB Gram works the other way round. We find the teacher who knows the subject guide, and the lesson happens over live video on your child's own screen, in Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is dispatched anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are an India-only part of our service and we say so on every page. The practical effect for an Al Wahda family is that the Maths AA HL specialist your child needs is available on Tuesday at 5pm whether that teacher is in Abu Dhabi, Dubai or Mumbai, and the hour you pay for is a teaching hour rather than a teaching hour plus a commute.

The rest of this page is the detail a parent actually needs: what the Abu Dhabi market charges and who publishes those figures, the Diploma calendar counted backwards, where DP1 students quietly lose a year, what ADEK's inspection reports mean, and the line between legitimate IA coaching and academic malpractice. Read the calendar section first if your child is in DP2. Read the honesty section before you pay anyone, anywhere, who offers to help with coursework.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.programmesIntro: Al Wahda children attend schools running the full IB continuum as well as British campuses that bolt a Diploma onto an IGCSE lower school. Which programme your child is in changes what tutoring is for, so start here before you book anything.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, which is why parents of primary children rarely need subject tutoring and often need something narrower: number fluency, reading stamina, or the English a child needs to access a unit of inquiry. A PYP hour that drills worksheets misses the point. A useful one builds the skill the classroom is assuming.
programmes.countryNote: Central Abu Dhabi primary intake is heavily mixed-nationality, and a PYP class in Al Wahda routinely contains children on their second or third curriculum. Under federal rules and ADEK licensing, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside the PYP, so a child here carries a mandatory-subject load the programme itself does not describe.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against criteria A to D in every subject, marked out of 8 each, and reported on a 1-7 scale that is not a percentage. Most MYP tutoring that works is criterion translation: showing a student that a criterion C task wants a process and a criterion D task wants an evaluation, and that writing more does not move either. The final year adds the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: Al Wahda families who move from an MYP school to a British campus mid-secondary hit a real gap, because MYP Year 11 and IGCSE Year 11 are assessing different things. We treat that as a bridging job with a defined end point rather than ongoing tuition.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a fifth to a quarter of the final grade, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The Diploma is where almost all Al Wahda tutoring demand sits, and where the calendar matters most, because nothing can be rescued after an upload deadline passes.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session. Confirm the exact examination and results dates with your school's IB coordinator rather than with any tutoring site, including this one, because the IB publishes that timetable to schools and it is the school that holds your child's candidate number.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a career-related study with a smaller set of DP courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a handful of UAE schools rather than most of them. Tutoring here is usually single-subject: the DP course a CP student is carrying, taught to the same standard as a full Diploma candidate's.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP provision is thin in Abu Dhabi, families in Al Wahda considering it are often choosing between a CP place further out of the city and a full Diploma closer to home. That is a school decision, not a tutoring decision, and your child's current coordinator is the person to ask.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.subjectsIntro: Demand from central Abu Dhabi runs heavily to the quantitative Higher Levels, because those are the courses where a strong MYP or IGCSE student can still stall. These are the Diploma subjects we are asked for most often by Al Wahda families, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA is the proof-and-calculus route. HL adds a third paper of extended problems with no structure, which is where most of the HL grade distribution is decided. Students who scored well in IGCSE maths frequently find AA HL unforgiving because it rewards method chains rather than single-step recall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling, statistics and technology-led. It is not the easy option: AI HL contains serious statistical inference and graph theory. The route choice matters for admissions, so check whether the engineering or economics course your child wants names AA specifically.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks go missing in two predictable places: multi-step mechanics where a student substitutes before rearranging, and the explain-type questions where a correct answer earns nothing because the physics was never stated. The HL extension topics reward students who can work in symbols.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium are the two topics that most often need outside help. The Internal Assessment is where Chemistry grades are made or lost, because a weak research question limits the mark ceiling before a single data point is collected.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Biology rewards precise command-term discipline: describe, explain, outline and evaluate carry different mark expectations, and students who write a paragraph for a two-mark describe question run out of time in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world examples carry the paper marks; the three commentaries carry the Internal Assessment. HL adds a quantitative paper that catches students who treated the course as essay writing. Abu Dhabi students often have strong examples available and never use them.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A content-light, technique-heavy subject. The pre-released case study rewards months of preparation and most students start it weeks late. Tool application, not tool recall, is what separates a 5 from a 7.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question, and the skill is narrowing fast rather than covering everything. The Individual Oral needs a global issue and two texts chosen months ahead; late choices produce thin orals.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students whose English is strong but not first-language. The productive skills are the issue: writing to a text type with the right register, and speaking at length about a stimulus image without drifting into narration.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and the HL abstract data structures topic are the common failure points. The solution requires a working product and documented development; a project started in Term 2 of DP2 rarely reaches the top criteria bands.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.regionsTitle: Al Wahda and the rest of central Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.regionsIntro: We teach across the emirate, and the practical difference between these communities is not our service but the school run and the time a session can realistically start. Here is how that plays out around Al Wahda.

regions.name: Al Wahda
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks around Al Wahda Mall and Hazza Bin Zayed Street. Short school runs to the island campuses, long ones to Saadiyat or Khalifa City. A 4.30pm start works for island schools; 5.30pm is safer if the bus comes off the bridge.

regions.name: Al Rawdah
regions.note: A quieter mix of villas and low-rise apartments immediately south of Al Wahda. The same island school pattern, slightly easier parking, and the same late-afternoon pinch on Airport Road.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Older established villas on the western side of the island, close to several long-standing schools. Families here often have the shortest commute in the city and the earliest realistic session slot.

regions.name: the Corniche
regions.note: High-rise living along the waterfront. Evening sessions dominate because parents working in the central business district are rarely home before 6pm, and a shared desk needs a quiet room.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Newer towers a causeway from the island proper. The bridge traffic adds unpredictable minutes to a 3.30pm pick-up, which is why Al Reem families favour a fixed 6pm slot over a flexible one.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Low-density villa communities with several newer international campuses on the doorstep. School days finish later here, and the sensible booking is after 5pm with a hard stop.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Mainland villa suburbs with a heavy bus culture. A child can be on a bus for 45 minutes each way, so the gap between arriving home and starting work is short and should not be squeezed further.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer residential cluster with campuses still filling. Diploma cohorts are small, which makes niche HL subjects harder to staff locally and online matching more useful.

schoolClusters.city: Central Abu Dhabi island
schoolClusters.note: The island's long-established schools draw most Al Wahda enrolment, and between them they cover both the British route to IGCSE and A Level and the IB Diploma. Students we support attend schools of this kind; we have no relationship with any of them.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Raha and the Khalifa City corridor
schoolClusters.note: The newer campuses out of the centre take a share of Al Wahda families who choose a longer bus ride for a specific programme. Diploma cohorts here are often small, which is precisely when a niche Higher Level is hard to staff from inside one neighbourhood.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: A fixed hour or ninety minutes each week with the same teacher, tracking your child's own school scheme of work rather than a generic syllabus order. This is the right shape for DP1 and for the first half of DP2, because it builds the subject at the speed the class is moving and catches a gap in the week it appears rather than in the mock.

modes.title: Paper-level exam sprint
modes.description: A short, dense block in the run-up to mocks or the May session, built entirely around timed papers. Each hour is a paper attempted, marked against the real criteria, and then dissected for the two or three habits costing marks. A sprint is not for teaching new content, and we will say so if your child needs content rather than technique.

modes.title: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay clinics
modes.description: Scheduled reviews of work your child has already written, against the published criteria, strand by strand. A tutor reads the draft, names which criterion is capping the mark and why, and sets the revision the student then does alone. We do not write, redraft or complete any part of an assessed piece, and no reputable tutor will.

sections.heading: What an Al Wahda parent is really asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: The search term is "IB home tutor in Al Wahda", but the question underneath it is almost never about location. It is: can someone who genuinely knows this syllabus start working with my child soon, and will it fit around the school day? Location is in the search only because that is how people have always found tutors. Answer the real question and the location part turns out to matter much less than a parent expects.

Here is the honest position. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE; that part of our service exists only in India. UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the lesson on your child's own laptop in whatever room is quiet at 5pm. We would rather state that in the first screen than bury it, because a family who wants someone physically in the room should know before they fill in a form.

What replaces the in-room tutor is a far bigger pool of the right teacher. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist, a Maths Analysis and Approaches HL teacher who has taught Paper 3, an Economics teacher who has marked commentaries: those people are scarce in any one neighbourhood and plentiful across a whole timezone. The parent who insists on physical proximity is, in practice, choosing from whoever is prepared to drive to Hazza Bin Zayed Street this week, and then paying extra for the drive.

The comparison tables further down this page set the two options side by side on cost, travel, tutor pool and rescheduling, using rates the providers themselves publish. Read them and decide. Plenty of Al Wahda families still prefer someone at the kitchen table, and that is a legitimate preference; we simply do not sell it here.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar counted backwards, and what each date demands
paragraphs: Every Diploma deadline that matters sits inside a chain, and the chain runs backwards from the examination window. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, so the final Internal Assessment submissions, the Extended Essay upload and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition all land in the preceding months, and the school fixes its own internal dates earlier again to leave marking time. By the time a parent notices a problem in a report card, two or three of those internal dates have usually already gone.

This is why the useful question in November is not "how is my child doing" but "which of these dates is next, and what has to exist by then". A DP2 student eight weeks from a mock window needs timed papers. A DP2 student six weeks from an IA deadline needs a marked draft, not more teaching. A DP1 student needs neither, and selling either to them wastes a term.

The table below is the chain as an Abu Dhabi family will meet it. Note what it does not contain: specific IB examination and results dates. The IB publishes those to schools, and your child's coordinator holds the authoritative version against your candidate number. Any tutoring site quoting you an exact IB date, including this one, should be checked against the coordinator before you plan a holiday around it.

For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the position is different and public. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE centres, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Those timetables live on the boards' own sites and should be read there rather than copied from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve, by year group
paragraphs: Take a DP2 student in Term 1. Eight weeks is enough for one timed paper per subject with the marks dissected, one Internal Assessment lifted from unmarked draft to marked draft, and one genuine conversation about whether three Higher Levels is still the right shape. That is it. A plan that promises more in eight weeks is either padding the hours or ignoring the fact that the student also has school, Creativity Activity Service and sleep.

A DP1 student in the same eight weeks has a different list: the HL foundations that Year 13 will assume, the research question for at least one Internal Assessment, and the reading habit the Extended Essay will need. Nothing on that list is exam technique, and exam technique sold to a DP1 student in November is the single most common way Abu Dhabi families waste tutoring money.

A Year 11 student in an MYP or IGCSE year who is heading for the Diploma has a third list again: closing the specific gap between what they are finishing and what DP1 will assume. In maths that gap is usually algebraic fluency and function notation. In the sciences it is quantitative work and uncertainty. In English it is sustained analytical writing without a scaffold.

We write the eight-week plan down at the start, in plain language, with what the student will have produced by the end. If the plan is met early we say so and stop, and if the real problem turns out to be something a tutor cannot fix, such as a subject choice that was wrong from the start, we say that too and point you at the coordinator.

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs in central Abu Dhabi, and who publishes the figures
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a family budgets. A single weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor, at published market rates, lands somewhere between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month, and an exam-year specialist running one hour a week sits nearer AED 1,000 to AED 2,000. Bestimate's Dubai rate work for 2026 puts budget weekly tutoring at AED 240-600 a month and mid-range at AED 600-1,200, which is the clearest published monthly framing available in this market.

Hourly figures matter because they are how everyone quotes. The cheapest end of the online market, usually university students, is advertised from AED 45-65 by EdFlik and from AED 33-52 by Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors online are listed from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB by Unitors. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist work. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner-branded end. Those are the providers' own published numbers, read in October 2026, not ours.

The figure that deserves the most attention is the in-home band, quoted at AED 180-500 an hour, because part of it is travel rather than teaching. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide either by the teaching minutes and the gap is the travel premium. Over an eight-week sprint that premium is roughly the cost of four additional teaching hours.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, and we would be suspicious of a page that did while also claiming to be the cheapest. What we do instead is quote for the actual subject, level and frequency after a free trial lesson, so you are comparing a real number against the bands in the table rather than against a headline.

sections.heading: Al Wahda specifically: online against a tutor who drives to you
paragraphs: Al Wahda is a central, well-connected district, which cuts both ways. A tutor can reach it from most of the island in twenty minutes outside peak hours, and cannot reliably reach it in forty during the late-afternoon school and office overlap. Any parent who has waited on Airport Road at 5pm knows which of those is the real number on a Tuesday in term time.

That unreliability has a cost that is rarely priced. An in-home session booked for 4.30pm that starts at 4.50pm is not a 90-minute session, and across a term the lost minutes add up to a meaningful fraction of what you paid. An online session starts when the clock says so, from a bedroom desk, and the tutor is already set up with the past paper on screen.

The second difference is the pool. Ask for general maths help in central Abu Dhabi and you will find plenty of people. Ask for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, with experience of Paper 3, and the local list shortens dramatically. Ask for Chemistry HL in the same week your child's school has announced a mock, and it may be empty. Online matching does not solve scarcity, but it draws from a timezone instead of a postcode.

The third is the record. Screen-shared sessions leave annotated scripts, saved plans and a trail a parent can actually look at. A verbal session at the dining table leaves a page of working and a memory. In a Diploma year, the trail is what makes the next eight weeks planned rather than improvised.
