sections.heading: Home or online: the honest version of the decision
paragraphs: Having set out the case for online delivery, it is worth stating the case against it, because a page that pretends one format suits every child is not being useful. There are students for whom a visiting tutor is the better answer and the characteristics are fairly predictable.

A younger student who needs physical presence to stay on task is one. A student who will close a laptop and open something else the moment attention wanders is another, and a parent generally knows which of their children that describes. A student with a particular need that makes a screen itself an obstacle is a third. And a household without a quiet room, a reliable connection or a workable surface may find the practical obstacles larger than the travel loading, though all three are fixable and the last section of this page is about fixing them.

For the typical Diploma student in Baniyas, though, the arithmetic favours video and the reason is specialism rather than convenience. A Higher Level specialist in a given subject is scarce across the whole emirate. Requiring one of them to make a sixty-kilometre round trip for a single lesson reduces that already small set to almost nothing, and what families actually end up buying is a generalist who is available. Published budget rates start at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, and at that level the hour is a review of work already attempted, which is a different product sold under the same name.

So the recommendation is conditional rather than absolute. For a Diploma student working on criteria-based assessed pieces and Higher Level papers, match on subject and level over video and solve the room. For a student who cannot work without someone physically present, be honest about that and choose accordingly, understanding that the choice narrows the specialist pool and raises the rate. We will tell you during a free trial if we think the format is wrong for your child, which is a conversation we would rather have in week one.

sections.heading: Tuition or a school change? Separating two different decisions
paragraphs: Families in the mainland districts sometimes arrive at tuition as a substitute for a school decision they are avoiding, and it is worth separating the two because tuition cannot fix a structural problem at a school and should not be sold as though it can.

The questions that distinguish them are specific. Is the difficulty in one subject or across most of them? Does the school's own data show the student below their own earlier performance, or below the class? Is the subject taught by a specialist this year? Does the school offer the Higher Level combination the student needs for their intended route? Has the student's attendance or wellbeing changed? One subject with a diagnosable fault is a tuition problem. Most subjects declining at once, or a course not being taught by a specialist, is not.

ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, which is the right first stop for a family weighing a move. What a rating cannot tell you is subject-level: whether this year's Higher Level set has a specialist teacher, whether a department is carrying a vacancy, or whether the Diploma results in a particular subject group have been consistent. Those are questions for the school's admissions office and head of sixth form, and they are reasonable questions to ask.

Where a move is being considered mid-Diploma, the honest warning is that it is expensive. Internal assessment progress, supervisor relationships and the school's own deadline chain do not transfer cleanly, and a student changing school in DP2 loses time at the worst possible point. A tuition arrangement is sometimes the right way to hold a situation together until the end of the programme rather than the right way to fix it, and we would rather describe it that way than pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: Setting up: the room, the connection and the first month
paragraphs: If lessons are happening over video, the physical setup is part of the service rather than an afterthought, and a bad setup is the most common reason a good match underperforms in the first month. The requirements are modest and worth getting right before the first paid session.

The room: a door that closes, a surface large enough for an A4 pad and a textbook, and a chair at the right height. Not a bed, not a sofa, not the kitchen table during dinner preparation. The equipment: a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, because the student needs to see shared working at legible size; headphones, which halve the number of repeated sentences in a session; and a phone kept nearby purely to photograph written work for marking, which is the single most useful habit a family can establish.

The connection: test it at the time of day the lesson will actually happen, not at eleven in the morning. Evening performance in a busy residential district differs from midday performance, and a session that stutters for the first fortnight erodes a student's willingness before the teaching has had a chance. If the connection is genuinely poor at the preferred hour, moving the slot is cheaper than enduring it.

The first month, then, has a shape. Week one establishes the diagnosis and the habit of photographing written work. Week two is the first marked return, which is when a parent should look at what came back and ask whether it is marks against criteria or a tick. Week three tests whether the slot survives an ordinary bad week. Week four is a short review: has the fault frequency moved, is the written work actually happening, and is this format working for this child. Those four checks, asked plainly, prevent most of the quiet failures in this market.

sections.heading: The permit, the claims we do not make, and what we decline
paragraphs: A tutor who teaches a Baniyas household, whether they drive in off the Abu Dhabi–Al Ain road or appear on a screen in the study, needs a private tutoring work permit before any fee changes hands. The categories the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation admits are set out rather than left to judgement: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The instrument behind the scheme is Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It carries no charge at all — the ministry's own service page lists no fee — it runs for two years before renewal, and that page states a two working day completion time once an application goes in through the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system. Two days and nothing to pay is a low enough bar that a Baniyas parent can ask to see the permit without feeling they have asked for a favour.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, and press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording.

On status: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform. It holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. It is not a registered examination centre and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Our tutors are not described as current examiners for any board, because that status cannot be evidenced in a form a parent could check, and examiner language should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased papers.

On what we decline: producing any part of an assessed piece, at any price; supplying solutions for live assessed work; sitting with a student during an assessment; reproducing or distributing board material, which belongs to the organisations that publish it; and promising a grade, a points total or a university outcome, which no tutor can do. We also publish no star rating or satisfaction statistic, because doing so honestly would require the sample size, the date and the method alongside it. What we commit to is a diagnosis, marked work, a review date and a straight answer.

process.title: Decide the format honestly
process.description: Ask whether your child can work with somebody present on a screen rather than in the room. Most secondary students can; some cannot, and knowing which you have before paying matters more than any rate comparison. The free trial is partly there to test exactly this.

process.title: Ration the hours deliberately
process.description: Name the one or two subjects where an hour returns the most marks rather than the subject your child complains about most. If a core component such as Theory of Knowledge is unsupported, say so, because it is usually the best value available.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the setup already working
process.description: A closed door, a laptop, headphones, an A4 pad and a phone to photograph written work. One live video lesson with the matched specialist, who has read the marked evidence first. You decide afterwards, with no card required and nothing starting automatically.

process.title: Check four things in the first month
process.description: Whether written work is actually being set and returned marked against criteria, whether the slot survives an ordinary bad week, whether the fault frequency has moved, and whether the format suits the child. Four plain questions that prevent most quiet failures.

whyPoints.title: The travel loading is named rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run from AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. From Baniyas that gap is a journey, and a family paying it should know that is what it buys.

whyPoints.title: We will decline a subject
whyPoints.description: A subject already at the top of its range is a poor purchase and we say so. The question worth putting to any provider is which subject they would refuse, because the answer shows how they make decisions about your money.

whyPoints.title: Core components are treated as marks
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge carries twenty marks and the Extended Essay thirty-four, with word limits that decide whether the analysis survives. Both are routinely unfunded, and a short block on either often returns more than a fourth subject.

whyPoints.title: Supervision roles written down
whyPoints.description: School supervisor, private tutor and student each have a defined part, and only one of them produces text. We state that to the student directly, which removes the ambiguity in which honesty problems grow.

whyPoints.title: An honest case against our own format
whyPoints.description: Live video does not suit every child, and we would rather establish that during a free trial than in month three. Younger students and those who need physical presence to stay on task are genuine exceptions and we name them.

whyPoints.title: Figures with sources, and none of them ours
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to a published market source and dated October 2026, and no statistic appears without a date and a method behind it. IB Gram publishes no price list here and no rating anywhere.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a home tutor to Baniyas?
faqs.answer: No. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Baniyas or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors in the emirate do visit, and published rates for that run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors. From a district thirty kilometres from the island, a meaningful share of that difference is the journey.

faqs.question: What is the travel loading on a home tutor's rate in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the source, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online, all read in October 2026. The gap is not a quality premium; it is a journey, and from Baniyas it is a long one with unpredictable afternoon traffic, so the loading sits toward the upper end of those ranges. What the premium buys is physical presence, which genuinely helps some students.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject repays tuition best for a Baniyas household?
faqs.answer: Mathematics most consistently, because its faults are specific and diagnosable and because Higher Level Paper 3 is worth a fifth of the grade and is the least practised component in the Diploma. After that, any subject where the fault is structural rather than diffuse: evaluation missing in Economics, describing rather than answering in Business Management, writing without marked feedback in the sciences. And Theory of Knowledge, which carries twenty marks and almost nobody funds.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor supervise my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters. The Diploma assigns a supervisor at the school who advises on the research question, meets the student at defined points, comments on a draft within the organisation's rules, and authenticates the work. A private tutor sits outside that structure, authenticates nothing, and must not give advice that contradicts the supervisor. What a tutor legitimately adds is teaching the criteria, questioning a draft and marking practice work.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Extended Essay actually worth?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four, across focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking alone carries twelve of those, which is more than a third of the essay, and it tells a student exactly where the final fortnight should go. The essay also stops at four thousand words and nothing beyond that limit is marked, so compressing a finished argument late tends to cut precisely the analytical passages that criterion rewards.

faqs.question: Does the sector we live in within Baniyas change our options?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and not in the ways that matter. Your sector affects which school cluster is nearest, how long the afternoon return takes, and whether an evening trip to a tuition centre in Mussafah or out towards Khalifa City is plausible. It does not change the Diploma's criteria, the word limits, the weight of Higher Level Paper 3 or the scarcity of Higher Level specialists, which is a feature of the whole emirate rather than of any address inside it.

faqs.question: Is online tuition suitable for every Diploma student?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather say so. Live video works well for most secondary students and genuinely does not suit some: younger children, students who will close a laptop and open something else the moment attention wanders, and students for whom a screen is itself a barrier. A parent usually knows which of their children that describes. The free trial lesson exists partly to test the format rather than only the tutor, and we will give you our view.

faqs.question: What equipment does a Baniyas household actually need?
faqs.answer: A room with a door that closes, a surface big enough for an A4 pad and a textbook, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone so shared working is legible, headphones, which halve the number of repeated sentences in a session, and a phone kept nearby purely to photograph written work for marking. Test the connection at the hour the lesson will happen rather than at midday, because evening performance in a busy residential district is different.

faqs.question: Should we pay for tuition or consider changing school?
faqs.answer: Two separate decisions, and tuition cannot fix a structural problem. One subject with a diagnosable fault is a tuition problem. Most subjects declining at once, or a Higher Level course not being taught by a specialist this year, is not. ADEK publishes inspection outcomes for Abu Dhabi private schools, which is the right first stop, but a rating cannot tell you who teaches a particular set this year. Ask the school that directly.

faqs.question: Is it worth changing school during DP2?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the cost is higher than families expect. Internal assessment progress, supervisor relationships and the school's own deadline chain do not transfer cleanly, and a move in the final year removes time at the worst possible point. Sometimes a tuition arrangement is the right way to hold a situation together to the end of the programme rather than the right way to fix it, and we would rather describe it in those terms than imply more.

faqs.question: What does a month of Diploma tuition cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: In monthly terms, the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates roughly AED 240 to 600 for a weekly hour at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those were read in October 2026, belong to the market, and are not our price list.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see the document rather than accepting an assurance.

faqs.question: Why is Theory of Knowledge such good value to support?
faqs.answer: Because it carries twenty marks — ten for the essay and ten for the exhibition — against published instruments with strict word limits of sixteen hundred and nine hundred and fifty words, and most students receive very little structured teaching on how those instruments are applied to what they have written. Three to five sessions aimed exactly at that often returns more per dirham than the same money added to a fourth subject, and virtually no household budgets for it.

faqs.question: What will you refuse to do for my child's assessed work?
faqs.answer: Produce any part of it, at any price. We will not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions for live assessed work, or sit with a student during an assessment. We also do not reproduce board material, which belongs to the organisations that publish it. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on your child's whole entry.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-baniyas.closingHeading: Name the format, ration the hours, check the marking
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-baniyas.closingBody: Three decisions settle this, and none of them is about distance. Decide whether your child can work with a tutor on a screen rather than in the room, because that is a real question and the trial lesson is partly there to answer it. Decide which one or two subjects return the most marks per hour, and consider whether a core component is unsupported. Then check, in week two, whether written work is coming back marked against published criteria or merely ticked. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, and the trial is one lesson.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a subject problem
paragraphs: Parents plan Diploma support around the final examinations, which UAE schools sit in the May session. The pressure does not land there. It lands in the middle, across a nine-month stretch where four or five Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, Creativity Activity Service requirements and two rounds of mocks arrive in an order nobody has written down for the student in one place.

Unlike the British pathway, almost none of that is published nationally. The IGCSE calendar is set by examination boards with entry deadlines and dated timetables. The Diploma's internal calendar is set by your child's school, issued in a document in the first week of the course, and never looked at again by anybody. That single difference explains most of the panic that reaches us from Corniche households in January.

The chain also runs in a particular order, and the links are sequential rather than parallel. A science Internal Assessment needs data collected while laboratory access exists, which puts the method decision months before the write-up. A mathematics exploration needs a topic narrow enough to finish, which is a decision rather than a task, and students defer decisions far longer than tasks. The Extended Essay needs a supervised draft before the Internal Assessments start arriving.

Because no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which returns an error to automated checking, this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publishes no specific IB date at all. Confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative version for your child's cohort. A date restated on a website is not a source to act on.

The Corniche adds a practical layer rather than an academic one. This is apartment living along the waterfront, with schools a short drive inland towards Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and Al Khalidiyah. Journeys are short but building access, visitor parking and lift waits are real obstacles to anything that involves somebody arriving, and none of that appears in an hourly rate. A tutor held at reception for ten minutes has still charged the hour, and across a term that adds up to several sessions of waiting.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video. The rest of this page is the calendar: the two years month by month, the Extended Essay chain, Theory of Knowledge, Creativity Activity Service, the weeks Ramadan and the spring break remove, and what each phase costs. Every dirham figure carries the source it came from and the month it was read.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-corniche.programmesIntro: The four IB stages have very different calendars, and only one of them is genuinely crowded. Support is worth most where the deadlines are densest and cheapest where there are none.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment and no deadline pressure, which makes this the only IB stage with genuine calendar space. The work worth doing is arithmetic fluency and sentence construction, both of which respond to short frequent practice and neither of which is urgent. Nothing has to be fitted around anything else.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche primary pupils attend schools a short drive inland and are commonly home by 15:00 with the afternoon clear. Two short sessions a week fit easily and work better at this age than one hour. This is the stage where the whole year is available rather than only the gaps between deadlines.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with extended tasks across the year and the Personal Project in the final year, assessed against three criteria of eight marks each. The calendar is entirely internal, so unit deadlines cluster unpredictably and the Personal Project dominates the last year.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students on the Corniche have the earliest home-by time in the household and the widest choice of hours. Use the late afternoon rather than the evening: criteria-based writing degrades badly when attempted at nine at night, and the Personal Project needs a Saturday morning rather than a weekday hour.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service, to a maximum of 45 points including up to three from the core. The internal deadline chain across the middle of the two years is the genuinely difficult calendar in the whole continuum.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche Diploma students travel inland to schools in Al Bateen, Al Mushrif or Al Khalidiyah, and several run study periods after a 15:30 finish. That gives a workable 17:30 or 19:30, and the deciding factor is usually which hour the student can write in rather than which hour the road allows.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with career-related study and a reflective project. Where a school offers it, the Diploma courses inside are examined on the same papers with the same weightings and the same Internal Assessments, so their internal deadline chain is identical even though the overall qualification differs.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi schools run the Career-related Programme, so most Corniche families are comparing the Diploma against A Levels or an American diploma. If your child is on it, say so when booking, because the deadline map a tutor plans around is the Diploma one.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-corniche.subjectsIntro: Each Diploma subject has its own internal deadline and its own point in the year where support is worth most. These are the ones Corniche families ask about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is twenty per cent and needs a topic narrowed early, because a question too broad to finish damages four of the five criteria at once. At Higher Level, Paper 3 needs format practice across months rather than weeks, which makes it a first-year commitment.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator fluency is examinable on every paper and can be drilled in a handful of sessions at any point in the calendar, which makes it ideal work for a crowded term. The exploration follows the same early-narrowing rule as the other course.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The investigation requires data collected while laboratory access exists, so the method decision sits months before the write-up. Paper 2 at forty-four per cent is the heaviest component and rewards command-term work, which can happen in any term.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same investigation constraint as Physics, with the added point that a research question must be narrow enough to measure in the laboratory time available. Equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the content to secure before the second-year mock cycle.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest specification in the science group, which means recall work has to be spaced across both years rather than compressed. The investigation shares the laboratory-access constraint, and terminology precision is the slow build that decides the final grade.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The commentary portfolio needs articles found and diagrams planned per commentary, and three commentaries treated as one late task is the standard failure. Higher Level Paper 3 arrives as a quantitative demand that needs its own practice in the second year.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral has a school-set date and is prepared worst because it feels informal. It needs extracts chosen and a global issue settled weeks ahead, then rehearsing aloud. At Higher Level the essay adds another internal deadline on top.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two components with separate school-set deadlines: the exhibition of three objects and the sixteen-hundred-word essay on a prescribed title. Both compete for hours with six subjects, which is why Theory of Knowledge is the first thing dropped and the easiest core marks to lose.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised research with a chain of school-set milestones. The marks are decided by the research question in the first fortnight, which is why early hours are worth several times late ones and why a late start is almost impossible to rescue.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: MYP and DP ab initio or B
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. It runs steadily all year rather than peaking, which makes it the subject most suited to short regular practice and least suited to an intensive.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-corniche.regionsIntro: The Corniche runs along the city's waterfront, with Al Khalidiyah and Al Markaziyah immediately inland. These are the neighbouring districts and what differs practically for a Diploma family in each.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Immediately inland, sharing schools and the same tower-living logistics. Al Khalidiyah households face the same building access and visitor parking constraints, which is why both districts lean towards online delivery more than the villa communities do.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: West along the coast, holding several long-established schools Corniche students attend. Journeys are short in both directions, so the limiting factor on a session is the school's own study-period arrangement rather than the road.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Further inland with more established school provision. Corniche students travelling here are home slightly later, commonly between 15:45 and 16:15, which shifts their Diploma sessions towards 19:30.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: East of Al Mushrif with its own schools and a comparable commute profile. Corniche and Al Nahyan students frequently share schools, so their internal deadline calendars coincide more closely than most pairs of Abu Dhabi districts.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Tower living across a bridge, with its own schools. Al Reem Diploma students finish on broadly similar timetables, which means they want the same early-evening specialist hours Corniche families want.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island

regions.name: Khalifa City

sections.heading: Can you get an IB home tutor in the Corniche, and does the format matter
paragraphs: In-home tutoring exists in this part of Abu Dhabi and the market price is public. In-home one-to-one visits across the Emirates are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, per the Bestimate rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. The Corniche is central, so distance is not the obstacle here.

What is an obstacle is everything else about tower living. Visitor parking, building access, lift waits and reception procedures all consume time that belongs to the hour, and none of it appears in anybody's quote. Families in Al Khalidiyah and along the Corniche report this more than families in the villa communities, which is why online delivery is more common here than in Khalifa City or Al Raha Gardens.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and that is the position across every country page on this site. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own school material on screen, at an hour chosen by the household rather than by a tutor's route.

The honest case for a visit remains and it is worth naming. A younger child, or a student who will not stay at the table without an adult physically present, benefits from presence in a way no video quality replaces. If that describes your child you want a provider who does visits, and we will tell you so rather than talk you into a format that cannot work.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years, month by month
paragraphs: This is the map most Diploma families never see. It is approximate because every school sets its own internal dates, so take the structure and write your school's actual deadlines into it. What matters is the shape: a light first autumn, a crowded first summer, a very crowded second autumn and winter, and a second spring where everything becomes conversion.

The pattern that causes trouble is the one where nothing happens for the first two terms. A student who coasts through the first Diploma autumn and spring arrives at the first summer with an Extended Essay question unchosen, an exploration topic undecided and no Internal Assessment method agreed. From that point every month contains two things that should have been one, and the student never catches up.

The opposite pattern, which costs less and works better, front-loads the decisions. Choose the Extended Essay question in the first spring. Settle the exploration topic before the first summer. Agree the science investigation method while laboratory access is easy. None of those is a large piece of work; all of them are decisions, and decisions deferred are what make the second year unmanageable.

Use the table as a conversation rather than a schedule. Sit down with your child and the school's own deadline list, and mark the three weeks in the year where two deadlines collide. In most households they are the same weeks every year, and knowing which ones they are lets you front-load support instead of reacting to it in the fortnight it arrives.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay chain, link by link
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is four thousand words of supervised independent research in one subject, combining with Theory of Knowledge for up to three bonus points towards the maximum of forty-five. It is also the component where the gap between an early start and a late one is widest, because the marks are substantially decided by the research question and the question is chosen at the beginning.

A question too broad cannot be answered in four thousand words, and the essay then reads as a survey rather than an investigation. A question with no accessible sources cannot be researched at all, which is discovered three months in. A question with no genuine inquiry in it produces a competent descriptive essay that cannot reach the upper bands however well written. All three failures are set at the start and none can be repaired later.

The chain of milestones is school-set and sequential. Subject chosen, supervisor assigned, question drafted, question narrowed and approved, sources gathered, first draft, supervisor feedback, reflections recorded, final submission. Each link depends on the previous one, which means a three-week slip at the start becomes a three-week slip at the end, arriving in the same term as Internal Assessment final submissions.

A tutor's useful contribution here is at the front of the chain rather than the back. Narrowing a question, testing whether sources exist, and checking that there is a genuine inquiry rather than a description are all work that takes two or three sessions and changes the ceiling of the essay. No tutor at IB Gram will write the Extended Essay, draft it or edit it to completion, and the school supervisor signs the work off.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: two components, two separate deadlines
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the core component students take least seriously and it carries real marks. It has two parts with separate school-set deadlines: an exhibition of three objects, and an essay of up to sixteen hundred words on a prescribed title. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three bonus points towards the Diploma total of forty-five.

The exhibition is usually taken in the first year and the essay in the second. Both reward specificity and both are routinely answered abstractly, which is the single reason most students score below their potential on them. An exhibition that discusses knowledge in general terms scores badly; one that uses three real, particular objects and says something precise about each scores well.

The essay works the same way. It is written on a prescribed title and the marks go to a clear claim held against real, specific examples drawn from the student's own experience of knowledge. Students who write about epistemology in the abstract produce fluent paragraphs that cannot reach the upper bands. Students who write about a specific disputed finding, a particular artwork, a named historical argument, do far better with less sophistication.

A tutor is useful here as an argument coach rather than a content teacher, and the time required is small. Three or four sessions on holding a claim, choosing real examples and structuring a response usually moves this component more than anything else available, because so little targeted teaching happens at school. The writing stays entirely the student's own.

sections.heading: Creativity Activity Service is a calendar requirement nobody schedules
paragraphs: Creativity Activity Service is a Diploma requirement rather than an extra, which means it cannot be dropped to make room for revision. It runs across both years, consumes two to four hours a week, requires reflections to be recorded as it goes, and has to be completed before the Diploma can be awarded. Students treat it as a box to be filled in later, and later is always the term with everything else in it.

The failure mode is specific and avoidable. A student does plenty of activity and records none of it, then spends a fortnight in the second year reconstructing reflections from memory. The reconstruction is obvious, the coordinator sends it back, and the fortnight is lost from a term that had no spare fortnight in it. Recording as you go takes ten minutes a week.

For Corniche families there is a practical wrinkle. Creativity Activity Service commitments are often scheduled at school immediately after the day ends, which extends the effective day for students travelling in from the waterfront to Al Mushrif or Khalifa City. That is a scheduling fact worth supplying when booking: a student with a Tuesday commitment is not available at 17:30 on a Tuesday however convenient that looks.

No tutor should be writing Creativity Activity Service reflections, and nobody at IB Gram does. What a tutor can usefully do is include it in the deadline map at the first session, so that it stops being invisible. A requirement that appears on the same sheet as the Internal Assessment dates gets done; a requirement nobody has written down does not.

sections.heading: The May session, and why no IB date appears on this page
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and that is the only thing about IB external dates this page will state. The reason is specific: ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or deadline in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources exist and they disagree, which is exactly why they are not good enough for a page a parent might act on.

That matters more than it sounds. A wrong date on a tutoring website is not a stylistic failure; it is a parent planning a family holiday across an examination week, or a student revising towards a deadline that moved. Several pages in this market publish specific IB dates with no source attached. We would rather publish nothing and tell you where the authoritative version lives.

The authoritative version lives with your school's Diploma coordinator. They hold the session dates for your child's cohort, the internal deadline list, the upload deadlines for internal components and the arrangements for study leave. Ask for all of it in writing in the first term. Most schools issue it and most students never pass it on, which is how a household ends up planning around guesswork.

For the British pathway, by contrast, the dates are published and this site states them: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson runs May, June and November with results dates that can be cited. The difference in how the two systems publish is itself worth knowing when you are planning a household.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the spring break and the weeks that are not there
paragraphs: A plan built on calendar weeks rather than teaching weeks will break, and in the UAE the gap between the two is large. Most Abu Dhabi private schools run three terms with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break towards the end of March, and the spring break falls squarely in the weeks when Diploma revision should be at its most intense.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls in the spring, which means it increasingly overlaps the run-up to the May session. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a poor teaching window because the household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly between 20:30 and 22:00, works much better and is easy to staff on video.

Some families would rather pause for the month and resume afterwards, and that is a legitimate choice we would rather you made deliberately than drifted into. Paying for sessions nobody attends is the worst available outcome. What matters is deciding in advance, because a month lost by accident at that point in the Diploma is expensive and a month paused on purpose is manageable.

Do the arithmetic before agreeing any plan. Take the session month, subtract the spring break, subtract the weeks your school has reserved for study leave, subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions then, and subtract travel you already know about. Most Corniche families find the real figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and the plan that follows is more honest for it.

sections.heading: What each phase costs, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Diploma support costs more per grade point in the second-year spring than in the first-year autumn, which is a market reality rather than a judgement. Demand concentrates before the session, the formats families want then are intensive, and specialists able to work on a named component are the scarcest part of the market. Buying earlier is cheaper for the same outcome.

The Abu Dhabi bands, with sources named, run as follows. University-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors have been quoted to AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, and monthly in-home packages have been seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. None of these figures is our price list; they are the market, published so any quote can be measured.

What we will not claim: no provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK, MoHRE or board approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay, composes a Theory of Knowledge essay or records Creativity Activity Service reflections.

process.title: Ask the school for the internal deadline list
process.description: Most Diploma schools issue one in the first term, and most students never show it to a parent. That document plus the session month is the whole planning input. If it has gone missing, email the Diploma coordinator; the request is routine and answered within a day or two.

process.title: Mark the collision weeks
process.description: Put the internal deadlines beside the mock dates and any Creativity Activity Service commitments, and mark the three weeks where two things land together. In most households they are the same weeks every year, which means support can be front-loaded rather than bought in a panic.

process.title: Send a marked script or a draft
process.description: A mock paper tells us where marks are being lost and in what pattern. An Internal Assessment draft tells us which criterion is weak. Those are different diagnoses needing different specialists, so say which one you are sending and what you are worried about.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, before any payment and with no card details taken. Ask the tutor what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve on the evidence in front of them. A specific answer is the best signal you will get about everything that follows.

process.title: Count the real weeks before committing
process.description: Subtract the spring break, study leave, Ramadan if you reduce sessions then, and any travel. Most Corniche families find the usable number four to six weeks lower than their first estimate. Agree the plan against that figure and against a stated objective.

whyPoints.title: The whole calendar, not just the session
whyPoints.description: The hardest part of the Diploma is the internal deadline chain across the middle of the two years, and it is school-set rather than published. We ask for it, put it on one sheet with the mock dates, and name the weeks where two deadlines collide.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. We name the May session and nothing more precise, and we point you at your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative version.

whyPoints.title: Front-loaded decisions, not late rescue
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay question, the exploration topic and the science method are decisions rather than tasks, and deferring them is what makes a second year unmanageable. Two or three sessions in the first year beats a term of rescue work later.

whyPoints.title: Tower logistics taken seriously
whyPoints.description: On the Corniche the obstacle to a visiting tutor is parking, building access and lift waits rather than distance, and none of that appears in an hourly rate. Online delivery removes it, which is why this part of Abu Dhabi uses it more than the villa communities do.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure here belongs to a named provider or a published rate table with the month it was read, and none is our price list. Three of the best-ranked pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: No provider can guarantee a grade including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, there is no Abu Dhabi office, and nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay or records Creativity Activity Service reflections.

faqs.question: When should an IB home tutor in the Corniche be brought in during the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and for a specific reason. The first Diploma year is the lightest part of the calendar and the point at which three decisions have to be made: the Extended Essay question, the mathematics exploration topic and the science investigation method. Two or three sessions on those in the first year prevents the second year becoming unmanageable. The common pattern of buying intensively in the final spring is the most expensive and least effective shape available.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a Corniche apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one to one over live video with your child's own school material on screen. On the Corniche the practical argument for that is not distance but tower logistics: visitor parking, building access and lift waits all consume time that belongs to the hour and appear in nobody's quoted rate.

faqs.question: Can you tell me the exact IB session dates for a Corniche school?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or deadline in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree with each other. A wrong date on a tutoring page is not a stylistic failure; it is a family planning a holiday across an examination week. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative dates for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: What is the hardest part of the Diploma calendar?
faqs.answer: The middle, not the end. Across roughly nine months in the second half of the course, four or five Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, Creativity Activity Service requirements and two rounds of mocks all arrive. None of it is published nationally; it is set by your school and issued in a document the student was given in the first week. Getting that document is the single most useful planning action available to a parent.

faqs.question: How early does the Extended Essay question need to be settled?
faqs.answer: In the first Diploma year, ideally the spring. The marks are substantially decided by the question, and three failures are all set at the start: a question too broad to answer in four thousand words, a question with no accessible sources, or a question with no genuine inquiry in it. None of those can be repaired later, because the chain of milestones is sequential and a three-week slip at the beginning becomes a three-week slip at the final submission.

faqs.question: Do Corniche Diploma students lose easy core points on TOK?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is unusually efficient because so little targeted teaching happens at school. It has two components with separate school-set deadlines, an exhibition of three objects and an essay of up to sixteen hundred words on a prescribed title, and together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three bonus points. Both components reward specific real examples and punish abstraction. Three or four sessions on holding a claim and choosing examples usually moves it more than content work anywhere else.

faqs.question: Can Creativity Activity Service be caught up at the end?
faqs.answer: Badly, and it costs a fortnight you will not have. The requirement runs across both years, needs reflections recorded as the activity happens, and has to be complete before the Diploma is awarded. Students who do plenty of activity and record none of it end up reconstructing reflections from memory in the second year; the reconstruction is obvious, the coordinator returns it, and the lost fortnight falls in the term with everything else in it. Ten minutes a week prevents all of that.

faqs.question: Which Corniche households have the latest usable session hour?
faqs.answer: Those travelling furthest inland. Students attending schools in Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah are home earliest and can use 17:30. Students travelling to Al Mushrif are commonly home between 15:45 and 16:15, which shifts them towards 19:30. Students attending island or Khalifa City schools are the latest and almost always settle on a fixed 19:30 slot for the year. Supply the actual arrival time when booking rather than the preferred start time.

faqs.question: How many usable weeks are there before the May session?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. Subtract the spring break, which most Abu Dhabi schools take towards the end of March. Subtract the weeks your school has reserved for study leave. Subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions then. Subtract travel you already know about. Most Corniche families find the real figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and doing that arithmetic before agreeing a plan is what stops a schedule collapsing in the spring.

faqs.question: Can Diploma tutoring continue through Ramadan here?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the hour changed. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a weak teaching window because the household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly between 20:30 and 22:00, works far better and is straightforward on video because nobody is driving late at night. Families who prefer to pause can do that; the important thing is deciding in advance rather than losing the weeks by accident.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a Diploma tutor produce?
faqs.answer: A single sheet, not a lesson plan. Every internal deadline the school has published, every external component, the Creativity Activity Service commitments, and the three weeks in the year where two of them collide. Everything after that is teaching against a known map rather than reacting to whatever arrived on Sunday. Families are frequently surprised that a first session is spent on administration, and it is reliably the most valuable hour of the engagement.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying specialist rates in the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is where the calendar changes the answer. In the first year the need is content and habits, which a qualified subject tutor at the middle band, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on published rates, delivers perfectly. The specialist band is worth paying in the second-year spring when a named component in a named paper needs somebody who teaches it. Paying top rates early is the most common overspend in Diploma support.

faqs.question: My son's mock went badly, so what should the next four weeks do?
faqs.answer: Diagnose first, then convert. Go through the script mark by mark and sort every lost mark into content not known, command term misread, reasoning not shown, or ran out of time. The tally decides the plan and routinely contradicts what he believes went wrong. A timing-heavy script does not need more content teaching; it needs marks-per-minute arithmetic and practice abandoning a stuck question. That is two sessions of work and often worth a grade boundary.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with an Internal Assessment draft in the busy term?
faqs.answer: With feedback, yes; with writing, never. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the research question is answerable, ask what the data actually shows, and say why a section is weak so the student can fix it. Nobody at IB Gram writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay or produces assessed work at any price. The school supervisor signs the work off and should know outside support exists.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff a 19:30 slot in the busy spring?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than offering an hour that will not work. Late weekday evenings before the May session are the tightest window in the Abu Dhabi year, and Corniche households compete with Al Reem, Al Bateen and Saadiyat families for them. Common subjects usually match within a few days; a narrow Higher Level component at a fixed hour can take longer. Hearing that early leaves you time to look elsewhere while it still matters.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-corniche.closingHeading: Get the deadline list, then we plan backwards
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-corniche.closingBody: One document makes the difference: your school's internal deadline list for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Send it with the mock dates and the most recent marked script, and we will put the whole year on one sheet, name the weeks where deadlines collide, and tell you which decisions need making now rather than in March. Then your child meets a Diploma specialist on a free trial lesson before anything is paid. Lessons run live online, one to one, at an hour a Corniche household can keep.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-eastern-mangr.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma courses across the subject groups at Standard and Higher Level, and support the core components within the boundary set out on this page. Sessions are placed against the school's own published deadlines rather than spread evenly across a term.

intro.heading: The core has its own calendar, and it governs the year
paragraphs: Families plan Diploma tuition around subjects and then collide with the core. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS each run on their own schedule, each consumes weekends rather than evenings, and together they produce two or three weeks a year in which a student can do almost nothing else. A tuition plan that treats the year as evenly busy will be rescheduled during exactly those weeks, which are the weeks it was most needed.

Eastern Mangroves sits on the north-eastern edge of Abu Dhabi island, waterfront apartment living beside the mangrove channels and the promenade, close to Al Salam Street. There is no school in the development, so every student travels — mostly to Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and the central districts, some out to the Khalifa City corridor — and the afternoon is correspondingly long. That reduces the week's slack, which makes placing sessions well more important rather than less.

The core is also where the marks nobody budgets for sit. The Extended Essay carries thirty-four marks across five criteria, and critical thinking alone accounts for twelve of them — more than a third of the essay. Theory of Knowledge carries twenty, ten for the essay and ten for the exhibition, both marked against published instruments. Those are substantial numbers attached to components that receive comparatively little structured teaching in most schools and almost no household spending anywhere.

Word limits are part of the calendar rather than a formatting detail, because they are what makes a late draft unsalvageable. The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay stops at sixteen hundred and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. Markers stop reading at the limit, so a student compressing a finished argument into the limit in the final week cuts the analytical passages — which is to say, the passages the largest criterion rewards.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Eastern Mangroves or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a calendar-driven plan that is a practical advantage: a video session can be moved to a different evening in a deadline week, run post-Iftar during Ramadan, continue while a family is travelling, and does not fail because a tutor is held up on Al Salam Street.

What follows is the core's calendar in usable form. The two-year chain across the three components. The Extended Essay milestone by milestone with the risk of arriving late at each. Theory of Knowledge and its two windows. An honest answer to the most common request we receive, which is for help only in the final stretch. What happens after results. When to pause sessions deliberately. The Eastern Mangroves afternoon. And the dates and limits we will not cross, including the examination dates we decline to publish.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-eastern-mangr.programmesIntro: The core components are what distinguish the Diploma from every alternative route, and they are the part a family is least likely to have planned for. These are the three, with their calendar shapes.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay
programmes.description: An independent research essay of up to four thousand words in a chosen subject, supervised at the school, marked against five criteria totalling thirty-four marks: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking carries twelve of those marks on its own.
programmes.countryNote: Its milestones span a year and each consumes a weekend, which makes it the single clearest argument for collecting the school's published deadline calendar at the start of DP1. For an Eastern Mangroves household with a long afternoon, those weekends are the real capacity being spent.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Two assessments against published instruments: an exhibition, with a commentary of up to nine hundred and fifty words, and an essay of up to sixteen hundred words on a prescribed title. Ten marks each. Taught across both years, usually in a weekly lesson, and assessed at two specific points.
programmes.countryNote: The component with the best return on a small amount of support and the one least often bought. Students generally receive little structured teaching on how the published instrument is actually applied to what they have written, which is exactly where three to five sessions make a difference.

programmes.name: Creativity, Activity, Service
programmes.description: A required programme of experiences and a project, not graded but necessary for the award of the Diploma. It occupies fixed afternoons and weekends in most schools, with a reflective record that students defer and then have to reconstruct.
programmes.countryNote: CAS is the most common reason a particular weekday is unavailable for tuition all year, and the most common reason a family's calendar has fewer usable evenings than they assumed. Asking the school which days it occupies, and whether that is fixed, is the first scheduling question of DP1.

programmes.name: The six subjects alongside the core
programmes.description: Three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each with its own internally assessed component carrying published criteria and word limits, and each with external papers at the end. Eighty per cent or so of each subject grade sits in those papers in most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The subject internal assessments and the core deadlines are set by the same school and frequently land in the same weeks, which is what produces the two or three impossible weeks a year. Mapping them together at the start of the year is the single most useful planning act available.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-eastern-mangr.subjectsIntro: These are the core and subject components with a calendar position, and what each needs at which point. Reading them as a chain rather than a list is what makes a plan possible.

subjects.name: Extended Essay research question
subjects.description: The decision that fixes the ceiling. A question too broad cannot be answered in four thousand words, and one too narrow cannot support the critical thinking criterion. Discussed with the school supervisor, who approves it within the school's process.

subjects.name: Extended Essay research and reading
subjects.description: Where the material for the critical thinking criterion is gathered, including the counter-evidence that an argument has to handle. Research done late produces an essay that asserts rather than weighs, which caps the largest criterion.

subjects.name: Extended Essay first full draft
subjects.description: The one formal opportunity for supervisor feedback within the rules, and students waste it by submitting an outline. A draft close to complete attracts feedback on substance; an outline attracts feedback on structure, which the student already knew.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge exhibition
subjects.description: Three objects and a commentary of up to nine hundred and fifty words, marked out of ten against the published instrument. Students treat the objects as the task; the commentary is where the marks are, and it is short enough that every sentence counts.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge essay
subjects.description: Up to sixteen hundred words on a prescribed title, marked out of ten. The common failure is writing about the topic rather than about knowledge, which is a conceptual misunderstanding rather than a writing problem and is correctable in two sessions.

subjects.name: Subject internal assessments
subjects.description: Each with its own criteria and limits: three thousand words for the sciences investigation, twenty marks for the mathematics exploration, twenty-five for the History internal assessment. They cluster with the core deadlines, which is what creates the impossible weeks.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3 preparation
subjects.description: Worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade in mathematics and in several sciences, and the last thing scheduled. It needs full papers sat to time in the term before the run-in rather than inside it.

subjects.name: Mocks
subjects.levels: DP2, usually a term before the series
subjects.description: Diagnostic rather than predictive, and frequently sat before the syllabus is complete. The week after a mock is the most valuable in the term because the scripts are the freshest evidence available all year.

subjects.name: The final run-in
subjects.description: Rehearsal only. Timing, exact form, command terms, calculator recording and question selection all improve reliably. Content never taught and underlying fluency do not, and we say so rather than implying otherwise.

subjects.name: After results
subjects.description: Reviewing a result, understanding what a remark or enquiry involves, and deciding whether to sit a subsequent session. All of it governed by the school and the organisation's own published deadlines rather than by any tutoring provider.

sections.heading: The core's two-year chain
paragraphs: Schools sequence the core differently, so the table is a typical shape rather than a rule, and your school's published calendar is the authority. What is consistent is that the chain runs continuously and does not pause for subject assessments, which is what produces the collisions.

The pattern worth noticing is that the core's heaviest moments are concentrated in the middle of the programme, roughly from the second half of DP1 to the middle of DP2. That is also when subject content is heaviest and when the subject internal assessments fall. Students therefore end up writing both the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay in the busiest months of the two years, and almost every version of the problem a family brings us in DP2 traces back to that overlap.

The remedy is unglamorous and effective: collect the published calendar in the first week of DP1, mark every core and subject deadline on a single household calendar, and look at which weeks collide. Those weeks are the ones to protect, and the only way to protect them is to do work earlier. The Extended Essay research question chosen in the second half of DP1 rather than at the start of DP2 is the single largest piece of protection available.

The table also shows where tuition belongs. Not spread evenly, but placed at the points where a student is making a decision that caps a criterion — the research question, the choice of Theory of Knowledge title, the first draft — and at the two or three points where a bounded block addresses a specific assessment. Even support across a Diploma year is almost always the wrong shape, and it is the shape most providers sell.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, milestone by milestone
paragraphs: Thirty-four marks, five criteria, four thousand words, a year of elapsed time and a single formal feedback opportunity. The Extended Essay rewards early work more clearly than any other component in the Diploma, and it punishes lateness in a way that cannot be recovered by effort in the final fortnight.

The criterion weighting explains why. Critical thinking carries twelve of the thirty-four marks — more than a third — and critical thinking is a function of the research. An essay built on material gathered in a hurry can describe and cannot weigh, because weighing requires counter-evidence the student never collected. Polishing presentation in the final week reaches four marks at most. No amount of late writing reaches the twelve.

The word limit compounds it. Markers stop at four thousand words, so a student who has written five thousand must cut a thousand, and under time pressure they cut the analysis rather than the description, because description feels like content and analysis feels like padding. That is precisely backwards against the criteria, and it is the most common self-inflicted loss on the component.

The boundary applies throughout and we state it to students directly. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a question can support them, read the student's own draft, ask the questions that expose an unsupported claim and name the criterion a section is failing. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece or produce any part of it. The school supervisor is the one inside the formal structure and the one who authenticates the work; a private tutor authenticates nothing and must never give advice that contradicts them.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: two assessments, two windows
paragraphs: Twenty marks sit here, split evenly between an exhibition and an essay, and both are marked against published instruments rather than against a marking grid of the kind students are used to from subjects. That difference is the reason students who write well elsewhere score poorly here: they produce a competent piece of writing about the wrong thing.

The exhibition comes first in most schools. Three objects, and a commentary of up to nine hundred and fifty words explaining how each connects to a prescribed prompt. Students treat selecting the objects as the task. The marks are in the commentary, and at that length every sentence has to do work: a paragraph of introduction is a tenth of the available space spent on nothing. A single session on how the instrument reads a commentary typically changes a student's whole approach.

The essay comes later, up to sixteen hundred words on a prescribed title, and the characteristic failure is writing about the topic rather than about knowledge. A title concerning historical evidence invites an essay about history; the marks are for an argument about how knowledge in history is produced and justified. Students who have not had that distinction made explicit write fluent, well-organised, low-scoring essays, and no amount of editing rescues one because the problem is the subject of the sentences.

Both are strong candidates for a short bounded block, which is why we recommend them more often than families expect. Three to five sessions, timed to each window, aimed at how the published instrument is actually applied to what the student has written. Against twenty marks and almost no structured teaching elsewhere, that is the best return available anywhere in the Diploma per dirham spent, and virtually nobody buys it.

sections.heading: 'We only want help for the final stretch'
paragraphs: This is the most common request we receive from Abu Dhabi families and it deserves a straight answer rather than an upsell. The honest version has two halves, and both are true at the same time.

The first half: a final-stretch block genuinely works on four things. Timing, through full papers sat to the clock with per-question timings recorded. Command-term discipline, which is a vocabulary problem solvable in two sessions. Exact form, rounding and notation habits, which are a single instruction consistently enforced across marked work. And question selection, including the rule that no part of a question is abandoned before the given working is attempted. On a paper where the content is broadly known, those together often produce a double-digit mark swing, and that is a real purchase with a real effect.

The second half: it does not rebuild underlying fluency, teach content that was never taught, or improve an internally assessed piece that has already been submitted. Fluency needs months of practice capacity that a final term does not contain. Untaught content needs teaching time the week no longer holds. And a submitted Extended Essay or exploration is finished — the marks are set, and a tutor who implies otherwise is describing something that would be malpractice anyway.

So the answer we give is conditional. Send the last marked script. If it shows technique faults — misread commands, early rounding, unrecorded working, unfinished papers — a final-stretch block is the right purchase and we will scope it, including a written list of what it will not attempt. If it shows content gaps spread across topics, the honest purchase is a plan for a later session rather than this one, and we will say so and decline the booking. Families find the second answer unwelcome and, in our experience, remember it.

sections.heading: After results: what happens and who acts
paragraphs: Results arrive and a family has a short period in which several decisions have to be made, usually with incomplete information. Knowing the shape of that period in advance converts it from a scramble into a sequence, and none of the steps belongs to a tutoring provider.

The first thing to understand is who acts at each stage. The school holds the relationship with the organisation and makes any enquiry about results on a candidate's behalf; a family cannot do it directly, and a tutor has no role whatsoever. Deadlines for enquiries and remarks are published and short, and they are the reason a disappointing result needs a conversation with the school within days rather than weeks. The coordinator is the single point of contact for all of it.

The second is that an enquiry is not an appeal against difficulty. It is a request for a specific review process, with its own fee and its own possible outcomes, including no change and, in some processes, a downward one. The school will explain what applies and what the realistic prospects are, and that conversation should happen before a request is made rather than afterwards. We are not a party to any of it and will not advise on the merits.

The third is the subsequent-session question. A candidate may sit a later session, and how internally assessed marks are handled between sessions is a matter for the coordinator rather than for any website. The table sets out the sequence and what to have ready at each step. No specific results date or deadline appears in it, because those come from the organisation's own published material and from your school, and a date a parent acts on should not come from a tutoring page.
