sections.heading: Pausing deliberately, rather than drifting
paragraphs: Most tuition arrangements end by drifting: a cancellation, a holiday, a deadline week, and then nobody restarts it. That is the worst way to stop, because it carries no decision and no information. Pausing on purpose is better in several specific situations and almost nobody offers it.

The clearest case is a deadline fortnight. A student with an Extended Essay final submission and two subject internal assessments in the same two weeks has no capacity for new teaching, and a session in that window produces nothing except guilt about the work not done. Moving the sessions out and placing extra time in the week afterwards is a better use of the same money, and the week after a deadline or a mock is genuinely the most valuable in the term.

The second case is a successful repair. Where a bounded block has fixed a named fault and the marked evidence shows it, the right action is to stop and see whether the repair holds. Continuing by default converts a defined purchase into an open-ended one and removes the evidence that the first block worked. We would rather close a block and have a family return in a term than bill continuously through a year.

The third case is a load problem. A competent student carrying three Higher Levels, the full core, mandatory subjects and a long daily journey may simply lack the hours the courses assume. Adding or continuing a session in that situation displaces the written practice that makes sessions work, so the intervention makes things worse. The honest response is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about level or subject load, and we will say so rather than keep a booking that is making a student's week harder.

sections.heading: Eastern Mangroves: waterfront apartments and a long afternoon
paragraphs: There is no school in the Eastern Mangroves development, so every student travels, and the practical planning number is arrival rather than the published finish time. From the eastern waterfront, journeys run to Al Zahiyah and the central districts, out to Al Mushrif and Al Bateen, and for some families across the bridges to the Khalifa City corridor.

The method is to measure rather than estimate. Record the actual arrival time for five consecutive days, take the latest of the five rather than the average, and add fifteen minutes for changing and eating. That is the slot. For a central island school it will usually be four o'clock or a little after; for a mainland school, five or later; and a school bus route adds thirty to fifty minutes to any published finish, which is the variable most often forgotten.

Apartment living adds two further practical points. A one-to-one session needs a door that closes and a surface large enough for an A4 pad and a laptop, and in a household with other children that space has to be allocated rather than assumed. And for a visiting arrangement there is parking, visitor registration and lift time at both ends of the hour, none of which is teaching and all of which is paid for — one reason published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Eastern Mangroves or anywhere in the UAE, since home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a calendar-driven Diploma plan the scheduling argument matters as much as the cost one: a video session can move to a different evening in a deadline week, run at a different hour during Ramadan, and continue while a family is away for part of the summer — which is when the most productive core work of the whole programme can happen.

sections.heading: Dates we will not publish, and the limits we keep
paragraphs: A page organised around a calendar has a particular obligation about dates, so the omissions here are deliberate. No Diploma examination window, upload deadline or results date appears, because the organisation's own site is the only place those can be confirmed, automated access to it is blocked, and any site quoting you one without citing it is passing on something unverified. The session UAE schools sit is the May one. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds every date that matters, including the internal ones that matter more than the examination.

Nor does any grade boundary appear. Boundaries are set after each session in light of that session's papers and candidate performance, and published afterwards; they move between sessions, and a fixed figure on a tutoring page is a fabricated certainty. What is stable and more useful is the published criteria: thirty-four marks across five Extended Essay criteria with twelve for critical thinking, ten each for the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the word limits of four thousand, sixteen hundred and nine hundred and fifty.

On assessed work, the boundary is firm and stated to students at the first session. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, discusses whether a question or title can support them, reads the student's own draft, questions it and names the criterion a section is failing. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions for live assessed work or sit beside a student during an assessment. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; we decline to produce assessed work at any price, and the consequence of buying it falls on the student's whole entry.

On status: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and it is not a registered examination centre. Any paid private tutor in the Emirates needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. No tutor can promise a grade or a points total, and we publish no rating or satisfaction statistic.

faqs.question: Why plan IB tuition around the core rather than the subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the core is what produces the impossible weeks. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS each run on their own schedule, each consumes weekends rather than evenings, and their deadlines frequently land in the same weeks as the subject internal assessments. A plan that treats the Diploma year as evenly busy gets rescheduled during exactly those weeks. Mapping the core and the subject deadlines on one calendar at the start of DP1 is the most useful planning act available.

faqs.question: How many marks does the Extended Essay carry, and where?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four across five criteria: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking alone carries twelve of them, which is more than a third of the essay, and it is a function of the research rather than of the writing. An essay built on hurried reading can describe and cannot weigh, because weighing requires counter-evidence that was never collected. Polishing presentation in the final week reaches four marks at most.

faqs.question: Why do word limits matter so much in the Diploma core?
faqs.answer: Because markers stop reading at the limit, so anything beyond it is unmarked. The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at sixteen hundred and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. A student cutting a thousand words under time pressure removes the analysis rather than the description, because description feels like content. That is exactly backwards against criteria that reward critical thinking most heavily.

faqs.question: What should be ready before the Extended Essay first draft?
faqs.answer: Something close to complete rather than an outline. The draft is the one formal opportunity for supervisor feedback within the organisation's rules, and a student who submits an outline receives feedback on structure they already knew. A near-complete draft attracts feedback on substance, which is the feedback worth having. The difference is a fortnight of earlier work, and it is worth more than any number of sessions bought afterwards.

faqs.question: Why do strong writers score poorly in Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Because they write a competent piece about the wrong thing. A prescribed title concerning historical evidence invites an essay about history, whereas the marks are for an argument about how knowledge in history is produced and justified. Students who have not had that distinction made explicit produce fluent, well-organised, low-scoring essays, and editing does not rescue one because the problem is the subject of the sentences rather than their quality.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary worth paying for?
faqs.answer: It is among the best value purchases in the whole Diploma and almost nobody makes it. Ten marks, a commentary of up to nine hundred and fifty words, and marking against a published instrument that most students have never had explained. At that length every sentence has to work: a paragraph of introduction spends a tenth of the space on nothing. One or two sessions on how the instrument reads a commentary often changes a student's entire approach.

faqs.question: Can you help only for the final stretch before the papers?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and we will tell you which case you are in after reading the last marked script. A final block reliably improves timing, command-term discipline, exact form and rounding habits, and question selection, which together often produce a double-digit swing where the content is known. It cannot rebuild fluency, teach untaught content, or change a submitted internal assessment. If the script shows content gaps across topics, we will say the honest purchase is a plan for a later session.

faqs.question: What is the best time to work on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The summer between DP1 and DP2. Nothing competes for the time: no homework in six subjects, no Theory of Knowledge deadline, no subject internal assessment. Research done then has room to include counter-evidence, which is what the critical thinking criterion rewards, and a real first draft can exist before DP2 begins. Specialist availability is also at its widest in that period, so plan it in the spring rather than in August.

faqs.question: Who makes an enquiry about results, and when?
faqs.answer: The school, never the family directly, and quickly. The school holds the relationship with the organisation and acts on a candidate's behalf, the deadlines are published and short, and a tutor has no role at all. So a disappointing result needs a conversation with the Diploma coordinator within days. An enquiry is a specific review process with its own fees and possible outcomes, including no change, and the coordinator will explain the realistic prospects before a request is made.

faqs.question: When should we deliberately pause tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: Three situations. In a deadline fortnight, when a student has no capacity for new teaching and the money is better spent in the week afterwards. After a bounded block has fixed a named fault and the marked evidence shows it, so you can see whether the repair holds. And where the diagnosis is load rather than learning, because adding sessions to a full week displaces the practice that makes sessions work. Drifting to a halt carries no decision and no information.

faqs.question: What time can a session start from Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: Measure rather than estimate: record the actual arrival time for five consecutive days, take the latest of the five rather than the average, and add fifteen minutes. For a central island school that is usually four o'clock or a little after. For a mainland school it is five or later. A school bus route adds thirty to fifty minutes to any published finish, which is the variable families most often forget when they book an unworkable slot.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in the Eastern Mangroves development?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors in the emirate do, and IB Gram does not. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and run no home visits in Eastern Mangroves or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we offer only in India. In apartment living, part of what a visiting rate covers is parking, visitor registration and lift time at both ends of the hour, which is one reason published in-home rates run from AED 180 to 500 against roughly AED 150 to 300 online.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on the Extended Essay with my child?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary we state to the student at the first session. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, discusses whether a question can support them, reads your child's own draft, asks the questions that expose an unsupported claim and names the criterion a section is failing. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece or produce any part of it. The school supervisor is inside the formal structure and authenticates the work; a tutor authenticates nothing.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the Diploma examination dates here?
faqs.answer: Because the organisation's own site is the only place they can be confirmed, automated access to it is blocked, and a date a parent might act on should not come from a tutoring page. The session UAE schools sit is the May one, with a second session available. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the examination windows, the upload deadlines and the results dates, and the internal deadlines they also hold matter more to a plan than the examination date does.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat-is.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level alongside Middle Years and Primary Years support, for families living on Hudayriyat Island and the western side of Abu Dhabi island.

intro.heading: One bridge, two directions, and a lot of sport
paragraphs: Hudayriyat Island sits off the south-western edge of Abu Dhabi island, connected by a single bridge, and it is unlike any other address in the emirate for one reason: it is where people come to exercise. The leisure and entertainment district, the cycling and running circuits, the beach and watersports facilities and the sports venues mean the island's traffic runs inbound at weekends and outbound on school mornings. For a family living here, that double pattern shapes the week more than any curriculum decision does.

There is no school on the island, so every school run crosses the bridge onto the main island, most often towards Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif or further east. That is the outbound half. The inbound half is the part nobody plans for: a good number of Hudayriyat children do their sport, their training and a meaningful share of their Creativity, Activity, Service hours back on the island, which means the day finishes with a second crossing in the opposite direction and an arrival home somewhere between six and half past seven.

That is the real constraint on tutoring here, and it is a timing problem rather than a distance problem. A 5pm session is fiction. A 6pm session works only on the days with no training. The dependable slot for a Hudayriyat Diploma student is 7pm, and on heavy training days 7.30pm. Any plan built on earlier hours will hold for a fortnight and then start shedding weeks, which in a cumulative subject during a Diploma year is the expensive kind of failure. Protecting a realistic hour is worth more than finding an ideal one.

In-home tuition struggles badly with this. A tutor arriving for a 7.30pm start has crossed the bridge, and will cross it back at nine. That journey reaches a family either as a higher hourly rate, with in-home one-to-one quoted in this market at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, or as a two-hour minimum nobody wants at that time of night, or as the quiet unreliability of a late session held by somebody facing a long drive home.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Hudayriyat Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The rest of this page maps the week properly, explains what a 7.30pm Diploma session should and should not attempt, and sets out how Internal Assessment deadlines interact with a sporting calendar, which is a collision this island produces more than most. None of what follows depends on anybody being nearby, which from this address is the point.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat-is.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum and Hudayriyat households, being a young community, often have children at two stages. The timetable pressure is different at each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based transdisciplinary units with maths and literacy embedded rather than timetabled separately, which makes gaps hard for a parent to see until the Middle Years begin. Support at this stage is short and infrequent, and for the youngest children the bridge crossing is the dominant factor in what energy remains.
programmes.countryNote: Hudayriyat's primary-age children travel to campuses in Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif. A reception or Year 1 child doing two crossings a day is a tired child by four o'clock, which is why primary sessions here work far better at a weekend than on a school evening.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject and a Personal Project in the final year. Sport commitments begin to bite here, with squad training and fixtures taking afternoons, and the Personal Project is usually the first internally assessed task a family discovers can collide with a competition calendar.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is the point at which Hudayriyat families most often seek help, because Higher Level choices made in Year 11 have to be weighed against a training commitment that will not reduce in Year 12 and may well increase.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects each with an Internal Assessment, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The Activity strand is often already satisfied several times over for a student training seriously, which helps, while the written core still has to be produced on the school's internal deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Hudayriyat travel across the bridge to campuses on the western and central island and sometimes further east. Higher Level cohorts are small, so matching on course and level rather than on who will cross a bridge at eight in the evening is the practical quality question.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat-is.subjectsIntro: The IB subjects Hudayriyat households ask about, with the component that actually decides each grade named rather than implied.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra-led with proof, calculus and, at Higher Level, the extended-response Paper 3. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and because school practice is calculator-rich this is where the recoverable marks sit. The scarcest teaching skill in the emirate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led interpretation, with graph theory and matrices at Higher Level. Marks go to justified choices and to conclusions stated in context, not to correct calculator output, which students discover late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and data questions that reward precise language. The Internal Assessment investigation carries a substantial share of the grade and needs laboratory time the student has to schedule around everything else.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides more marks than recall. Outline, explain, discuss and evaluate are marked differently and students answer them identically. Statistical handling in the Internal Assessment is the usual weak point and is teachable in two sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical fluency is the hidden prerequisite: students comfortable with the physics still lose marks to algebra under time pressure. Uncertainty handling and graph analysis in the investigation carry more weight than most students expect.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 option some Abu Dhabi campuses offer, covering anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and training theory with its own Internal Assessment. Where a school offers it, students with a serious training background often find it the most natural science choice available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, the Individual Oral and the comparative essay. Marks go to building an argument about how a text works rather than to describing what it says, which is a trainable skill and rarely trained deliberately.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation command terms carry the marks. The Internal Assessment commentaries have firm word limits, and exceeding them is an avoidable loss that cannot be repaired after submission.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A genuinely small specialism, so availability rather than price is the constraint. Families should ask in the autumn of Year 12 rather than in the term the essay is due, when the few people who teach it well are already committed.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Research question design, scope control and the criteria, taught explicitly. A tutor questions the argument and feeds back on the student's own drafts. No tutor may write, restructure or supply any part of it.

sections.heading: The Hudayriyat week, counted properly
paragraphs: A dependable IB session for a Hudayriyat student starts at 7pm, and 7.30pm on training days. That comes from adding the day up rather than from any theory about teenage attention. School on the main island ends between roughly 3.00pm and 3.30pm. Pick-up adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes before a car moves. The crossing back takes fifteen to thirty minutes depending on which campus and which hour. That alone puts a student home between 4.15pm and 4.50pm.

Then the second half, which is particular to this island. Training, squad sessions, swimming, cycling and a good share of Creativity, Activity, Service hours frequently happen on Hudayriyat itself or at the sports facilities nearby, which means a student who got home at half past four goes out again and returns between six and half past seven. On those days nothing before 7.30pm is real, and a plan that pretends otherwise produces a cancelled session in week three.

The table below sets out the common day patterns. What matters is not the exact minutes, which vary, but the rule that follows from them: place the fixed weekly slot at the hour that works on the busiest day of the week, not the quietest. A slot that fits three days in five is a slot that will be renegotiated every month until somebody gives up on it, and the cost of that is continuity in a subject where continuity is most of the value.

sections.heading: The weekend runs the other way
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi tutoring advice assumes weekends are free, and on Hudayriyat Island that is true in an unusual way. The island is a destination, so at weekends the bridge carries people in rather than out. For a resident family that means staying put is easy and leaving is slow, which inverts the usual calculation about where a Saturday or Sunday session should happen.

The practical consequence is that a weekend morning at home is the most valuable block of time a Hudayriyat household has, and it should be used for the work that cannot be done on a school evening. That means the Internal Assessment mathematics or the science investigation worked at length rather than in twenty-minute fragments. It means an Extended Essay draft discussed properly. It means a whole paper sat under real timing, which is impossible after two crossings and a training session.

It also means that any arrangement requiring the family to drive off the island at a weekend is paying a cost it does not need to pay. A group class at a mainland centre on a Saturday morning, which might be reasonable value from Khalifa City, becomes a long inbound-traffic journey from here. An online session at home at nine on a Saturday morning, with the student fresh and nothing scheduled, is the best hour available in a Hudayriyat week and the one most often left unused. Say this to any provider quoting a weekend slot, too. A Saturday morning class on the mainland sounds like the easy option and from this address it is the hard one, which is exactly the sort of thing a family knows and a timetable does not.

sections.heading: A new community and school choices made before the move
paragraphs: Hudayriyat is a young residential community, and a distinctive share of the families living here chose their school before they chose the address, or chose the address and kept the school. That produces a particular pattern: school runs that are longer than they would be if the choice were made today, and siblings at campuses in different directions.

It matters for tutoring in two ways. The first is simply the clock, already covered. The second is more subtle: a household that is settled in a school it loves but drives thirty minutes each way is making a trade it has already decided on, and the correct response is to build the support plan around that trade rather than to keep relitigating it. The slot goes at 7pm, the long tasks go to the weekend, and nobody spends energy wishing the commute were shorter.

The third pattern worth naming is that a new community has a thin informal tutoring network. There is no long-established group of resident teachers who tutor in the evenings, because the community has not existed long enough to accumulate one. Families here therefore reach for agencies, marketplaces or mainland centres earlier than families in Al Mushrif or Al Khalidiyah would, and they are more exposed to the quality variation in those channels because there is no local reputation to lean on. That is an argument for asking precise questions rather than for paying more. There is one exception worth making. If the commute is being driven by a school the child is unhappy in, that is a different conversation entirely and no amount of tutoring addresses it.

sections.heading: What a 7.30pm session must achieve, and must not attempt
paragraphs: A session at half past seven, after two crossings and a training session, is a real teaching opportunity and a narrow one. The student in front of the tutor has been awake since six, sat a full Diploma timetable, travelled twice and exercised hard. Treating that hour like a fresh afternoon wastes the slot the family protected.

What works is specific. Open with three or four minutes of something already secure, to get the subject moving before anything unfamiliar arrives. One objective for the hour, stated at the start, so the student knows what is being asked. The tutor writing while explaining, on a shared screen the student can reopen in March, because retention from a tired listening session is poor and retention from a saved document is not. End on time, with two minutes naming what was achieved and what comes next.

What does not work is volume or novelty. A dense new topic introduced at 7.45pm to a student who trained at six will be re-taught in a fortnight. Ninety minutes produces less than sixty. A whole timed paper is simply not viable and should not be attempted, which is precisely why the weekend morning exists. A tutor who proposes two hours on a training evening is either not paying attention or is selling hours, and the second hour is the most expensive unproductive time a Hudayriyat family will buy all year. Ask your child what the last session covered, two days later. If they can name the objective, the hour was built correctly for the state they were in; if they cannot, the hour was built for a student who had not been training.
bullets: Open with something secure before anything new arrives
One named objective per hour, stated at the start

sections.heading: Internal Assessment deadlines against a fixture calendar
paragraphs: This is the collision Hudayriyat produces more than other addresses. Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment on a school-set internal deadline, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge add their own milestones. A student training seriously also has a fixture and competition calendar that nobody at school is coordinating with those deadlines.

The result is predictable if nobody looks: a chemistry investigation write-up due in the same fortnight as a competition block, an Extended Essay draft due the week of a tournament, and a student choosing between them at eleven at night. The component that gives is almost always the written one, because it has no immediate external consequence, and it is worth a substantial share of a subject grade.

The remedy is a single sheet in September with both calendars on it. School internal deadlines on one side, fixtures and training blocks on the other. Where they collide, the written work moves earlier, not later, because a deadline cannot move and a draft can. Two short topic-interrogation sessions in the first fortnight of an Internal Assessment are worth more than six sessions in the week before submission anyway, so bringing the work forward costs nothing and removes the collision. The table shows how the two calendars usually overlap. Share the sheet with the tutor as well as keeping it. A tutor who knows a tournament falls in week six plans week five differently, and a tutor who does not plans week five as though week six will happen normally.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment boundary, stated plainly
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and it is where a grade can be improved substantially and where a Diploma can be lost entirely. The difference is what kind of help was bought, and the boundary comes from IB academic-honesty rules rather than from anyone's preference.

A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each rewards, naming the mark allocations. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and press hard on whether there is enough substance in them to reach the upper bands. A tutor may teach content the investigation requires, including material slightly beyond the taught course. A tutor may question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a sample or a model was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written themselves.

No tutor may write any part of the assessment, supply text to paste in, restructure the student's prose into their own, or produce results or mathematics for the student to transcribe. Bought-in work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it. There is a visible market in completed Internal Assessments in this region, advertised at four-figure dirham prices. Ask any provider to state its honesty position in writing before a first session; the ones who decline have answered the question. Tell your child the same boundary in the same words, because a student under deadline pressure at midnight is in a poor position to judge where it sits.
bullets: Criteria taught explicitly, with their mark allocations named

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and a schedule that bends without breaking
paragraphs: Three predictable interruptions hit a Hudayriyat Diploma year, and each costs more than the sessions it removes, because restarting a cumulative subject is slower than continuing it. Deciding what will happen to all three in September takes twenty minutes and saves a term.

Ramadan shortens the school day across the UAE, moves household energy to the evening and usually changes training times too. On this island that second effect matters: a session that sat at 7.30pm may now sit better after iftar, and two shorter sessions often suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 13 this is not a month to drop out of, because the interval before the May session is short and an Internal Assessment deadline may sit nearby.

The other two are travel and the winter break. Households here travel, including for competitions, and an in-home arrangement cancels every time while an online session follows the student with only a time-zone adjustment. The winter break lands shortly after mocks, which makes that fortnight either the most valuable of Year 13, spent dissecting scripts while they are still warm, or a complete write-off. Which it becomes is decided in November, when the sessions have to be booked, not in December when every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same days. The common factor across all three is that each one is visible months ahead and each one is usually handled a week before it arrives. Deciding in September what happens in each costs one conversation and removes three arguments.
bullets: Ramadan changes school hours and training times together
Two shorter sessions beat one long block during a shortened day

sections.heading: ADEK, permits and the two questions worth asking a tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Reading your school's report alongside its own reporting is free and useful, because the two documents answer different questions and sometimes disagree.

Private tutoring sits under a separate, federal rule. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified. ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

Beyond the permit, two questions matter more for an IB tutor than anything a credential conveys. Which course and level have you taught, named precisely rather than as IB maths or IB science, and how many cohorts? And what do you do with an Internal Assessment? A tutor who answers the first with a number and the second with a clear account of the honesty boundary has demonstrated exactly what you are buying. For completeness, IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and no school named here is a client.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session realistically start for a student living on Hudayriyat Island?
faqs.answer: Seven in the evening, and half past seven on training days. School on the main island ends between about 3.00pm and 3.30pm, pick-up adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes, and the crossing back takes fifteen to thirty depending on the campus, so a student is home between 4.15pm and 4.50pm. On the many days when training or activity happens back on the island, they go out again and return between six and half past seven. The fixed weekly slot should be placed at the hour that works on the busiest day of the week.

faqs.question: Are there schools on Hudayriyat Island itself?
faqs.answer: No, so every school run crosses the single bridge onto the main island, most often towards Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah or Al Mushrif. For tutoring that has two consequences. The obvious one is the clock: nothing before six is realistic and nothing before half past seven is realistic on a training day. The less obvious one is the thin local tutoring network, because a new community has not existed long enough to accumulate a pool of resident teachers who tutor in the evenings.

faqs.question: Will a tutor cross the bridge to Hudayriyat Island in the evening?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Some Abu Dhabi providers will, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs a round trip. At a 7.30pm start the bigger problem is reliability rather than price: a tutor facing a crossing at nine in the evening is the one most likely to ask to move a late session.

faqs.question: Why is a weekend morning at home so valuable on this island?
faqs.answer: Because the traffic runs the other way. Hudayriyat is a leisure and sports destination, so at weekends the bridge carries visitors in rather than residents out, which makes staying put easy and leaving slow. That inverts the usual assumption that a weekend class on the mainland is convenient. A session at home at nine on a Saturday morning, with the student fresh and nothing else scheduled, is the best hour in the week, and it is where Internal Assessment work and whole timed papers belong.

faqs.question: How does serious sport affect what a Diploma student can realistically fit in?
faqs.answer: It usually satisfies the Activity strand of Creativity, Activity, Service several times over, which helps, and it consumes exactly the hours a tutoring plan would otherwise use. Training, squad sessions and fixtures take two or three afternoons a week and rotate each term. The practical answer is to place the weekly slot at the hour that survives a training day, to keep long tasks on a weekend morning, and to plan the written work around the fixture calendar rather than discovering the collision in the week it happens.

faqs.question: What should a tutor avoid attempting in a 7.30pm session?
faqs.answer: Dense new content and anything timed. A student who trained at six will have a hard time absorbing an unfamiliar topic at a quarter to eight, and will need it re-taught in a fortnight, which wastes two hours rather than one. A whole paper under timing is not viable at all at that hour and gives a misleading result. What works instead is one named objective, opened with something already secure, written on a shared screen the student can reopen later, and finished on time rather than extended.

faqs.question: Is sixty minutes enough, or should we book ninety?
faqs.answer: Sixty, on a school evening. After a full Diploma timetable, two crossings and a training session, concentration on abstract material degrades noticeably after about seventy-five minutes, and the last stretch of a long late session is frequently the least productive hour a household pays for. If more time is needed, the right place for it is a weekend morning, where a longer block is genuinely productive because nothing has preceded it and no journey follows.

faqs.question: How do we stop Internal Assessment deadlines colliding with competition weeks?
faqs.answer: Put both calendars on one sheet in September. School-set internal deadlines on one side, fixtures and training blocks on the other, and look for the overlaps. Where they collide, the written work moves earlier rather than later, because a deadline cannot move and a draft can. This costs nothing, since two short topic-interrogation sessions in the first fortnight of an Internal Assessment are worth more than six sessions the week before submission anyway. Doing it in September rather than November is the whole trick.

faqs.question: Where does help on a science investigation stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria and what each rewards, with the mark allocations named. Discuss candidate topics and press on whether there is enough substance to reach the upper bands. Teach content the investigation needs, including material slightly beyond the taught course. Question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a sample or model was chosen, and feed back in writing on a draft the student wrote. What no tutor may do is write any part of it, supply text, restructure the prose, or produce results for the student to transcribe.

faqs.question: Our school is thirty minutes away because we moved after choosing it. Should we change?
faqs.answer: That is a question about the school rather than about tutoring, and a settled child in a school a family values is worth a long commute more often than not. What is worth changing is the planning around it. Accept the trade as decided, put the weekly session at 7pm or 7.30pm, move the long tasks to a weekend morning at home, and stop spending energy on the commute. Households that plan around the trade they already made do considerably better than those that keep reopening it each term.

faqs.question: Does the thin local tutoring network here matter?
faqs.answer: It changes which questions matter rather than making things worse. In an established district a family can lean on local reputation, which is informative even when it is imprecise. On a new community there is no accumulated reputation to consult, so families reach for agencies, marketplaces and mainland centres earlier and are more exposed to the quality variation in those channels. The protection is precision: ask which course and level a tutor has taught and how many cohorts, and ask what they do with an Internal Assessment.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue when we travel for competitions or holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a sporting household that is a substantial part of the argument for online delivery. An in-home arrangement cancels whenever the family leaves, which during a Diploma year can mean a three-week gap at exactly the wrong point in an Internal Assessment timetable. A live video session follows the student and the only adjustment is the time zone. Most families thin sessions rather than stopping over a long summer, because the technical fluency a Diploma course assumes decays quickly in a ten-week gap.

faqs.question: How should a plan handle Ramadan on this island?
faqs.answer: By moving the slot deliberately and deciding in advance, because Ramadan changes two things here rather than one: school hours shorten across the UAE and training times usually shift as well. A session that sat at half past seven often works better after iftar, and two shorter sessions suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 13 it is a poor month to drop out of, since the interval before the May session is short and an Internal Assessment deadline may sit nearby.

faqs.question: Which campuses do your students from Hudayriyat Island attend?
faqs.answer: Households here travel across the bridge, mostly to campuses in Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif, with some running further east. The names that recur include the American Community School of Abu Dhabi, Al Bateen Academy, The British School Al Khubairat, Abu Dhabi International School and Brighton College Abu Dhabi. Those names describe the local education map and nothing further. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and none of them is a client of ours.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to cover at a 7.30pm slot?
faqs.answer: The late hour narrows an already small pool. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the tightest, followed by Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the smaller Group 2 languages and Theory of Knowledge. Standard Level maths, biology, economics, business management and English A are comfortable. For a tight request at a late slot you get one of three answers: a waiting time with a date, a named tutor who covers the course but is not the deepest specialist with that stated, or an honest no.

intro.heading: Hydra Village against the next community over: what actually differs
paragraphs: Hydra Village is a villa community on the Abu Dhabi mainland out towards Al Shamkha and the Zayed City corridor, and families here routinely compare their position with neighbouring communities when they start looking for IB support. The comparison is worth making properly, because the honest version is narrow: what changes between Hydra Village, Al Shamkha, Shakhbout City and Al Rahba is drive time and the number of resident specialists. What does not change is the Diploma, which is set by the IB and is identical for every candidate in every one of those communities.

That distinction matters because the conversation usually drifts. A parent hears that a neighbouring community has better options, and what that nearly always means is that the drive to a tutor's house is shorter, or that someone knows a name. Neither affects the mark. Each IB subject carries its own components with their own weightings, each carries an Internal Assessment worth around a fifth of the grade, the Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word ceiling and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600, and 24 points is the minimum for the award with a maximum of 45. None of that is negotiated locally.

What the geography genuinely does is constrain supply. Hydra Village is residential rather than school-dense, and the emirate's IB capacity and its resident teaching staff are concentrated well to the west, around Khalifa City, the Al Raha belt and the island. A Diploma timetable is six separate specialisms, three of them at Higher Level, and the chance that somebody within a short drive of Hydra Village has taught your child's specific subject at their specific level to examination is low. For mathematics or biology it holds up. For a minority Higher Level subject it generally does not.

So the structure of this page is a comparison. It sets Hydra Village against its neighbours on the things that differ, separates what the IB controls from what a school controls, maps the Middle Years to Diploma transition that so many families here are in the middle of, and prices the commute in study hours rather than in minutes, because the hours lost to the car are hours the Extended Essay needed. Where the answer is the same for Hydra Village and Al Shamkha, it says so rather than inventing a local difference.

One statement before any of it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The phrase families search is home tutor, so this page uses it, and the delivery is one-to-one live video in Gulf Standard Time. From a community this far east that is not a compromise: it is the arrangement that lets a family choose the specialist rather than the nearest willing driver, which is the only variable in this comparison that moves a grade.

sections.heading: The comparison, made properly
paragraphs: Set Hydra Village beside Al Shamkha, Shakhbout City, Al Rahba and Khalifa City and three things vary. First, the drive to an IB school, which ranges from under twenty minutes in the western communities to the better part of an hour from the eastern ones at the wrong time of day. Second, the number of resident subject specialists, which rises steeply as you move west because that is where the schools and therefore the teaching staff are. Third, the in-home price, which tracks the first two: published in-home rates across Abu Dhabi run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and the quotes sit lower where the journeys are shorter.

Nothing else varies. The IB sets the subject guides, the components and their weightings, the Internal Assessment criteria, the word ceilings on the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay, and the points structure. Those are identical for a candidate in Hydra Village and a candidate anywhere else in the world. The emirate regulator, which for Abu Dhabi is the Department of Education and Knowledge, licenses and inspects the school rather than setting the Diploma.

The practical conclusion follows from the second variable rather than the first. In a community with few resident specialists, choosing in-home means choosing from a small pool, and inside that pool the number who have taught your child's subject at their level to examination may be zero. Families then accept a competent generalist because the alternative is nobody, and that substitution is the one trade in this comparison that costs marks. Online removes the geography and leaves only the question of whether the specialist exists, which the table below answers community by community.

sections.heading: What the IB sets, and what your school sets
paragraphs: Families comparing communities often conflate two different things: the programme, which is fixed, and the delivery, which is not. Separating them makes the comparison tractable. The IB sets the subject guides and syllabus content, the assessment components and their weightings, the Internal Assessment criteria and mark allocations, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge requirements including the 4,000-word and 1,600-word ceilings, and the points structure with 24 required and 45 available.

The school sets everything about the experience. Which subjects and levels it can timetable, which is the most consequential school-level variable and the one worth asking about at admission rather than afterwards. The internal deadlines for Internal Assessment drafts, which are set locally and are the dates a tutoring plan actually has to work to. The quality and availability of supervision for the Extended Essay. Mock timing. Class size. The regulator, ADEK, licenses and inspects the school and publishes its own outcomes; it does not alter any of the IB's requirements.

This is why a parent comparing two schools should ask school-level questions, and a parent comparing two tutors should ask IB-level ones. A tutor cannot change a timetable or a deadline, and does not need to; what they need to know is what each component is worth, what the criteria reward, and where candidates lose marks. The table separates the two columns so a family can direct each question to the right place and stop asking tutors about things schools decide.

sections.heading: From the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma
paragraphs: Many Hydra Village families are mid-transition rather than mid-crisis, and the transition has a specific shape worth naming. A student who has been assessed against criteria for five years arrives at the Diploma with real advantages: comfort with written reflection, familiarity with being marked against descriptors rather than percentages, and some experience of an independent project. What they often lack is examination stamina, because the MYP's assessment pattern does not require sitting long papers under time.

A student transferring in from a different system during Years 10 or 11 has the reverse profile. They are usually comfortable with written examinations and unfamiliar with criterion-referenced coursework, which is the part of the Diploma worth about a fifth of each subject grade. For that student the first useful work is not content at all; it is understanding how an Internal Assessment is marked, by letter, with the allocations attached, because without that the first draft is written to the wrong target.

The table maps the transition by subject area with the gap and a realistic session count, so a family can see the size of the job rather than guess at it. One scheduling note specific to this community: the transition work is best done in the summer before Diploma Year 1 or in its first term, when the commute has not yet collided with coursework deadlines. Left until the first Internal Assessment is due, it becomes remedial rather than preparatory, and remedial work under deadline is where the honesty boundary gets tested.

sections.heading: The commute, priced in study hours rather than minutes
paragraphs: This is where the community comparison stops being abstract. A Diploma student travelling from Hydra Village to a school in the Khalifa City or Al Raha belt loses somewhere between one and two hours a day to the road. Over a five-day week that is five to ten hours, and over a Diploma year it is several hundred. Those are not leisure hours. They are precisely the independent hours the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and six Internal Assessments were designed to consume.

The consequence is predictable and avoidable. Coursework slips, not because the student is weak but because the hours it needed were spent in a car, and the slippage surfaces in Year 2 when a fifth of each subject grade is already compromised. Families who recognise the commute as a study-time cost plan differently: they front-load the independent work into Diploma Year 1, book supervision while drafts are being written, and protect weekend blocks for the long tasks rather than hoping weekday evenings will stretch.

The second implication is about adding a second journey. An in-home tutor arriving from Khalifa City at the evening peak is committing forty minutes or more each way, which is billed either as a travel premium or as a shortened session, and over a two-year programme it shows up as cancellations. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. For a household already spending ten hours a week on the road, the online format is the one that does not add to that total.

sections.heading: Where supply genuinely differs, and what we do about it
paragraphs: The one real disadvantage of an eastern mainland address is specialist supply, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. A Diploma timetable is six specialisms across two levels, and the people who have taught a minority Higher Level subject to examination are few and mostly employed in schools. Within a short drive of Hydra Village, the chance of finding one for Economics at Higher Level, Computer Science, Digital Society, Arabic A Literature, Visual Arts, Music or Theatre is low at any price.

No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit, which does not mean they do not have one. Our position is to state it. If a combination is well covered you will have options within days. If it is scarce, you are told the expected wait and offered the nearest alternative with the difference explained, and where the specialist teaching your child's syllabus is based outside the UAE we say so, because two of the researched pages route UAE parents to a foreign phone number without ever mentioning it.

Sometimes the honest recommendation is a different intervention. A physics student losing marks to algebra gains more from a mathematics block than from waiting for a physics specialist. A Diploma student with secure paper technique and a weak exploration needs supervision hours rather than teaching hours. A student who has never sat a full paper to time needs a weekend rather than a term. Those answers are worth less to us than a long booking, which is a reasonable test of whether a comparison page is advising or selling.
bullets: Minority Higher Level subjects are thin across the whole emirate, not just out here
Ask about availability in Diploma Year 1, not in the spring of Year 2

sections.heading: ADEK, the school, and what a report does not measure
paragraphs: Private schools serving Hydra Village are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, which is a striking gap on pages written for Abu Dhabi parents. For a comparison page the relevant point is that the regulator assesses the school, not the Diploma, so two schools with different inspection outcomes still enter candidates for identical assessments.

Your child's report measures something narrower still: their position within that school's cohort. It does not tell you how an examiner applying the published criteria would mark their Internal Assessment, and it does not tell you how a timed paper would go. That is why a single diagnostic session is worth more than a term of reassurance, and why a draft marked against the criteria by somebody who has applied them before is a different kind of information from a predicted grade.

Two further notes for a household out here. Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, under a federal baseline requiring adherence to those subjects whatever curriculum a school is licensed for; they occupy timetable space that a Diploma revision plan must account for. And a caution about us: IB Gram holds no licence, approval, certification or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and has no premises in the UAE. Any provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth checking against a document.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries work produced outside the exam hall, so the boundary should be settled in Year 1 rather than negotiated under a Year 2 deadline. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, works comparable examples, sets practice, marks it and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce your child's coursework, does not supply submittable text, and does not edit a draft to the point where the thinking has stopped being theirs. That applies to every Internal Assessment, to the Extended Essay at its 4,000-word ceiling and to the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 words.

The reason to publish this rather than discuss it privately is that the exposure is one-sided. An authenticity problem is a malpractice matter for the candidate, with consequences for their diploma, while whoever supplied the work faces nothing. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. In a long-commute household, where coursework is the thing most likely to slip, this is the pressure point, and the honest version is also the more useful one: a student taught what a criterion rewards can write the next piece unaided.

The rest of what we will not claim belongs on a comparison page because comparison is what unverifiable claims exploit. No grade or points promise, since the Diploma is externally assessed and the result belongs to the student on the day. No satisfaction percentage, score-improvement figure, student count or star rating, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method. No examiner description for anyone whose status we cannot evidence. No publishing or supplying of IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own drafts; never supplied or completed text

faqs.question: Would my child be better off with a tutor from Al Shamkha or Shakhbout City instead?
faqs.answer: Only if that tutor has taught your child's subject at their level to examination. The Diploma is set by the IB, so the components, weightings, criteria and points structure are identical for a candidate in Hydra Village, Al Shamkha or Shakhbout City. What differs is the drive and the number of resident specialists, which rises as you move west towards Khalifa City. Choosing a nearer generalist over a specialist is the one decision in this comparison that reliably costs marks.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to a villa in Hydra Village?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The local in-home market exists and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The premium out here is largely the evening-peak journey from the western belt.

faqs.question: Does the school we choose change what the IB Diploma demands?
faqs.answer: No. The IB sets the subject guides, the assessment components and their weightings, the Internal Assessment criteria and mark allocations, the 4,000-word Extended Essay ceiling, the 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay and the points structure with 24 required and 45 available. What the school sets is which subjects and levels it can timetable, the internal draft deadlines, the mock timing and the quality of Extended Essay supervision. The first list is fixed; the second is the one worth asking about at admission.

faqs.question: What does a long commute from Hydra Village actually cost academically?
faqs.answer: Between five and ten independent study hours a week, which over a Diploma year runs into the hundreds. Those are precisely the hours the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and six Internal Assessments were designed to consume, so the predictable result is coursework that slips for reasons unrelated to ability. Households that treat the commute as a study-time cost front-load independent work into Diploma Year 1 and protect weekend blocks, rather than hoping weekday evenings will stretch.

faqs.question: My child is moving from the MYP into the Diploma. What needs work first?
faqs.answer: Usually examination stamina rather than coursework. A student assessed against criteria for five years is already comfortable with written reflection and with descriptors rather than percentages, and that is a real advantage in the Internal Assessments. What the MYP does not require is sitting long papers under time, so three or four sessions of timed practice in the first term pays off more than content teaching. The reverse applies to a student transferring in from an examination-heavy system.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hard to find a tutor for out on the eastern mainland?
faqs.answer: The same ones that are hard to find anywhere in the emirate, only more so: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre, then Computer Science and Digital Society, Arabic A Literature, and Higher Level Economics and Business Management. The sciences, both mathematics routes and English A are well covered. The constraint is that people who have taught a minority Higher Level subject to examination are few and mostly work in schools, and proximity makes a small pool smaller rather than creating one.

faqs.question: When should a Hydra Village family start Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, and for two reasons specific to this community. First, availability: a scarce specialism can be secured in Diploma Year 1 and may not be available in the spring of Year 2. Second, the commute, which squeezes exactly the independent hours coursework needs, so supervision placed in Year 1 reaches a fifth of each subject grade that a later intervention cannot. Starting early also spreads the cost across twenty-four months rather than concentrating it in one panicked term.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring simply unavailable this far east?
faqs.answer: Not unavailable, just thin and dearer. Tutors will travel from Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt, and the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour includes that travel, with quotes sitting towards the upper end out here. The practical issue over two Diploma years is reliability: a forty-minute run each way at the evening peak produces cancellations, and a cancelled journey is often chargeable. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor knows the Diploma or just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask what each component of your child's subject is worth, then ask for the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations, then ask where candidates most commonly lose marks and what they do about it. Someone who has planned and taught the course answers all three immediately and specifically. Someone who knows the subject generally will generalise or talk about confidence. It takes ten minutes of a free trial and requires no subject knowledge on your part.

faqs.question: Does ADEK's inspection outcome tell me anything about my child's Diploma prospects?
faqs.answer: It tells you about the school rather than the programme. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes its own outcomes, but two schools with different outcomes still enter candidates for identical IB assessments marked to the same standard. Read any rating on the regulator's own site rather than on a tutoring page. For your child specifically, a draft marked against the published criteria is far more informative than any school-level measure.

faqs.question: What help is permitted on the Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments?
faqs.answer: Teaching the criteria, scoping a research question answerable inside the 4,000-word ceiling, working comparable examples, and giving feedback on your child's own drafts. The school remains the supervisor. What is not permitted is choosing the topic for them, supplying text, or editing a draft until the thinking is no longer theirs. An authenticity problem is a malpractice matter whose consequences fall on the candidate, and one provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

faqs.question: Can a tutor see written working properly over video for maths and the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the free trial is where to test it rather than take it on faith. Most students write on a tablet with a stylus into a shared whiteboard that the tutor sees stroke by stroke and can annotate as the method forms. The alternative is paper under a phone or document camera, which works and is clumsier. Watching method develop is often more diagnostic than seeing a finished page. If neither arrangement suits your child, you find out before committing anything.

faqs.question: Will you promise a points total if we commit to two years of support?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. The Diploma is externally assessed, the maximum is 45 points with 24 required for the award, and the result belongs to the student on the day. We publish no score-improvement figures or satisfaction percentages either, because we could not show you the sample size, the date and the method behind them. What a good match reliably buys is a student who knows what each mark is awarded for, which is the part of the outcome that can be influenced.

faqs.question: If nobody covers my child's subject, what is the honest alternative?
faqs.answer: We say so, name the expected wait and explain the nearest alternative with the difference stated. Sometimes a different intervention is genuinely better: a physics student losing marks to algebra gains more from a mathematics block than from waiting for a physics specialist, and a student with secure paper technique and a weak exploration needs supervision hours rather than teaching hours. Those recommendations are worth less to us than a long booking, which is a fair test of the advice.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-khalifa-city.tutorsIntro: Khalifa City enquiries that include a bell time and a bus arrival get a workable schedule first time. We match the subject and level, then the hour your household can genuinely keep in a busy fortnight rather than a quiet one.

intro.heading: Work out the hour before you choose the tutor
paragraphs: Khalifa City is a large low-rise community inland from the Abu Dhabi islands, with several well-known schools inside it and others a short drive away. That geography is kinder than most of the emirate: journeys are generally short, and many children attend school within the community itself. The limiting factor on tutoring here is therefore rarely the road. It is what else is already in the week.

A Diploma student carries six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. Add school contact time, travel, homework, a sport or a musical instrument and eight hours of sleep, and the discretionary hours left in a week are fewer than most parents assume. A tutoring session does not arrive in empty space; it displaces something, and it is worth knowing what.

That is why this page starts with arithmetic rather than with an argument about formats. Later on there is a table setting out where a Khalifa City Diploma week's hours actually go. Families who run that exercise before booking tend to make one of two sensible choices: they drop a commitment deliberately, or they choose one subject rather than three. Families who skip it tend to cut sleep, which costs more than the session gains.

The second thing this page does is set out the bell times and bus patterns across the schools Khalifa City feeds, because the useful hour varies more than you would expect across a single community. A student at a school inside Khalifa City can be home at 15:00. A student travelling to Al Bateen or Al Mushrif can be home at 16:30. Those two households need different session times and often get offered the same one, because a tutor driving between addresses is selling the hours a route allows rather than the hours a student can use.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Khalifa City is one-to-one teaching over live video, which matters here less for the travel saving and more for the hour: a 19:45 Tuesday is exactly as easy for us to staff as a 16:30 one, and the second of those is unusable for a student who is still in a minibus.

The rest of the page covers the schools and what each does to an evening, the weekly hours budget, how Creativity Activity Service and sport compete for the same slot, how to read a school report before buying anything, what the market charges for a visit in this part of Abu Dhabi, and the line a tutor does not cross on assessed work. Every figure carries the source it came from and the month it was read.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-khalifa-city.programmesIntro: The four IB stages make very different demands on a household's week, and the right amount of support is set by what else is already committed rather than by the programme name.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment and a light homework load, which makes this the stage with genuine space in the week. The useful work is arithmetic fluency and sentence construction, both of which respond to short frequent practice. Nothing here needs to displace anything, which is why it is the cheapest useful tutoring a family ever buys.
programmes.countryNote: Khalifa City primary pupils mostly attend schools inside the community or minutes away, and are often home before 15:00 with the afternoon clear. Two twenty-minute sessions a week fit comfortably, and at this age they beat a single hour because a nine-year-old's attention on arithmetic does not last sixty minutes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, converted into a one-to-seven grade. The week fills noticeably from the third year onwards as extended tasks and the community project arrive. Criterion coaching is the work that pays, and it needs a session where the student is alert enough to read a strand carefully.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Khalifa City typically have a usable 16:30 slot, which is earlier than their Diploma siblings and earlier than most of Abu Dhabi. Use it: criteria-based writing work degrades badly when attempted at nine in the evening, and the alternative slot is a Saturday morning.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service, to a maximum of 45 points including up to three from the core. This is the stage where the week genuinely runs out of room, and where a decision about what to drop usually has to be made explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Khalifa City Diploma students attending schools inside the community are commonly home by 15:30; those travelling to Al Bateen, Al Mushrif or the islands are closer to 16:30. Both groups then have Creativity Activity Service commitments and homework, which is why 19:30 and Saturday morning are the two slots that actually survive a busy fortnight.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with career-related study and a reflective project. Rare in Abu Dhabi, and where a school runs it the Diploma courses inside are examined on the same papers with the same weightings and the same Internal Assessments. The weekly load is usually lighter than a full Diploma, which changes what is schedulable.
programmes.countryNote: Few Khalifa City schools run the Career-related Programme, so most families here are comparing the Diploma with A Levels or an American diploma. If your child is on it, say so when booking, because the component weightings a tutor plans around are the Diploma ones even though the overall qualification differs.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-khalifa-city.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Khalifa City families ask about most, with the part of each that justifies taking an hour out of an already full week.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade, a long scaffolded investigation with no Standard Level equivalent. It needs its own practice and it is the component most commonly deferred, which makes it the strongest single case for a fixed weekly slot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Every paper permits a calculator, so menu fluency is examinable rather than convenient. A large share of lost marks is calculator technique, which is fast to fix and therefore a good use of a short session rather than a long one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is thirty-six per cent across multiple-choice and data-based sections, Paper 2 forty-four, the investigation twenty. Uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation decide a large share of the data marks, and both reward weekly repetition.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium carry the Higher Level difficulty. The habitual loss is moles arithmetic written without units or significant figures, which is a discipline fixable in short sessions rather than long ones.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume science, where terminology precision rather than understanding decides marks. Short timed recall twice a week outperforms a single long session by a wide margin, which suits a packed Khalifa City week unusually well.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy earns marks before prose is read and is the quickest available gain in the subject. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a quantitative policy paper whose arithmetic demand is specific and drillable rather than general.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers plus the Individual Oral, with an extra essay at Higher Level. The Individual Oral is the component prepared worst because it feels informal; it is a rehearsed ten-minute argument and needs a slot where the student can speak aloud without an audience.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A sixteen-hundred-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. It competes for hours with six subjects and is therefore the first thing dropped. A small number of sessions on argument structure is unusually efficient here.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research, combining with Theory of Knowledge for up to three bonus points. The marks are decided by the research question in the first fortnight, so early hours are worth several times late ones on this component.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: MYP and DP ab initio or B
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. It sits in the week all year rather than peaking, so short regular oral practice beats an exam-term push.

sections.heading: Can you get an IB home tutor in Khalifa City, and should the session be at home at all
paragraphs: In-home tutoring exists in Khalifa City and the market price is knowable. In-home one-to-one visits across the Emirates are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, per the Bestimate rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Khalifa City is inland and well served, so the travel loading here is lower than for the island communities.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and that is the position across every country page on this site. What we deliver to Khalifa City is one-to-one teaching over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own school material on screen.

The reason that suits Khalifa City specifically is about the hour rather than the money. The real constraint in this community is not distance but the density of a Diploma week, and the hours that actually survive are late: 19:30 on a weekday, 10:00 on a Saturday. Those are difficult hours for a visiting tutor to offer and trivial hours for us to staff, because nobody is driving to or from anywhere.

The honest case for a visit still exists. For a younger child, or a student who will not stay at the table without an adult physically present, somebody in the room can decide the outcome and no amount of video quality replaces it. If that describes your child, you want a provider who does visits, and we would rather say so than persuade you into a format that will not work.
