sections.heading: Khalifa City bell times and the hour that actually survives
paragraphs: Home-by times vary more inside this one community than families expect, and the variation decides the schedule. A student at a school within Khalifa City or minutes away can be through the door by 15:00 or 15:30. A student travelling to Al Bateen, Al Mushrif or across the bridges is closer to 16:30, and may have a Creativity Activity Service commitment at school before that journey even starts.

The table below sets out the pattern. It is not an argument for booking late for its own sake; some students work well at 16:30 and should be booked then. It is a correction to the default assumption that a late-afternoon slot works for everybody, which is the assumption most agencies make because it suits a tutor driving between two addresses.

The single most useful thing a parent can supply when booking is the actual arrival time rather than the preferred start time. A tutor who knows the student walks in at 16:20 plans a different first ten minutes from one who assumes a 15:30 finish. That one sentence removes most of the back-and-forth and prevents the first fortnight being spent discovering the schedule does not work.

Friday deserves a mention because it is underused. Most Abu Dhabi private schools finish around midday on a Friday and the weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, which makes a Saturday 10:00 block the one session in the week with a rested student in it. Families who move their heaviest subject there report it as the session that gets cancelled least.

sections.heading: Where a Khalifa City Diploma week's hours actually go
paragraphs: This is the exercise almost no family runs and almost every family benefits from. Write down the week as it is, in hours, before deciding how much tutoring to buy. School contact time, travel, homework and reading, Creativity Activity Service, any sport or instrument, and eight hours of sleep a night. Then look at what is left.

The number is usually smaller than expected, and the discovery changes the decision. A household that finds six discretionary hours in the week does not buy three subjects of tutoring; it buys one, and perhaps drops something. A household that cannot find any hours without cutting sleep has a workload problem rather than a tutoring problem, and buying hours will make the grades worse rather than better.

That second case is more common than providers admit. A Diploma student sleeping six hours and underperforming is not short of teaching. The honest advice there is to reduce the load, talk to the school about the Higher Level combination, and come back to tutoring afterwards. We would rather say that in a free trial lesson than take a year of fees for an engagement that was never going to work.

Where there is room, the arithmetic also tells you the format. Two short sessions fit a full week better than one long one, because two forty-five-minute holes are easier to find than a ninety-minute block. And a Saturday morning is additive rather than displacing, which is why it is the slot we suggest first for extended work.

sections.heading: Creativity Activity Service and sport compete for the same slot
paragraphs: Creativity Activity Service is a Diploma requirement rather than an extra, which means it cannot simply be dropped to make room. It typically consumes two to four hours a week and is often scheduled at school, immediately after the day ends, which extends the effective school day for exactly the students who already travel furthest.

Sport and music are different: they are genuinely optional and they are usually the thing a household sacrifices when a grade slips. That trade should be made consciously rather than by drift. A student who gives up the one commitment that gets them outdoors and away from a screen in order to add a weekly tutoring hour has not obviously improved their position, and the effect on sleep and mood is real.

The practical resolution in Khalifa City households tends to be one of three. Move the tutoring to a Saturday morning, which is additive rather than displacing. Reduce the training commitment by one session a week rather than abandoning it. Or accept one subject of tutoring instead of two, which is almost always the better of the available compromises.

Where a student is in an examination year and genuinely overloaded, the conversation worth having is with the school about the Higher Level combination rather than with a tutor about hours. Three Higher Levels is the requirement; which three, and whether a student should be carrying a particular one, is a decision the school can revisit in the first Diploma year and almost never does unprompted.

sections.heading: Reading the school report before you buy anything
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions in Khalifa City are triggered by a report, and most reports are read for the grade alone. A report contains considerably more usable information than that, and reading it properly often changes what should be bought, or whether anything should be bought at all.

Look for four things. A grade compared against the same subject a term earlier, which tells you about direction rather than level. A predicted grade compared against the current one, which tells you what the teacher thinks is reachable. Effort or engagement indicators, because a strong grade with weak engagement and a weak grade with strong engagement are completely different problems. And any comment naming a specific component or skill.

That fourth item is the one worth chasing. A comment saying extended written answers lack development is a diagnosis you can act on; a comment saying should continue to work hard is not. If the report contains nothing specific, email the subject teacher and ask one question: which component or skill is costing the marks. Teachers answer that question well and parents rarely ask it.

Abu Dhabi private schools are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. A school-level evaluation outcome is a whole-school judgement across every phase and subject, and your child sits in one subject in one year group, so it tells you far less about their lessons than the subject report does. Read the subject detail and check the date on anything published.

sections.heading: What the market charges around Khalifa City
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked tutoring pages for Abu Dhabi queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no Khalifa City family transacts in. This section publishes the dirham bands with the source of each, so you can measure any quote you receive, including ours, against something checkable.

At the entry level, university-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages. That band buys supervision and fluency work, which is genuinely useful for a Middle Years student or a primary pupil and is the wrong purchase for a Higher Level Diploma component eight weeks out.

The middle band, a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, is where most useful Diploma support sits, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. At one weekly session that is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's own mid-band estimate. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above; premium named tutors have been quoted to AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. None of the figures in this section is an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, permits, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own, and the boundary is worth stating plainly because parts of this market blur it. A tutor may teach content, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a research question is answerable, suggest reading, model technique on a different example, and say why a paragraph is weak. All of that raises marks legitimately.

No tutor at IB Gram will write an Internal Assessment, draft an Extended Essay, compose a Theory of Knowledge essay or produce coursework. We do not sell completed assessments at any price. One operation in this market openly offers finished Internal Assessments, and the consequence of that falls on the student as a malpractice finding rather than on the seller.

On permits, the position in the UAE is clear and usable as a screening tool. Private tutoring is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to school and government teachers, private and public-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify the current policy if it matters. Either way, it is an arrangement we never facilitate, and no regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram.

Lessons for Khalifa City families are one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and your child's own school material on screen. The practical advantage here is the hour rather than the money: the slots that survive a Diploma week are late, and those are difficult for a visiting tutor and trivial for us.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student actually have free?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most parents expect. Thirty to thirty-five hours of school contact time, four to eight travelling depending on the school, ten to fifteen on homework and Internal Assessment work, two to four on Creativity Activity Service, three to six on sport or music, and fifty-six on sleep at eight hours a night. Write that down before buying tutoring. Households that run the arithmetic usually buy one subject rather than three, which is almost always the better decision.

faqs.question: What should a tutoring hour displace in a full Khalifa City week?
faqs.answer: Not sleep, which is the trade most households make by accident and the one that costs more than the session gains. A tired student learns less than an untaught one. The honest options are to move the session to a Saturday morning, which is additive rather than displacing, to reduce a sport or music commitment by one session rather than abandoning it, or to support one subject instead of two. All three are better than borrowing from the night.

faqs.question: Can Creativity Activity Service be dropped to make room for tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, because it is a Diploma requirement rather than an extra. It typically consumes two to four hours a week and is often scheduled at school immediately after the day ends, which extends the effective day for exactly the students who already travel furthest. That is why it appears in the weekly hours table as fixed rather than flexible, and why the realistic trades sit elsewhere in the week.

faqs.question: My son sleeps six hours and his grades are falling, so how much tutoring does he need?
faqs.answer: Probably none yet. A student sleeping six hours and underperforming is not short of teaching, and adding an hour will make the position worse rather than better. The conversation worth having is with the school about the Higher Level combination and the overall load, which schools can revisit in the first Diploma year and rarely do unprompted. We would rather tell you that in a free trial lesson than take a year of fees for an engagement that cannot work.

faqs.question: Why is Saturday morning the slot you recommend first?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only hour in an Abu Dhabi week with a rested student in it. Most private schools finish around midday on a Friday and the weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, so a 10:00 Saturday session catches a student before the week has restarted. It is also additive rather than displacing: it does not compete with homework, training or sleep. Families report it as the session least likely to be cancelled, which matters most in the fortnight before a deadline.

faqs.question: How should I read my daughter's school report before booking anything?
faqs.answer: Look for four things rather than one. The grade compared against the same subject a term earlier, which shows direction. The predicted grade against the current one, which shows what the teacher thinks is reachable. Effort indicators, because a weak grade with strong effort and a strong grade with weak effort are different problems. And any comment naming a specific component or skill, which is the most useful line in the document and the brief for any tutoring.

faqs.question: What if the report says nothing specific about the problem?
faqs.answer: Email the subject teacher one question: which component or skill is costing the marks. Teachers answer that question well and parents almost never ask it, usually because reports feel like finished documents rather than the start of a conversation. A reply naming extended written answers, or data analysis, or unshown working, is a tutoring brief you can act on. A reply saying your child should continue to work hard is not, and tells you to ask again differently.

faqs.question: Does a school evaluation rating tell me about my child's lessons?
faqs.answer: Much less than most parents assume. Abu Dhabi private schools are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and a school-level evaluation outcome is a whole-school judgement across every phase and subject. Your child sits in one subject in one year group. The subject-level report and the teacher's own comment tell you considerably more, and anything published should be checked for its date.

faqs.question: Is one long session or two short ones better in a packed week?
faqs.answer: Two short ones, for two reasons. Practically, two forty-five-minute holes are easier to find in a committed week than a single ninety-minute block. Educationally, accuracy and fluency work consolidates in the gap between contacts, so two sessions halve that gap and double the number of times a recurring error is caught. The exception is extended work, an Internal Assessment draft or a full timed paper, which needs a Saturday morning rather than a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What do Khalifa City families typically pay for Diploma support?
faqs.answer: At published market bands rather than ours, a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is about AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly session on Bestimate's mid-band estimate. Student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 65, specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Measure any quote, including ours, against those figures.

faqs.question: Is it allowed for a Khalifa City teacher to tutor their own pupil for a fee?
faqs.answer: You should assume not. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact regulatory wording and verify the current policy if it matters. Either way, it is an arrangement we never facilitate and never advertise.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with my daughter's Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: With feedback, yes; with writing, never. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether her research question is answerable, suggest reading, and tell her which section is weak and why so that she can fix it herself. Nobody at IB Gram writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay or produces coursework at any price. The school supervisor signs the work off and should know outside support exists; concealment creates a risk that falls on her.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff the late slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than offering a time that will not work. Late weekday evenings and Saturday mornings are the two windows most in demand across Abu Dhabi, and Khalifa City competes with Saadiyat, Al Reem, Yas and Al Raha households for them. Common subjects usually match within a few days; a narrow Higher Level combination at one fixed hour can take longer. Being told early leaves you time to look elsewhere while it still matters.

intro.heading: Does anybody near Madinat Zayed actually teach this course?
paragraphs: That is the question, and it deserves a real answer rather than a page of reassurance. Madinat Zayed sits in central Abu Dhabi, close to Al Markaziyah, Al Danah and Khalidiya, within easy reach of the island's school network. Finding someone willing to tutor nearby is not difficult. Finding someone who has taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level, or Economics internal assessment commentaries, or Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, within driving distance and free at five o'clock on a Tuesday, is a different proposition entirely.

The arithmetic is simple and nobody in this market publishes it. The Diploma is offered by a modest number of schools in Abu Dhabi. Each school runs a single cohort per course per year, sometimes in single figures at Higher Level. The adults qualified to teach a specific Higher Level course are therefore a small group, most of them employed full-time, and some of them barred from tutoring students at their own school under professional-ethics rules. A family searching for one of those people inside a twenty-minute radius is searching a very small space.

For a popular Standard Level subject the picture is better. Standard Level mathematics, Business Management and English have reasonable coverage, and an in-home arrangement in Madinat Zayed is genuinely achievable at published market rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. The trouble starts where the need is specific, and specific needs are exactly what families tend to have by the time they start searching.

This matters because the alternative to disclosure is a bad outcome three weeks in. A family pays for a tutor described as an IB specialist, discovers in session three that the tutor is learning the course alongside the student, and has lost both the money and the weeks. That pattern is common enough in this market that it is worth arming a parent against it, which is what the five-question test further down this page is for. Ten minutes of specific questions, asked before any money changes hands, filters out most of the people who should not be teaching a Diploma course, and none of those questions requires the parent to understand the subject.

IB Gram's answer is to widen the pool rather than to pretend it is wide. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the exact course and level, which removes distance from the selection entirely. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. And when the specialist a family needs is not available, we say so, give an expected wait, and put the alternatives in writing instead of quietly matching whoever is free.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-madinat-zayed.programmesIntro: Availability behaves differently in each programme, and knowing where your child sits tells you how hard the search will be before you start it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with internal assessments carrying substantial weight in most subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Grades run 1 to 7 inside a 45-point total. The specialism required is narrow: a tutor needs the course and the level, not the subject.
programmes.countryNote: This is where coverage is tightest in Abu Dhabi. Diploma provision concentrates in a limited number of schools, Higher Level cohorts are small, and demand for the same specialists peaks simultaneously across the city before mock windows and internal assessment deadlines. A family in Madinat Zayed should expect to search outside the neighbourhood and plan earlier than feels necessary.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked 0 to 8, with a Personal Project in the final year. Subject demand is broader and less specialised, so the available pool of competent tutors is considerably larger than at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where a local arrangement is easiest to defend on its own terms. The teaching need is general rather than course-specific, so proximity costs a family less here than it would at Higher Level, and a parent in Madinat Zayed choosing an in-home tutor for an MYP 3 student is not sacrificing much.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, transdisciplinary and without external examinations. Support is about reading, number fluency and confidence, and the honest position is that most primary students do not need paid tutoring at all.
programmes.countryNote: Coverage here is not the problem; necessity is. If a Madinat Zayed family is being sold a long weekly commitment for a primary-aged child, ask what specific outcome it is aimed at and what would signal that it should stop. Short, infrequent work is almost always the better answer at this stage.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses studied alongside a career-related study and a personal and professional skills core. Offered by far fewer schools, which makes both school places and tutoring coverage narrower again than for the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: A family asking about the Career-related Programme in Abu Dhabi usually has one specific school in mind. Confirm which DP courses sit inside that school's programme before looking for a tutor, because the subject mix differs between strands and a tutor has to be matched to the actual DP course rather than to the programme name.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-madinat-zayed.subjectsIntro: The list below is ordered by how hard the specialist is to find rather than by faculty, because that is the information a searching parent actually needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
subjects.description: Proof by induction, complex numbers, Maclaurin series, differential equations and Paper 3 problem solving. The narrowest common specialism in Abu Dhabi, and the one most likely to require a tutor outside the emirate. A Standard Level tutor cannot stretch into it; the content is different in kind.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
subjects.description: Chi-squared testing, the Poisson distribution, hypothesis testing and graph theory. Scarcer again than AA Higher Level in practice, because fewer teachers have taught the statistics extensions in depth. Expect a wait or a tutor based elsewhere.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Higher Level
subjects.description: Energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, organic mechanisms and the individual investigation. Demand peaks sharply in investigation season, when every school in the city needs the same small group of people during the same six weeks.

subjects.name: Physics, Higher Level
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion, thermodynamics and the individual investigation, where uncertainty handling and graph treatment carry marks students rarely practise. Another seasonal pinch point around investigation deadlines.

subjects.name: Biology, Higher Level
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where command terms decide a large share of marks. Coverage is better than in chemistry and physics, partly because more teachers have taught it and partly because demand is spread more evenly through the year.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Internal assessment commentaries built on published news articles, with diagram marks routinely lost to missing labels. Commentary coaching is a specific skill and the people who have marked them are a smaller group than the people who have taught the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
subjects.description: The broadest pool of the four mathematics combinations, with reasonable local coverage. A sensible place to accept a nearby arrangement if proximity matters to your household for other reasons.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Good coverage at both levels. The common failure is description where analysis and evaluation were required, which is a writing problem and responds well to feedback on the student's own work rather than to more content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Broad coverage, with oral components fixed in the school calendar. The usual waste of hours is reading more texts rather than practising timed analysis of texts already studied, which any competent tutor should redirect.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Reasonable coverage, with marks most often lost in the methodology and ethics sections of the internal assessment rather than in content. Quick to fix with a tutor who has marked them before.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Seasonal rather than scarce. Demand concentrates around the school's interim deadlines, and support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts only. Nothing may be written for a student.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: Required in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate class organisation for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. Frequently left out of a family's tutoring plan and then urgent.

sections.heading: The honest answer to the question in the search box
paragraphs: Direct response first: an IB home tutor in Madinat Zayed, through IB Gram, means a Diploma specialist matched to your child's exact course and level, teaching one-to-one over live video at an Abu Dhabi-friendly hour, with a free trial lesson first. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If a tutor physically in your home is the requirement, we are not the provider, and it is better to know that now.

The reason the format exists is the scarcity described above. If the pool of adults who have taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level in Abu Dhabi is small, and the subset willing to drive to Madinat Zayed on a weekday evening is smaller, then insisting on proximity is choosing from almost nobody. Removing distance from the selection is not a sales device; it is the only way to make course-level matching possible in a market this size.

It is worth saying what this does not solve. It does not make specialists infinite. Higher Level mathematics and science tutors fill up before mock windows and internal assessment deadlines, when demand across the city peaks in the same six weeks. It does not substitute for school teaching, and it does not supply motivation a student does not have. A provider claiming otherwise is making promises the market cannot keep.

What it does do is change the question a family is asking from who is nearby to who has taught this. The rest of this page is about how to answer that second question properly: how to test a tutor, how to verify them, what to do when none is free, and what honest disclosure looks like when the tutor turns out to be based somewhere else.

sections.heading: Why the specialist pool is thin in Abu Dhabi, with the arithmetic
paragraphs: The Diploma is a minority provision in Abu Dhabi. Most private schools follow British, Indian or American curricula, and the schools offering the Diploma run one cohort per course per year. At Higher Level those cohorts are frequently small. That immediately bounds the number of people in the emirate who have taught a particular Higher Level course to a recent syllabus.

Three further constraints cut into that number. Most of those teachers are in full-time employment and have limited evening capacity. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, so the nearest qualified person is often the one person who may not teach your child. And demand for the remainder peaks simultaneously, because every school's internal deadlines fall within a few weeks of each other.

Put those together and the practical position is clear. For a named Higher Level course in a specific six-week window, the available local pool can be zero. That is not a failure of any particular agency; it is the shape of the market. What distinguishes providers is whether they tell you this before taking a payment or after.

The honest implication for a Madinat Zayed family is to plan earlier than feels necessary. Booking internal assessment support four to six weeks before the school's draft deadline costs the same as booking it two weeks before and is far more likely to get the right person. The families who struggle most are not the ones with the hardest problems; they are the ones who started looking last.

sections.heading: Five questions that test whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: A parent does not need subject expertise to test a tutor. They need five questions whose answers are either specific or evasive, and the difference is audible within ten minutes. Ask them before paying, on a call or in the free trial lesson, and listen for whether the answer contains the syllabus or only enthusiasm.

The questions are these. First: which exact course and level have you taught, and in which years. A specialist names the course and the level without being prompted; a generalist says mathematics or science. Second: what is the weighting of each component in this course. A specialist knows the paper percentages and the internal assessment share; a generalist estimates. Third: name the assessment criteria for the internal assessment in this subject and what each is worth. A specialist can list them; a generalist describes the task instead.

Fourth: where do students in this course most often lose marks, and what do you do about it. A specialist gives two or three diagnosable failures and the drill for each; a generalist talks about confidence and practice. Fifth: what would make you tell us to stop. A specialist has an answer, usually involving a measurable change in an error log; a provider selling hours changes the subject.

Run those five on any provider, including us. They are also a reasonable test of this page: if the sections above and below do not contain that level of specificity about Diploma assessment, the page is marketing. A family that asks these questions once will never again mistake a confident tutor for a qualified one, which is worth more than any single lesson.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor in the UAE: permit, status and the claims that cannot be true
paragraphs: Testing competence is one thing; verifying legitimacy is another, and it is quicker. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service page for it is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted at you is unverified; one figure circulating in this market could not be confirmed and should not be repeated.

Then there are claims that cannot be true of a tutor at all. Nobody is a KHDA-approved or ADEK-approved tutor, because those bodies license and inspect schools rather than approving individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific thing with a number attached.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. Nor can any tutor be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner without evidence of current examiner status, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. A provider making any of these claims has told you how much of the rest to believe.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody is free, set out as a ladder
paragraphs: Most providers answer this question with silence, which is why it is worth answering explicitly. When no specialist for a course and level is available, there are four options and a fifth that is sometimes correct, and a family should be offered all of them in writing rather than having one chosen for them.

Option one: a different qualified tutor on the same course at a different time. This works when the constraint is the slot rather than the specialism, and it is the most common resolution. Option two: a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same IB course, working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before booking. The syllabus is identical wherever the tutor sits; the time zone is a scheduling fact with a clear answer, and concealing it is the actual problem rather than the arrangement itself.

Option three: shorter sessions at higher frequency with an available qualified tutor while the preferred slot clears, described openly as a holding pattern with the error log carried across when the permanent tutor takes over. Option four: a named wait with a date, so a family can plan around it instead of calling weekly. Option five, which providers rarely offer: wait and do nothing paid for now. In DP1 term one that is frequently the right advice, and a provider who never gives it is not advising.

The reason to publish this ladder is that it makes a promise checkable. If you contact us about AI Higher Level in internal assessment season and the answer is an immediate confident yes with no mention of location or wait, something has gone wrong with our own process and you should ask which rung of this ladder you are actually on.

sections.heading: The tutor who is not in the UAE: what changes and what does not
paragraphs: Families are entitled to care where a tutor sits, and entitled to be told. Several ranking sites in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. The problem in each case is the concealment rather than the geography, and the fix is disclosure before booking.

What does not change when a tutor is based elsewhere: the IB syllabus, the assessment criteria, the paper structures, the command terms, the internal assessment requirements and the mark schemes. These are set by the IB and are identical in every country. A tutor who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level has taught the same course your child is taking, regardless of which city they were in when they taught it.

What does change: the time zone, and therefore the slots available. A tutor several hours behind Gulf Standard Time cannot teach at 4pm your time without it being early morning theirs, which is fine for some tutors and not others. Local context also changes: a tutor outside the UAE will not know your school's internal calendar, the ADEK inspection position or the Arabic and Islamic Education requirements sitting on the timetable, so those have to be supplied rather than assumed.

Our practice is to state the tutor's location in the match, before any payment, and to set the slot on Gulf Standard Time. If a family would rather wait for a UAE-based specialist, that is a legitimate preference and we will give the expected wait instead. What we will not do is take the booking and let the time-zone conversation happen in week two.

sections.heading: What scarcity does to price, and what it should not do
paragraphs: Scarcity raises prices, and in tutoring it raises them most at exactly the moment a family is least able to judge. The published bands, read in October 2026, run as follows: budget online tuition at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270; and premium named or examiner-led tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above, BartyED publishing AED 650.

A Higher Level specialist in investigation season sits at the upper end of those bands for a straightforward reason: there are few of them and everybody wants them in the same six weeks. That is legitimate pricing. What is not legitimate is a premium charged for scarcity the provider has manufactured by not telling you that a cheaper, equally qualified tutor is free next week, or by implying a shortage that does not exist for the course your child actually takes.

The protection against both is the diagnosis. If the first lesson establishes that your child's problem is uncertainty treatment in a physics graph and the Exploration being three weeks late, you now know what you are buying and roughly how long it takes. A rate of AED 270 an hour for six sessions of precisely that is a defensible purchase. The same rate for an open-ended arrangement with no diagnosis is not, whatever the tutor's credentials.

Every figure here is a market rate from a named published source rather than an IB Gram price; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson, when the course, level and session length are known. And the other side of honest pricing is honest finishing: a provider that tells you when the work is done forgoes revenue, which is precisely why it is the signal worth looking for.

sections.heading: The one thing no specialist may do, however scarce they are
paragraphs: Scarcity creates pressure, and pressure is where academic honesty gets compromised. A family three weeks from an internal assessment deadline with no specialist available is exactly the family most likely to be offered something they should refuse. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the price is lower than a block of legitimate coaching.

The boundary is set by IB rules rather than by preference. A tutor may discuss and narrow a research question, explain a technique the student then applies, check that the work sits at the level of the course, give criterion-level feedback on a draft the student wrote, and help build a schedule that finishes before the school's deadline. A tutor may not produce any part of it, supply calculations, rewrite text or edit a piece to completion.

The consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than the provider. The supervisor signs to the authenticity of the student's work, so submitting purchased or ghost-written material puts the student's own declaration in question and can lead to a malpractice finding affecting the whole Diploma rather than one subject. No deadline is worth that exposure, and a provider that offers it when a family is desperate has identified the moment to exploit rather than the moment to help.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. They are published by the IB and the examination boards and should be reached there or through the school; reproducing them is a copyright matter. What a tutor adds is teaching a student to use them, which is the part that keeps working after the session ends.

faqs.question: Is there anybody in central Abu Dhabi who has actually taught my child's Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and fewer than you would expect. Diploma provision in Abu Dhabi sits in a limited number of schools, Higher Level cohorts are often small, most qualified teachers are employed full-time with limited evening capacity, and professional-ethics rules are reported to bar them from paid tutoring of students at their own school. For a named Higher Level course in a six-week peak window the available local pool can be zero. That is the shape of the market rather than any agency's failure.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Ask five questions. Which exact course and level have you taught, and when. What is each component worth. Name the internal assessment criteria and their marks. Where do students in this course lose marks, and what do you do about it. And what would make you tell us to stop. A specialist answers all five specifically; a generalist talks about confidence and practice. The difference is audible in about ten minutes and requires no subject knowledge from you.

faqs.question: Could we pay the teacher who already teaches the class instead?
faqs.answer: Because it is barred. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. The practical effect is that the nearest qualified person is often the one who may not teach your child, which is part of why the local pool is so thin.

faqs.question: What do you do if no specialist is free for our subject?
faqs.answer: You get the options in writing rather than a substitute chosen quietly: a different qualified tutor on the same course at another time; a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before booking; shorter and more frequent sessions with an available tutor as a stated holding pattern; a named wait with a date; or the advice to wait and buy nothing yet. The last is often right in DP1 term one, when nothing is urgent.

faqs.question: Does it matter if the tutor is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It matters for scheduling and local context, and not at all for the syllabus. The IB sets the courses, criteria, paper structures and mark schemes identically everywhere, so a tutor who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level has taught your child's course. What changes is the time zone, which bounds the available slots, and local knowledge of your school's internal calendar and the mandatory UAE subjects. Those have to be supplied rather than assumed, and the location should be stated before you pay.

faqs.question: When is the worst time to start looking for a Diploma specialist?
faqs.answer: Two weeks before an internal assessment draft deadline, or in the fortnight before a mock window. Demand across the city peaks in the same few weeks because schools set their internal deadlines independently but within a similar period, so the same small group of specialists is wanted everywhere at once. Booking four to six weeks earlier costs the same and is far more likely to secure the right person. The families who struggle most are usually the ones who started last.

faqs.question: Why would a tutoring company admit it might not have anybody available?
faqs.answer: Because the alternative is a worse outcome in week three. A family that pays for an advertised specialist and discovers the tutor is learning the course alongside the student has lost the money and the weeks, which is a more expensive failure than a disclosed wait. Publishing a fallback ladder also makes the promise checkable: if you are given an immediate confident yes in peak season with no mention of location or wait, you can ask which option you are actually on.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Since it costs nothing, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor not to hold one, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be described as KHDA approved or ADEK approved?
faqs.answer: No. Those bodies license and inspect schools rather than approving individual tutors. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain; KHDA does the equivalent in Dubai. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permit with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal. If a provider uses approval language, ask for the permit number and see what arrives.

faqs.question: What should I think when a site advertises a satisfaction percentage?
faqs.answer: Ask for the sample size, the date and the method, and treat the absence of all three as your answer. Pages in this market publish satisfaction figures and average tutor scores with nothing behind them, and some show star ratings that differ between the visible page and the markup behind it. A number without a basis is a marketing device. A rate band with a named published source and a date, which is what the figures on this page are, is something you can go and check yourself.

faqs.question: Our internal assessment deadline is in three weeks and nobody is available. What now?
faqs.answer: The honest options are narrower than the usual ones. A short block with an available qualified tutor in the same subject, aimed at finishing what the student already has rather than reshaping the question. Help building a schedule that gets the draft submitted on time. And nothing else: no part of the work may be produced for the student, and a provider offering to supply a finished internal assessment is creating a malpractice exposure that can reach the whole Diploma rather than one subject grade.

faqs.question: How many sessions does Higher Level support usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is a habit or a hole. Habits such as uncertainty treatment, missing method marks or incomplete graph labelling take two or three sessions each. Genuine content gaps at Higher Level take a term of weekly work, because the material is new rather than mislearnt. The diagnosis in the first lesson should tell you which one you have, and a tutor who cannot distinguish the two after a lesson with a marked paper has not diagnosed anything.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level easier to find a tutor for than Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Considerably. Standard Level mathematics, Business Management and English have reasonable coverage in Abu Dhabi, and a local arrangement is genuinely achievable for them. Higher Level sciences and both Higher Level mathematics courses are the narrow specialisms, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is the narrowest of all because fewer teachers have taught the statistics extensions in depth. If your need is Standard Level, you have more options than this page's tone implies.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing we can send with an enquiry?
faqs.answer: The exact course and level, the school, the nearest dated deadline, and a photograph of a recent marked piece of work. Those four let us say immediately whether a specialist is likely to be free or whether this is a wait, and they let the tutor arrive at the first lesson already knowing what to test. An enquiry that says help with IB science produces a sales conversation; one with those four items produces an answer.

The first lesson is free and is used as a diagnosis. Tuition runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

Ask any of them to describe the paper structure of the course your child sits, and you will get an answer in specifics rather than reassurance. intro.heading: The problem with hiring a tutor in a district with no school
paragraphs: Masdar City is an unusual address to tutor into. It is a planned low-carbon district next to Abu Dhabi International Airport, built around a university campus, a free zone and the offices of energy and technology firms. The streets are shaded and walkable, the residential stock is apartments rather than villas, and there is no private K-12 school inside the district. Every school-age child here travels out, most often into the Khalifa City corridor or Mohammed Bin Zayed City.

That has a direct consequence for finding a tutor. In a community built around a school, the nearest competent person is often a teacher from that school, and local word of mouth carries real information. Masdar City has no such channel. The adults nearby are engineers, researchers and free-zone employees, and the tutoring adverts that surface for the district are placed by agencies based elsewhere in the emirate. Nothing about the distance tells you whether the person understands the Diploma.

Families here tend to be comfortable with that framing, because many of them assess suppliers for a living. The useful question is not where is the nearest tutor but what evidence exists that this tutor can teach the course. That evidence is cheap to collect and almost nobody collects it, which is why this page leads with six questions rather than with a sales pitch. The questions work on any provider in the emirate, and they work on us. We publish them knowing some readers will use them to hire somebody else, because a market where parents ask for specifics is a market in which subject specialists do better than generalists with a wide advert and a short drive. That is a better outcome for every family in the district.

The IB makes verification easier than most curricula, because the structure is public and specific. A Diploma course has a defined set of assessment components with published weightings, an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria, and command terms that dictate what an answer must do. Somebody who teaches it can describe all of that from memory in plain language. Somebody who has only read about it cannot, and the gap shows within two minutes of conversation.

IB Gram's own position should be stated before the checks, because it is part of the honest answer. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Masdar City family, the lesson happens over live video, one student and one teacher, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own marked work on the screen. The remainder of this page covers what the in-home market actually charges, so you can judge that choice against a real number rather than a slogan.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-masdar-city.programmesIntro: Masdar City children sit all three IB programmes, usually at schools in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. The programme matters because the thing that needs fixing is different in each one: criteria in the Middle Years Programme, coursework calendars in the Diploma, habits in the Primary Years.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at higher level, plus theory of knowledge, the extended essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria identified by letter. The final papers are only part of the picture; a weak internal assessment caps a grade before the student walks into the exam hall.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates living in Masdar City are commuting to Khalifa City, Al Raha or the islands, which costs them an hour of usable evening that a classmate walking home keeps. We plan around that by front-loading coursework coaching into the autumn term, when the timetable still has slack, rather than running it alongside final-paper revision in the spring.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with command terms carrying most of the weight. Students arriving from a right-answer culture score badly at first, not because the content defeats them but because a correct answer with no justification earns almost nothing. The personal project in the final year is the first extended independent work most of them meet.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the Middle Years to Diploma step generates more tutoring requests than any other transition. A student can hold strong criterion scores and still lack the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches assumes in its first fortnight. That is a specific, testable gap, and six to ten weeks of focused work usually closes it.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with transdisciplinary units rather than subject silos, and no external examinations. Support here is about number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of explaining thinking out loud, because those are what the Middle Years Programme will start marking. Parents are often told everything is fine and then meet criterion-based marking at Year 7 with no warning.
programmes.countryNote: For Masdar City families this is usually the quiet decision point. A Primary Years child here will likely move into the Middle Years Programme at the same school, so the useful work is arithmetic fluency and written explanation now, in short sessions, rather than remediation later under assessment pressure.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-masdar-city.subjectsIntro: These are the IB courses Masdar City families ask about most. Each description names what the assessment actually tests, because that is the level of specificity a tutor should be able to match in conversation before you hire them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation. Higher level adds Maclaurin series, differential equations and harder integration, and Paper 3 asks for an unfamiliar idea to be extended under time pressure. The marks lost are usually justification marks: a correct final answer with no visible reasoning collects less than a flawed attempt that shows method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and deliberate use of technology. Students pick it expecting an easier ride and meet hypothesis testing, chi-squared and, at higher level, graph theory and matrices. The calculator is assessed as a skill, so a student who cannot operate their own handset at speed loses marks unrelated to mathematics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics is the gateway and the data-analysis work is the differentiator. Uncertainty propagation, graph linearisation and error discussion are where strong students lose marks, and they are teachable in a handful of lessons because the technique is finite rather than open-ended.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate grades at higher level. The internal assessment causes more damage than any topic: a research question that cannot generate enough quantitative data to analyse properly caps the mark, and that is decided in September rather than discovered in February.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the trap and command terms are the remedy. A student who writes everything they know scores below a student who answers the verb in the question. Timed extended-response practice marked against the published scheme moves grades faster than any amount of note revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most candidates draw them incompletely, with unlabelled axes or no shifted curve. The higher-level quantitative paper is mechanical once drilled, which makes it the cheapest block of marks on the course for anyone currently avoiding it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time, plus an individual oral connecting a global issue to two texts. Shape beats cleverness here: a single argument held cleanly across ten minutes outscores a sharper reading delivered without structure. Most of the gain comes from planning discipline rather than wider reading.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, both marked against criteria that reward precise handling of knowledge claims. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score low. Coaching is about structure, example selection and keeping the essay anchored to the title rather than drifting into general commentary.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece in a chosen subject, with a supervisor and a research question that has to be answerable in that length. The commonest failure is a question too broad to answer, which is a fifteen-minute conversation in September and an unrecoverable problem in March.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the IB in UAE private schools by federal requirement, and it is routinely the subject nobody plans for. Support works from the school's own scheme of work and its assessments, because additional or different content for the mandatory subjects needs Ministry permission.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-masdar-city.regionsIntro: Masdar City sits on the eastern side of the city near the airport, which puts a particular set of neighbourhoods and schools within reach. Each one changes the school run, and the school run decides what time a weekday lesson can start.

This is the default for a core Diploma subject and the format that benefits most from the short commute Masdar City offers.

sections.heading: Six questions that reveal whether a tutor really knows the IB
paragraphs: Ask a prospective tutor to describe the assessment structure of the exact course your child sits. Not the IB in general: Physics HL, or Analysis and Approaches SL, or Economics HL. A teacher of that course will tell you how many papers there are, roughly what each is worth, what the internal assessment contributes and how it is marked. Someone who has only read a prospectus will answer in adjectives.

The second question is about criteria. IB internal assessments are marked against criteria identified by letter, and each has a published descriptor and mark allocation. A specialist can tell you which criterion your child's last piece of work lost marks on and what the next band up requires. This is the single most diagnostic question available to a parent, and it takes ten seconds to ask.

The remaining four cover command terms, the difference between the two maths routes, how the tutor handles coursework, and whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. The command-term question matters because evaluate, justify and compare demand different answers, and a tutor who treats them as synonyms will teach your child to lose marks politely. The coursework question matters because an offer to help write an internal assessment is an offer to put your child in front of a malpractice panel.

None of this requires you to know the subject. You are listening for specificity and for comfort with the detail, the same way you would assess any technical supplier. A tutor who welcomes the questions is usually the one worth hiring, and a tutor who deflects them has told you something useful at no cost.

sections.heading: What "home tutor" means for an address inside Masdar City
paragraphs: The phrase is worth taking apart, because Masdar City makes the usual assumptions wrong. The district is compact and pedestrian-first, with shaded streets and parking largely held at the edges. A tutor driving in for an hour is parking and walking at each end of the lesson, and that time is priced into whatever they charge.

The housing stock is apartments, which also shapes the practical question. A home visit assumes a room where a stranger can work undisturbed with a teenager for an hour while the household continues around them. In a two or three bedroom apartment, that room is usually the one everybody else is in. Many families discover this in week two and then start moving lessons to the kitchen table, which is not what they paid for.

The market for in-home tutoring in Abu Dhabi is real and priced accordingly. Bestimate's rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500. Against a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300, the difference is a travel premium. For a Masdar City address that premium buys a drive from wherever the tutor lives plus parking at the district edge, and it narrows your choice to people prepared to do it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so there is no sales motive in that comparison; we run them in India only. What we offer a Masdar City family instead is the whole specialist pool rather than the subset willing to drive, at the lower end of the two price bands, with sessions that can be 45 minutes when 45 minutes is what the work needs.

sections.heading: The IB courses Masdar City students sit, with the detail that matters
paragraphs: Parents often ask which IB subject needs tutoring most, and the honest answer is that it depends less on the subject than on where in the course the student is. A Diploma year has two distinct crises: the coursework crisis in the autumn, when internal assessments and the extended essay collide with ordinary teaching, and the technique crisis in the spring, when content is broadly known and marks are still being dropped.

The table below sets out the components that do the damage in the subjects Masdar City families request most. It is deliberately specific, because a tutor should be able to discuss any row in it without preparation. If you use one row as an opening question in a trial lesson, you will learn more than a profile page can tell you.

Two patterns are worth naming. First, the internal assessment is where the largest recoverable margin sits in most science subjects, and it is recoverable only early, because the research question constrains everything downstream. Second, in mathematics the loss is rarely conceptual. Students who can do the mathematics drop marks on presentation of method, on calculator discipline and on misreading what the question's verb asked for.

A Masdar City family with a Diploma candidate should therefore make one decision in September rather than six in March: which two components are going to be attacked this term. Everything else can wait, and attempting everything at once in a year that already contains theory of knowledge and the extended essay is how students end up doing many things badly.

sections.heading: What Abu Dhabi families pay, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because most budgets are built upwards. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that level you are buying supervision: someone to sit with a student through a problem set and keep them honest about doing it. That has value for a Year 8 who will not start homework alone. It will not touch an internal assessment or a Paper 3 technique problem.

The next band is a qualified subject tutor working online, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Unitors is the only competitor in this market that publishes an hourly rate at all, listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sits the specialist band for IB, IGCSE and A-level teaching, around AED 200 to 450 and beyond, where TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate's table shows AED 200 to 450 plus. The premium named tier, where BartyED quotes AED 650, is a different purchase again.

Monthly figures are more useful for planning than hourly ones. Published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. For one hour a week, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist support in an exam year.

Every number above is a market rate published by the provider named beside it, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. sections.heading: The permit question, and how a parent asks it without awkwardness
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rules are more parent-friendly than most people assume. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, which removes the usual excuse that compliance is expensive.

The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no fee listed, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fines is published, so if any provider quotes you a specific amount, they are repeating something unverified. The question to ask is simply whether the tutor holds the permit, and the answer is either yes with evidence or something less than that.

One Abu Dhabi specific belongs here. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK document, but do not arrange lessons with your child's own classroom teacher. Beyond the rule, a second teacher explaining a topic a different way is frequently what makes it land.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of weekly lessons can honestly achieve
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what they are buying over a term rather than over an hour. Eight weekly sessions is roughly a half-term block and it is enough to do one substantial thing well. It is not enough to rebuild two years of shaky foundations in three subjects, and anybody promising that is selling something else.

In practice a well-used eight weeks looks like this. Week one is diagnostic: a timed past paper or a recent marked assessment, gone through properly, with the lost marks grouped by cause. Weeks two to six attack the largest group, which for most students is narrower than expected, often a single topic plus a habit in how solutions are written out. Week seven consolidates under timed conditions. Week eight re-tests the original diagnostic so there is evidence rather than impression.

For a coursework block the shape differs. The first two sessions settle the research question and the data or text selection, which is where the ceiling on the mark gets set. The middle sessions teach the analysis the criteria require, with feedback on drafts the student has written. The final sessions are criterion-by-criterion review against the published descriptors, still on the student's own text.

What eight weeks will not do is move a grade in a subject where the student has not done the practice between lessons. That is worth saying plainly at the start. An hour a week is four per cent of a school week, and its job is to make the other ninety-six per cent productive. A tutor who tells you otherwise is managing your expectations rather than your child's learning.

sections.heading: Where our help stops, written down
paragraphs: The Abu Dhabi search results that return tutors also return services selling finished coursework. One operator in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. A student who submits purchased work risks a malpractice finding, and in a Diploma year that can cost the qualification rather than a grade. This is the clearest line in the business and it deserves to be written out rather than implied.

A tutor may teach the content an assessment draws on, explain how each lettered criterion is applied and what distinguishes one band from the next, press on a research question until it is answerable, teach data handling and referencing, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. That is teaching, and it is what the criteria expect a supervisor and a teacher to do.

A tutor may not supply text that reaches the submission, rewrite a passage into final form, produce the analysis, or hand over an exemplar to be adapted. IB Gram does not write, finish or supply assessed work of any kind, and a tutor asked to will decline and tell us. We would rather lose a booking than have a Masdar City student sitting in front of an academic-honesty panel.

The same restraint applies to materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We cite the official source and teach from material the student legitimately holds through school. A provider offering a library of mark schemes has told you how it treats rules in general.

sections.heading: Coverage, waiting time and what we do when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor page researched in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is odd, because every network has one. Requests are not spread evenly: Diploma mathematics and the sciences are asked for constantly, while a smaller higher-level option can sit quiet for weeks and then need a specialist within days.

For a Masdar City family that means an expectation rather than a promise. Core Diploma maths and science usually match within a week, trial lesson included. A narrower higher-level subject, or a request for one tutor to cover two subjects, can take up to a fortnight at peak times. We say which case you are in at the enquiry, not after you have waited, because a family planning a term needs the information before it is useless.

When no UAE-based specialist is free, we offer the alternative explicitly: a specialist elsewhere in the network teaching the same course over the same platform, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time so the evening is unaffected. That is disclosed before booking. Several providers route UAE families to numbers in other countries without mentioning it, and the concealment rather than the geography is the problem.

If the match is wrong after the trial, say so and we change it. The free trial lesson exists for exactly that, and your child's opinion counts, because an hour a week with somebody they cannot talk to achieves very little however strong the subject knowledge. There is no obligation after the trial and no cost to saying no.
