faqs.question: Is there an IB school inside Masdar City itself?
faqs.answer: No. Masdar City is a planned low-carbon district built around a university campus, a free zone and commercial offices, and it contains no private K-12 school. Children living here travel out, most often into the Khalifa City corridor, Mohammed Bin Zayed City or Al Raha, where the emirate's IB continuum and British-curriculum provision sits. That matters for tutoring because there is no local teacher population attached to a nearby campus, so a tutor who is physically close to you is close by coincidence rather than because they teach your child's course.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor into Masdar City apartments?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. For a Masdar City family the lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own marked work on screen. We still target the home-tutor search because it is what parents type, and then answer it properly: the in-home market here is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the comparison with an online specialist at AED 150 to 300 is set out above.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor actually understands the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe the assessment components of the exact course and level your child sits, and roughly what each is worth. Then ask which lettered criterion your child's last piece of internal assessment work lost marks on, and what the band above requires. A teacher of that course answers both in specifics. Someone who has only read about the programme answers in adjectives. You do not need subject knowledge to run this check, only to listen for whether the detail is there.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Masdar City children attend?
faqs.answer: Predominantly schools in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, which carries the emirate's IB continuum alongside British and American provision, and schools in Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah for families choosing value or a particular curriculum. All are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its inspection outcomes. We name schools as local context only and claim no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday lesson realistically start from Masdar City?
faqs.answer: For a child at a Khalifa City or Al Reef school, around 16:45 is workable, because a 15:30 finish usually becomes a 16:10 arrival. For a school on Al Raha Beach or the islands, 17:30 or later is more honest. We set the slot around the bad afternoon rather than the good one, because a student arriving at a lesson already worn out gets very little from the hour and you still pay for it. The slot then holds through the term.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a real substitute for someone sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: For an IB course at Diploma or Middle Years level, usually yes, and in some ways better. Both people annotate the same past paper, graphs are built live rather than copied, and the session can be recorded for revision. Two things must hold: a quiet room for the hour and a stable connection. For a much younger child who needs physical presence to stay on task, the honest answer is different, and we will tell you that rather than sell you a format that will not work.

faqs.question: What does a qualified IB tutor cost per hour for an Abu Dhabi family?
faqs.answer: Published rates give the shape of the market. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB teaching runs AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase quoting AED 270. In-home visits including travel are AED 180 to 500. Those are the market's published figures, read in October 2026; our own fee follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should I hire a tutor from my child's own school in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the exact wording against the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is clear. There is also a teaching argument: a second teacher explaining a topic differently is often what finally makes it make sense to a struggling student.

faqs.question: How much can eight weekly sessions change before a Diploma mock?
faqs.answer: Enough to do one substantial thing well. A realistic block opens with a marked timed paper, groups the lost marks by cause, spends four or five weeks attacking the largest group, then consolidates and re-tests. That usually means one topic plus one habit in how solutions are presented. It will not rebuild two years of shaky foundations across three subjects, and it depends on practice happening between lessons. An hour a week is about four per cent of a school week; its job is to make the rest productive.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's internal assessment in Masdar City?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the content the assessment draws on, explain how each lettered criterion is applied, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, teach data handling and referencing, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor cannot supply text for the submission, rewrite a passage into final form, produce the analysis or hand over an exemplar to adapt. IB Gram does not write or finish assessed work, and services advertising completed internal assessments expose the candidate to a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should my child take for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme's published entry requirements before deciding, because they vary and they are the only authority that matters. Broadly, Analysis and Approaches is the proof and calculus route that engineering and mathematics departments usually expect, and Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route suited to social sciences, design and business. A tutor can tell you which course your child is actually coping with; the admissions page tells you which one the degree will accept. Both questions need answering, in that order.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Masdar City family need to be permitted?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine schedule is published, so a quoted amount is unverified.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi IB students sit exams in the same session as everyone else?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We do not print a specific IB examination or results date here, because the IB organisation blocks automated checking and an unverified date is exactly the kind of detail a parent would act on wrongly. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed calendar, and the internal coursework deadlines on it usually matter more than the exam dates, because they land while teaching is still running and they cap the marks available.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IB subjects for the same Masdar City student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for, because a single tutor holding both courses sees patterns across them. Physics with Analysis and Approaches is the pairing that works most often, since the mathematics underpins the physics. Chemistry with Biology is common too. Two humanities subjects rarely sit with the same specialist. If the combination is not available, we say so rather than putting a generalist on both, because one strong subject specialist plus one more beats two mediocre matches.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Masdar City family get started?
faqs.answer: For core Diploma mathematics and the sciences, usually within the same week, with the free trial lesson included in that. For a narrower higher-level option, or a request for one tutor across two subjects, up to a fortnight at peak times. We tell you which case applies at the enquiry rather than after you have waited, and if we have nobody suitable at all we say that instead of booking you in and hoping somebody frees up.

faqs.question: What happens to lessons during Ramadan for a Masdar City family?
faqs.answer: Timings move and the structure holds. Lessons can shift to later evening slots after iftar, and because nobody is travelling, a change of time costs nothing but coordination. Revision plans adjust too: shorter, more frequent sessions work better than long ones in a month where sleep patterns change. Give us notice if a slot needs to move permanently so the tutor's week can be rebuilt; one-off moves are routine. Scheduling stays in Gulf Standard Time unless you ask otherwise.

intro.heading: Start with the number, because every other decision follows from it
paragraphs: A family in Mohammed Bin Zayed City typing "IB home tutor" into Google is usually three weeks past the point where a school report said something uncomfortable. The search is practical, not exploratory. It needs a rate, a format, a start date and an honest answer about whether the money will do anything. A university-student or budget online tutor in Abu Dhabi is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; EdFlik lists rates from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject specialist working online sits in the AED 150 to AED 300 band, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, with the travel built in, is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 by the providers who publish anything. A named Diploma specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, and the premium end, BartyED among them, reaches AED 650. Those are market figures read from provider pages in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

The gap between AED 150 and AED 500 is where most of the money in this market is lost, and it is rarely lost on quality. It is lost on geography. Mohammed Bin Zayed City is a large mainland grid of numbered zones south of the island, bordered by Mussafah on one side and the Sweihan road corridor on the other. A tutor who lives on Abu Dhabi island and agrees to come to a villa in Zone 12 is pricing a round trip of forty to seventy minutes into every single hour you buy. At the mid band that premium is AED 60 to AED 150 a session, and it buys nothing a student can write in an exam.

The second place money disappears is subject fit. Diploma Programme assessment is specific to the point of being unforgiving. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL sets a Paper 3 worth a fifth of the grade and tests problem-solving in extended, unfamiliar contexts. Chemistry HL asks for data analysis under a rubric most generalist tutors have never read. A competent all-rounder who lives fifteen minutes away will be cheaper per hour and more expensive per mark than a specialist two emirates or two time zones away who has taught that exact component for years. Online delivery removes the geography constraint entirely, which is the whole reason IB Gram works this way.

What follows is the full cost picture for an MBZ City family: the rate bands with their sources, the travel premium priced out, the costs that sit outside the hourly rate, the four most common ways parents overspend, and the honest position on what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Mohammed Bin Zayed City address; home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video, and the comparison table further down is the argument for why that is the better buy rather than a consolation.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-.programmesIntro: Mohammed Bin Zayed City households sit across the full International Baccalaureate range, from primary-age children in the PYP to Diploma candidates in their second year. The cost of support changes sharply between them, so each programme below carries its own price logic rather than a single blended rate.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examinations. Support here is about literacy fluency, number sense and the habits that make the Middle Years Programme survivable: reading for inference, showing working, finishing a task. Sessions are short, usually thirty to forty-five minutes, because attention rather than content is the limiting factor at this age.
programmes.countryNote: For an MBZ City family this is the cheapest intervention available and the one with the longest payback. A weekly half-hour at the lower end of the market band costs less per month than a single exam-year session at the specialist rate. Parents who wait until Year 10 pay several times more for the same gap in fractions or sentence construction.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a one-to-eight level rather than a percentage. Students lose marks for not meeting command terms in the task instruction, not for lacking content. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of genuinely independent work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: MYP support is the band where MBZ City parents most often buy the wrong thing. A tutor who drills content will not move a criterion-C level, because criterion C rewards communication. One term of fortnightly work on how the criteria are worded costs under a thousand dirhams at market mid rates and changes the reports more than a year of content revision.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade, and the externally examined papers carry the rest. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with three bonus points available from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the AED 200 to AED 450 specialist band applies and where it is worth paying. A Diploma candidate in MBZ City typically needs two subjects supported, not six, and a defined block of hours around the Internal Assessment deadlines their own school sets. Costed properly, that is a planned spend rather than an open-ended monthly bill.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma Programme courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits students who want applied study alongside recognised DP subjects rather than the full six-subject Diploma load.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP students usually take only two or three DP courses, the support bill is smaller and more predictable. An MBZ City family with a CP candidate is generally buying one subject at the specialist rate plus occasional help structuring the reflective project, which lands at the bottom of the monthly bands quoted above.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-.subjectsIntro: Price varies by subject more than most parents expect, because the supply of tutors who have actually taught a component differs enormously between subjects. The notes below name what each course assesses and where marks go missing, which is what you are really buying hours against.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, calculus. HL adds a third paper worth twenty per cent of the grade, sat without a syllabus prompt and built around extended problem-solving. Marks go on method lines left unwritten and on calculus notation that examiners will not infer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Graphical calculator work runs through both papers, with modelling, statistics and financial mathematics weighted far more heavily than in Analysis and Approaches. The common failure is treating it as the easy route: AI HL contains serious content and the Exploration is marked against the same twenty-mark rubric as AA.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields, nuclear and quantum physics, with an HL extension in each. Multiple-choice Paper 1A punishes unit slips; Paper 2 extended response punishes answers that describe rather than explain. The scientific investigation is the single largest block of coursework marks in the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity organised around two overarching themes, with organic mechanisms and energetics the two topics MBZ City students most often ask about. Data-based questions require a stated uncertainty and a conclusion that matches the data rather than the textbook.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. The volume of content misleads students into memorising at the expense of command-term precision: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each carry different mark-scheme expectations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed partly through portfolio commentaries built on published news articles. HL adds a quantitative paper. Commentaries lose marks on diagram labelling and on failing to apply a key concept explicitly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing and operations. The HL research project and the SL business idea both require primary or secondary evidence handled properly. Answers that recite theory without applying it to the named organisation stall at the middle bands.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, comparative essay work and an individual oral linking a global issue to two texts. HL adds a written essay. The individual oral is the component that most benefits from rehearsal, because the ten-minute structure is as marked as the content.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects answering a prescribed prompt, plus a 1,600-word essay on a title set by the IB. TOK contributes to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students lose marks by describing objects instead of justifying their link to the prompt.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies alongside their licensed international curriculum. KHDA, as the Dubai regulator, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students on these subjects, and the federal rule behind that requirement applies across the emirates.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Mohammed Bin Zayed City costs, by provider model
paragraphs: The honest summary is a range, because the Abu Dhabi market is not a single market. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised in the AED 150 to AED 300 band. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. A named Diploma specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, and the premium end of the market reaches AED 650 an hour. Budget providers advertise from AED 33 to AED 150, usually with university students teaching. All of those figures were read from provider pages in October 2026, and every one of them belongs to the provider named, not to IB Gram.

The table below compares the models rather than the brands, because comparing brands on price is how this market generates its misleading claims. What matters to a parent in Zone 18 is not which agency is cheapest but which model puts a specialist in front of their child for the fewest wasted dirhams. The columns that decide that are the travel element, the permit position and whether a replacement is possible if the match is wrong.

Two columns deserve a note. The permit column refers to the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and issued free of charge for two years. Anyone providing private lessons in the UAE without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you. The replacement column matters because the single largest hidden cost in tutoring is paying for six sessions with a tutor who was never the right fit and starting again.

Read the table as a shopping guide rather than a ranking. A tuition centre group class at the bottom of the rate range is genuinely good value for IGCSE content revision. It is poor value for a Higher Level Internal Assessment, where the whole point is individual method. Matching the model to the task is what reduces the bill.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced out for a Zone 18 villa
paragraphs: Take a concrete case. A tutor living in Al Khalidiyah agrees to teach a Diploma student in one of the central MBZ City zones at six in the evening. The drive out is twenty-five to forty minutes depending on how the Mussafah approach is running; the drive back is similar. That is roughly an hour of the tutor's working evening consumed by the road, on top of the hour taught. A tutor who needs to earn AED 200 for an hour of teaching has to charge something closer to AED 300 to make the journey worth making, and the published in-home bands reflect exactly that arithmetic.

The parent pays that premium, and it is worth being clear about what it purchases. It purchases the tutor being physically present. It does not purchase more teaching time, better subject knowledge, a specialist in the right component, or availability on the evening the student actually needs. At the top of the in-home band, AED 500 an hour, something like a third of the fee is road.

There is a second cost nobody quotes, which is scheduling fragility. A tutor driving across the emirate for one lesson will cancel when the traffic is bad, when a prior lesson overruns, or when a family event intervenes. Over a Diploma year that attrition matters more than the hourly rate, because the sessions lost are usually the ones closest to a deadline. Online slots do not fail for traffic.

None of that makes in-home tutoring a bad product. For a Year 3 child who cannot yet work independently on a screen, a person in the room is the right answer, and families in MBZ City who want that should budget the published AED 180 to AED 500 for it. What it does mean is that for a Diploma candidate, the premium is the least efficient dirham in the whole budget. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our Mohammed Bin Zayed City lessons run one-to-one over live video, and the comparison below is the reason.

sections.heading: The four ways MBZ City families overspend on IB tutoring
paragraphs: The first is buying breadth instead of depth. A Diploma student with a struggling grade in two subjects does not need six tutors; they need two, for a defined number of weeks, with the rest of the time protected for independent practice. Families who buy a tutor per subject typically spend three times what the problem required and leave the student with no time to consolidate. The hour the student spends alone redoing a question is the hour that moves the grade.

The second is paying weekly through the quiet terms. Diploma pressure is not evenly distributed: the Internal Assessment deadlines cluster, the mocks cluster, and the final push before the May session is its own distinct phase. A standing weekly commitment from September through to May at the specialist rate is a large annual figure for a service that was genuinely needed in perhaps eighteen of those weeks. Buying blocks against the school's own deadline calendar costs materially less and achieves more.

The third is paying for a generalist at specialist rates. The question to ask is narrow and specific: has this tutor taught Paper 3 of Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and can they describe how it differs from Paper 2? If the answer is vague, the rate should be a budget rate, because that is what is being supplied. Rates above AED 300 are only defensible for someone who knows the component cold.

The fourth is buying a promise rather than a plan. Any provider who offers a guaranteed grade should be treated with real scepticism, because no tutor controls what a student writes in an examination hall. What a provider can legitimately commit to is a named tutor, a stated number of hours, a defined focus, written feedback and a replacement if the match fails. That list is checkable before you pay. A score promise is not.
bullets: Two supported subjects beat six, at a third of the cost

sections.heading: The costs that sit outside the hourly rate
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a much larger education budget, and the hourly rate is a small part of what a Diploma year costs an Abu Dhabi family. Private school fees dominate. In Dubai, the regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the following academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package; Abu Dhabi fee changes run through ADEK's own approval process, which is worth checking before assuming a flat year. Either way, tuition support is being added on top of a fee that is already the largest number in the conversation.

Then there are the costs specific to the examination year. Candidates entered through their school pay entry fees via the school; private candidates pay examination centre fees directly and those are set by the centre, not by the board. A remark or enquiry upon results carries its own fee. A retake in the November Cambridge series, or a resit of a Diploma subject, means a second entry fee and often a second block of tutoring, which is why spending earlier is usually cheaper than spending later.

Coursework support is its own budget line and the one families most often underestimate. The Extended Essay runs over most of a year. Internal Assessments in several subjects land within a few weeks of each other. Theory of Knowledge needs an exhibition and an essay. Treating these as a planned block of checkpoint sessions, rather than emergencies solved at short notice, is both cheaper and considerably less stressful in a household where two or three children are in school at once.

Set against all of this, the question is not whether tutoring is expensive in absolute terms. It is whether a few thousand dirhams, spent in the right eighteen weeks on the right two subjects, protects a much larger spend that is already committed. Framed that way, the overspending described above looks less like extravagance and more like a budgeting error that is easy to avoid.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment support: what the fee can and cannot buy
paragraphs: This is the point at which price and integrity collide, and it needs stating plainly. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not tutoring. Under IB academic honesty rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. No price makes that a sensible purchase.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and it is where the marks actually are. They can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, so the student knows that the Mathematics Exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and roughly how many marks each carries. They can interrogate a proposed topic until it is narrow enough to be doable. They can read a draft the student has written and ask the questions a moderator would ask. They can teach the referencing convention. None of that involves producing the work.

In practice this makes coursework support one of the better-value things to buy, because the hours are few and their effect is concentrated. A student who understands why reflection is a separately marked criterion writes a different document from one who treats reflection as a closing paragraph. Three or four well-timed sessions, costed as a block, usually do more for a Diploma point total than a term of weekly content revision.

The boundary is also the test of a provider. Ask directly what happens if your child sends over a half-finished essay a day before the deadline. A provider who says they will review it, mark it against the criteria and send questions back is describing teaching. A provider who offers to finish it is describing a risk to your child's Diploma that no tutoring fee should ever purchase.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to charge you?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached, and a surprising number of parents paying cash each week have never asked about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The ministry's own service page lists the application through its smart app, website and e-services system, states no fee, and gives a completion time of two working days. The permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen can all apply. What the permit carries with it is a code of conduct, and one condition inside that code matters to Abu Dhabi families in particular: a teacher may not take paid private work with students affiliated with their own school. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes the same prohibition on tutoring students enrolled at the teacher's own school.

So the sentence "your child's own teacher, privately" is not a feature. It is the arrangement the rules exist to prevent, and it exposes the teacher rather than the family. The useful question to a prospective tutor is simply whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and whether your child's school is one they are permitted to work with. A tutor operating properly will answer in a sentence.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and the ministry has not specified amounts, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal category again, needing an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant regulator, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram does not operate premises in the UAE and should not be described as holding any such permit.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection reports and the spend you have already made
paragraphs: Mohammed Bin Zayed City sits in Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes, which is a free and underused source of information for a family deciding where tutoring money should go. It is also the regulator that no competitor page in this market names at all, which tells you something about how locally those pages were written.

An inspection report is more useful to a tutoring decision than a league table. It describes teaching quality by phase and by subject group, names the areas the school has been asked to improve, and gives a view on student outcomes in external examinations. If a report flags secondary mathematics as an area for development, that is a stronger reason to buy Higher Level mathematics support than any marketing claim, and it is published evidence rather than a sales line.

The report also tells you what you should not be buying. Where a school is strong, paid support duplicates provision you have already paid for in fees. Many Abu Dhabi schools run their own after-school clinics, subject surgeries and Internal Assessment workshops at no extra cost. Asking the subject teacher what internal support exists before engaging a tutor is the cheapest step in this entire process and is skipped constantly.

Across the emirates the regulator changes but the principle does not. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the Ministry of Education. The Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods, so regulation in this country reaches considerably further than inspection alone.

sections.heading: What the next step costs, and what it does not
paragraphs: The first session with IB Gram is a free trial lesson, with no card required and no package attached before it. Its purpose is narrow: to find out whether this particular tutor and this particular student can work together, and to confirm that the tutor genuinely knows the component in question. A trial that produces a vague, encouraging conversation has told you nothing. A trial that produces a diagnosis of where marks are being lost has told you everything you needed to decide.

After the trial, the shape of the spend is agreed before it starts: which subject, which component, how many hours, at what frequency, finishing on what date. For an MBZ City family that usually means one or two subjects, a fixed evening slot after the drive home, and a review point six sessions in. If the match is wrong, the tutor is changed rather than the family starting over with another provider.

Where a niche Higher Level subject has no UAE-based specialist free, we say so rather than substituting a generalist at a specialist rate. In those cases the match may be a tutor in another time zone teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and the rate and the reasoning are stated upfront. Disclosing a coverage limit is uncomfortable commercially and is the opposite of what this market usually does, which is precisely why it is worth doing.

What the next step does not include is a promise about a number. Nobody can sell a 7 in Chemistry Higher Level, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling something they cannot deliver. What is being offered here is a specialist, a defined block of hours, honest feedback about what the student is actually getting wrong, and a cost you can calculate in advance to the dirham.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not "maths help" but "Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, losing marks on Paper 3". The narrower the brief, the better the match and the fewer hours you buy. Include the school, the year group and the next deadline that matters.

process.title: We name the tutor and state the coverage honestly
process.description: You get a named specialist with the subjects and levels they teach, not a pool. If no UAE-based tutor covers that component, we say so and explain what the alternative is and what it costs, before you commit anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: A real diagnostic lesson in an evening slot that fits the MBZ City school run. No card details and no package. You should finish it knowing what is going wrong and whether this tutor can fix it.

process.title: Agree the hours, the focus and the end date
process.description: Weekly through a term, or a defined block before a mock or the May session. The hour count, the focus and the finishing date are set in advance, so the spend is a known figure rather than a rolling bill.

process.title: Review at six sessions and adjust
process.description: A short written review of what has moved and what has not, against the same component you started with. If the answer is that the subject no longer needs support, we say that and stop, which is the review's whole purpose.

Three of the pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and two quote in dollars. A parent should not have to telephone to learn the shape of a market.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so none of the fee funds a drive across the emirate to the MBZ zones. At the mid market band that removes roughly AED 60 to AED 150 of dead cost from every session you buy.

whyPoints.title: Component-level specialists, not local availability
whyPoints.description: The match is made on whether a tutor has taught the exact paper and level your child sits, rather than on who lives within a twenty-minute drive of Zone 18. For Higher Level sciences and mathematics that difference is the whole value of the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught by letter, drafts questioned, referencing covered, and the student writing every word. We decline requests to produce assessed work, because IB malpractice findings land on the student and no fee is worth that risk.

whyPoints.title: Costs stated before they are incurred
whyPoints.description: An hour count, a focus, a frequency and an end date agreed at the start, with a review point six sessions in. Open-ended monthly billing is how families in this market end up spending several times what their problem required.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed, not concealed
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject, we say so and explain the alternative and its rate. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several hide non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Mohammed Bin Zayed City cost per hour?
faqs.answer: The Abu Dhabi market splits into bands. Budget online tutors, usually university students, advertise from around AED 33 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject specialist online sits between AED 150 and AED 300. In-home one-to-one visits with travel included are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, and named Diploma specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, with the premium end reaching AED 650. Those are provider-published market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's own price list. For an MBZ City address the in-home band carries a travel element the online band does not.

faqs.question: Why is an MBZ City in-home rate higher than an online rate for the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Because you are funding the road. A tutor coming from Abu Dhabi island to a central MBZ City zone spends forty to seventy minutes driving around a one-hour lesson. To earn the same for the evening, they have to charge more per taught hour, and the published in-home bands reflect that arithmetic. At the top of the band something like a third of the fee is travel. That money buys physical presence, which genuinely matters for a young child, but it buys no extra teaching, no better subject knowledge and no specialist in the component your Diploma candidate is losing marks on.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in the MBZ City zones?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. Mohammed Bin Zayed City lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and a digital whiteboard. The practical effect is that your choice of tutor is not limited to people willing to drive to Zone 18 after work. A Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has taught the data-analysis component for years becomes available to you, and the travel premium disappears from the fee entirely.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB tutoring should an MBZ City family budget for?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families assume, spent more deliberately. A Diploma candidate with two weak subjects usually needs those two supported, not all six, and needs them in concentrated phases rather than evenly across the year. A realistic shape is weekly sessions in one subject through a term, plus a defined block of three or four coursework checkpoint sessions, plus an intensive block of two sessions a week in the weeks before the May examinations. Market monthly estimates for a weekly specialist session run roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200, with exam-year intensity reaching AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether the package matches the term you are in. Packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A package is good value during a phase of genuine need, such as the run-up to mocks or an Internal Assessment deadline cluster. It is poor value as a standing arrangement through quiet terms, which is where families overspend. Buy blocks against your school's own deadline calendar rather than a rolling commitment.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects cost the most to find support for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The scarce ones. Higher Level mathematics, physics and chemistry command the top of the rate band because the pool of tutors who have actually taught those components is small, and smaller still in the mainland districts. Group 2 languages at Higher Level and specialist options such as Higher Level economics quantitative work are similarly thin. Group 1 English and Standard Level humanities are much better supplied and therefore cheaper. Online delivery flattens this somewhat, because the match is made from a national pool rather than from whoever is free within driving distance of Mohammed Bin Zayed City.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a false economy at Diploma level. Mathematics and physics sometimes pair credibly in the same person. Chemistry and biology rarely do at Higher Level, because the assessment demands differ. The question to ask is component-specific: has this tutor taught that exact paper at that exact level, and can they describe how its mark scheme differs from the paper before it? If the answer covers one subject convincingly and the others vaguely, you are paying a specialist rate for generalist teaching in two of three subjects.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Mohammed Bin Zayed City need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, the ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time, and eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored privately by their own teacher from school?
faqs.answer: That arrangement is the one the rules are designed to prevent. The code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff being prohibited from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their school. The exposure falls on the teacher rather than on your family, but it is still not a sound basis for a working relationship. A tutor with no connection to the school is the straightforward route.

faqs.question: Can an MBZ City tutor help with the Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permitted help is where most of the available marks sit. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, narrow an unworkable topic into a doable one, read a draft the student has written and ask the questions a moderator would ask, and teach the referencing convention. What no tutor may do is produce the work. Submitting anything that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB academic honesty rules, and the consequence lands on the student. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a risk no fee justifies.

faqs.question: When do UAE students actually sit their exams, and how does that affect cost?
faqs.answer: IB Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session, with November available as a second session at some schools. Cambridge International runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE family should be planning around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cost follows the calendar: rates do not change but intensity does, and the weeks before a session are when families buy two or three sessions a week instead of one. Planning that block early is cheaper than booking it in panic.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if exams are two months away?
faqs.answer: No, but what the money can achieve changes. With eight weeks left, new content is a poor investment and examination technique is a good one: past papers under timed conditions, command-term precision, mark-scheme reading, and the two or three topics where the student loses the most marks for the least effort. That is a defined block, usually two sessions a week, with an end date. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of Higher Level mathematics, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling optimism rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying a tutor anything in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Five questions settle it. Which exact papers and levels have you taught for this subject, and how do their mark schemes differ? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? What happens after six sessions if nothing has moved? Will I get written feedback I can read? And what will you do if my child sends you an unfinished Internal Assessment the night before the deadline? The last answer is the most revealing: review and question is teaching, finishing it for them is a risk to your child's Diploma.

faqs.question: Does ADEK publish anything that helps me decide where to spend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes describing teaching quality by phase and subject group, alongside the areas a school has been asked to improve. If a report flags secondary mathematics, that is published evidence for buying Higher Level mathematics support rather than a marketing claim. The same report also shows where a school is strong, which is where paid support duplicates provision your fees already cover. Many Abu Dhabi schools run free subject clinics worth asking about first.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based tutor covers my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not the market norm. For a niche Higher Level option there may be no Abu Dhabi specialist with a free evening slot. In that case the match may be a specialist in another time zone teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we state that and the rate before anything is agreed. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign contact number; disclosing a coverage limit upfront is less comfortable commercially and considerably more useful to a parent trying to plan an exam year.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-.closingHeading: Work out the number before you commit to it
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-.closingBody: Tutoring in Abu Dhabi is not expensive so much as badly budgeted. The AED bands on this page are the market, published by the providers named and read in October 2026, and they show where the waste sits: travel premiums that buy no teaching, generalists charged at specialist rates, and standing monthly commitments through terms when nothing was needed. A Mohammed Bin Zayed City family who supports two subjects for a defined block of hours, online and on Gulf Standard Time, spends a fraction of what the open-ended version costs. Start with a free trial lesson, ask the component-level question, and agree the hours before the first dirham moves.

intro.heading: Price it by the month, because that is how the money leaves
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring page in this market quotes an hourly rate, and almost no family thinks in hourly rates. A Mussafah household deciding whether to support a DP1 student in two subjects is making a monthly commitment that will run for eighteen months. The question that matters is what that costs between now and the May session, and what the household gets for it. Mussafah is also a district where the gap between the advertised rate and the delivered rate is unusually wide, so the arithmetic is worth doing properly rather than guessing at it from a headline figure on an agency homepage.

Work the arithmetic forward. Two subjects, one session each per week, at the market rate for a qualified online subject tutor, is eight sessions a month. Market monthly packages advertised in the Emirates sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and in-home packages of four two-hour visits are quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Over a two-year Diploma that difference compounds into a figure most families have not consciously decided to spend. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Mussafah makes the in-home end of that market particularly expensive, and not because anyone is overcharging. The residential Shabiya districts sit well south of the island and away from the Khalifa City school corridor where most IB specialists are concentrated. A tutor travelling here in the early evening gives up the better part of ninety minutes to the round trip, and that time appears inside the hourly rate whether or not it is itemised. Families often read the higher figure as better teaching. It is mostly a transport cost.

The second thing worth understanding is where tuition money actually disappears, because it is rarely the headline rate. It disappears in sessions spent re-teaching content the student already has, in a tutor who knows the subject but not the assessment, in blocks bought for a term when six focused weeks would have done, and in cancelled visits that still get paid for. Those four leaks together cost more than the gap between a mid-band and a premium tutor. Each of them is avoidable, and none of them is avoided by paying more per hour.

IB Gram is a matching platform, and for families in the UAE every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates — home visits are offered only in India — so there is no travel premium inside the rate and no session shortened by the Mussafah run. What follows sets out the market figures, with sources, and then shows what a monthly plan for a Mussafah student should look like.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mussafah.programmesIntro: Mussafah families requesting IB support are almost always in one of three places: the Middle Years Programme, the first year of the Diploma, or the final stretch before the May session. Each has a different monthly cost profile, and knowing which you are in prevents buying the wrong shape of help.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked A to D against band descriptors rather than percentages. There are no external papers for most students, so the cost of support here is lower and the purpose is different: keeping criterion-level work at a consistent standard and preparing for the step into Diploma assessment.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest point at which a Mussafah family can intervene usefully. A single weekly session through MYP 4 and 5 costs a fraction of an exam-year intensive and removes most of the reason for one. Families who wait until DP1 pay more for the same gap.

programmes.name: IB Diploma, first year
programmes.description: Six subjects selected, three at Higher Level, with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge beginning and the first Internal Assessment work starting. Nothing is examined externally yet, which is exactly why this is the year where money spent produces the most marks later.
programmes.countryNote: A DP1 plan for a Mussafah household is usually one or two subjects at one session a week, costing well under the exam-year figure. The decision that drives the bill is subject choice: a student carrying three sciences at Higher Level will need more support than one with a balanced block, and that is worth modelling before the choices are locked.

programmes.name: IB Diploma, final year
programmes.description: Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay all reach school-set deadlines across the year, and the written papers sit in the May session. The cost profile is front-loaded around deadlines and then back-loaded around paper technique, with a quiet stretch in between.
programmes.countryNote: The most common Mussafah overspend happens here: a family books a weekly session for the whole year when the actual need is two deadline blocks and an eight-week paper run. Mapping the year against the school's own deadline calendar usually cuts the total without cutting the marks.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE, the feeder route
programmes.description: Many Mussafah students arrive at the Diploma from an international GCSE rather than from MYP, sitting Cambridge syllabuses such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics or Pearson equivalents including 4MA1. UAE centres sit the June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE-to-Diploma transfer student often needs a short, cheap bridging block in the summer term rather than a long Diploma support arrangement. Identifying that correctly is the single biggest saving available to a Mussafah family moving between systems.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mussafah.subjectsIntro: The subject mix from Mussafah leans towards maths, the sciences and business, which also happen to be the subjects where specialist supply is tightest and where a mismatch costs the most. Each note below says what the subject assesses and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes manipulation weaknesses that a calculator has masked for years. HL marks are lost in proof, complex numbers and harder calculus. The exploration loses marks when the mathematics is correct but too shallow for the level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology. Every paper assumes a graphical calculator is used quickly and correctly, and students taught by hand lose time rather than knowledge. The exploration rewards a genuine data set and a question with a real answer.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, fields and the long-answer questions produce the widest spread. Students describe where the command term asked them to explain, and lose the final marks of a six- or seven-mark question that they had otherwise answered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry gate everything downstream, so a weakness there reads as weakness across the paper. Organic mechanisms at Higher Level are the topic most often needing rebuilding rather than revision, and the practical scheme of work is where Mussafah transfer students have gaps.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content tempts students into reading rather than writing. Marks sit in data analysis and in comparative questions with a stated measure. Command terms carry more weight here than in any other science.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with one sentence of explanation scores where three paragraphs do not. Higher Level calculation questions are arithmetically simple and verbally tricky, so timed practice matters more than extra content.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish general answers. Marks come from applying a named tool to the stimulus firm and then evaluating it, and most candidates stop before the evaluation. Higher Level adds extension topics and a longer research component.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of unseen text is the trainable component. Students write about what a text says rather than how it works, which caps the mark regardless of vocabulary. A planned structure is worth more than fluency.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum as a mandatory subject in UAE private schools, with genuinely separate first-language and additional-language routes. Support focuses on reading fluency and written register rather than conversational ability.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers reward precision about algorithms, data structures and system fundamentals more than coding ability. Marks are lost in pseudocode conventions and in a solution that works but is barely documented against the criteria.

regions.name: Mussafah Shabiya
regions.note: The main residential districts, with dense apartment housing and a large school-bus population heading north each morning. Weekday sessions realistically start after 17:00 once students are home and fed.

regions.name: Mussafah Industrial Area

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City

regions.name: Baniyas and Al Shawamekh

regions.name: Khalifa City

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Coastal communities with IB provision nearby. A Mussafah student enrolled here has one of the longer daily commutes in the emirate.

regions.note: The island holds the oldest established private schools. Families from Mussafah who enrol there accept close to an hour each way as the cost of the programme.

schoolClusters.city: Mussafah and the near mainland
schoolClusters.note: Schools within a short drive of the Shabiya districts, mostly following Indian or British curricula. IB Diploma provision is not located here, which is why Mussafah IB families commute north and why the local tutor pool is thin in Diploma subjects.

schoolClusters.note: Where most Mussafah students following the Diploma or an international GCSE actually attend. The cluster mixes British and IB provision within a few kilometres, so two children from the same building can be on different assessment calendars.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Mussafah costs by the month
paragraphs: The honest starting figure is a range, because the market is wide and the published numbers come from providers with very different models. At the budget end, online tuition from generalist or university-student tutors is advertised in the Emirates from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour — Tutopiya publishes from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor working online sits higher: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A-Level work are quoted from about AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270, and premium named tutors advertised far higher again — BartyED quotes AED 650.

Turn those into months. One session a week at the budget end is roughly AED 130 to 260 a month. At the qualified-subject band it is AED 600 to 1,200. At the specialist exam-year band it is AED 800 to 1,800 or more. Two subjects doubles each figure. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session land in the same places: AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

In-home visiting tuition is the expensive column. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors in the Emirates at AED 200 to 500 including travel, with monthly in-home packages quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. None of these are IB Gram's prices; they are the market, published by those providers and read in October 2026. What IB Gram offers instead is a free trial lesson and a consultation that sets a monthly plan against your child's actual deadlines.

sections.heading: The four places Mussafah families lose tuition money
paragraphs: The first leak is re-teaching. A tutor who starts at the beginning of a topic the student already half knows is comfortable and expensive. Two sessions of a four-session month can disappear into revisiting material that a marked script would have shown was already secure. The fix is unglamorous: session one works through the student's most recent marked paper and sorts every lost mark into did not know it, knew it and wrote it badly, or knew it and ran out of time.

The second is subject knowledge without assessment knowledge. A tutor can be an excellent mathematician and still not know that an IB exploration is marked against criteria with specified weightings, or how a Paper 2 mark scheme credits a method line. That gap shows up as sessions that feel productive and marks that do not move. Ask a prospective tutor to describe the assessment structure of the exact course your child sits, not the subject in general.

The third is buying the wrong duration. Families commonly buy a year of weekly sessions when the real need was two deadline blocks and an eight-week paper run, or buy an eight-week intensive when the problem is a two-year foundation gap that an intensive cannot touch. Mapping the plan against the school's own deadline calendar before agreeing anything usually reduces the total spend without reducing the marks.

The fourth is specific to in-home arrangements in a district like Mussafah: paid-for sessions that do not happen, or happen short. A tutor caught in traffic on the mainland road arrives at 17:50 for a 17:30 session and leaves at the agreed time. Over a term that is several hours of teaching bought and not received, and it is the leak nobody budgets for.

sections.heading: Why a visit to Shabiya costs more than the lesson inside it
paragraphs: The published premium on in-home tuition is not a quality premium. It is mostly a transport charge, and in Mussafah it is a large one. The specialist IB tutor pool in Abu Dhabi clusters near the island and the Khalifa City school corridor, because that is where the IB schools are. A tutor coming south to the Shabiya districts at 17:00 and returning at 19:30 has spent perhaps ninety minutes travelling for sixty minutes of teaching, and no sensible person does that at the same hourly rate they charge for a session they log into from home.

That arithmetic has a second consequence that matters more than the money. A tutor willing to make the Mussafah trip is selected by geography, not by specialism. The question stops being who teaches Chemistry Higher Level well and becomes who is prepared to drive here on a Tuesday. For a common subject at a common level that may be a tolerable trade. For Physics HL in the final year of the Diploma it usually is not, and the families who feel most let down by tuition are the ones who made that substitution without noticing.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. The model for Mussafah families is one-to-one live video, which removes both halves of the problem: no travel inside the rate, and a tutor chosen from everyone who teaches the subject rather than from everyone who can reach the postcode. There is one thing the in-home format genuinely offers that video does not: a physical presence enforcing attention on a student who will not otherwise sit down. If that is the real problem, it is worth naming, because it is a supervision need rather than a teaching need and it can be met more cheaply than by hiring an IB specialist to drive to Shabiya.

sections.heading: What you are actually paying for in the Diploma: the internal components
paragraphs: Families budgeting for Diploma tuition usually budget for exam preparation, and then find that the expensive months are the ones around internal deadlines. Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment — an exploration in Mathematics, practical investigation work in the sciences, a commentary portfolio in Economics — and all of it is marked against published criteria and submitted to school-set deadlines across DP1 and DP2. On top sit the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

The reason these cost money is that they are the parts school classes have least time for. A teacher with a full timetable can explain the criteria once and read one draft. A student who has never been shown what the difference between the middle and top band of a criterion looks like in practice will produce competent work and score in the middle, which over six subjects is a meaningful number of points.

What a tutor can do here is bounded and worth stating plainly before any money changes hands. A tutor may teach the content the assessment needs, explain each criterion in ordinary language, read the student's own draft and say where it falls short of the criterion, teach method — structuring an argument, presenting data, referencing properly — and ask the questions that make the student find the weakness. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft or supply any part of the work, may not invent data, and may not edit a draft into something the student could not have produced.

That line is not decoration. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student, who signs the authenticity declaration, not on the seller. A coordinator conducting an Extended Essay viva is experienced at noticing a draft whose voice shifts between paragraphs.

sections.heading: Higher Level, Standard Level and what each adds to the monthly figure
paragraphs: Subject choice is the lever that moves a Diploma tuition budget most, and it is pulled in DP1 before most families have thought about tuition at all. Higher Level carries more taught content, an extra paper in most subjects, and a heavier Internal Assessment expectation. A student with three Higher Levels in mathematics and the sciences is carrying a workload that produces more tutoring demand than one with a balanced block, and the monthly cost follows.

The practical question is not whether Higher Level is harder — it is — but whether a particular Higher Level is needed. University prerequisites are the honest test. A student heading for engineering or medicine will need specific Higher Levels, and paying for support in them is a rational investment. A student taking Higher Level Physics because a classmate did, with no course ahead that requires it, is generating tuition demand for nothing.

The second lever is the Mathematics route. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses, not harder and easier versions of one. AA rewards algebraic fluency and proof; AI rewards modelling, statistics and confident use of a graphical calculator. A student placed in the wrong one spends two years and a great deal of tuition fighting the course rather than learning it, and the right time to get this right is before the choice is submitted.
The table sets the two levels against each other on the points a parent budgeting for support actually needs.

sections.heading: What a free trial lesson should tell you before you spend anything
paragraphs: A trial lesson is worth something only if it is a working session rather than a conversation. The useful version takes a recent marked paper or a draft the student has written and does real work on it for an hour, after which the tutor should be able to say three things concretely: what the recurring mark loss is, what the next six to ten weeks should contain, and what they cannot fix in that time.

Three questions separate a tutor who will add marks from one who will add reassurance. First, can they describe the assessment structure of the exact course — the papers, the weightings, the criteria — without being prompted. Second, can they look at a marked script and name the pattern in the losses rather than calling a topic weak. Third, will they state the academic-honesty boundary on Internal Assessment work before you ask about it. A tutor who volunteers that third answer has worked with coordinators before.

A trial also tells you something about scheduling that no amount of discussion will. A Mussafah student who finishes the bus journey at 15:45 is a different student at 16:30 than at 18:30, and the trial is the cheapest way to find out which one learns. Running the trial in the slot you intend to keep is worth more than running it at a convenient time.

Because the trial is free there is no sunk cost pushing a family towards a tutor who is not right. Any condition attached to a trial should be stated on the same screen as the word free — length, eligibility, whether a card is required — and if it is not, that is a reason to ask.

sections.heading: Permits, legality and what a very cheap tutor may be skipping
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted work. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

The free-of-charge point matters for a cost-focused page, because it removes an excuse. A tutor who implies the paperwork is prohibitively expensive is not describing the UAE system. Individuals offering private tuition without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, but the ministry has not published a fine schedule — Khaleej Times reported that it did not specify the amounts or detail the penalties — so figures circulating online should be treated as unverified rather than repeated.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, showing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A tuition business with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs an institutional permit — in Dubai, a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring provider should claim one it cannot evidence.

One further rule shapes who you should hire. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction. That is press-reported and worth checking against the current ADEK policy document, but it means a very cheap offer from your child's own teacher is the wrong kind of bargain.

sections.heading: Fitting sessions around the Mussafah school run without paying for dead time
paragraphs: Mussafah's residential districts send most of their secondary students north by bus, and the day is long at both ends. A departure before 07:00 and a return between 15:30 and 16:15 is normal for a student at a Khalifa City or island school. That produces a real weekday window from about 17:00 to 20:30, and a student who is noticeably better at the back of it than the front.

Paying for the wrong end of that window is a quiet waste. A session at 16:00 straight off the bus often runs at perhaps two thirds of the productivity of the same hour at 18:30, and over a twelve-week block the difference is several sessions of effective teaching. Families who treat session timing as an academic decision rather than a diary decision get more for the same money.

Weekends are where longer work belongs. A full past paper sat to time needs an uninterrupted two hours and cannot be squeezed into a weekday evening after a bus journey, so the pattern that works for most Mussafah exam-year students is one or two shorter weekday sessions plus a weekend slot long enough for a paper and its mark-scheme walkthrough.

Term structure matters too. Ramadan shortens the school day and reorganises evenings around iftar, and sessions moved to after iftar — often 20:30 to 22:00 — work better than sessions attempted mid-afternoon on a fasting day. Winter and spring breaks are the only stretches where sustained foundation work is possible without school homework competing, which makes them the cheapest weeks of the year to buy.

Full past papers belong at the weekend, not after the bus
