faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Mussafah cost per month?
faqs.answer: Taken from published market rates, one weekly session with a qualified online subject tutor works out at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, because Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and the qualified band runs to about AED 300. Two subjects doubles that. In-home visiting packages are quoted higher — around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition in Shabiya priced above online lessons?
faqs.answer: Mostly transport. The specialist IB tutor pool in Abu Dhabi sits near the island and the Khalifa City school corridor where the IB schools are, so a tutor visiting the Mussafah residential districts at 17:00 gives up around ninety minutes of travel for sixty minutes of teaching. That time is inside the hourly rate whether or not it is itemised, which is why published in-home bands run AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The second cost is invisible: a visiting tutor is selected by who will drive to Mussafah rather than by who teaches the subject best.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a Mussafah apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, because in-home tuition is a service offered only in India. Every lesson for a family in Mussafah or the Shabiya districts runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that the match is made by subject and level rather than by who covers the south mainland, and the session starts at the agreed minute rather than whenever the road allows. The free trial lesson works the same way, so you can judge the format as well as the tutor before committing to anything.

faqs.question: How many sessions a month does a DP1 student in Mussafah usually need?
faqs.answer: Four, in one subject, is the usual starting point in the first Diploma year, and it is enough when nothing external is close. The purpose in DP1 is to stop a gap forming and to get the Internal Assessment started properly, both of which respond to steady weekly work rather than intensity. Families who carry three Higher Levels in mathematics and the sciences often need two subjects supported, which doubles the figure. The expensive mistake is buying an exam-year intensive in DP1, when the same money spread across the year produces more marks and leaves the exam term lighter.

faqs.question: Where do Mussafah families most often waste tuition money?
faqs.answer: Four places. Re-teaching content the student already had, because nobody read a marked script first. Hiring subject expertise without assessment expertise, so sessions feel useful but marks do not move. Buying the wrong duration — a year of weekly work when two deadline blocks and an eight-week exam run was the need, or an intensive when the gap is two years deep. And, with visiting tutors, paying for sessions that arrive late or not at all because of the mainland road. Those four together usually cost more than the gap between a mid-band and a premium hourly rate.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online tutor at AED 50 an hour ever the right choice for Mussafah?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. Tutopiya publishes from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and at that level you are buying structure and company rather than syllabus expertise. For an MYP student who will work if someone sits with them, or for homework supervision across several subjects, it can be exactly right and it is a fraction of the specialist rate. It is the wrong purchase for a DP2 student eight weeks from the May session, where the whole value is in knowing the mark scheme, and where an inexpensive generalist will produce comfortable sessions and no extra marks.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects cost the most to support from Mussafah?
faqs.answer: The ones where specialist supply is tightest: Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and any Group 2 language outside the common ones. Rates rise because fewer tutors can teach the course to the mark scheme, not because the subject is harder to arrange. Supply is also why these are the subjects where a geographic search hurts a Mussafah family most — the pool willing to drive to the south mainland for a Tuesday evening session is far smaller than the pool teaching the subject. Matching online removes that constraint entirely.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my Mussafah child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because it reduces the monthly figure. Mathematics with Physics, or Economics with Business Management, are pairings a single tutor can often handle properly. Chemistry with English is not, and a tutor who says yes to every combination is telling you something. The test is whether they can describe the assessment structure of both courses specifically — papers, weightings, criteria — rather than talking about the subjects in general. Where a genuine pairing exists, one tutor also gives you a single view of the student's working habits, which is useful in its own right.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Mussafah students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though the ministry has published no fine schedule, so amounts quoted online are unverified. The official route is MoHRE's private tutor licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my child's Internal Assessment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content the assessment needs, explain each criterion in plain language, read a draft your child wrote and say where it does not yet meet the criterion, teach method such as structuring an argument or presenting data, and ask the questions that make your child find the weakness. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft or supply any part of it, may not invent or provide data, and may not edit a draft into work your child could not have produced. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level worth the extra tuition cost for a Mussafah student?
faqs.answer: Only when a course ahead requires it. Higher Level carries additional taught topics, an extra paper in most subjects and a heavier Internal Assessment expectation, so it generates more tutoring demand across two years. That is a rational spend for a student heading into engineering or medicine who needs the specific Higher Levels. It is money spent for nothing when a Higher Level was chosen because a classmate took it. The same logic applies to the Mathematics route: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses, and a student in the wrong one spends two years fighting it.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time in the year to buy support?
faqs.answer: The winter and spring breaks, because they are the only stretches where a student can do sustained work on a weak foundation without school homework competing for the same evening. Foundation repair done in a break removes the need for a longer and more expensive exam-term intensive later. The most expensive weeks are the six to ten before the May session, when demand for specialists peaks and when the work can only be technique rather than content. A Mussafah family that uses a break for repair and the final weeks for paper drilling spends less in total.

faqs.question: Can lessons move after iftar during Ramadan without extra cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise evenings around iftar, so a slot that ran at 17:30 typically moves to somewhere between 20:30 and 22:00, where a fasting student is measurably sharper than mid-afternoon. Session length often drops while frequency holds, which keeps the compounding that makes revision work. Because the lesson is delivered over live video there is no travel to reschedule and no surcharge for an unusual hour. The pattern that costs most is pausing for the month and resuming three weeks before papers.

faqs.question: What should I ask in a free trial before paying for a block?
faqs.answer: Three things. Ask the tutor to describe the assessment structure of the exact course your child sits — the papers, the weightings, the criteria — without prompting. Ask them to look at a marked script and name the pattern in the lost marks rather than calling a topic weak. And ask where the line sits on Internal Assessment help; a tutor who states it before you raise it has worked with coordinators. Run the trial in the slot you actually intend to keep, because a Mussafah student straight off the school bus is not the same student as one working at 18:30.

faqs.question: What happens if we want to stop after a month?
faqs.answer: You say so, and the plan stops. A monthly shape is used rather than a long block precisely so that the decision point comes round often, and because a plan built against your school's deadline calendar has natural stopping places — after an Internal Assessment deadline, after a mock, after the exam run. If the issue is the match rather than the need, a different tutor is proposed instead, without an argument about the remaining sessions. The free trial exists so that this conversation is rare: most mismatches are visible in that first working hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-mussafah.closingBody: Tell us the subject, the year group, the next hard deadline and what you are willing to spend each month. The free trial lesson costs nothing and runs in the slot you intend to keep, so you see the teaching and the timing before any money moves. abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-isla.tutorsIntro: Saadiyat Island enquiries tend to open with a budget rather than a subject, which is a sensible place to start. We work the other way for matching: subject and level first, then the hours the budget actually supports, then the person. Diploma and Middle Years specialists, all delivering on video.

intro.heading: The number nobody in this market will print
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked tutoring pages for Abu Dhabi queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family on Saadiyat Island actually transacts in. One of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. That gap is the reason this page opens with dirhams rather than with reassurance.

Here are the bands, each attributed. In-home one-to-one visits across the Emirates are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the Bestimate Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Student tutors online start lower, from AED 33 to 65.

The gap between the in-home band and the online band is not a quality gap. A substantial part of it is the car. A tutor driving to a Saadiyat Beach villa from the mainland is pricing the journey into the hour, and on an island reached by bridges that journey is not trivial at four in the afternoon. You are buying a tutor's travel time at the same rate as their teaching time.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Saadiyat Island is one-to-one teaching over live video, which removes the travel component from the price and, more usefully, removes it from the choice of tutor. That second effect is worth more than the first and almost nobody frames it that way.

The rest of this page is arithmetic rather than argument. What the travel premium buys when it is worth buying. The full Abu Dhabi market as a monthly figure rather than an hourly one. Where families reliably waste money, which is a longer list than the one on which they save it. A two-year Diploma budget. Who may legally tutor in Abu Dhabi and how you check. And what a free trial lesson should tell you before anything is paid.

One note on honesty before the numbers. None of the figures below is an IB Gram price list. We publish the market so you can measure any quote against it, including ours, and so that a provider refusing to name a number has to explain why. A page that shows its sources is more useful than a page that shows confidence, and it lets you do the arithmetic yourself rather than take anybody's word for it.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-isla.programmesIntro: Cost per useful hour varies enormously across the IB continuum, and families routinely spend most where the return is lowest. These are the four stages and what each is actually worth paying for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment, so nothing is urgent and nothing should be expensive. The genuine need at this stage is arithmetic fluency and sentence construction, both of which respond to short frequent practice rather than to subject expertise. The budget band is the right band here, and spending at the specialist band is money with nowhere useful to go.
programmes.countryNote: Saadiyat Island primary pupils are mostly at schools on the island or a short drive across the bridge, so they are home early and have capacity. Two twenty-minute sessions a week at the lower market band is a few hundred dirhams a month and is the single best-value tutoring a Saadiyat family will ever buy, precisely because nothing is at stake yet.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, converted into a one-to-seven grade. The paid work worth doing here is criterion coaching, which is a qualified-teacher skill rather than an examiner one. That puts the right spend in the middle band, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on published market rates, and rarely above it.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years families on Saadiyat Island often buy too late and then too much. A single weekly hour across a year costs less in total than an exam-term intensive and builds the criterion-reading skill the Diploma will test again at seventeen. The Personal Project year is the one place a few specialist hours at the start are genuinely worth the higher band.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. This is where specialist rates make arithmetic sense, because a named component weakness in a Higher Level paper needs somebody who teaches that paper. Two hours at the right band beats twelve at the wrong one, consistently.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students on Saadiyat Island typically finish between 15:00 and 15:45 and face a bridge crossing if they attend a mainland school. That makes a 17:00 or 19:30 online slot far more reliable than a visit timed around traffic, and it removes the risk of paying for an hour that starts twenty minutes late.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with career-related study and a reflective project. Rare in Abu Dhabi, but where it runs the Diploma courses inside it are examined on the same papers with the same weightings and the same Internal Assessments, so the cost of supporting them is the cost of supporting a Diploma subject.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi schools run the Career-related Programme, so Saadiyat Island families are usually comparing the Diploma against A Levels or an American diploma. If your child is on it, say so when asking for a quote, because a provider pricing it as something lighter than the Diploma has misunderstood what is being examined.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-isla.subjectsIntro: Cost per hour is the same across subjects in this market; cost per grade point is not. These are the subjects Saadiyat Island families ask about, with the part of each that justifies paying for expertise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, a fifth of the grade and unlike anything at Standard Level. That paper is the clearest case in the Diploma for paying the specialist band, because format practice with mark-scheme reading cannot be improvised by a general mathematics tutor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-dependent throughout, with statistics and modelling carrying the content. A large share of lost marks is calculator fluency rather than mathematics, which is cheap to fix and therefore poor value at premium rates. Middle band, drilled properly, is the right purchase.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent across multiple-choice and data-based sections, Paper 2 forty-four, the investigation twenty. Uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation are specialist territory; general problem practice is not, and families often buy the second while needing the first.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium carry Higher Level difficulty. The habitual mark loss is moles arithmetic written without units, which is a discipline problem fixable at the middle band. Paying specialist rates to correct unit discipline is the most common overspend in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High volume, and the marks turn on terminology precision rather than on understanding. Short timed recall work delivers most of the available improvement and does not require an examiner. The investigation and the data-based section are where expertise earns its premium.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the most reliably available mark in the course and the cheapest to fix. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a quantitative policy paper, where a specialist is worth paying for because the arithmetic demand is specific and drillable rather than general.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers plus the Individual Oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. The Individual Oral is the component most under-prepared and the one where a few expert hours change most, because it is a rehearsed ten-minute argument rather than an informal conversation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A sixteen-hundred-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. A small number of hours spent on argument structure and on choosing real specific examples is unusually good value, because almost nobody receives any targeted teaching on it at school.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research, combining with Theory of Knowledge for up to three bonus points. The marks are decided in the first fortnight by the research question, which makes early hours worth several times what late hours are worth on this component.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language

sections.heading: Can you get an IB home tutor in Saadiyat Island, and what does it cost
paragraphs: Yes, in-home tutoring exists on Saadiyat Island, and the market price for it is knowable. Independent tutors and agencies quote roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for a one-to-one visit across the Emirates, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and individual home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages seen in the market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions.

On an island reached by bridges, those figures carry a particular meaning. A mainland tutor driving to a Saadiyat Beach villa or to Mamsha Al Saadiyat at four in the afternoon is spending real time on the road, and that time is priced into the hour. The same tutor quoting the same rate to a Khalifa City family is selling a materially larger share of teaching per dirham. Nobody itemises this, and it is most of the premium.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and that is the position across every country page on this site. What we deliver to Saadiyat Island is one-to-one teaching over live video, at an hour your household chooses, with the student's own school material on screen and a whiteboard that can be saved and reread.

The honest case for a visit still exists and it is worth stating. For a young child, or a student who will not stay at the table without an adult physically present, somebody in the room can decide the outcome, and no amount of video quality replaces that. If that describes your child, you want a provider who does visits, and we will say so rather than talk you into a format that will not work.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and when it is worth it
paragraphs: A premium is only waste if it buys nothing. The in-home premium does buy things, and a family deciding how to spend should know what they are. Physical presence keeps a reluctant student at the table. It removes the device as a distraction, which for some twelve-year-olds is decisive. It lets a tutor see a worksheet, a textbook and a school planner at once without anybody photographing anything.

What it does not buy is depth of expertise, and that is the trade everybody makes without noticing. The pool of tutors willing to cross the bridge to Saadiyat Island at a given hour is small. The pool who teach, say, Chemistry at Higher Level weekly and know how the data-based section is marked is also small. The intersection of two small pools is very small indeed, and it is almost never the best available teacher for that component.

There is a second cost nobody quotes for. A visit has a travel risk attached, and travel risk lands on the family. A tutor stuck on the bridge arrives twenty minutes late and the hour is still charged. Across a term that is several hours of paid time converted into waiting, and it is the kind of loss that never appears in anybody's comparison because it is invisible per occurrence.

The decision rule that holds up: if your child needs an adult present to work at all, buy presence and accept a narrower choice of teacher. If your child can work with somebody competent on a screen, buy expertise and spend the difference on more hours or on a better-matched specialist. Most Diploma students are in the second category and most primary pupils are in the first.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi market as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Hourly rates are a poor unit for a family budget, because nobody buys one hour. The monthly figure is the one that decides whether a plan survives contact with a household's actual finances, and it is calculable from published bands. The table below does that arithmetic with every band attributed to the provider or rate table it came from.

Read it from the bottom up rather than the top down, because the cheapest viable option is the one families skip past. A university-student tutor online at AED 33 to 65 an hour, one session a week, is a few hundred dirhams a month and is genuinely the right purchase for arithmetic fluency, vocabulary drilling or keeping a Middle Years student on top of homework. Buying the specialist band for that work is money with nowhere to go.

The middle band, a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300, works out at about AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly hour on Bestimate's own mid-band estimate. That is where most useful Diploma support sits for most of the year. Specialist exam-year support at two sessions a week reaches AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above on the same source, which is a different kind of commitment.

A note on fees in context. Abu Dhabi private school fees are approved through ADEK rather than set freely by schools, and fee-increase applications go through the regulator. This page publishes no Abu Dhabi fee band, because no figure for it has been verified for this project and an invented number would be worse than none. Your school's fee schedule is published on its own site, and that is the right denominator for any tutoring decision.

sections.heading: Where Saadiyat families reliably waste money
paragraphs: The waste is patterned and almost all of it comes from buying before diagnosing. A family notices a grade, feels the urgency, and purchases a package of hours. Nobody has yet established whether the problem is content, command-term reading, unshown working or pacing, and those four need different remedies, different people and different numbers of hours.

The second pattern is breadth. A Diploma student in difficulty often ends up with tutoring in four subjects at once, which is unaffordable and counterproductive, because the limiting resource at seventeen is the student's remaining hours rather than the family's money. Two subjects done properly beats four done thinly, and the student has a life to live alongside it.

The third pattern is band mismatch in both directions. Paying premium rates to correct unit discipline in Chemistry is overspending on a problem the middle band solves. Paying the budget band to prepare a Higher Level Paper 3 is underspending on a problem the budget band cannot touch. Both are common and both come from choosing a price before identifying a job, which is the wrong order and the expensive one.

The fourth is resources. Nobody needs a purchased archive of papers and mark schemes, and in any case those documents belong to the examination boards. We reference and link official material rather than supplying it, because reproducing board documents is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to everything required, and a tutor who needs a paper can work from the copy the school already holds.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma budget, built from published bands
paragraphs: Most families never cost the Diploma as a two-year project, and the result is a series of urgent decisions each more expensive than the last. The table below builds an indicative plan from published market bands. It is not a quote and it is not our price list; it is arithmetic you can run yourself and then compare any proposal against.

The shape that produces the lowest total is counter-intuitive. Spend steadily and modestly through the first Diploma year on the subject that is genuinely weakest, at the middle band. Spend a defined block on the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay early, because marks on both are decided by the research question in the first fortnight. Then spend intensively only in the final term, and only on named components identified from mock scripts.

The shape that produces the highest total is the common one: nothing for eighteen months, then everything at once in the spring of the second year, across four subjects, at specialist rates, when the student has the fewest spare hours they will ever have. That pattern can cost several times as much and return less, because the weeks available no longer match the work required.

Build the plan with the school calendar in front of you. Internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge cluster in a nine-month stretch, and knowing where two of them collide tells you which month will need help. Because no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in Abu Dhabi, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is both a legal point and a practical screening tool. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Because the permit costs nothing, a UAE-based tutor who does not hold one has no financial excuse. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Abu Dhabi has an additional layer worth knowing about. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and verify against the current policy document if it matters to your situation.

The practical consequence for a Saadiyat Island family is a short script. Ask whether the tutor is UAE-based. If yes, ask to see the permit. Ask whether your child is enrolled at the school where the tutor teaches. Decline the arrangement if the answer is yes. And do not accept a claim of regulator approval from any agency: a KHDA educational services permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises, and IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind.

sections.heading: What a free trial should tell you before any money moves
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a test you are running on the provider, not a sales appointment they are running on you. Ours is one per family, booked before any payment and with no card details taken. It is a real lesson on your child's own material, and three things should come out of it that a conversation cannot give you.

First, a specific diagnosis. At the end the tutor should be able to name what is going wrong in a way you can check against the marked work: lost marks clustering in one command term, unshown working in multi-step questions, a topic missing from two years ago, or pacing. A tutor who offers encouragement instead of a diagnosis has told you what the engagement will be like.

Second, evidence of subject depth. Ask what Paper 2 is worth in your child's subject at their level, or which Internal Assessment criterion carries the most marks. Those figures are published, so hesitation is informative. For a Higher Level component this matters more than anything else, and it is the thing proximity-based searching optimises away.

Third, a straight answer on hours. A good tutor will tell you roughly how many sessions removing the identified problem usually takes, and will say when the answer is more than the remaining weeks allow. No provider can guarantee a grade or an improvement, and anyone offering one is selling. Eight focused weeks can move a boundary; they rarely move three.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Saadiyat Island cost?

What we deliver to Saadiyat Island is one-to-one teaching over live video, at an hour your household chooses, with your child's own school material on screen. If you specifically need somebody physically present, you want a different provider and we will tell you so.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring more expensive than online in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Mostly the car. A tutor crossing to Saadiyat Island from the mainland in the late afternoon spends real time travelling, and that time is priced into the hour at the same rate as teaching. There is a second, unquoted cost: travel risk sits with the family, so a tutor delayed on the bridge arrives twenty minutes late and the hour is still charged. Across a term that quietly converts several paid hours into waiting, and no comparison table in this market accounts for it.

faqs.question: When is paying the in-home premium actually worth it?
faqs.answer: When your child will not work without an adult physically present. For a young child, or a student for whom the device itself is the distraction, presence can decide the outcome and no video quality substitutes for it. What the premium does not buy is subject depth, because the people willing to cross the bridge at a given hour and the people who teach a specific Higher Level component weekly are two small groups whose overlap is smaller still.

faqs.question: What should a Saadiyat family expect to spend a month on IB support?
faqs.answer: At published market bands, one weekly hour with a student tutor online is roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's budget estimate. One weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor sits around AED 600 to 1,200. Exam-year specialist support at two sessions a week reaches AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. In-home packages are quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are the market's numbers, not ours, and any quote you receive should be measurable against them.

faqs.question: Which is the cheapest Diploma support that actually works?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour at the middle band, started in the first Diploma year on the genuinely weakest subject, plus a short defined block on the Extended Essay research question. At published rates that is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month plus one block, and it produces the lowest total cost per grade point available. The most expensive pattern is the common one: nothing for eighteen months, then four subjects at specialist rates in the final spring when the student has fewest spare hours.

faqs.question: Is a group class cheaper than one-to-one for an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and that is sometimes the right trade. A group class suits a student who is near target and needs structure, pace and company. It cannot address one student's specific error pattern, because the group moves at group pace and your child's unshown working or misread command terms are invisible in it. The practical combination that works is a group class for structure plus occasional one-to-one for the identified weakness, rather than one replacing the other.

faqs.question: Do we need to pay for past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone selling them. Examination board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to everything required. We reference and link the official sites and work from the school's own papers, which costs nothing and carries no risk.

faqs.question: How do I check an Abu Dhabi tutor is legally allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tutor work permit. MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a UAE-based tutor without one has no excuse, and those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored by a teacher from their own Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: You should assume not. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording and verify against the current policy if it matters. Either way, it is an arrangement we never facilitate.

faqs.question: How does tutoring cost compare with Abu Dhabi school fees?
faqs.answer: That depends on your school, and this page deliberately publishes no Abu Dhabi fee band because no figure for it has been verified for this project, and an invented number would be worse than none. Abu Dhabi private school fees are approved through ADEK rather than set freely by schools, and fee-increase applications go through the regulator. Your school publishes its own fee schedule, and that is the right denominator when you are deciding how much tutoring is proportionate.

faqs.question: Should we buy a ten-hour package to get a lower rate?
faqs.answer: Not before a marked script has been read. The discount is real and the risk is larger: you are committing hours before anybody has established whether the problem is content, command-term reading, unshown working or pacing, and those four need different people. Buy one diagnostic session, get a classification you can check against the marked work, then buy a block with a stated objective. The cheapest line in any tutoring budget is the hour that turned out not to be needed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor do my son's Internal Assessment if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No, at any price. Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own, and no tutor at IB Gram will write an Internal Assessment, draft an Extended Essay or produce coursework. One operation in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student as a malpractice finding, not on the seller. What a tutor can do is narrow the research question, challenge the method and give feedback against the criteria, which raises the mark legitimately.

faqs.question: Will you tell us if tutoring is not the right spend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens regularly. Some problems are school problems, where the right first step is a conversation with the department rather than a purchase. Some are workload or sleep problems that no tutor touches. Some are subjects already at target, where a changed revision routine beats a weekly hour. We would rather say that in a free trial lesson than take a year of fees for an engagement that was never going to move anything.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free for the subject and hour we can afford?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist at the price you named. Common Diploma subjects at common hours usually match within a few days. A narrow Higher Level combination at one fixed evening hour can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is available at any band. Hearing that honestly leaves you time to look elsewhere, which is worth more than discovering in session three that the specification is unfamiliar to the tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-cit.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Shakhbout City families work to your school's calendar: the subject specialist is chosen for the named course and level, and the first conversation is about which deadline is next rather than which chapter to open.

intro.heading: Start from the deadline and work backwards
paragraphs: Shakhbout City is a villa community on the Abu Dhabi mainland, within the broader Khalifa City corridor and sitting between Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City. It was built as family housing rather than as a commercial district, the streets are compound rather than tower, and most children here attend one of the international schools in that corridor or in the communities immediately around it. It is, in short, a neighbourhood of school runs and homework tables.

What brings a parent here to a search engine is almost never curiosity about the Diploma. It is a date. An Internal Assessment draft due in three weeks. A mock series starting after the break. A Theory of Knowledge essay that has not been started. A Mathematics exploration with a topic that will not carry the mathematics. The useful response to that is not a description of the IB; it is a plan that runs backwards from the date.

Which is why this page is organised as a calendar. The Diploma is two years long and it has far more deadlines than families expect, most of them set by the school rather than by the IB. The external examination window gets all the attention and arrives last. The internal coursework calendar arrives first, repeatedly, and across six subjects at once, and that is where Diploma terms actually go wrong.

One important limit on what this page will tell you. IB exam and results dates are set by the IB and revised from time to time, and we publish none of them here, because the only version worth acting on is the one your school's IB coordinator holds. Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session; beyond that, ask the coordinator and write the dates down. A tutoring page quoting an IB date to you is offering you a liability dressed as a service.

On delivery, the direct answer to the search. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor will arrive at a Shakhbout City address. Lessons are live one-to-one video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the named course and level rather than for proximity.

That is a calendar argument as much as a logistics one. A tutor whose week is a driving route cannot move a session into the fortnight where three deadlines collide, because the route is the business. An online slot can shift, double for a defined period, and pause across an exam week without being reassigned. In a Diploma year that flexibility is worth more than any individual hour.

What follows is the calendar in detail: the two years counted backwards, the internal deadlines that govern a term, how Ramadan reshapes revision, mock season as diagnosis rather than prediction, the boundary on coursework help, and what the market charges per term rather than per hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-cit.programmesIntro: A Shakhbout City family may be at any stage of an IB education, and each stage has a different calendar shape. These are the four, with what each one's year actually looks like.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with no external examination. Assessment is continuous, teacher-led and portfolio-based, culminating in the Year 6 Exhibition. The calendar is gentle and the support that matters is mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure, and the habit of recording thinking rather than only answers.
programmes.countryNote: In a villa community the practical constraint at this age is the length of the day rather than any deadline. A primary child home at four after a school run is better served by thirty or forty focused minutes than by an hour, and an online session from the kitchen table avoids a second journey at the end of an already long afternoon.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by school-set boundaries, with no external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. The calendar is a steady rhythm of criterion-marked tasks rather than a build towards one window, and the Personal Project runs through Year 10 or 11.
programmes.countryNote: The deadline that matters here is the Personal Project, which families consistently underestimate because it has no external examination attached. It is a long piece of independent work with a process journal, and a student who starts it late produces a thin report regardless of how good the product is. Mark it on the calendar in September of the year it falls.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of its grade. The externally examined papers arrive at the end; the internal deadlines arrive continuously across both years, across all six subjects at once.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. We publish no IB dates here — confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator, including the internal deadlines, which are the ones that actually structure a term. The commonest Diploma failure in this emirate is not weak teaching; it is six internal calendars colliding in one fortnight that nobody mapped in September.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. The Diploma-course components are assessed identically to the full Diploma, so their calendars are the same, with the reflective project adding its own.
programmes.countryNote: A smaller cohort in Abu Dhabi than the full Diploma but a real one. The calendar advantage is that there are fewer internal deadlines to collide, and the risk is that the reflective project receives no attention until late because it sits outside the subject timetable. Treat it as a deadline with the same weight as an Internal Assessment.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-cit.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Shakhbout City families most often need, with the internal component each one carries — because that component is what sets the term's deadlines.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with HL adding a third paper of extended investigations. Its internal component is an individual exploration of twelve to twenty pages, which needs a viable topic chosen a term before the draft is due.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The exploration here usually rests on data the student gathers, which adds a collection stage to the calendar that students forget to budget for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics with HL extensions. The internal investigation needs an experiment designed, run and written up, and uncertainty analysis treated as a criterion rather than an appendix.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. The investigation requires laboratory access through the school, so its timing is constrained by the school's own schedule, not only by the student's.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology. The data-based paper separates grades, and the investigation often involves fieldwork or a long data-collection window that has to be planned months ahead.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and development. The internal portfolio is three commentaries on real published articles, each with its own deadline, which spreads the workload across both years rather than concentrating it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. The HL research project needs a focused question early; a vague one cannot be rescued in the final term no matter how many hours are bought.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Literary and non-literary texts, the Individual Oral, the HL Essay and guided analysis. The Individual Oral has a fixed recording window set by the school, which makes it one of the least movable deadlines in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries, and an essay on a prescribed title. Both have school-set deadlines and both are routinely left until they collide with subject Internal Assessments in the same fortnight.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent essay with a supervisor and staged school deadlines for proposal, interim draft and final submission. Those staged deadlines are the whole calendar: a student who meets them writes a decent essay almost automatically.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks actually have to achieve
paragraphs: Answer first, because this is why most Shakhbout City families arrive here. In any eight-week stretch of a Diploma year there is one thing that genuinely has to be delivered and several that merely feel urgent. Identifying which is which is the whole of the planning, and it takes twenty minutes with a calendar rather than a consultation.

The test is simple: which of these dates is set by someone other than my child? A school Internal Assessment deadline is set by the school and moving it requires permission. A mock date is fixed. An Individual Oral recording window is fixed. A subject test is fixed. Against those, a self-imposed revision plan or a vague intention to "catch up on chemistry" has no date at all and will lose every collision with something that does.

So the eight-week plan starts by listing every externally imposed date in that window across all six subjects plus the core, and then asking what each one requires to be already done. An Internal Assessment deadline in week six requires a complete draft by week four, which requires a method and data by week two, which means the work starts now rather than in week five. Written out, most Diploma crises turn out to have been visible eight weeks earlier.

That list is also the brief for any tutoring. A block of sessions aimed at the one deliverable that cannot move is worth more than the same number of hours spread across three subjects by feel. And where the list shows nothing immovable in the next eight weeks, the honest answer is that this is the cheap window — the moment to fix habits and close content gaps rather than to buy crisis hours.
bullets: List every date in the window that somebody other than your child controls
Work out what each one needs already finished, and when
Aim any tutoring at the deliverable that cannot move
A window with no immovable date is the cheap window — use it on habits

sections.heading: The Diploma counted backwards
paragraphs: Families plan forwards from today and run out of weeks. The Diploma rewards the opposite: start at the end and work back, because every stage has a predecessor that has to be complete before it can begin. This is not a scheduling nicety; it is the difference between an Extended Essay written across a year and one written across a fortnight.

Read backwards, the two years have a clear shape. The examination window sits at the end of DP2 and nothing can be changed by then. The weeks before it are for timed papers and error patterns only. Before that, the final internal submissions for Internal Assessments, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which in most schools cluster in the first half of DP2 and are the real pressure point of the whole programme. Before that, DP1 is for choosing topics, gathering data, doing the laboratory work and establishing the habits that make DP2 survivable.

The stage families skip is topic choice, and it is the cheapest stage and the most consequential. A Mathematics exploration with a topic that cannot carry mathematics at the course level, or an Extended Essay with a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, cannot be rescued by effort later. Half an hour of interrogation at the proposal stage saves a term.

We publish no IB dates in the table below, deliberately. The stages are universal; the dates are your school's and the IB's. Get them from your IB coordinator in September of DP1, write them on one sheet, and the rest of this plan builds itself.

sections.heading: Internal deadlines beat external ones, every time
paragraphs: Parents arrive focused on the examination window because it is the thing with a name. Students experience something different: a continuous sequence of school-set deadlines across six subjects and three core components, any two of which can land in the same week. That sequence, not the examination, is what determines whether a Diploma year goes well.

The arithmetic is worth seeing. Six Internal Assessments, each with at least a proposal, a draft and a final submission. An Extended Essay with staged submissions and supervisor meetings. A Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, each with its own drafts. That is well over twenty school-set dates across two years, set independently by different departments, none of whom are coordinating with each other around your child's particular combination.

The single most valuable thing a Diploma family can do costs nothing: collect every internal deadline in September, put them on one sheet in date order, and find the collisions. There is always at least one fortnight with three deliverables in it. Knowing about it in September means the Economics commentary gets written in October instead. Discovering it in the week itself means a compromise on all three.

This is also where online tutoring has a structural advantage that is easy to overlook. A session can double in frequency for three weeks around a collision and return to normal afterwards, because nothing depends on a tutor's route through the city. A visiting tutor with a fixed driving schedule cannot do that, which means the help is available in the weeks you did not need it and unavailable in the week you did.

sections.heading: Ramadan, school holidays and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A UAE academic calendar is not a European one with the names changed, and a revision plan written as though it were will fail in a predictable place. Ramadan falls inside the school year, school days are shortened, family routines change substantially, and the hours when a teenager can concentrate move later. None of that is an obstacle if it is planned for, and all of it is an obstacle if it is discovered.

In practice, sessions move to post-Iftar timing and the slot is held rather than reassigned. That works well and students are often sharper then than in a shortened school afternoon. What does not work is pretending the month is a normal one: three subjects scheduled at the usual times, homework volumes unchanged, and a mock series immediately afterwards with no adjustment. The sensible plan treats the month as a lower-intensity period and loads the weeks either side.

The same logic applies to the long summer break and to the mid-year break. These are the only extended stretches in a Diploma where a student has uninterrupted time, which makes them the natural home for the work that needs continuity: data collection, an Extended Essay draft, a Mathematics exploration write-up. A student who arrives in DP2 with an Extended Essay draft written over the summer is in a materially different position from one who does not.

Travel is the other UAE-specific variable. Families in this corridor travel, sometimes for weeks, and an in-home arrangement simply stops when they do. An online slot follows the family, which in a Diploma year means a three-week absence costs nothing rather than costing a unit.

sections.heading: Mock season is data, not a prediction
paragraphs: Mock results produce more anxiety per unit of information than anything else in a Diploma year, and the anxiety is misdirected. A mock grade is one data point from one day under unfamiliar conditions, often on partially taught content, marked by a teacher calibrating against a boundary set internally. As a prediction it is weak. As teaching material it is the best thing the school will produce all year, and most of it gets filed.

What a marked mock script shows is how your child behaves under timing. Which question they abandoned. Where they ran out of minutes. Whether the lost marks are knowledge, method presentation, command-term misreading or time management — four completely different problems with four different fixes, indistinguishable from the grade alone and obvious from the script.

So the high-value move after mocks is not more revision. It is one or two sessions spent working through the scripts, question by question, naming each loss and sorting it into those four categories. The output is a short list that tells you where the remaining months should go, and it frequently contradicts what the family assumed. A student "weak at physics" turns out to be losing eleven marks to running out of time and four to physics.

There is a scheduling point too. The fortnight either side of mocks is swallowed by them, so any tutoring planned in that window should be either mock preparation or script review, not new content. Families who book ordinary weekly sessions straight through mock season pay for hours the student has no capacity to use.

sections.heading: Where a Shakhbout City afternoon fits
paragraphs: The geography here is kinder than in much of the emirate, and it is worth saying so rather than manufacturing a problem. Shakhbout City sits inside the Khalifa City corridor, which holds the densest concentration of international schools in Abu Dhabi, and most families here have a short school run. A day ending around 3.15pm commonly puts a student home before four.

That makes a genuine afternoon slot available — 4.30pm or 5pm with a student who is still functioning — which is not true of families commuting from the islands or across the city. For a Diploma student this matters more than it sounds, because late sessions compete with homework volumes that are already heavy in DP2, and a 7pm start on top of three hours of coursework is a session about exhaustion.

The families here who do have a long run are those who chose a school on Yas, Saadiyat or in the city for a specific programme rather than for proximity. For them the honest answer is an evening slot, planned for a realistic arrival time rather than an optimistic one, and often shorter and more frequent rather than long and weekly.

An in-home tutor would be drawing from the same corridor, which makes the travel argument weaker here than elsewhere — and the calendar argument stronger. The reason not to use a visiting tutor in Shakhbout City is not the distance; it is that a driving route cannot double its frequency for the three weeks when three deadlines collide, which is precisely when a Diploma family needs it to.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: Given that this entire page is about deadlines on assessed work, the boundary needs stating precisely. It is set by IB academic-honesty rules, the student signs an authenticity declaration, and a breach is an expulsion-level risk for them rather than a reprimand for us. So the line is not a policy preference; it is the only version of this service that is safe for your child.

A tutor may teach the subject content the task rests on. Explain what each criterion rewards and in what proportion. Question a method until the student notices its weakness themselves. Read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion it is underselling and why. Teach referencing, citation and how to describe a method so another person could repeat it. Run a timed practice task on a different topic entirely. Interrogate whether a research question is answerable in the word count.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, draft a paragraph for the student to adapt, edit a draft to completion, rewrite sentences so the final text is partly theirs, generate a research question and hand it over, supply data the student did not gather, or provide a worked model of the actual task. An operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and it is not a service we offer at any fee.

One related boundary parents ask about. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads — we reference them and link the official source. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, nor use examiner status to imply access to marking or boundaries.
bullets: Allowed: teaching content, explaining criteria, questioning a draft, teaching citation
Allowed: interrogating whether a research question is answerable at the word count
Not allowed: writing, drafting, rewriting or editing assessed work to completion
Not allowed: supplying research questions, data, or a model of the live task

sections.heading: What it costs, priced by term rather than by hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a calendar-driven decision. A Diploma family does not need a constant number of hours; they need more in the fortnight where three deadlines collide and fewer in the quiet stretches. So the useful way to price this is per term, with a plan behind it.

The published market bands, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500 with the journey inside the fee. A named IB or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates give AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Mapped onto a Diploma calendar that becomes manageable. A deadline block of three to six sessions is a one-off cost in the term it falls. Weekly teaching in one subject across a term sits in the mid-range monthly band. A pre-mock or pre-session intensive sits in the specialist exam-year band for a few weeks only. The error is to buy the exam-year intensity for two years, which exhausts both the budget and the student.

faqs.question: We have an IA deadline in three weeks. Is it too late to get help in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes shape. Three weeks before a submission the job is not to improve the mathematics or the method; it is to make the existing draft score what it is capable of scoring against the criteria. That means a criterion-by-criterion read of the student's own draft, naming what each section is underselling, and two or three focused revisions the student writes. What cannot be fixed in three weeks is a topic that was never viable, which is why topic interrogation is the cheapest session in the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Which deadlines actually matter most in a Diploma year?
faqs.answer: The ones somebody other than your child controls. School-set Internal Assessment submissions, the Extended Essay's staged deadlines, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, a fixed Individual Oral recording window, mock dates and school-scheduled laboratory access. Against those, any self-imposed revision intention has no date and will lose every collision. List the immovable dates across all six subjects plus the core, work out what each needs already finished, and most Diploma crises turn out to have been visible two months earlier.

faqs.question: Why do you not publish the IB exam and results dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the IB sets them, revises them periodically, and our sources for them could not be verified directly against the IB itself. A date a parent acts on has to be right, and the only version worth acting on is the one your school's IB coordinator holds. What we will say is that Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. Treat any tutoring page that quotes you a specific IB exam or results date with caution, because it is offering you a liability rather than a service.

faqs.question: How many school-set deadlines does a Diploma student actually have?
faqs.answer: More than twenty across the two years, and that is the number families find surprising. Six Internal Assessments, each with at least a proposal, a draft and a final submission. An Extended Essay with staged submissions and supervisor meetings. A Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, each with drafts. They are set independently by different departments, none of whom are coordinating around your child's particular six-subject combination, which is why collisions happen and why collecting the dates in September is the single highest-value free action available.

faqs.question: What is the one free thing a Shakhbout City Diploma family should do first?
faqs.answer: Collect every internal deadline from the school in September of DP1 and put them on one sheet in date order. Then look for the fortnight with three deliverables in it, because there is always at least one. Knowing in September means the Economics commentary gets written in October rather than compromised in February. Discovering it in the week itself means three compromised pieces of work. This costs nothing, takes one meeting with the IB coordinator, and prevents more damage than any amount of tutoring bought later.

faqs.question: How should we plan around Ramadan in a Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a lower-intensity period and load the weeks either side, rather than running a normal schedule through it. School days shorten, routines shift later, and students concentrate better after Iftar than in a compressed afternoon. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing and the slot is held rather than reassigned. What fails is pretending the month is ordinary: full session loads, unchanged homework expectations and a mock series immediately afterwards with no adjustment. Plan the month in advance and it costs nothing academically.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma student do over the mid-year and summer breaks?
faqs.answer: The work that needs continuity, because those are the only uninterrupted stretches in two years. Extended Essay drafting is the obvious one: a student who arrives in DP2 with a draft written over the summer is in a materially different position from one who does not. Data collection for a Mathematics exploration or a science investigation also suits a break, since it needs time rather than teaching. What does not suit a break is content revision, which is better done in term when the teaching is live alongside it.

faqs.question: Are mock results worth worrying about?
faqs.answer: Not as a prediction, and enormously as data. A mock grade is one data point from one day under unfamiliar conditions, often on partially taught content, marked against internally set boundaries. The marked script, though, shows exactly how your child behaves under timing: which question they abandoned, where the minutes ran out, whether the losses are knowledge, method presentation, command-term misreading or time management. Those are four different problems with four different fixes, invisible in the grade and obvious in the script. Most families file the script and keep the anxiety.

faqs.question: Should we book weekly sessions straight through mock season?
faqs.answer: No. The fortnight either side of mocks is swallowed by them, and a student sitting six papers has no capacity to absorb new content in that window. Anything booked there should be either mock preparation — a timed paper and its review — or script review afterwards. Ordinary weekly teaching through mock season is hours paid for and not used. The high-value booking is one or two sessions in the week after results come back, spent working through the scripts and sorting every lost mark into a category.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to a villa in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. In this corridor the reason is not distance — a visiting tutor would come from the same school belt — it is the calendar. A driving route cannot double its frequency for the three weeks when three deadlines collide, and that is exactly the week a Diploma family needs it to.

faqs.question: Can the frequency change during the year rather than staying fixed?
faqs.answer: That is the point of planning by calendar. A slot can double for three weeks around a deadline collision and return to weekly afterwards, pause across mock and examination weeks without being reassigned, shift post-Iftar through Ramadan, and follow a family travelling for a fortnight. None of that is possible when a tutor's week is built around a driving route through the city, which is why an in-home arrangement tends to deliver help in the quiet weeks and nothing in the busy ones.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor may interrogate whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words, explain what the assessment criteria reward, teach the subject content the essay rests on, read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion it undersells, and teach referencing and citation properly. A tutor may not generate the research question and hand it over, write or redraft any part of the text, edit to completion, or supply sources the student has not read. The student signs an authenticity declaration, and under IB rules a breach is an expulsion-level risk for them.

faqs.question: What does Diploma support cost across a term in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: Price it per term rather than per hour. Published market figures read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and a named IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with Bestimate's 2026 estimates giving AED 600 to 1,200 a month for mid-range weekly sessions and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A deadline block of three to six sessions is a one-off in the term it falls. The error is buying exam-year intensity for two full years.

faqs.question: When is the cheap window to buy Diploma help?
faqs.answer: Any eight-week stretch with no immovable date in it, which in most schools means the autumn term of DP1. That is when habits can be changed rather than patched: working presentation, how to read a command term, how to write a method somebody else could repeat, how to choose a topic that will carry the work. Nobody buys then because nothing has gone wrong, and it is the period where the same money does the most. By the final term the only purchase available is damage limitation at exam-year rates.

faqs.question: What do you need from a Shakhbout City family before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: The named course and level, the school, the next immovable deadline, and the actual piece of work in front of it — a draft, a proposal, a marked script. Plus the time your child is home, which in this corridor is usually before four and occasionally much later if you chose a school on the islands. With that, the trial hour works on the real deliverable, and at the end you should know what the next two weeks contain rather than having heard a description of the Diploma.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-cit.closingBody: Diploma terms in Shakhbout City rarely go wrong because of weak teaching. They go wrong because six internal calendars collide in one fortnight nobody mapped in September. Get every deadline from your IB coordinator, put them on one sheet, find the collision, and aim help at the deliverable that cannot move. We teach Shakhbout City students live over one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, flex the frequency with the calendar, publish no IB dates we cannot verify, and run no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Send the course, the next deadline and the work in front of it.
